title: Chinese HSK 5
description: The fifth step in Mandarin Chinese, from HSK 4 to the new HSK 5 (HSK 3.0). Grammar lessons cover 一旦…就, 哪怕…也, 假如, 万一, 不但不…反而, 没有…就没有, 再…也, 为的是, the extended uses of 下来, 下去, 起来 and 过来, 被…给 passives, 把 with two objects, comparisons such as 他大我三岁, adverbs of mood (毕竟, 居然, 果然, 简直, 反正, 根本) and the written style of notices, news and arguments (便, 较, 及, 其, 某, 如何, 从而, 可见, 因而). The first four-character idioms come with the stories behind them. Topics follow first jobs, health and lifestyles, relationships, study and technology, city and country, the law and the media. The 1,600 new words (3,600 in all) are learned through typed review cards and the 431 new characters (1,527 in all) through notecards, words and tracing, with pinyin you can turn off and a switch to traditional characters. Readings grow to about 600 characters, and the last lessons practise the picture story, the essay, the speaking test and the exam format. Requires Chinese HSK 4.
author: Erudior

lessons.title: A first job
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

Welcome to HSK 5. You know 2,000 words and 1,096 characters, the complex sentences of HSK 4 ({尽管|jǐn guǎn}…{但是|dàn shì},
{即使|jí shǐ}…{也|yě}, {不管|bù guǎn}…{都|dōu}, {既然|jì rán}…{就|jiù}) and the first words of **[[written style]]** ({此|cǐ}, {与|yǔ}, {由|yóu}, {将|jiāng}, {已|yǐ}, {仅|jǐn}). This course
adds 1,600 words and 431 characters, and three things grow:

- **Register.** More and more of what you read is written Chinese: contracts, notices, news, reports.
  Each written word is taught beside its spoken partner, and you learn which one fits where.
- **Idioms.** This lesson brings the first four-character idiom, {各行各业|gè háng gè yè}. Lesson 20's honors
  lessons tell where idioms come from.
- **Length.** Readings are 400 to 600 characters, like the texts of the HSK 5 exam, and from this
  module on you write a short story from four pictures.

The course follows the same people as before. It's 2030: {王芳|Wáng Fāng} has started as a reporter
({记者|jì zhě}, HSK 4) at a news website, {李明|Lǐ Míng} is doing a master's in England, {安娜|Ān nà} is in her final year
and {大卫|Dà wèi} is about to leave his company.

This lesson is about getting a first job. Its grammar is about time: {自从|zì cóng}…{以来|yǐ lái} (since) and
{曾经|céng jīng} (once, at one time), set against {已经|yǐ jīng} (already).

## {自从|zì cóng}…{以来|yǐ lái}: since

{自从|zì cóng} + a past starting point says when a situation began; {以来|yǐ lái} closes the phrase. The rest of the
sentence says what has been true from then until now:

{自从|zì cóng}{去年|qù nián}{来|lái}{这儿|zhèr}{实习|shí xí}{以来|yǐ lái}，{她|tā}{写|xiě}{了|le}{三十|sān shí}{多|duō}{篇|piān}{文章|wén zhāng}。 — Since she came here as an intern last year, she has
written more than thirty articles.

{自从|zì cóng}{开始|kāi shǐ}{工作|gōng zuò}{以来|yǐ lái}，{我|wǒ}{每|měi}{天|tiān}{都|dōu}{很|hěn}{忙|máng}。 — I've been busy every day since I started work.

{自从|zì cóng}{毕业|bì yè}{以来|yǐ lái}，{他|tā}{一直|yì zhí}{在|zài}{新闻|xīn wén}{行业|háng yè}{工作|gōng zuò}。 — He has worked in the news business ever since he graduated.

The starting point can be a time word or a whole event ({来|lái}{这儿|zhèr}{实习|shí xí}, {开始|kāi shǐ}{工作|gōng zuò}, {毕业|bì yè}). The second half
usually has {一直|yì zhí}, {都|dōu}, {已经|yǐ jīng} or a verb with {了|le}: something that has lasted or added up.

Either half of the frame can go:

- {自从|zì cóng}… without {以来|yǐ lái}: {自从|zì cóng}{她|tā}{来|lái}{了|le}{以后|yǐ hòu}，{办公室|bàn gōng shì}{热闹|rè nao}{多|duō}{了|le}。 (Since she came, the office has been much
  livelier.) {自从|zì cóng}…{以后|yǐ hòu} is the most common spoken form.
- …{以来|yǐ lái} without {自从|zì cóng}, straight after a time word: {去年|qù nián}{以来|yǐ lái}, {三|sān}{月|yuè}{以来|yǐ lái}, {工作|gōng zuò}{以来|yǐ lái}, and after a length of
  time, {三|sān}{年|nián}{以来|yǐ lái} (over the past three years). This is the usual form in written reports: 2025{年|nián}{以来|yǐ lái}，{这个|zhè ge}{行业|háng yè}
  {的|de}{员工|yuán gōng}{越|yuè}{来|lái}{越|yuè}{多|duō}。 (Since 2025, this industry has had more and more employees.)

Two limits:

- {自从|zì cóng} looks back from now, so its starting point is always past. For a start in the future, say
  {从|cóng}…{起|qǐ} or {从|cóng}…{开始|kāi shǐ}: {从|cóng}{下|xià}{个|gè}{月|yuè}{开始|kāi shǐ}，{我|wǒ}{每|měi}{天|tiān}{八|bā}{点|diǎn}{上班|shàng bān}。 (From next month I start work at eight.) ×{自从|zì cóng}{明天|míng tiān}{以来|yǐ lái} is
  wrong.
- {以来|yǐ lái} is "since then, up to now". For "after" a single past event, use {以后|yǐ hòu}: {毕业|bì yè}{以后|yǐ hòu}，{他|tā}{去|qù}{了|le}{上海|Shàng hǎi}。 (After
  he graduated, he went to Shanghai.) {毕业|bì yè}{以来|yǐ lái} would mean the whole time since.

| Form | Register | Example |
|---|---|---|
| {自从|zì cóng} X {以后|yǐ hòu}… | speech and writing | {自从|zì cóng}{结婚|jié hūn}{以后|yǐ hòu}，{他|tā}{很|hěn}{少|shǎo}{加班|jiā bān}{了|le}。 |
| {自从|zì cóng} X {以来|yǐ lái}… | a little formal | {自从|zì cóng}{公司|gōng sī}{成立|chéng lì}{以来|yǐ lái}… (lesson 02's {成立|chéng lì}: to be founded) |
| X {以来|yǐ lái}… | written reports, news | {今年|jīn nián}{以来|yǐ lái}，{就业|jiù yè}{的|de}{人|rén}{越|yuè}{来|lái}{越|yuè}{多|duō}。 |
| {从|cóng} X {起|qǐ} / {开始|kāi shǐ}… | any; also future | {从|cóng}{明天|míng tiān}{起|qǐ}，{你|nǐ}{就是|jiù shì}{正式|zhèng shì}{员工|yuán gōng}{了|le}。 |

## {曾经|céng jīng} and {曾|céng}: once, at one time

{曾经|céng jīng} is a **[[time adverb]]**: it says that something happened, or was true, at some time in the past,
and usually that it no longer is. It goes before the verb, often with {过|guo}:

{他|tā}{曾经|céng jīng}{是|shì}{公务员|gōng wù yuán}，{后来|hòu lái}{辞职|cí zhí}{了|le}。 — He was once a civil servant; later he resigned. ({辞职|cí zhí} is lesson 05's word:
to resign.)

{我|wǒ}{曾经|céng jīng}{在|zài}{一|yì}{家|jiā}{公司|gōng sī}{实习|shí xí}{过|guo}{三|sān}{个|gè}{月|yuè}。 — I once did a three-month internship at a company.

{这|zhè}{条|tiáo}{街|jiē}{曾经|céng jīng}{很|hěn}{安静|ān jìng}，{现在|xiàn zài}{热闹|rè nao}{多|duō}{了|le}。 — This street was once quiet; now it's much livelier.

{曾|céng} alone is the written form, common in reports, biographies and CVs: {本人|běn rén}{曾|céng}{在|zài}{新闻|xīn wén}{网站|wǎng zhàn}{实习|shí xí}。 (I worked
as an intern at a news website: a line from a CV.)

### {曾经|céng jīng} vs {已经|yǐ jīng}

They look alike, and English sometimes translates both as "have done", but they look at time from
opposite ends:

- {已经|yǐ jīng} (already): the action is done *and its result is still here*. {他|tā}{已经|yǐ jīng}{找|zhǎo}{到|dào}{工作|gōng zuò}{了|le}。 (He has found a
  job: he has one now.)
- {曾经|céng jīng} (once): the action or state belongs to *the past and is over*. {他|tā}{曾经|céng jīng}{找|zhǎo}{到|dào}{过|guo}{一|yí}{份|fèn}{工作|gōng zuò}。 (He did once
  find a job: it's history.)

| | {已经|yǐ jīng} | {曾经|céng jīng} |
|---|---|---|
| Time | up to now, still true | at a past time, over |
| Usual partner | {了|le} | {过|guo} |
| Example | {她|tā}{已经|yǐ jīng}{签|qiān}{了|le}{合同|hé tong}。 She has signed the contract. | {她|tā}{曾经|céng jīng}{签|qiān}{过|guo}{一|yí}{份|fèn}{合同|hé tong}。 She once signed a contract. |

The negative of {曾经|céng jīng} is {没|méi}({有|yǒu})…{过|guo} in speech: {我|wǒ}{没|méi}{在|zài}{大|dà}{公司|gōng sī}{工作|gōng zuò}{过|guo}。 (I've never worked at a big company.)
Written Chinese also has {不曾|bù céng} and {未曾|wèi céng}, which you'll see in books but needn't use.

### {早已|zǎo yǐ}: long since (preview)

{早已|zǎo yǐ} is written style for "long ago, already for a long time": {这|zhè}{件|jiàn}{事|shì}{他|tā}{早已|zǎo yǐ}{忘|wàng}{了|le}。 (He forgot about that
long ago.) In speech, say {早|zǎo}{就|jiù}: {他|tā}{早|zǎo}{就|jiù}{忘|wàng}{了|le}。 It returns in lesson 27 with the written register.

## Words for work and careers

### Looking for work

| Word | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| {就业|jiù yè} | to get a job; employment | {大学生|dà xué shēng}{就业|jiù yè} (graduate employment) |
| {职场|zhí chǎng} | the workplace, working life | {刚|gāng}{进|jìn}{职场|zhí chǎng}{的|de}{年轻|nián qīng}{人|rén} (young people new to working life) |
| {简历|jiǎn lì} | CV, résumé | {写|xiě}{简历|jiǎn lì}, {一|yí}{份|fèn}{简历|jiǎn lì} |
| {学历|xué lì} | educational background | {学历|xué lì}{要求|yāo qiú}：{本科|běn kē}{以上|yǐ shàng} (education required: a first degree or above) |
| {证书|zhèng shū} | certificate | {毕业|bì yè}{证书|zhèng shū}, {汉语|Hàn yǔ}{水平|shuǐ píng}{证书|zhèng shū} |
| {资格|zī gé} | qualification, being entitled | {有|yǒu}{资格|zī gé}{参加|cān jiā}{考试|kǎo shì} (be entitled to sit the exam) |
| {具备|jù bèi} | to have, possess (qualities, conditions) | {具备|jù bèi}{一定|yí dìng}{的|de}{工作|gōng zuò}{经验|jīng yàn} (have some work experience) |
| {人才|rén cái} | talented person; talent | {公司|gōng sī}{急需|jí xū}{人才|rén cái}。 (The company badly needs talent: {急需|jí xū} is lesson 03's word.) |
| {人力|rén lì} | manpower, people | {人力|rén lì}{不够|bú gòu} (not enough people) |
| {打听|dǎ ting} | to ask around, inquire | {打听|dǎ ting}{一下|yí xià}{这|zhè}{家|jiā}{公司|gōng sī}{的|de}{待遇|dài yù} |
| {聘请|pìn qǐng} | to hire, engage (formal) | {公司|gōng sī}{聘请|pìn qǐng}{她|tā}{当|dāng}{顾问|gù wèn}。 ({顾问|gù wèn} gù wèn: adviser) |

{具备|jù bèi} takes abstract objects ({条件|tiáo jiàn}, {能力|néng lì}, {经验|jīng yàn}, {资格|zī gé}), never a thing you can hold: ×{具备|jù bèi}{一|yì}{台|tái}{电脑|diàn nǎo}. {打听|dǎ ting} is to
find out by asking around, not to ask one person a question: {我|wǒ}{向|xiàng}{同事|tóng shì}{打听|dǎ ting}{了|le}{一下|yí xià}{新|xīn}{经理|jīng lǐ}{的|de}{情况|qíng kuàng}。 (I asked my
colleagues about the new manager.) Its second syllable is light: dǎ ting.

### The job

| Word | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| {员工|yuán gōng} | employee, staff (of a company) | {公司|gōng sī}{有|yǒu}{三百|sān bǎi}{多|duō}{名|míng}{员工|yuán gōng}。 |
| {职工|zhí gōng} | staff, workers (of an organisation; also in official names) | {职工|zhí gōng}{食堂|shí táng} (staff canteen) |
| {公务员|gōng wù yuán} | civil servant | {考|kǎo}{公务员|gōng wù yuán} (sit the civil-service exam) |
| {从事|cóng shì} | to work in, be engaged in (formal) | {从事|cóng shì}{新闻|xīn wén}{工作|gōng zuò} |
| {行|háng} | trade, line of work | {做|zuò}{哪|nǎ}{一|yì}{行|háng}？ (What line are you in?) |
| {行业|háng yè} | industry, line of business | {新闻|xīn wén}{行业|háng yè}, {服务|fú wù}{行业|háng yè} |
| {本人|běn rén} | oneself; I (formal); in person | {本人|běn rén}{签字|qiān zì} (signed in person) |
| {个人|gè rén} | individual; personal | {个人|gè rén}{简历|jiǎn lì} (personal CV), {这|zhè}{是|shì}{我|wǒ}{个人|gè rén}{的|de}{看法|kàn fǎ}。 |
| {临时|lín shí} | temporary; at the last moment | {临时|lín shí}{工作|gōng zuò} (a temporary job), {临时|lín shí}{决定|jué dìng} |
| {固定|gù dìng} | fixed, regular | {固定|gù dìng}{工作|gōng zuò}, {工作|gōng zuò}{时间|shí jiān}{不|bú}{固定|gù dìng} |
| {实习|shí xí} | to do an internship; internship | {在|zài}{网站|wǎng zhàn}{实习|shí xí} |
| {培训|péi xùn} | to train; training | {新|xīn}{员工|yuán gōng}{培训|péi xùn} |
| {报到|bào dào} | to report for duty, register on arrival | {九|jiǔ}{点|diǎn}{到|dào}{人事部|rén shì bù}{报到|bào dào} ({人事部|rén shì bù} rén shì bù: personnel department) |
| {挣|zhèng} | to earn | {挣|zhèng}{钱|qián}, {挣|zhèng}{得|de}{不|bù}{多|duō} |
| {待遇|dài yù} | pay and conditions | {待遇|dài yù}{很|hěn}{好|hǎo} |
| {出色|chū sè} | outstanding, excellent | {工作|gōng zuò}{很|hěn}{出色|chū sè} |

- {员工|yuán gōng} and {职工|zhí gōng} overlap: {员工|yuán gōng} is the everyday word for a company's staff; {职工|zhí gōng} is "staff and workers",
  older and more official, as in names ({职工|zhí gōng}{医院|yī yuàn}). Neither is {工人|gōng rén} (HSK 4), a factory or building worker.
- 行 has two readings. {行|háng} is a trade or a row: {行业|háng yè}, {各行各业|gè háng gè yè}, {一|yì}{行|háng}{字|zì} (a line of characters). {行|xíng}
  (HSK 3) is "to go; OK": {行人|xíng rén} (passer-by), {不行|bù xíng}. {银行|yín háng} (bank) has háng too.
- {挣|zhèng} is "earn by working": {挣|zhèng}{钱|qián}, {挣|zhèng}{工资|gōng zī}. {赚|zhuàn} (HSK 4) is "make money, profit", also from business: {这|zhè}{次|cì}
  {买卖|mǎi mai}{赚|zhuàn}{了|le}{不|bù}{少|shǎo}。 {挣|zhèng} is zhèng, fourth tone, the same syllable as {正|zhèng}.
- {临时|lín shí} as an adverb means "at the last moment": {会议|huì yì}{临时|lín shí}{取消|qǔ xiāo}{了|le}。 (The meeting was cancelled at the last
  moment.) As an adjective, before a noun, it's "temporary": {临时|lín shí}{工|gōng} (a temp).
- {待遇|dài yù} is more than salary: pay, holidays, insurance, housing, the whole package.

### The contract

{合同|hé tong} (hé tong, second syllable light) is a contract. {签|qiān} is "to sign"; {签订|qiān dìng} is "to sign, conclude" with
an agreement or contract as its object; {签字|qiān zì} is "to put one's signature" (a verb with its object
built in, so no other object follows):

- {签|qiān}{合同|hé tong} / {签订|qiān dìng}{合同|hé tong} — to sign a contract ({签订|qiān dìng} is more formal).
- {在|zài}{这儿|zhèr}{签字|qiān zì} / {请|qǐng}{您|nín}{签|qiān}{个|gè}{字|zì} — sign here / please sign ({签字|qiān zì} takes no object: ×{签字|qiān zì}{合同|hé tong}).
- {签名|qiān míng} (lesson 15) is to sign your name, as on a card or a book.

## {各行各业|gè háng gè yè}: the first idiom

Chinese has thousands of fixed four-character expressions, {成语|chéng yǔ} (idioms; the word itself is
HSK 6's). Some tell a whole story in four characters; others, like {各行各业|gè háng gè yè}, are a simple pattern.

- **Parts.** {各|gè} (each, every: HSK 4) + {行|háng} (trade) + {各|gè} + {业|yè} (line of work, as in {行业|háng yè}, {就业|jiù yè}). Literally
  "each trade, each line": every trade and profession.
- **The pattern {各|gè} A {各|gè} B** repeats {各|gè} before two words of similar meaning. You'll meet more: {各种|gè zhǒng}{各|gè}{样|yàng} (all
  kinds of).
- **In a sentence** it works like a noun: as a subject or object, or before {的|de} as an attributive.
  - {各行各业|gè háng gè yè}{都|dōu}{需要|xū yào}{人才|rén cái}。 — Every trade needs talented people. (subject, with {都|dōu})
  - {他|tā}{认识|rèn shi}{各行各业|gè háng gè yè}{的|de}{人|rén}。 — He knows people in every line of work. (attributive, with {的|de})
  - {来自|lái zì}{各行各业|gè háng gè yè} — from all walks of life (object of {来自|lái zì}, "come from": written)
- **Register.** Neutral: you hear it in speech and read it in news. It almost always comes with {都|dōu} or
  {的|de}, as above.

## Dialogue: the first day

{王芳|Wáng Fāng} (Wang Fang) reports for her first day as a full-time reporter. Her editor {郑华|Zhèng Huá} (Zheng Hua), an
{编辑|biān jí} (editor), and her colleague {孟洁|Mèng Jié} (Meng Jie) are in the newsroom. Staff call
{郑华|Zhèng Huá} {郑|Zhèng}{老师|lǎo shī}, as Chinese newsrooms often call senior colleagues {老师|lǎo shī}.

```dialogue
# {报到|bào dào}
王芳: {郑|Zhèng}{老师|lǎo shī}，{早|zǎo}！{我|wǒ}{今天|jīn tiān}{来|lái}{报到|bào dào}。
= Morning, Ms Zheng! I'm here to report for my first day.
郑华: {欢迎|huān yíng}{欢迎|huān yíng}！{自从|zì cóng}{你|nǐ}{去年|qù nián}{来|lái}{实习|shí xí}{以来|yǐ lái}，{大家|dà jiā}{都|dōu}{觉得|jué de}{你|nǐ}{工作|gōng zuò}{很|hěn}{出色|chū sè}。{现在|xiàn zài}{你|nǐ}{是|shì}{正式|zhèng shì}{员工|yuán gōng}{了|le}。
= Welcome! Since you came here as an intern last year, everyone has thought your work outstanding. Now you're a member of staff.
王芳: {谢谢|xiè xie}{您|nín}。{合同|hé tong}{我|wǒ}{已经|yǐ jīng}{看|kàn}{过|guo}{了|le}，{在|zài}{哪儿|nǎr}{签字|qiān zì}？
= Thank you. I've read the contract already. Where do I sign?
郑华: {这儿|zhèr}，{最后|zuì hòu}{一|yí}{页|yè}，{本人|běn rén}{签字|qiān zì}。{签|qiān}{好|hǎo}{了|le}{交|jiāo}{给|gěi}{人事部|rén shì bù}{就|jiù}{行|xíng}。
= Here, on the last page: you sign it yourself. When you've signed, just give it to Personnel.
孟洁: {王芳|Wáng Fāng}，{你|nǐ}{的|de}{座位|zuò wèi}{在|zài}{我|wǒ}{旁边|páng biān}。{这|zhè}{张|zhāng}{桌子|zhuō zi}{以前|yǐ qián}{是|shì}{临时|lín shí}{用|yòng}{的|de}，{现在|xiàn zài}{归|guī}{你|nǐ}{了|le}。
= Wang Fang, your desk is next to mine. It used to be a spare desk; now it's yours.
王芳: {太|tài}{好|hǎo}{了|le}！{孟洁|Mèng Jié}，{新|xīn}{员工|yuán gōng}{要|yào}{参加|cān jiā}{培训|péi xùn}{吗|ma}？
= Great! Meng Jie, do new staff have to do training?
```

## A written text: the contract's first clauses

Contracts are written in a stiff, exact style. {王芳|Wáng Fāng}'s begins like this. {甲方|jiǎ fāng} and {乙方|yǐ fāng} ({甲方|jiǎ fāng},
{乙方|yǐ fāng}: Party A and Party B; {甲|jiǎ} and {乙|yǐ} are lesson 27's characters) are the two sides.

Notes on the written style:

- {以下|yǐ xià}{简称|jiǎn chēng} (yǐ xià jiǎn chēng): "hereafter called" ({简称|jiǎn chēng}: short name). {本|běn}{公司|gōng sī} and {本|běn}{合同|hé tong}: {本|běn} is "this" in
  written Chinese (lesson 02 has more).
- {聘请|pìn qǐng} X {为|wéi} Y: "engage X as Y". {为|wéi} here is "as, to be" (HSK 4).
- {与|yǔ} = {和|hé} (HSK 4), {须|xū} = {必须|bì xū} (must), {于|yú} = {在|zài} (at, on): three written words in one clause.
  {须|xū} and {于|yú} are later words; read them as their spoken partners.
- {等|děng} (HSK 4): "and so on", closing a list: {简历|jiǎn lì}、{学历|xué lì}{证书|zhèng shū}{等|děng}{材料|cái liào}.
- {真实|zhēn shí} (zhēn shí): true, genuine (lesson 24).
- …{的|de}, at the end of a condition ("{工作|gōng zuò}{时间|shí jiān}{不|bú}{固定|gù dìng}{的|de}"), is a written "in the case where": where the
  hours aren't fixed…

- 曾 céng is also read zēng, as a surname and in 曾祖父 (zēng zǔ fù, great-grandfather). It's the
  sound part of 层 céng's traditional form 層, of {增|zēng} zēng ({增加|zēng jiā}, HSK 4) and of {赠|zèng} zèng (lesson 15:
  {赠送|zèng sòng}, to present). Learn them as a family: 曾 → 增 赠 層.
- 固 is 古 gǔ (old: lesson 25's word) inside the enclosure 囗; 古 gives the sound (gǔ → gù).
  The same part sounds in 故 gù ({故事|gù shi}, {故意|gù yì}) and 姑 gū. A memory aid: something old and walled in is
  hard to move.
- 临 has nothing in common with its traditional form 臨 except the general outline: the
  simplified shape is far simpler. Make Me a Hanzi files it under 丨, its first stroke.
- 培 is 土 (earth) + 咅 pǒu: the same right side as 部 bù ({部门|bù mén}, HSK 4), 陪 péi ({陪|péi}, HSK 4) and 赔
  péi (lesson 23: to compensate). 培 and 陪 sound alike and differ in the left side: 土 earth or
  the hill 阝. A memory aid: earth heaped round a young plant to make it grow ({培|péi}, to foster).
- 训 is 讠 (speech) + 川 chuān (river). The sound has drifted, but the pair {训|xùn} / {川|chuān} is easy to
  see. Traditional 訓 has the full 言.
- 挣 is 扌 (hand) + 争 zhēng, the right side of 净 jìng and 静 jìng (HSK 3). Here the sound
  still matches closely: zhēng → zhèng.

### Stroke order

- **曾**: the two short strokes on top (a dot, then a left-falling stroke), then the box: its left
  vertical, the top-and-right turn, the short strokes inside, and the bottom horizontal that closes
  it; 日 at the bottom last.
- **临**: the short vertical on the left, then the long one; then the right side: a left-falling
  stroke, a horizontal and a dot at the top, and the box below: its left vertical, the top-and-right
  turn, the vertical that divides it, and the bottom horizontal last.
- **固**: the left side and top of 囗 first, then 古 inside, and the bottom stroke closes the box
  last (outside, inside, close the door).
- **训**: 讠 (a dot, then the horizontal that turns down and flicks up), then 川 from left to right:
  a left-falling stroke and two verticals.

<summary>Model answer</summary>

{小|xiǎo}{王|Wáng}{大学|dà xué}{毕业|bì yè}{以后|yǐ hòu}，{一直|yì zhí}{在|zài}{找|zhǎo}{工作|gōng zuò}。{一|yì}{天|tiān}{晚上|wǎn shang}，{他|tā}{认真|rèn zhēn}{地|de}{写|xiě}{好|hǎo}{了|le}{自己|zì jǐ}{的|de}{简历|jiǎn lì}，{发|fā}{给|gěi}{了|le}{一|yì}{家|jiā}{他|tā}{很|hěn}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{的|de}{公司|gōng sī}。{几|jǐ}{天|tiān}{以后|yǐ hòu}，{公司|gōng sī}{让|ràng}{他|tā}{去|qù}
{面试|miàn shì}。{那|nà}{天|tiān}{他|tā}{很|hěn}{紧张|jǐn zhāng}，{带|dài}{上|shàng}{了|le}{毕业|bì yè}{证书|zhèng shū}{和|hé}{各种|gè zhǒng}{证书|zhèng shū}，{早早|zǎo zǎo}{就|jiù}{到|dào}{了|le}{公司|gōng sī}。{面试|miàn shì}{的|de}{时候|shí hou}，{他|tā}{回答|huí dá}{得|de}{很|hěn}{出色|chū sè}，{经理|jīng lǐ}{很|hěn}{满意|mǎn yì}，{当场|dāng chǎng}{就|jiù}{跟|gēn}{他|tā}
{签订|qiān dìng}{了|le}{合同|hé tong}。{第|dì}{二|èr}{天|tiān}{早上|zǎo shang}{九|jiǔ}{点|diǎn}，{小|xiǎo}{王|Wáng}{来|lái}{公司|gōng sī}{报到|bào dào}。{同事|tóng shì}{们|men}{都|dōu}{很|hěn}{热情|rè qíng}，{他|tā}{觉得|jué de}{自己|zì jǐ}{的|de}{职场|zhí chǎng}{生活|shēng huó}{开始|kāi shǐ}{了|le}。

(about 150 characters) {当场|dāng chǎng} (dāng chǎng): on the spot. "After graduating, Xiao Wang kept looking for a
job. One evening he carefully wrote his CV and sent it to a company he liked. A few days later the
company asked him to an interview. He was nervous that day; he took his degree certificate and his
other certificates and got there early. In the interview he answered very well, the manager was
pleased, and signed a contract with him on the spot. At nine the next morning Xiao Wang reported
for work. His colleagues were friendly, and he felt his working life had begun."

A checklist: pictures in order; {以后|yǐ hòu}, {那|nà}{天|tiān}, {第|dì}{二|èr}{天|tiān} to move the story on; a last sentence that closes it.
</details>

## Say it

```speak
# Starting a job
{我|wǒ}{今天|jīn tiān}{来|lái}{报到|bào dào}。
= I'm here to report for my first day.
{请问|qǐng wèn}{在|zài}{哪儿|nǎr}{签字|qiān zì}？
= Excuse me, where do I sign?
{自从|zì cóng}{毕业|bì yè}{以来|yǐ lái}，{我|wǒ}{一直|yì zhí}{在|zài}{这个|zhè ge}{行业|háng yè}{工作|gōng zuò}。
= I've worked in this industry ever since I graduated.
{我|wǒ}{曾经|céng jīng}{在|zài}{一|yì}{家|jiā}{网站|wǎng zhàn}{实习|shí xí}{过|guo}。
= I once did an internship at a website.
{各行各业|gè háng gè yè}{都|dōu}{需要|xū yào}{人才|rén cái}。
= Every trade needs talented people.
{您|nín}{能|néng}{帮|bāng}{我|wǒ}{打听|dǎ ting}{一下|yí xià}{吗|ma}？
= Could you ask around for me?
```

## Pronunciation

- 曾 céng and 层 céng (floor, HSK 3) are the same syllable; *c* is *ts* with a puff of air.
- 挣 zhèng and 正 zhèng (HSK 2) sound the same. Don't confuse it with 争 zhēng (to compete, lesson 14),
  first tone.
- {合同|hé tong} hé tong and {打听|dǎ ting} dǎ ting have a light second syllable.
- {各行各业|gè háng gè yè} gè háng gè yè: four syllables, each {各|gè} a falling tone; {行|háng} rises.
- 签 qiān and 欠 qiàn (lesson 05: to owe) differ only in tone.
- {职工|zhí gōng} zhí gōng and {职场|zhí chǎng} zhí chǎng: zh with the tongue curled back, then a rising tone.

## Common mistakes

- ~~{自从|zì cóng}{明天|míng tiān}{以来|yǐ lái}，{我|wǒ}{每|měi}{天|tiān}{八|bā}{点|diǎn}{上班|shàng bān}~~: {自从|zì cóng} looks back from a past point. For the future, {从|cóng}{明天|míng tiān}{起|qǐ} / {从|cóng}{明天|míng tiān}{开始|kāi shǐ}，
  {我|wǒ}{每|měi}{天|tiān}{八|bā}{点|diǎn}{上班|shàng bān}。
- ~~{我|wǒ}{曾经|céng jīng}{已经|yǐ jīng}{去|qù}{过|guo}~~: {曾经|céng jīng} (once, over) and {已经|yǐ jīng} (already, still true) don't combine. {我|wǒ}{曾经|céng jīng}{去|qù}{过|guo} or {我|wǒ}{已经|yǐ jīng}{去|qù}{了|le}.
- {曾经|céng jīng} usually implies it's no longer so: {他|tā}{曾经|céng jīng}{是|shì}{公务员|gōng wù yuán} suggests he isn't one now. For "he's always been
  one", say {他|tā}{一直|yì zhí}{是|shì}{公务员|gōng wù yuán}.
- ~~{签字|qiān zì}{合同|hé tong}~~: {签字|qiān zì} has its object built in. Say {签|qiān}{合同|hé tong} or {在|zài}{合同|hé tong}{上|shàng}{签字|qiān zì} (sign on the contract).
- ~~{具备|jù bèi}{一|yì}{台|tái}{电脑|diàn nǎo}~~: {具备|jù bèi} takes qualities and conditions ({具备|jù bèi}{条件|tiáo jiàn}, {具备|jù bèi}{资格|zī gé}). For things, {有|yǒu}.
- {毕业|bì yè}{以来|yǐ lái} for one event after graduating: "After he graduated he went to Shanghai" is {毕业|bì yè}{以后|yǐ hòu}，{他|tā}{去|qù}{了|le}{上海|Shàng hǎi}.

## Key points

- {自从|zì cóng} + past point + {以来|yǐ lái} / {以后|yǐ hòu}: since; X {以来|yǐ lái} alone in written reports ({今年|jīn nián}{以来|yǐ lái}); never for the future
  ({从|cóng}…{起|qǐ} / {开始|kāi shǐ}).
- {曾经|céng jīng} (written {曾|céng}) + verb (+ {过|guo}): once, at one time, no longer so. {已经|yǐ jīng} + verb + {了|le}: already, still so.
  {早已|zǎo yǐ} is written for {早|zǎo}{就|jiù}.
- {各行各业|gè háng gè yè}: every trade; {各|gè} A {各|gè} B; as a subject (+ {都|dōu}) or attributive (+ {的|de}).
- {签|qiān}{合同|hé tong} / {签订|qiān dìng}{合同|hé tong}, {签字|qiān zì} (no object), {行|háng} vs {行|xíng}, {挣|zhèng} (earn by work) vs {赚|zhuàn} (make money).
- New characters: 曾 固 临 培 训 挣.

The words from this lesson are listed below; they join your vocabulary reviews when you complete
the lesson.

lessons.title: Inside a company
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

Lesson 01 got {王芳|Wáng Fāng} into her job. This lesson looks at how an organisation is put together: who
leads it, who answers to whom, what its departments do, and how meetings are called and run. The
grammar is the language of descriptions and notices:

- {由|yóu}…{组成|zǔ chéng}: to be made up of;
- {以及|yǐ jí}: "and, as well as" in writing;
- {事先|shì xiān}: in advance;
- the written pronoun {本|běn} ({本|běn}{公司|gōng sī}, {本人|běn rén}, {本|běn}{周|zhōu}): "this, our".

At the end you can read a company's introduction, take and pass on a message at work, and talk about
the keyboard and screen in front of you.

## {由|yóu}…{组成|zǔ chéng}: be made up of

To say what a whole consists of, put the whole first, then {由|yóu} + the parts + {组成|zǔ chéng} (zǔ chéng, "to make up,
form": next lesson's word):

{我们|wǒ men}{部门|bù mén}{由|yóu}{五|wǔ}{个|gè}{人|rén}{组成|zǔ chéng}。 — Our department is made up of five people.

{这个|zhè ge}{项目|xiàng mù}{组|zǔ}{由|yóu}{客户|kè hù}{和|hé}{我们|wǒ men}{公司|gōng sī}{的|de}{员工|yuán gōng}{组成|zǔ chéng}。 — The project group is made up of the client's people and our
own staff.

{公司|gōng sī}{的|de}{领导|lǐng dǎo}{机构|jī gòu}{由|yóu}{董事会|dǒng shì huì}{和|hé}{总|zǒng}{经理|jīng lǐ}{组成|zǔ chéng}。 — The company's leadership is made up of the board and the general
manager. ({董事会|dǒng shì huì} dǒng shì huì: board of directors; {总|zǒng}{经理|jīng lǐ}: general manager)

{由|yóu} is the {由|yóu} of HSK 4 ({这|zhè}{件|jiàn}{事|shì}{由|yóu}{他|tā}{负责|fù zé}: he is responsible for this): it introduces the agent or the
source. In {由|yóu}…{组成|zǔ chéng} it introduces the members. Three things to know:

- The whole is the subject; the parts come after {由|yóu}. ×{五|wǔ}{个|gè}{人|rén}{由|yóu}{我们|wǒ men}{部门|bù mén}{组成|zǔ chéng} turns it upside down.
- {组成|zǔ chéng} can also be an ordinary verb with the whole as its object: {我们|wǒ men}{五|wǔ}{个|gè}{人|rén}{组成|zǔ chéng}{了|le}{一|yí}{个|gè}{小组|xiǎo zǔ}。 (The five of
  us formed a group.)
- In written texts you'll also meet {由|yóu}…{构成|gòu chéng} (lesson 26's {构成|gòu chéng}: to constitute) for things that aren't
  people: {这|zhè}{座|zuò}{大厦|dà shà}{由|yóu}{三|sān}{部分|bù fen}{构成|gòu chéng}。 (The building consists of three parts.)

## {以及|yǐ jí}: and, as well as (written)

{以及|yǐ jí} joins words, phrases or clauses, usually as the last link in a list. It's written style and formal
speech; in conversation say {和|hé} or {还|hái}{有|yǒu}.

{会议|huì yì}{的|de}{内容|nèi róng}{包括|bāo kuò}{今年|jīn nián}{的|de}{业务|yè wù}、{明年|míng nián}{的|de}{计划|jì huà}{以及|yǐ jí}{新|xīn}{项目|xiàng mù}{的|de}{方案|fāng àn}。 — The meeting will cover this year's business,
next year's plan and the proposal for the new project.

{请|qǐng}{把|bǎ}{你|nǐ}{的|de}{姓名|xìng míng}、{电话|diàn huà}{以及|yǐ jí}{住址|zhù zhǐ}{写|xiě}{在|zài}{这|zhè}{张|zhāng}{表|biǎo}{上|shàng}。 — Please write your name, phone number and address on this form.
({住址|zhù zhǐ} zhù zhǐ: address, lesson 15)

How it differs from {和|hé}:

- {和|hé} joins words and short phrases ({我|wǒ}{和|hé}{你|nǐ}, {老板|lǎo bǎn}{和|hé}{秘书|mì shū}), but not two clauses. {以及|yǐ jí} can join phrases and
  clauses: {我们|wǒ men}{要|yào}{了解|liǎo jiě}{客户|kè hù}{需要|xū yào}{什么|shén me}，{以及|yǐ jí}{他们|tā men}{为什么|wèi shén me}{需要|xū yào}。 (We need to understand what clients need and why.)
- {以及|yǐ jí} often comes after a pause (a comma or 、), before the last item, and it can mark that item as
  a different or less central kind: {经理|jīng lǐ}、{主任|zhǔ rèn}{以及|yǐ jí}{其他|qí tā}{员工|yuán gōng} (the managers, the department heads and the other
  staff).
- {和|hé} is neutral; {以及|yǐ jí} sounds like a notice or a report. {以及|yǐ jí} also appears as a word in lesson 27, with
  the rest of the written register.

## {事先|shì xiān}: in advance

{事先|shì xiān} is "beforehand, in advance" (before the event in question). It goes before the verb:

{开会|kāi huì}{以前|yǐ qián}，{请|qǐng}{事先|shì xiān}{把|bǎ}{报告|bào gào}{看|kàn}{一|yí}{遍|biàn}。 — Before the meeting, please read the report through in advance.

{他|tā}{事先|shì xiān}{没|méi}{告诉|gào su}{我|wǒ}，{我|wǒ}{不|bù}{知道|zhī dào}{他|tā}{今天|jīn tiān}{不|bù}{来|lái}。 — He didn't tell me in advance; I didn't know he wasn't coming today.

Compare {提前|tí qián} (HSK 4), "earlier than planned, ahead of time": {会议|huì yì}{提前|tí qián}{了|le}{半|bàn}{个|gè}{小时|xiǎo shí}。 (The meeting was brought
forward by half an hour.) {提前|tí qián} moves a time; {事先|shì xiān} means "before it happens".

| | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| {事先|shì xiān} | before the event | {事先|shì xiān}{通知|tōng zhī}{大家|dà jiā} (tell everyone beforehand) |
| {提前|tí qián} | earlier than planned | {提前|tí qián}{一|yì}{天|tiān}{出发|chū fā} (set off a day early) |

## {本|běn}: this, our (written)

{本|běn}, the measure word for books ({一|yì}{本|běn}{书|shū}), is also a written pronoun before a noun: "this (one), our
own". It appears in notices, contracts and announcements:

| {本|běn} + noun | Meaning | Spoken |
|---|---|---|
| {本|běn}{公司|gōng sī} | this company, our company | {我们|wǒ men}{公司|gōng sī} |
| {本人|běn rén} (lesson 01) | I, myself; in person | {我|wǒ} / {自己|zì jǐ} |
| {本|běn}{周|zhōu} | this week | {这个|zhè ge}{星期|xīng qī} |
| {本|běn}{次|cì}{会议|huì yì} | this meeting | {这|zhè}{次|cì}{会|huì} |

{本|běn}{公司|gōng sī}{由|yóu}{三|sān}{个|gè}{部门|bù mén}{组成|zǔ chéng}。 — Our company is made up of three departments.

{本|běn}{周|zhōu}{五|wǔ}{下午|xià wǔ}{召开|zhào kāi}{全体|quán tǐ}{员工|yuán gōng}{大会|dà huì}。 — There will be a meeting of all staff this Friday afternoon. ({全体|quán tǐ}, {大会|dà huì}:
lesson 03)

Lesson 13 brings {本|běn} as an adverb ({本来|běn lái}, "originally").

## Words for an organisation

### Kinds of organisation

| Word | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| {企业|qǐ yè} | enterprise, company (as a business) | {大|dà}{企业|qǐ yè}, {小|xiǎo}{企业|qǐ yè} |
| {机构|jī gòu} | organisation, institution, body | {政府|zhèng fǔ}{机构|jī gòu} (a government body), {培训|péi xùn}{机构|jī gòu} |
| {总部|zǒng bù} | headquarters | {公司|gōng sī}{总部|zǒng bù}{在|zài}{上海|Shàng hǎi}。 |
| {内部|nèi bù} / {外部|wài bù} | internal / external | {内部|nèi bù}{会议|huì yì}, {外部|wài bù}{客户|kè hù} |
| {大厦|dà shà} | (tall) building, tower | {国际|guó jì}{大厦|dà shà} (often in names) |
| {成立|chéng lì} | to found, set up; be founded | {公司|gōng sī}{成立|chéng lì}{于|yú}2010{年|nián}。 ({成立|chéng lì}{于|yú}: written, "was founded in") |
| {设立|shè lì} | to set up, establish (an office, a post, a fund) | {在|zài}{北京|Běi jīng}{设立|shè lì}{办公室|bàn gōng shì} |
| {包括|bāo kuò} | to include | {包括|bāo kuò}{我|wǒ}{在内|zài nèi}，{一共|yí gòng}{八|bā}{个|gè}{人|rén}。 (Eight in all, me included.) |

{企业|qǐ yè} is a business seen from outside (the economy's word); {公司|gōng sī} is the everyday word and the legal
name. {成立|chéng lì} is used of a whole organisation coming into being; {设立|shè lì} of setting up a part of it: {公司|gōng sī}{成立|chéng lì}
{了|le}, {公司|gōng sī}{在|zài}{上海|Shàng hǎi}{设立|shè lì}{了|le}{一|yí}{个|gè}{办公室|bàn gōng shì}.

### People and posts

| Word | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| {领导|lǐng dǎo} | leader, the people in charge; to lead | {我们|wǒ men}{的|de}{领导|lǐng dǎo}, {领导|lǐng dǎo}{一|yí}{个|gè}{团队|tuán duì} ({团队|tuán duì}: a team, lesson 03) |
| {老板|lǎo bǎn} | boss, owner (spoken) | {我们|wǒ men}{老板|lǎo bǎn}{人|rén}{很|hěn}{好|hǎo}。 |
| {主任|zhǔ rèn} | director, head (of an office or department) | {办公室|bàn gōng shì}{主任|zhǔ rèn} |
| {主席|zhǔ xí} | chair, chairperson (of a meeting, a committee) | {会议|huì yì}{主席|zhǔ xí}, {学生会|xué shēng huì}{主席|zhǔ xí} |
| {秘书|mì shū} | secretary | {经理|jīng lǐ}{的|de}{秘书|mì shū} |
| {客户|kè hù} | client, customer (of a business) | {接待|jiē dài}{客户|kè hù} |
| {担任|dān rèn} | to hold (a post), serve as | {她|tā}{担任|dān rèn}{主任|zhǔ rèn}{已经|yǐ jīng}{五|wǔ}{年|nián}{了|le}。 |
| {能干|néng gàn} | capable, able (of a person) | {她|tā}{很|hěn}{能干|néng gàn}。 |

- {老板|lǎo bǎn} is the owner, or "the boss" in speech. In an organisation people say {领导|lǐng dǎo} for their superiors,
  or use the title: {王|Wáng}{主任|zhǔ rèn}, {吴经理|Wú jīng lǐ}.
- {客户|kè hù} is a business's client; {顾客|gù kè} (HSK 4) is a shop's customer.
- {能干|néng gàn} praises someone who gets things done: {他|tā}{又|yòu}{聪明|cōng ming}{又|yòu}{能干|néng gàn}。

### Work, meetings and messages

| Word | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| {业务|yè wù} | business, line of work; professional skill | {公司|gōng sī}{的|de}{主要|zhǔ yào}{业务|yè wù}, {业务|yè wù}{能力|néng lì} |
| {项目|xiàng mù} | project; item, event | {新|xīn}{项目|xiàng mù}, {比赛|bǐ sài}{项目|xiàng mù} |
| {方案|fāng àn} | plan, proposal, scheme | {提出|tí chū}{一|yí}{个|gè}{方案|fāng àn} |
| {原则|yuán zé} | principle | {原则|yuán zé}{上|shàng}{同意|tóng yì} (agree in principle) |
| {手段|shǒu duàn} | means, method | {管理|guǎn lǐ}{手段|shǒu duàn} |
| {报告|bào gào} | report; to report | {写|xiě}{报告|bào gào}, {向|xiàng}{领导|lǐng dǎo}{报告|bào gào} |
| {召开|zhào kāi} | to convene, hold (a meeting) | {召开|zhào kāi}{会议|huì yì} |
| {出席|chū xí} | to attend (formally) | {出席|chū xí}{会议|huì yì} |
| {发言|fā yán} | to speak (at a meeting); a statement | {在|zài}{会|huì}{上|shàng}{发言|fā yán} |
| {讲话|jiǎng huà} | to speak, give a talk; a speech | {经理|jīng lǐ}{讲话|jiǎng huà} |
| {接待|jiē dài} | to receive (visitors, clients) | {接待|jiē dài}{客户|kè hù} |
| {转告|zhuǎn gào} | to pass on (a message) | {请|qǐng}{你|nǐ}{转告|zhuǎn gào}{他|tā}。 |
| {派|pài} | to send, dispatch (someone) | {公司|gōng sī}{派|pài}{我|wǒ}{去|qù}{上海|Shàng hǎi}。 |
| {调|diào} diào | to transfer (to a post or place) | {他|tā}{调|diào}{到|dào}{总部|zǒng bù}{去|qù}{了|le}。 |
| {批|pī} / {批准|pī zhǔn} | to approve | {经理|jīng lǐ}{批|pī}{了|le}{我|wǒ}{的|de}{假|jià}。 / {批准|pī zhǔn}{这个|zhè ge}{方案|fāng àn} |
| {领|lǐng} | to receive, collect; to lead | {领|lǐng}{工资|gōng zī}, {领|lǐng}{快递|kuài dì} |
| {事先|shì xiān} | in advance | {事先|shì xiān}{准备|zhǔn bèi}{好|hǎo} |

### Stroke order

- **立**: a dot, a horizontal, then the dot and the left-falling stroke in the middle, and the long
  bottom horizontal last.
- **席**: 广 (dot, horizontal, left-falling), then a horizontal, two short verticals and the
  horizontal below them, then 巾 last (vertical, the turn with a hook, and the long vertical through
  the middle).
- **鼠**: thirteen strokes. The top, like 臼: a left-falling stroke, a vertical, a horizontal, the
  top-and-right turn and two short horizontals; then the lower part from left to right: a vertical that flicks up, two dots, a
  second vertical with its flick, two more dots, and the long curved hook last.
- **派**: 氵, then the right side: a short left-falling stroke, a long left-falling stroke, a
  short left-falling stroke inside, the vertical that flicks up, and the last two strokes falling
  left and right.
- **召**: 刀 first (the turn with a hook, then the left-falling stroke), then 口.

## Write it: a picture story

1. Morning: a secretary at a computer types a notice: "Staff meeting, Friday 3 p.m."
2. Friday: a long table, a manager speaking, a screen behind him showing a new plan.
3. A young employee stands and speaks; the others listen.
4. The manager smiles and nods; the plan on the screen has a tick next to it.

Write 100–150 characters. Use at least three of: {召开|zhào kāi}, {屏幕|píng mù}, {方案|fāng àn}, {发言|fā yán}, {批准|pī zhǔn}, {事先|shì xiān}.

<details>
<summary>Model answer</summary>

{星期|xīng qī}{一|yī}{早上|zǎo shang}，{秘书|mì shū}{小|xiǎo}{李|Lǐ}{在|zài}{电脑|diàn nǎo}{上|shàng}{写|xiě}{了|le}{一|yí}{个|gè}{通知|tōng zhī}：{本|běn}{周|zhōu}{五|wǔ}{下午|xià wǔ}{三|sān}{点|diǎn}{召开|zhào kāi}{全体|quán tǐ}{员工|yuán gōng}{大会|dà huì}，{请|qǐng}{大家|dà jiā}{事先|shì xiān}{准备|zhǔn bèi}{好|hǎo}{意见|yì jiàn}。{星期|xīng qī}{五|wǔ}{下午|xià wǔ}，
{大家|dà jiā}{都|dōu}{来|lái}{到|dào}{会议|huì yì}{室|shì}。{经理|jīng lǐ}{先|xiān}{讲话|jiǎng huà}，{屏幕|píng mù}{上|shàng}{是|shì}{公司|gōng sī}{明年|míng nián}{的|de}{新|xīn}{方案|fāng àn}。{经理|jīng lǐ}{说|shuō}{完|wán}{以后|yǐ hòu}，{年轻|nián qīng}{的|de}{员工|yuán gōng}{小|xiǎo}{张|Zhāng}{站|zhàn}{起来|qǐ lái}{发言|fā yán}。{他|tā}{说|shuō}，{这个|zhè ge}{方案|fāng àn}
{很|hěn}{好|hǎo}，{可是|kě shì}{应该|yīng gāi}{多|duō}{听听|tīng ting}{客户|kè hù}{的|de}{意见|yì jiàn}。{大家|dà jiā}{都|dōu}{觉得|jué de}{他|tā}{说|shuō}{得|de}{有|yǒu}{道理|dào li}。{最后|zuì hòu}，{经理|jīng lǐ}{笑|xiào}{着|zhe}{说|shuō}：“{好|hǎo}，{方案|fāng àn}{批准|pī zhǔn}{了|le}，{就|jiù}{按|àn}{小|xiǎo}{张|Zhāng}{说|shuō}{的|de}{再|zài}{改一改|gǎi yi gǎi}。”

"On Monday morning the secretary, Xiao Li, typed a notice on the computer: a meeting of all staff at
3 p.m. this Friday; please prepare your comments in advance. On Friday afternoon everyone came to the
meeting room. The manager spoke first, with the company's new plan for next year on the screen.
When he had finished, a young employee, Xiao Zhang, stood up and spoke. He said the plan was good, but
they should listen more to the clients. Everyone thought he had a point. Finally the manager smiled
and said: 'Good, the plan is approved; we'll just change it a little the way Xiao Zhang said.'"
(about 150 characters; {全体|quán tǐ}{员工|yuán gōng}{大会|dà huì}: a meeting of all staff, lesson 03; {道理|dào li}: reason, sense, lesson 26)
</details>

## Say it

```speak
# At the office
{吴经理|Wú jīng lǐ}{今天|jīn tiān}{在|zài}{吗|ma}？
= Is Mr Wu in today?
{请|qǐng}{您|nín}{转告|zhuǎn gào}{他|tā}，{我|wǒ}{明天|míng tiān}{再|zài}{来|lái}。
= Please tell him I'll come again tomorrow.
{我们|wǒ men}{部门|bù mén}{由|yóu}{五|wǔ}{个|gè}{人|rén}{组成|zǔ chéng}。
= Our department is made up of five people.
{方案|fāng àn}{已经|yǐ jīng}{批准|pī zhǔn}{了|le}。
= The proposal has been approved.
{开会|kāi huì}{以前|yǐ qián}{请|qǐng}{事先|shì xiān}{看|kàn}{一下|yí xià}{报告|bào gào}。
= Please look at the report before the meeting.
{我|wǒ}{的|de}{鼠标|shǔ biāo}{坏|huài}{了|le}。
= My mouse is broken.
```

## Pronunciation

- 厦 shà in {大厦|dà shà}; the city Xiamen {厦门|Xià mén} reads it xià.
- 调 diào (to transfer) vs tiáo ({空调|kōng tiáo}, {调整|tiáo zhěng}): same character, different words.
- {主任|zhǔ rèn} zhǔ rèn and {主人|zhǔ rén} zhǔ rén (host, lesson 15) differ only in the tone of the second syllable.
- {秘书|mì shū} mì shū: 秘 is mì, not bì, though 必 bì is its sound part.
- 企 qǐ is third tone: {企业|qǐ yè} qǐ yè.
- {能干|néng gàn} néng gàn: simplified {={干|gàn}=} is gàn here (to do), not gān (dry); traditional writes {+{能干|néng gàn}+}.

## Common mistakes

- ~~{五|wǔ}{个|gè}{人|rén}{由|yóu}{我们|wǒ men}{部门|bù mén}{组成|zǔ chéng}~~: the whole comes first: {我们|wǒ men}{部门|bù mén}{由|yóu}{五|wǔ}{个|gè}{人|rén}{组成|zǔ chéng}.
- {以及|yǐ jí} in a chat ({我|wǒ}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{喝|hē}{茶|chá}{以及|yǐ jí}{咖啡|kā fēi}) sounds like a report: it's written style. In conversation say
  {我|wǒ}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{喝|hē}{茶|chá}{和|hé}{咖啡|kā fēi}.
- ~~{他|tā}{事先|shì xiān}{了|le}{半|bàn}{个|gè}{小时|xiǎo shí}{来|lái}~~: {事先|shì xiān} isn't a length of time; "half an hour early" is {他|tā}{提前|tí qián}{半|bàn}{个|gè}{小时|xiǎo shí}{来|lái}{了|le}.
- ~~{召开|zhào kāi}{一|yí}{个|gè}{电话|diàn huà}~~: {召开|zhào kāi} takes meetings ({召开|zhào kāi}{会议|huì yì}, {召开|zhào kāi}{大会|dà huì}); a phone call is {打|dǎ}{一|yí}{个|gè}{电话|diàn huà}.
- {老板|lǎo bǎn} for any superior: in a company or office, people say {领导|lǐng dǎo} or use the title ({吴经理|Wú jīng lǐ}, {王|Wáng}{主任|zhǔ rèn}).
- {顾客|gù kè} for a company's clients: {客户|kè hù} is a business client; {顾客|gù kè} a shop's customer.

## Key points

- Whole + {由|yóu} + parts + {组成|zǔ chéng}: {我们|wǒ men}{部门|bù mén}{由|yóu}{五|wǔ}{个|gè}{人|rén}{组成|zǔ chéng}. Also {组成|zǔ chéng} + whole: {组成|zǔ chéng}{一|yí}{个|gè}{小组|xiǎo zǔ}.
- {以及|yǐ jí}: written "and, as well as", before the last item, can join clauses; speech uses {和|hé}.
- {事先|shì xiān} (before the event) vs {提前|tí qián} (earlier than planned).
- {本|běn} + noun: this, our (written): {本|běn}{公司|gōng sī}, {本人|běn rén}, {本|běn}{周|zhōu}, {本|běn}{次|cì}.
- Formal pairs: {召开|zhào kāi}{会议|huì yì} / {开会|kāi huì}, {出席|chū xí} / {参加|cān jiā}; {发言|fā yán} (take the floor), {讲话|jiǎng huà} (a speech).
- {调|diào} diào, to transfer; {批|pī} / {批准|pī zhǔn}, to approve; {派|pài}, to send; {领|lǐng}, to collect; {担任|dān rèn}, to hold a post.
- New characters: 括 立 席 厦 构 领 秘 屏 幕 企 派 设 鼠 召.

The words from this lesson are listed below; they join your vocabulary reviews when you complete
the lesson.

lessons.title: Working as a team
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

A company runs on teams: people who share out the work, keep each other informed and pull together
when time is short. This lesson has the words for that, and two kinds of grammar that go with it:

- **[[degree adverbs]]** stronger and more particular than {很|hěn}: {相当|xiāng dāng} (quite, rather), {格外|gé wài} (especially,
  unusually), {极其|jí qí} (extremely, written) and a first look at {过于|guò yú} (too, excessively; lesson 07);
- {一旦|yí dàn}…{就|jiù}: once…, if ever…: a condition that, the moment it happens, sets off the result.

The story: {大卫|Dà wèi}'s team at his company plans a volunteer day with a residents' committee, and a
written text gives the minutes of their meeting.

## Degree adverbs: {相当|xiāng dāng}, {格外|gé wài}, {极其|jí qí}, {过于|guò yú}

You know {很|hěn}, {非常|fēi cháng}, {特别|tè bié}, {十分|shí fēn} (HSK 4), {挺|tǐng} (spoken), {太|tài}, {有点儿|yǒu diǎnr} and {比较|bǐ jiào}. Four more, each with its own job:

### {相当|xiāng dāng}: quite, rather

{相当|xiāng dāng} puts the degree fairly high, higher than {比较|bǐ jiào}, without the force of {非常|fēi cháng}. It's common in speech
and writing:

{这个|zhè ge}{项目|xiàng mù}{相当|xiāng dāng}{难|nán}，{我们|wǒ men}{得|děi}{早点儿|zǎo diǎnr}{开始|kāi shǐ}。 — This project is quite hard; we'd better start early.

{他|tā}{的|de}{汉语|Hàn yǔ}{说|shuō}{得|de}{相当|xiāng dāng}{好|hǎo}。 — He speaks Chinese rather well.

{相当|xiāng dāng} is also a verb, "to match, be equivalent to": {两|liǎng}{个|gè}{人|rén}{的|de}{水平|shuǐ píng}{相当|xiāng dāng} (the two are at about the same
level). {相当|xiāng dāng}{于|yú} is "equal to, the same as": {一|yì}{公斤|gōng jīn}{相当|xiāng dāng}{于|yú}{两|liǎng}{斤|jīn}。 (A kilo is two jin.)

### {格外|gé wài}: especially, unusually

{格外|gé wài} says that something is more so than usual, often because of something just mentioned:

{下|xià}{过|guo}{雨|yǔ}{以后|yǐ hòu}，{空气|kōng qì}{格外|gé wài}{新鲜|xīn xiān}。 — After the rain, the air is especially fresh.

{今天|jīn tiān}{是|shì}{她|tā}{第|dì}{一|yī}{天|tiān}{上班|shàng bān}，{所以|suǒ yǐ}{格外|gé wài}{紧张|jǐn zhāng}。 — It's her first day at work, so she's especially nervous.

{格外|gé wài} always compares with the usual state; {特别|tè bié} can do that too, but also just means "very". So for
"he's really tall" say {他|tā}{特别|tè bié}{高|gāo}; {格外|gé wài} needs a comparison ({在|zài}{人群|rén qún}{里|lǐ}{他|tā}{显得|xiǎn de}{格外|gé wài}{高|gāo}: in a crowd he looks especially
tall; {显得|xiǎn de} xiǎn de, to look, lesson 06).

### {极其|jí qí}: extremely (written)

{极其|jí qí} is the strongest of the four and belongs to written style. It goes before adjectives and verbs of
two syllables or more:

{这|zhè}{次|cì}{合作|hé zuò}{极其|jí qí}{重要|zhòng yào}。 — This cooperation is extremely important.

{情况|qíng kuàng}{极其|jí qí}{复杂|fù zá}。 — The situation is extremely complicated.

It sounds wrong before a single syllable ({极其|jí qí}{好|hǎo}, {极其|jí qí}{大|dà}): say {非常|fēi cháng}{好|hǎo}, or put {极|jí}{了|le} after it (HSK 3): {好|hǎo}{极|jí}{了|le}.

### {过于|guò yú}: too, excessively (preview)

{过于|guò yú} is the written partner of {太|tài}: more than is right. {你|nǐ}{过于|guò yú}{紧张|jǐn zhāng}{了|le} (you're too tense). Lesson 07 brings it
with {尽量|jǐn liàng} and {适当|shì dàng}.

| Adverb | Degree | Register | Before | Example |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| {比较|bǐ jiào} | fairly | any | anything | {比较|bǐ jiào}{忙|máng} |
| {相当|xiāng dāng} | quite, rather | any | anything | {相当|xiāng dāng}{忙|máng} |
| {很|hěn} / {非常|fēi cháng} / {十分|shí fēn} | very | any | anything | {非常|fēi cháng}{忙|máng} |
| {格外|gé wài} | more than usual | any | adjectives, some verbs | {今天|jīn tiān}{格外|gé wài}{忙|máng} |
| {极其|jí qí} | extremely | written | two-syllable words | {极其|jí qí}{重要|zhòng yào} |
| {过于|guò yú} | too much | written | adjectives, verbs | {过于|guò yú}{担心|dān xīn} |

## {一旦|yí dàn}…{就|jiù}: once…, if ever…

{一旦|yí dàn} sets up a condition that may or may not happen, and says that *as soon as it does*, the result
follows. The result often has {就|jiù}, and it's usually something serious, hard to undo, or a turning
point:

{一旦|yí dàn}{决定|jué dìng}{了|le}，{就|jiù}{不要|bú yào}{再|zài}{改|gǎi}{了|le}。 — Once it's decided, don't change it again.

{一旦|yí dàn}{出|chū}{了|le}{问题|wèn tí}，{我们|wǒ men}{就|jiù}{要|yào}{马上|mǎ shàng}{处理|chǔ lǐ}。 — If ever a problem comes up, we have to deal with it at once.

{人|rén}{一旦|yí dàn}{习惯|xí guàn}{了|le}，{就|jiù}{很|hěn}{难|nán}{改变|gǎi biàn}。 — Once people get used to something, it's hard to change.

{一旦|yí dàn} can go before or after the subject: {一旦|yí dàn}{你|nǐ}{签|qiān}{了|le}{字|zì}…, {你|nǐ}{一旦|yí dàn}{签|qiān}{了|le}{字|zì}… Compare the three:

| Pattern | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| {一|yī}…{就|jiù} (HSK 3) | as soon as (a real, often repeated sequence) | {他|tā}{一|yí}{下班|xià bān}{就|jiù}{回|huí}{家|jiā}。 He goes home as soon as he finishes work. |
| {如果|rú guǒ}…{就|jiù} (HSK 3) | if (a plain supposition) | {如果|rú guǒ}{下雨|xià yǔ}，{我们|wǒ men}{就|jiù}{不|bú}{去|qù}{了|le}。 |
| {一旦|yí dàn}…{就|jiù} | once, if ever (a condition that changes things) | {一旦|yí dàn}{下|xià}{大|dà}{雨|yǔ}，{活动|huó dòng}{就|jiù}{得|děi}{取消|qǔ xiāo}。 Should it pour, the event will have to be called off. |

{一旦|yí dàn} is neutral to formal and very common in rules and warnings: {一旦|yí dàn}{发现|fā xiàn}{问题|wèn tí}，{请|qǐng}{马上|mǎ shàng}{报告|bào gào}。 (Report any
problem at once.)

## Words for teamwork

### The team

| Word | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| {团队|tuán duì} | team (at work) | {一|yí}{个|gè}{高效|gāo xiào}{的|de}{团队|tuán duì} |
| {团|tuán} | group, party (of people) | {代表团|dài biǎo tuán}, {旅行|lǚ xíng}{团|tuán} (a tour group) |
| {成员|chéng yuán} | member | {团队|tuán duì}{成员|chéng yuán}, {家庭|jiā tíng}{成员|chéng yuán} |
| {队伍|duì wǔ} | team, contingent; line, procession | {志愿者|zhì yuàn zhě}{队伍|duì wǔ}, {队伍|duì wǔ}{很|hěn}{长|cháng} |
| {集体|jí tǐ} | collective, group (as a whole) | {集体|jí tǐ}{活动|huó dòng}, {集体|jí tǐ}{的|de}{力量|lì liang} ({力量|lì liang}: strength) |
| {全体|quán tǐ} | all, the whole (of a group) | {全体|quán tǐ}{员工|yuán gōng} |
| {双方|shuāng fāng} | both sides, the two parties | {双方|shuāng fāng}{都|dōu}{同意|tóng yì}。 |
| {各自|gè zì} | each, one's own | {各自|gè zì}{的|de}{任务|rèn wu} |
| {志愿者|zhì yuàn zhě} | volunteer | {当|dāng}{志愿者|zhì yuàn zhě} |
| {代表|dài biǎo} | representative; to represent | {员工|yuán gōng}{代表|dài biǎo}, {我|wǒ}{代表|dài biǎo}{公司|gōng sī}{欢迎|huān yíng}{大家|dà jiā}。 |
| {大会|dà huì} | conference, general meeting | {全体|quán tǐ}{员工|yuán gōng}{大会|dà huì} |

{团队|tuán duì} is the modern word for a working team; {队|duì} (HSK 4) is a sports team; {队伍|duì wǔ} is a larger group on the
move, or a queue. {全体|quán tǐ} is "all of a group" before a noun ({全体|quán tǐ}{成员|chéng yuán}); {集体|jí tǐ} is the group as one body
({集体|jí tǐ}{的|de}{决定|jué dìng}, a collective decision).

### Working together

| Word | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| {合作|hé zuò} | to cooperate (as partners) | {跟|gēn}{客户|kè hù}{合作|hé zuò} |
| {配合|pèi hé} | to coordinate, work in with | {互相|hù xiāng}{配合|pèi hé} |
| {联合|lián hé} | to unite, join; joint | {联合|lián hé}{举办|jǔ bàn} (jointly organise) |
| {组织|zǔ zhī} | to organise; organisation | {组织|zǔ zhī}{活动|huó dòng} |
| {组成|zǔ chéng} | to form, make up | {由|yóu}{五|wǔ}{个|gè}{人|rén}{组成|zǔ chéng} (lesson 02) |
| {组合|zǔ hé} | combination; to combine | {不同|bù tóng}{的|de}{组合|zǔ hé} |
| {沟通|gōu tōng} | to communicate, get through to each other | {跟|gēn}{同事|tóng shì}{沟通|gōu tōng} |
| {协议|xié yì} | agreement | {签订|qiān dìng}{协议|xié yì} |
| {达成|dá chéng} | to reach (an agreement) | {达成|dá chéng}{协议|xié yì}, {达成|dá chéng}{一致|yí zhì} |
| {一致|yí zhì} | unanimous, consistent | {大家|dà jiā}{的|de}{意见|yì jiàn}{很|hěn}{一致|yí zhì}。 |
| {紧密|jǐn mì} | close (cooperation, ties) | {紧密|jǐn mì}{合作|hé zuò} |

- {合作|hé zuò} is two sides working together as equals; {配合|pèi hé} is fitting in with someone, playing your part in
  their plan: {我们|wǒ men}{跟|gēn}{警察|jǐng chá}{合作|hé zuò} (we cooperate with the police) but {请|qǐng}{大家|dà jiā}{配合|pèi hé} (please cooperate: do as asked).
- {沟通|gōu tōng} is more than talking: making yourself understood and understanding the other side. {我们|wǒ men}{得|děi}{多|duō}{沟通|gōu tōng}。
- {达成|dá chéng} takes only a few objects: {达成|dá chéng}{协议|xié yì} (reach an agreement), {达成|dá chéng}{一致|yí zhì} (reach a consensus).

### Sharing the work

| Word | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| {分配|fēn pèi} | to allocate, assign | {分配|fēn pèi}{任务|rèn wu} |
| {承担|chéng dān} | to take on, bear (a task, responsibility, cost) | {承担|chéng dān}{责任|zé rèn} |
| {负担|fù dān} | burden; to bear (a cost) | {工作|gōng zuò}{负担|fù dān}{很|hěn}{重|zhòng} |
| {处理|chǔ lǐ} | to handle, deal with | {处理|chǔ lǐ}{问题|wèn tí} |
| {参与|cān yù} | to take part in, be involved | {参与|cān yù}{讨论|tǎo lùn} |
| {投入|tóu rù} | to throw oneself into; to put in (money) | {投入|tóu rù}{工作|gōng zuò}, {他|tā}{工作|gōng zuò}{很|hěn}{投入|tóu rù}。 |
| {发挥|fā huī} | to bring into play, make the most of | {发挥|fā huī}{优势|yōu shì} |
| {优势|yōu shì} | advantage, strength | {我们|wǒ men}{的|de}{优势|yōu shì} |
| {不足|bù zú} | insufficient; shortcoming | {经验|jīng yàn}{不足|bù zú}, {不足|bù zú}{的|de}{地方|dì fang} |
| {效率|xiào lǜ} | efficiency | {效率|xiào lǜ}{很|hěn}{高|gāo} |
| {高效|gāo xiào} | highly efficient | {高效|gāo xiào}{的|de}{团队|tuán duì} |
| {环节|huán jié} | link, stage (in a process) | {每|měi}{个|gè}{环节|huán jié}{都|dōu}{很|hěn}{重要|zhòng yào}。 |
| {完善|wán shàn} | to improve, perfect; complete | {完善|wán shàn}{方案|fāng àn} |
| {改进|gǎi jìn} | to improve (methods, work) | {改进|gǎi jìn}{工作|gōng zuò}{方法|fāng fǎ} |

lesson 19), {细心|xì xīn} (xì xīn, careful), {长处|cháng chù} (cháng chù, strong point, lesson 11), {肯定|kěn dìng} (to recognise, HSK 4), {群|qún}
(qún, a group, lesson 22), {道理|dào li} (dào li, sense, lesson 26).

1. What is the main idea of the text?
2. According to the second point, why do teams often run into problems?
3. What does a good leader do when sharing out work?
4. What does the closing saying suggest about teamwork?

<details>
<summary>Answers and translation</summary>

1. Working well with others matters a great deal at work, and a good team communicates, shares the
   work fairly, takes the initiative and shares its success (and its lessons).
2. Not lack of ability but poor communication: if members understand the goal differently, the more
   they do, the bigger the problem ({一旦|yí dàn}{大家|dà jiā}{对|duì}{目标|mù biāo}{的|de}{理解|lǐ jiě}{不|bù}{一致|yí zhì}…).
3. Lets each person use their strengths, and doesn't leave most of the work to a few.
4. Alone you may be faster, but together you get further: a team achieves more over time.

"At work there's hardly any job one person can finish alone. A project often has many stages and
needs different people to complete it together. So whether you can work with others has become an
extremely important requirement when you look for a job. What, then, is a good team like? First,
members must communicate often. Many problems come not from a lack of ability but from a lack of
communication. Once people understand the goal differently, the more work they do, the bigger the
problem may become. So before starting, a team should make the goal clear in advance, draw up a plan
and reach agreement. Second, work must be shared out sensibly. Everyone has their strengths: some
are good at dealing with clients, some are very careful with data. A good leader lets each person
make the most of their strong points, instead of letting a few carry most of the work. If one
person's load is too heavy while others have nothing to do, the team won't be efficient. Third,
members must take the initiative. In an efficient team nobody waits to be chased. When they see
someone with too much to do, people go and help of their own accord, and work in with each other.
Finally, a team's success is a collective success. When a project is over, the leader should
recognise everyone's contribution, and together they should find what fell short and improve their
methods for next time. That way the team grows especially close, and the next collaboration goes
more smoothly too. Someone said: 'One person can walk fast; a group can walk far.' At work today,
that saying makes a lot of sense."
</details>

## Characters

**The 一致 {致|zhì}, 制订 {制|zhì} and 组织 {织|zhī}** of this lesson's words are lesson 04's characters: read them with
their pinyin for now.

### A new radical: 手 (hand)

You know 扌, the hand at the left side ({打|dǎ}, {找|zhǎo}, and this lesson's {搞|gǎo} {拼|pīn} {投|tóu} {挥|huī}). 手 is the same radical in its
full form, used when the hand stands at the bottom or in the middle. The characters with it so far:
手 itself (HSK 1), 拿 (to hold, HSK 2: 合 over 手), and this lesson's 承, where the hand is hidden in the
middle (the three horizontals and the vertical hook). Lesson 11 adds 掌 (palm). Four characters of levels 1–5 have 手; dozens have 扌.

### Families and look-alikes

- **勾 gōu**: 沟 gōu (ditch: {沟通|gōu tōng} is "to open a channel between"), 构 gòu (lesson 02), 购 gòu ({购买|gòu mǎi}). Traditional
  writes 溝 構 購 with 冓, a different shared part.
- **并 bìng**: 拼 pīn, 屏 píng (lesson 02), 饼 bǐng ({饼干|bǐng gān}). The sound has drifted, but the family is clear.
- **军 jūn**: 挥 huī and 辉 huī ({光辉|guāng huī}, brilliant). Traditional 揮 has 軍.
- **工 gōng**: 贡 gòng, 功 gōng ({成功|chéng gōng}), 红 hóng, 江 jiāng, 空 kōng. 贡 is 工 over 贝: compare 员 (口 over 贝).
- **弋 yì** in 代 dài and 式 shì / 试 shì. A memory aid for 代: a person (亻) who takes another's place. Don't confuse 代 with 化 huà ({变化|biàn huà}): 化 has 匕, no dot.
- **五 wǔ** gives 伍 wǔ exactly, and **崔 cuī** gives 催 cuī exactly: easy ones.
- **殳**: 投 tóu, 设 shè (lesson 02), 没 méi: three characters with the same simplified right side.
- **集**: 隹 (a short-tailed bird) over 木 (tree). Shuowen explains it as birds gathering on a tree.
- **齐**: Shuowen describes the old form as ears of grain standing level. Traditional 齊 keeps more of
  that picture.
- **团**: 囗 around 才. Traditional 團 has 專 (zhuān) inside, which gave the sound; simplified 才 is a
  simple stand-in (and a memory aid: talent inside a ring of people).
- **善** has 羊 at the top, as 美 does. Shuowen glosses 善 as "auspicious" and writes it with 羊.
- **率** has two readings: lǜ in {效率|xiào lǜ} and {汇率|huì lǜ} (a rate), shuài in {率领|shuài lǐng} (to lead) and {坦率|tǎn shuài} (frank).

### Stroke order

- **承**: the top stroke that turns down (like the top of 了), the vertical hook, then the three short
  horizontals, then the left side (a horizontal that turns down to the left) and the right side
  (a left-falling and a right-falling stroke).
- **齐**: 文 first (dot, horizontal, left-falling, right-falling), then the left-falling stroke and the
  vertical below.
- **团**: 囗's left side and top, then 才 inside (horizontal, vertical hook, left-falling), and
  the bottom stroke closes it.
- **代**: 亻, then 弋: the horizontal, the long slanting hook, and the dot last.
- **集**: 隹 first (eight strokes), then 木.

## Write it: a picture story

1. A notice on an office wall: "Volunteers wanted! Saturday, clean-up in the park."
2. Saturday morning: a group of people with gloves and bags gather at a park gate; one is handing
   out tasks.
3. They pick up rubbish in small groups; two of them carry a heavy bag together.
4. The park is clean; everyone takes a photo together, tired but happy.

Write 100–150 characters with at least three of: {志愿者|zhì yuàn zhě}, {集合|jí hé}, {分配|fēn pèi}, {配合|pèi hé}, {一旦|yí dàn}…{就|jiù}, {相当|xiāng dāng}, {格外|gé wài}.

<details>
<summary>Model answer</summary>

{上|shàng}{个|gè}{星期|xīng qī}，{公司|gōng sī}{发|fā}{了|le}{一|yí}{个|gè}{通知|tōng zhī}：{周|zhōu}{六|liù}{上午|shàng wǔ}{要|yào}{搞|gǎo}{一|yí}{次|cì}{环保|huán bǎo}{活动|huó dòng}，{急需|jí xū}{志愿者|zhì yuàn zhě}。{很|hěn}{多|duō}{同事|tóng shì}{都|dōu}{主动|zhǔ dòng}{报|bào}{了|le}{名|míng}。{周|zhōu}{六|liù}{早上|zǎo shang}{八|bā}{点|diǎn}，{大家|dà jiā}{在|zài}{公园|gōng yuán}
{门口|mén kǒu}{集合|jí hé}。{小|xiǎo}{王|Wáng}{把|bǎ}{任务|rèn wu}{分配|fēn pèi}{给|gěi}{每|měi}{个|gè}{小组|xiǎo zǔ}，{有的|yǒu de}{人|rén}{捡|jiǎn}{垃圾|lā jī}，{有的|yǒu de}{人|rén}{打扫|dǎ sǎo}{道路|dào lù}。{有|yǒu}{一|yí}{个|gè}{袋子|dài zi}{相当|xiāng dāng}{重|zhòng}，{两|liǎng}{个|gè}{同事|tóng shì}{互相|hù xiāng}{配合|pèi hé}，{一起|yì qǐ}{把|bǎ}{它|tā}{抬|tái}{了|le}
{起来|qǐ lái}。{到|dào}{了|le}{中午|zhōng wǔ}，{公园|gōng yuán}{变|biàn}{得|de}{格外|gé wài}{干净|gān jìng}。{大家|dà jiā}{虽然|suī rán}{很|hěn}{累|lèi}，{但是|dàn shì}{都|dōu}{非常|fēi cháng}{开心|kāi xīn}，{最后|zuì hòu}{一起|yì qǐ}{拍|pāi}{了|le}{一|yì}{张|zhāng}{照片|zhào piàn}。

"Last week the company sent round a notice: on Saturday morning there would be an environmental event,
and volunteers were badly needed. Many colleagues signed up of their own accord. At eight on Saturday
morning everyone gathered at the park gate. Xiao Wang shared out the tasks among the groups: some
picked up rubbish, some swept the paths. One bag was quite heavy; two colleagues worked together and
lifted it up between them. By midday the park was especially clean. Everyone was tired but very
happy, and at the end they took a photo together." ({捡|jiǎn} jiǎn: to pick up, lesson 09; {道路|dào lù} dào lù: road, path; {袋子|dài zi} dài zi: bag; {抬|tái} tái: to
lift, carry)
</details>

## Say it

```speak
# In a team
{大家|dà jiā}{都|dōu}{到|dào}{齐|qí}{了|le}{吗|ma}？
= Is everyone here?
{我们|wǒ men}{先|xiān}{把|bǎ}{任务|rèn wu}{分配|fēn pèi}{一下|yí xià}。
= Let's share out the tasks first.
{这|zhè}{件|jiàn}{事|shì}{我|wǒ}{来|lái}{承担|chéng dān}。
= I'll take this one on.
{我|wǒ}{会|huì}{尽力|jìn lì}{的|de}。
= I'll do my best.
{一旦|yí dàn}{有|yǒu}{问题|wèn tí}，{就|jiù}{马上|mǎ shàng}{告诉|gào su}{我|wǒ}。
= If there's ever a problem, tell me straight away.
{只要|zhǐ yào}{大家|dà jiā}{互相|hù xiāng}{配合|pèi hé}，{一定|yí dìng}{能|néng}{搞|gǎo}{好|hǎo}。
= As long as we all work together, it's sure to go well.
```

## Pronunciation

- {极其|jí qí} jí qí: two rising tones. {机器|jī qì} jī qì (machine, lesson 19) has the same syllables with tones 1 and 4.
- {参与|cān yù} cān yù: 与 is yù here, not yǔ ({与|yǔ} = and, HSK 4).
- {处理|chǔ lǐ} chǔ lǐ: 处 chǔ (to deal with), not chù (a place, lesson 23). Third tone + third tone: said chú lǐ.
- {效率|xiào lǜ} xiào lǜ: lǜ with ü (lips rounded, tongue as for *ee*).
- {队伍|duì wǔ} duì wǔ, {志愿者|zhì yuàn zhě} zhì yuàn zhě, {贡献|gòng xiàn} gòng xiàn.
- {齐|qí} qí and {骑|qí} qí (to ride) sound the same.

## Common mistakes

- {极其|jí qí} before one syllable ({极其|jí qí}{好|hǎo}) sounds wrong: {极其|jí qí} goes before words of two syllables or more:
  {极其|jí qí}{重要|zhòng yào}; for one syllable say {好|hǎo}{极|jí}{了|le}, {非常|fēi cháng}{大|dà}.
- Less natural: {他|tā}{一旦|yí dàn}{下班|xià bān}{就|jiù}{回|huí}{家|jiā} for a daily routine. {一旦|yí dàn} is for a condition that may or may not come;
  a routine is {他|tā}{一|yí}{下班|xià bān}{就|jiù}{回|huí}{家|jiā}.
- ~~{达成|dá chéng}{计划|jì huà}~~: {达成|dá chéng} takes {协议|xié yì}, {一致|yí zhì} or {目标|mù biāo} (a goal). A plan is drawn up ({制订|zhì dìng}{计划|jì huà}) or carried out ({完成|wán chéng}{计划|jì huà}).
- {参与|cān yù} vs {参加|cān jiā}: {参加|cān jiā}{会议|huì yì} is attending a meeting; {参与|cān yù} is having a part in something ({参与|cān yù}{讨论|tǎo lùn}, {参与|cān yù}{决定|jué dìng}).
- {搞|gǎo} is spoken: in a report write {举办|jǔ bàn}{活动|huó dòng}, {开展|kāi zhǎn}{工作|gōng zuò}, not {搞|gǎo}{活动|huó dòng}.

## Key points

- {相当|xiāng dāng} (quite), {格外|gé wài} (more than usual), {极其|jí qí} (extremely, written, two-syllable words), {过于|guò yú} (too, written).
- {一旦|yí dàn}…{就|jiù}: once / if ever this happens, then…: rules, warnings, turning points.
- {合作|hé zuò} (partners) vs {配合|pèi hé} (play your part); {参与|cān yù} (have a part) vs {参加|cān jiā} (attend); {开展|kāi zhǎn}{活动|huó dòng} vs {展开|zhǎn kāi}{讨论|tǎo lùn};
  {承担|chéng dān}{责任|zé rèn} vs {负担|fù dān} (a burden); {制订|zhì dìng}{计划|jì huà} (draw up).
- {达成|dá chéng}{协议|xié yì} / {达成|dá chéng}{一致|yí zhì}; {分配|fēn pèi}{任务|rèn wu}; {发挥|fā huī}{优势|yōu shì}; {作出|zuò chū}{贡献|gòng xiàn}; {人|rén}{到|dào}{齐|qí}{了|le}.
- New radical 手; new characters: 避 承 代 伍 催 挥 配 搞 集 贡 献 沟 拼 齐 团 投 善 率
  势 协.

lessons.title: Products, markets and money
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

Every job sits somewhere in an economy: something is made, packed, sent, sold, and somebody pays.
This lesson has the words for that chain, from the factory to the customer, and for the money along
the way (cost, profit, demand). The grammar is about numbers and conclusions:

- **[[comparison with a quantity]]**: {这|zhè}{件|jiàn}{比|bǐ}{那|nà}{件|jiàn}{贵|guì}{两|liǎng}{百|bǎi}{块|kuài} (review) and the short form {他|tā}{大|dà}{我|wǒ}{三|sān}{岁|suì};
- {可见|kě jiàn}: "so it's clear that…", drawing a conclusion from facts (a preview of lesson 26).

The texts describe how business works. They don't recommend anything: what a company should do is
not our subject.

## Comparing with a quantity

### A {比|bǐ} B + adjective + quantity (review)

You know this from HSK 3: the difference goes *after* the adjective.

{这|zhè}{件|jiàn}{衣服|yī fu}{比|bǐ}{那|nà}{件|jiàn}{贵|guì}{两|liǎng}{百|bǎi}{块|kuài}。 — This garment is two hundred yuan dearer than that one.

{新|xīn}{产品|chǎn pǐn}{比|bǐ}{旧|jiù}{产品|chǎn pǐn}{轻|qīng}{一|yì}{公斤|gōng jīn}。 — The new product is a kilo lighter than the old one.

{今年|jīn nián}{的|de}{利润|lì rùn}{比|bǐ}{去年|qù nián}{多|duō}{百|bǎi}{分|fēn}{之|zhī}{十|shí}。 — This year's profit is ten per cent higher than last year's.

With a verb, the comparison word goes *before* the verb and the amount after it: {他|tā}{比|bǐ}{我|wǒ}{早|zǎo}{来|lái}{十|shí}{分钟|fēn zhōng} (he came
ten minutes earlier than me), {这|zhè}{家|jiā}{店|diàn}{比|bǐ}{那|nà}{家|jiā}{多|duō}{卖|mài}{了|le}{三百|sān bǎi}{杯|bēi} (this shop sold three hundred cups more than that
one).

### A + adjective + B + quantity: {他|tā}{大|dà}{我|wǒ}{三|sān}{岁|suì}

With a few adjectives, mostly of age, height and time, Chinese can drop {比|bǐ} and put B straight after
the adjective:

{他|tā}{大|dà}{我|wǒ}{三|sān}{岁|suì}。 — He's three years older than me. (= {他|tā}{比|bǐ}{我|wǒ}{大|dà}{三|sān}{岁|suì}。)

{我|wǒ}{姐姐|jiě jie}{小|xiǎo}{我|wǒ}{两|liǎng}{岁|suì}。 — My sister is two years younger than me.

{他|tā}{早|zǎo}{我|wǒ}{一|yì}{年|nián}{进|jìn}{公司|gōng sī}。 — He joined the company a year before me.

This short form needs the quantity: ×{他|tā}{大|dà}{我|wǒ} alone isn't a sentence. It is at home with a small set of measurable
one-syllable adjectives: above all {大|dà} / {小|xiǎo} (age), {高|gāo} / {矮|ǎi} (height) and {早|zǎo} / {晚|wǎn} (time). Speakers also stretch it to
a few more, especially {多|duō} / {少|shǎo}, {长|cháng} / {短|duǎn} and {重|zhòng} / {轻|qīng} ({他|tā}{多|duō}{我|wǒ}{两|liǎng}{分|fēn}: he has two points more than me). With most
other adjectives ({贵|guì}, {便宜|pián yi}, {好|hǎo}, {漂亮|piào liang}…) it isn't standard: use {比|bǐ}.

| Pattern | Example | Works with |
|---|---|---|
| A {比|bǐ} B + adj + quantity | {这|zhè}{件|jiàn}{比|bǐ}{那|nà}{件|jiàn}{贵|guì}{两|liǎng}{百|bǎi}{块|kuài}。 | any adjective |
| A + adj + B + quantity | {他|tā}{大|dà}{我|wǒ}{三|sān}{岁|suì}。 {他|tā}{高|gāo}{我|wǒ}{五|wǔ}{厘米|lí mǐ}。 | {大|dà}, {小|xiǎo}, {高|gāo}, {矮|ǎi}, {早|zǎo}, {晚|wǎn} (also heard with {多|duō}, {少|shǎo}, {长|cháng}, {短|duǎn}, {重|zhòng}, {轻|qīng}) |
| A {比|bǐ} B + {早|zǎo} / {晚|wǎn} / {多|duō} / {少|shǎo} + verb + quantity | {他|tā}{比|bǐ}{我|wǒ}{早|zǎo}{到|dào}{十|shí}{分钟|fēn zhōng}。 | verbs |

({厘米|lí mǐ} lí mǐ, centimetre, is lesson 28's word.)

## {可见|kě jiàn}: so it's clear that

{可见|kě jiàn} joins a fact to the conclusion it proves. It starts the second clause, after a comma or a full
stop: "this shows that", "it's clear, then, that":

{这|zhè}{家|jiā}{店|diàn}{每|měi}{天|tiān}{都|dōu}{排|pái}{很|hěn}{长|cháng}{的|de}{队|duì}，{可见|kě jiàn}{他们|tā men}{的|de}{东西|dōng xi}{很|hěn}{受|shòu}{欢迎|huān yíng}。 — There's a long queue at this shop every day, which

> {这样|zhè yàng}{算|suàn}{下来|xià lái}，{一|yì}{杯|bēi}{二十|èr shí}{块|kuài}{的|de}{奶茶|nǎi chá}，{商家|shāng jiā}{最后|zuì hòu}{只能|zhǐ néng}{挣|zhèng}{两|liǎng}{三|sān}{块|kuài}，{有|yǒu}{时候|shí hou}{甚至|shèn zhì}{亏|kuī}{钱|qián}。{可见|kě jiàn}，{奶茶|nǎi chá}{的|de}{价格|jià gé}{里|lǐ}，{原料|yuán liào}{只|zhǐ}{占|zhàn}{很|hěn}{小|xiǎo}{的|de}{部分|bù fen}，
> {大|dà}{部分|bù fen}{是|shì}{房租|fáng zū}、{人工|rén gōng}{和|hé}{配送|pèi sòng}{的|de}{花费|huā fèi}。{当然|dāng rán}，{规模|guī mó}{大|dà}{的|de}{品牌|pǐn pái}{可以|kě yǐ}{大批|dà pī}{进|jìn}{原料|yuán liào}，{成本|chéng běn}{比|bǐ}{小|xiǎo}{店|diàn}{低|dī}{不|bù}{少|shǎo}，{这|zhè}{也|yě}{是|shì}{大|dà}{品牌|pǐn pái}{越|yuè}{开|kāi}{越|yuè}{多|duō}{的|de}{原因|yuán yīn}
> {之|zhī}{一|yī}。
>
> {下|xià}{次|cì}{你|nǐ}{买|mǎi}{奶茶|nǎi chá}{的|de}{时候|shí hou}，{可以|kě yǐ}{想一想|xiǎng yi xiǎng}：{这|zhè}{二十|èr shí}{块|kuài}{钱|qián}，{都|dōu}{花|huā}{在|zài}{哪儿|nǎr}{了|le}？

Words to know: {中心|zhōng xīn} (zhōng xīn, centre, lesson 21), {原料|yuán liào} (yuán liào, raw materials), {糖|táng} (táng, sugar, HSK 3), {平方米|píng fāng mǐ} (píng fāng mǐ, square metre),
{平均|píng jūn} (píng jūn, average, lesson 28), {吸管|xī guǎn} (xī guǎn, straw, lesson 07), {袋子|dài zi} (dài zi, bag), {平台|píng tái} (platform,
lesson 20), {吸引|xī yǐn} (xī yǐn, to attract, HSK 4), {半价|bàn jià} (bàn jià, half price), {甚至|shèn zhì} (shèn zhì, even, HSK 4), {亏|kuī}
(kuī, to lose money, lesson 05), {占|zhàn} (zhàn, to make up, lesson 28), {人工|rén gōng} (rén gōng, labour, lesson 19), {原因|yuán yīn}
{之|zhī}{一|yī} (one of the reasons).

1. What is the main point of the text?
2. Which costs about as much per cup as the raw materials?
3. Why can big brands keep costs down?
4. What does the writer want readers to do?

<details>
<summary>Answers and translation</summary>

1. The raw materials are only a small part of the price: most of it goes on rent, labour,
   packaging and delivery, so the seller earns far less than people think ({可见|kě jiàn}，…{原料|yuán liào}{只|zhǐ}{占|zhàn}{很|hěn}{小|xiǎo}{的|de}{部分|bù fen}).
2. Rent (about four or five yuan a cup).
3. They buy raw materials in large quantities ({大批|dà pī}{进|jìn}{原料|yuán liào}), so their costs are lower.
4. Think, next time, about where the money goes.

"Many people have a cup of milk tea every day. If a cup sells for twenty yuan, how much does the
seller earn? Let's work it out. First, the ingredients. Milk, tea, sugar and fruit come to about four
or five yuan. Many people think that with ingredients so cheap, the profit must be high. In fact the
ingredients are only part of the cost. Second, rent. Milk-tea shops usually open in shopping centres
or near schools, where rent is quite expensive. A small shop of twenty square metres may pay twenty
or thirty thousand a month. Spread over each cup, that's another four or five yuan or so. Third,
labour. A shop needs at least three or four staff, plus their training: the labour cost per cup is
three or four yuan too. Fourth, packaging and delivery. Cups, straws and bags cost money; and if a
customer orders a takeaway online, the seller has to give the platform a share. So a cup earns two
or three yuan less. On top of that the seller pays for water and electricity: costs too. Finally, to attract consumers, sellers often run promotions, such as 'second cup
half price'. During a promotion they sell more, but earn less on each cup. Add it all up, and on a
twenty-yuan cup of milk tea the seller may end up earning only two or three yuan, and sometimes even
loses money. Clearly, then, the ingredients are only a small part of the price; most of it is rent,
labour and delivery. Of course, a large-scale brand can buy ingredients in bulk, at a lower cost than
a small shop: that's one of the reasons big brands keep opening more shops. Next time you buy a milk
tea, think: where did those twenty yuan go?"
</details>

## Characters
{=

| Character | Meaning | Pinyin | Radical | Strokes | Words |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 致 ✎ | to send; to cause; fine | zhì | 至 | 10 | {一致|yí zhì} (lesson 03), {导致|dǎo zhì} (lesson 23) |
| 制 ✎ | to make; to control; system | zhì | 刂 | 8 | {制订|zhì dìng} (lesson 03), {控制|kòng zhì} (lesson 06), {制作|zhì zuò} (lesson 10) |
| 织 (traditional 織) ✎ | to weave | zhī | 纟 | 8 | {组织|zǔ zhī} (lesson 03) |
| 促 | to urge, promote | cù | 亻 | 9 | {促销|cù xiāo}, {促进|cù jìn} (lesson 21) |
| 销 (traditional 銷) | to sell; to cancel | xiāo | 钅 | 12 | {促销|cù xiāo}, {销售|xiāo shòu} |
| 型 | model, type | xíng | 土 | 9 | {大型|dà xíng}, {小型|xiǎo xíng} |
| 档 (traditional 檔) | grade, level; file | dàng | 木 | 10 | {高档|gāo dàng} |
| 模 | model, pattern | mó | 木 | 14 | {规模|guī mó}, {模式|mó shì} |
| 润 (traditional 潤) | moist; profit | rùn | 氵 | 10 | {利润|lì rùn} |
| 益 ✎ | benefit | yì | 皿 | 10 | {利益|lì yì}, {有益|yǒu yì} (lesson 07) |
| 币 (traditional 幣) ✎ | money, currency | bì | 巾 | 4 | {人民币|rén mín bì} |
| 退 ✎ | to retreat; to return | tuì | 辶 | 9 | {退|tuì}, {退还|tuì huán}, {退休|tuì xiū} (lesson 05) |
| 营 (traditional 營) | to run, manage; camp | yíng | 艹 | 11 | {营业|yíng yè}, {经营|jīng yíng} (lesson 05) |
| 限 | limit | xiàn | 阝 | 8 | {有限|yǒu xiàn}, {限制|xiàn zhì} (lesson 23) |

Traditional strokes: 織 18, 銷 15, 檔 17, 潤 15, 幣 14, 營 16. Make Me a Hanzi files 营 under 艹;
in traditional 營 the top is two 火 (fire), not grass.

**制 has two traditional forms.** In {制订|zhì dìng}, {控制|kòng zhì}, {制度|zhì dù} (system, lesson 27) and {限制|xiàn zhì} (to limit) it stays 制; in
the "make" words {制作|zhì zuò}, {制造|zhì zào} (lesson 19) and {复制|fù zhì} (lesson 20) Taiwan writes 製, which adds 衣 (clothes)
below. 致 also stands for 緻 (fine, delicate) in a few words outside the course; in {一致|yí zhì} and {导致|dǎo zhì} it
stays 致.

### Families and look-alikes

- **只 in simplified**: 织 zhī, 职 zhí ({职业|zhí yè}, {职工|zhí gōng}) and 识 shí ({认识|rèn shi}) all have 只, where traditional has
  戠 (織, 職, 識). Simplified uses 只 as a short, sound-like stand-in.
- **肖 xiào**: 销 xiāo, 消 xiāo ({消费|xiāo fèi}: the same sound and the same family). 销 has 钅 (metal):
  money and trade; 消 has 氵 (water): to disappear, to use up.
- **莫 mò**: 模 mó (this lesson), 幕 mù (lesson 02), and later 摸 mō (lesson 09) and 漠 mò (lesson 22).
- **当 dāng → 档 dàng**: traditional 檔 has 當.
- **闰 rùn → 润 rùn**: the sound matches exactly.
- **足 zú → 促 cù**: 亻 + 足; the sound has drifted.
- **艮** at the right or bottom: 退 tuì, 限 xiàn, 很 hěn, 跟 gēn, 根 gēn, 眼 yǎn, 银 yín. In 根 and
  跟 it still helps with the sound; elsewhere it doesn't.
- **The simplified top 艹** in 营 yíng stands for traditional 𤇾 (two fires over a cover), as it does in 劳
  (lesson 24, 勞) and 荣 (lesson 21, 榮): the same shortcut, three characters.
- **益** is 皿 (a vessel) with water above: Shuowen explains it as water overflowing a vessel, "more than
  enough", hence benefit.
- **币** is 巾 (cloth) under a short stroke; traditional 幣 has 敝 bì, the sound part.
- **型** is 刑 xíng (the sound) over 土 (earth): a clay mould.

### Stroke order

- **致**: 至 first (horizontal, the turn down to the left, a dot, then 土's horizontal, vertical and rising
  stroke), then 攵 (left-falling, horizontal, left-falling, right-falling).
- **制**: the left part (left-falling, two horizontals, the vertical, the turn with a hook, the short
  vertical), then 刂.
- **币**: a left-falling stroke, then 巾: vertical, the turn with a hook, and the long vertical through
  the middle. Only four strokes.
- **退**: 艮 first, 辶 last: the dot, the bent stroke, then the long sweep along the bottom.
- **限**: 阝 first (two strokes), then 艮.

## Write it: a picture story

1. A woman looks at two coats in a shop window: one with a big brand name, one without.
2. She checks the prices: the brand coat is 800, the other 500.
3. She tries on the cheaper coat; it fits well, and the label says "high quality wool".
4. At home she shows it to her friend, who says: "Good choice!"

Write 100–150 characters. Use at least three of: {名牌|míng pái}, {品质|pǐn zhì}, {比|bǐ}…{贵|guì}, {节省|jié shěng}, {可见|kě jiàn}, {消费者|xiāo fèi zhě}.

<details>
<summary>Model answer</summary>

{周末|zhōu mò}，{小|xiǎo}{夏|Xià}{去|qù}{商场|shāng chǎng}{买|mǎi}{大衣|dà yī}。{她|tā}{看中|kàn zhòng}{了|le}{两|liǎng}{件|jiàn}：{一|yí}{件|jiàn}{是|shì}{名牌|míng pái}，{一|yí}{件|jiàn}{不|bú}{是|shì}。{名牌|míng pái}{的|de}{那|nà}{件|jiàn}{八百|bā bǎi}{块|kuài}，{比|bǐ}{另|lìng}{一|yí}{件|jiàn}{贵|guì}{三百|sān bǎi}{块|kuài}。{小|xiǎo}{夏|Xià}{想|xiǎng}{了|le}{想|xiǎng}，{先|xiān}{试|shì}{了|le}
{便宜|pián yi}{的|de}{那|nà}{件|jiàn}。{没|méi}{想|xiǎng}{到|dào}{这|zhè}{件|jiàn}{大衣|dà yī}{不但|bú dàn}{很|hěn}{合适|hé shì}，{而且|ér qiě}{品质|pǐn zhì}{也|yě}{不错|bú cuò}，{用|yòng}{的|de}{是|shì}{优质|yōu zhì}{的|de}{羊毛|yáng máo}。{她|tā}{决定|jué dìng}{买|mǎi}{这|zhè}{件|jiàn}，{节省|jié shěng}{了|le}{三百|sān bǎi}{块|kuài}。{回|huí}{家|jiā}{以后|yǐ hòu}，{她|tā}
{给|gěi}{朋友|péng you}{看|kàn}{了|le}{新|xīn}{大衣|dà yī}，{朋友|péng you}{说|shuō}：“{真|zhēn}{好看|hǎo kàn}，{还|hái}{这么|zhè me}{便宜|pián yi}！”{可见|kě jiàn}，{做|zuò}{一|yí}{个|gè}{聪明|cōng ming}{的|de}{消费者|xiāo fèi zhě}，{不|bù}{一定|yí dìng}{要|yào}{买|mǎi}{名牌|míng pái}。

"At the weekend Xiao Xia went to the shopping centre to buy a coat. Two caught her eye: one a famous
brand, one not. The brand one cost eight hundred, three hundred more than the other. Xiao Xia
thought for a moment and tried the cheaper one first. To her surprise it not only fitted well but
was good quality too, made of fine wool. She decided to buy it and saved three hundred yuan. At home
she showed her friend the new coat, and her friend said: 'It looks great, and it's so cheap!' Clearly
a smart consumer doesn't have to buy famous brands." ({看中|kàn zhòng} kàn zhòng: to take a fancy to; {羊毛|yáng máo} yáng
máo: wool)
</details>

## Say it

```speak
# Shopping and business
{这|zhè}{件|jiàn}{比|bǐ}{那|nà}{件|jiàn}{贵|guì}{两|liǎng}{百|bǎi}{块|kuài}。
= This one's two hundred yuan more than that one.
{他|tā}{大|dà}{我|wǒ}{三|sān}{岁|suì}。
= He's three years older than me.
{七|qī}{天|tiān}{之|zhī}{内|nèi}{可以|kě yǐ}{退|tuì}{货|huò}{吗|ma}？
= Can I return it within seven days?
{您|nín}{的|de}{店|diàn}{几|jǐ}{点|diǎn}{营业|yíng yè}？
= What time does your shop open?
{这样|zhè yàng}{能|néng}{节省|jié shěng}{不|bù}{少|shǎo}{成本|chéng běn}。
= That saves quite a lot of cost.
{天天|tiān tiān}{排队|pái duì}，{可见|kě jiàn}{东西|dōng xi}{很|hěn}{受|shòu}{欢迎|huān yíng}。
= There's a queue every day: clearly people love it.
```

## Pronunciation

- {买卖|mǎi mai} mǎi mai (business): 卖 is light here. {买|mǎi} mǎi and {卖|mài} mài on their own differ only in tone.
- {省|shěng} shěng (to save) and {省|shěng} shěng (province) are the same syllable.
- {利润|lì rùn} lì rùn: *r* then *un*; {利益|lì yì} lì yì: two falling tones.
- {促销|cù xiāo} cù xiāo: *c* (ts with a puff of air), then *x*.
- {规模|guī mó} guī mó: 模 is mó here (and in {模式|mó shì}); in {模样|mú yàng} (looks) it's mú.
- {人民币|rén mín bì} rén mín bì: two rising tones, then a falling one.

## Common mistakes

- ~~{这|zhè}{件|jiàn}{衣服|yī fu}{贵|guì}{两|liǎng}{百|bǎi}{块|kuài}{比|bǐ}{那|nà}{件|jiàn}~~: the difference follows the adjective, and {比|bǐ} + B comes before it:
  {这|zhè}{件|jiàn}{衣服|yī fu}{比|bǐ}{那|nà}{件|jiàn}{贵|guì}{两|liǎng}{百|bǎi}{块|kuài}.
- Not standard: {这|zhè}{件|jiàn}{衣服|yī fu}{贵|guì}{那|nà}{件|jiàn}{两|liǎng}{百|bǎi}{块|kuài}. The short form A + adjective + B + quantity belongs to a few
  measurable adjectives ({大|dà}, {小|xiǎo}, {高|gāo}, {矮|ǎi}, {早|zǎo}, {晚|wǎn}, and in speech {多|duō}, {长|cháng}, {重|zhòng}…). With {贵|guì}, use {比|bǐ}:
  {这|zhè}{件|jiàn}{衣服|yī fu}{比|bǐ}{那|nà}{件|jiàn}{贵|guì}{两|liǎng}{百|bǎi}{块|kuài}.
- ~~{他|tā}{大|dà}{我|wǒ}~~: the short form needs the amount: {他|tā}{大|dà}{我|wǒ}{三|sān}{岁|suì}. Without one, say {他|tā}{比|bǐ}{我|wǒ}{大|dà}.
- ~~{可见|kě jiàn}~~ before the evidence: {可见|kě jiàn} introduces the conclusion: {天天|tiān tiān}{排队|pái duì}，{可见|kě jiàn}{很|hěn}{受|shòu}{欢迎|huān yíng}, not {可见|kě jiàn}{很|hěn}{受|shòu}{欢迎|huān yíng}，{天天|tiān tiān}{排队|pái duì}.
- {利益|lì yì} for interest on a bank account: that's {利息|lì xī} (lì xī).

## Key points

- A {比|bǐ} B + adjective + quantity: {这|zhè}{件|jiàn}{比|bǐ}{那|nà}{件|jiàn}{贵|guì}{两|liǎng}{百|bǎi}{块|kuài}; A {比|bǐ} B + {早|zǎo} / {多|duō} + verb + quantity: {他|tā}{比|bǐ}{我|wǒ}{早|zǎo}{到|dào}{十|shí}{分钟|fēn zhōng}.
- A + adjective + B + quantity, mainly with {大|dà}, {小|xiǎo}, {高|gāo}, {矮|ǎi}, {早|zǎo}, {晚|wǎn} (in speech also {多|duō}, {长|cháng}, {重|zhòng}…): {他|tā}{大|dà}{我|wǒ}{三|sān}{岁|suì}.
- {可见|kě jiàn}: fact, {可见|kě jiàn} conclusion (formal; speech: {看来|kàn lái}, {说明|shuō míng}).
- The chain: {生产|shēng chǎn} → {加工|jiā gōng} → {包装|bāo zhuāng} → {运输|yùn shū} / {配送|pèi sòng} → {销售|xiāo shòu}; money: {成本|chéng běn}, {利润|lì rùn}, {利益|lì yì}, {花费|huā fèi}, {节省|jié shěng} / {省|shěng}.
- Register: {出售|chū shòu} / {卖|mài}, {消费|xiāo fèi} / {花|huā}, {退还|tuì huán} / {退|tuì}.
- New characters: 致 制 织 促 销 型 档 模 润 益 币 退 营 限.

lessons.title: Changing jobs and starting a business
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

Sooner or later most people think about a change: a new job, their own business, a different
life. This lesson has the words for that (resigning, savings, risk, courage) and the grammar of
weighing up what might happen:

- {假如|jiǎ rú} (if, supposing) and {万一|wàn yī} (in case, if by any chance): two kinds of **hypothetical
  sentence**;
- {不然|bù rán} / {要不|yào bù} / {要不然|yào bù rán} (otherwise) and {要不是|yào bu shì} (if it weren't for);
- {哪怕|nǎ pà}…{也|yě} (even if): a **[[concessive sentence]]**, stronger and more spoken than {即使|jí shǐ}…{也|yě};
- {说不定|shuō bu dìng} (maybe, it could be that) and {没法儿|méi fǎr} (there's no way to).

The story: {大卫|Dà wèi} tells his manager, {吴经理|Wú jīng lǐ}, that he's leaving to run the small company his friend {白涛|Bái Tāo} has
just set up for the two of them.

## {假如|jiǎ rú} and {万一|wàn yī}: if, and in case

### {假如|jiǎ rú}: if, supposing

{假如|jiǎ rú} is "if" for a supposition, often one that isn't true or hasn't happened. It's a little more
formal than {如果|rú guǒ} (HSK 3), and it works in the same frame, with {就|jiù} or {会|huì} in the second clause:

{假如|jiǎ rú}{我|wǒ}{是|shì}{你|nǐ}，{我|wǒ}{就|jiù}{不|bú}{会|huì}{辞职|cí zhí}。 — If I were you, I wouldn't resign.

{假如|jiǎ rú}{明天|míng tiān}{的|de}{会|huì}{取消|qǔ xiāo}{了|le}，{我|wǒ}{就|jiù}{去|qù}{上海|Shàng hǎi}。 — If tomorrow's meeting is cancelled, I'll go to Shanghai.

{假如|jiǎ rú}{没有|méi yǒu}{你们|nǐ men}{的|de}{帮助|bāng zhù}，{我们|wǒ men}{的|de}{公司|gōng sī}{不|bù}{可能|kě néng}{成立|chéng lì}。 — Without your help, our company couldn't have been founded.

{假如|jiǎ rú} is common in writing and in careful speech; {如果|rú guǒ} is the everyday word. Both can close with {的话|de huà}:
{假如|jiǎ rú}…{的话|de huà}.

### {万一|wàn yī}: in case, if by any chance

{万一|wàn yī} (literally "one in ten thousand") is for a possibility that is *unlikely and usually unwelcome*: "if
by any chance", "in case". The second clause is often a question ({怎么办|zěn me bàn}?) or a precaution:

{万一|wàn yī}{下雨|xià yǔ}{怎么办|zěn me bàn}？ — What if it rains?

{带|dài}{上|shàng}{伞|sǎn}{吧|ba}，{万一|wàn yī}{下雨|xià yǔ}{呢|ne}。 — Take an umbrella, in case it rains.

{万一|wàn yī}{失败|shī bài}{了|le}，{你|nǐ}{还|hái}{有|yǒu}{存款|cún kuǎn}{吗|ma}？ — If it should fail, do you still have savings?

{万一|wàn yī} can also be a noun, "an emergency, the unlikely event": {以|yǐ}{防|fáng}{万一|wàn yī} (just in case: {防|fáng}, to guard against,
is lesson 08's). Compare:

| Word | The possibility is… | Example |
