## {不然|bù rán}, {要不|yào bù}, {要不然|yào bù rán}: otherwise

These three link a warning to what will happen if you don't follow it. They start the second clause:

{快|kuài}{走|zǒu}{吧|ba}，{不然|bù rán}{要|yào}{迟到|chí dào}{了|le}。 — Let's go, or we'll be late.

{你|nǐ}{最好|zuì hǎo}{事先|shì xiān}{跟|gēn}{他|tā}{说|shuō}{一|yì}{声|shēng}，{要不|yào bù}{他|tā}{会|huì}{不|bù}{高兴|gāo xìng}{的|de}。 — You'd better tell him in advance, otherwise he won't be pleased.

{我|wǒ}{得|děi}{多|duō}{存|cún}{点儿|diǎnr}{钱|qián}，{要不然|yào bù rán}{没法儿|méi fǎr}{创业|chuàng yè}。 — I have to save more, or I'll have no way of starting a business.

{不然|bù rán} is the most neutral; {要不|yào bù} and {要不然|yào bù rán} are spoken. {要不|yào bù} has a second use, a suggestion: "how about…?"

{这个|zhè ge}{周末|zhōu mò}{太|tài}{忙|máng}{了|le}，{要不|yào bù}{我们|wǒ men}{下|xià}{周|zhōu}{再|zài}{谈|tán}？ — This weekend's too busy: how about we talk next week?

## {要不是|yào bu shì}: if it weren't for

{要不是|yào bu shì} looks at something that *did* happen and imagines it hadn't. The second clause says what would
have been different, often with {就|jiù}, {早|zǎo}{就|jiù} or {也|yě}:

{要不是|yào bu shì}{你|nǐ}{帮|bāng}{我|wǒ}，{我|wǒ}{早|zǎo}{就|jiù}{放弃|fàng qì}{了|le}。 — If it weren't for your help, I'd have given up long ago.

{要不是|yào bu shì}{汇率|huì lǜ}{变动|biàn dòng}，{我们|wǒ men}{的|de}{成本|chéng běn}{不|bú}{会|huì}{这么|zhè me}{高|gāo}。 — If it weren't for the change in the exchange rate, our costs
wouldn't be this high.

{要不是|yào bu shì} is always counterfactual: the speaker knows the first clause is true. ×{要不是|yào bu shì}{明天|míng tiān}{下雨|xià yǔ} makes no
sense, because tomorrow hasn't happened.

## {哪怕|nǎ pà}…{也|yě}: even if

{哪怕|nǎ pà} introduces an extreme case, and {也|yě} (or {都|dōu}) says the result holds anyway:

{哪怕|nǎ pà}{失败|shī bài}{了|le}，{我|wǒ}{也|yě}{不|bú}{后悔|hòu huǐ}。 — Even if I fail, I won't regret it.

{哪怕|nǎ pà}{只有|zhǐ yǒu}{一|yí}{个|gè}{客户|kè hù}，{我们|wǒ men}{也|yě}{要|yào}{做|zuò}{好|hǎo}。 — Even if we have only one client, we must do it well.

{哪怕|nǎ pà} is the spoken, emphatic partner of HSK 4's {即使|jí shǐ}…{也|yě}. Both are concessive: the condition doesn't change
the outcome. {哪怕|nǎ pà} stresses how extreme the case is ("even if it's only…, even if it comes to…").

| | Register | Example |
|---|---|---|
| {即使|jí shǐ}…{也|yě} | neutral, written | {即使|jí shǐ}{条件|tiáo jiàn}{艰苦|jiān kǔ}，{他|tā}{也|yě}{坚持|jiān chí}{了|le}{下来|xià lái}。 |
| {哪怕|nǎ pà}…{也|yě} | spoken, emphatic | {哪怕|nǎ pà}{再|zài}{苦|kǔ}，{我|wǒ}{也|yě}{要|yào}{试一试|shì yi shì}。 |

({坚持|jiān chí}{下来|xià lái}: to see it through; {再|zài}{苦|kǔ}: however hard.)

## {说不定|shuō bu dìng} and {没法儿|méi fǎr}

{说不定|shuō bu dìng} is "perhaps, it could well be", a guess with some hope or worry in it. It goes before the verb or
at the start: {说不定|shuō bu dìng}{他|tā}{已经|yǐ jīng}{知道|zhī dào}{了|le}。 (Maybe he knows already.) {说不定|shuō bu dìng}{我们|wǒ men}{的|de}{公司|gōng sī}{以后|yǐ hòu}{会|huì}{很|hěn}{成功|chéng gōng}。 It can also be a
predicate: {这|zhè}{件|jiàn}{事|shì}{还|hái}{说不定|shuō bu dìng}。 (That's not certain yet.)

{没法儿|méi fǎr} (spoken: the erhua 法儿 fǎr) is "there's no way to, can't": {没法儿|méi fǎr}{跟|gēn}{他|tā}{说|shuō} (no way to tell him), {这么|zhè me}{多|duō}{钱|qián}，
{我|wǒ}{没法儿|méi fǎr}{还|huán}。 (I can't pay back that much money.) Written Chinese says {无法|wú fǎ} (HSK 4).

1. What is the text mainly about?
2. Why did Cheng Liang leave a job many people envied?
3. What does "{要不是|yào bu shì}{我|wǒ}{太太|tài tai}{一直|yì zhí}{支持|zhī chí}{我|wǒ}，{我|wǒ}{说不定|shuō bu dìng}{早|zǎo}{就|jiù}{回去|huí qù}{开|kāi}{飞机|fēi jī}{了|le}" tell us?

<details>
<summary>Answers and translation</summary>

1. How a pilot gave up a stable job to open a bakery, the difficulties he faced, how he overcame
   them, and his advice.
2. He had always wanted his own bakery, and he didn't want to spend his life wondering "what if"
   ({要是|yào shi}{当时|dāng shí}{试一试|shì yi shì}{呢|ne}).
3. His wife supported him all along; without her, he might well have given up and gone back to
   flying. (Her support is the reason he kept going.)
4. Courage and an optimistic attitude, more than money ({最|zuì}{需要|xū yào}{的|de}{不|bú}{是|shì}{钱|qián}，{而|ér}{是|shì}{勇气|yǒng qì}{和|hé}{乐观|lè guān}{的|de}{心态|xīn tài}).

"Cheng Liang is thirty-eight. Five years ago he was still a pilot: a high income, a stable job, envied
by many. But in his heart he had always had a wish: to open a bakery of his own. 'If I'd kept on
flying, my life wouldn't have been bad,' he says, 'but I'd always have wondered: what if
I'd tried?' The year he turned thirty-three, he finally made his decision: to resign and start a
business. His family were very worried. His mother said: 'What if it fails? How many years will your
savings last?' His friends tried to talk him out of it too: 'You're over thirty. Better be careful, or
later you won't even find a stable job.' Cheng Liang didn't hesitate. He spent two years learning to
bake, then took out all his savings and rented a small shop near his home. In the first year after
opening, the challenges came one after another: few customers, expensive ingredients, and he was
behind on the rent. At the worst point there were only a few hundred yuan left in his account. 'At
that time I thought about giving up too,' he says. 'If my wife hadn't supported me all along, I might
well have gone back to flying long ago.' To overcome the difficulties he tried many things: he got up
at five every morning to bake the bread himself, introduced his products online, and invited
customers to taste for free. Slowly more and more people came to the shop. In the third year the
bakery finally began to make money. Now Cheng Liang's little shop is well known. He says what
starting a business needs most is not money but courage and an optimistic attitude. 'However hard it
is, if it's work you love, it's worth fighting for.' His advice to young people who want to start a
business: boldly pursue your dream, but have a long-term plan too, and don't just look at short-term
gain."

### Stroke order

- **斗**: the two dots first (from the top), then the horizontal, then the long vertical through
  it.
- **亏**: two horizontals, then the stroke that turns twice and ends in a hook.
- **挑**: 扌, then 兆: a left-falling stroke, a dot and a rising stroke on the left, then the
  long bent hook, then a left-falling stroke and a dot on the right.
- **战**: 占 first (vertical, horizontal, then 口), then 戈: the horizontal, the long slanting
  hook, the left-falling stroke, and the dot last.
- **未**: the short horizontal, the long horizontal, the vertical, then the left- and right-falling
  strokes.
- **追** and **途**: 辶 last, as always.

"Xiao Tian worked at a company with a steady income, but she always had a wish: to open her own café.
Every day at work she would look at the little café across the street. One evening she added up her
savings and felt they were about enough. She hesitated for a long time: what if it failed? But in the
end she made up her mind: even if I fail, I want to try. The next day she gave her letter of
resignation to her manager, who was very surprised. A year later Xiao Tian's café opened, with lots
of customers: she had finally made her wish come true." ({咖啡馆|kā fēi guǎn} kā fēi guǎn: café; {吃惊|chī jīng} chī jīng: to be
surprised, HSK 4)
</details>

## Say it

```speak
# Big decisions
{我|wǒ}{想|xiǎng}{辞职|cí zhí}，{自己|zì jǐ}{创业|chuàng yè}。
= I want to resign and start my own business.
{万一|wàn yī}{失败|shī bài}{了|le}{怎么办|zěn me bàn}？
= What if it fails?
{哪怕|nǎ pà}{失败|shī bài}{了|le}，{我|wǒ}{也|yě}{不|bú}{后悔|hòu huǐ}。
= Even if I fail, I won't regret it.
{要不是|yào bu shì}{你|nǐ}{帮|bāng}{我|wǒ}，{我|wǒ}{早|zǎo}{就|jiù}{放弃|fàng qì}{了|le}。
= If it weren't for your help, I'd have given up long ago.
{快|kuài}{走|zǒu}{吧|ba}，{不然|bù rán}{要|yào}{迟到|chí dào}{了|le}。
= Let's go, or we'll be late.
{说不定|shuō bu dìng}{明年|míng nián}{我们|wǒ men}{就|jiù}{开业|kāi yè}{了|le}。
= Who knows, maybe we'll open next year.
```

## Pronunciation

- {说不定|shuō bu dìng} shuō bu dìng: 不 is light here, in the middle of a set phrase.
- {要不是|yào bu shì} yào bu shì: light 不 too. {要不|yào bù} yào bù: a full fourth tone on 不.
- {没法儿|méi fǎr} méi fǎr: the erhua joins 法 (fǎ + r).
- {万一|wàn yī} wàn yī: 一 keeps its first tone at the end of the word.
- {犹豫|yóu yù} yóu yù, {谨慎|jǐn shèn} jǐn shèn, {汇率|huì lǜ} huì lǜ (ü), {艰苦|jiān kǔ} jiān kǔ.
- 欠 qiàn (to owe) and 签 qiān (to sign, lesson 01) differ only in tone.
- {奋斗|fèn dòu} fèn dòu: 斗 dòu here; the dipper is dǒu.

## Common mistakes

- ~~{要不是|yào bu shì}{明天|míng tiān}{下雨|xià yǔ}，{我们|wǒ men}{就|jiù}{去|qù}{爬|pá}{山|shān}~~: {要不是|yào bu shì} imagines a real past or present fact away. For the future, use {如果|rú guǒ} or
  {万一|wàn yī}: {如果|rú guǒ}{明天|míng tiān}{不|bú}{下雨|xià yǔ}，{我们|wǒ men}{就|jiù}{去|qù}{爬|pá}{山|shān}.
- Jokey rather than plain: {万一|wàn yī}{我|wǒ}{中|zhòng}{了|le}{大|dà}{奖|jiǎng}，{我|wǒ}{就|jiù}{请|qǐng}{大家|dà jiā}{吃|chī}{饭|fàn}. {万一|wàn yī} mostly introduces an unwelcome possibility;
  with a lucky one it sounds like a joke about long odds. For a plain happy daydream, {假如|jiǎ rú} or {如果|rú guǒ}: {假如|jiǎ rú}{我|wǒ}{中|zhòng}{了|le}{大|dà}{奖|jiǎng}… ({中大奖|zhòng dà jiǎng} zhòng dà jiǎng: to win the jackpot).
- ~~{哪怕|nǎ pà}{失败|shī bài}{了|le}，{我|wǒ}{不|bú}{后悔|hòu huǐ}~~: the result needs {也|yě} (or {都|dōu}): {哪怕|nǎ pà}{失败|shī bài}{了|le}，{我|wǒ}{也|yě}{不|bú}{后悔|hòu huǐ}.
- ~~{不然|bù rán}{快|kuài}{走|zǒu}{吧|ba}，{要|yào}{迟到|chí dào}{了|le}~~: {不然|bù rán} starts the clause of what will happen otherwise: {快|kuài}{走|zǒu}{吧|ba}，{不然|bù rán}{要|yào}{迟到|chí dào}{了|le}.
- {辞职|cí zhí} for being let go: {辞职|cí zhí} is your own decision. Being let go is {被|bèi}{辞退|cí tuì} (bèi cí tuì: dismissed) or {失业|shī yè}.

## Key points

- {假如|jiǎ rú} (if, often untrue; a little formal), {万一|wàn yī} (in case, unlikely and usually unwelcome; {以|yǐ}{防|fáng}{万一|wàn yī}).
- {不然|bù rán} / {要不|yào bù} / {要不然|yào bù rán}: otherwise; {要不|yào bù} also "how about…?".
- {要不是|yào bu shì} + a real fact, ({早|zǎo}){就|jiù}…: if it weren't for…
- {哪怕|nǎ pà}…{也|yě}: even if (spoken, emphatic); {即使|jí shǐ}…{也|yě} is neutral.
- {说不定|shuō bu dìng}: maybe, it could be; {没法儿|méi fǎr}: no way to (written {无法|wú fǎ}).
- {辞职|cí zhí} / {离职|lí zhí} / {失业|shī yè} / {退休|tuì xiū}; {创业|chuàng yè} / {开业|kāi yè} / {经营|jīng yíng}; {争取|zhēng qǔ} / {追求|zhuī qiú} / {实现|shí xiàn}; {乐观|lè guān} / {消极|xiāo jí}.
- New radicals 舌 and 斗; new characters: 创 辞 款 斗 胆 汇 艰 亏 谨 慎 途 欠 税 挑 战 未 拥
  稳 追 犹.

The words from this lesson are listed below; they join your vocabulary reviews when you complete
the lesson.

lessons.title: Su Shi
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

This honors lesson meets one of the best-loved writers in Chinese: {苏轼|Sū Shì} (Sū Shì, Su Shi, also known as
{苏东坡|Sū Dōng pō} Sū Dōngpō), poet, essayist, calligrapher and official of the Song dynasty. You read one short poem
in full and the closing lines of a famous song lyric, both of which Chinese speakers still quote
every day. Each comes with pinyin, notes on the classical words, a paraphrase in modern Chinese and our
own translation.

Classical Chinese packs a lot into few characters. Don't try to read it like a modern text: read the
notes, then the paraphrase, then come back to the original and read it aloud.

## Su Shi's life in a paragraph

{苏轼|Sū Shì} lived from 1037 to 1101, in the Northern Song ({北宋|Běi Sòng} Běi Sòng). He came from {眉山|Méi shān} (Méishān) in today's
Sichuan, passed the imperial examinations young, together with his younger brother {苏辙|Sū Zhé} (Sū Zhé), and
spent his life as an official. His career rose and fell: more than once he was sent away from the
capital to distant posts, as far south as the island of Hainan. In {黄州|Huáng zhōu} (Huángzhōu), where he was sent
in 1080, he farmed a plot of land on an eastern slope, {东坡|Dōng pō}, and took the name {东坡居士|Dōng pō Jū shì} (the hermit of
the Eastern Slope): hence {苏东坡|Sū Dōng pō}. He wrote poems ({诗|shī}), song lyrics ({词|cí} cí: verses written to set tunes),
essays and letters; he painted and was one of the great calligraphers of his time. Many dishes and
places in China are named after him ({东坡肉|Dōng pō ròu}, Dongpo pork, is the best known).

## 《{题西林壁|Tí Xī lín Bì}》: Written on the wall at Xilin Temple

{苏轼|Sū Shì} wrote this poem in 1084, when he was leaving {黄州|Huáng zhōu} for a new post and travelled by way of {庐山|Lú Shān} (Lú Shān,
Mount Lu, in today's Jiangxi). {西林|Xī lín} is {西林寺|Xī lín sì}, a temple at the foot of the mountain, and {题|tí} is "to write
(a poem) on": poets often wrote on the walls of temples and inns.

> {横|héng}{看|kàn}{成|chéng}{岭|lǐng}{侧|cè}{成|chéng}{峰|fēng}，
>
> {远近|yuǎn jìn}{高低|gāo dī}{各|gè}{不同|bù tóng}。
>
> {不|bù}{识|shí}{庐山|Lú Shān}{真|zhēn}{面目|miàn mù}，
>
> {只|zhǐ}{缘|yuán}{身|shēn}{在|zài}{此|cǐ}{山|shān}{中|zhōng}。

| Word | Meaning |
|---|---|
| {横|héng}{看|kàn} | looked at from the front, along the range |
| {岭|lǐng} lǐng | a ridge, a range |
| {侧|cè} cè | the side (here: from the side, end on) |
| {峰|fēng} fēng | a peak |
| {各|gè}{不同|bù tóng} | each different ({各|gè}, HSK 4) |
| {识|shí} shí | to know, recognise (as in {认识|rèn shi}) |
| {真面目|zhēn miàn mù} | true face, real appearance |
| {只|zhǐ}{缘|yuán} | only because ({缘|yuán}: because of, written) |
| {身|shēn} | oneself (as in {本身|běn shēn}) |
| {此|cǐ} | this (HSK 4's written {此|cǐ}) |

**In modern Chinese**: {从|cóng}{正面|zhèng miàn}{看|kàn}，{庐山|Lú Shān}{是|shì}{一|yí}{道|dào}{长长|cháng cháng}{的|de}{山岭|shān lǐng}；{从|cóng}{侧面|cè miàn}{看|kàn}，{它|tā}{又|yòu}{成|chéng}{了|le}{一|yí}{座|zuò}{高高|gāo gāo}{的|de}{山峰|shān fēng}。{从|cóng}{远|yuǎn}{处|chù}、{近|jìn}{处|chù}、{高|gāo}{处|chù}、{低|dī}{处|chù}{看|kàn}，
{样子|yàng zi}{都|dōu}{不|bù}{一样|yí yàng}。{我们|wǒ men}{之所以|zhī suǒ yǐ}{看不清|kàn bu qīng}{庐山|Lú Shān}{真正|zhēn zhèng}{的|de}{样子|yàng zi}，{只是|zhǐ shì}{因为|yīn wèi}{我们|wǒ men}{自己|zì jǐ}{就|jiù}{在|zài}{这|zhè}{座|zuò}{山|shān}{里|lǐ}。

({正面|zhèng miàn} / {侧面|cè miàn}: the front / the side; {山岭|shān lǐng}: a mountain range; {之所以|zhī suǒ yǐ}…{只是|zhǐ shì}{因为|yīn wèi}…: the reason why… is only that…)

**Our translation**:

> Seen from the front, a range; from the end, a peak;
> far or near, high or low, each view differs.
> I cannot tell the true face of Mount Lu,
> only because I stand inside the mountain.

The last two lines are quoted every day, far from any mountain: when you're inside a situation, you
can't see it whole. {不|bù}{识|shí}{庐山|Lú Shān}{真面目|zhēn miàn mù} on its own means "not to see what something is really like", and
people say {只|zhǐ}{缘|yuán}{身|shēn}{在|zài}{此|cǐ}{山|shān}{中|zhōng} of anyone too close to a problem to judge it. A saying with the same idea is
{当局者迷|dāng jú zhě mí}，{旁观者清|páng guān zhě qīng} (dāng jú zhě mí, páng guān zhě qīng): the player is confused, the onlooker sees clearly.

Pronunciation: the poem is read in modern Mandarin. {不|bù}{识|shí} is bù shí ({识|shí} is second tone, so {不|bù} doesn't
change); {只|zhǐ}{缘|yuán} zhǐ yuán.

## 《{水调歌头|Shuǐ diào gē tóu}》: the closing lines

《{水调歌头|Shuǐ diào gē tóu}》 (Shuǐ diào gē tóu) is the name of a tune; poets wrote words to it. {苏轼|Sū Shì}'s most famous one,
which begins {明月几时有|míng yuè jǐ shí yǒu} (When did the bright moon first appear?), was written at the Mid-Autumn
Festival of 1076, in {密州|Mì zhōu} (Mìzhōu, in today's Shandong). His preface says he drank till dawn and wrote it
thinking of his brother {子由|Zǐ yóu} (Zǐyóu, {苏辙|Sū Zhé}'s other name), whom he hadn't seen for years. These are its
last lines:

> {人|rén}{有|yǒu}{悲欢离合|bēi huān lí hé}，{月|yuè}{有|yǒu}{阴晴圆缺|yīn qíng yuán quē}，{此|cǐ}{事|shì}{古|gǔ}{难|nán}{全|quán}。
>
> {但|dàn}{愿|yuàn}{人|rén}{长久|cháng jiǔ}，{千里|qiān lǐ}{共|gòng}{婵娟|chán juān}。

| Word | Meaning |
|---|---|
| {悲欢离合|bēi huān lí hé} | sorrow and joy, parting and reunion (four contrasts in four characters) |
| {阴晴圆缺|yīn qíng yuán quē} | clouded and clear, full and waning (the moon's changes) |
| {此|cǐ}{事|shì} | this (that both should be perfect at once) |
| {古|gǔ}{难|nán}{全|quán} | has always been hard to make complete ({古|gǔ} = {自|zì}{古|gǔ}, since ancient times) |
| {但|dàn}{愿|yuàn} | I only wish ({但|dàn}: "only", written) |
| {长久|cháng jiǔ} | long-lasting (lesson 11) |
| {千|qiān}{里|lǐ} | a thousand li apart ({里|lǐ} lǐ, an old unit of distance) |
| {共|gòng} | together, to share |
| {婵娟|chán juān} chán juān | (literary) the lovely one: the moon |

**In modern Chinese**: {人|rén}{有|yǒu}{悲伤|bēi shāng}{和|hé}{快乐|kuài lè}，{有|yǒu}{分别|fēn bié}{也|yě}{有|yǒu}{团聚|tuán jù}；{月亮|yuè liang}{有时|yǒu shí}{被|bèi}{云|yún}{挡住|dǎng zhù}，{有时|yǒu shí}{很|hěn}{明亮|míng liàng}，{有时|yǒu shí}{圆|yuán}，{有时|yǒu shí}{缺|quē}。{这样|zhè yàng}{的|de}{事|shì}，{自|zì}{古|gǔ}{以来|yǐ lái}
{就|jiù}{很|hěn}{难|nán}{样样|yàng yàng}{都|dōu}{好|hǎo}。{只|zhǐ}{希望|xī wàng}{我们|wǒ men}{都|dōu}{健健康康|jiàn jiàn kāng kāng}，{活|huó}{得|de}{长长久久|cháng cháng jiǔ jiǔ}，{哪怕|nǎ pà}{相隔|xiāng gé}{千|qiān}{里|lǐ}，{也|yě}{能|néng}{一起|yì qǐ}{欣赏|xīn shǎng}{这|zhè}{美丽|měi lì}{的|de}{月亮|yuè liang}。

({团聚|tuán jù} tuán jù: to be together again; {挡住|dǎng zhù} dǎng zhù: to block, cover; {健健康康|jiàn jiàn kāng kāng}: healthy, {健康|jiàn kāng} repeated; {相隔|xiāng gé} xiāng gé:
to be apart; {欣赏|xīn shǎng} xīn shǎng: to enjoy, lesson 10)

**Our translation**:

> People have sorrow and joy, parting and meeting; the moon is dim or bright, full or on the wane:
> it has never been easy to have it all.
> I only wish us long lives, and though a thousand miles apart, to share this lovely moon.

At Mid-Autumn, when families who can't be together look at the same full moon, {但|dàn}{愿|yuàn}{人|rén}{长久|cháng jiǔ}，{千|qiān}{里|lǐ}{共|gòng}{婵娟|chán juān} is on
cards, in messages and in songs. {悲欢离合|bēi huān lí hé} is used today as an idiom: {人生|rén shēng}{的|de}{悲欢离合|bēi huān lí hé} (the joys and sorrows of
life).

## Reading: why people still quote Su Shi

> {九百|jiǔ bǎi}{多|duō}{年|nián}{过去|guò qù}{了|le}，{苏轼|Sū Shì}{的|de}{很|hěn}{多|duō}{诗|shī}{句|jù}{今天|jīn tiān}{的|de}{中国|Zhōng guó}{人|rén}{还|hái}{常常|cháng cháng}{说|shuō}。{为什么|wèi shén me}{他|tā}{的|de}{诗|shī}{这么|zhè me}{受|shòu}{欢迎|huān yíng}{呢|ne}？
>
> {第|dì}{一|yī}，{他|tā}{的|de}{诗|shī}{很|hěn}{好|hǎo}{懂|dǒng}。《{题西林壁|Tí Xī lín Bì}》{只有|zhǐ yǒu}{二十八|èr shí bā}{个|gè}{字|zì}，{用|yòng}{的|de}{都|dōu}{是|shì}{简单|jiǎn dān}{的|de}{字|zì}，{可是|kě shì}{说|shuō}{出|chū}{了|le}{一|yí}{个|gè}{深刻|shēn kè}{的|de}{道理|dào li}：{看|kàn}{问题|wèn tí}{的|de}{时候|shí hou}，
> {站|zhàn}{的|de}{位置|wèi zhì}{不同|bù tóng}，{看|kàn}{到|dào}{的|de}{样子|yàng zi}{也|yě}{不同|bù tóng}；{一|yí}{个|gè}{人|rén}{在|zài}{事情|shì qing}{中间|zhōng jiān}{的|de}{时候|shí hou}，{常常|cháng cháng}{看不清楚|kàn bu qīng chu}{事情|shì qing}{的|de}{全部|quán bù}。{这|zhè}{首|shǒu}{诗|shī}{很|hěn}{多|duō}{孩子|hái zi}{在|zài}{小学|xiǎo xué}{就|jiù}{学|xué}{过|guo}{了|le}。{今天|jīn tiān}，{学生|xué sheng}{写|xiě}{作文|zuò wén}、{老师|lǎo shī}{上课|shàng kè}、
> {领导|lǐng dǎo}{讲话|jiǎng huà}，{都|dōu}{会|huì}{用|yòng}{到|dào}“{不|bù}{识|shí}{庐山|Lú Shān}{真面目|zhēn miàn mù}，{只|zhǐ}{缘|yuán}{身|shēn}{在|zài}{此|cǐ}{山|shān}{中|zhōng}”。
>
> {第|dì}{二|èr}，{他|tā}{的|de}{诗|shī}{里|lǐ}{有|yǒu}{真实|zhēn shí}{的|de}{感情|gǎn qíng}。{写|xiě}《{水调歌头|Shuǐ diào gē tóu}》{的|de}{时候|shí hou}，{他|tā}{已经|yǐ jīng}{好|hǎo}{几|jǐ}{年|nián}{没|méi}{见|jiàn}{到|dào}{弟弟|dì di}{了|le}。{中秋节|zhōng qiū jié}{本来|běn lái}{是|shì}{家人|jiā rén}{团圆|tuán yuán}{的|de}{日子|rì zi}，{他|tā}{却|què}
> {不|bù}{能|néng}{和|hé}{弟弟|dì di}{一起|yì qǐ}{看|kàn}{月亮|yuè liang}。{可是|kě shì}{他|tā}{没有|méi yǒu}{一直|yì zhí}{难过|nán guò}{下去|xià qù}，{而|ér}{是|shì}{想|xiǎng}{到|dào}：{人|rén}{有|yǒu}{分别|fēn bié}，{月|yuè}{有|yǒu}{圆|yuán}{缺|quē}，{这|zhè}{是|shì}{自|zì}{古|gǔ}{就|jiù}{有|yǒu}{的|de}{事|shì}。{只要|zhǐ yào}{大家|dà jiā}{都|dōu}{平平安安|píng píng ān ān}，
> {哪怕|nǎ pà}{离|lí}{得|de}{很|hěn}{远|yuǎn}，{也|yě}{能|néng}{看|kàn}{着|zhe}{同一|tóng yī}{个|gè}{月亮|yuè liang}。{这|zhè}{种|zhǒng}{乐观|lè guān}{的|de}{心态|xīn tài}，{让|ràng}{很|hěn}{多|duō}{离开|lí kāi}{家|jiā}{的|de}{人|rén}{感到|gǎn dào}{安慰|ān wèi}。
>
> {第|dì}{三|sān}，{他|tā}{自己|zì jǐ}{的|de}{生活|shēng huó}{就是|jiù shì}{一|yí}{个|gè}{故事|gù shi}。{他|tā}{曾经|céng jīng}{是|shì}{很|hěn}{有名|yǒu míng}{的|de}{官员|guān yuán}，{后来|hòu lái}{又|yòu}{多|duō}{次|cì}{被|bèi}{派|pài}{到|dào}{很|hěn}{远|yuǎn}{的|de}{地方|dì fang}。{条件|tiáo jiàn}{最|zuì}{艰苦|jiān kǔ}{的|de}{时候|shí hou}，{他|tā}{在|zài}{黄州|Huáng zhōu}

Words to know: {深刻|shēn kè} (shēn kè, profound, lesson 26), {作文|zuò wén} (zuò wén, a school essay, HSK 4), {团圆|tuán yuán} (tuán yuán,
reunion), {却|què} (què, but, HSK 4), {平平安安|píng píng ān ān} (safe and well: {平安|píng ān} repeated, lesson 25), {安慰|ān wèi} (ān wèi, comfort,
lesson 14), {官员|guān yuán} (guān yuán, official, HSK 6), {亲切|qīn qiè} (qīn qiè, warm, lesson 15), {种地|zhòng dì} (zhòng dì, to farm), {研究|yán jiū} (yán jiū, to study, HSK 4),
{乐趣|lè qù} (lè qù, pleasure, lesson 10), {面对|miàn duì} (miàn duì, to face, HSK 4), {分别|fēn bié} (fēn bié, to part, lesson 11).

<details>
<summary>Translation</summary>

"More than nine hundred years have passed, and Chinese people today still often quote Su Shi's lines.
Why are his poems so popular? First, his poems are easy to understand. 'Written on the wall at Xilin
Temple' has only twenty-eight characters, all simple ones (many children learn it at primary school), yet it expresses a profound truth: when you
look at a problem, where you stand changes what you see, and when you're in the middle of something,
you often can't see the whole of it. Today students writing essays, teachers in class and leaders
giving speeches all use 'I cannot tell the true face of Mount Lu, only because I stand inside the
mountain'. Second, his poems have real feeling in them. When he wrote 'Shui diao ge tou', he hadn't
seen his brother for several years. Mid-Autumn is meant to be a day of family reunion, but he couldn't
watch the moon with his brother. Yet he didn't stay sad: he thought that people part and the moon waxes
and wanes, as they always have; as long as everyone is safe and well, however far apart, they can look
at the same moon. This optimistic attitude has comforted many people far from home. Third, his own
life is a story. He was once a famous official, and later he was sent far away again and again. When
conditions were hardest, in Huangzhou, he farmed the land himself and worked out how to cook. But
whatever the difficulty, he could find pleasure in life and write good poems. Fourth, he knew how to live. He loved cooking, and drinking tea and chatting with
friends. Many of his essays are about the small things of life: a meal, a trip, a friend. Reading
them, you feel he isn't someone from nine hundred years ago but an old friend who lives next door.
So Chinese people today, when they mention him, often call him warmly 'Dongpo'. So many people say that
reading Su Shi is not just reading poetry but learning how to face life."
</details>

## Key points

- {苏轼|Sū Shì} ({苏东坡|Sū Dōng pō}, 1037–1101): Northern Song poet, writer of song lyrics, essayist, calligrapher, official.
- 《{题西林壁|Tí Xī lín Bì}》 (1084): {横|héng}{看|kàn}{成|chéng}{岭|lǐng}{侧|cè}{成|chéng}{峰|fēng}，{远|yuǎn}{近|jìn}{高|gāo}{低|dī}{各|gè}{不同|bù tóng}。{不|bù}{识|shí}{庐山|Lú Shān}{真面目|zhēn miàn mù}，{只|zhǐ}{缘|yuán}{身|shēn}{在|zài}{此|cǐ}{山|shān}{中|zhōng}。: you can't see a thing whole
  from inside it.
- 《{水调歌头|Shuǐ diào gē tóu}》 (Mid-Autumn 1076): {人|rén}{有|yǒu}{悲欢离合|bēi huān lí hé}，{月|yuè}{有|yǒu}{阴晴圆缺|yīn qíng yuán quē}，{此|cǐ}{事|shì}{古|gǔ}{难|nán}{全|quán}。{但|dàn}{愿|yuàn}{人|rén}{长久|cháng jiǔ}，{千|qiān}{里|lǐ}{共|gòng}{婵娟|chán juān}。
- Classical words: {识|shí} (= {认识|rèn shi}), {缘|yuán} (because), {此|cǐ} (this), {但|dàn} (only), {共|gòng} (together), {古|gǔ} (= {自|zì}{古|gǔ}).

lessons.title: The first paper money
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

Lesson 04 talked about cost, trade and money. This honors lesson goes back about a thousand years, to
the place where, as far as historians know, a government first issued paper money: Sichuan, in the
Northern Song. The notes were called {交子|jiāo zǐ} (jiāo zǐ). The story uses this module's words ({商人|shāng rén}, {交易|jiāo yì}, {信用|xìn yòng},
{风险|fēng xiǎn}, {机构|jī gòu}) and is told as economic history: what happened and how it worked.

## Why paper, and why Sichuan?

In the Song dynasty most of China paid with copper coins ({铜钱|tóng qián} tóng qián). In Sichuan, then a busy
trading region, the coins in everyday use were mostly *iron* ({铁钱|tiě qián} tiě qián). Iron coins were worth
much less than copper ones, so the same price needed many more of them, and they were heavy: a large
deal meant carrying a great weight of metal. Merchants needed something lighter.

The answer came from the merchants themselves. Toward the end of the tenth century, merchants in {成都|Chéng dū}
(Chéngdū, then called {益州|Yì zhōu} Yìzhōu) began to take in customers' iron coins and give them a paper receipt.
The receipt could be handed on in trade and changed back into coins. These private notes were the
first {交子|jiāo zǐ}. The name's origin is explained in more than one way; its {交|jiāo} is the {交|jiāo} of {交易|jiāo yì} and {交换|jiāo huàn} (to
exchange, lesson 15).

## From private notes to government money

Private notes depend on trust ({信用|xìn yòng}). When an issuer couldn't pay out, people who held its notes lost
their money, and disputes followed. The government stepped in. At the end of 1023 by the Chinese
calendar (early 1024 by ours), the court approved an official office in {益州|Yì zhōu} to issue {交子|jiāo zǐ}, the {益州交子务|Yì zhōu jiāo zǐ wù}
(the Yizhou jiaozi office), and the first official notes appeared in 1024. Historians often call them
the world's first paper money issued by a government.

| Before | After |
|---|---|
| issued by merchants ({民间交子|mín jiān jiāo zǐ}) | issued by a government office ({官交子|guān jiāo zǐ}) |
| trust in one issuer | backed by the state, with reserves of coin |
| local, private | official, used for a fixed term, then renewed |

Each issue of official notes could be used only for a fixed term (two years at first, by one account), after
which old notes were changed for new ones. Later Song
paper money ({会子|huì zǐ} huì zǐ) and the paper money of the Yuan dynasty grew from the same idea.

## Words for money, old and new

| Word | Meaning |
|---|---|
| {纸币|zhǐ bì} zhǐ bì | paper money, banknote ({纸|zhǐ} + {币|bì}: lesson 04's {币|bì}) |
| {铜钱|tóng qián} / {铁钱|tiě qián} | copper coins / iron coins |
| {发行|fā xíng} fā xíng | to issue (money, stamps, a book: HSK 6) |
| {信用|xìn yòng} | trust, credit (lesson 04) |
| {兑换|duì huàn} duì huàn | to change, exchange (money) |
| {机构|jī gòu} | institution, office (lesson 02) |
| {印刷|yìn shuā} yìn shuā | to print (lesson 24) |

## Reading: a note from a thousand years ago

> {交子|jiāo zǐ}{的|de}{出现|chū xiàn}，{说明|shuō míng}{当时|dāng shí}{的|de}{商业|shāng yè}{已经|yǐ jīng}{很|hěn}{发达|fā dá}，{人们|rén men}{需要|xū yào}{一|yì}{种|zhǒng}{又|yòu}{轻|qīng}{又|yòu}{方便|fāng biàn}{的|de}{钱|qián}。{可见|kě jiàn}，{纸币|zhǐ bì}{不|bú}{是|shì}{谁|shéi}{一下子|yí xià zi}{想|xiǎng}{出来|chū lái}{的|de}，{而|ér}{是|shì}{在|zài}{交易|jiāo yì}{中|zhōng}
> {慢慢|màn màn}{产生|chǎn shēng}{的|de}。

dì, local, lesson 21), {值钱|zhí qián} (zhí qián, valuable), {一|yì}{匹|pǐ}{布|bù} (yì pǐ bù, a bolt of cloth: {匹|pǐ}, lesson 10), {力气|lì qi}
(lì qi, effort, HSK 4), {官府|guān fǔ} (guān fǔ, the authorities, in old China), {从此|cóng cǐ} (cóng cǐ, from then on, HSK 4),
{产生|chǎn shēng} (chǎn shēng, to come into being, HSK 4).

<details>
<summary>Translation</summary>

"Today we often pay for things by phone and rarely carry cash. But did you know that the world's
first paper money issued by a government appeared a thousand years ago in Sichuan, China? In the
Northern Song, trade in Sichuan was well developed: there were many merchants, and deals were on a
large scale. But the money used there was mainly iron coins. Iron coins were not only heavy but worth
little: to buy a bolt of cloth you had to carry a great many of them, which was very inconvenient.
And if you met robbers on the road, the risk was great too. To save effort, some merchants in Chengdu
came up with a plan: customers left their iron coins with them, and they gave the customer a piece
of paper with the sum written on it. With this paper you could go and buy things, or change it back
into iron coins. This paper was called jiaozi. Jiaozi grew more and more popular, but problems
appeared too. Some merchants issued too many and in the end couldn't pay everyone back. People holding
jiaozi lost money and went to the authorities. To solve the problem, the government decided to issue
jiaozi itself. In 1024 an office the government had set up in Yizhou began issuing official jiaozi.
From then on, jiaozi had the state's credit behind them, and people used them with more confidence.
Official jiaozi had a period of use: a batch lasted about two years, and when it expired it had to be
changed for new notes. For the government, issuing jiaozi had advantages too: they were light and easy
to transport, and when notes were renewed the government could collect a small fee. But if too many
were issued, jiaozi would lose their value, and people would stop trusting them again. So the government set the amount of each batch. The appearance of jiaozi shows that trade was already highly developed and people needed a light,
convenient kind of money. Clearly, then, paper money wasn't suddenly thought up by somebody: it grew
slowly out of trade. If you travel to Chengdu, you can visit a museum there and learn more about the
story of jiaozi."
</details>

## Key points

- {交子|jiāo zǐ}: paper notes of the Northern Song, first issued privately by merchants in {成都|Chéng dū} ({益州|Yì zhōu}), where heavy
  iron coins ({铁钱|tiě qián}) made trade hard.
- At the end of 1023 (Chinese calendar; early 1024) the court approved the {益州交子务|Yì zhōu jiāo zǐ wù}, and official {交子|jiāo zǐ}
  were issued in 1024: often called the world's first government-issued paper money.
- Words: {纸币|zhǐ bì}, {发行|fā xíng}, {信用|xìn yòng}, {兑换|duì huàn}, {铜钱|tóng qián} / {铁钱|tiě qián}; and from the module: {商人|shāng rén}, {交易|jiāo yì}, {规模|guī mó}, {风险|fēng xiǎn}, {机构|jī gòu}, {设立|shè lì}, {亏|kuī}, {没法儿|méi fǎr}.

lessons.title: Busy lives: sleep, stress and leisure
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

Module 2 is about how people live: sleep and stress, food, health, the home and free time. This
first lesson is about busy lives. {王芳|Wáng Fāng} (Wang Fang) is a reporter now, and reporters keep late
hours; {安娜|Ān nà} (Anna), in her last year, shares the flat with her and has opinions about sleep.

The grammar is about how a speaker sees things:

- {似乎|sì hū}, {仿佛|fǎng fú} and {好像|hǎo xiàng}…{似的|shì de}: it seems, as if;
- {反正|fǎn zhèng}: anyway, whatever happens;
- {刚好|gāng hǎo}: just right, as it happens;
- {从不|cóng bù} and {从|cóng}{没|méi}: never;
- {看|kàn}{了|le}{一|yì}{眼|yǎn}: {眼|yǎn} as a measure word for looks;
- the **[[state complement]]**: {累|lèi}{得|de}{站不起来|zhàn bu qǐ lái} (so tired one can't stand up).

You also get the words for the body, strength and movement, and for sleep, stress and leisure. The
reading is a short article on young people's sleep, and the speaking task asks your opinion.

## {似乎|sì hū}, {仿佛|fǎng fú} and {好像|hǎo xiàng}…{似的|shì de}: it seems, as if

You know {好像|hǎo xiàng} (it seems; to be like) from HSK 3. HSK 5 adds two more formal partners and the particle
{似的|shì de}. They are **[[adverbs of mood]]**: they tell you how sure the speaker is, or how the speaker sees
what's described, not what happened.

| Word | Register | Use | Example |
|---|---|---|---|
| {好像|hǎo xiàng} | spoken and written | it seems; as if | {他|tā}{好像|hǎo xiàng}{病|bìng}{了|le}。 He seems to be ill. |
| {似乎|sì hū} | more formal, written | it seems (a guess from what you can see) | {他|tā}{似乎|sì hū}{不|bú}{太|tài}{高兴|gāo xìng}。 He doesn't seem very happy. |
| {仿佛|fǎng fú} | literary, written | as if (often something that isn't really so) | {那|nà}{天|tiān}{的|de}{事|shì}{仿佛|fǎng fú}{就|jiù}{在|zài}{昨天|zuó tiān}。 That day feels as if it were yesterday. |
| …{似的|shì de} | spoken and written | closes an "as if" phrase | {他|tā}{累|lèi}{得|de}{像|xiàng}{三|sān}{天|tiān}{没|méi}{睡|shuì}{似的|shì de}。 He's so tired it's as if he hadn't slept for three days. |

{似乎|sì hū} makes a careful guess. The speaker has seen something and draws a conclusion, but softly:

{王芳|Wáng Fāng}{最近|zuì jìn}{似乎|sì hū}{很|hěn}{忙|máng}，{周末|zhōu mò}{也|yě}{不|bù}{休息|xiū xi}。 — Wang Fang seems to have been very busy lately; she doesn't even rest at weekends.

{大家|dà jiā}{似乎|sì hū}{都|dōu}{同意|tóng yì}{这个|zhè ge}{办法|bàn fǎ}。 — Everyone seems to agree with this plan.

{仿佛|fǎng fú} compares what happens with something else, often something unreal. It belongs to stories,
descriptions and essays:

{他|tā}{站|zhàn}{在|zài}{那儿|nàr}{一|yí}{动|dòng}{不|bú}{动|dòng}，{仿佛|fǎng fú}{没|méi}{听见|tīng jiàn}{我|wǒ}{的话|de huà}。 — He stood there without moving, as if he hadn't heard me.

{似的|shì de} (said *shì de*, not *sì de*) closes the comparison, the way "as if… did" closes it in
English. It goes at the end of the phrase, and the phrase is opened by {像|xiàng}, {好像|hǎo xiàng} or {仿佛|fǎng fú}:

{她|tā}{高兴|gāo xìng}{得|de}{像|xiàng}{个|gè}{孩子|hái zi}{似的|shì de}。 — She was as happy as a child.

{他|tā}{好像|hǎo xiàng}{什么|shén me}{都|dōu}{知道|zhī dào}{似的|shì de}。 — He acts as if he knows everything.

{我|wǒ}{一|yì}{闲|xián}{下来|xià lái}，{就|jiù}{仿佛|fǎng fú}{有|yǒu}{很|hěn}{多|duō}{事|shì}{没|méi}{做|zuò}{完|wán}{似的|shì de}。 — As soon as I have nothing to do, it's as if I've left lots of things unfinished.

{似的|shì de} can also follow a noun or phrase with nothing before it, in speech: {他|tā}{跑|pǎo}{得|de}{飞|fēi}{快|kuài}，{跟|gēn}{风|fēng}{似的|shì de} (he ran as
fast as the wind). The spoken equivalent of {似的|shì de} is {一样|yí yàng}: {像|xiàng}{孩子|hái zi}{一样|yí yàng}, {像|xiàng}{孩子|hái zi}{似的|shì de}.

Two things to keep apart. {似乎|sì hū} is a guess about a fact ("it seems that…"), so it seldom takes {似的|shì de}.
{仿佛|fǎng fú} and {好像|hǎo xiàng}…{似的|shì de} are comparisons ("as if…"), and they often say something the speaker knows
isn't true: {他|tā}{仿佛|fǎng fú}{三|sān}{天|tiān}{没|méi}{睡|shuì}{似的|shì de} doesn't claim he really missed three nights' sleep.

## The state complement: {累|lèi}{得|de}{站不起来|zhàn bu qǐ lái}

HSK 2 and 3 taught the degree complement, which judges how an action is done: {她|tā}{说|shuō}{得|de}{很|hěn}{好|hǎo} (she speaks
well). HSK 5 adds the **[[state complement]]**. After {得|de} comes not a judgement but the state that the
action or feeling leads to, often a whole phrase:

| Pattern | Example | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| verb / adjective + {得|de} + verb phrase | {我|wǒ}{累|lèi}{得|de}{不|bù}{想|xiǎng}{说话|shuō huà}。 | I'm so tired I don't want to talk. |
| | {她|tā}{高兴|gāo xìng}{得|de}{跳|tiào}{了|le}{起来|qǐ lái}。 | She was so happy she jumped up. |
| verb / adjective + {得|de} + a clause with its own subject | {他|tā}{说|shuō}{得|de}{大家|dà jiā}{都|dōu}{笑|xiào}{了|le}。 | He spoke so (funnily) that everyone laughed. |
| | {音乐|yīn yuè}{声|shēng}{大|dà}{得|de}{我|wǒ}{睡不着|shuì bu zháo}。 | The music was so loud I couldn't sleep. |
| adjective + {得|de} + {像|xiàng}…{似的|shì de} | {她|tā}{忙|máng}{得|de}{像|xiàng}{个|gè}{陀螺|tuó luó}{似的|shì de}。 | She was as busy as a spinning top. ({陀螺|tuó luó} tuóluó: a top) |

English often uses "so… that…" for these. The state can be anything the first part leads to:

{王芳|Wáng Fāng}{忙|máng}{得|de}{连|lián}{吃|chī}{饭|fàn}{的|de}{时间|shí jiān}{都|dōu}{没有|méi yǒu}。 — Wang Fang is so busy she doesn't even have time to eat.

{跑|pǎo}{完|wán}{步|bù}，{他|tā}{累|lèi}{得|de}{站不起来|zhàn bu qǐ lái}{了|le}。 — After the run he was so tired he couldn't get up.

{天|tiān}{太|tài}{热|rè}，{我们|wǒ men}{热|rè}{得|de}{出|chū}{了|le}{一|yì}{身|shēn}{汗|hàn}。 — It was so hot that we were dripping with sweat.

The negative goes inside the state, not before {得|de}: {我|wǒ}{累|lèi}{得|de}{不|bù}{想|xiǎng}{吃|chī}{饭|fàn} (so tired I don't want to eat).
Lesson 07 adds the strongest state of all, {得|de}{不得了|bù dé liǎo} ({好吃|hǎo chī}{得|de}{不得了|bù dé liǎo}: delicious beyond words), and the
reference sheet on complements has all the complements of levels 1–5.

## {反正|fǎn zhèng}: anyway, whatever happens

{反正|fǎn zhèng} says that a conclusion holds whatever else is true. It often gives the reason that makes the
rest not matter, and it can stand before or after the subject:

{反正|fǎn zhèng}{明天|míng tiān}{不|bú}{上班|shàng bān}，{今天|jīn tiān}{晚|wǎn}{一点儿|yì diǎnr}{睡|shuì}{也|yě}{没关系|méi guān xi}。 — I'm not working tomorrow anyway, so it doesn't matter if I go to bed a bit later tonight.

{你|nǐ}{去|qù}{不|bu}{去|qù}{都|dōu}{行|xíng}，{反正|fǎn zhèng}{我|wǒ}{是|shì}{要|yào}{去|qù}{的|de}。 — Whether you go or not is up to you: I'm going anyway.

{我们|wǒ men}{打车|dǎ chē}{去|qù}{吧|ba}，{反正|fǎn zhèng}{也|yě}{不|bù}{远|yuǎn}。 — Let's take a taxi: it isn't far anyway.

After a list of possibilities, {反正|fǎn zhèng} sums up: "whichever it is…": {不管|bù guǎn}{是|shì}{今天|jīn tiān}{还是|hái shi}{明天|míng tiān}，{反正|fǎn zhèng}{这个|zhè ge}{星期|xīng qī}{要|yào}{做|zuò}{完|wán} (today
or tomorrow, either way it must be done this week). {不管|bù guǎn}…{反正|fǎn zhèng} goes well together. {反正|fǎn zhèng} is mostly spoken.

## {刚好|gāng hǎo}: just right, as it happens

{刚好|gāng hǎo} has two uses. As an adjective it means "just right, exactly enough":

{这|zhè}{双|shuāng}{鞋|xié}{不|bú}{大|dà}{不|bù}{小|xiǎo}，{刚好|gāng hǎo}。 — These shoes are neither too big nor too small: just right.

As an adverb, before a verb, it means "it happened that, by luck":

{我|wǒ}{去|qù}{找|zhǎo}{他|tā}{的|de}{时候|shí hou}，{他|tā}{刚好|gāng hǎo}{在|zài}{家|jiā}。 — When I went to see him, he happened to be in.

{你|nǐ}{要|yào}{去|qù}{超市|chāo shì}{吗|ma}？{我|wǒ}{刚好|gāng hǎo}{也|yě}{要|yào}{去|qù}，{一起|yì qǐ}{走|zǒu}{吧|ba}。 — You're going to the supermarket? I'm going too, as it happens: let's go together.

{刚好|gāng hǎo} and HSK 4's {正好|zhèng hǎo} mean the same and are equally common. Don't confuse either with {刚|gāng} (just now):
{他|tā}{刚|gāng}{走|zǒu} is "he has just left".

## {从不|cóng bù} and {从|cóng}{没|méi}: never

{从|cóng} + a negative means "never". The negative decides what kind of "never":

| Form | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| {从不|cóng bù} + verb | never (a habit, a rule) | {他|tā}{从不|cóng bù}{抽|chōu}{烟|yān}。 He never smokes. |
| {从|cóng}{没|méi}({有|yǒu}) + verb + {过|guo} | never (in one's experience, up to now) | {我|wǒ}{从|cóng}{没|méi}{去|qù}{过|guo}{酒吧|jiǔ bā}。 I've never been to a bar. |

{从不|cóng bù} is the compact form of {从来|cóng lái}{不|bù} (HSK 4), a little more written. {从不|cóng bù} never takes {过|guo}, and {从|cóng}{没|méi} nearly always
does: not ~~{我|wǒ}{从不|cóng bú}{去|qù}{过|guo}~~. Compare:

{我|wǒ}{从不|cóng bù}{熬夜|áo yè}。 — I never stay up late. (it's my rule)

{我|wǒ}{从|cóng}{没|méi}{熬|áo}{过|guo}{夜|yè}。 — I've never stayed up all night. (it's never happened)

## {眼|yǎn}: a look, a glance

As a noun, {眼|yǎn} is "eye" (a little more written than {眼睛|yǎn jing}). After a number it is a measure word for
looks, like {次|cì} for times:

{他|tā}{看|kàn}{了|le}{我|wǒ}{一|yì}{眼|yǎn}。 — He glanced at me.

{我|wǒ}{回|huí}{头|tóu}{看|kàn}{了|le}{一|yì}{眼|yǎn}，{没有|méi yǒu}{人|rén}。 — I looked back: there was nobody.

{这么|zhè me}{好看|hǎo kàn}{的|de}{照片|zhào piàn}，{大家|dà jiā}{都|dōu}{多|duō}{看|kàn}{了|le}{几|jǐ}{眼|yǎn}。 — Such a good photo: everyone took a second look.

A pronoun object goes before {一|yì}{眼|yǎn}: {看|kàn}{了|le}{我|wǒ}{一|yì}{眼|yǎn}, {看|kàn}{了|le}{他|tā}{一|yì}{眼|yǎn}. A noun object can go either side: {看|kàn}{了|le}{一|yì}{眼|yǎn}{手机|shǒu jī}, {看|kàn}{了|le}{手机|shǒu jī}{一|yì}{眼|yǎn}
(both "glanced at the phone").

## Words: the body, strength and movement

The body. {人体|rén tǐ} is the human body as a subject of study ({人体|rén tǐ}{的|de}{肌肉|jī ròu}, the body's muscles);
{身材|shēn cái} is someone's figure or build ({她|tā}{身材|shēn cái}{很|hěn}{好|hǎo}).

| Word | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| {肌肉|jī ròu} | muscle | {多|duō}{运动|yùn dòng}，{可以|kě yǐ}{增强|zēng qiáng}{肌肉|jī ròu}{的|de}{力量|lì liang}。 Exercise makes your muscles stronger. |
| {腰|yāo} | waist; the lower back | {坐|zuò}{久|jiǔ}{了|le}，{腰|yāo}{会|huì}{疼|téng}。 Sit too long and your back aches. |
| {手指|shǒu zhǐ} | finger | {他|tā}{用|yòng}{手指|shǒu zhǐ}{在|zài}{桌子|zhuō zi}{上|shàng}{写|xiě}{了|le}{一|yí}{个|gè}{字|zì}。 He wrote a character on the table with his finger. |
| {嘴巴|zuǐ ba} | mouth (spoken) | {孩子|hái zi}{张|zhāng}{开|kāi}{嘴巴|zuǐ ba}{笑|xiào}{了|le}。 The child opened their mouth and laughed. |
| {汗水|hàn shuǐ} | sweat (written) | {跑|pǎo}{完|wán}{步|bù}，{他|tā}{的|de}{衣服|yī fu}{上|shàng}{都|dōu}{是|shì}{汗水|hàn shuǐ}。 After the run his clothes were wet with sweat. |
| {脚步|jiǎo bù} | footstep(s) | {我|wǒ}{听见|tīng jiàn}{门|mén}{外|wài}{有|yǒu}{脚步|jiǎo bù}{声|shēng}。 I heard footsteps outside the door. |

Strength. {力|lì} is force or strength on its own, mostly in set phrases ({用力|yòng lì}, {有|yǒu}{力气|lì qi}); {力量|lì liang} is strength or
power in general, of the body or of people together; {体力|tǐ lì} is physical strength, stamina. {用力|yòng lì} is "to use
strength, push hard".

{他|tā}{很|hěn}{有|yǒu}{力量|lì liang}，{一|yí}{个|gè}{人|rén}{就|jiù}{能|néng}{搬|bān}{动|dòng}{这|zhè}{张|zhāng}{桌子|zhuō zi}。 — He's very strong: he can move this table on his own.

{爬|pá}{了|le}{一|yì}{天|tiān}{山|shān}，{大家|dà jiā}{的|de}{体力|tǐ lì}{都|dōu}{用|yòng}{完|wán}{了|le}。 — After a whole day's climbing, everyone's stamina had run out.

{别|bié}{太|tài}{用力|yòng lì}，{门|mén}{一|yì}{推|tuī}{就|jiù}{开|kāi}。 — Don't push too hard: the door opens with a little push.

{弱|ruò} is weak (opposite {强|qiáng}): {他|tā}{小时候|xiǎo shí hou}{身体|shēn tǐ}{很|hěn}{弱|ruò} (he was frail as a child). {紧|jǐn} is tight or tense: {这|zhè}{双|shuāng}{鞋|xié}{有点儿|yǒu diǎnr}{紧|jǐn}
(these shoes are a bit tight); {时间|shí jiān}{很|hěn}{紧|jǐn} (time is tight).

Moving. {伸|shēn} is to stretch out (a hand, an arm); {伸一伸|shēn yi shēn} is a quick stretch. {姿势|zī shì} is posture or the way
you hold yourself. {平衡|píng héng} is balance, or balanced:

{坐|zuò}{了|le}{两|liǎng}{个|gè}{小时|xiǎo shí}，{站|zhàn}{起来|qǐ lái}{伸一伸|shēn yi shēn}{腰|yāo}{吧|ba}。 — You've been sitting for two hours: get up and stretch your back.

{写|xiě}{字|zì}{的|de}{时候|shí hou}，{姿势|zī shì}{要|yào}{对|duì}。 — Hold yourself properly when you write.

{他|tā}{一|yì}{只|zhī}{脚|jiǎo}{站|zhàn}{着|zhe}，{很|hěn}{难|nán}{保持|bǎo chí}{平衡|píng héng}。 — He was standing on one foot and could hardly keep his balance.

{工作|gōng zuò}{和|hé}{生活|shēng huó}{要|yào}{平衡|píng héng}。 — Work and life should be in balance.

{呼吸|hū xī} is to breathe, or breathing: {深|shēn}{呼吸|hū xī} is a deep breath.

### A new radical: {行|xíng} "go, road"

{衡|héng} is the first character whose radical is {行|xíng} (xíng, to go; first a drawing of a crossroads). The
radical is split in two: 彳 on the left and 亍 on the right, and the rest goes in the middle. You
already write two of the three characters of levels 1–5 that have it: {行|xíng} itself and {街|jiē} (street, with
圭 in the middle). In {衡|héng} the middle is {角|jiǎo} over {大|dà}.

### Sound parts and families

- {申|shēn} shēn sounds in {伸|shēn} shēn (stretch) and {神|shén} shén (spirit), as it does in {申请|shēn qǐng} (shēnqǐng, to apply).
- {要|yào} yào in {腰|yāo} yāo (waist): flesh ⺼ + {要|yào}, a close sound.
- {方|fāng} fāng in {仿|fǎng} fǎng; 弗 fú in {佛|fú} fú; {民|mín} mín in {眠|mián} mián ({目|mù} eye + {民|mín}).
- {由|yóu} yóu in {抽|chōu} chōu: the sound has drifted (compare {油|yóu} yóu, {邮|yóu} yóu, where it hasn't).
- {空|kōng} kōng in {控|kòng} kòng (hand 扌 + {空|kōng}); {几|jǐ} jǐ in {肌|jī} jī.
- 艮 is the radical of {良|liáng} liáng; you'll see {良|liáng} again as a sound part in {粮|liáng} (grain, lesson 08) and {娘|niáng} (in
  {新娘|xīn niáng}, the bride, lesson 12).
- ⺼ "flesh" (the {月|yuè} of the body) makes a family: {肌|jī} {腰|yāo} {胖|pàng} {脚|jiǎo} {脸|liǎn} {脑|nǎo} {肚|dù}, all body words.
- 扌 "hand": {抽|chōu} {控|kòng}, with {推|tuī} {拉|lā} {挂|guà} {打|dǎ} from earlier levels.

### Look-alikes and stroke traps

- {似|sì} sì and {以|yǐ} yǐ: {似|sì} is 亻 + {以|yǐ}. Keep the sound in mind: {似乎|sì hū} sì hū, but {似的|shì de} shì de.
- {弱|ruò}: two identical halves, each 弓 with two short strokes inside (a dot and a rising stroke). Write
  the left half completely, then the right.
- {衡|héng}: 彳 first, then the middle ({角|jiǎo}, then {大|dà}), then 亍 last, as in {街|jiē}.
- {熬|áo}: 敖 on top ({土|tǔ} and {方|fāng} on the left, 攵 on the right), then the four dots of 灬.
- {显|xiǎn}: {日|rì} on top, then {业|yè} below (the two short verticals, the dot and the left-falling stroke, then the
  long horizontal).
- {享|xiǎng} and 亨 differ by one stroke at the bottom: {享|xiǎng} ends in {子|zi}.

to relieve. So how can you sleep well? First, go to bed and get up at fixed times every day, and
don't let the weekend differ too much. Second, don't look at your phone for an hour before bed,
because its light stimulates the eyes and makes it harder to fall asleep. Third, take more exercise
in the day: it builds up your stamina, and you'll fall asleep more easily at night. Fourth, don't
drink too much coffee or tea in the evening. If you still can't sleep after lying down for half an
hour, don't worry: get up, read for a while, and go back when you feel sleepy.

Of course, leisure and entertainment matter too. In a busy life, people need to enjoy their own
time. The point is to keep the time under control and not overdo it. Only with good habits can
you be in good shape, and work and live better."
</details>

## Speaking: your opinion

The speaking test ends with opinion questions (two, as reported, with a few minutes to prepare).
Give your view, a reason or two, an example, and a conclusion. Try this one aloud for about a minute
and a half: {你|nǐ}{觉得|jué de}{年轻|nián qīng}{人|rén}{熬夜|áo yè}{是|shì}{一|yí}{个|gè}{大|dà}{问题|wèn tí}{吗|ma}？{为什么|wèi shén me}？

<details>
<summary>A model answer</summary>

{我|wǒ}{觉得|jué de}{熬夜|áo yè}{是|shì}{一|yí}{个|gè}{问题|wèn tí}，{但是|dàn shì}{不|bù}{能|néng}{都|dōu}{说|shuō}{是|shì}{年轻|nián qīng}{人|rén}{的|de}{错|cuò}。{第|dì}{一|yī}，{现在|xiàn zài}{的|de}{工作|gōng zuò}{和|hé}{学习|xué xí}{压力|yā lì}{很|hěn}{大|dà}，{很|hěn}{多|duō}{人|rén}{白天|bái tiān}{太|tài}{忙碌|máng lù}，{晚上|wǎn shang}{才|cái}{有|yǒu}{一点儿|yì diǎnr}{自己|zì jǐ}{的|de}{时间|shí jiān}。{第|dì}{二|èr}，{手机|shǒu jī}{上|shàng}{的|de}{娱乐|yú lè}{太|tài}{多|duō}{了|le}，{一|yí}{看|kàn}{就是|jiù shì}{一两|yì liǎng}{个|gè}{小时|xiǎo shí}。{我|wǒ}{自己|zì jǐ}{也|yě}{熬|áo}{过|guo}{夜|yè}，{第|dì}{二|èr}{天|tiān}{精神|jīng shén}{很|hěn}{差|chà}，{什么|shén me}{都|dōu}{做不好|zuò bu hǎo}。{所以|suǒ yǐ}{我|wǒ}{觉得|jué de}，{熬夜|áo yè}{偶尔|ǒu ěr}{一|yí}{次|cì}{没关系|méi guān xi}，{但是|dàn shì}{不|bù}{能|néng}{长期|cháng qī}{这样|zhè yàng}。{我们|wǒ men}{应该|yīng gāi}{控制|kòng zhì}{好|hǎo}{时间|shí jiān}，{保持|bǎo chí}{好|hǎo}{的|de}{睡眠|shuì mián}{习惯|xí guàn}。

"I think staying up late is a problem, but we can't put it all down to young people. First, the pressure of
work and study is high now: many people are too busy in the day and only have a bit of time of
their own in the evening. Second, there's too much entertainment on our phones: once you start,
it's an hour or two. I've stayed up late myself, and the next day I felt terrible and couldn't do
anything well. So I think staying up once in a while is fine, but it can't go on long-term. We
should keep our time under control and keep good sleeping habits."
</details>

## Write it: a picture story

The writing test's first task is a story of at least 100 characters from four pictures. Here the
pictures are described in words. Write 100–150 characters, with a time word or connector to start
each step ({那|nà}{天|tiān}, {第|dì}{二|èr}{天|tiān}{早上|zǎo shang}, {结果|jié guǒ}, {从|cóng}{那|nà}{以后|yǐ hòu}).

1. Late at night a young man sits at his desk with his phone; the clock shows half past one.
2. In the morning the alarm clock rings, but he's still asleep.
3. He runs to the bus stop, out of breath; the bus is driving away.
4. That evening he puts his phone in another room and goes to bed at eleven.

<details>
<summary>A model story</summary>

{那|nà}{天|tiān}{晚上|wǎn shang}，{小|xiǎo}{张|zhāng}{一直|yì zhí}{在|zài}{看|kàn}{手机|shǒu jī}，{不知不觉|bù zhī bù jué}{就|jiù}{到|dào}{了|le}{半夜|bàn yè}{一|yī}{点|diǎn}{半|bàn}。{第|dì}{二|èr}{天|tiān}{早上|zǎo shang}，{闹钟|nào zhōng}{响|xiǎng}{了|le}{好|hǎo}{几|jǐ}{次|cì}，{他|tā}{都|dōu}{没|méi}{听见|tīng jiàn}。{等|děng}{他|tā}{醒|xǐng}{来|lái}，{已经|yǐ jīng}{八|bā}{点|diǎn}{了|le}。{他|tā}{连|lián}{早饭|zǎo fàn}{都|dōu}{没|méi}{吃|chī}，{就|jiù}{跑|pǎo}{出|chū}{了|le}{门|mén}，{累|lèi}{得|de}{满|mǎn}{身|shēn}{是|shì}{汗|hàn}。{可是|kě shì}{到|dào}{了|le}{车站|chē zhàn}，{公共|gōng gòng}{汽车|qì chē}{刚好|gāng hǎo}{开|kāi}{走|zǒu}{了|le}。{结果|jié guǒ}，{他|tā}{上班|shàng bān}{迟到|chí dào}{了|le}。{从|cóng}{那|nà}{以后|yǐ hòu}，{小|xiǎo}{张|zhāng}{每|měi}{天|tiān}{睡觉|shuì jiào}{以前|yǐ qián}{都|dōu}{把|bǎ}{手机|shǒu jī}{放|fàng}{在|zài}{客厅|kè tīng}{里|lǐ}，{十一|shí yī}{点|diǎn}{就|jiù}{睡觉|shuì jiào}。

(147 characters. {满|mǎn}{身|shēn}{是|shì}{汗|hàn}: covered in sweat.)

"That night Xiao Zhang kept looking at his phone, and before he knew it, it was half past one. The
next morning the alarm went off several times, but he didn't hear it. When he woke up it was already
eight. He ran out without even having breakfast, so worn out he was covered in sweat. But when he got
to the stop, the bus had just pulled away. He was late for work. From then on, Xiao Zhang left his
phone in the living room every night and went to bed at eleven."
</details>

## Say it

```speak
# Busy lives
{我|wǒ}{最近|zuì jìn}{似乎|sì hū}{太|tài}{忙|máng}{了|le}，{晚上|wǎn shang}{常常|cháng cháng}{失眠|shī mián}。
= I seem to have been too busy lately: I often can't sleep at night.
{他|tā}{累|lèi}{得|de}{站不起来|zhàn bu qǐ lái}{了|le}。
= He was so tired he couldn't get up.
{反正|fǎn zhèng}{明天|míng tiān}{不|bú}{上班|shàng bān}，{我们|wǒ men}{去|qù}{看|kàn}{电影|diàn yǐng}{吧|ba}。
= I'm not working tomorrow anyway: let's go and see a film.
{我|wǒ}{刚好|gāng hǎo}{也|yě}{要|yào}{去|qù}{便利店|biàn lì diàn}，{一起|yì qǐ}{走|zǒu}{吧|ba}。
= I'm going to the shop too, as it happens: let's go together.
{他|tā}{从不|cóng bù}{熬夜|áo yè}，{每|měi}{天|tiān}{十一|shí yī}{点|diǎn}{就|jiù}{睡觉|shuì jiào}。
= He never stays up late: he's in bed by eleven every night.
{她|tā}{看|kàn}{了|le}{我|wǒ}{一|yì}{眼|yǎn}，{好像|hǎo xiàng}{什么|shén me}{都|dōu}{知道|zhī dào}{似的|shì de}。
= She glanced at me as if she knew everything.
```

## Pronunciation

- {似|sì} has two readings: sì in {似乎|sì hū} sì hū (and {相似|xiāng sì}, lesson 18), shì in {似的|shì de} shì de. {似的|shì de} is light at the end.
- {熬夜|áo yè} áo yè: rising, then falling. {熬|áo} starts with a vowel: no consonant before *áo*.
- {呼吸|hū xī} hū xī: *h* is breathed from the throat, *x* from the front of the mouth, like a thin *sh*.
- {弱|ruò} ruò: the Chinese *r*, between the *r* of "run" and the *s* of "pleasure". {肉|ròu} ròu (in {肌肉|jī ròu}) has it too.
- {腰|yāo} yāo and {要|yào} yào: the same syllable, first tone for the waist, fourth for "want".
- {精神|jīng shén} jīng shén: in the sense "lively" many speakers say jīng shen, with a light second syllable.

## Common mistakes

- ~~{他|tā}{看|kàn}{了|le}{一|yì}{眼|yǎn}{我|wǒ}~~: a pronoun object goes before {一|yì}{眼|yǎn}: {他|tā}{看|kàn}{了|le}{我|wǒ}{一|yì}{眼|yǎn}.
- ~~{我|wǒ}{从不|cóng bú}{去|qù}{过|guo}{酒吧|jiǔ bā}~~: {从不|cóng bù} is a habit and doesn't take {过|guo}; experience is {我|wǒ}{从|cóng}{没|méi}{去|qù}{过|guo}{酒吧|jiǔ bā}.
- {似的|shì de} read as *sì de*: it's shì de.
- ~~{他|tā}{累|lèi}{得|de}{很|hěn}{站不起来|zhàn bu qǐ lái}~~: after {得|de} comes the state itself: {他|tā}{累|lèi}{得|de}{站不起来|zhàn bu qǐ lái}.
- ~~{我|wǒ}{不|bú}{累|lèi}{得|de}{想|xiǎng}{睡觉|shuì jiào}~~: the negative goes in the state: {我|wǒ}{累|lèi}{得|de}{不|bù}{想|xiǎng}{睡觉|shuì jiào} (so tired I don't want to sleep), or
  plain {我|wǒ}{不|bú}{累|lèi} (I'm not tired).
- {似乎|sì hū} in a "pretend" comparison: {他|tā}{仿佛|fǎng fú}{三|sān}{天|tiān}{没|méi}{睡|shuì}{似的|shì de} (as if he hadn't slept for three days) is a
  comparison; {他|tā}{似乎|sì hū}{三|sān}{天|tiān}{没|méi}{睡|shuì} claims it may really be so.

## Key points

- {好像|hǎo xiàng} (spoken), {似乎|sì hū} (a careful guess, formal), {仿佛|fǎng fú} (as if, literary); {像|xiàng} / {好像|hǎo xiàng} / {仿佛|fǎng fú}…{似的|shì de} closes an "as if"
  comparison. {似的|shì de} is shì de.
- The state complement: verb / adjective + {得|de} + the state it leads to ({累|lèi}{得|de}{站不起来|zhàn bu qǐ lái}, {说|shuō}{得|de}{大家|dà jiā}{都|dōu}{笑|xiào}{了|le}).
- {反正|fǎn zhèng}: anyway, whatever happens; {刚好|gāng hǎo}: just right, or as it happens.
- {从不|cóng bù} + verb: a habit; {从|cóng}{没|méi} + verb + {过|guo}: experience.
- {看|kàn}{了|le}{我|wǒ}{一|yì}{眼|yǎn}: {眼|yǎn} counts looks; a pronoun object comes before it.
- New characters: {豫|yù} {熬|áo} {抽|chōu} {刺|cì} {良|liáng} {仿|fǎng} {佛|fú} {肌|jī} {缓|huǎn} {神|shén} {控|kòng} {碌|lù} {伸|shēn} {衡|héng} {弱|ruò} {眠|mián} {似|sì} {腰|yāo} {显|xiǎn} {享|xiǎng} (✎ {抽|chōu} {良|liáng} {佛|fú} {神|shén} {似|sì} {显|xiǎn}); the new radical {行|xíng}.

The words from this lesson are listed below; they join your vocabulary reviews when you complete
the lesson.

lessons.title: Food, diet and nutrition
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

Last lesson was about sleep; this one is about food. {李明|Lǐ Míng} (Li Ming) is studying in the north of England
and has had to learn to cook, and {王芳|Wáng Fāng} (Wang Fang) is on a diet again. The written texts are the
kind you read in a kitchen: a food label and a recipe.

The grammar is about how much, and what you mustn't do:

- {尽量|jǐn liàng}: as far as possible;
- {适当|shì dàng}: suitable, in moderation;
- {过于|guò yú}: too, excessively (written);
- {得|de}{不得了|bù dé liǎo}: extremely, beyond words ({好吃|hǎo chī}{得|de}{不得了|bù dé liǎo});
- V{不得|bu de}: mustn't, shouldn't ({吃不得|chī bu de}, {去不得|qù bu de}), the **potential V{不得|bu de}**.

You also get the words for fruit and staples, cooking, tastes and nutrition, and for eating out:
night markets, hot pot and take-away boxes.

## {尽量|jǐn liàng}: as far as possible

{尽量|jǐn liàng} (jǐnliàng) is an adverb: do as much as you can, go as far as you can. It goes before the verb,
or before an adjective with a verb:

{我|wǒ}{尽量|jǐn liàng}{每|měi}{天|tiān}{自己|zì jǐ}{做饭|zuò fàn}。 — I try to cook for myself every day as far as I can.

{晚上|wǎn shang}{尽量|jǐn liàng}{少|shǎo}{吃|chī}{甜品|tián pǐn}。 — Eat as few desserts as you can in the evening.

{你|nǐ}{尽量|jǐn liàng}{早|zǎo}{点儿|diǎnr}{回来|huí lái}。 — Try to come back as early as you can.

{请|qǐng}{尽量|jǐn liàng}{说|shuō}{慢|màn}{一点儿|yì diǎnr}。 — Please speak as slowly as you can.

{尽量|jǐn liàng} often goes with {多|duō} / {少|shǎo} / {早|zǎo} / {快|kuài} + verb. It's a polite way to make a request (it admits that the
other person may not manage fully) and an honest way to promise: {我|wǒ}{尽量|jǐn liàng} (I'll do my best). In
traditional characters it's written {+{尽量|jǐn liàng}+}; {尽力|jìn lì} (lesson 03, to try one's hardest) is {+{尽力|jìn lì}+}, a
different character.

## {适当|shì dàng} and {过于|guò yú}: in moderation, too much

{适当|shì dàng} (shìdàng) is an adjective: suitable, appropriate, not too much and not too little. As an
adverbial it says "in moderation", "a reasonable amount":

{适当|shì dàng}{运动|yùn dòng}{对|duì}{身体|shēn tǐ}{有益|yǒu yì}。 — Exercise in moderation is good for you.

{减肥|jiǎn féi}{可以|kě yǐ}{适当|shì dàng}{少|shǎo}{吃|chī}{一点儿|yì diǎnr}，{但是|dàn shì}{不要|bú yào}{不|bù}{吃|chī}{饭|fàn}。 — When you're dieting you can eat a bit less, but don't skip meals.

{在|zài}{适当|shì dàng}{的|de}{时候|shí hou}，{我|wǒ}{会|huì}{告诉|gào su}{他|tā}。 — I'll tell him at the right moment.

{过于|guò yú} (guòyú) is the written "too": {过于|guò yú}{紧张|jǐn zhāng} (too tense), {过于|guò yú}{担心|dān xīn} (worry too much). It means the same as
{太|tài}, but:

| | {太|tài} | {过于|guò yú} |
|---|---|---|
| register | spoken and written | written, formal |
| with {了|le} | usually: {太|tài}{甜|tián}{了|le} | seldom: {过于|guò yú}{甜|tián} |
| tone | often a complaint or an exclamation | a measured judgement, often in advice |

{这个|zhè ge}{菜|cài}{太|tài}{甜|tián}{了|le}！ — This dish is far too sweet! (a complaint)

{饮食|yǐn shí}{不要|bú yào}{过于|guò yú}{简单|jiǎn dān}。 — Your diet shouldn't be too simple. (advice in writing)

You met {过度|guò dù} (excessive) in lesson 06. {过度|guò dù} is an adjective or adverb of amount ("over-": {过度|guò dù}{使用|shǐ yòng}{手机|shǒu jī},
overusing one's phone); {过于|guò yú} is a degree adverb before an adjective ("too": {过于|guò yú}{甜|tián}, too sweet). Lesson 03
grouped {过于|guò yú} with the other written degree adverbs {相当|xiāng dāng}, {格外|gé wài} and {极其|jí qí}.

## {得|de}{不得了|bù dé liǎo}: beyond words

{不得了|bù dé liǎo} (bù dé liǎo) is a set phrase. After an adjective (or a verb of feeling) and {得|de}, it's the
strongest degree there is: "extremely", "unbearably", "beyond words". **{得|de}{不得了|bù dé liǎo}** is the state complement of
lesson 06 at its limit:

{夜市|yè shì}{的|de}{烧烤|shāo kǎo}{好吃|hǎo chī}{得|de}{不得了|bù dé liǎo}。 — The barbecue at the night market is unbelievably good.

{听|tīng}{到|dào}{这个|zhè ge}{消息|xiāo xi}，{她|tā}{高兴|gāo xìng}{得|de}{不得了|bù dé liǎo}。 — When she heard the news she was over the moon.

{今天|jīn tiān}{热|rè}{得|de}{不得了|bù dé liǎo}。 — It's terribly hot today.

On its own, {不得了|bù dé liǎo} is an exclamation: something terrible has happened, or is about to. {不得了|bù dé liǎo}{了|le}，{水|shuǐ}{开|kāi}{了|le}！
(Oh no, the water's boiling over!) {没|méi}{什么|shén me}{不得了|bù dé liǎo}{的|de} is "it's no big deal". In speech, {得|de}{要命|yào mìng} (de yàomìng)
and {得|de}{很|hěn} (HSK 3) are close partners: {累|lèi}{得|de}{要命|yào mìng} (dead tired).

| Degree | Example | Strength |
|---|---|---|
| {很|hěn} + adjective | {很|hěn}{好吃|hǎo chī} | plain |
| adjective + {得|de}{很|hěn} | {好吃|hǎo chī}{得|de}{很|hěn} | strong, spoken |
| adjective + {极|jí}{了|le} | {好吃|hǎo chī}{极|jí}{了|le} | very strong |
| adjective + {得|de}{不得了|bù dé liǎo} | {好吃|hǎo chī}{得|de}{不得了|bù dé liǎo} | the strongest; spoken and lively writing |

## The potential V{不得|bu de}: mustn't, shouldn't

You know potential complements from HSK 3: {吃不完|chī bu wán} (can't finish), {听不懂|tīng bu dǒng} (can't understand). The result
won't come. HSK 5 adds a different kind: **V{不得|bu de}**, a verb + {不得|bu de} (both syllables light). It doesn't say
that something can't be done, but that it mustn't be done, because of what would happen:

{过期|guò qī}{的|de}{牛奶|niú nǎi}{喝不得|hē bu de}。 — You mustn't drink milk that's past its date. (it would make you ill)

{这|zhè}{种|zhǒng}{菜|cài}{生|shēng}{的|de}{吃不得|chī bu de}，{一定|yí dìng}{要|yào}{煮|zhǔ}{熟|shú}。 — You can't eat this vegetable raw: it must be cooked through.

{那个|nà ge}{地方|dì fang}{太|tài}{危险|wēi xiǎn}，{去不得|qù bu de}。 — That place is too dangerous: you mustn't go there.

{这|zhè}{件|jiàn}{事|shì}{急不得|jí bu de}，{要|yào}{慢|màn}{慢|màn}{来|lái}。 — This can't be rushed: take it slowly.

Compare the three negatives of possibility:

| Form | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| {不|bù}{能|néng} + verb | not allowed; not possible | {这儿|zhèr}{不|bù}{能|néng}{抽|chōu}{烟|yān}。 No smoking here. |
| V{不了|bu liǎo} | unable to (a limit of amount or ability) | {我|wǒ}{吃不了|chī bu liǎo}{这么|zhè me}{多|duō}。 I can't eat this much. |
| V{不得|bu de} | mustn't (the result would be harmful) | {这个|zhè ge}{蘑菇|mó gu}{吃不得|chī bu de}。 This mushroom mustn't be eaten. ({蘑菇|mó gu} mógu: a mushroom) |

The positive, V{得|de} ({吃得|chī de}), is rare and appears mostly in questions or answers to them: {这个|zhè ge}{吃得|chī de}{吗|ma}？—{吃得|chī de} (can
I eat this? — yes). V{不得|bu de} belongs to a few common verbs ({吃|chī}, {喝|hē}, {说|shuō}, {去|qù}, {急|jí}, {动|dòng}); for most others,
use {不|bù}{能|néng} or {千万|qiān wàn}{别|bié} (HSK 4).

## Words: fruit, staples and the kitchen

Fruit: {橙子|chéng zi} (orange), {橘子|jú zi} (tangerine), {梨|lí} (pear), {桃|táo} (peach). {橙子|chéng zi} is the large orange and {橘子|jú zi} the small one
you peel by hand.

Staples. {粮食|liáng shi} is grain, food as a crop; {大米|dà mǐ} is uncooked rice (cooked, it's {米饭|mǐ fàn}); {玉米|yù mǐ} is maize, corn. {主食|zhǔ shí} is
the staple of a meal: rice, noodles, bread. {={面|miàn}=} (miàn) here is noodles or flour: {一|yì}{碗|wǎn}{面|miàn} (a bowl of
noodles), {面条|miàn tiáo}. With the traditional script on you'll see the difference: noodles are {+{面条|miàn tiáo}+}, while
{面|miàn} "side, face" ({+{面前|miàn qián}+}) stays {面|miàn}. {饼|bǐng} is a flatbread or pancake: {饼|bǐng} for bread, {饼干|bǐng gān} (HSK 4) for biscuits.

{北方|běi fāng}{人|rén}{的|de}{主食|zhǔ shí}{是|shì}{面|miàn}，{南方|nán fāng}{人|rén}{的|de}{主食|zhǔ shí}{是|shì}{大米|dà mǐ}。 — In the north people mainly eat noodles; in the south, rice.

- {东|dōng} dōng in {冻|dòng} dòng (ice 冫 + {东|dōng}), the same family as {冬|dōng} and {冰|bīng} for cold.
- 炎 yán in {淡|dàn} dàn (water 氵 + 炎); compare {谈|tán} tán (to talk, HSK 4).

- {登|dēng} dēng in {橙|chéng} chéng ({木|mù} + {登|dēng}): drifted too, but you can remember {橙|chéng} as the tree's fruit, {木|mù}.

- {叉|chā} and {又|yòu}: {叉|chā} is {又|yòu} with one dot inside. Three strokes only: {又|yòu}'s two, then the dot. A memory aid: a fork
  held between the fingers.
- {臭|chòu} is {自|zì} over 犬 (a dog), not {大|dà}: don't forget the dot at the top right. Ten strokes.
- {含|hán} is {今|jīn} over {口|kǒu}; {念|niàn} (lesson 13) is {今|jīn} over {心|xīn}.
- {充|chōng} is 亠 over {允|yǔn} (厶 and {儿|ér}): it ends in {儿|ér}'s two strokes, the second a vertical-bend-hook.
- {番|fān} begins with 丿 and {米|mǐ}, then 田 below: 12 strokes. {番|fān} is also the "foreign" of {番茄|fān qié} ("foreign

- {锅|guō}: 钅 on the left, then 呙 ({口|kǒu} on top, then {内|nèi}-like 冂 with {人|rén} inside).
- {豆|dòu} is a radical too: its last stroke is the long bottom horizontal, after the two short strokes.

## Pronunciation

- {切|qiē} qiē (to cut): first tone, with *q* and *ie*. The same character is qiè in {一切|yí qiè} (everything, HSK 4).
- {炸|zhá} zhá (to deep-fry): second tone. {炸|zhá} zhà, fourth tone, is "to explode" (HSK 6).
- {称|chēng} chēng (to weigh, and in lesson 12 to call): first tone, with *ch* and *eng*.
- {豆腐|dòu fu} dòu fu: the second syllable is light; {豆浆|dòu jiāng} dòu jiāng keeps both tones.
- {臭|chòu} chòu and {抽|chōu} chōu (lesson 06): the same syllable, fourth and first tones.
- {不得了|bù dé liǎo} bù dé liǎo: here {得|de} is dé and {了|le} is liǎo; in V{不得|bu de} ({喝不得|hē bu de}) both are light.
- {尽量|jǐn liàng} jǐn liàng: third tone, as in {尽快|jǐn kuài} (lesson 08); {尽力|jìn lì} (lesson 03) is jìn lì, fourth.

## Common mistakes

- {这个|zhè ge}{菜|cài}{过于|guò yú}{甜|tián}{了|le} mixes registers: written {过于|guò yú} seldom takes the spoken {了|le} at the end. Say {这个|zhè ge}{菜|cài}{过于|guò yú}{甜|tián} (written) or {这个|zhè ge}{菜|cài}{太|tài}{甜|tián}{了|le} (spoken).
- ~~{我|wǒ}{吃不得|chī bu de}{这么|zhè me}{多|duō}~~ for "I can't eat this much": a limit of amount is {吃不了|chī bu liǎo}: {我|wǒ}{吃不了|chī bu liǎo}{这么|zhè me}{多|duō}. {吃不得|chī bu de} means
  you mustn't eat it.
- ~~{他|tā}{高兴|gāo xìng}{得|de}{很|hěn}{不得了|bù dé liǎo}~~: nothing goes between {得|de} and {不得了|bù dé liǎo}: {他|tā}{高兴|gāo xìng}{得|de}{不得了|bù dé liǎo}.
- {必需|bì xū} and {必须|bì xū}: same sound, different words. ~~{我|wǒ}{必需|bì xū}{去|qù}~~ → {我|wǒ}{必须|bì xū}{去|qù} (I must go); {水|shuǐ}{是|shì}{人体|rén tǐ}{必需|bì xū}{的|de} (water is essential to
  the body).
- {尽量|jǐn liàng} read jìn liàng: it's jǐn liàng.
- {我|wǒ}{尽量|jǐn liàng}{去|qù} is fine as "I'll try to go", but not for "I'll go as soon as I can": that's {我|wǒ}{尽快|jǐn kuài}{去|qù} (lesson 08).

## Key points

- {尽量|jǐn liàng} + verb: as far as possible ({尽量|jǐn liàng}{少|shǎo}{吃|chī}, {尽量|jǐn liàng}{早|zǎo}{点儿|diǎnr}{回来|huí lái}); traditional {+{尽量|jǐn liàng}+}.
- {适当|shì dàng}: suitable, in moderation ({适当|shì dàng}{运动|yùn dòng}); {过于|guò yú} + adjective: too (written; seldom with {了|le}).
- Adjective + {得|de}{不得了|bù dé liǎo}: the strongest degree ({好吃|hǎo chī}{得|de}{不得了|bù dé liǎo}); {不得了|bù dé liǎo} alone: a disaster!
- V{不得|bu de}: mustn't, the result would be bad ({喝不得|hē bu de}, {去不得|qù bu de}); compare {不|bù}{能|néng} (not allowed) and V{不了|bu liǎo} (unable).
- Written and spoken food words: {番茄|fān qié} / {西红柿|xī hóng shì}, {蔬菜|shū cài} / {菜|cài}, {饮食|yǐn shí} / {吃|chī}{的|de}.
- New characters: {闲|xián} {状|zhuàng} {姿|zī} {娱|yú} {叉|chā} {橙|chéng} {炒|chǎo} {称|chēng} {充|chōng} {臭|chòu} {豆|dòu} {腐|fǔ} {浆|jiāng} {番|fān} {茄|qié} {冻|dòng} {淡|dàn} {锅|guō} {含|hán} {肥|féi} (✎ {闲|xián} {状|zhuàng} {叉|chā} {称|chēng} {充|chōng} {臭|chòu} {豆|dòu} {冻|dòng} {含|hán}).

The words from this lesson are listed below; they join your vocabulary reviews when you complete
the lesson.

lessons.title: At the hospital
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

HSK 4 taught you to tell a doctor where it hurts. This lesson goes into the hospital itself:
registering, waiting, the emergency department, a diagnosis, a stay on a ward and getting better.
{安娜|Ān nà} (Anna) has a fever, and {王芳|Wáng Fāng} (Wang Fang) takes her to an outpatient clinic; then {王芳|Wáng Fāng} tells the
story of her grandmother's fall, in paragraphs for you to put in order, as the exam does.

The grammar is about speed and change:

- {立刻|lì kè}, {立即|lì jí}, {马上|mǎ shàng}, {赶紧|gǎn jǐn}, {连忙|lián máng} and {急忙|jí máng}: six ways to say "at once", sorted by register and use;
- {尽快|jǐn kuài} (as soon as possible) and {随时|suí shí} (at any time);
- {一旦|yí dàn}…{就|jiù} (once…, if ever…), from lesson 03;
- the **[[extended direction complement]]**: {醒|xǐng}{过来|guò lái} (come round), {好|hǎo}{起来|qǐ lái} (get better), {坚持|jiān chí}{下去|xià qù} (keep going),
  {安静|ān jìng}{下来|xià lái} (quieten down).

The lesson describes what happens in a hospital; it gives no medical advice beyond the everyday
(rest, drink water, see a doctor).

## {立刻|lì kè}, {立即|lì jí}, {马上|mǎ shàng}, {赶紧|gǎn jǐn}, {连忙|lián máng}, {急忙|jí máng}: at once

All six put an action straight after something else. They differ in register and in whether you can
use them to tell someone what to do:

| Word | Register | In a request or order? | Use | Example |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| {马上|mǎ shàng} (HSK 2) | spoken | yes | right away, very soon | {我|wǒ}{马上|mǎ shàng}{来|lái}！ I'll be right there! |
| {立刻|lì kè} | spoken and written | yes | at once, with no gap | {请|qǐng}{立刻|lì kè}{离开|lí kāi}{这儿|zhèr}。 Please leave at once. |
| {立即|lì jí} | written, formal | yes | immediately (notices, rules, news) | {发现|fā xiàn}{问题|wèn tí}，{请|qǐng}{立即|lì jí}{报告|bào gào}。 Report any problem immediately. |
| {赶紧|gǎn jǐn} (HSK 4) | spoken | yes | hurry up and… | {快|kuài}{下雨|xià yǔ}{了|le}，{赶紧|gǎn jǐn}{回|huí}{家|jiā}{吧|ba}！ It's about to rain: hurry home! |
| {连忙|lián máng} | written and narration | no | promptly, in reaction to something | {他|tā}{看见|kàn jiàn}{老人|lǎo rén}{摔倒|shuāi dǎo}{了|le}，{连忙|lián máng}{跑|pǎo}{过去|guò qù}。 Seeing the old man fall, he hurried over. |
| {急忙|jí máng} | written and narration | no | hastily, anxiously | {她|tā}{听说|tīng shuō}{孩子|hái zi}{病|bìng}{了|le}，{急忙|jí máng}{赶|gǎn}{到|dào}{医院|yī yuàn}。 Hearing her child was ill, she rushed to the hospital. |

Three things decide the choice:

- *Commands and promises* take {马上|mǎ shàng}, {立刻|lì kè}, {立即|lì jí} or {赶紧|gǎn jǐn}. {连忙|lián máng} and {急忙|jí máng} only narrate what someone did:
  not ~~{请|qǐng}{你|nǐ}{连忙|lián máng}{来|lái}~~, but {请|qǐng}{你|nǐ}{马上|mǎ shàng}{来|lái}.
- *Register*: {立即|lì jí} is the word of notices ({一旦|yí dàn}{发现|fā xiàn}{火情|huǒ qíng}，{请|qǐng}{立即|lì jí}{打|dǎ} 119: if you see a fire, call 119
  immediately); {马上|mǎ shàng} and {赶紧|gǎn jǐn} belong to speech; {立刻|lì kè} is at home in both.
- *Feeling*: {急忙|jí máng} adds worry and haste, and doubles as {急急忙忙|jí jí máng máng} (in a great rush); {连忙|lián máng} is quick and
  willing ({他|tā}{连忙|lián máng}{说|shuō}："{没关系|méi guān xi}，{没关系|méi guān xi}。").

{马上|mǎ shàng} can also mean "soon" with a time ahead: {马上|mǎ shàng}{就|jiù}{要|yào}{考试|kǎo shì}{了|le} (the exam's coming up soon). {立刻|lì kè} and {立即|lì jí} can't.

## {尽快|jǐn kuài} and {随时|suí shí}: as soon as possible, at any time

{尽快|jǐn kuài} (jǐnkuài: "to the limit" + {快|kuài}) is "as soon as possible". Unlike {马上|mǎ shàng}, it allows some time to
pass; it's polite and common in writing:

{请|qǐng}{尽快|jǐn kuài}{回复|huí fù}。 — Please reply as soon as you can.

{你|nǐ}{的|de}{病|bìng}{要|yào}{尽快|jǐn kuài}{治疗|zhì liáo}。 — Your illness needs treating as soon as possible.

Like {尽量|jǐn liàng} (lesson 07), it's written {+{尽快|jǐn kuài}+} in traditional.

{随时|suí shí} (suíshí) is "at any time, whenever": {有|yǒu}{问题|wèn tí}{随时|suí shí}{给|gěi}{我|wǒ}{打电话|dǎ diàn huà} (call me any time you have a problem). It also
says something may happen at any moment: {病人|bìng rén}{的|de}{状况|zhuàng kuàng}{随时|suí shí}{可能|kě néng}{变化|biàn huà} (the patient's condition could change at any
time).

## {一旦|yí dàn}…{就|jiù}: once…, if ever…

Lesson 03 introduced {一旦|yí dàn}…{就|jiù}. It sets a condition that hasn't happened yet but might, often an
unwelcome one, and what must follow at once:

{一旦|yí dàn}{发|fā}{高烧|gāo shāo}，{就|jiù}{要|yào}{立刻|lì kè}{去|qù}{医院|yī yuàn}。 — If you ever get a high fever, go to the hospital at once.

{这|zhè}{种|zhǒng}{病|bìng}{一旦|yí dàn}{发现|fā xiàn}，{就|jiù}{要|yào}{尽快|jǐn kuài}{治疗|zhì liáo}。 — Once this illness is found, it must be treated as soon as possible.

Compared with {如果|rú guǒ} (if: any supposition), {一旦|yí dàn} stresses the moment it happens: "the moment that…". It's
more formal, and it's the natural word in rules and medical leaflets. It also works for the past,
"once it had happened": {习惯|xí guàn}{一旦|yí dàn}{养成|yǎng chéng}，{就|jiù}{很|hěn}{难|nán}{改|gǎi}{了|le} (once a habit has formed, it's hard to change).

## The extended direction complement: {醒|xǐng}{过来|guò lái}, {好|hǎo}{起来|qǐ lái}, {坚持|jiān chí}{下去|xià qù}

The direction complements {过来|guò lái}, {过去|guò qù}, {起来|qǐ lái}, {下来|xià lái}, {下去|xià qù} first say where something moves ({走|zǒu}{过来|guò lái}, came over;
{站|zhàn}{起来|qǐ lái}, stood up). Used with other verbs and adjectives, they say how a state changes. This is the
**[[extended direction complement]]**, and hospital talk is full of it:

| Complement | Extended sense | Examples |
|---|---|---|
| {过来|guò lái} | back to the normal state | {醒|xǐng}{过来|guò lái} (come round, wake up), {恢复|huī fù}{过来|guò lái} (recover), {明白|míng bai}{过来|guò lái} (realise) |
| {过去|guò qù} | out of the normal state | {晕|yūn}{过去|guò qù} (faint; {晕|yūn} yūn), {睡|shuì}{过去|guò qù} (fall asleep) |
| {起来|qǐ lái} | a state begins and grows | {好|hǎo}{起来|qǐ lái} (get better), {疼|téng}{起来|qǐ lái} (start to hurt), {热|rè}{起来|qǐ lái} (warm up), {笑|xiào}{起来|qǐ lái} |
| {下来|xià lái} | settling, calming; keeping | {安静|ān jìng}{下来|xià lái} (quieten down), {停|tíng}{下来|xià lái} (come to a stop), {记|jì}{下来|xià lái} (write down) |
| {下去|xià qù} | carrying on | {坚持|jiān chí}{下去|xià qù} (keep going), {说|shuō}{下去|xià qù} (go on speaking), {住|zhù}{下去|xià qù} (stay on) |

{手术|shǒu shù}{以后|yǐ hòu}，{他|tā}{睡|shuì}{了|le}{一|yì}{天|tiān}{才|cái}{醒|xǐng}{过来|guò lái}。 — After the operation he slept for a day before he came round.

{天气|tiān qì}{慢|màn}{慢|màn}{热|rè}{起来|qǐ lái}{了|le}。 — It's slowly getting warmer.

{吃|chī}{了|le}{药|yào}，{她|tā}{的|de}{心情|xīn qíng}{也|yě}{好|hǎo}{起来|qǐ lái}{了|le}。 — After the medicine she started to feel better in spirits too.

{孩子|hái zi}{哭|kū}{了|le}{一会儿|yí huìr}，{慢|màn}{慢|màn}{安静|ān jìng}{下来|xià lái}{了|le}。 — The child cried for a while, then gradually calmed down.

{医生|yī shēng}{说|shuō}，{只要|zhǐ yào}{坚持|jiān chí}{下去|xià qù}，{你|nǐ}{的|de}{腰|yāo}{就|jiù}{会|huì}{好|hǎo}{的|de}。 — The doctor says your back will get better as long as you keep at it.

Two patterns help: {过来|guò lái} and {过去|guò qù} are a pair (back to normal / away from normal); {起来|qǐ lái} starts a change,
{下去|xià qù} continues one. The object of {起来|qǐ lái} goes in the middle: {下|xià}{起|qǐ}{雨|yǔ}{来|lái}{了|le} (it's started to rain). {看|kàn}{起来|qǐ lái} (it looks
as if) and {想|xiǎng}{起来|qǐ lái} (to remember) are the ones you'll use every day. All are in the reference sheet on
complements.

## Words: at the hospital

Going to hospital. A big Chinese hospital has an outpatient department, {门诊|mén zhěn}, and an emergency
department, {急诊|jí zhěn} (A&E), open at night too ({夜间|yè jiān}{急诊|jí zhěn}). You {挂号|guà hào} (register) at a desk or on your phone, or
{预约|yù yuē} (book) ahead; {登记|dēng jì} is to register, sign in (at a hotel or a hospital); {手续|shǒu xù} are the formalities.
You {等候|děng hòu} (formal) or {等待|děng dài} (written) your turn, {咨询|zī xún} (consult, ask for advice) at an information desk, and
{领取|lǐng qǔ} (collect) medicine or reports. {救护车|jiù hù chē} is an ambulance; {病房|bìng fáng} is a ward.

| Spoken | Written or formal |
|---|---|
| {等|děng} | {等待|děng dài}, {等候|děng hòu} |
| {问|wèn} | {咨询|zī xún} |
| {拿|ná} | {领取|lǐng qǔ} |
| {看病|kàn bìng} | {治疗|zhì liáo}, {诊断|zhěn duàn} |

What's wrong. {疾病|jí bìng} is illness, disease (written); {毛病|máo bìng} is a fault or a minor ailment ({我|wǒ}{的|de}{胃|wèi}{有点儿|yǒu diǎnr}{毛病|máo bìng}: my
stomach isn't quite right), and also a bad habit. {流感|liú gǎn} is flu; {过敏|guò mǐn} an allergy, to be allergic ({他|tā}{对|duì}{海鲜|hǎi xiān}{过敏|guò mǐn});
{着凉|zháo liáng} (zháoliáng) is to catch a chill. {伤|shāng} is an injury or wound ({他|tā}{的|de}{伤|shāng}{不|bú}{重|zhòng}); {疼痛|téng tòng} is pain (written); {摔|shuāi} is to fall
({摔倒|shuāi dǎo}, to fall over) or drop something. Body words: {胃|wèi} stomach, {消化|xiāo huà} to digest, {牙齿|yá chǐ} teeth, and {背|bèi} the
back, which you know from HSK 4 as {背|bēi} (to carry on the back).

What the doctor says. {脸色|liǎn sè} is your colour, the look on your face ({脸色|liǎn sè}{不|bù}{好|hǎo}: looking pale); {病情|bìng qíng} the patient's
condition, {状况|zhuàng kuàng} the state of things ({身体|shēn tǐ}{状况|zhuàng kuàng}, health). {诊断|zhěn duàn} is a diagnosis; {治|zhì} and {治疗|zhì liáo} are to treat, to
cure ({治|zhì}{病|bìng}, {治疗|zhì liáo}{疾病|jí bìng}); {手术|shǒu shù} is an operation ({做|zuò}{手术|shǒu shù}). Then {好转|hǎo zhuǎn} (to get better), {恢复|huī fù} (to recover). In an
emergency, {抢救|qiǎng jiù} is to try to save a life ({抢救|qiǎng jiù}{病人|bìng rén}), {救|jiù} to save ({救|jiù}{人|rén}, {救命|jiù mìng}: help!), {命|mìng} life (his life
was saved: {他|tā}{的|de}{命|mìng}{保住|bǎo zhù}{了|le}, {保住|bǎo zhù} bǎozhù: to keep safe).

Medicine. {医学|yī xué} is medicine as a science; {医疗|yī liáo} medical care ({医疗|yī liáo}{费|fèi}, medical costs); {药品|yào pǐn} and {药物|yào wù} are
medicines (written; {药|yào} is the everyday word). {中医|zhōng yī} is traditional Chinese medicine and its doctors;
{中药|zhōng yào} its herbal remedies. Many Chinese hospitals have both a Western and a Chinese-medicine
department, and some patients use both.

Prevention. {预防|yù fáng} and {防止|fáng zhǐ} are both "to prevent": {预防|yù fáng} is ahead of time ({预防|yù fáng}{流感|liú gǎn}), {防止|fáng zhǐ} is to stop
something happening ({防止|fáng zhǐ}{摔倒|shuāi dǎo}); {防|fáng} is the short, written form ({防火|fáng huǒ}, fire prevention). {定期|dìng qī} is
regular, at fixed intervals ({定期|dìng qī}{检查|jiǎn chá}, regular check-ups).

Two adjectives of urgency: {紧急|jǐn jí} (urgent, emergency: {紧急|jǐn jí}{情况|qíng kuàng}) and its opposite in speech, {不要紧|bú yào jǐn} (it's
nothing serious, never mind).

17).

### Sound parts and families

- {方|fāng} fāng, a sound series you know: {房|fáng} fáng, {放|fàng} fàng, {访|fǎng} (lesson 24), and now {防|fáng} fáng (阝 + {方|fāng}).
- 兆 zhào in {桃|táo} táo and in HSK 3's {跳|tiào} tiào: the sound has drifted, but the family is easy to see.
- {良|liáng} liáng from lesson 06 in {粮|liáng} liáng (rice {米|mǐ} + {良|liáng}); {农|nóng} nóng in {浓|nóng} nóng (water 氵 + {农|nóng}).
- {灰|huī} huī (grey, lesson 10) in {恢|huī} huī (heart 忄 + {灰|huī}); {了|le} liǎo in {疗|liáo} liáo.
- {率|lǜ} (lesson 03's {效率|xiào lǜ}, lǜ; also shuài) in {摔|shuāi} shuāi (hand 扌 + {率|lǜ}).
- {者|zhě} zhě in {煮|zhǔ} zhǔ; 乍 in {炸|zhá} zhá (compare {作|zuò} zuò, {昨|zuó} zuó, {怎|zěn} zěn); {每|měi} měi in {敏|mǐn} mǐn: all drifted.
- 疒 "sickness": {疾|jí} {疗|liáo}, with {病|bìng} {疼|téng} {痛|tòng} {瘦|shòu} from earlier levels. 攵 (a hand with a stick): {敏|mǐn} {救|jiù}, as in {教|jiāo} {收|shōu} {放|fàng} {改|gǎi}.
- {木|mù} "tree" for fruit: {桃|táo} {梨|lí} {橘|jú}, and {橙|chéng} from lesson 07.

### Look-alikes and stroke traps

- {玉|yù} and 王: {玉|yù} is 王 with a dot at the bottom right. The dot is the last stroke.
- {疾|jí} has 矢 (an arrow) inside 疒; {疗|liáo} has {了|le}. Write 疒 first: dot, horizontal, left-falling, then the two
  short strokes on the left (a dot and a rising stroke).
- {胃|wèi}: 田 on top, then ⺼ below (not {月|yuè} beside it). 9 strokes.
- {齿|chǐ}: {止|zhǐ} on top (4 strokes), then the box with {人|rén} inside it: the 凵 shape is written last.
- {救|jiù}: {求|qiú} on the left (its dot comes last), then 攵.
- {摔|shuāi}: 扌, then {率|lǜ} (亠, then 幺 in the middle, the two short strokes on its left and the two on its right, then {十|shí}).
- {煮|zhǔ}: {者|zhě} on top, 灬 below; {熬|áo} (lesson 06) is built the same way.

## Pronunciation

- {背|bèi} has two readings: bèi (the back, a noun) and bēi (to carry on the back, HSK 4). {背后|bèi hòu} (behind, lesson
  14) is bèi.
