- {尽快|jǐn kuài} jǐn kuài, {尽量|jǐn liàng} jǐn liàng: third tone. {尽力|jìn lì} (lesson 03) is jìn lì.
- {摔|shuāi} shuāi: three vowels in a row, *u-a-i*, and a first tone.
- {胃|wèi} wèi and {喂|wèi} wèi (hello; to feed, lesson 10): the same syllable.
- {疾病|jí bìng} jí bìng and {急诊|jí zhěn} jí zhěn: {疾|jí} and {急|jí} are both jí.

## Common mistakes

- ~~{请|qǐng}{你|nǐ}{连忙|lián máng}{来|lái}~~: {连忙|lián máng} and {急忙|jí máng} only narrate. A request takes {马上|mǎ shàng} or {立刻|lì kè}: {请|qǐng}{你|nǐ}{马上|mǎ shàng}{来|lái}.
- {他|tā}{立即|lì jí}{说|shuō}："{谢谢|xiè xie}。" is stiff in a story about a chat: {立即|lì jí} is for notices and formal writing. {他|tā}{连忙|lián máng}{说|shuō} or {他|tā}{马上|mǎ shàng}{说|shuō}
  is natural.
- ~~{我|wǒ}{一旦|yí dàn}{有|yǒu}{时间|shí jiān}{就|jiù}{去|qù}~~ for "whenever I have time": {一旦|yí dàn} is a single, often unwelcome turn of events. "Whenever"
  is {我|wǒ}{有|yǒu}{时间|shí jiān}{就|jiù}{去|qù} or {只要|zhǐ yào}{有|yǒu}{时间|shí jiān}{就|jiù}{去|qù}.
- ~~{他|tā}{慢|màn}{慢|màn}{地|de}{醒|xǐng}{起来|qǐ lái}{了|le}~~: back to consciousness is {过来|guò lái}: {他|tā}{慢|màn}{慢|màn}{醒|xǐng}{过来|guò lái}{了|le}.
- {着凉|zháo liáng} read zhe liáng: it's zháo liáng.

## Key points

- {马上|mǎ shàng} / {立刻|lì kè} / {立即|lì jí} / {赶紧|gǎn jǐn}: at once, also in requests ({立即|lì jí} written); {连忙|lián máng} / {急忙|jí máng}: hurriedly, in narration only.
- {尽快|jǐn kuài}: as soon as possible; {随时|suí shí}: at any time (or "at any moment").
- {一旦|yí dàn}…{就|jiù}: once (something happens), at once…; formal, often an unwelcome event.
- Extended direction complements: {过来|guò lái} back to normal ({醒|xǐng}{过来|guò lái}), {过去|guò qù} away from it ({晕|yūn}{过去|guò qù}), {起来|qǐ lái} a change begins
  ({好|hǎo}{起来|qǐ lái}), {下来|xià lái} settling ({安静|ān jìng}{下来|xià lái}), {下去|xià qù} continuing ({坚持|jiān chí}{下去|xià qù}).
- New characters: {橘|jú} {梨|lí} {粮|liáng} {浓|nóng} {蔬|shū} {桃|táo} {玉|yù} {炸|zhá} {煮|zhǔ} {防|fáng} {疾|jí} {敏|mǐn} {恢|huī} {诊|zhěn} {救|jiù} {抢|qiǎng} {胃|wèi} {摔|shuāi} {齿|chǐ} {疗|liáo} (✎ {玉|yù} {防|fáng} {胃|wèi} {疗|liáo}).

The words from this lesson are listed below; they join your vocabulary reviews when you complete
the lesson.

lessons.title: Furnishing, repairs and housework
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

HSK 4 rented a flat: the landlady {唐阿姨|Táng ā yí}, the keys, a broken window. Now {安娜|Ān nà} (Anna) and {王芳|Wáng Fāng} (Wang
Fang) want to make their flat in the {新城|Xīn chéng} compound their own. They turn a small storeroom into a
study, put up a bookshelf and break a glass, and the building's management sends a notice about
repairs.

The grammar is the {把|bǎ} sentence at HSK 5:

- **{把|bǎ} with two objects**: {把|bǎ}{钥匙|yào shi}{交|jiāo}{给|gěi}{师傅|shī fu} (give the keys to the workman), {把|bǎ}{储藏室|chǔ cáng shì}{改|gǎi}{成|chéng}{书房|shū fáng} (turn the storeroom
  into a study), {把|bǎ}{他|tā}{当|dàng}{朋友|péng you} (treat him as a friend);
- {把|bǎ} + {一|yī} + verb: {他|tā}{把|bǎ}{门|mén}{一|yì}{关|guān}，{就|jiù}{走|zǒu}{了|le} (he shut the door and was gone);
- the measure words {架|jià}, {套|tào} and {单元|dān yuán}.

You also get the words for rooms and furniture, for repairs and DIY, and for what things are like
(thin, soft, hard, square, tidy). The speaking task tells a story from three photos.

## {把|bǎ} with two objects

You know the {把|bǎ} sentence from HSK 3 and 4: {把|bǎ} brings the object forward, and the verb says what
happens to it, with something after it ({把|bǎ}{作业|zuò yè}{交|jiāo}{了|le}, {把|bǎ}{书|shū}{放|fàng}{在|zài}{桌子|zhuō zi}{上|shàng}). At HSK 5 the verb often has a second
object after it. The {把|bǎ} object is the thing handled; the second says who gets it, what it becomes,
or what it counts as.

| Pattern | Example | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| {把|bǎ} A + verb + {给|gěi} + B | {把|bǎ}{钥匙|yào shi}{交|jiāo}{给|gěi}{师傅|shī fu} | hand the keys to the workman |
| | {把|bǎ}{这|zhè}{本|běn}{书|shū}{送|sòng}{给|gěi}{她|tā} | give this book to her |
| {把|bǎ} A + verb + {成|chéng} + B | {把|bǎ}{储藏室|chǔ cáng shì}{改|gǎi}{成|chéng}{书房|shū fáng} | turn the storeroom into a study |
| | {把|bǎ}{这|zhè}{段|duàn}{话|huà}{翻译|fān yì}{成|chéng}{中文|Zhōng wén} | translate this passage into Chinese |
| {把|bǎ} A + {当|dàng}({作|zuò}) / {当成|dàng chéng} + B | {把|bǎ}{他|tā}{当|dàng}{朋友|péng you} | treat him as a friend |
| | {把|bǎ}{这儿|zhèr}{当作|dàng zuò}{自己|zì jǐ}{的|de}{家|jiā} | make yourself at home ("treat this as your own home") |

{我|wǒ}{出去|chū qù}{一下|yí xià}，{你|nǐ}{把|bǎ}{安装费|ān zhuāng fèi}{交|jiāo}{给|gěi}{送|sòng}{书架|shū jià}{的|de}{师傅|shī fu}{吧|ba}。 — I'm popping out: give the installation fee to the man delivering the bookshelf, would you.

{我们|wǒ men}{把|bǎ}{阳台|yáng tái}{改|gǎi}{成|chéng}{了|le}{一|yí}{个|gè}{小|xiǎo}{花园|huā yuán}。 — We've turned the balcony into a little garden.

{房东|fáng dōng}{把|bǎ}{这|zhè}{套|tào}{公寓|gōng yù}{租|zū}{给|gěi}{了|le}{两|liǎng}{个|gè}{学生|xué sheng}。 — The landlord let this flat to two students.

{请|qǐng}{把|bǎ}{这个|zhè ge}{词|cí}{写|xiě}{成|chéng}{汉字|hàn zì}。 — Please write this word in characters.

Three things to keep in mind:

- The {把|bǎ} object is something definite: these keys, that room. {把|bǎ}{一些|yì xiē}{钥匙|yào shi}{交|jiāo}{给|gěi}{他|tā} is unusual; {把|bǎ}{钥匙|yào shi}{交|jiāo}{给|gěi}{他|tā} is
  "the keys".
- {了|le} comes after the verb, or after the whole phrase: {把|bǎ}{阳台|yáng tái}{改|gǎi}{成|chéng}{了|le}{花园|huā yuán} / {把|bǎ}{阳台|yáng tái}{改|gǎi}{成|chéng}{花园|huā yuán}{了|le}.
- {当|dàng} here is dàng, "to treat as" (lesson 12's word): {别|bié}{把|bǎ}{我|wǒ}{当|dàng}{孩子|hái zi} (don't treat me like a child). {当作|dàng zuò} and
  {当成|dàng chéng} are its fuller forms, both common.

The negative and modal verbs go before {把|bǎ}, as always: {你|nǐ}{别|bié}{把|bǎ}{钥匙|yào shi}{交|jiāo}{给|gěi}{别人|bié ren} (don't give the keys to anyone
else); {我|wǒ}{想|xiǎng}{把|bǎ}{书房|shū fáng}{改|gǎi}{成|chéng}{卧室|wò shì}.

## {把|bǎ} + {一|yī} + verb: one quick action, and its result

{把|bǎ} + object + {一|yī} + a verb (usually of one syllable) tells of a single, sudden movement. A second clause, often with
{就|jiù}, says what followed. It belongs to storytelling:

{他|tā}{把|bǎ}{门|mén}{一|yì}{关|guān}，{就|jiù}{走|zǒu}{了|le}。 — He shut the door and was off.

{她|tā}{把|bǎ}{被子|bèi zi}{一|yí}{盖|gài}，{就|jiù}{睡着|shuì zháo}{了|le}。 — She pulled up the duvet and fell straight asleep.

{师傅|shī fu}{把|bǎ}{书架|shū jià}{一|yì}{推|tuī}，{它|tā}{就|jiù}{移|yí}{过去|guò qù}{了|le}。 — The workman gave the bookshelf a push, and it slid across.

{我|wǒ}{把|bǎ}{窗户|chuāng hu}{一|yì}{打开|dǎ kāi}，{外面|wài miàn}{的|de}{声音|shēng yīn}{就|jiù}{进来|jìn lái}{了|le}。 — The moment I opened the window, the noise came in.

{一|yī} here is said with its normal tone change (yì before {关|guān}, yí before {放|fàng}): {把|bǎ}{门|mén}{一|yì}{关|guān} yì guān, {把|bǎ}{书|shū}{一|yí}{放|fàng} yí fàng. Don't
confuse it with the light {一|yi} of V{一|yi}V ({看一看|kàn yi kàn}: have a look).

## {架|jià}, {套|tào} and {单元|dān yuán}: three measure words

| Measure word | For | Example |
|---|---|---|
| {架|jià} | planes; pianos; things on a frame | {一|yí}{架|jià}{飞机|fēi jī}, {一|yí}{架|jià}{钢琴|gāng qín} (a piano), {两|liǎng}{架|jià}{照相机|zhào xiàng jī} |
| {套|tào} | a set; a flat | {一|yí}{套|tào}{家具|jiā jù} (a set of furniture), {一|yí}{套|tào}{衣服|yī fu} (a suit, an outfit), {一|yí}{套|tào}{书|shū}, {一|yí}{套|tào}{公寓|gōng yù} (a flat) |
| {单元|dān yuán} | a unit, an entrance (of a block of flats); a unit (of a course) | {三|sān}{号|hào}{楼|lóu}{二|èr}{单元|dān yuán} (Building 3, Entrance 2), {第|dì}{五|wǔ}{单元|dān yuán} |

As nouns, {架|jià} is a frame or shelf ({书架|shū jià}, bookshelf), {套|tào} a cover or case. A Chinese address often gives
the building ({楼|lóu}), the entrance ({单元|dān yuán}) and the flat number: {新城|Xīn chéng}{小区|xiǎo qū}{三|sān}{号|hào}{楼|lóu}{二|èr}{单元|dān yuán}1201 (Xincheng compound,
Building 3, Entrance 2, flat 1201). {一|yí}{套|tào}{房子|fáng zi} is a flat or house to own or rent, counted as one set of rooms.

## Words: rooms and furniture

Housing. {住房|zhù fáng} is housing ({住房|zhù fáng}{问题|wèn tí}); {公寓|gōng yù} is a block of flats or a flat in one, the written word (in
speech, {房子|fáng zi}); {中介|zhōng jiè} is an estate agency or agent ("go-between"); {租金|zū jīn} is rent (written; HSK 4's {房租|fáng zū} is the
everyday word); {物业|wù yè} is the building's management company ({物业|wù yè}{费|fèi}, the service charge).

Rooms. {卧室|wò shì} bedroom, {书房|shū fáng} study, {阳台|yáng tái} balcony, {车库|chē kù} garage ({库|kù} alone is a store, a warehouse), {窗台|chuāng tái} windowsill,
{台阶|tái jiē} steps. {空间|kōng jiān} is space, room ({空间|kōng jiān}{很|hěn}{大|dà}: there's lots of room); {墙|qiáng} is a wall; {里头|lǐ tou} is the spoken "inside"
({里头|lǐ tou}{没有|méi yǒu}{人|rén}). With the traditional script on, {台|tái} stays {台|tái} in all these words (but {台灯|tái dēng}, below, is {+{台灯|tái dēng}+}).

Furniture and things. {柜子|guì zi} cupboard, {书架|shū jià} bookshelf, {台灯|tái dēng} desk lamp, {被子|bèi zi} quilt, duvet, {床单|chuáng dān} bed sheet, {拖鞋|tuō xié}
slippers. {电器|diàn qì} and {家电|jiā diàn} are electrical and household appliances; {日用品|rì yòng pǐn} daily necessities, {用品|yòng pǐn} articles,
supplies ({学习|xué xí}{用品|yòng pǐn}, {厨房|chú fáng}{用品|yòng pǐn}); {物品|wù pǐn} articles, belongings (written: {个人|gè rén}{物品|wù pǐn}). The tools: {工具|gōng jù} a tool, {剪刀|jiǎn dāo} scissors
({剪|jiǎn} is to cut with them), {锁|suǒ} a lock or to lock, {盆|pén} a basin or pot ({花盆|huā pén}, a flowerpot). Materials: {玻璃|bō li} glass,
{木头|mù tou} wood.

| Spoken | Written |
|---|---|
| {房子|fáng zi} | {公寓|gōng yù}, {住房|zhù fáng} |
| {房租|fáng zū} | {租金|zū jīn} |
| {东西|dōng xi} | {物品|wù pǐn}, {用品|yòng pǐn} |
| {里面|lǐ miàn}, {里头|lǐ tou} | {内|nèi} |

## Words: doing up a flat

{装修|zhuāng xiū} is to renovate, fit out a flat (paint, floors, kitchen); {装饰|zhuāng shì} to decorate (pictures, plants,
colours); {安装|ān zhuāng} to install, put up ({安装|ān zhuāng}{空调|kōng tiáo}, {安装|ān zhuāng}{书架|shū jià}); {维修|wéi xiū} to maintain, repair (written; {修|xiū} and {修理|xiū lǐ} are HSK 4);
{更换|gēng huàn} to replace (written: {更换|gēng huàn}{水管|shuǐ guǎn}). {动手|dòng shǒu} is to set to work, do it oneself ({自己|zì jǐ}{动手|dòng shǒu}). {存放|cún fàng} is to keep, store.

The verbs of handling things are short and exact:

| Verb | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| {插|chā} | to insert, plug in | {把|bǎ}{电|diàn}{插|chā}{上|shàng} (plug it in) |
| {拆|chāi} | to take apart, pull down | {拆|chāi}{墙|qiáng} (knock down a wall), {拆|chāi}{开|kāi} (unpack) |
| {盖|gài} | to cover; to build; a lid | {盖|gài}{被子|bèi zi} (pull up the duvet), {盖|gài}{房子|fáng zi} (build a house), {锅|guō}{盖|gài} (a lid) |
| {隔|gé} | to separate; at intervals | {隔|gé}{一|yì}{天|tiān} (every other day) |
| {移|yí} | to move (a thing) | {把|bǎ}{书架|shū jià}{往|wǎng}{左|zuǒ}{移|yí}{一点儿|yì diǎnr} |
| {堆|duī} | to pile up; a pile | {东西|dōng xi}{堆|duī}{在|zài}{门口|mén kǒu} |
| {捡|jiǎn} | to pick up | {把|bǎ}{地上|dì shang}{的|de}{纸|zhǐ}{捡|jiǎn}{起来|qǐ lái} |
| {浇|jiāo} | to water, pour on | {浇|jiāo}{花|huā} (water the plants) |
| {洒|sǎ} | to spill, sprinkle | {水|shuǐ}{洒|sǎ}{了|le}{一|yí}{地|dì} (water all over the floor) |
| {摸|mō} | to touch, feel | {他|tā}{摸|mō}{了|le}{摸|mō}{孩子|hái zi}{的|de}{头|tóu} (he stroked the child's head) |
| {漏|lòu} | to leak | {水管|shuǐ guǎn}{漏|lòu}{水|shuǐ}{了|le} (the pipe's leaking) |
| {碎|suì} | broken to pieces | {杯子|bēi zi}{摔|shuāi}{碎|suì}{了|le} (the glass smashed) |
| {调|tiáo} | to adjust | {把|bǎ}{空调|kōng tiáo}{的|de}{温度|wēn dù}{调|tiáo}{高|gāo}{一点儿|yì diǎnr} |

{调|tiáo} is tiáo here, as in {调整|tiáo zhěng} (lesson 06) and {空调|kōng tiáo}; the {调|diào} of lesson 02 (to transfer) is a different
word. {随手|suí shǒu} is "as you go, without extra effort": {随手|suí shǒu}{关|guān}{门|mén} (close the door behind you), {随手|suí shǒu}{关|guān}{灯|dēng}. {家务|jiā wù} is
housework ({做|zuò}{家务|jiā wù}).

What things are like: {薄|báo} (báo) thin ({薄|báo}{被子|bèi zi}, a thin duvet; opposite {厚|hòu}, HSK 4), {软|ruǎn} soft, {硬|yìng} hard, {方|fāng} square
({方|fāng}{桌|zhuō}, a square table), {单|dān} single ({单|dān}{人|rén}{床|chuáng}, a single bed; also {单|dān} "a list, a bill" as in {菜单|cài dān}), {舒适|shū shì} comfortable
(written; {舒服|shū fu} is the everyday word), {整齐|zhěng qí} tidy, neat ({房间|fáng jiān}{收拾|shōu shi}{得|de}{很|hěn}{整齐|zhěng qí}).

## Characters
{=

| Character | Meaning | Pinyin | Radical | Strokes | Words |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| {旦|dàn} ✎ | dawn; day | dàn | {日|rì} | 5 | {一旦|yí dàn} (lesson 08), {元旦|yuán dàn} (lesson 25) |
| {治|zhì} ✎ | govern; treat | zhì | 氵 | 8 | {治|zhì}, {治疗|zhì liáo} (lesson 08) |
| {咨|zī} (in {咨询|zī xún}: traditional {+{咨询|zī xún}+}) | consult | zī | {口|kǒu} | 9 | {咨询|zī xún} (lesson 08) |
| {询|xún} (traditional {+{询|xún}+}) | enquire | xún | 讠 | 8 | {咨询|zī xún} (lesson 08), {询问|xún wèn} (lesson 15) |
| {玻|bō} | glass | bō | 王 | 9 | {玻璃|bō li} |
| {璃|lí} | glass | lí (light in {玻璃|bō li}) | 王 | 14 | {玻璃|bō li} |
| {库|kù} (traditional {+{库|kù}+}) | storehouse | kù | {广|guǎng} | 7 | {库|kù}, {车库|chē kù} |
| {插|chā} | insert | chā | 扌 | 12 | {插|chā} |
| {拆|chāi} | take apart | chāi | 扌 | 8 | {拆|chāi} |
| {薄|báo} | thin | báo | 艹 | 16 | {薄|báo} |
| {器|qì} | utensil; device | qì | {口|kǒu} | 16 | {电器|diàn qì}, {机器|jī qì} (lesson 19) |
| {盖|gài} (traditional {+{盖|gài}+}) | cover; lid | gài | 皿 | 11 | {盖|gài} |
| {堆|duī} | pile | duī | {土|tǔ} | 11 | {堆|duī} |
| {隔|gé} | separate | gé | 阝 | 12 | {隔|gé} |
| {寓|yù} | residence | yù | 宀 | 12 | {公寓|gōng yù} |
| {柜|guì} ✎ (traditional {+{柜|guì}+}) | cupboard | guì | {木|mù} | 8 | {柜子|guì zi} |
| {架|jià} ✎ | frame, shelf | jià | {木|mù} | 9 | {架|jià}, {书架|shū jià} |
| {剪|jiǎn} | cut (with scissors) | jiǎn | {刀|dāo} | 11 | {剪|jiǎn}, {剪刀|jiǎn dāo} |
| {捡|jiǎn} (traditional {+{捡|jiǎn}+}) | pick up | jiǎn | 扌 | 10 | {捡|jiǎn} |
| {浇|jiāo} (traditional {+{浇|jiāo}+}) | pour; water | jiāo | 氵 | 9 | {浇|jiāo} |

Seven differ in traditional: {+{询|xún}+} ({言|yán}, 13 strokes), {+{库|kù}+} (車 in {广|guǎng}, 10), {+{盖|gài}+} (14), {+{柜|guì}+} ({木|mù} + 匱, 18),
{+捡+} (僉, 16), {+浇+} (堯, 15), and 咨, which Taiwan writes {+咨询+} in this word: 諮 (16 strokes) has 言 on
the left. Alone, {咨|zī} doesn't change.

### Sound parts and families

- {离|lí} lí in {璃|lí} (an exact match); {皮|pí} pí in {玻|bō} bō, as in 波 bō (a wave) and {破|pò} pò (HSK 4).
- 禺 in {寓|yù} yù, as in {遇|yù} yù ({遇到|yù dào}, HSK 4): roof 宀 + 禺.
- 佥 in {捡|jiǎn} jiǎn, the family of {检|jiǎn} jiǎn ({检查|jiǎn chá}), {脸|liǎn} liǎn, {险|xiǎn} xiǎn, {签|qiān} qiān: all with the same right or top part.

"**Notice.** To all residents: Because of a leaking pipe in Entrance 2 of Building 3, the management
will carry out repairs from 9 a.m. to 12 noon this Saturday, replacing the old pipes. During the
repairs the water in Building 3 will be off; please store water in advance. The garage will also be out
of use: please park at the compound gate. Residents of Entrance 2 are also asked to move things away
from the kitchen pipes so that the workmen can get at them. If you have any questions, please ask at the
management office. Thank you for your co-operation! Xincheng Compound Management, 10 January.

**Our new study.** The flat Wang Fang and I live in isn't big: just two bedrooms, a living room and a
tiny storeroom. The storeroom was piled high with boxes, and we'd long wanted to turn it into a
study. Before, we both studied and worked at the living-room table, which was awkward: one reading,
the other on the phone, and neither getting anything done. Last weekend we finally got to work. First we moved the boxes onto the balcony and threw away
everything we didn't need. Our landlady, {唐阿姨|Táng ā yí}, said we could decorate any way we liked as long as we
didn't knock down any walls. We didn't spend much on doing it up; we just did it ourselves: we hung a
few pictures on the wall, put a plant on the windowsill and bought a wooden bookshelf and a desk lamp
online. The man who delivered the bookshelf put it together for us; with one push, it
slid over to the wall. Now our little study is comfortable and tidy. I write my thesis here, and Wang
Fang her reports. We even have a rule: whoever leaves the study last turns off the light. Wang Fang says it's her favourite room, because
it's quiet and sunny."

<summary>A model story</summary>

{小王|Xiǎo Wáng}{终于|zhōng yú}{租|zū}{到|dào}{了|le}{一|yí}{套|tào}{自己|zì jǐ}{的|de}{公寓|gōng yù}。{房子|fáng zi}{不|bú}{大|dà}，{但是|dàn shì}{空间|kōng jiān}{不错|bú cuò}，{里头|lǐ tou}{什么|shén me}{都|dōu}{没有|méi yǒu}。{周末|zhōu mò}，{他|tā}{请|qǐng}{朋友|péng you}{来|lái}{帮忙|bāng máng}。{他们|tā men}{先|xiān}{把|bǎ}{沙发|shā fā}{搬|bān}{上|shàng}{了|le}{台阶|tái jiē}，{又|yòu}{把|bǎ}{书架|shū jià}{安装|ān zhuāng}{在|zài}{墙|qiáng}{上|shàng}。{朋友|péng you}{说|shuō}{书架|shū jià}{有点儿|yǒu diǎnr}{斜|xié}，{小王|Xiǎo Wáng}{就|jiù}{把|bǎ}{它|tā}{往|wǎng}{左|zuǒ}{移|yí}{了|le}{一点儿|yì diǎnr}。{忙|máng}{了|le}{一|yì}{整|zhěng}{天|tiān}，{房间|fáng jiān}{收拾|shōu shi}{得|de}{整整齐齐|zhěng zhěng qí qí}。{晚上|wǎn shang}，{两|liǎng}{个|gè}{人|rén}{坐|zuò}{在|zài}{新|xīn}{沙发|shā fā}{上|shàng}，{累|lèi}{得|de}{一|yí}{句|jù}{话|huà}{都|dōu}{不|bù}{想|xiǎng}{说|shuō}，{可是|kě shì}{心里|xīn li}{都|dōu}{很|hěn}{高兴|gāo xìng}。

(144 characters. {斜|xié} xié: crooked, lesson 22.)

"Xiao Wang has finally rented a flat of his own. It isn't big, but there's a decent amount of space,
and there's nothing in it. At the weekend he asked a friend to help. First they carried the sofa up
the steps, then put the bookshelf up on the wall. His friend said it was a bit crooked, so Xiao Wang
moved it a little to the left. After a whole day's work the room was neat and tidy. In the evening
the two of them sat on the new sofa, too tired to say a word, but happy."
</details>

## Say it

```speak
# At home
{我们|wǒ men}{把|bǎ}{储藏室|chǔ cáng shì}{改|gǎi}{成|chéng}{了|le}{书房|shū fáng}。
= We've turned the storeroom into a study.
{你|nǐ}{把|bǎ}{钥匙|yào shi}{交|jiāo}{给|gěi}{师傅|shī fu}{吧|ba}。
= Give the keys to the workman.
{别|bié}{把|bǎ}{我|wǒ}{当|dàng}{孩子|hái zi}。
= Don't treat me like a child.
{他|tā}{把|bǎ}{门|mén}{一|yì}{关|guān}，{就|jiù}{走|zǒu}{了|le}。
= He shut the door and was off.
{请|qǐng}{随手|suí shǒu}{关|guān}{灯|dēng}。
= Please turn off the light behind you.
{这|zhè}{套|tào}{公寓|gōng yù}{又|yòu}{舒适|shū shì}{又|yòu}{整齐|zhěng qí}。
= This flat is comfortable and tidy.
```

## Pronunciation

- {薄|báo} báo (thin) is second tone here. In written words such as {薄弱|bó ruò} it's bó; learn báo for "thin".
- {调|tiáo} (to adjust) and {调|diào} (to transfer, lesson 02): same character, different words.
- {剪|jiǎn} jiǎn and {捡|jiǎn} jiǎn: the same syllable, the same tone. Context tells them apart ({剪|jiǎn}{纸|zhǐ}, cutting paper; {捡|jiǎn}{起来|qǐ lái},
  pick up).
- {玻璃|bō li} bō li: the second syllable is light. {木头|mù tou} mù tou and {里头|lǐ tou} lǐ tou end in a light *tou*.
- {插|chā} chā and {拆|chāi} chāi: *a* and *ai*, both first tone.
- {一|yī} in {把|bǎ}{门|mén}{一|yì}{关|guān} is yì (before a first tone); in {把|bǎ}{书架|shū jià}{一|yì}{推|tuī} yì too; before a fourth tone, yí ({把|bǎ}{书|shū}{一|yí}{放|fàng}, yí fàng).

## Common mistakes

- ~~{我|wǒ}{把|bǎ}{钥匙|yào shi}{交|jiāo}{他|tā}~~: after {交|jiāo}, the person needs {给|gěi}: {我|wǒ}{把|bǎ}{钥匙|yào shi}{交|jiāo}{给|gěi}{他|tā}.
- ~~{把|bǎ}{阳台|yáng tái}{改|gǎi}{花园|huā yuán}~~: the result needs {成|chéng}: {把|bǎ}{阳台|yáng tái}{改|gǎi}{成|chéng}{花园|huā yuán}.
- ~~{我|wǒ}{没有|méi yǒu}{把|bǎ}{房间|fáng jiān}{改|gǎi}{成|chéng}{卧室|wò shì}{了|le}~~: a negative {把|bǎ} sentence doesn't take {了|le}: {我|wǒ}{没有|méi yǒu}{把|bǎ}{房间|fáng jiān}{改|gǎi}{成|chéng}{卧室|wò shì}.
- {把|bǎ} + {一|yī} + verb on its own, ~~{他|tā}{把|bǎ}{门|mén}{一|yì}{关|guān}。~~: the pattern needs a second clause saying what followed: {他|tā}{把|bǎ}{门|mén}{一|yì}{关|guān}，{就|jiù}{走|zǒu}{了|le}。
- {舒适|shū shì} in a chat: {这个|zhè ge}{沙发|shā fā}{很|hěn}{舒适|shū shì} is fine but formal; friends say {这个|zhè ge}{沙发|shā fā}{很|hěn}{舒服|shū fu}.
- {薄|báo} read bó for "thin": it's báo.

## Key points

- {把|bǎ} A + verb + {给|gěi} B (hand to), + {成|chéng} B (turn into), + {当|dàng}({作|zuò}) B (treat as): {把|bǎ}{钥匙|yào shi}{交|jiāo}{给|gěi}{他|tā}, {把|bǎ}{阳台|yáng tái}{改|gǎi}{成|chéng}{花园|huā yuán}, {把|bǎ}{他|tā}{当|dàng}{朋友|péng you}.
- {把|bǎ} + object + {一|yī} + verb, {就|jiù}…: one quick action and what followed ({把|bǎ}{门|mén}{一|yì}{关|guān}，{就|jiù}{走|zǒu}{了|le}).
- {架|jià} (planes, pianos; {书架|shū jià}), {套|tào} (a set; {一|yí}{套|tào}{公寓|gōng yù}), {单元|dān yuán} (an entrance of a block; a unit of a course).
- Written and spoken home words: {公寓|gōng yù} / {房子|fáng zi}, {租金|zū jīn} / {房租|fáng zū}, {物品|wù pǐn} / {东西|dōng xi}, {舒适|shū shì} / {舒服|shū fu}.
- New characters: {旦|dàn} {治|zhì} {咨|zī} {询|xún} {玻|bō} {璃|lí} {库|kù} {插|chā} {拆|chāi} {薄|báo} {器|qì} {盖|gài} {堆|duī} {隔|gé} {寓|yù} {柜|guì} {架|jià} {剪|jiǎn} {捡|jiǎn} {浇|jiāo} (✎ {旦|dàn} {治|zhì} {柜|guì} {架|jià}).

The words from this lesson are listed below; they join your vocabulary reviews when you complete
the lesson.

lessons.title: Arts, crafts and hobbies
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

The last lesson of the module is about free time well spent: painting, photography, music, dance,
crafts and pets. {安娜|Ān nà} (Anna), who is writing her thesis on porcelain with {罗教授|Luó jiào shòu} (Professor Luo), takes
{大卫|Dà wèi} (David) to an exhibition at the museum where she hopes to work after graduating. David, busy with
the company he has just started with {白涛|Bái Tāo} (Bai Tao), needs the break.

The grammar is a pair of four-character patterns and some words for counting and liking:

- {说|shuō}A{就|jiù}A: {说|shuō}{走|zǒu}{就|jiù}{走|zǒu} (off the moment it's said);
- {没|méi}A{没|méi}B: {没完没了|méi wán méi liǎo} (endless), {没日没夜|méi rì méi yè} (day and night);
- the measure words {支|zhī} ({一|yì}{支|zhī}{歌|gē}, a song) and {匹|pǐ} ({一|yì}{匹|pǐ}{马|mǎ}, a horse);
- {好|hào}, "to be fond of": {好学|hào xué}, {好动|hào dòng}, {好客|hào kè}.

You also get the words of the arts and of exhibitions, colours ({红|hóng}, {青|qīng}, {紫|zǐ}, {灰色|huī sè}, {五颜六色|wǔ yán liù sè}), and the
words for being keen on something ({热爱|rè ài}, {擅长|shàn cháng}, {迷|mí}). The reading is an exhibition notice and a short
newspaper profile, the kind {王芳|Wáng Fāng} (Wang Fang) writes.

## {说|shuō}A{就|jiù}A: no sooner said than done

{说|shuō} + a verb + {就|jiù} + the same verb describes doing something the moment it's mentioned, with no
planning and no delay. It can be admiring (decisive, spontaneous) or critical (impulsive):

{他们|tā men}{说|shuō}{走|zǒu}{就|jiù}{走|zǒu}，{第|dì}{二|èr}{天|tiān}{就|jiù}{去|qù}{了|le}{海|hǎi}{边|biān}。 — No sooner said than done: they were at the seaside the next day.

{这儿|zhèr}{的|de}{天气|tiān qì}{说|shuō}{变|biàn}{就|jiù}{变|biàn}，{你|nǐ}{带|dài}{上|shàng}{伞|sǎn}{吧|ba}。 — The weather here changes in an instant: take an umbrella.

{孩子|hái zi}{说|shuō}{哭|kū}{就|jiù}{哭|kū}，{说|shuō}{笑|xiào}{就|jiù}{笑|xiào}。 — Children cry one moment and laugh the next.

The verb is usually one syllable ({走|zǒu}, {来|lái}, {变|biàn}, {哭|kū}, {做|zuò}). {说|shuō}{走|zǒu}{就|jiù}{走|zǒu}{的|de}{旅行|lǚ xíng} (a trip taken on the spur of the moment)
is a popular phrase, used as an attributive with {的|de}.

## {没|méi}A{没|méi}B: without… or…

{没|méi} + A + {没|méi} + B, with A and B a pair of opposites or near-synonyms, makes a four-character phrase that is
nearly always critical:

| Phrase | Literally | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|---|
| {没完没了|méi wán méi liǎo} | no end, no finish | endless, on and on | {他|tā}{的|de}{电话|diàn huà}{没完没了|méi wán méi liǎo}。 His phone calls never stop. |
| {没日没夜|méi rì méi yè} | no day, no night | day and night | {她|tā}{没日没夜|méi rì méi yè}{地|de}{工作|gōng zuò}。 She works day and night. |
| {没大没小|méi dà méi xiǎo} | no old, no young | cheeky to one's elders | {这|zhè}{孩子|hái zi}{没大没小|méi dà méi xiǎo}{的|de}。 This child has no respect for their elders. |

These phrases work like adjectives or adverbs: {没完没了|méi wán méi liǎo}{的|de}{会|huì} (an endless meeting), {没日没夜|méi rì méi yè}{地|de}{练习|liàn xí} (practise day
and night). The pattern doesn't make new phrases freely: learn these as set expressions. They're
lively spoken style, also common in stories.

## {支|zhī} and {匹|pǐ}: two measure words

| Measure word | For | Example |
|---|---|---|
| {支|zhī} | songs and tunes; pens; teams; long thin things | {一|yì}{支|zhī}{歌|gē}, {一|yì}{支|zhī}{笔|bǐ}, {一|yì}{支|zhī}{球队|qiú duì} |
| {匹|pǐ} | horses; a length of cloth | {一|yì}{匹|pǐ}{马|mǎ}, {一|yì}{匹|pǐ}{布|bù} (a bolt of cloth; {布|bù} bù) |

For songs, HSK 4's {首|shǒu} is more common ({一|yì}{首|shǒu}{歌|gē}); {支|zhī} belongs to songs and tunes played or sung ({唱|chàng}{一|yì}{支|zhī}{歌|gē}). {支|zhī} is also a verb in later levels (to prop up).

{他|tā}{唱|chàng}{了|le}{一|yì}{支|zhī}{很|hěn}{好听|hǎo tīng}{的|de}{歌|gē}。 — He sang a lovely song.

{草地|cǎo dì}{上|shàng}{有|yǒu}{几|jǐ}{匹|pǐ}{马|mǎ}。 — There are a few horses in the field.

## {好|hào}: to be fond of

You've known {好|hǎo} (good) since your first lesson, and {爱好|ài hào} ài hào (a hobby) is read with the other tone.
{好|hào} is a verb: "to like, to be fond of, to be given to". It mostly makes adjectives that describe
someone's nature, with a one-syllable verb after it:

| Word | Meaning |
|---|---|
| {好学|hào xué} hào xué | eager to learn, studious |
| {好动|hào dòng} hào dòng | always on the move, restless |
| {好客|hào kè} hào kè | hospitable (fond of guests) |
| {好奇|hào qí} hào qí | curious (lesson 19) |

{这个|zhè ge}{孩子|hái zi}{很|hěn}{好动|hào dòng}，{一|yì}{分钟|fēn zhōng}{也|yě}{坐不住|zuò bu zhù}。 — This child never stops moving: can't sit still for a minute.

{那里|nà lǐ}{的|de}{人|rén}{非常|fēi cháng}{好客|hào kè}。 — The people there are very hospitable.

So {好|hǎo} is hǎo when it's "good" ({好看|hǎo kàn}, {好吃|hǎo chī}, {好|hǎo}{学生|xué sheng}) and hào when it's "fond of" ({好学|hào xué}, {爱好|ài hào}). {好学|hào xué} hào xué
(studious) and {好|hǎo}{学|xué} hǎo xué (easy to learn) are written the same: {这个|zhè ge}{孩子|hái zi}{很|hěn}{好学|hào xué} (hào), but {汉语|Hàn yǔ}{不|bù}{好|hǎo}{学|xué} (hǎo).

## Words: the arts

Painting. {美术|měi shù} is fine art ({美术|měi shù}{学院|xué yuàn}, an art school); {国画|guó huà} Chinese painting, with {毛笔|máo bǐ} (a writing brush) and ink;
{图画|tú huà} a picture, a drawing (in children's books); {色彩|sè cǎi} colour, colours ({色彩|sè cǎi}{很|hěn}{淡|dàn}: pale colours) and
{彩色|cǎi sè} coloured, in colour ({彩色|cǎi sè}{照片|zhào piàn}). {画面|huà miàn} is the picture you see, on a screen or in a painting.

Colours. {红|hóng} (red) you know, but HSK 5 adds a sense: popular, famous ({这|zhè}{首|shǒu}{歌|gē}{现在|xiàn zài}{很|hěn}{红|hóng}: this song is big now).
{青|qīng} is a blue-green, the colour of the sky or of grass, mostly in set words ({青|qīng}{山|shān}, green hills); {紫|zǐ} is
purple; {灰色|huī sè} grey. {五颜六色|wǔ yán liù sè} is the idiom for "every colour": five colours, six colours, so "all the
colours". It describes things directly ({五颜六色|wǔ yán liù sè}{的|de}{气球|qì qiú}, balloons of every colour; {气球|qì qiú} qìqiú is lesson 15's word) or as a predicate ({公园|gōng yuán}{里|lǐ}{的|de}{花|huā}
{五颜六色|wǔ yán liù sè}).

Performing. {戏|xì} is a play or an opera ({看|kàn}{戏|xì}, to see a show); {戏剧|xì jù} drama as an art; {剧场|jù chǎng} a theatre; {舞台|wǔ tái} a stage
({台|tái} stays {台|tái} in traditional); {舞蹈|wǔ dǎo} dance (as an art; {跳舞|tiào wǔ} is to dance); {武术|wǔ shù} martial arts; {鼓|gǔ} a drum ({打|dǎ}{鼓|gǔ}, to
play the drums); {歌曲|gē qǔ} a song, {歌词|gē cí} lyrics. On screen: {导演|dǎo yǎn} a director, to direct; {角色|jué sè} (jué sè) a role, a
part; {明星|míng xīng} a star; {动画|dòng huà} animation, a cartoon; {拍摄|pāi shè} to film, to shoot; {摄影|shè yǐng} photography.

Making. {手工|shǒu gōng} is handmade, by hand ({手工|shǒu gōng}{制作|zhì zuò}); {工艺|gōng yì} a craft, craftsmanship ({手工艺|shǒu gōng yì}, handicraft); {设计|shè jì} design, to
design; {创作|chuàng zuò} to create (a work of art), a creation; {制作|zhì zuò} to make, produce (a programme, a model, a dish);
{风格|fēng gé} style; {独特|dú tè} unique, distinctive; {经典|jīng diǎn} a classic, classic.

Exhibitions. {博物馆|bó wù guǎn} a museum; {展览|zhǎn lǎn} an exhibition, to exhibit; {展出|zhǎn chū} to be on show; {展示|zhǎn shì} to display, show; {展现|zhǎn xiàn}
to show, reveal (a quality: {展现|zhǎn xiàn}{了|le}{城市|chéng shì}{的|de}{色彩|sè cǎi}). {欣赏|xīn shǎng} is to appreciate, enjoy (art, music, a view) and to
admire (a person); {鼓掌|gǔ zhǎng} to clap, applaud, and {掌声|zhǎng shēng} applause.

| Word | Used for | Example |
|---|---|---|
| {展出|zhǎn chū} | what is on show | {博物馆|bó wù guǎn}{展出|zhǎn chū}{了|le}{一百|yì bǎi}{多|duō}{件|jiàn}{作品|zuò pǐn}。 |
| {展示|zhǎn shì} | showing something to people | {他|tā}{向|xiàng}{大家|dà jiā}{展示|zhǎn shì}{了|le}{自己|zì jǐ}{的|de}{作品|zuò pǐn}。 |
| {展现|zhǎn xiàn} | revealing a quality, a side | {这些|zhè xiē}{照片|zhào piàn}{展现|zhǎn xiàn}{了|le}{老|lǎo}{城|chéng}{的|de}{美|měi}。 |
| {展览|zhǎn lǎn} | the exhibition itself | {这个|zhè ge}{展览|zhǎn lǎn}{下|xià}{个|gè}{月|yuè}{结束|jié shù}。 |

## Words: keen on it

| Word | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| {热爱|rè ài} | to love (deeply, a cause, an art) | {他|tā}{热爱|rè ài}{音乐|yīn yuè}。 |
| {擅长|shàn cháng} | to be good at | {她|tā}{擅长|shàn cháng}{画|huà}{国画|guó huà}。 |
| {迷|mí} | to be crazy about; a fan | {他|tā}{迷|mí}{上|shàng}{了|le}{摄影|shè yǐng}；{球迷|qiú mí} (a football fan) |
| {乐趣|lè qù} | pleasure, fun | {画|huà}{画儿|huàr}{给|gěi}{我|wǒ}{带|dài}{来|lái}{很|hěn}{多|duō}{乐趣|lè qù}。 |
| {业余|yè yú} | spare-time, amateur | {业余|yè yú}{画家|huà jiā} (an amateur painter), {业余|yè yú}{时间|shí jiān} |
| {户外|hù wài} | outdoors | {户外|hù wài}{活动|huó dòng} (outdoor activities) |

The adjectives of praise: {了不起|liǎo bu qǐ} (amazing, remarkable: {你|nǐ}{真|zhēn}{了不起|liǎo bu qǐ}！), {完美|wán měi} (perfect), {优美|yōu měi} (graceful, of
music, dance or scenery), {动人|dòng rén} (moving), {超级|chāo jí} (super, spoken: {超级|chāo jí}{好看|hǎo kàn}). And the strong ones: {疯狂|fēng kuáng} (crazy,
wild), {激烈|jī liè} (fierce, intense: {激烈|jī liè}{的|de}{比赛|bǐ sài}).

Pets and play. {宠物|chǒng wù} is a pet; {={喂|wèi}=} to feed ({喂|wèi}{猫|māo}, {喂|wèi}{鱼|yú}): the same character as the {={喂|wèi}=} of the
phone, but a different word, written 餵 in traditional. {玩具|wán jù} is a toy. {投|tóu} is to throw ({投|tóu}{球|qiú}), and {挥|huī} to wave
({挥|huī}{手|shǒu}); {哈|hā} is the "ha" of laughter ({哈|hā}{哈|hā}).

## Characters
{=

| Character | Meaning | Pinyin | Radical | Strokes | Words |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| {木|mù} | wood; tree | mù | {木|mù} | 4 | {木头|mù tou} (lesson 09), {树木|shù mù} (lesson 22) |
| {漏|lòu} | leak | lòu | 氵 | 14 | {漏|lòu} (lesson 09) |
| {摸|mō} | touch | mō | 扌 | 13 | {摸|mō} (lesson 09) |
| {盆|pén} ✎ | basin | pén | 皿 | 9 | {盆|pén} (lesson 09) |
| {墙|qiáng} (traditional {+{墙|qiáng}+}) | wall | qiáng | {土|tǔ} | 14 | {墙|qiáng} (lesson 09) |
| {洒|sǎ} (traditional {+{洒|sǎ}+}) | sprinkle, spill | sǎ | 氵 | 9 | {洒|sǎ} (lesson 09) |

"**'The Colours of the City': a photography exhibition.** Dates: 1 to 31 January (closed on Mondays).
Place: City Museum, first floor. This exhibition shows over a hundred photos taken by fifty amateur
photographers, showing the many-coloured life of the city. Admission is free. To protect the works,
please do not touch the photographs.

**Keeping the changing city in photos.** Sixty-five-year-old Fang Ming is the oldest photographer
in the exhibition. Before he retired he worked in a factory; after retiring he became hooked on
photography. For ten years he's left home at five every morning to take photos outdoors. What he's
best at is the old hutongs: little shops selling soy milk in the morning, old people playing chess,
children coming home from school.

Fang Ming says photography has brought him a lot of pleasure. 'When I started I couldn't even use a
camera, and my photos weren't good. I looked at other people's work every day and practised slowly,
and now at last I know how to get a good picture.'

Of the ten photos of his on show, one is the most popular: a child standing at the end of a hutong
holding a red balloon, with grey old houses behind. Many people stop in front of it and look at it
for a long time. One visitor said: 'The colours are simple, but it's so moving.'

At first Fang Ming's family didn't really understand: 'Going out so early every day, aren't you
tired?' Now his granddaughter is learning photography from him too.

Fang Ming has one more wish: to turn these photos into a book, so that more people can see how the
city has changed."

"One rainy evening, on her way home, Xiaoxue saw a little cat. It was soaking wet and looked cold and
hungry. Xiaoxue carried it home and fed it some milk. When it had had enough, it began to play with
a little ball, running all over the place, terribly sweet. Xiaoxue watched it and laughed out loud.
From then on the cat was her pet. Now, every evening when Xiaoxue paints, the cat sleeps on her
desk."

## Pronunciation

- {好|hào} (fond of) in {好学|hào xué}, {好动|hào dòng}, {好客|hào kè}, {好奇|hào qí} and {爱好|ài hào}; {好|hǎo} (good, easy to) in the other words of this course.
- {={喂|wèi}=} wèi (to feed; 餵 in traditional) is the same syllable as {={喂|wèi}=} wèi (hello) and {胃|wèi} wèi (stomach, lesson 08).
- {角色|jué sè} jué sè: {角|jué} is jué here, not jiǎo (horn, corner).
- {曲|qǔ} qǔ (a song) in {歌曲|gē qǔ}; qū (bent) in other words.
- {擅长|shàn cháng} shàn cháng: {长|cháng} is cháng (long), not zhǎng.
- {了不起|liǎo bu qǐ} liǎo bu qǐ: {了|liǎo} is liǎo, {不|bu} is light.

## Common mistakes

- ~~{没|méi}{完|wán}{没|méi}{完|wán}~~: {没|méi}A{没|méi}B has two different parts: {没完没了|méi wán méi liǎo}.
- ~~{说|shuō}{走|zǒu}{走|zǒu}~~: the pattern needs {就|jiù}: {说|shuō}{走|zǒu}{就|jiù}{走|zǒu}.
- {好学|hào xué} read hǎo xué for "studious": it's hào xué. ({汉语|Hàn yǔ}{不|bù}{好|hǎo}{学|xué}, "Chinese isn't easy to learn", is hǎo.)
- {我|wǒ}{很|hěn}{擅长|shàn cháng} with nothing after it only works as a reply, when the skill has just been named: {擅长|shàn cháng} normally takes an object: {我|wǒ}{很|hěn}{擅长|shàn cháng}{画|huà}{画儿|huàr}.
- {展览|zhǎn lǎn}{了|le}{一百|yì bǎi}{张|zhāng}{照片|zhào piàn} for "showed a hundred photos": the verb is {展出|zhǎn chū} (or {展览|zhǎn lǎn} + {了|le} is heard, but {展出|zhǎn chū} is
  usual): {展出|zhǎn chū}{了|le}{一百|yì bǎi}{张|zhāng}{照片|zhào piàn}. {展览|zhǎn lǎn} is mostly the noun, the exhibition.

## Key points

- {说|shuō}A{就|jiù}A ({说|shuō}{走|zǒu}{就|jiù}{走|zǒu}): done the moment it's mentioned.
- {没|méi}A{没|méi}B: {没完没了|méi wán méi liǎo} (endless), {没日没夜|méi rì méi yè} (day and night), {没大没小|méi dà méi xiǎo} (cheeky to elders); set phrases.
- {支|zhī} (songs, pens, teams), {匹|pǐ} (horses, cloth); {首|shǒu} is the usual word for songs.
- {好|hào} + verb: fond of, given to ({好学|hào xué}, {好动|hào dòng}, {好客|hào kè}; {爱好|ài hào}).

lessons.title: Porcelain: celadon, blue-and-white and Jingdezhen
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

{安娜|Ān nà} (Anna) is writing her thesis on porcelain with {罗教授|Luó jiào shòu} (Professor Luo), and while she finishes
her degree she guides visitors at a museum. This honors lesson is what she tells them: what porcelain is
and how it's made, the green celadon and the blue-and-white, the porcelain town of Jingdezhen, and
how Chinese porcelain travelled the world and gave English a word. Dates are given as the sources
give them, and the earliest history of porcelain, which specialists still debate, is left aside.
New words are glossed and aren't added to your reviews.

The key word is {瓷器|cí qì} (cíqì, porcelain, china; HSK 6), with {瓷|cí} (cí) on its own in words such as {青瓷|qīng cí}.
{陶器|táo qì} (táoqì) is pottery, made of ordinary clay and fired at a lower heat.

## What porcelain is

Porcelain is a hard, white, fine ceramic, fired at a very high temperature, well over 1,200 °C. At
that heat its body turns glassy: a thin piece lets light through and rings when it's tapped. Its
two raw materials are:

| Material | Chinese | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| kaolin, china clay | {高岭土|gāo lǐng tǔ} (gāolǐngtǔ) | a white clay that keeps the shape in the fire |
| china stone, petuntse | {瓷石|cí shí} (císhí) | a crushed stone that melts and binds the body |

Kaolin is named after {高岭|Gāo lǐng} (Gāolǐng, "High Ridge"), hills near Jingdezhen whose clay the potters used
for centuries. The making, in five steps:

1. {做坯|zuò pī} (zuò pī): the clay is shaped, on a wheel or in a mould, and dried;
2. {画|huà} (huà): it is painted, if it will be;
3. {上釉|shàng yòu} (shàng yòu): it is covered with a glaze, {釉|yòu} (yòu), a coating that melts into glass;
4. {烧|shāo} (shāo): it is fired in a kiln, {窑|yáo} (yáo), for many hours ({烧|shāo} is lesson 07's word, "to cook, burn");
5. it cools slowly, and only then is the kiln opened.

## Celadon: {青瓷|qīng cí}

{青瓷|qīng cí} (qīngcí) is porcelain with a green or blue-green glaze: the {青|qīng} of lesson 10, the colour of hills
and young leaves. Celadon was the pride of the Song dynasty ({宋代|Sòng dài}, 960–1279), above all from the
Longquan kilns ({龙泉|Lóng quán}, Lóngquán) in Zhejiang. Its beauty is in the glaze and the shape, usually with
little or no painting; some glazes are crackled on purpose.

## Jingdezhen: the porcelain town

{景德镇|Jǐng dé zhèn} (Jǐngdézhèn) is a city in Jiangxi province. It took its name in 1004, the first year of the
Song emperor's Jingde ({景德|Jǐng dé}) reign. It had the clay and the stone close by, and wood for the kilns,
and over the centuries it became the most famous centre of porcelain in China: in the Ming ({明代|Míng dài}) and
Qing ({清代|Qīng dài}) dynasties it made huge quantities for the court and for sale abroad, and it's still known
as {瓷都|cí dū} (cídū, "the porcelain capital"). Its old kilns are kept as a museum site today.

## Blue-and-white: {青花|qīng huā}

{青花|qīng huā} (qīnghuā, blue-and-white) is painted with a cobalt pigment, {钴|gǔ} (gǔ), straight onto the dried
body. A clear glaze goes over it, and the piece is fired once: the blue comes out under the glass,
where it can't wear off. The technique was established in the Yuan dynasty ({元代|Yuán dài}, 1271–1368): the
earliest dated pieces bear the year 1351. The cobalt was imported from Iran ({波斯|Bō sī}, Bōsī, Persia, as
Chinese sources called it), and much of the Yuan blue-and-white was made for export.

## Porcelain on the move

Porcelain went west along the land routes of the Silk Road ({丝绸之路|sī chóu zhī lù}, sīchóu zhī lù) and, in far larger
quantities, by sea, to Southeast Asia, India, the Middle East, Japan and, from the sixteenth century,
Europe. Europeans couldn't make true porcelain for a long time, and in English it came to be called
simply "china", after the country it came from. Kaolin is "china clay" in English for the same reason.

## Dialogue: Anna's thesis

{安娜|Ān nà} talks to {罗教授|Luó jiào shòu} about what her thesis might cover; the written plan comes in lesson 17.
{论文|lùn wén} (lùnwén, a thesis) is lesson 17's word.

{展厅|zhǎn tīng} (zhǎntīng): an exhibition hall; {度|dù} (dù, lesson 22): degree; {透光|tòu guāng} (tòu guāng): to let light through; {在于|zài yú} (zàiyú, lesson 26): lies
in; {颜料|yán liào} (yánliào): pigment; {鲜|xiān} (HSK 4): fresh, bright; {展品|zhǎn pǐn} (zhǎnpǐn): an exhibit; {闪光灯|shǎn guāng dēng} (shǎnguāngdēng):
a flash.

1. What are the two raw materials of porcelain, according to the guide?
2. What do the celadons in the room look like, and where is their beauty?
3. Why is the blue of blue-and-white still so bright?
4. What does the guide think the English word "china" shows?

<details>
<summary>Answers and translation</summary>

1. White kaolin ({高岭土|gāo lǐng tǔ}) and china stone ({瓷石|cí shí}).
2. A pale blue-green, like hills in spring, with almost no painting; their beauty is in the colour
   and the shape ({它们|tā men}{的|de}{美|měi}{在于|zài yú}{颜色|yán sè}{和|hé}{样子|yàng zi}).
3. The pigment is painted under the glaze ({画|huà}{在|zài}{釉|yòu}{的|de}{下面|xià miàn}), so centuries later the colour is still fresh.
4. That for a long time, foreigners thought of China as soon as they saw porcelain.

"Welcome to the porcelain hall, everyone. This hall has over two hundred works on show, from celadons
of more than a thousand years ago to blue-and-white of a little over a century ago. Today I'm going to tell you about Chinese porcelain.
Porcelain is different from ordinary pottery. It takes two materials: white kaolin and china stone.
The workers first shape them into a bowl or a plate, leave it for a few days, paint it, add a coat of glaze, and
finally put it in the kiln to fire. The kiln has to be hotter than 1,200 degrees, and the finished
porcelain is white and hard, and where it's very thin it even lets light through.

Please look at these celadons on the left. They are from the Song dynasty, and their colour is a
pale blue-green, like hills in spring. There's hardly any painting on them: their beauty lies in
the colour and the shape, very simple, and very classic.

The blue-and-white pieces in front of you are called blue-and-white porcelain, and most of them were
fired in Jingdezhen, in Jiangxi. Jingdezhen has had that name since the Song, and by the Ming and
Qing it was China's most famous porcelain town. The blue is painted with a pigment imported from
abroad, under the glaze, so after several hundred years the colour is still as bright as this.

Much Yuan blue-and-white was made specially for foreign buyers: large pieces, covered with flowers
and birds. From the Ming on, Europeans began to buy Chinese porcelain in great quantities too. In
some rich homes there was even a room set aside to show off the porcelain bought from China.

Chinese porcelain was sold all over the world very early on, along the Silk Road and by sea. In English,
porcelain and China share one word, 'china'. That shows that for a very long time, the moment
people abroad saw porcelain, they thought of China.

Now you're free to look round. Please don't touch the exhibits, and please don't use a flash when you
take photos. Thank you!"
</details>

## Say it

```speak
# At the porcelain hall
{瓷器|cí qì}{跟|gēn}{一般|yì bān}{的|de}{陶器|táo qì}{不|bù}{一样|yí yàng}。
= Porcelain is different from ordinary pottery.
{这|zhè}{件|jiàn}{青瓷|qīng cí}{是|shì}{宋代|Sòng dài}{的|de}{作品|zuò pǐn}。
= This celadon is from the Song dynasty.
{青花|qīng huā}{的|de}{蓝|lán}{色|sè}{画|huà}{在|zài}{釉|yòu}{的|de}{下面|xià miàn}。
= The blue of blue-and-white is painted under the glaze.
{景德镇|Jǐng dé zhèn}{是|shì}{有名|yǒu míng}{的|de}{瓷都|cí dū}。
= Jingdezhen is the famous porcelain capital.
{请|qǐng}{不要|bú yào}{用|yòng}{手|shǒu}{摸|mō}{展品|zhǎn pǐn}。
= Please don't touch the exhibits.
```

## Key points

- {瓷器|cí qì} (porcelain, HSK 6) is made of kaolin ({高岭土|gāo lǐng tǔ}) and china stone ({瓷石|cí shí}), glazed ({上釉|shàng yòu}) and fired ({烧|shāo}) in a
  kiln ({窑|yáo}) at well over 1,200 °C; {陶器|táo qì} is pottery.
- {青瓷|qīng cí} (celadon): a green glaze, the glory of the Song (960–1279), above all from Longquan.
- {景德镇|Jǐng dé zhèn}: named in 1004, the porcelain capital, making for the court and for export under the Ming and Qing.
- {青花|qīng huā} (blue-and-white): cobalt painted under a clear glaze, fired once; established in the Yuan, with
  imported cobalt.
- Porcelain travelled by land and sea; English calls it "china", and kaolin "china clay".

lessons.title: Zu Chongzhi and π
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

{祖冲之|Zǔ Chōng zhī} (Zǔ Chōngzhī) was a mathematician and astronomer of the fifth century whose value of π stayed
the most exact in the world for about nine hundred years. This honors lesson tells what he
calculated, how such a value can be reached with polygons (his own method is lost, so this is what
historians suggest), and the calendar he made. It's history of science: the facts are those the
sources agree on, and where they differ (his dates, his method) the lesson says so. New words are
glossed and aren't added to your reviews.

Two words you'll need: {圆周率|yuán zhōu lǜ} (yuánzhōulǜ), the ratio of a circle's circumference to its diameter, π;
and {数学|shù xué} (shùxué, HSK 3), mathematics, with {数学家|shù xué jiā}, a mathematician.

## Who he was

Zu Chongzhi lived from 429 to 500 (some sources give 501), in the time of the Southern Dynasties
({南朝|Nán cháo}, Náncháo), when China was divided between northern and southern states. He was born in Jiankang,
today's Nanjing, into a family of officials who studied astronomy and the calendar, and he served
the courts of the south. He worked in mathematics, astronomy and engineering.

## What he calculated

The official history of the Sui dynasty, 《{隋书|Suí shū}》 (*Suí shū*), compiled in the seventh century, records
three results of his:

| Result | Chinese name | Value |
|---|---|---|
| π lies between two bounds | — | 3.1415926 < π < 3.1415927 |
| the "close ratio" | {密率|mì lǜ} (mìlǜ) | 355/113 = 3.14159292… |
| the "approximate ratio" | {约率|yuē lǜ} (yuēlǜ) | 22/7 = 3.142857… |

The bounds give π correctly to seven decimal places, and 355/113 is correct to six. It was the most
exact value known anywhere until the fifteenth century, when the Persian astronomer al-Kashi
calculated further: roughly nine hundred years. In Chinese a fraction is read denominator first:
355/113 is {一百一十三|yì bǎi yī shí sān}{分|fēn}{之|zhī}{三百五十五|sān bǎi wǔ shí wǔ}, 22/7 is {七|qī}{分|fēn}{之|zhī}{二十二|èr shí èr}.

## How it can be done: polygons

Zu's book on mathematics, 《{缀术|Zhuì shù}》 (*Zhuì shù*), was lost centuries ago, so nobody knows exactly how he
worked. Historians think he used the method that the third-century mathematician {刘徽|Liú Huī} (Liú Huī) had
described, {割圆术|gē yuán shù} (gēyuánshù, "cutting the circle"):

1. Draw a circle, and inside it a regular hexagon ({六边形|liù biān xíng}, liùbiānxíng), its six corners on the
   circle. Its perimeter is a little less than the circle's.
2. Double the sides: 12, 24, 48… Each time the polygon hugs the circle more closely, and its perimeter
   (or area) comes nearer to the circle's.
3. Work out each new side from the last with square roots ({开方|kāi fāng}, kāifāng), very carefully.

To reach seven correct places this way, the polygon needs about 12,288 or 24,576 sides, and the
square roots have to be taken to many digits, all by hand, with counting rods ({算筹|suàn chóu}, suànchóu). That
is what historians suggest Zu did; it shows how much patience the result took.

## His calendar

Zu also made a calendar, the {大明历|Dà míng lì} (Dàmíng lì, the Daming calendar). He presented it around 462; it
was adopted only in 510, after his death, with the help of his son {祖暅|Zǔ Gèng} (Zǔ Gèng). It was the first
Chinese calendar to take account of the slow drift of the stars against the seasons (the precession
of the equinoxes, {岁差|suì chā} suìchā), and it fitted 144 extra months into every 391 years, closer to the
true cycle of the moon and the sun than the calendar before it. His son, also a mathematician, found how to
calculate the volume of a sphere (some sources credit father and son together).

## Reading: a value that lasted nine hundred years

> {祖冲之|Zǔ Chōng zhī}{是|shì}{中国|Zhōng guó}{南朝|Nán cháo}{的|de}{一|yí}{位|wèi}{数学家|shù xué jiā}，{也|yě}{是|shì}{一|yí}{位|wèi}{天文学家|tiān wén xué jiā}。{他|tā}{生活|shēng huó}{在|zài}{一千五百|yì qiān wǔ bǎi}{多|duō}{年|nián}{前|qián}，{那|nà}{时候|shí hou}{没有|méi yǒu}{计算机|jì suàn jī}，{也|yě}{没有|méi yǒu}{计算器|jì suàn qì}，{人们|rén men}{用|yòng}{一|yì}{种|zhǒng}{叫|jiào}"{算筹|suàn chóu}"{的|de}{小|xiǎo}{木棍|mù gùn}{来|lái}{计算|jì suàn}。{他|tā}{家|jiā}{里|lǐ}{好|hǎo}{几|jǐ}{代|dài}{人|rén}{都|dōu}{研究|yán jiū}{天文|tiān wén}{和|hé}{历法|lì fǎ}，{他|tā}{从小|cóng xiǎo}{就|jiù}{对|duì}{数学|shù xué}{很|hěn}{感兴趣|gǎn xìng qù}。

>
> {他|tā}{是|shì}{怎么|zěn me}{算|suàn}{出来|chū lái}{的|de}{呢|ne}？{他|tā}{写|xiě}{的|de}{书|shū}《{缀术|Zhuì shù}》{已经|yǐ jīng}{找不到|zhǎo bu dào}{了|le}，{所以|suǒ yǐ}{我们|wǒ men}{不|bù}{知道|zhī dào}{他|tā}{具体|jù tǐ}{的|de}{方法|fāng fǎ}。{很|hěn}{多|duō}{人|rén}{认为|rèn wéi}，{他|tā}{用|yòng}{的|de}{是|shì}{刘徽|Liú Huī}{的|de}"{割圆术|gē yuán shù}"：{在|zài}{圆|yuán}{里|lǐ}{画|huà}{一|yí}{个|gè}{正六边形|zhèng liù biān xíng}，{然后|rán hòu}{把|bǎ}{边|biān}{一|yí}{次|cì}{一|yí}{次|cì}{地|de}{加倍|jiā bèi}，{变成|biàn chéng}{十二|shí èr}{边|biān}、{二十四|èr shí sì}{边|biān}……{边|biān}{越|yuè}{多|duō}，{这个|zhè ge}{多边形|duō biān xíng}{就|jiù}{越|yuè}{接近|jiē jìn}{圆|yuán}。{要|yào}{得到|dé dào}{这么|zhè me}{准确|zhǔn què}{的|de}{数字|shù zì}，{可能|kě néng}{要|yào}{算|suàn}{到|dào}{两万|liǎng wàn}{多|duō}{边|biān}，{每|měi}{一|yí}{步|bù}{都|dōu}{要|yào}{开方|kāi fāng}，{非常|fēi cháng}{麻烦|má fan}。{祖冲之|Zǔ Chōng zhī}{能|néng}{做|zuò}{到|dào}{这|zhè}{一|yì}{点|diǎn}，{说明|shuō míng}{他|tā}{不但|bú dàn}{聪明|cōng ming}，{而且|ér qiě}{非常|fēi cháng}{有|yǒu}{耐心|nài xīn}。{他|tā}{的|de}{儿子|ér zi}{祖暅|Zǔ Gèng}{也|yě}{是|shì}{数学家|shù xué jiā}，{找|zhǎo}{到|dào}{了|le}{计算|jì suàn}{球|qiú}{的|de}{体积|tǐ jī}{的|de}{方法|fāng fǎ}。
>
> {除了|chú le}{圆周率|yuán zhōu lǜ}，{祖冲之|Zǔ Chōng zhī}{还|hái}{制定|zhì dìng}{了|le}{一|yí}{部|bù}{新|xīn}{的|de}{历法|lì fǎ}，{叫|jiào}"{大明历|Dà míng lì}"。{大明历|Dà míng lì}{第|dì}{一|yī}{次|cì}{考虑|kǎo lǜ}{了|le}{岁差|suì chā}，{比|bǐ}{以前|yǐ qián}{的|de}{历法|lì fǎ}{更|gèng}{准确|zhǔn què}。{可是|kě shì}，{这|zhè}{部|bù}{历法|lì fǎ}{直到|zhí dào}{他|tā}{去世|qù shì}{以后|yǐ hòu}{才|cái}{开始|kāi shǐ}{使用|shǐ yòng}。{今天|jīn tiān}，{月球|yuè qiú}{上|shàng}{有|yǒu}{一|yí}{个|gè}{环形山|huán xíng shān}{就是|jiù shì}{用|yòng}{他|tā}{的|de}{名字|míng zi}{命名|mìng míng}{的|de}。{人们|rén men}{常|cháng}{说|shuō}，{他|tā}{的|de}{成就|chéng jiù}{告诉|gào su}{我们|wǒ men}：{了不起|liǎo bu qǐ}{的|de}{发现|fā xiàn}，{常常|cháng cháng}{来自|lái zì}{一|yí}{步|bù}{一|yí}{步|bù}{认真|rèn zhēn}{的|de}{工作|gōng zuò}。

{天文学家|tiān wén xué jiā} (tiānwénxuéjiā): an astronomer; {计算器|jì suàn qì} (jìsuànqì): a calculator; {木棍|mù gùn} (mùgùn): a stick; {分数|fēn shù} (fēnshù):
a fraction (HSK 4's {分数|fēn shù} is a mark, a score); {准确|zhǔn què} (HSK 4): exact; {多边形|duō biān xíng} (duōbiānxíng): a polygon; {加倍|jiā bèi} (jiābèi):
to double; {耐心|nài xīn} (HSK 4): patient; {历法|lì fǎ} (lìfǎ): a calendar system; {月球|yuè qiú} (yuèqiú): the moon; {环形山|huán xíng shān} (huánxíngshān): a crater; {命名|mìng míng} (mìngmíng):
to name after. From later lessons: {制定|zhì dìng} (zhìdìng, 27) to draw up, {计算机|jì suàn jī} (jìsuànjī, 19) a computer, {成就|chéng jiù} (chéngjiù, 19) an achievement,
{具体|jù tǐ} (jùtǐ, 26) exact, specific, {接近|jiē jìn} (jiējìn, 28) to come close to, {去世|qù shì} (qùshì, 13) to die. {据|jù}…{记载|jì zǎi} (lesson 24's {据|jù} and lesson 25's {记载|jì zǎi}): according to the records of…

1. What did people calculate with in Zu Chongzhi's time?
2. What are the {约率|yuē lǜ} and the {密率|mì lǜ}?
3. Why don't we know exactly how he calculated π?
4. What lesson does the writer draw from his work?

<details>
<summary>Answers and translation</summary>

1. Counting rods, small sticks of wood ({算筹|suàn chóu}); there were no computers or calculators.
2. Two fractions for π: 22/7 ({约率|yuē lǜ}, the approximate ratio) and 355/113 ({密率|mì lǜ}, the close ratio).
3. His book, 《{缀术|Zhuì shù}》, has been lost ({已经|yǐ jīng}{找不到|zhǎo bu dào}{了|le}).
4. That remarkable discoveries often come from careful work, done step by step.

"Zu Chongzhi was a mathematician, and an astronomer too, of China's Southern Dynasties. He lived over
fifteen hundred years ago, when there were no computers or calculators, and people calculated with
small sticks of wood called counting rods. Several generations of his family had studied astronomy and
the calendar, and he was interested in mathematics from childhood.

Zu Chongzhi's most famous achievement is his calculation of π. According to the *Book of Sui*, he
found that π lies between 3.1415926 and 3.1415927. He also gave two fractions: 22/7, called the
'approximate ratio', and 355/113, called the 'close ratio'. The close ratio differs from the true
value of π by less than three ten-millionths. For more than nine hundred years afterwards, nobody
in the world calculated it more exactly than he did. Today, with computers, we can work out millions
of digits of π in a few seconds; but fifteen hundred years ago, a result like his was remarkable.

How did he work it out? His book, the *Zhui shu*, can no longer be found, so we don't know his
exact method. Many people think he used Liu Hui's method of 'cutting the circle': draw a regular
hexagon inside a circle, then double the sides again and again, to twelve, twenty-four… The more
sides, the closer the polygon comes to the circle. To get such an exact figure he might have had to
go to over twenty thousand sides, taking square roots at every step: very laborious. That Zu
Chongzhi managed this shows he was not only clever but also extremely patient. His son Zu Geng was a mathematician too, and found a way to
calculate the volume of a sphere.

Besides π, Zu Chongzhi also drew up a new calendar, the Daming calendar. It was the first to take the precession into account, and it was more exact than
the calendars before it. But it only came into use after
his death. Today a crater on the moon is named after him. People often say his achievements teach
us that remarkable discoveries often come from careful work, done step by step."
</details>

## Say it

```speak
# Zu Chongzhi
{祖冲之|Zǔ Chōng zhī}{是|shì}{一|yí}{位|wèi}{了不起|liǎo bu qǐ}{的|de}{数学家|shù xué jiā}。
= Zu Chongzhi was a remarkable mathematician.
{他|tā}{算|suàn}{出|chū}{圆周率|yuán zhōu lǜ}{在|zài}{三|sān}{点|diǎn}{一四一五九二六|yī sì yī wǔ jiǔ èr liù}{和|hé}{三|sān}{点|diǎn}{一四一五九二七|yī sì yī wǔ jiǔ èr qī}{之间|zhī jiān}。
= He found that π lies between 3.1415926 and 3.1415927.
{一百一十三|yì bǎi yī shí sān}{分|fēn}{之|zhī}{三百五十五|sān bǎi wǔ shí wǔ}{叫|jiào}{密率|mì lǜ}。
= 355/113 is called the close ratio.
{边|biān}{越|yuè}{多|duō}，{多边形|duō biān xíng}{就|jiù}{越|yuè}{接近|jiē jìn}{圆|yuán}。
= The more sides, the closer the polygon comes to the circle.
```

## Key points

- {祖冲之|Zǔ Chōng zhī} (429–500, or 501), of the Southern Dynasties, born in Jiankang (Nanjing): mathematician,
  astronomer, engineer.
- The 《{隋书|Suí shū}》 (seventh century) records his bounds 3.1415926 < π < 3.1415927, the {密率|mì lǜ} 355/113 and the {约率|yuē lǜ}
  22/7; the best value in the world for about nine hundred years, until al-Kashi in the fifteenth century.
- His book 《{缀术|Zhuì shù}》 is lost; historians think he doubled the sides of polygons ({刘徽|Liú Huī}'s {割圆术|gē yuán shù}) to some
  12,288 or 24,576 sides.
- The {大明历|Dà míng lì}: presented around 462, adopted in 510; the first Chinese calendar to allow for {岁差|suì chā}.
- Fractions are read denominator first: {七|qī}{分|fēn}{之|zhī}{二十二|èr shí èr} (22/7).

lessons.title: Friends and acquaintances
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

Module 3 is about people: friends, partners, families, quarrels and good manners. This first
lesson gives you the words to talk about how friendships start, grow and last, and about the
difference between a friend, an acquaintance and a stranger. Wang Fang runs into a school friend
she hasn't seen for ten years, and Li Ming, a few months into his master's in England, writes about
making friends in a city where he knew no one.

The grammar is a set of small, precise words that HSK 5 texts use all the time:

- {彼此|bǐ cǐ}: each other, the two (or more) sides (a pronoun, beside HSK 4's {互相|hù xiāng});
- {始终|shǐ zhōng}: from beginning to end, all along (beside {一直|yì zhí});
- {分别|fēn bié}: to part from someone, and as an adverb "separately, respectively";
- {单独|dān dú} and {独自|dú zì}: two ways of saying "alone";
- {不但|bú dàn}{不|bù}…{反而|fǎn ér}…: not only not…, but on the contrary (a preview: lesson 14 teaches {反而|fǎn ér} in full).

You'll also meet the words of getting along: {相处|xiāng chǔ}, {处|chǔ}, {合得来|hé de lái}, {对待|duì dài}, {信任|xìn rèn}, {靠|kào}.

## {彼此|bǐ cǐ}: each other

{彼此|bǐ cǐ} is a pronoun made of two old written words: {彼|bǐ} (that, the other side) and {此|cǐ} (this, HSK 4).
"This and that" means the two sides of a relationship, each to the other.

{我们|wǒ men}{认识|rèn shi}{十|shí}{年|nián}{了|le}，{彼此|bǐ cǐ}{都|dōu}{很|hěn}{了解|liǎo jiě}。 — We've known each other for ten years and understand each other well.

{同事|tóng shì}{之间|zhī jiān}{应该|yīng gāi}{彼此|bǐ cǐ}{信任|xìn rèn}。 — Colleagues should trust each other.

You know {互相|hù xiāng} (HSK 4), and often either works: {彼此|bǐ cǐ}{帮助|bāng zhù} = {互相|hù xiāng}{帮助|bāng zhù} (to help each other). The
difference is grammar. {互相|hù xiāng} is an adverb and only goes before a verb. {彼此|bǐ cǐ} is a pronoun, so it can
also stand before {的|de} or {之间|zhī jiān} and describe a noun:

{这|zhè}{次|cì}{谈话|tán huà}{增进|zēng jìn}{了|le}{彼此|bǐ cǐ}{的|de}{了解|liǎo jiě}。 — This conversation improved our understanding of each other.

{彼此|bǐ cǐ}{之间|zhī jiān}{没有|méi yǒu}{秘密|mì mì}。 — There are no secrets between us.

In those last two, {互相|hù xiāng} would be unusual; use {彼此|bǐ cǐ}. And when someone pays you a compliment that you could
return, {彼此|bǐ cǐ}{彼此|bǐ cǐ} is a light, friendly "same to you":

"{你|nǐ}{的|de}{汉语|Hàn yǔ}{提高|tí gāo}{得|de}{真|zhēn}{快|kuài}！""{彼此|bǐ cǐ}{彼此|bǐ cǐ}。" — "Your Chinese is improving so fast!" "So's yours."

## {始终|shǐ zhōng}: from beginning to end

{始终|shǐ zhōng} is "from start ({始|shǐ}) to finish ({终|zhōng})": the same the whole time. It's an adverb before the verb,
and it's very often negative:

{那|nà}{天|tiān}{晚上|wǎn shang}{他|tā}{始终|shǐ zhōng}{没|méi}{说话|shuō huà}。 — He didn't say a word the whole evening.

{我|wǒ}{始终|shǐ zhōng}{相信|xiāng xìn}，{真诚|zhēn chéng}{的|de}{人|rén}{能|néng}{交|jiāo}{到|dào}{真诚|zhēn chéng}{的|de}{朋友|péng you}。 — I've always believed that sincere people make sincere friends.

Compare {一直|yì zhí} (HSK 3). Both say "all along", but:

- {始终|shǐ zhōng} stresses the whole stretch, from the start to the end, and sounds a little more written: {他|tā}{始终|shǐ zhōng}{不|bù}{同意|tóng yì} (he never once agreed, from start to finish).
- {一直|yì zhí} can run up to a point in time; {始终|shǐ zhōng} can't: {我|wǒ}{一直|yì zhí}{等到|děng dào}{十|shí}{点|diǎn} (I waited until ten), not ×{我|wǒ}{始终|shǐ zhōng}{等到|děng dào}{十|shí}{点|diǎn}.
- {一直|yì zhí} also means "straight on" ({一直|yì zhí}{往|wǎng}{前|qián}{走|zǒu}); {始终|shǐ zhōng} never does.

## {分别|fēn bié}: to part; separately; respectively

{分别|fēn bié} has two uses. As a verb, it's to part from someone, usually for a long time:

{我们|wǒ men}{高中|gāo zhōng}{毕业|bì yè}{以后|yǐ hòu}{就|jiù}{分别|fēn bié}{了|le}。 — We went our separate ways after high school.

{分别|fēn bié}{的|de}{时候|shí hou}，{她|tā}{哭|kū}{了|le}。 — When we said goodbye, she cried.

As an adverb before a verb, it means "separately" (each one on its own) or "respectively" (each
to its own thing, in the order given):

{经理|jīng lǐ}{分别|fēn bié}{跟|gēn}{每|měi}{个|gè}{员工|yuán gōng}{谈|tán}{了|le}{话|huà}。 — The manager talked to each member of staff separately.

{他们|tā men}{俩|liǎ}{分别|fēn bié}{来自|lái zì}{北京|Běi jīng}{和|hé}{上海|Shàng hǎi}。 — The two of them come from Beijing and Shanghai respectively.

The adverb sense is common in written reports and news; in speech you'd often say {一|yí}{个|gè}{一|yí}{个|gè}{地|de} or
just leave it out.

## {单独|dān dú} and {独自|dú zì}: alone

Both mean "alone", and both have {独|dú} (single, alone; lesson 10's {独特|dú tè}). They are used differently.

- {单独|dān dú} is "on one's own, apart from the others". It can go before a verb, and with {的|de} before a noun:
  {我|wǒ}{想|xiǎng}{跟|gēn}{你|nǐ}{单独|dān dú}{谈|tán}{谈|tán}。 (I'd like to talk to you in private.) {每|měi}{个|gè}{人|rén}{都|dōu}{有|yǒu}{一|yí}{个|gè}{单独|dān dú}{的|de}{房间|fáng jiān}。 (Everyone has a room of
  their own.)
- {独自|dú zì} is "by oneself, with no one else", often with {一|yì}{人|rén} and a note of loneliness or independence.
  It only goes before a verb: {他|tā}{独自|dú zì}{一|yì}{人|rén}{来|lái}{到|dào}{这个|zhè ge}{陌生|mò shēng}{的|de}{城市|chéng shì}。 (He came to this strange city all on his own.)

So you can say {单独|dān dú}{的|de}{房间|fáng jiān} but not ×{独自|dú zì}{的|de}{房间|fáng jiān}, and {跟|gēn}{他|tā}{单独|dān dú}{谈|tán} ("with him, just the two of us") but not
×{跟|gēn}{他|tā}{独自|dú zì}{谈|tán}: {独自|dú zì} means no one else is there at all.

## {不但|bú dàn}{不|bù}…{反而|fǎn ér}…: not only not… but on the contrary

You know {不但|bú dàn}…{而且|ér qiě} (not only… but also). With a negative first half and {反而|fǎn ér} (on the contrary,
instead) in the second, the sentence says that the result went against what you'd expect: a
**[[counter-expectation]]** sentence.

{我|wǒ}{说|shuō}{错|cuò}{了|le}{话|huà}，{他|tā}{不但|bú dàn}{不|bù}{生气|shēng qì}，{反而|fǎn ér}{笑|xiào}{了|le}。 — I said the wrong thing, but far from being angry, he laughed.

{吃|chī}{了|le}{药|yào}{以后|yǐ hòu}，{病|bìng}{不但|bú dàn}{没|méi}{好|hǎo}，{反而|fǎn ér}{更|gèng}{重|zhòng}{了|le}。 — After taking the medicine, the illness didn't get better: it got worse.

{不但|bú dàn}{不|bù} is for habits and the present, {不但|bú dàn}{没|méi}({有|yǒu}) for what happened. Lesson 14 comes back to {反而|fǎn ér} on
its own.

## Getting along: {相处|xiāng chǔ}, {处|chǔ}, {合得来|hé de lái}, {对待|duì dài}

| Word | Use | Example |
|---|---|---|
| {相处|xiāng chǔ} | to get along, spend time together | {他|tā}{跟|gēn}{同事|tóng shì}{相处|xiāng chǔ}{得|de}{很|hěn}{好|hǎo}。 He gets on well with his colleagues. |
| {处|chǔ} | the same, mostly in speech | {我们|wǒ men}{俩|liǎ}{处|chǔ}{得|de}{不错|bú cuò}。 We get on fine. |
| {合得来|hé de lái} / {合不来|hé bu lái} | to be (not) compatible | {我|wǒ}{跟|gēn}{他|tā}{合不来|hé bu lái}。 He and I don't get on. |
| {对待|duì dài} | to treat (people, a matter) | {你|nǐ}{怎么|zěn me}{对待|duì dài}{别人|bié ren}，{别人|bié ren}{就|jiù}{怎么|zěn me}{对待|duì dài}{你|nǐ}。 People treat you the way you treat them. |
| {交往|jiāo wǎng} | to associate with; to go out with | {我们|wǒ men}{交往|jiāo wǎng}{了|le}{三|sān}{年|nián}。 We've been seeing each other for three years. |
| {接触|jiē chù} | to come into contact with | {在|zài}{国|guó}{外|wài}，{我|wǒ}{接触|jiē chù}{了|le}{很|hěn}{多|duō}{新|xīn}{的|de}{文化|wén huà}。 Abroad, I came into contact with lots of new cultures. |

A few notes:

- {处|chǔ} is read chǔ (third tone) when it means "to get along with, to deal with": {相处|xiāng chǔ} xiāng chǔ, and
  HSK 5's {处理|chǔ lǐ} chǔ lǐ (to handle, lesson 03). It's chù (fourth tone) for "place, point": {到处|dào chù}, {好处|hǎo chù},
  and {长处|cháng chù} / {短处|duǎn chù} (strong and weak points, below). Same character, two words.
- {合|hé} hé is "to fit, to suit" ({合得来|hé de lái}, and {合适|hé shì} from HSK 3), and also "to close": {合|hé}{上|shàng}{书|shū} (close the book).
- {交往|jiāo wǎng} is a little formal for friends; between two people it often means dating.
- {靠|kào} is "to lean on" ({靠|kào}{在|zài}{门|mén}{上|shàng}), and then "to rely on": {在|zài}{国|guó}{外|wài}{只能|zhǐ néng}{靠|kào}{自己|zì jǐ} (abroad you can only rely on
  yourself). Someone you can rely on is {可靠|kě kào} (reliable).
- {信任|xìn rèn} is "to trust", and also the noun "trust": {建立|jiàn lì}{信任|xìn rèn} (build trust).

## People: friends, acquaintances and strangers

| Word | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| {伙伴|huǒ bàn} | companion, partner (in an activity) | {学习|xué xí}{伙伴|huǒ bàn} study partner; {合作|hé zuò}{伙伴|huǒ bàn} business partner |
| {熟人|shú rén} | acquaintance, someone you know | {在|zài}{这儿|zhèr}{我|wǒ}{一|yí}{个|gè}{熟人|shú rén}{也|yě}{没有|méi yǒu}。 I don't know a soul here. |
| {陌生|mò shēng} | unfamiliar, strange | {陌生|mò shēng}{人|rén} a stranger; {陌生|mò shēng}{的|de}{城市|chéng shì} a strange city |
| {他人|tā rén} | others (written) | {尊重|zūn zhòng}{他人|tā rén} respect others (spoken: {别人|bié ren}) |
| {私人|sī rén} | private, personal | {私人|sī rén}{问题|wèn tí} a personal question; {私人|sī rén}{生活|shēng huó} private life |
| {秘密|mì mì} | secret | {这|zhè}{是|shì}{我们|wǒ men}{俩|liǎ}{的|de}{秘密|mì mì}。 This is our secret. |
| {人际|rén jì} | between people | {人际|rén jì}{关系|guān xi} relationships with other people |
| {伙|huǒ} | a group, a gang (measure word) | {一|yì}{伙|huǒ}{人|rén} a bunch of people |

{熟人|shú rén} is the in-between word English often lacks: not a close friend, but not a stranger. {伙|huǒ} as a
measure word is informal and often a little negative ({一|yì}{伙|huǒ}{人|rén}{在|zài}{门口|mén kǒu}{大|dà}{声|shēng}{说话|shuō huà} "a bunch of people talking loudly at the
door"). {伙伴|huǒ bàn} is neutral or warm.

## Building a friendship

The verbs that go with friendship come in fixed pairs. Learn them together:

| Verb | Goes with | Example |
|---|---|---|
| {建立|jiàn lì} | {关系|guān xi}, {友谊|yǒu yì}, {信任|xìn rèn} | {我们|wǒ men}{建立|jiàn lì}{了|le}{深厚|shēn hòu}{的|de}{友谊|yǒu yì}。 We built a deep friendship. |
| {增进|zēng jìn} | {了解|liǎo jiě}, {感情|gǎn qíng}, {友谊|yǒu yì} | {一起|yì qǐ}{旅行|lǚ xíng}{能|néng}{增进|zēng jìn}{感情|gǎn qíng}。 Travelling together brings people closer. |
| {付出|fù chū} | {时间|shí jiān}, {努力|nǔ lì}, {感情|gǎn qíng} | {友谊|yǒu yì}{需要|xū yào}{双方|shuāng fāng}{付出|fù chū}。 Friendship takes effort from both sides. |
| {寻找|xún zhǎo} | {朋友|péng you}, {机会|jī huì}, {答案|dá àn} | {他|tā}{一直|yì zhí}{在|zài}{寻找|xún zhǎo}{真正|zhēn zhèng}{的|de}{朋友|péng you}。 He's always been looking for real friends. |
| {提起|tí qǐ} | a person, a matter | {他|tā}{很|hěn}{少|shǎo}{提起|tí qǐ}{他|tā}{的|de}{家人|jiā rén}。 He rarely mentions his family. |
| {约定|yuē dìng} | a time, a place; also "an agreement" | {我们|wǒ men}{约定|yuē dìng}{每|měi}{年|nián}{见|jiàn}{一|yí}{次|cì}{面|miàn}。 We agreed to meet once a year. |

{寻找|xún zhǎo} is the written partner of {找|zhǎo}: {找|zhǎo}{朋友|péng you} in chat, {寻找|xún zhǎo} in a story or an article. A conversation is a
{谈话|tán huà} (or {谈|tán} + {话|huà}: {谈|tán}{了|le}{一|yí}{次|cì}{话|huà}), and its topic is a {话题|huà tí}: {我们|wǒ men}{有|yǒu}{很|hěn}{多|duō}{共同|gòng tóng}{的|de}{话题|huà tí} (we have lots to talk about).

## Good qualities, deep friendships

- **People**: {真诚|zhēn chéng} (sincere), {热心|rè xīn} (warm-hearted, keen to help), {善良|shàn liáng} (kind-hearted, good), {可靠|kě kào}
  (reliable). Everyone has a {个性|gè xìng} (personality, individuality), {长处|cháng chù} (strong points) and {短处|duǎn chù}
  (weak points): {多|duō}{看|kàn}{别人|bié ren}{的|de}{长处|cháng chù} (look for the good in people).
- **Friendships**: {深厚|shēn hòu} (deep), {密切|mì qiè} (close: {关系|guān xi}{密切|mì qiè}, {密切|mì qiè}{联系|lián xì}), {长久|cháng jiǔ} (lasting): {长久|cháng jiǔ}{的|de}{友谊|yǒu yì}.
- **{唯一|wéi yī}** is "only, sole": {他|tā}{是|shì}{我|wǒ}{唯一|wéi yī}{的|de}{朋友|péng you}。 (He's my only friend.) It describes a noun, with {的|de}. "I only
  have one friend" is {我|wǒ}{只有|zhǐ yǒu}{一|yí}{个|gè}{朋友|péng you}.

## By chance: {偶然|ǒu rán}, {碰|pèng}, {碰见|pèng jiàn}, {哦|ò}

{偶然|ǒu rán} is "by chance, accidental": {一|yí}{次|cì}{偶然|ǒu rán}{的|de}{机会|jī huì} (a chance opportunity), {我们|wǒ men}{是|shì}{偶然|ǒu rán}{认识|rèn shi}{的|de} (we met by
chance). Don't confuse it with HSK 4's {偶尔|ǒu ěr} (occasionally, now and then): same {偶|ǒu}, different meaning.

{碰|pèng} is "to bump, to touch": {别|bié}{碰|pèng}{我|wǒ}{的|de}{电脑|diàn nǎo} (don't touch my computer). {碰见|pèng jiàn} is "to run into someone",
the spoken partner of {遇见|yù jiàn}: {我|wǒ}{在|zài}{超市|chāo shì}{碰见|pèng jiàn}{了|le}{老师|lǎo shī} (I ran into my teacher at the supermarket).

{哦|ò} ò, said with a falling tone, is "oh, I see": the sound of understanding something just now.
"{他|tā}{是|shì}{我|wǒ}{中学|zhōng xué}{同学|tóng xué}。""{哦|ò}，{原来|yuán lái}{是|shì}{这样|zhè yàng}。" ("He's a school friend of mine." "Oh, I see.")

## Characters
{=

Fourteen of this lesson's twenty characters are lesson 10's: its arts words used them before they
were taught. Now you learn to write them. The last six are this lesson's own.

| Character | Meaning | Pinyin | Radical | Strokes | Words |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 狂 | mad, wild | kuáng | 犭 | 7 | {疯狂|fēng kuáng} (lesson 10) |
| 灰 | ash; grey | huī | 火 | 6 | {灰色|huī sè} (lesson 10), {灰|huī} (lesson 22) |
| 掌 | palm (of the hand) | zhǎng | 手 | 12 | {鼓掌|gǔ zhǎng}, {掌声|zhǎng shēng} (lesson 10), {掌握|zhǎng wò} (lesson 16) |
| 烈 | fierce, intense ✎ | liè | 灬 | 10 | {激烈|jī liè} (lesson 10), {强烈|qiáng liè} (lesson 14), {热烈|rè liè} (lesson 15) |
| 哈 | (laughter; ha) ✎ | hā | 口 | 9 | {哈|hā} (lesson 10) |
| 擅 | be good at | shàn | 扌 | 16 | {擅长|shàn cháng} (lesson 10) |
| 匹 | (measure word for horses) ✎ | pǐ | 匸 | 4 | {一|yì}{匹|pǐ}{马|mǎ} (lesson 10) |
| 蹈 | step, tread | dǎo | 足 | 17 | {舞蹈|wǔ dǎo} (lesson 10) |
| 武 | martial, military ✎ | wǔ | 止 | 8 | {武术|wǔ shù} (lesson 10) |
| 欣 | glad | xīn | 欠 | 8 | {欣赏|xīn shǎng} (lesson 10) |
| 赏 | admire; reward | shǎng | 贝 | 12 | {欣赏|xīn shǎng} (lesson 10), {赏|shǎng} (lesson 25) |
| 余 | surplus, spare ✎ | yú | 人 | 7 | {业余|yè yú} (lesson 10), {其余|qí yú} (lesson 27) |
| 览 | look at | lǎn | 见 | 9 | {展览|zhǎn lǎn} (lesson 10), {浏览|liú lǎn} (lesson 20) |
| 紫 | purple | zǐ | 糸 | 12 | {紫|zǐ} (lesson 10) |
