> {李明|Lǐ Míng}

New words: {视频|shì pín} (video, HSK 4: {视频|shì pín}{聊天|liáo tiān} is a video call), {不耐烦|bú nài fán} (impatient, HSK 6), {西班牙|Xī bān yá}
Xī bān yá (Spain). {因为|yīn wèi}…{而|ér}… is "because of…" in a more written
style ({而|ér} links the cause to the result).

1. What is the email mainly about?
2. How did Li Ming meet Harry, and what do they do every Wednesday?
3. What does Li Ming think matters most in making friends?
4. What does the last paragraph suggest about how Li Ming feels?

<details>
<summary>Answers and translation</summary>

1. How Li Ming made friends after arriving alone in a strange city.
2. Through the university's "study partner" scheme for international students ({学校|xué xiào}{给|gěi}{留学生|liú xué shēng}{组织|zǔ zhī}{了|le}{一|yí}{个|gè}"{学习|xué xí}{伙伴|huǒ bàn}"{活动|huó dòng}); they have lunch together and teach each other English and Chinese.
3. Being sincere ({最|zuì}{重要|zhòng yào}{的|de}{是|shì}{真诚|zhēn chéng}), and looking at people's strong points.
4. He's made friends, but he still misses his friends in Beijing and Wang Fang most: he's a little homesick.

"Fangfang, Hi! Last time we video-called, you asked whether I'd made any friends here. I've got
some time today, so I'm writing you a few lines. When I first came, I was all on my own: the
city was strange to me, the people in the streets were strangers, and I didn't know a soul. For
the first few weeks I went back to where I live every day after class, cooked alone, read alone,
and felt a bit low. Still, the strangers here were all friendly to me: once, when I asked the way
in the street, an old lady kindly walked me there, more than ten minutes. Then the university organised a 'study partner' scheme for international
students: every newcomer could make friends with a British student. My partner is called Harry,
and he's very warm-hearted. Far from getting impatient because my English is slow, he often
starts conversations with me himself. We agreed to have lunch together every Wednesday: he helps
me practise English, and I teach him a little Chinese. Gradually, through Harry, I've met more
people. I've found that making friends doesn't really take any special method; what matters most is
being sincere. If you treat people sincerely, they'll trust you too. Everyone has strong points
and weak points, and if you look at people's strong points when you're with them, you get on
better and better. Last month I ran into a student from Spain in the library, called Carlos. He
came here to study on his own too, and we got on the moment we met. Now the three of us often go
and play football. But the people I think of most are still my old friends in
Beijing, and you. Please say hi to Anna for me! Li Ming"
</details>

## Write it: a story in four pictures

The writing part of HSK 5 begins with a story of at least 100 characters about four pictures. Here
are four pictures, described in words. Write the story (100–150 characters), using at least four of
{独自|dú zì}, {陌生|mò shēng}, {碰|pèng}, {热心|rè xīn}, {偶然|ǒu rán}, {相处|xiāng chǔ}, {彼此|bǐ cǐ}.

1. A young woman carries a big box into a lift in a new block of flats. She's on her own.
2. The lift stops; the box falls and things roll across the floor. A woman of about the same age
   helps her pick them up.
3. In the corridor they talk and laugh: it turns out they work in the same building.
4. A month later the two of them are cooking dinner together in a kitchen.

<details>
<summary>Model answer</summary>

> {小林|Xiǎo Lín}{刚|gāng}{搬|bān}{到|dào}{一|yí}{个|gè}{陌生|mò shēng}{的|de}{城市|chéng shì}，{独自|dú zì}{住|zhù}{在|zài}{一|yí}{套|tào}{小|xiǎo}{公寓|gōng yù}{里|lǐ}。{搬家|bān jiā}{那|nà}{天|tiān}，{她|tā}{抱|bào}{着|zhe}{一|yí}{个|gè}{大|dà}{箱子|xiāng zi}{进|jìn}{了|le}{电梯|diàn tī}。{电梯|diàn tī}{门|mén}{一|yì}{开|kāi}，{箱子|xiāng zi}{碰|pèng}{到|dào}{了|le}{门|mén}，{东西|dōng xi}{掉|diào}{了|le}{一|yí}{地|dì}。{旁边|páng biān}{一|yí}{个|gè}{女孩儿|nǚ háir}{马上|mǎ shàng}{帮|bāng}{她|tā}{捡|jiǎn}。{两|liǎng}{个|gè}{人|rén}{一边|yì biān}{捡|jiǎn}{一边|yì biān}{聊|liáo}，{才|cái}{发现|fā xiàn}{她们|tā men}{竟然|jìng rán}{在|zài}{一|yí}{个|gè}{大|dà}{楼|lóu}{里|lǐ}{上班|shàng bān}。{这个|zhè ge}{女孩儿|nǚ háir}{非常|fēi cháng}{热心|rè xīn}，{后来|hòu lái}{常常|cháng cháng}{请|qǐng}{小林|Xiǎo Lín}{去|qù}{她|tā}{家|jiā}{吃|chī}{饭|fàn}。{一|yí}{个|gè}{月|yuè}{以后|yǐ hòu}，{她们|tā men}{已经|yǐ jīng}{成|chéng}{了|le}{好|hǎo}{朋友|péng you}，{相处|xiāng chǔ}{得|de}{非常|fēi cháng}{愉快|yú kuài}。

(133 characters.) {小林|Xiǎo Lín} Xiǎo Lín is a name; {在|zài}{一|yí}{个|gè}{大|dà}{楼|lóu}{里|lǐ} is "in the same building" ({一|yí}{个|gè} means "the same" in speech); {公寓|gōng yù} (flat) and {捡|jiǎn} (to pick up) are lesson 09's; {愉快|yú kuài} (happy,
HSK 4). Check your own story: four pictures in order, a beginning and an end, connectors ({后来|hòu lái}, {一|yí}{个|gè}{月|yuè}{以后|yǐ hòu}),
at least 100 characters.
</details>

## Say it

```speak
# Friends
{我们|wǒ men}{认识|rèn shi}{十|shí}{年|nián}{了|le}，{彼此|bǐ cǐ}{都|dōu}{很|hěn}{了解|liǎo jiě}。
= We've known each other for ten years, and we understand each other well.
{他|tā}{始终|shǐ zhōng}{没|méi}{说话|shuō huà}。
= He didn't say a word the whole time.
{我|wǒ}{想|xiǎng}{跟|gēn}{你|nǐ}{单独|dān dú}{谈|tán}{谈|tán}。
= I'd like to talk to you in private.
{他|tā}{独自|dú zì}{一|yì}{人|rén}{来|lái}{到|dào}{这个|zhè ge}{陌生|mò shēng}{的|de}{城市|chéng shì}。
= He came to this strange city on his own.
{我|wǒ}{在|zài}{超市|chāo shì}{偶然|ǒu rán}{碰见|pèng jiàn}{了|le}{一|yí}{个|gè}{熟人|shú rén}。
= I ran into someone I know at the supermarket.
{我们|wǒ men}{俩|liǎ}{很|hěn}{合得来|hé de lái}。
= We get on really well.
```

## Pronunciation

- {处|chǔ} chǔ in {相处|xiāng chǔ} (xiāng chǔ, to get along) is third tone; {长处|cháng chù} cháng chù and {短处|duǎn chù} duǎn chù have the
  fourth-tone chù of {到处|dào chù}. Don't let them swap.
- {彼此|bǐ cǐ} bǐ cǐ: two third tones, said bí cǐ (third-tone sandhi). {此|cǐ} has the *c* of {次|cì} (ts with a puff of
  air), not *ch*.
- {陌生|mò shēng} mò shēng: {陌|mò} is mò, not bǎi, even though {百|bǎi} is inside.
- {熟人|shú rén} shú rén: {熟|shú} is shú here (in speech also shóu, as in {熟|shú}{了|le} "ripe"); the course writes shú.
- {哦|ò} ò: falling, short, like a nod. (A rising ó is "oh?", surprised; the course's word is ò.)
- {唯一|wéi yī} wéi yī: {一|yī} keeps yī at the end of the word.

## Common mistakes

- Before {的|de}, use the pronoun: {彼此|bǐ cǐ}{的|de}{了解|liǎo jiě}, {彼此|bǐ cǐ}{之间|zhī jiān} (with {互相|hù xiāng} these are unusual). Before a verb, both work: {彼此|bǐ cǐ}{帮助|bāng zhù}, {互相|hù xiāng}{帮助|bāng zhù}.
- ~~{我|wǒ}{始终|shǐ zhōng}{等|děng}{到|dào}{十|shí}{点|diǎn}~~: up to a point in time, use {一直|yì zhí}: {我|wǒ}{一直|yì zhí}{等到|děng dào}{十|shí}{点|diǎn}.
- ~~{一个|yí gè}{独自|dú zì}{的|de}{房间|fáng jiān}~~: {独自|dú zì} only goes before a verb. A room of one's own is {单独|dān dú}{的|de}{房间|fáng jiān}.
- {偶然|ǒu rán} (by chance) is not {偶尔|ǒu ěr} (occasionally): {我们|wǒ men}{偶然|ǒu rán}{认识|rèn shi}{了|le} (we met by chance); {我|wǒ}{偶尔|ǒu ěr}{给|gěi}{他|tā}{打电话|dǎ diàn huà} (I call him now and then).
- {相处|xiāng chǔ} is xiāng chǔ, not xiāng chù.
- ~~{我|wǒ}{唯一|wéi yī}{有|yǒu}{一个|yí gè}{朋友|péng you}~~: {唯一|wéi yī} describes a noun: {他|tā}{是|shì}{我|wǒ}{唯一|wéi yī}{的|de}{朋友|péng you}, or say {我|wǒ}{只有|zhǐ yǒu}{一|yí}{个|gè}{朋友|péng you}.

## Key points

- {彼此|bǐ cǐ} (pronoun): each other; also before {的|de} / {之间|zhī jiān} ({彼此|bǐ cǐ}{的|de}{了解|liǎo jiě}). {互相|hù xiāng} is an adverb only. {彼此|bǐ cǐ}{彼此|bǐ cǐ}: same to you.
- {始终|shǐ zhōng}: from start to finish, often negative ({始终|shǐ zhōng}{没|méi}{说话|shuō huà}); {一直|yì zhí} for "up to a time" and "straight on".
- {分别|fēn bié}: to part (verb); separately, respectively (adverb).
- {单独|dān dú}: apart from the others (adverb or {单独|dān dú}{的|de} + noun); {独自|dú zì}: all by oneself (adverb only).
- {不但|bú dàn}{不|bù} / {没|méi}…{反而|fǎn ér}…: the result goes against what you'd expect.
- {相处|xiāng chǔ} / {处|chǔ} chǔ (get along), {合得来|hé de lái}, {对待|duì dài}, {交往|jiāo wǎng}, {接触|jiē chù}, {靠|kào} / {可靠|kě kào}, {信任|xìn rèn}.
- {熟人|shú rén} (acquaintance) between {朋友|péng you} and {陌生|mò shēng}{人|rén}; {他人|tā rén} is the written {别人|bié ren}.
- New characters: {狂|kuáng} {灰|huī} {掌|zhǎng} {烈|liè} {哈|hā} {擅|shàn} {匹|pǐ} {蹈|dǎo} {武|wǔ} {欣|xīn} {赏|shǎng} {余|yú} {览|lǎn} {紫|zǐ} {彼|bǐ} {伴|bàn} {触|chù} {靠|kào} {陌|mò} {碰|pèng}; new radicals 匸 and {角|jiǎo}.

The words from this lesson are listed below; they join your vocabulary reviews when you complete
the lesson.

lessons.title: Love, marriage and a wedding
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

Wang Fang goes to a university friend's wedding, and tells Li Ming all about it on a video call
from England. On the way you'll learn the words of going out, falling in love, breaking up and
getting married, and the different words for husband and wife, which depend very much on who is
talking to whom.

The grammar:

- {被|bèi} / {叫|jiào} / {让|ràng} + doer + {给|gěi} + verb: the **[[spoken passive]]** with {给|gěi} ({我|wǒ}{的|de}{蛋糕|dàn gāo}{被|bèi}{弟弟|dì di}{给|gěi}{吃|chī}{了|le});
- {居然|jū rán} and {果然|guǒ rán}: "to my surprise" and "just as expected", two **[[adverbs of mood]]**;
- {当|dàng}, {当成|dàng chéng}, {当作|dàng zuò}: to treat as, to take for ({把|bǎ} A {当成|dàng chéng} B);
- {称|chēng} chēng: to call ({称|chēng}…{为|wéi}…, written).

## The passive with {给|gěi}

You know the {被|bèi} sentence (HSK 3) and its spoken partners {叫|jiào} and {让|ràng} (HSK 4): the receiver comes
first, then {被|bèi} / {叫|jiào} / {让|ràng} and the doer, then the verb with a result.

{我|wǒ}{的|de}{蛋糕|dàn gāo}{被|bèi}{弟弟|dì di}{吃|chī}{了|le}。 — My cake's been eaten by my little brother.

In speech, a {给|gěi} often goes straight before the verb. It doesn't change the meaning; it makes the
sentence sound more lively and colloquial, and it's typical when something unwelcome has happened:

{我|wǒ}{的|de}{蛋糕|dàn gāo}{被|bèi}{弟弟|dì di}{给|gěi}{吃|chī}{了|le}！ — My cake got eaten by my little brother!

{我|wǒ}{的|de}{自行车|zì xíng chē}{叫|jiào}{人|rén}{给|gěi}{骑|qí}{走|zǒu}{了|le}。 — Someone's gone off with my bike.

{窗户|chuāng hu}{让|ràng}{风|fēng}{给|gěi}{吹|chuī}{开|kāi}{了|le}。 — The window was blown open by the wind.

Three more things about this {给|gěi}:

- {叫|jiào} and {让|ràng} must name the doer ({叫|jiào}{人|rén}, {让|ràng}{风|fēng}); {被|bèi} needn't ({我|wǒ}{的|de}{自行车|zì xíng chē}{被|bèi}{骑|qí}{走|zǒu}{了|le}).
- {给|gěi} can be the passive marker on its own, with no {被|bèi} and no doer: {杯子|bēi zi}{给|gěi}{打|dǎ}{碎|suì}{了|le} (the glass got
  broken). This is very colloquial.
- {给|gěi} also turns up in {把|bǎ} sentences, in the same spot and with the same feel: {他|tā}{把|bǎ}{我|wǒ}{的|de}{电脑|diàn nǎo}{给|gěi}{弄|nòng}{坏|huài}{了|le} (he's
  gone and broken my computer).

This {给|gěi} belongs to conversation. In a report or a notice, leave it out (formal writing has its own
passive, {为|wéi}…{所|suǒ}, in lesson 27). The patterns are collected in the reference sheet "{把|bǎ} and {被|bèi} at HSK 5".

## {居然|jū rán} and {果然|guǒ rán}: surprised or not

Both are adverbs before the verb (or the subject, for {果然|guǒ rán}), and both tell you how the speaker feels
about what happened. They are opposites:

| | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| {居然|jū rán} | to my surprise; it's hard to believe | {他|tā}{居然|jū rán}{忘|wàng}{了|le}{自己|zì jǐ}{的|de}{婚礼|hūn lǐ}{是|shì}{哪|nǎ}{天|tiān}！ He'd actually forgotten the date of his own wedding! |
| {果然|guǒ rán} | just as expected; sure enough | {我|wǒ}{说|shuō}{他|tā}{会|huì}{迟到|chí dào}，{他|tā}{果然|guǒ rán}{迟到|chí dào}{了|le}。 I said he'd be late, and sure enough he was. |

- {居然|jū rán} is the same as HSK 4's {竟然|jìng rán}; both are common in speech and writing. The surprise can be
  pleasant: {十|shí}{年|nián}{没|méi}{见|jiàn}，{她|tā}{居然|jū rán}{还|hái}{记得|jì de}{我|wǒ}{的|de}{名字|míng zi} (ten years on, and she still remembered my name).
- {果然|guǒ rán} confirms something said or thought before, so there's usually an earlier clause with {说|shuō},
  {觉得|jué de}, {听说|tīng shuō}: {听说|tīng shuō}{这|zhè}{家|jiā}{饭馆|fàn guǎn}{很|hěn}{好吃|hǎo chī}，{果然|guǒ rán}{不错|bú cuò} (I'd heard this restaurant was good, and it really is).
  It can open its clause with a comma: {果然|guǒ rán}，{第|dì}{二|èr}{天|tiān}{就|jiù}{下|xià}{雪|xuě}{了|le} (sure enough, it snowed the next day).

Words like these, which add the speaker's attitude rather than facts, are **[[adverbs of mood]]**.
You've met {反正|fǎn zhèng} and {似乎|sì hū} in module 2; {毕竟|bì jìng} and {根本|gēn běn} come in lesson 13, {简直|jiǎn zhí} and {反而|fǎn ér} in lesson 14.

## {当|dàng}, {当成|dàng chéng}, {当作|dàng zuò}: to treat as, to take for

{把|bǎ} A {当成|dàng chéng} B (or {当作|dàng zuò} B, or just {当|dàng} B) says that someone treats A as B, or takes A for B:

{她|tā}{把|bǎ}{我|wǒ}{当成|dàng chéng}{亲|qīn}{妹妹|mèi mei}。 — She treats me like her own sister.

{别|bié}{把|bǎ}{我|wǒ}{当|dàng}{孩子|hái zi}！ — Don't treat me like a child!

{我|wǒ}{把|bǎ}{他|tā}{当成|dàng chéng}{服务员|fú wù yuán}{了|le}。 — I took him for a waiter.

The last one is a mistake, and {当成|dàng chéng} is the usual word for that: {当成|dàng chéng} is "to take for, to mistake for"
as well as "to treat as". {当作|dàng zuò} is a little more written and is mostly "to treat as, to use as": {把|bǎ}
{阳台|yáng tái}{当作|dàng zuò}{书房|shū fáng} (use the balcony as a study). Without {把|bǎ}, {当|dàng} can take a whole clause in speech: {他们|tā men}{当|dàng}{我|wǒ}{是|shì}{一|yì}{家人|jiā rén}
(they treat me as one of the family).

In all of these the character is read dàng, fourth tone. In {当时|dāng shí} (at that time), {当然|dāng rán} (of course)
and lesson 13's {当年|dāng nián} (in those years) it's dāng, first tone. {服务员|fú wù yuán} (a waiter, a member of staff) is
from HSK 3.

## {称|chēng}: to call

{称|chēng} chēng is "to call (someone something)", in writing: {称|chēng} A {为|wéi} B, or in the passive, A {被|bèi}{称为|chēng wéi} B:

{人们|rén men}{称|chēng}{昆明|Kūn míng}{为|wéi}"{春城|chūn chéng}"。 — People call Kunming "the City of Spring".

{结婚|jié hūn}{常|cháng}{被|bèi}{称为|chēng wéi}"{人生|rén shēng}{大事|dà shì}"。 — Marriage is often called "the great event of a lifetime".

In speech you'd say {叫|jiào}: {大家|dà jiā}{都|dōu}{叫|jiào}{他|tā}{老王|lǎo Wáng}. (The same character, also chēng, means "to weigh" in lesson 07's
{称|chēng}{一|yì}{称|chēng}; lesson 18 has {称为|chēng wéi} "to be called" as one word.)

## Going out, falling in love, breaking up

| Word | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| {恋爱|liàn ài} | romantic love; to be in love | {谈|tán}{恋爱|liàn ài} to go out with someone; {他们|tā men}{谈|tán}{了|le}{五|wǔ}{年|nián}{恋爱|liàn ài}。 |
| {对象|duì xiàng} | a partner (boyfriend, girlfriend, with marriage in view) | {你|nǐ}{有|yǒu}{对象|duì xiàng}{了|le}{吗|ma}？ Are you seeing anyone? |
| {追|zhuī} | to chase; to court, try to win someone | {他|tā}{追|zhuī}{了|le}{她|tā}{一|yì}{年|nián}{多|duō}。 He tried to win her for over a year. |
| {魅力|mèi lì} | charm, attraction | {她|tā}{很|hěn}{有|yǒu}{魅力|mèi lì}。 She has a lot of charm. |
| {打扮|dǎ ban} | to dress up; how someone is dressed | {她|tā}{今天|jīn tiān}{打扮|dǎ ban}{得|de}{很|hěn}{漂亮|piào liang}。 She's dressed up beautifully today. |
| {惊喜|jīng xǐ} | a pleasant surprise; pleasantly surprised | {我|wǒ}{给|gěi}{你|nǐ}{准备|zhǔn bèi}{了|le}{一|yí}{个|gè}{惊喜|jīng xǐ}。 I've got a surprise for you. |
| {拥抱|yōng bào} | to hug | {两|liǎng}{个|gè}{人|rén}{拥抱|yōng bào}{在|zài}{一起|yì qǐ}。 The two of them hugged. |
| {珍惜|zhēn xī} | to treasure, to cherish | {珍惜|zhēn xī}{在|zài}{一起|yì qǐ}{的|de}{时间|shí jiān} cherish the time together |
| {陪伴|péi bàn} | to keep someone company; company | {谢谢|xiè xie}{你|nǐ}{一直|yì zhí}{陪伴|péi bàn}{我|wǒ}。 Thank you for always being there with me. |
| {分手|fēn shǒu} | to break up | {他们|tā men}{分手|fēn shǒu}{了|le}。 They've split up. |
| {失恋|shī liàn} | to be dumped, to lose one's love | {他|tā}{失恋|shī liàn}{了|le}，{心情|xīn qíng}{很|hěn}{不|bù}{好|hǎo}。 He's been dumped and he's very down. |
| {离婚|lí hūn} | to divorce | {他们|tā men}{离婚|lí hūn}{了|le}。 They got divorced. |

## The wedding

{婚礼|hūn lǐ} is the wedding (a ceremony and a party), with the {新郎|xīn láng} (groom) and the {新娘|xīn niáng} (bride), together
the {新人|xīn rén} (the newlyweds; {新人|xīn rén} also means "a newcomer"). After it they're a {夫妇|fū fù}, a married couple:
a written word, used like "Mr and Mrs": {秦天|Qín Tiān}{夫妇|fū fù} (Qin Tian and his wife). {结|jié} jié is "to tie, to
form", in {结婚|jié hūn} (to marry, HSK 3). Marriage is a {大事|dà shì}, an important event.

For the wedding clothes: a man wears a {西装|xī zhuāng} (a Western-style suit) and a {领带|lǐng dài} (a tie: {打|dǎ}{领带|lǐng dài}, to put on a
tie). In winter guests come with a {围巾|wéi jīn} (scarf: {戴|dài}{围巾|wéi jīn}) and {手套|shǒu tào} (gloves: {戴|dài}{手套|shǒu tào}), and the young ones
in {牛仔裤|niú zǎi kù} (jeans: {穿|chuān}{牛仔裤|niú zǎi kù}).

- {老公|lǎo gōng} and {老婆|lǎo po} are what many couples call each other, and what friends say among themselves. They are
  too casual for a formal introduction or a letter to someone you don't know well.
- {太太|tài tai} is "wife" and "Mrs"; to address an older married woman you don't know, {阿姨|ā yí} is safer.
- {爱人|ài ren} (HSK 3) works for husband or wife; it's heard less among young people.

### Stroke order

- **{丑|chǒu}**: four strokes: the horizontal-turn at the top left, the vertical, the middle horizontal,
  and the long bottom horizontal last.
- **{寻|xún}**: 彐 first (three strokes), then {寸|cùn} (the horizontal, the vertical hook, the dot).
- **{妇|fù}**: {女|nǚ} (three strokes), then 彐.
- **{郎|láng}**: the left side is a shortened {良|liáng}: the dot, the box, a vertical that ends with a rising flick,

- **{魅|mèi}**: write {鬼|guǐ} in full first (its long curving stroke is the seventh of nine), then {未|wèi} on the
  right, above the end of the curve.

> {秦天|Qín Tiān}{这个|zhè ge}{人|rén}{不|bú}{太|tài}{会|huì}{打扮|dǎ ban}，{也|yě}{不|bú}{会|huì}{说|shuō}{好听|hǎo tīng}{的|de}{话|huà}，{可是|kě shì}{他|tā}{总|zǒng}{把|bǎ}{我|wǒ}{的|de}{事|shì}{当作|dàng zuò}{他|tā}{自己|zì jǐ}{的|de}{大事|dà shì}。{有|yǒu}{一|yí}{次|cì}{我|wǒ}{说|shuō}{想|xiǎng}{看|kàn}{一|yì}{本|běn}{书|shū}，{没|méi}{过|guò}{几|jǐ}{天|tiān}，{那|nà}{本|běn}{书|shū}{就|jiù}{出现|chū xiàn}{在|zài}{了|le}{我|wǒ}{的|de}{桌子|zhuō zi}{上|shàng}。{我|wǒ}{生病|shēng bìng}{的|de}{时候|shí hou}，{他|tā}{一|yí}{夜|yè}{没|méi}{睡|shuì}，{在|zài}{医院|yī yuàn}{陪伴|péi bàn}{我|wǒ}；{我|wǒ}{工作|gōng zuò}{不|bú}{顺利|shùn lì}{的|de}{时候|shí hou}，{他|tā}{总是|zǒng shì}{最|zuì}{耐心|nài xīn}{地|de}{听|tīng}{我|wǒ}{说话|shuō huà}。
>
> {人们|rén men}{常|cháng}{称|chēng}{结婚|jié hūn}{为|wéi}"{人生|rén shēng}{大事|dà shì}"。{我|wǒ}{想|xiǎng}，{结婚|jié hūn}{不|bú}{是|shì}{爱情|ài qíng}{的|de}{结束|jié shù}，{而|ér}{是|shì}{一|yí}{个|gè}{新|xīn}{的|de}{开始|kāi shǐ}。{从|cóng}{今天|jīn tiān}{起|qǐ}，{我们|wǒ men}{就是|jiù shì}{夫妇|fū fù}{了|le}。{我们|wǒ men}{一定|yí dìng}{会|huì}{珍惜|zhēn xī}{彼此|bǐ cǐ}，{互相|hù xiāng}{照顾|zhào gù}，{好好|hǎo hǎo}{过日子|guò rì zi}。
>
> {最后|zuì hòu}，{再|zài}{一|yí}{次|cì}{感谢|gǎn xiè}{我们|wǒ men}{的|de}{父母|fù mǔ}，{也|yě}{感谢|gǎn xiè}{今天|jīn tiān}{来|lái}{到|dào}{这里|zhè lǐ}{的|de}{每|měi}{一|yí}{位|wèi}{朋友|péng you}。{谢谢|xiè xie}{大家|dà jiā}！

{说|shuō}{起来|qǐ lái} is "come to think of it"; {吵|chǎo} (to quarrel) is lesson 14's word. {不|bú}{是|shì}…{而|ér}{是|shì}… (not… but…) is HSK 4's.

1. What is the speech mainly about?
2. What did He Yu think of Qin Tian at first, and why?
3. What did He Yu learn after the three months without contact?
4. What does the speech suggest about what kind of person Qin Tian is?

<details>
<summary>Answers and translation</summary>

1. How the couple met, what they went through, and what marriage means to the bride.
2. Not much: he wore old jeans and wasn't very polite ({我|wǒ}{对|duì}{他|tā}{的|de}{印象|yìn xiàng}{并|bìng}{不|bù}{好|hǎo}).
3. That loving someone isn't only being happy together but not leaving when things are hard ({更|gèng}{是|shì}{在|zài}{困难|kùn nan}{的|de}{时候|shí hou}{不|bù}{离开|lí kāi}).
4. He doesn't say sweet things, but he is caring and reliable: he takes her problems as seriously as his own ({总|zǒng}{把|bǎ}{我|wǒ}{的|de}{事|shì}{当作|dàng zuò}{他|tā}{自己|zì jǐ}{的|de}{大事|dà shì}), stayed up all night with her in hospital and listens patiently.

"Family and friends, good afternoon! Today is the day Qin Tian and I get married, and thank you
for coming to our wedding. Qin Tian and I met at an event at university. You may not believe it,
but the first time we met I didn't think much of him: he was wearing a pair of old jeans and
wasn't very polite. But after that, would you believe it, he waited for me at the library door
every day, for over a year. My classmates all said he was taking the chase far too seriously. We
went out for five years; we quarrelled and we broke up too. The worst time, we didn't speak for
three months. He was the one who rang first, and said to me: 'I've thought about it for a long
time: you're the most important person in my life.' At that moment I understood that loving
someone isn't only being happy together, it's also not leaving when things get hard. Qin Tian
isn't much good at dressing up, and he isn't good at saying sweet things, but he always treats my
problems as if they were his own big ones. Once I said I wanted to read a certain book, and a few
days later there it was on my desk. When I was ill, he stayed up all night with me at the
hospital; when work wasn't going well, he was always the one who listened most patiently. People
often call marriage 'the great event of a lifetime'. I think marriage isn't the end of love, but
a new beginning. From today we are husband and wife. We will cherish each other, look after each
other and make a good life together. Finally, thank you once again to our parents, and to every
friend who has come here today. Thank you all!"
</details>

## Say it: retell a story

The HSK 5 speaking test asks you to retell short passages (about 1½ minutes each, as reported).
Listen to this one, read it twice, then close the text and tell it in your own words. You don't
need every detail: who, what happened, how it turned out.

```speak
# A bunch of roses
{老张|Lǎo Zhāng}{和|hé}{太太|tài tai}{结婚|jié hūn}{三十|sān shí}{年|nián}{了|le}。
= Old Zhang and his wife have been married for thirty years.
{结婚纪念日|jié hūn jì niàn rì}{那|nà}{天|tiān}，{太太|tài tai}{早上|zǎo shang}{起来|qǐ lái}，{发现|fā xiàn}{老张|Lǎo Zhāng}{已经|yǐ jīng}{出门|chū mén}{了|le}。
= On their anniversary, his wife got up in the morning and found he'd already gone out.
{她|tā}{有点儿|yǒu diǎnr}{失望|shī wàng}，{心|xīn}{想|xiǎng}：{他|tā}{居然|jū rán}{把|bǎ}{这么|zhè me}{重要|zhòng yào}{的|de}{日子|rì zi}{给|gěi}{忘|wàng}{了|le}。
= She was a little disappointed, and thought: he's actually forgotten such an important day.
{晚上|wǎn shang}，{门|mén}{开|kāi}{了|le}，{老张|Lǎo Zhāng}{手|shǒu}{里|lǐ}{拿|ná}{着|zhe}{一|yí}{大|dà}{束|shù}{玫瑰|méi guī}{走|zǒu}{了|le}{进来|jìn lái}。
= In the evening the door opened, and in came Old Zhang with a big bunch of roses.
{原来|yuán lái}{他|tā}{一大早|yí dà zǎo}{就|jiù}{去|qù}{了|le}{花店|huā diàn}，{又|yòu}{去|qù}{饭馆|fàn guǎn}{订|dìng}{了|le}{位子|wèi zi}，{想|xiǎng}{给|gěi}{太太|tài tai}{一|yí}{个|gè}{惊喜|jīng xǐ}。
= It turned out he'd gone to the florist first thing, then booked a table at a restaurant, to give her a surprise.
{太太|tài tai}{笑|xiào}{着|zhe}{说|shuō}："{我|wǒ}{就|jiù}{知道|zhī dào}{你|nǐ}{不|bú}{会|huì}{忘|wàng}。"
= His wife laughed: "I knew you wouldn't forget."
{老张|Lǎo Zhāng}{说|shuō}："{你|nǐ}{看|kàn}，{我|wǒ}{果然|guǒ rán}{没|méi}{让|ràng}{你|nǐ}{失望|shī wàng}{吧|ba}？"
= Old Zhang said: "See? I didn't let you down, just as you thought, did I?"
```

{结婚纪念日|jié hūn jì niàn rì} is a wedding anniversary ({纪念|jì niàn} is lesson 25's word), {束|shù} a bunch (lesson 15), {订|dìng} to book (HSK 4)
and {位子|wèi zi} a seat, a table.

<details>
<summary>A model retelling</summary>

> {老张|Lǎo Zhāng}{和|hé}{太太|tài tai}{结婚|jié hūn}{三十|sān shí}{年|nián}{了|le}。{纪念日|jì niàn rì}{那|nà}{天|tiān}{早上|zǎo shang}，{老张|Lǎo Zhāng}{很|hěn}{早|zǎo}{就|jiù}{出门|chū mén}{了|le}，{太太|tài tai}{以为|yǐ wéi}{他|tā}{忘|wàng}{了|le}{这个|zhè ge}{日子|rì zi}，{心里|xīn li}{很|hěn}{失望|shī wàng}。{可是|kě shì}{晚上|wǎn shang}{老张|Lǎo Zhāng}{居然|jū rán}{拿|ná}{着|zhe}{一|yí}{大|dà}{束|shù}{玫瑰|méi guī}{回来|huí lái}{了|le}。{原来|yuán lái}{他|tā}{是|shì}{去|qù}{买|mǎi}{花|huā}、{订|dìng}{饭馆|fàn guǎn}{了|le}，{想|xiǎng}{给|gěi}{太太|tài tai}{一|yí}{个|gè}{惊喜|jīng xǐ}。{太太|tài tai}{很|hěn}{高兴|gāo xìng}，{说|shuō}{她|tā}{早|zǎo}{就|jiù}{知道|zhī dào}{老张|Lǎo Zhāng}{不|bú}{会|huì}{忘|wàng}。

Retell in the third person, keep the order of events, and use the linking words you know ({可是|kě shì},
{原来|yuán lái}, {后来|hòu lái}). About a minute and a half is enough.
</details>

## Write it: a story in four pictures

Write a story of 100–150 characters about these four pictures. Use at least four of {玫瑰|méi guī}, {惊喜|jīng xǐ},
{居然|jū rán}, {果然|guǒ rán}, {被|bèi}…{给|gěi}, {等|děng}, {拥抱|yōng bào}.

1. A young man in a suit stands outside an office building at six in the evening, holding red
   roses.
2. It begins to rain. He holds the roses inside his jacket, and gets wet himself.
3. A young woman comes out of the building and stops in surprise.
4. She opens her umbrella over both of them, and they laugh.

<details>
<summary>Model answer</summary>

> {今天|jīn tiān}{是|shì}{小美|Xiǎo Měi}{的|de}{生日|shēng rì}。{下班|xià bān}{的|de}{时候|shí hou}，{男朋友|nán péng you}{小刚|Xiǎo Gāng}{拿|ná}{着|zhe}{一|yí}{束|shù}{红|hóng}{玫瑰|méi guī}，{站|zhàn}{在|zài}{她|tā}{公司|gōng sī}{楼|lóu}{下|xià}{等|děng}{她|tā}，{想|xiǎng}{给|gěi}{她|tā}{一|yí}{个|gè}{惊喜|jīng xǐ}。{没想到|méi xiǎng dào}，{天|tiān}{突然|tū rán}{下|xià}{起|qǐ}{了|le}{雨|yǔ}。{小刚|Xiǎo Gāng}{怕|pà}{玫瑰|méi guī}{被|bèi}{雨|yǔ}{给|gěi}{打|dǎ}{坏|huài}{了|le}，{就|jiù}{把|bǎ}{花|huā}{放|fàng}{在|zài}{外套|wài tào}{里|lǐ}，{自己|zì jǐ}{的|de}{头发|tóu fa}{和|hé}{衣服|yī fu}{都|dōu}{湿|shī}{了|le}。{小美|Xiǎo Měi}{一|yì}{出门|chū mén}{就|jiù}{看见|kàn jiàn}{了|le}{他|tā}，{又惊又喜|yòu jīng yòu xǐ}：{他|tā}{居然|jū rán}{在|zài}{雨|yǔ}{里|lǐ}{等|děng}{了|le}{半|bàn}{个|gè}{多|duō}{小时|xiǎo shí}！{她|tā}{赶快|gǎn kuài}{打开|dǎ kāi}{伞|sǎn}，{两|liǎng}{个|gè}{人|rén}{在|zài}{伞|sǎn}{下|xià}{笑|xiào}{了|le}{起来|qǐ lái}。

(124 characters.) {小美|Xiǎo Měi} and {小刚|Xiǎo Gāng} are names; {又惊又喜|yòu jīng yòu xǐ} is "surprised and delighted" ({又|yòu}…{又|yòu}…, HSK 3); {湿|shī} (wet) is
lesson 22's word.
</details>

## Pronunciation

- {当|dàng} in {当成|dàng chéng}, {当作|dàng zuò} and "treat as" is dàng (fourth tone); {当时|dāng shí}, {当然|dāng rán} have dāng.
- {恋爱|liàn ài} liàn ài: two fourth tones. {恋|liàn} is liàn, like {练|liàn} and {炼|liàn}.
- {玫瑰|méi guī} méi guī: you'll often hear the second syllable light (méi gui).
- {打扮|dǎ ban} dǎ ban and {老婆|lǎo po} lǎo po end on a light syllable.
- {新郎|xīn láng} xīn láng and {新娘|xīn niáng} xīn niáng: -áng both times, with and without the *i*.
- {居然|jū rán} jū rán: {居|jū} is jū, the same as in {邻居|lín jū} lín jū.

## Common mistakes

- ~~{杯子|bēi zi}{叫|jiào}{打碎|dǎ suì}{了|le}~~: {叫|jiào} and {让|ràng} need the doer: {杯子|bēi zi}{叫|jiào}{他|tā}{打|dǎ}{碎|suì}{了|le}, or {杯子|bēi zi}{被|bèi}{打|dǎ}{碎|suì}{了|le} / {杯子|bēi zi}{给|gěi}{打|dǎ}{碎|suì}{了|le}.
- ~~{我|wǒ}{说|shuō}{他|tā}{会|huì}{迟到|chí dào}，{他|tā}{居然|jū rán}{迟到|chí dào}{了|le}~~: if you said he would, it's no surprise: {他|tā}{果然|guǒ rán}{迟到|chí dào}{了|le}.
- {当成|dàng chéng} is dàng chéng, not dāng chéng.
- ~~{我|wǒ}{当成|dàng chéng}{他|tā}{服务员|fú wù yuán}~~: with {当成|dàng chéng}, the person treated goes after {把|bǎ}: {我|wǒ}{把|bǎ}{他|tā}{当成|dàng chéng}{服务员|fú wù yuán}{了|le}.
- {老公|lǎo gōng} / {老婆|lǎo po} in a formal introduction sounds too casual: say {这|zhè}{是|shì}{我|wǒ}{先生|xiān sheng} / {这|zhè}{是|shì}{我|wǒ}{太太|tài tai}, or {我|wǒ}{丈夫|zhàng fu} / {我|wǒ}{妻子|qī zi}.
- In a formal written report, leave out the spoken {给|gěi}: {窗户|chuāng hu}{被|bèi}{风|fēng}{吹|chuī}{坏|huài}{了|le}, not {窗户|chuāng hu}{被|bèi}{风|fēng}{给|gěi}{吹|chuī}{坏|huài}{了|le}.

## Key points

- {被|bèi} / {叫|jiào} / {让|ràng} + doer + {给|gěi} + verb: spoken passive, often for bad news; {叫|jiào} / {让|ràng} need the doer; {给|gěi} alone and {把|bǎ}…{给|gěi} too.
- {居然|jū rán} (= {竟然|jìng rán}): to my surprise. {果然|guǒ rán}: just as expected (after something said or thought before).
- {把|bǎ} A {当成|dàng chéng} / {当作|dàng zuò} / {当|dàng} B: treat A as B; {当成|dàng chéng} also "mistake A for B". {当|dàng} is dàng here.
- {称|chēng} A {为|wéi} B, A {被|bèi}{称为|chēng wéi} B: to call (written); spoken {叫|jiào}.
- {谈|tán}{恋爱|liàn ài}, {追|zhuī}, {分手|fēn shǒu}, {失恋|shī liàn}, {离婚|lí hūn}; {婚礼|hūn lǐ}, {新郎|xīn láng}, {新娘|xīn niáng}, {新人|xīn rén}, {夫妇|fū fù}.
- {丈夫|zhàng fu} / {妻子|qī zi} (neutral), {先生|xiān sheng} / {太太|tài tai} (polite), {爱人|ài ren} (older), {老公|lǎo gōng} / {老婆|lǎo po} (spoken, warm).
- New characters: {哦|ò} {私|sī} {唯|wéi} {寻|xún} {丑|chǒu} {妇|fù} {扮|bàn} {婆|pó} {玫|méi} {瑰|guī} {魅|mèi} {恋|liàn} {郎|láng} {珍|zhēn}; new radical 彐.

lessons.title: Grandparents, parents and children
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

On a free Sunday, Wang Fang goes back to her family's flat, where her grandmother lives, and her
grandmother gets out the old photos. This lesson is about families across three generations:
how people lived "in those years", what has changed, and what hasn't. It also sorts out the words
for grandparents, which depend on which side of the family they're on, and on where you're from.

The grammar is mostly adverbs that carry the speaker's view:

- {毕竟|bì jìng}: after all (the reason that settles it);
- {根本|gēn běn}: at all ({根本|gēn běn}{不|bù} / {根本|gēn běn}{没|méi}), and "fundamental";
- {本|běn} běn: originally (written; the {本来|běn lái} of speech), and "this" in {本人|běn rén}, {本|běn}{公司|gōng sī};
- {看|kān} kān (first tone): to look after, to mind ({看|kān}{孩子|hái zi});
- {一代|yí dài} and {代|dài}: a generation; and {代|dài} "on behalf of" ({代|dài}{我|wǒ}{问|wèn}{好|hǎo});
- {舍得|shě de} and {舍不得|shě bu de}: to be willing, or not willing, to part with something;
- the pattern A{着|zhe}A{着|zhe}: in the middle of doing A ({讲着讲着|jiǎng zhe jiǎng zhe}{就|jiù}{笑|xiào}{了|le}).

## {毕竟|bì jìng}: after all

{毕竟|bì jìng} gives the fact that decides the matter, the one you can't argue with. It goes before the
verb or the predicate:

{别|bié}{生|shēng}{他|tā}{的|de}{气|qì}{了|le}，{他|tā}{毕竟|bì jìng}{还是|hái shi}{个|gè}{孩子|hái zi}。 — Don't be angry with him: he's only a child, after all.

{奶奶|nǎi nai}{毕竟|bì jìng}{七十|qī shí}{多|duō}{岁|suì}{了|le}，{走路|zǒu lù}{比|bǐ}{以前|yǐ qián}{慢|màn}{多|duō}{了|le}。 — Grandma is over seventy, after all: she walks much more slowly
than she used to.

Often the {毕竟|bì jìng} clause explains why the other clause is reasonable, or why something can't be helped.
HSK 4's {到底|dào dǐ} also means "after all" in statements ({他|tā}{到底|dào dǐ}{是|shì}{个|gè}{孩子|hái zi}), but {到底|dào dǐ} is much more common in
questions, "…on earth?": {你|nǐ}{到底|dào dǐ}{想|xiǎng}{说|shuō}{什么|shén me}？ (What on earth are you trying to say?) {毕竟|bì jìng} is never used in
questions.

## {根本|gēn běn}: at all; fundamental

Before a negative, {根本|gēn běn} is "at all, simply (not)": stronger than {完全|wán quán}{不|bù} and very common in speech.

{我|wǒ}{根本|gēn běn}{不|bú}{认识|rèn shi}{他|tā}。 — I don't know him at all.

{那|nà}{时候|shí hou}{结婚|jié hūn}{根本|gēn běn}{没有|méi yǒu}{什么|shén me}{婚礼|hūn lǐ}。 — In those days there simply wasn't a wedding to speak of.

With {就是|jiù shì} it means "simply, really": {这|zhè}{根本|gēn běn}{就是|jiù shì}{两|liǎng}{回|huí}{事|shì} (these are two completely different things). Before
a noun it's an adjective, "fundamental, basic": {根本|gēn běn}{原因|yuán yīn} (the root cause), {根本|gēn běn}{问题|wèn tí} (the basic problem).
Don't use it to soften a sentence: {根本|gēn běn} makes it stronger, never weaker.

## {本|běn}: originally; this

{本|běn} běn (lesson 13's adverb; HSK 1's {本|běn} is the measure word for books) is the written partner of {本来|běn lái}
(HSK 4): what was planned or true before something changed.

{我|wǒ}{本|běn}{想|xiǎng}{周末|zhōu mò}{去|qù}{看|kàn}{你|nǐ}，{可是|kě shì}{公司|gōng sī}{突然|tū rán}{要|yào}{加班|jiā bān}。 — I'd meant to come and see you at the weekend, but work suddenly needed me.

{这|zhè}{件|jiàn}{事|shì}{本|běn}{应|yīng}{早点儿|zǎo diǎnr}{告诉|gào su}{你|nǐ}。 — I should have told you about this sooner.

{本|běn} also means "this, our, my" in formal language: {本人|běn rén} (I, myself; the person concerned: lesson 01),
{本|běn}{公司|gōng sī} (this company: lesson 02), {本|běn}{周|zhōu} (this week), {本|běn}{次|cì}{活动|huó dòng} (this event). You'll see it in notices and
formal letters, not in chat.

## {看|kān}: to look after

{看|kàn} is kàn (to look, to read) almost everywhere. Read kān, first tone, it means "to look after, to
keep an eye on":

{我|wǒ}{上班|shàng bān}{的|de}{时候|shí hou}，{邻居|lín jū}{大妈|dà mā}{帮|bāng}{我|wǒ}{看|kān}{孩子|hái zi}。 — While I was at work, the neighbour looked after my child.

{你|nǐ}{帮|bāng}{我|wǒ}{看|kān}{一下|yí xià}{行李|xíng li}，{我|wǒ}{去|qù}{买|mǎi}{水|shuǐ}。 — Keep an eye on my luggage for me: I'm going to buy some water.

{看|kān}{门|mén} (to keep the gate), {看|kān}{家|jiā} (to look after the house). For a person who needs care (an old person,
a patient) {照顾|zhào gù} is the usual word; {看|kān} kān is more like "mind, watch over".

## {一代|yí dài} and {代|dài}: generations

{代|dài} is a generation, and a dynasty or period ({唐代|Táng dài}, the Tang). With a number it's a measure word:

{我们|wǒ men}{家|jiā}{三|sān}{代|dài}{人|rén}{住|zhù}{在|zài}{一起|yì qǐ}。 — Three generations of our family live together.

{年轻|nián qīng}{一代|yí dài} (the younger generation), {我们|wǒ men}{这|zhè}{一代|yí dài}{人|rén} (people of my generation), {下|xià}{一代|yí dài} (the next generation).

{代|dài} is also a verb, "to stand in for, to do on someone's behalf": {请|qǐng}{代|dài}{我|wǒ}{向|xiàng}{你|nǐ}{父母|fù mǔ}{问|wèn}{好|hǎo} (please give my
regards to your parents). {代表|dài biǎo} (to represent, lesson 03) and {代替|dài tì} (to replace, lesson 19) share this sense.

## {舍得|shě de} and {舍不得|shě bu de}

{舍|shě} is "to give up, to let go". {舍得|shě de} is to be willing to part with something (money, a thing, a
person); {舍不得|shě bu de} is the opposite, and much more common:

{这些|zhè xiē}{老|lǎo}{照片|zhào piàn}，{奶奶|nǎi nai}{一|yì}{张|zhāng}{也|yě}{舍不得|shě bu de}{扔|rēng}。 — Grandma can't bear to throw away a single one of these old photos.

{他|tā}{很|hěn}{舍得|shě de}{给|gěi}{孩子|hái zi}{花|huā}{钱|qián}，{自己|zì jǐ}{却|què}{舍不得|shě bu de}{买|mǎi}{一|yí}{件|jiàn}{新|xīn}{衣服|yī fu}。 — He'll spend freely on his children, but won't buy himself a
new coat.

A question: {你|nǐ}{舍得|shě de}{吗|ma}？ (Can you bear to?) Before a verb, {舍不得|shě bu de} means "can't bear to do": {舍不得|shě bu de}{离开|lí kāi} (can't
bear to leave). {舍|shě} is shě here; in {宿舍|sù shè} (dormitory, lesson 17) it's shè, and the traditional forms differ
too ({+{舍不得|shě bu de}+}, {+{宿舍|sù shè}+}).

## A{着|zhe}A{着|zhe}: in the middle of doing something

The verb repeated with {着|zhe} twice says that something happened while an action was going on, often
without anyone planning it:

{奶奶|nǎi nai}{讲着讲着|jiǎng zhe jiǎng zhe}，{就|jiù}{笑|xiào}{了|le}{起来|qǐ lái}。 — Grandma was telling the story, and in the middle of it she started laughing.

{孩子|hái zi}{看着看着|kàn zhe kàn zhe}{就|jiù}{睡着|shuì zháo}{了|le}。 — The child fell asleep watching.

{我们|wǒ men}{走着走着|zǒu zhe zǒu zhe}，{就|jiù}{到|dào}{了|le}{以前|yǐ qián}{住|zhù}{的|de}{胡同|hú tòng}。 — We walked and walked, and found ourselves at the hutong where we used to live.

The first half is the ongoing action (V{着|zhe}V{着|zhe}), the second what happened unexpectedly, usually with
{就|jiù} or a result: {说着说着|shuō zhe shuō zhe}{哭|kū}{了|le} (started crying in the middle of talking). The verb is one syllable. This
is one of HSK 5's four-character patterns, like lesson 10's {说|shuō}{走|zǒu}{就|jiù}{走|zǒu}.

| {当年|dāng nián} | in those years; that year | {当年|dāng nián}{我们|wǒ men}{住|zhù}{在|zài}{胡同|hú tòng}{里|lǐ}。 Back then we lived in a hutong. |

- {从前|cóng qián} opens stories ({从前|cóng qián}{有|yǒu}{一|yí}{个|gè}{老人|lǎo rén}…: once upon a time there was an old man…) and also means "formerly".
- {当年|dāng nián} dāng nián is "back then, in those days" (the time you're talking about); {当年|dāng nián} dàng nián (that same year) is a
  different word you won't need yet.
- {如今|rú jīn} is {现在|xiàn zài} in a story or an article, usually in contrast with the past.
- {依然|yī rán} is the written {还是|hái shi} / {仍然|réng rán} (HSK 4).
- {胡同|hú tòng} hú tòng (lesson 21) are Beijing's old lanes, lined with courtyard houses (HSK 3 05h1).

## The family: who's who

- **Grandparents on the mother's side**: {外公|wài gōng} and {外婆|wài pó} in the south and in much of standard Chinese;
  **{姥爷|lǎo ye} lǎo ye and {姥姥|lǎo lao} lǎo lao** in the north, Beijing included. On the father's side everyone says
  {爷爷|yé ye} and {奶奶|nǎi nai}.
- **Children**: {儿女|ér nǚ} (sons and daughters), {子女|zǐ nǚ} (children, a little more formal: {子女|zǐ nǚ}{教育|jiào yù}). {宝贝|bǎo bèi} (treasure)
  is what parents call a small child: {宝贝|bǎo bèi}，{快|kuài}{来|lái}{吃|chī}{饭|fàn}！ {宝|bǎo} is short for it, as in {宝宝|bǎo bao} (baby).
- **Relatives**: {亲人|qīn rén} (one's family, the people closest to you), {亲情|qīn qíng} (family love). {亲|qīn} as an adjective
  is "one's own, by blood": {亲|qīn}{兄弟|xiōng dì} (brothers), {亲|qīn}{姐妹|jiě mèi}, {亲生|qīn shēng} (one's own birth child).
- **Strangers of your grandparents' age**: {大爷|dà ye} dà ye (uncle) and {大妈|dà mā} (auntie), especially in Beijing.
  In other places you'll hear {叔叔|shū shu} / {阿姨|ā yí} for people your parents' age and {爷爷|yé ye} / {奶奶|nǎi nai} for older people.
- **Written words**: {男子|nán zǐ} (a man) and {女子|nǚ zǐ} (a woman) in news and on signs ({男子|nán zǐ}{组|zǔ}, the men's group), and
  {妇女|fù nǚ} (women, as a group: {妇女|fù nǚ}{节|jié}, International Women's Day). In speech, {男|nán}{的|de} / {女|nǚ}{的|de}, {男人|nán rén} / {女人|nǚ rén}.

## Respect and love

{尊敬|zūn jìng} is "to respect, to look up to" ({尊敬|zūn jìng}{老人|lǎo rén}, {尊敬|zūn jìng}{老师|lǎo shī}); HSK 4's {尊重|zūn zhòng} is "to respect" a choice, a
right, a person's wishes. {看望|kàn wàng} is "to visit, to call on" (someone you care about: {看望|kàn wàng}{父母|fù mǔ}, {看望|kàn wàng}{病人|bìng rén}).
{想念|xiǎng niàn} is "to miss" (a person, a place: {想念|xiǎng niàn}{故乡|gù xiāng}), a little more written than {想|xiǎng}. {依靠|yī kào} is "to rely on",
and the person or thing you rely on ({老人|lǎo rén}{只能|zhǐ néng}{依靠|yī kào}{子女|zǐ nǚ}). {扶|fú} is "to support with the hand": {扶|fú}{老人|lǎo rén}{过|guò}{马路|mǎ lù}
(help an old person across the road). {藏|cáng} cáng is "to hide, to keep hidden": {奶奶|nǎi nai}{把|bǎ}{照片|zhào piàn}{藏|cáng}{在|zài}{柜子|guì zi}{里|lǐ}.

Precious things: {宝贵|bǎo guì} (precious, of time, experience, advice: {宝贵|bǎo guì}{的|de}{经验|jīng yàn}), {珍贵|zhēn guì} (precious and rare,
of objects and memories: {珍贵|zhēn guì}{的|de}{照片|zhào piàn}), and {难得|nán dé} (rare, hard to come by; also "for once": {难得|nán dé}{回|huí}{家|jiā}{一|yí}{次|cì}).

Two more: {地位|dì wèi} (position, status: {妇女|fù nǚ}{的|de}{地位|dì wèi} the status of women) and {身份|shēn fèn} (identity, status: {身份证|shēn fèn zhèng}, an
ID card).

"My grandmother was born in a hutong in Beijing more than seventy years ago. When she was little,
several families lived in one courtyard, everyone shared one tap, and in winter you had to light
your own fire. People didn't have much money, but neighbours were very close. Grandma says that back then, a family owning a bicycle was a big event. Later,
Grandma and Grandpa married, and both worked in a factory. They worked during the day and cooked
and washed clothes when they got home in the evening, and they asked the neighbours to mind their
child. Life was hard, but the family was together, and Grandma says she never felt it was hard.
By the time of my parents' generation, people began moving into blocks of flats, and homes had a
TV and a fridge. My mum is from the south; after university she came to Beijing on her own to
work, and left her parents behind. She often says that what she missed most then was her
mother's cooking, but she couldn't even bring herself to pay for a long-distance call: she could only write her
mother a letter once a month, and a letter took several days to arrive. Today my
generation is growing up in a completely different age. We have mobile phones and the internet,
and we can go wherever we like. Many young people become independent early: some go to work in
other cities, some go abroad to study, and get home only once or twice a year. My boyfriend is studying in Britain right now, and we can
video-call every day. Life has changed so much over three generations. But I've found there's
one thing that has never changed: however far apart we are, a family always misses each other and
relies on each other. I think that's what family love is."

## Pronunciation

- {看|kān} kān (look after) is first tone: {看|kān}{孩子|hái zi} kān hái zi. {看望|kàn wàng} (to visit) and {看见|kàn jiàn} have kàn.
- {舍|shě} (third tone) in {舍得|shě de} shě de and {舍不得|shě bu de} shě bu de; shè in {宿舍|sù shè}.
- {姥姥|lǎo lao} lǎo lao and {姥爷|lǎo ye} lǎo ye: {姥|lǎo} is third tone, the second syllable light. Don't confuse {姥爷|lǎo ye} with {老|lǎo}{爷|yé}.
- {大爷|dà ye} dà ye: light second syllable; {大妈|dà mā} dà mā keeps its first tone.
- {当年|dāng nián} dāng nián (back then); {当|dàng} dàng in {当成|dàng chéng} (lesson 12).
- {宝贝|bǎo bèi} bǎo bèi: in speech often bǎo bei.

## Common mistakes

- {毕竟|bì jìng} doesn't go in questions: for "what on earth?", say {到底|dào dǐ}: {你|nǐ}{到底|dào dǐ}{想|xiǎng}{说|shuō}{什么|shén me}？
- {根本|gēn běn} strengthens a negative ({根本|gēn běn}{不|bù}{知道|zhī dào}); don't use it to mean "basically, more or less" (that's {基本上|jī běn shang}, HSK 4).
- {看|kān}{孩子|hái zi} is kān hái zi, not kàn hái zi (which would mean "to look at the children").
- {我|wǒ}{很|hěn}{想念|xiǎng niàn}{北京|Běi jīng} is fine; ~~{我|wǒ}{想念|xiǎng niàn}{北京|Běi jīng}{去|qù}~~ isn't: {想念|xiǎng niàn} takes a person or a place, not a verb. (I'd like to go to Beijing: {我|wǒ}{想|xiǎng}{去|qù}{北京|Běi jīng}.)
- {尊敬|zūn jìng} is respect for a person ({尊敬|zūn jìng}{老人|lǎo rén}); for a choice or a wish, {尊重|zūn zhòng}: {尊重|zūn zhòng}{孩子|hái zi}{的|de}{选择|xuǎn zé}.
- {舍不得|shě bu de} + a verb is "can't bear to": {舍不得|shě bu de}{离开|lí kāi} (can't bear to leave). {舍不得|shě bu de} + a noun is "can't bear to part with": {舍不得|shě bu de}{这些|zhè xiē}{照片|zhào piàn}.

## Key points

- {毕竟|bì jìng}: after all (a deciding fact); not in questions. {到底|dào dǐ} for "on earth?".
- {根本|gēn běn}{不|bù} / {根本|gēn běn}{没|méi}: not at all; {根本|gēn běn} + noun: fundamental.
- {本|běn} běn (written): originally, had meant to ({本|běn}{想|xiǎng}…); this ({本人|běn rén}, {本|běn}{公司|gōng sī}, {本|běn}{周|zhōu}).
- {看|kān} kān: to look after, mind ({看|kān}{孩子|hái zi}, {看|kān}{家|jiā}).
- {代|dài}: generation ({三|sān}{代|dài}{人|rén}, {年轻|nián qīng}{一代|yí dài}); on behalf of ({代|dài}{我|wǒ}{问|wèn}{好|hǎo}).
- {舍得|shě de} / {舍不得|shě bu de}: willing / can't bear to part with or to do; {舍|shě}.
- A{着|zhe}A{着|zhe} + {就|jiù}…: something happened in the middle of A ({说着说着|shuō zhe shuō zhe}{就|jiù}{哭|kū}{了|le}).
- {从前|cóng qián}, {当年|dāng nián}, {如今|rú jīn}, {依然|yī rán}: then, back then, nowadays, still.
- {外公|wài gōng} / {外婆|wài pó} and {姥爷|lǎo ye} / {姥姥|lǎo lao} (north) for the mother's parents; {爷爷|yé ye} / {奶奶|nǎi nai} for the father's.
- New characters: {宝|bǎo} {贝|bèi} {藏|cáng} {扶|fú} {姥|lǎo} {舍|shě} {念|niàn} {依|yī} {敬|jìng}.

The words from this lesson are listed below; they join your vocabulary reviews when you complete
the lesson.

lessons.title: Arguments and making up
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

Every flat-share has its bad week. Wang Fang's job keeps her out until midnight, Anna's coursework
keeps her up, the washing-up piles high, and one night it all comes out. This lesson gives you the
words to quarrel, complain, apologise and comfort someone, and to describe feelings and faces in
the kind of detail an HSK 5 story needs.

The grammar:

- X {也|yě}{不|bú}{是|shì}，Y {也|yě}{不|bú}{是|shì}: caught between two bad choices ({说|shuō}{也|yě}{不|bú}{是|shì}，{不|bù}{说|shuō}{也|yě}{不|bú}{是|shì});
- {反而|fǎn ér}: on the contrary, instead (lesson 11 previewed {不但|bú dàn}{不|bù}…{反而|fǎn ér});
- {简直|jiǎn zhí}: simply, practically (strong exaggeration);
- {难以|nán yǐ}: hard to (written: {难以|nán yǐ}{相信|xiāng xìn});
- {令|lìng}: to make, to cause (written: {令|lìng}{人|rén}{失望|shī wàng}).

## X {也|yě}{不|bú}{是|shì}，Y {也|yě}{不|bú}{是|shì}: no way out

When both choices are bad, Chinese puts them side by side, each with {也|yě}{不|bú}{是|shì} ("isn't right either"):

{我|wǒ}{知道|zhī dào}{他|tā}{的|de}{秘密|mì mì}，{告诉|gào su}{他|tā}{妻子|qī zi}{也|yě}{不|bú}{是|shì}，{不|bú}{告诉|gào su}{也|yě}{不|bú}{是|shì}。 — I know his secret: I can't tell his wife, and I can't
not tell her.

{他|tā}{站|zhàn}{在|zài}{门口|mén kǒu}，{进|jìn}{也|yě}{不|bú}{是|shì}，{走|zǒu}{也|yě}{不|bú}{是|shì}。 — He stood at the door, not knowing whether to go in or leave.

The two halves are usually opposites ({说|shuō} / {不|bù}{说|shuō}, {进|jìn} / {走|zǒu}, {笑|xiào} / {哭|kū}), and the pattern often comes after a
description of someone's awkward position: {我|wǒ}{当时|dāng shí}{真|zhēn}{是|shì}…{也|yě}{不|bú}{是|shì}，…{也|yě}{不|bú}{是|shì}. This **[[dilemma pattern]]** is one of
the fixed formats of HSK 5.

## {反而|fǎn ér}: on the contrary

{反而|fǎn ér} introduces a result that goes against what you'd expect, or the opposite of what was
intended. It's an adverb, before the verb:

{我|wǒ}{想|xiǎng}{帮|bāng}{他|tā}，{他|tā}{反而|fǎn ér}{生气|shēng qì}{了|le}。 — I wanted to help him, but he got angry instead.

{吃|chī}{了|le}{药|yào}{以后|yǐ hòu}，{病|bìng}{反而|fǎn ér}{更|gèng}{重|zhòng}{了|le}。 — After taking the medicine, the illness actually got worse.

{雨|yǔ}{下|xià}{得|de}{越|yuè}{来|lái}{越|yuè}{大|dà}，{可是|kě shì}{来|lái}{的|de}{人|rén}{反而|fǎn ér}{更|gèng}{多|duō}{了|le}。 — The rain grew heavier, but more people came, not fewer.

With {不但|bú dàn}{不|bù} / {不但|bú dàn}{没|méi} in the first clause (lesson 11), the contrast is spelt out: {他|tā}{不但|bú dàn}{没|méi}{生气|shēng qì}，{反而|fǎn ér}{笑|xiào}{了|le}
(far from being angry, he laughed). {反而|fǎn ér} needs that expectation in the background; for a plain "but",
use {可是|kě shì} or {但是|dàn shì}. The full pattern {不但|bú dàn}{不|bù} / {没|méi}…{反而|fǎn ér}… is a **[[counter-expectation]]** sentence.

## {简直|jiǎn zhí}: simply, practically

{简直|jiǎn zhí} exaggerates: "it's practically…, it's just like…". It's emotional and very common in speech:

{这里|zhè lǐ}{的|de}{冬天|dōng tiān}{简直|jiǎn zhí}{太|tài}{冷|lěng}{了|le}！ — The winters here are just unbearably cold!

{他|tā}{做|zuò}{的|de}{菜|cài}{简直|jiǎn zhí}{跟|gēn}{饭馆|fàn guǎn}{的|de}{一样|yí yàng}{好吃|hǎo chī}。 — His cooking is practically as good as a restaurant's.

{我|wǒ}{简直|jiǎn zhí}{不|bù}{敢|gǎn}{相信|xiāng xìn}{自己|zì jǐ}{的|de}{耳朵|ěr duo}。 — I simply couldn't believe my ears.

Typical company: {简直|jiǎn zhí}{太|tài}…{了|le}, {简直|jiǎn zhí}{像|xiàng}…{一样|yí yàng}, {简直|jiǎn zhí}{不|bù}{敢|gǎn}{相信|xiāng xìn}, {简直|jiǎn zhí}{是|shì} + noun ({简直|jiǎn zhí}{是|shì}{浪费|làng fèi}{时间|shí jiān}, a complete waste
of time). Don't use it for plain facts: ~~{这|zhè}{本|běn}{书|shū}{简直|jiǎn zhí}{两百|liǎng bǎi}{页|yè}~~ makes no sense; {简直|jiǎn zhí} needs something to
exaggerate.

## {难以|nán yǐ}: hard to (written)

{难以|nán yǐ} + a two-syllable verb is the written way to say "hard to…, -able":

{难以|nán yǐ}{相信|xiāng xìn} (hard to believe), {难以|nán yǐ}{接受|jiē shòu} (hard to accept), {难以|nán yǐ}{忘记|wàng jì} (unforgettable), {难以|nán yǐ}{理解|lǐ jiě} (hard to
understand), {难以|nán yǐ}{想象|xiǎng xiàng} (hard to imagine, lesson 19's {想象|xiǎng xiàng}).

{那|nà}{件|jiàn}{事|shì}{令|lìng}{我|wǒ}{难以|nán yǐ}{忘记|wàng jì}。 — That incident is something I'll never forget.

In speech you'd say {很|hěn}{难|nán} + verb: {很|hěn}{难|nán}{相信|xiāng xìn}. {难以|nán yǐ} is followed by a verb of two syllables, not one: ~~{难以|nán yǐ}{吃|chī}~~
(say {很|hěn}{难|nán}{吃|chī} for "tastes awful").

## {令|lìng}: to make (someone feel)

{令|lìng} is the written causative, like {让|ràng} and {使|shǐ} (HSK 4): {令|lìng} + a person + a feeling or a reaction.

{他|tā}{的|de}{话|huà}{令|lìng}{人|rén}{失望|shī wàng}。 — What he said was disappointing.

{这个|zhè ge}{消息|xiāo xi}{令|lìng}{大家|dà jiā}{非常|fēi cháng}{吃惊|chī jīng}。 — The news astonished everyone.

Most often it's {令|lìng}{人|rén} + a two-syllable word: {令|lìng}{人|rén}{感动|gǎn dòng} (moving), {令|lìng}{人|rén}{难忘|nán wàng} (unforgettable), {令|lìng}{人|rén}{吃惊|chī jīng} (astonishing),
{令|lìng}{人|rén}{满意|mǎn yì} (satisfactory). In conversation, {让|ràng}{人|rén}: {让|ràng}{人|rén}{失望|shī wàng}.

## Quarrelling

| Word | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| {矛盾|máo dùn} | conflict, contradiction | {她们|tā men}{之间|zhī jiān}{有|yǒu}{了|le}{矛盾|máo dùn}。 Trouble had come between them. |
| {吵|chǎo} | noisy; to quarrel | {楼|lóu}{下|xià}{太|tài}{吵|chǎo}{了|le}。 It's too noisy downstairs. {她们|tā men}{吵|chǎo}{了|le}{一|yí}{架|jià}。 They had a row. |
| {争|zhēng} | to argue; to compete for | {两|liǎng}{个|gè}{人|rén}{争|zhēng}{了|le}{起来|qǐ lái}。 The two of them started arguing. |
| {闹|nào} | to make a scene, to fuss; noisy | {别|bié}{闹|nào}{了|le}！ Stop it! |
| {骂|mà} | to scold, to swear at | {他|tā}{被|bèi}{老板|lǎo bǎn}{骂|mà}{了|le}{一|yí}{顿|dùn}。 He got a telling-off from the boss. |
| {怪|guài} | to blame; strange | {这|zhè}{不|bù}{能|néng}{怪|guài}{你|nǐ}。 It's not your fault. |
| {抱怨|bào yuàn} | to complain | {他|tā}{总是|zǒng shì}{抱怨|bào yuàn}{工作|gōng zuò}{太|tài}{累|lèi}。 He's always complaining that work is too tiring. |
| {打断|dǎ duàn} | to interrupt | {别|bié}{打断|dǎ duàn}{我|wǒ}！ Don't interrupt me! |
| {过分|guò fèn} | going too far | {你|nǐ}{这样|zhè yàng}{说|shuō}{太|tài}{过分|guò fèn}{了|le}。 That's going too far. |

- {吵|chǎo} is an adjective (noisy) and a verb (to quarrel): {吵架|chǎo jià} (HSK 6) is the full word, and the
  measure is {一|yí}{架|jià} ({吵|chǎo}{了|le}{一|yí}{架|jià}) or {一|yí}{次|cì}.
- {怪|guài} as a verb is "to blame": {都|dōu}{怪|guài}{我|wǒ} (it's all my fault). As an adjective it's "strange" (HSK 3).
- {骂|mà} is to scold angrily, or to swear at someone; {骂|mà}{人|rén} is swearing.
- **{滚|gǔn}** is "to roll" (a ball rolls: {球|qiú}{滚|gǔn}{到|dào}{了|le}{床|chuáng}{下|xià}). Shouted at a person, {滚|gǔn}！ or {滚|gǔn}{出去|chū qù}！ means "get out!"
  and is very rude: it ends conversations and sometimes friendships. Know it; don't use it.

## Saying sorry, making up

| Word | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| {承认|chéng rèn} | to admit | {我|wǒ}{承认|chéng rèn}{是|shì}{我|wǒ}{错|cuò}{了|le}。 I admit I was wrong. |
| {否认|fǒu rèn} | to deny | {他|tā}{否认|fǒu rèn}{自己|zì jǐ}{说|shuō}{过|guo}{这|zhè}{句|jù}{话|huà}。 He denies having said it. |
| {劝|quàn} | to advise, to try to persuade | {朋友|péng you}{劝|quàn}{她|tā}{别|bié}{生气|shēng qì}{了|le}。 Her friend tried to talk her out of her anger. |
| {说服|shuō fú} | to persuade (successfully) | {我|wǒ}{终于|zhōng yú}{说服|shuō fú}{了|le}{他|tā}。 I finally talked him round. |
| {请求|qǐng qiú} | to ask, to request; a request | {我|wǒ}{有|yǒu}{一|yí}{个|gè}{请求|qǐng qiú}。 I have a request. |
| {安慰|ān wèi} | to comfort | {她|tā}{哭|kū}{了|le}，{我|wǒ}{不|bù}{知道|zhī dào}{怎么|zěn me}{安慰|ān wèi}{她|tā}。 She cried, and I didn't know how to comfort her. |
| {同情|tóng qíng} | sympathy; to sympathise | {大家|dà jiā}{都|dōu}{很|hěn}{同情|tóng qíng}{他|tā}。 Everyone felt sorry for him. |
| {忍|rěn} | to bear, to put up with | {我|wǒ}{忍|rěn}{了|le}{很|hěn}{久|jiǔ}，{最后|zuì hòu}{还是|hái shi}{说|shuō}{了|le}。 I held it in for ages, then said it in the end. |
| {在乎|zài hu} | to care about, to mind | {我|wǒ}{不|bú}{在乎|zài hu}{钱|qián}，{我|wǒ}{在乎|zài hu}{你|nǐ}。 I don't care about the money; I care about you. |

{劝|quàn} is trying; {说服|shuō fú} is succeeding: {我|wǒ}{劝|quàn}{了|le}{他|tā}{很|hěn}{久|jiǔ}，{可是|kě shì}{没|méi}{说服|shuō fú}{他|tā} (I tried for ages, but didn't persuade him).
{理解|lǐ jiě} (HSK 4) is to understand someone's position, the word that ends many arguments: {我|wǒ}{理解|lǐ jiě}{你|nǐ}.
{忍不住|rěn bu zhù} is "can't help (doing)": {她|tā}{忍不住|rěn bu zhù}{哭|kū}{了|le} (she couldn't help crying).

## Feelings

| Word | Meaning |
|---|---|
| {情绪|qíng xù} | mood, emotions ({情绪|qíng xù}{不|bù}{好|hǎo}, {控制|kòng zhì}{情绪|qíng xù} control your feelings) |
| {情感|qíng gǎn} | emotion, feeling (more written: {人|rén}{的|de}{情感|qíng gǎn}) |
| {心理|xīn lǐ} | psychology; state of mind ({心理|xīn lǐ}{压力|yā lì} mental pressure) |
| {痛苦|tòng kǔ} | pain, suffering; painful (very strong) |
| {伤害|shāng hài} | to hurt, to harm; harm ({伤害|shāng hài}{了|le}{她|tā}{的|de}{感情|gǎn qíng} hurt her feelings) |
| {遗憾|yí hàn} | regret; a pity ({很|hěn}{遗憾|yí hàn} what a pity; {太|tài}{遗憾|yí hàn}{了|le}) |
| {无奈|wú nài} | helpless; it can't be helped ({无奈|wú nài}{地|de}{笑|xiào}{了|le}{笑|xiào}) |
| {不幸|bú xìng} | unfortunate; misfortune ({不幸|bú xìng}{的|de}{是|shì}… unfortunately…) |
| {敏感|mǐn gǎn} | sensitive ({他|tā}{很|hěn}{敏感|mǐn gǎn} he's easily hurt) |
| {坚强|jiān qiáng} | strong, resilient |
| {胆小|dǎn xiǎo} | timid, cowardly |
| {傻|shǎ} | foolish, silly ({别|bié}{傻|shǎ}{了|le} don't be silly) |
| {强烈|qiáng liè} | strong, intense ({强烈|qiáng liè}{的|de}{感情|gǎn qíng}, {强烈|qiáng liè}{反对|fǎn duì}) |

{情绪|qíng xù}, {情感|qíng gǎn}, {情景|qíng jǐng} (a scene, a situation: {当时|dāng shí}{的|de}{情景|qíng jǐng}) and {表情|biǎo qíng} (a facial expression) share {情|qíng} (feeling).
{心理|xīn lǐ} is mind and psychology; HSK 3's {心里|xīn li} (in one's heart) sounds almost the same: {理|lǐ} keeps its full third
tone in {心理|xīn lǐ} xīn lǐ, while {里|li} is light in {心里|xīn li} xīn li. Don't confuse them.

## Faces and silences

- {表情|biǎo qíng} (an expression): {她|tā}{的|de}{表情|biǎo qíng}{很|hěn}{严肃|yán sù} (her expression was serious).
- {目光|mù guāng} (gaze, look): {大家|dà jiā}{的|de}{目光|mù guāng}{都|dōu}{看|kàn}{向|xiàng}{他|tā} (everyone's eyes turned to him).
- {低头|dī tóu} (to lower one's head), and its opposite {抬头|tái tóu} (HSK 4).
- {沉默|chén mò} (silent; silence): {她|tā}{沉默|chén mò}{了|le}{很|hěn}{久|jiǔ} (she was silent for a long time).
- {平静|píng jìng} (calm): {她|tā}{的|de}{声音|shēng yīn}{很|hěn}{平静|píng jìng} (her voice was calm).
- {严肃|yán sù} (serious, stern).
- {悄悄|qiāo qiāo} (quietly, without being noticed): {她|tā}{悄悄|qiāo qiāo}{地|de}{走|zǒu}{了|le} (she slipped away).
- {背后|bèi hòu} (behind; behind someone's back): {在|zài}{背后|bèi hòu}{说|shuō}{别人|bié ren} (talk about people behind their backs).
- {泪|lèi}, {泪水|lèi shuǐ}, {眼泪|yǎn lèi} (tears): {眼泪|yǎn lèi} in speech, {泪水|lèi shuǐ} in writing, {泪|lèi} alone mostly in set phrases ({流|liú}{泪|lèi}, to shed tears).
- {反应|fǎn yìng} (reaction; to react): {他|tā}{的|de}{反应|fǎn yìng}{很|hěn}{快|kuài}.
- {意识|yì shí} (awareness; to realise): {意识|yì shí}{到|dào} (to realise): {我|wǒ}{这|zhè}{才|cái}{意识|yì shí}{到|dào}{自己|zì jǐ}{错|cuò}{了|le}.
- {彻底|chè dǐ} (thorough, completely): {彻底|chè dǐ}{解决|jiě jué} (solve once and for all).
- {轻易|qīng yì} (lightly, easily): {不要|bú yào}{轻易|qīng yì}{放弃|fàng qì} (don't give up easily).

## Sighs and exclamations

| Word | Pinyin | Use |
|---|---|---|
| {哎|āi} | āi | to call someone's attention, or mild surprise: {哎|āi}，{你|nǐ}{等|děng}{一下|yí xià}！ Hey, wait a moment! |
| {哎呀|āi yā} | āi yā | dismay, or surprise: {哎呀|āi yā}，{我|wǒ}{忘|wàng}{带|dài}{钥匙|yào shi}{了|le}！ Oh no, I've forgotten my keys! |
| {唉|ài} | ài | a sigh: {唉|ài}，{怎么|zěn me}{又|yòu}{下雨|xià yǔ}{了|le}。 Sigh, it's raining again. |
| {呀|yā} | yā | surprise: {呀|yā}，{下|xià}{雪|xuě}{了|le}！ Oh, it's snowing! (Also a particle, ya, after a word ending in a, i, o.) |

The tone matters: {哎|āi} āi calls, {唉|ài} ài sighs.

### Sound families

- **{令|lìng}** lìng is a sound part you've met many times: {冷|lěng} lěng (cold), {领|lǐng} lǐng (lesson 02), {铃|líng} líng
  (lesson 17's bell), {零|líng} líng (zero) and {邻|lín} lín ({邻居|lín jū}). Now you write {令|lìng} itself: five strokes, {人|rén} on
  top, then the dot and a 7-like stroke (横撇) with a last dot below.
- **{口|kǒu} + a sound part** makes interjections: {哎|āi} āi ({口|kǒu} + {艾|ài}), {呀|yā} yā ({口|kǒu} + {牙|yá} yá), {唉|ài} ài ({口|kǒu} + {矣|yǐ}),
  and lesson 11's {哈|hā} hā ({口|kǒu} + {合|hé}). {吵|chǎo} chǎo is {口|kǒu} + {少|shǎo} shǎo: noise comes out of mouths.
- **{马|mǎ}** mǎ gives {骂|mà} mà its sound; on top are two mouths (吅). Traditional 罵 has 罒 (a net) over 馬.
- **{刃|rèn}** (a blade: {刀|dāo} with a dot) gives {忍|rěn} rěn its sound. A memory aid: a blade over the heart, and
  you bear it.
- **{者|zhě}** zhě is the right side of {绪|xù} xù (the sound has drifted, as in {都|dōu} dōu), with 纟 (silk: the end
  of a thread, which is what {绪|xù} first meant; {情绪|qíng xù} is the "threads" of feeling).

### Families of meaning

- **氵 (water)**: {泪|lèi} (氵 + {目|mù}, water from the eye), {沉|chén} (to sink), {滚|gǔn} (to roll, of water boiling: {开水|kāi shuǐ}{滚|gǔn}{了|le}).
  Traditional 淚 has 戾 on the right.
- **{心|xīn} / 忄 (heart)** in feeling words: {慰|wèi} (尉 over {心|xīn}), {怨|yuàn} (夗 over {心|xīn}), {忍|rěn}, {悄|qiāo} (忄 + {肖|xiào} xiào), and lesson 15's {憾|hàn}.
- **{矛|máo} and {盾|dùn}**: a spear and a shield. {矛盾|máo dùn} comes from a story in the 《{韩非子|Hán Fēi zǐ}》 (Hán Fēizǐ, 3rd
  century BCE): a man selling spears and shields boasted that his spears could pierce anything and his
  shields could stop anything. "What if I use your spear on your shield?" asked a bystander. The
  man had no answer.
- **{又|yòu} as a stand-in**: simplified {劝|quàn} is {又|yòu} + {力|lì}; traditional 勸 has 雚 on the left. {又|yòu} replaces
  complicated parts in many simplified characters ({对|duì}, {欢|huān}, {难|nán}, {汉|hàn}, {鸡|jī}).

### Stroke order

- **{劝|quàn}**: {又|yòu} (two strokes), then {力|lì} (the horizontal-turn-hook, then the left-falling stroke).
- **{令|lìng}**: {人|rén} (left-falling, right-falling), the dot, the 横撇 (a horizontal turning down to the left),
  the last dot.
- **{骂|mà}**: the two {口|kǒu} on top (left one first), then {马|mǎ} (the horizontal-turn, the vertical-turn-turn-hook,
  the horizontal last).
- **{泪|lèi}**: 氵 (dot, dot, rising stroke), then {目|mù} (vertical, horizontal-turn, three horizontals).
- **{忍|rěn}**: {刃|rèn} (the horizontal-turn-hook, the left-falling stroke, the dot), then {心|xīn}.
- **{沉|chén}**: 氵, then the cover (dot, 横撇), the left-falling stroke and the long curving hook.
- **{吵|chǎo}**: {口|kǒu}, then {少|shǎo} (the vertical, the left dot, the right dot, the long left-falling stroke).
- **{遗|yí}**: {贵|guì} first ({中|zhōng} and the horizontal, then {贝|bèi}), and 辶 last.

1. A row between Anna and Wang Fang, the awkward day after it, and how they made up.

"Thursday. The atmosphere between Wang Fang and me these past two days has been simply
unbearable. On Tuesday night we had a row, the first since we started living together. To
tell the truth, I regretted it as soon as it was over. I'm not a sensitive person, but that night I
lay in bed going over what she'd said, 'That's going too far'. She thinks all I care about is whether the
flat is clean, and that I don't care at all how tired she is. I just couldn't sleep. The next
morning we ran into each other in the kitchen and neither of us said a word. She kept her head
down over her coffee, and I pretended to look at my phone. Several times I wanted to say
something, but one look at her stern face and I lost my nerve. All morning the flat was so quiet it
was painful. This 'cold war' was worse than the row. I messaged my sister, and she advised me:
'Don't wait for her to apologise first. Between friends, it doesn't matter who speaks first.' But
before I'd worked out how to start, Wang Fang came home that evening carrying two bowls of
noodles. The moment she came in she said: 'Yesterday was my fault.' For a moment I couldn't say a word,
and I nearly cried. It turned out she'd been miserable all day too. We talked over the noodles for a
long time, and as we talked, we both started laughing. Only then did I realise how much pressure she's been under at work, while all I'd seen
was the dirty bowls; and she admitted she'd been so busy she'd neglected our home. We agreed that
from now on, if anything bothers us, we'll say it calmly, not keep it bottled up, and not lose our
tempers easily. I think real friends aren't people who never quarrel, but people who, after a
quarrel, still want to understand each other."

The last part of the HSK 5 speaking test asks for your opinion on a question, with reasons (as
reported: a few minutes to prepare, then about two and a half minutes). Try this one aloud: {你|nǐ}{觉得|jué de}
{朋友|péng you}{之间|zhī jiān}{吵架|chǎo jià}{是|shì}{好|hǎo}{事|shì}{还是|hái shi}{坏|huài}{事|shì}？{为什么|wèi shén me}？ (Do you think it's a good or a bad thing for friends to argue? Why?)

<details>
<summary>A model answer</summary>

> {我|wǒ}{觉得|jué de}，{朋友|péng you}{之间|zhī jiān}{吵架|chǎo jià}{不|bù}{一定|yí dìng}{是|shì}{坏|huài}{事|shì}。{首先|shǒu xiān}，{吵架|chǎo jià}{说明|shuō míng}{两|liǎng}{个|gè}{人|rén}{都|dōu}{很|hěn}{在乎|zài hu}{这|zhè}{段|duàn}{关系|guān xi}。{如果|rú guǒ}{一点儿|yì diǎnr}{也|yě}{不|bú}{在乎|zài hu}，{就|jiù}{根本|gēn běn}{不|bú}{会|huì}{生气|shēng qì}。{其次|qí cì}，{很|hěn}{多|duō}{矛盾|máo dùn}{如果|rú guǒ}{一直|yì zhí}{忍|rěn}{着|zhe}，{不|bù}{说|shuō}{出来|chū lái}，{反而|fǎn ér}{会|huì}{越|yuè}{来|lái}{越|yuè}{大|dà}。{吵|chǎo}{一|yí}{次|cì}{架|jià}，{把|bǎ}{心里|xīn li}{的|de}{话|huà}{都|dōu}{说|shuō}{出来|chū lái}，{有|yǒu}{时候|shí hou}{能|néng}{让|ràng}{彼此|bǐ cǐ}{更|gèng}{了解|liǎo jiě}{对方|duì fāng}。{当然|dāng rán}，{吵架|chǎo jià}{的|de}{时候|shí hou}{也|yě}{要|yào}{注意|zhù yì}，{不|bù}{能|néng}{说|shuō}{太|tài}{过分|guò fèn}{的|de}{话|huà}，{更|gèng}{不|bù}{能|néng}{伤害|shāng hài}{对方|duì fāng}。{总之|zǒng zhī}，{我|wǒ}{认为|rèn wéi}，{吵架|chǎo jià}{本身|běn shēn}{没|méi}{什么|shén me}{可怕|kě pà}{的|de}，{重要|zhòng yào}{的|de}{是|shì}{吵|chǎo}{完|wán}{以后|yǐ hòu}，{双方|shuāng fāng}{都|dōu}{愿意|yuàn yì}{承认|chéng rèn}{自己|zì jǐ}{的|de}{错|cuò}，{互相|hù xiāng}{理解|lǐ jiě}。

{首先|shǒu xiān}…{其次|qí cì}…{总之|zǒng zhī} (first… second… in short) are the linking words of an opinion ({总之|zǒng zhī} is lesson 16's);
{段|duàn} is the measure for a relationship ({这|zhè}{段|duàn}{关系|guān xi}); {本身|běn shēn} běn shēn is "itself"; {可怕|kě pà} (frightening) is lesson
23's. Give your view in the first sentence, two reasons, and a conclusion.
</details>

```speak
# Arguments and apologies
{对不起|duì bu qǐ}，{昨天|zuó tiān}{是|shì}{我|wǒ}{不|bù}{好|hǎo}。
= Sorry, yesterday was my fault.
{我|wǒ}{承认|chéng rèn}{是|shì}{我|wǒ}{错|cuò}{了|le}。
= I admit I was wrong.
{你|nǐ}{这样|zhè yàng}{说|shuō}{太|tài}{过分|guò fèn}{了|le}。
= That's going too far.
{我|wǒ}{想|xiǎng}{帮|bāng}{他|tā}，{他|tā}{反而|fǎn ér}{生气|shēng qì}{了|le}。
= I wanted to help him, but he got angry instead.
{我|wǒ}{当时|dāng shí}{说|shuō}{也|yě}{不|bú}{是|shì}，{不|bù}{说|shuō}{也|yě}{不|bú}{是|shì}。
= I didn't know whether to say anything or not.
{这|zhè}{件|jiàn}{事|shì}{真|zhēn}{令|lìng}{人|rén}{难以|nán yǐ}{相信|xiāng xìn}。
= This is really hard to believe.
```

## Write it: a story in four pictures

Write 100–150 characters about these four pictures, using at least four of {吵|chǎo}, {沉默|chén mò}, {反而|fǎn ér}, {简直|jiǎn zhí},
{承认|chéng rèn}, {安慰|ān wèi}, {眼泪|yǎn lèi}.

1. Two boys argue over a football in a park; one pushes the other.
2. The ball rolls into the road; both stop, silent.
3. An old man picks up the ball and talks to them.
4. The two boys shake hands, then play together again.

<details>
<summary>Model answer</summary>

> {周末|zhōu mò}，{小刚|Xiǎo Gāng}{和|hé}{小亮|Xiǎo Liàng}{在|zài}{公园|gōng yuán}{里|lǐ}{踢|tī}{足球|zú qiú}。{踢着踢着|tī zhe tī zhe}，{两|liǎng}{个|gè}{人|rén}{为了|wèi le}{一|yí}{个|gè}{球|qiú}{吵|chǎo}{了|le}{起来|qǐ lái}，{小刚|Xiǎo Gāng}{还|hái}{推|tuī}{了|le}{小亮|Xiǎo Liàng}{一下|yí xià}。{这|zhè}{时候|shí hou}，{球|qiú}{滚|gǔn}{到|dào}{了|le}{马路|mǎ lù}{上|shàng}，{两|liǎng}{个|gè}{人|rén}{都|dōu}{不|bù}{说话|shuō huà}{了|le}。{一|yí}{位|wèi}{老|lǎo}{大爷|dà ye}{帮|bāng}{他们|tā men}{把|bǎ}{球|qiú}{捡|jiǎn}{了|le}{回来|huí lái}，{笑|xiào}{着|zhe}{说|shuō}："{你们|nǐ men}{是|shì}{好|hǎo}{朋友|péng you}，{为了|wèi le}{一|yí}{个|gè}{球|qiú}{吵架|chǎo jià}，{值得|zhí de}{吗|ma}？"{小刚|Xiǎo Gāng}{低|dī}{下|xià}{了|le}{头|tóu}，{承认|chéng rèn}{是|shì}{自己|zì jǐ}{不|bú}{对|duì}。{小亮|Xiǎo Liàng}{不但|bú dàn}{没有|méi yǒu}{生气|shēng qì}，{反而|fǎn ér}{笑|xiào}{了|le}。{两|liǎng}{个|gè}{人|rén}{握|wò}{了|le}{握手|wò shǒu}，{又|yòu}{高|gāo}{高兴|gāo xìng}{兴|xìng}{地|de}{踢|tī}{起|qǐ}{球|qiú}{来|lái}。

(132 characters.) {小亮|Xiǎo Liàng} Xiǎo Liàng is a name; {踢着踢着|tī zhe tī zhe} is "in the middle of playing" (A{着|zhe}A{着|zhe}, lesson
13's pattern); {推|tuī} (to push, HSK 4); {值得|zhí de} (worth it, HSK 4); {握手|wò shǒu} (to shake hands) is lesson 15's.
</details>

## Pronunciation

- {哎|āi} āi (first tone, calling) and {唉|ài} ài (fourth tone, sighing) are the same syllable with different
  tones and different jobs.
- {吵|chǎo} chǎo and {炒|chǎo} chǎo (to stir-fry, lesson 07) sound the same: {口|kǒu} for noise, {火|huǒ} for cooking.
- {心理|xīn lǐ} xīn lǐ (psychology) and {心里|xīn li} xīn li (in one's heart): the second syllable is full in {心理|xīn lǐ} and
  light in {心里|xīn li}.
- {傻|shǎ} shǎ: *sh* and a dipping tone; {杀|shā} (to kill, HSK 6) is first tone.
- {骂|mà} mà: the same syllable as {吗|ma}, {妈|mā} and {马|mǎ}, with a falling tone.
- {劝|quàn} quàn: *q* + *üan* (written uan after q): quàn, not kuàn.

## Common mistakes

- {反而|fǎn ér} isn't a plain "but": {我|wǒ}{很|hěn}{累|lèi}，{但是|dàn shì}{还|hái}{要|yào}{工作|gōng zuò}, not ~~{我|wǒ}{很|hěn}{累|lèi}，{反而|fǎn ér}{还|hái}{要|yào}{工作|gōng zuò}~~. {反而|fǎn ér} needs a result against expectation.
- ~~{难以|nán yǐ}{吃|chī}~~: {难以|nán yǐ} takes a two-syllable verb ({难以|nán yǐ}{接受|jiē shòu}); for food, say {很|hěn}{难|nán}{吃|chī}.
- {令|lìng} is written: in conversation, {让|ràng}{人|rén}{失望|shī wàng} sounds more natural than {令|lìng}{人|rén}{失望|shī wàng}.
- {劝|quàn} isn't {说服|shuō fú}: {我|wǒ}{劝|quàn}{了|le}{他|tā}，{可是|kě shì}{他|tā}{不|bù}{听|tīng} (I tried to persuade him, but he wouldn't listen) is fine; ~~{我|wǒ}{说服|shuō fú}{了|le}{他|tā}，{可是|kě shì}{他|tā}{不|bù}{听|tīng}~~ contradicts itself.
- {在乎|zài hu} is mostly used with a negative or in questions: {我|wǒ}{不|bú}{在乎|zài hu}, {你|nǐ}{在乎|zài hu}{吗|ma}？ To say "I care about you" warmly, {我|wǒ}{在乎|zài hu}{你|nǐ} is fine.
- {滚|gǔn} to a person is an insult, not "go away" in a neutral sense: say {你|nǐ}{走|zǒu}{吧|ba} or {请|qǐng}{你|nǐ}{出去|chū qù}.

## Key points

- X {也|yě}{不|bú}{是|shì}，Y {也|yě}{不|bú}{是|shì}: caught between two bad choices.
- {反而|fǎn ér}: the result goes against expectation; {不但|bú dàn}{不|bù} / {没|méi}…{反而|fǎn ér}….
- {简直|jiǎn zhí}: practically, simply (exaggeration): {简直|jiǎn zhí}{太|tài}…{了|le}, {简直|jiǎn zhí}{像|xiàng}…{一样|yí yàng}, {简直|jiǎn zhí}{不|bù}{敢|gǎn}{相信|xiāng xìn}.
- {难以|nán yǐ} + two-syllable verb (written): {难以|nán yǐ}{相信|xiāng xìn}, {难以|nán yǐ}{忘记|wàng jì}.
- {令|lìng}{人|rén} + feeling (written): {令|lìng}{人|rén}{失望|shī wàng}, {令|lìng}{人|rén}{感动|gǎn dòng}; spoken {让|ràng}{人|rén}.
- Quarrels: {矛盾|máo dùn}, {吵|chǎo}, {争|zhēng}, {骂|mà}, {怪|guài}, {抱怨|bào yuàn}, {打断|dǎ duàn}, {过分|guò fèn}; making up: {承认|chéng rèn}, {劝|quàn}, {说服|shuō fú}, {安慰|ān wèi}, {理解|lǐ jiě}, {忍|rěn}, {在乎|zài hu}.
- {哎|āi} āi (hey), {哎呀|āi yā} (oh no), {唉|ài} ài (sigh), {呀|yā} yā (oh!).
- New characters: {慰|wèi} {怨|yuàn} {沉|chén} {吵|chǎo} {彻|chè} {哎|āi} {呀|yā} {唉|ài} {滚|gǔn} {泪|lèi} {矛|máo} {盾|dùn} {令|lìng} {骂|mà} {绪|xù} {劝|quàn} {忍|rěn} {傻|shǎ} {悄|qiāo} {遗|yí}.

The words from this lesson are listed below; they join your vocabulary reviews when you complete
the lesson.

lessons.title: Gifts, visits and good manners
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

At the Spring Festival, Anna is invited to the home of her professor, {罗教授|Luó jiào shòu} Professor Luo. She
takes presents, meets a guest who gives her a business card, eats, toasts and takes photos, and
afterwards writes a thank-you letter and posts it. This lesson is about being a good guest and a
good host in Chinese: greetings and compliments, gifts and what not to give, cards, handshakes and
letters, and the post office.

The grammar:

- {替|tì}: for, in place of, on behalf of ({替|tì}{我|wǒ}{问|wèn}{好|hǎo});
- {亲自|qīn zì}: in person, oneself;
- {朝|cháo} and {向|xiàng}: two ways to say "towards" ({朝|cháo} is lesson 22's word: a preview);
- the measure words {朵|duǒ}, {束|shù} and {副|fù} ({一|yì}{朵|duǒ}{花|huā}, {一|yí}{束|shù}{花|huā}, {一|yí}{副|fù}{眼镜|yǎn jìng});
- two verbs for fastening: {别|bié} bié (to pin) and {={系|jì}=} jì (to tie);
- the idiom {亲朋好友|qīn péng hǎo yǒu} (friends and relatives).

## {替|tì}: for, in place of

{替|tì} + a person + a verb says that you do something for someone: in their place, or on their
behalf.

{你|nǐ}{在|zài}{家|jiā}{休息|xiū xi}{吧|ba}，{我|wǒ}{替|tì}{你|nǐ}{去|qù}{开会|kāi huì}。 — You stay at home and rest: I'll go to the meeting for you.

{请|qǐng}{替|tì}{我|wǒ}{向|xiàng}{你|nǐ}{父母|fù mǔ}{问|wèn}{好|hǎo}。 — Please give your parents my regards.

{听说|tīng shuō}{你|nǐ}{考|kǎo}{上|shàng}{了|le}{研究生|yán jiū shēng}，{我|wǒ}{真|zhēn}{替|tì}{你|nǐ}{高兴|gāo xìng}！ — I hear you got into a master's course: I'm so happy for you!

Compare the other "for" words:

- {给|gěi} marks who receives the action: {给|gěi}{他|tā}{打电话|dǎ diàn huà} (phone him), {给|gěi}{妈妈|mā ma}{买|mǎi}{礼物|lǐ wù} (buy Mum a present).
- {替|tì} is "instead of, on behalf of": {替|tì}{他|tā}{打电话|dǎ diàn huà} (make the call for him, so he needn't).
- {为|wèi} (HSK 3) is "for the sake of", a little more written: {为|wèi}{你|nǐ}{高兴|gāo xìng} = {替|tì}{你|nǐ}{高兴|gāo xìng}.
- {代|dài} (lesson 13) is the most formal: {代|dài}{我|wǒ}{问|wèn}{好|hǎo}.

{替|tì}{我|wǒ}{问|wèn}{好|hǎo} = {代|dài}{我|wǒ}{问|wèn}{好|hǎo}, and {替|tì}{你|nǐ}{高兴|gāo xìng} = {为|wèi}{你|nǐ}{高兴|gāo xìng}; in {替|tì}{你|nǐ}{去|qù}{开会|kāi huì} (go instead of you), only {替|tì} or {代|dài} fits.

## {亲自|qīn zì}: in person

{亲自|qīn zì} stresses that someone did a thing personally rather than leaving it to others, usually
someone you wouldn't expect to:

{罗教授|Luó jiào shòu}{亲自|qīn zì}{做|zuò}{了|le}{一|yì}{桌子|zhuō zi}{菜|cài}。 — Professor Luo cooked a whole table of dishes himself.

{这|zhè}{件|jiàn}{事|shì}{很|hěn}{重要|zhòng yào}，{经理|jīng lǐ}{要|yào}{亲自|qīn zì}{去|qù}{一|yí}{趟|tàng}。 — This matters: the manager is going to go in person.

It sounds odd with things everyone does for themselves: ~~{我|wǒ}{亲自|qīn zì}{吃|chī}{饭|fàn}~~. {自己|zì jǐ} is the plain "oneself":
{我|wǒ}{自己|zì jǐ}{做饭|zuò fàn} (I cook for myself).

## {朝|cháo} and {向|xiàng}: towards

Both mark a direction and can take a person: {朝|cháo}{他|tā}{笑|xiào}{了|le}{笑|xiào} = {向|xiàng}{他|tā}{笑|xiào}{了|le}{笑|xiào} (she smiled at him), {朝|cháo}{前|qián}{走|zǒu} = {向|xiàng}{前|qián}{走|zǒu}
(walk on). The differences:

- {朝|cháo} is physical: facing, turning, moving towards something you can see. It is also "to face":
  {这|zhè}{间|jiān}{房子|fáng zi}{朝|cháo}{南|nán} (this flat faces south), a use that lesson 22 teaches.
- {向|xiàng} can also take abstract things, where {朝|cháo} can't: {向|xiàng}{他|tā}{学习|xué xí} (learn from him), {向|xiàng}{你|nǐ}{道歉|dào qiàn} (apologise
  to you), {向|xiàng}{你|nǐ}{父母|fù mǔ}{问|wèn}{好|hǎo} (give my regards to your parents). Not ×{朝|cháo}{他|tā}{学习|xué xí}.
- {向|xiàng} is the usual word in writing; {朝|cháo} is common in speech and stories.

## Counting flowers and pairs: {朵|duǒ}, {束|shù}, {副|fù}

| Measure word | For | Example |
|---|---|---|
| {朵|duǒ} | single flowers, clouds | {一|yì}{朵|duǒ}{花|huā}, {一|yì}{朵|duǒ}{白|bái}{云|yún} (a white cloud) |
| {束|shù} | bunches (flowers), beams (light) | {一|yí}{束|shù}{花|huā}, {一|yí}{束|shù}{玫瑰|méi guī} (a bunch of roses) |
| {副|fù} | pairs and sets; a face, a look | {一|yí}{副|fù}{眼镜|yǎn jìng} (a pair of glasses), {一|yí}{副|fù}{手套|shǒu tào} (a pair of gloves), {一|yí}{副|fù}{笑|xiào}{脸|liǎn} (a smiling face) |

{副|fù} is for things that come as a set and are used together: glasses, gloves, a pack of playing
cards. Shoes and socks, which you count in pairs too, take {双|shuāng} (HSK 3): {一|yì}{双|shuāng}{鞋|xié}.

## {别|bié} and {={系|jì}=}: pinning and tying

- {别|bié} bié, as a verb, is "to pin, to fasten with a pin": {新娘|xīn niáng}{的|de}{衣服|yī fu}{上|shàng}{别|bié}{着|zhe}{一|yì}{朵|duǒ}{花|huā} (the bride had a flower pinned
  to her dress). It's the same character as HSK 2's {别|bié} (don't): context tells them apart.
- {={系|jì}=} jì is "to tie, to fasten (with a knot)": {系|jì}{领带|lǐng dài} (to do up a tie), {系鞋带|jì xié dài} (to tie a shoelace), {在|zài}{礼物|lǐ wù}
  {上|shàng}{系|jì}{一|yì}{条|tiáo}{红|hóng}{带|dài}{子|zi} (tie a red ribbon round the present). It's jì, not the xì of {关系|guān xi} or of lesson 17's {={系|xì}=}
  (a university department). In traditional characters "to tie" has its own form, {+{系|jì}{领带|lǐng dài}+}.

## Being a good guest

| Word | Meaning | Use |
|---|---|---|
| {主人|zhǔ rén} | host; owner | {主人|zhǔ rén}{很|hěn}{热情|rè qíng}。 The hosts were very welcoming. |
| {光临|guāng lín} | to honour with one's presence | {欢迎|huān yíng}{光临|guāng lín}！ Welcome! (shops, invitations) |
| {贵姓|guì xìng} | your (honourable) surname | {您|nín}{贵姓|guì xìng}？ May I ask your name? |
| {恭喜|gōng xǐ} | congratulations | {恭喜|gōng xǐ}{恭喜|gōng xǐ}！ / {恭喜|gōng xǐ}{你|nǐ}！ Congratulations! |
| {称赞|chēng zàn} | to praise | {大家|dà jiā}{都|dōu}{称赞|chēng zàn}{她|tā}{的|de}{汉语|Hàn yǔ}。 Everyone praised her Chinese. |
| {亲切|qīn qiè} | cordial, warm (of manner) | {老师|lǎo shī}{说话|shuō huà}{很|hěn}{亲切|qīn qiè}。 The teacher has a warm way of speaking. |
| {热烈|rè liè} | warm, enthusiastic | {热烈|rè liè}{欢迎|huān yíng}！ A very warm welcome! |
| {温暖|wēn nuǎn} | warm | {温暖|wēn nuǎn}{的|de}{家|jiā} a warm home |
| {讲究|jiǎng jiu} | to be particular about; etiquette | {送|sòng}{礼|lǐ}{有|yǒu}{很|hěn}{多|duō}{讲究|jiǎng jiu}。 There's a lot of etiquette to giving gifts. |
| {改天|gǎi tiān} | some other day | {改天|gǎi tiān}{再|zài}{来|lái}{玩儿|wánr}！ Come again some time! |

- **{贵姓|guì xìng}**: {您|nín}{贵姓|guì xìng}？ is the polite way to ask someone's surname. Answer with the surname alone: {我|wǒ}{姓|xìng}{王|Wáng},
  or, very modestly, {免贵|miǎn guì}{姓|xìng}{王|Wáng} (miǎn guì: "no 'honourable' needed"). Never say ~~{我|wǒ}{贵姓|guì xìng}{王|Wáng}~~: {贵|guì} is
  only for the other person.
- **{光临|guāng lín}** is formal: {欢迎|huān yíng}{光临|guāng lín} is what shop staff say as you come in, and {敬请光临|jìng qǐng guāng lín} (we request the
  pleasure of your company) ends invitations.
- **{恭喜|gōng xǐ}** is for good news (a wedding, a new job, a baby) and the New Year: {恭喜发财|gōng xǐ fā cái} (wishing you
  prosperity: {发财|fā cái}, to get rich) is the classic New Year greeting.
- **{亲切|qīn qiè}** is how a person seems to you: kind, warm, easy to talk to. **{热烈|rè liè}** is warmth with energy:
  {热烈|rè liè}{的|de}{掌声|zhǎng shēng} (warm applause). **{温暖|wēn nuǎn}** is warmth you feel: the weather, a home, a kind word.

## Gifts

{送|sòng}{礼|lǐ} (giving presents) is full of {讲究|jiǎng jiu}. A few that most people know:

- Bring something when you visit a home: fruit, {点心|diǎn xin} (pastries, snacks) or a {特产|tè chǎn} (a local
  speciality) from your home town or country.
- Don't give a clock: {送钟|sòng zhōng} sòng zhōng sounds like {送终|sòng zhōng} sòng zhōng, to attend a dying parent. Many
  people avoid giving pears to share, because {分梨|fēn lí} fēn lí sounds like {分离|fēn lí} (to part, lesson 13).
- Give and receive with both hands. Your host may refuse a present once or twice to be polite;
  insist gently.
- Presents aren't always opened in front of the giver.

{赠送|zèng sòng} and {赠|zèng} are the written words for giving as a present ({本|běn}{店|diàn}{赠送|zèng sòng}{一|yí}{个|gè}{气球|qì qiú}: "a free balloon with every
purchase"); in speech, {送|sòng}. {交换|jiāo huàn} is to exchange: {交换|jiāo huàn}{礼物|lǐ wù}, {交换|jiāo huàn}{名片|míng piàn}. {递|dì} is to hand something to someone:
{把|bǎ}{名片|míng piàn}{递|dì}{给|gěi}{他|tā}; {传递|chuán dì} is to pass along (from one to the next): {传递|chuán dì}{消息|xiāo xi} (pass on news).

## Cards, handshakes and photos

- **{名片|míng piàn}** (a business card): offer and take it with both hands, read it, and don't put it straight in
  your {口袋|kǒu dài} (pocket).
- **{握手|wò shǒu}** (to shake hands): {握|wò} is "to grip, to hold": {握|wò}{着|zhe}{她|tā}{的|de}{手|shǒu} (holding her hand).
- **{摇|yáo}** is "to shake, to wave": {摇|yáo}{头|tóu} (to shake one's head: no), {摇|yáo}{手|shǒu} (to wave one's hand: no, or goodbye).
- **{微笑|wēi xiào}** (a smile; to smile): {她|tā}{微笑|wēi xiào}{着|zhe}{点|diǎn}{了|le}{点头|diǎn tóu} (she smiled and nodded).
- **{合影|hé yǐng}** (a group photo; to have a photo taken together) and **{相册|xiàng cè}** (a photo album).
- **{签名|qiān míng}** (to sign one's name; a signature): {请|qǐng}{您|nín}{签|qiān}{个|gè}{名|míng} (please sign here; may I have your autograph?).
- **{气球|qì qiú}** (a balloon) and **{醉|zuì}** (drunk): {他|tā}{喝|hē}{醉|zuì}{了|le} (he's drunk).
- **{安|ān}** is "peaceful, calm", in {平安|píng ān}, {晚安|wǎn ān}, {不|bù}{安|ān} (uneasy), and in wishes: {一路|yí lù}{平安|píng ān}.
- **{愿|yuàn}** is "to wish, to hope", in letters and toasts: {愿|yuàn}{你|nǐ}{一切|yí qiè}{顺利|shùn lì} (wishing you every success).

## The idiom {亲朋好友|qīn péng hǎo yǒu}

{亲朋好友|qīn péng hǎo yǒu} qīn péng hǎo yǒu is "friends and relatives". Its four characters are two pairs: {亲|qīn} (relatives)
and {朋|péng} (friends), then {好友|hǎo yǒu} (good friends). Unlike many four-character idioms, which describe or comment,
it is a noun phrase, used as the subject or the object:

{婚礼|hūn lǐ}{那|nà}{天|tiān}，{亲朋好友|qīn péng hǎo yǒu}{都|dōu}{来|lái}{了|le}。 — On the wedding day, all our friends and relatives came.

{过年|guò nián}{的|de}{时候|shí hou}，{我们|wǒ men}{会|huì}{去|qù}{看望|kàn wàng}{亲朋好友|qīn péng hǎo yǒu}。 — At New Year we visit friends and relatives.

It's a little formal: at home people say {亲戚|qīn qi}{朋友|péng you} (HSK 4's {亲戚|qīn qi}, relatives). You'll find it in speeches,
invitations and written stories.

New words: {受到|shòu dào} (to receive), {拉|lā} (to pull, to take by the hand), {一|yí}{道|dào}{菜|cài} (a dish: {道|dào}, HSK 4's measure
word), {年年有余|nián nián yǒu yú} (may there be plenty every year: {余|yú} yú sounds like {鱼|yú} yú, fish), {请客|qǐng kè} (to treat
someone, to have guests), {随信寄上|suí xìn jì shàng} (enclosed with this letter), {洗|xǐ} (to print, of photos).

At the post office she asks the clerk: "{您|nín}{好|hǎo}，{寄|jì}{一|yì}{封|fēng}{平信|píng xìn}{到|dào}{本市|běn shì}，{要|yào}{贴|tiē}{多少|duō shao}{钱|qián}{的|de}{邮票|yóu piào}？" (Hello, how
much postage for an ordinary letter within the city?) She writes the {住址|zhù zhǐ} on the {信封|xìn fēng}, sticks on
the {邮票|yóu piào} and posts it.

1. What is the letter mainly about?
2. Why did Professor Luo's wife say people eat fish at New Year?
3. How has Anna's view of Chinese etiquette changed?
4. What does Anna send with the letter?

<details>
<summary>Answers and translation</summary>

1. Thanking the professor and his wife for the New Year visit, and what Anna learned from it.
2. For "{年年有余|nián nián yǒu yú}": {余|yú} (surplus) sounds like {鱼|yú} (fish), so fish stands for having plenty every year.
3. She used to find all the etiquette of gifts and hospitality hard to understand; now she sees respect and care for others behind it ({这些|zhè xiē}{讲究|jiǎng jiu}{背后|bèi hòu}，{其实|qí shí}{都|dōu}{是|shì}{对|duì}{别人|bié ren}{的|de}{尊重|zūn zhòng}{和|hé}{关心|guān xīn}).
4. A print of the photo they took together that day ({随信寄上|suí xìn jì shàng}{我们|wǒ men}{那|nà}{天|tiān}{的|de}{合影|hé yǐng}).

"Dear Professor Luo and Mrs Luo, I hope you're both well! Thank you very much for your kind and
warm hospitality when I visited your home on the second day of the New Year. It was the first
time I'd spent the New Year at a Chinese teacher's home, and I still remember the day very
clearly. As soon as I came in, Mrs Luo took my hand with a smile, and I felt as warm as if I'd come
home. Professor Luo cooked a whole table of dishes himself, and every one was delicious. My
favourite was the fish: Mrs Luo told me that eating fish at New Year is a wish for 'plenty every
year'. Mrs Luo taught me to make dumplings too: mine didn't look very good, but everyone praised them. Ms
Lu was very kind as well, and told me a lot about working at a museum; I'll definitely go to see
their porcelain exhibition next month. After the meal we
had a photo taken together, and Professor Luo signed his new book for me. I'll treasure it. The red balloon your little grandson
gave me is hanging in my room, and Wang Fang says it's lovely too. After
so many years in China, I like the people and the culture here more and more. I used to think
the etiquette of giving presents and having guests was so complicated it was hard to understand.
Now I see that behind it all is respect and care for others. With this letter I'm sending the
photo of us from that day: I've put it in my album, and had a copy printed for you. I'll come and
see you again some time. Wishing you both a happy New Year and good health! With respectful
greetings, your student, Anna. 8 February."
</details>

{平信|píng xìn} is an ordinary (not registered) letter; {本市|běn shì} is "this city" ({本|běn}, lesson 13).

## Write it: a story in four pictures

Write 100–150 characters about these four pictures, using at least four of {替|tì}, {亲自|qīn zì}, {一|yí}{束|shù}, {恭喜|gōng xǐ}, {握手|wò shǒu},
{微笑|wēi xiào}, {改天|gǎi tiān}.

1. A young man at a flower shop chooses a bunch of flowers.
2. He rings the doorbell of a flat; an old couple open the door, smiling.
3. Inside, he hands them the flowers and a card; they shake hands.
4. As he leaves, the old man waves from the door.
