book). {想起|xiǎng qǐ}: to recall.

1. What is the text mainly about?
2. What did the second group of students do after reading?
3. When did the first group do better?
4. What does the writer suggest you do?

<details>
<summary>Answers and translation</summary>

1. That testing yourself (recalling what you've learned) helps memory more than rereading, as an
   experiment showed.
2. They didn't look at the passage again but wrote down what they remembered ({把|bǎ}{记得|jì de}{的|de}{内容|nèi róng}{写|xiě}{下来|xià lái}).
3. Only in the test five minutes later ({五|wǔ}{分钟|fēn zhōng}{以后|yǐ hòu}{测试|cè shì}，{第|dì}{一|yī}{组|zǔ}{记得|jì de}{更|gèng}{多|duō}); after two days and a week the second
   group did much better.
4. To close the book and test yourself before looking at the answers.

"**What's the best way to revise?** What's the best way to revise? The day before an exam, the library is full of students bent over
their books. Many students read their textbook over and over, some marking the important sentences in different colours: the more they read, the more firmly they feel they remember it. But is this
really the best method? Psychologists have done an experiment like this. They asked two groups of
students to read a short text. After reading it, the first group read it a few more times; the
second group didn't look at it again but wrote down what they remembered. Both groups spent the
same amount of time. Finally the researchers
tested both groups, some after five minutes and some after two days or a week. The results surprised
many people. When tested after five minutes, the first group remembered more; but tested after two
days or a week, the second group did much better. The researchers called this the 'testing
effect'. Why should this be? Experts think that the process
of 'getting' knowledge out of the brain is itself a kind of practice: each time you 'get it out',
the memory gets deeper. It's like running: watching other people run won't make you any stronger. Rereading a book, on the other hand, easily makes people feel they've
remembered everything when in fact they haven't. This finding has already been applied in many
fields. Quite a few phone apps for studying now make use of this pattern, having users answer questions
first and then see the answers; some also use your answers to schedule your next review. Of course, this doesn't mean reading is useless: reading carefully
first and then testing yourself may work best. So next time you revise, you could close the book first and test yourself on
how much you can recall."

(The experiment described, in simplified form, is a well-known one from 2006, by the psychologists Henry Roediger and
Jeffrey Karpicke; the text keeps to what it found.)
</details>

## Speaking: a story from three photos

In the speaking test you see three numbered photos and tell a story that joins them (as reported,
about three minutes to prepare and two to speak). Here are the photos in words:

1. At a school science fair, a girl's small robot falls over and a wheel comes off.
2. That evening, she and a friend sit at a table full of tools, fixing it.
3. A week later, she stands holding a certificate beside the robot.

Plan with time words ({那|nà}{天|tiān}, {晚上|wǎn shang}, {一|yí}{个|gè}{星期|xīng qī}{以后|yǐ hòu}) and connectors ({结果|jié guǒ}, {于是|yú shì}, {终于|zhōng yú}), and give the people
feelings ({着急|zháo jí}, {失望|shī wàng}, {高兴|gāo xìng}).

<details>
<summary>Model story</summary>

{上|shàng}{个|gè}{月|yuè}，{学校|xué xiào}{举办|jǔ bàn}{了|le}{科技节|kē jì jié}。{小李|Xiǎo Lǐ}{做|zuò}{了|le}{一|yí}{个|gè}{小|xiǎo}{机器人|jī qì rén}，{她|tā}{觉得|jué de}{它|tā}{一定|yí dìng}{能|néng}{吸引|xī yǐn}{很|hěn}{多|duō}{人|rén}。{可是|kě shì}{比赛|bǐ sài}{的|de}{时候|shí hou}，{机器人|jī qì rén}{刚|gāng}{走|zǒu}{了|le}{几|jǐ}{步|bù}{就|jiù}{倒|dǎo}{了|le}，{一|yí}{个|gè}{轮子|lún zi}{也|yě}{掉|diào}{了|le}{下来|xià lái}。{小李|Xiǎo Lǐ}{又|yòu}{着急|zháo jí}{又|yòu}{失望|shī wàng}。

{那|nà}{天|tiān}{晚上|wǎn shang}，{她|tā}{的|de}{好|hǎo}{朋友|péng you}{来|lái}{帮|bāng}{她|tā}。{两|liǎng}{个|gè}{人|rén}{把|bǎ}{机器人|jī qì rén}{拆|chāi}{开|kāi}，{一|yí}{个|gè}{零件|líng jiàn}{一|yí}{个|gè}{零件|líng jiàn}{地|de}{检查|jiǎn chá}，{终于|zhōng yú}{找|zhǎo}{到|dào}{了|le}{问题|wèn tí}。{她们|tā men}{一直|yì zhí}{修|xiū}{到|dào}{半夜|bàn yè}。

{一|yí}{个|gè}{星期|xīng qī}{以后|yǐ hòu}，{学校|xué xiào}{又|yòu}{进行|jìn xíng}{了|le}{一|yí}{次|cì}{比赛|bǐ sài}。{这|zhè}{一|yí}{次|cì}，{小李|Xiǎo Lǐ}{的|de}{机器人|jī qì rén}{走|zǒu}{得|de}{又|yòu}{快|kuài}{又|yòu}{稳|wěn}，{她|tā}{得|dé}{了|le}{一等奖|yì děng jiǎng}。{小李|Xiǎo Lǐ}{说|shuō}："{失败|shī bài}{了|le}{不要紧|bú yào jǐn}，{找|zhǎo}{到|dào}{原因|yuán yīn}，{下|xià}{次|cì}{就|jiù}{能|néng}{做|zuò}{得|de}{更|gèng}{好|hǎo}。"

({科技节|kē jì jié}: a science festival; {轮子|lún zi} lún zi: a wheel; {零件|líng jiàn} líng jiàn: a part; {稳|wěn}: steady, lesson 05's {稳定|wěn dìng};
{一等奖|yì děng jiǎng}: first prize.)
</details>

## Write it: a picture story

Four pictures, 100–150 characters.

1. A grandmother looks at her new smartphone, puzzled.
2. Her grandson shows her how to make a video call.
3. She calls her daughter, who lives in another city, and they see each other.
4. The grandmother smiles; the grandson gives a thumbs-up.

<details>
<summary>Model story</summary>

{奶奶|nǎi nai}{买|mǎi}{了|le}{一|yí}{部|bù}{智能|zhì néng}{手机|shǒu jī}，{可是|kě shì}{她|tā}{不|bú}{会|huì}{用|yòng}，{拿|ná}{着|zhe}{手机|shǒu jī}{看|kàn}{来|lái}{看|kàn}{去|qù}，{不|bù}{知道|zhī dào}{怎么办|zěn me bàn}。{孙子|sūn zi}{看见|kàn jiàn}{了|le}，{就|jiù}{坐|zuò}{在|zài}{奶奶|nǎi nai}{旁边|páng biān}，{一|yí}{步|bù}{一|yí}{步|bù}{地|de}{教|jiāo}{她|tā}{怎么|zěn me}{打|dǎ}{视频电话|shì pín diàn huà}。{奶奶|nǎi nai}{学|xué}{得|de}{很|hěn}{认真|rèn zhēn}，{还|hái}{用|yòng}{本子|běn zi}{记录|jì lù}{了|le}{下来|xià lái}。{学|xué}{会|huì}{以后|yǐ hòu}，{她|tā}{马上|mǎ shàng}{给|gěi}{在|zài}{外地|wài dì}{工作|gōng zuò}{的|de}{女儿|nǚ ér}{打|dǎ}{了|le}{一|yí}{个|gè}{视频电话|shì pín diàn huà}。{看|kàn}{到|dào}{女儿|nǚ ér}{的|de}{脸|liǎn}，{奶奶|nǎi nai}{高兴|gāo xìng}{得|de}{笑|xiào}{了|le}。{孙子|sūn zi}{说|shuō}："{奶奶|nǎi nai}，{您|nín}{真|zhēn}{厉害|lì hai}！"

({视频电话|shì pín diàn huà}: a video call; {外地|wài dì}: another place, out of town; {厉害|lì hai}: amazing, HSK 4.)

## Write it: technology and me

Write 200–300 characters on one way technology has changed your life: what it was like before, the
change, one example, good and bad sides, and your conclusion. Use {凭借|píng jiè} or {依据|yī jù}, a word with {化|huà}, and
{从|cóng}…{来|lái}{看|kàn}.

<details>
<summary>Model essay</summary>

{十|shí}{年|nián}{前|qián}，{我|wǒ}{出门|chū mén}{旅行|lǚ xíng}{的|de}{时候|shí hou}，{总是|zǒng shì}{要|yào}{带|dài}{一|yì}{张|zhāng}{地图|dì tú}，{还|hái}{要|yào}{提前|tí qián}{订|dìng}{好|hǎo}{酒店|jiǔ diàn}，{查|chá}{好|hǎo}{火车|huǒ chē}{的|de}{时间|shí jiān}。{现在|xiàn zài}，{这些|zhè xiē}{事情|shì qing}{一|yí}{部|bù}{手机|shǒu jī}{就|jiù}{能|néng}{做|zuò}{完|wán}。

{科技|kē jì}{让|ràng}{旅行|lǚ xíng}{变|biàn}{得|de}{更|gèng}{方便|fāng biàn}{了|le}。{去年|qù nián}{我|wǒ}{去|qù}{一|yí}{个|gè}{从来|cóng lái}{没|méi}{去|qù}{过|guo}{的|de}{城市|chéng shì}，{凭借|píng jiè}{手机|shǒu jī}{上|shàng}{的|de}{地图|dì tú}，{我|wǒ}{一|yí}{个|gè}{人|rén}{找|zhǎo}{到|dào}{了|le}{所有|suǒ yǒu}{想|xiǎng}{去|qù}{的|de}{地方|dì fang}。{在|zài}{饭馆|fàn guǎn}{里|lǐ}，{我|wǒ}{用|yòng}{翻译|fān yì}{软件|ruǎn jiàn}{跟|gēn}{服务员|fú wù yuán}{交流|jiāo liú}，{点菜|diǎn cài}{也|yě}{没有|méi yǒu}{问题|wèn tí}。{可以|kě yǐ}{说|shuō}，{旅行|lǚ xíng}{越|yuè}{来|lái}{越|yuè}{智能化|zhì néng huà}{了|le}。

{不过|bú guò}，{科技|kē jì}{也|yě}{有|yǒu}{不|bù}{好|hǎo}{的|de}{地方|dì fang}。{有|yǒu}{一|yí}{次|cì}{手机|shǒu jī}{没电|méi diàn}{了|le}，{我|wǒ}{在|zài}{街|jiē}{上|shàng}{站|zhàn}{了|le}{半天|bàn tiān}，{不|bù}{知道|zhī dào}{往|wǎng}{哪儿|nǎr}{走|zǒu}，{也|yě}{不好意思|bù hǎo yì si}{问路|wèn lù}。{从|cóng}{这|zhè}{件|jiàn}{事|shì}{来|lái}{看|kàn}，{我们|wǒ men}{不|bù}{能|néng}{完全|wán quán}{依靠|yī kào}{手机|shǒu jī}，{基本|jī běn}{的|de}{能力|néng lì}，{比如|bǐ rú}{看|kàn}{地图|dì tú}、{开口|kāi kǒu}{问路|wèn lù}，{还是|hái shi}{应该|yīng gāi}{有|yǒu}{的|de}。

{总之|zǒng zhī}，{科技|kē jì}{是|shì}{一|yí}{个|gè}{很|hěn}{好|hǎo}{的|de}{工具|gōng jù}，{但是|dàn shì}{它|tā}{不|bù}{能|néng}{代替|dài tì}{我们|wǒ men}{自己|zì jǐ}。

({酒店|jiǔ diàn}: a hotel; {没电|méi diàn}{了|le}: the battery's flat; {依靠|yī kào}: to rely on, lesson 13; {工具|gōng jù}: a tool, lesson 09.)

Checklist: before and now; one example with details; a {不过|bú guò} paragraph for the other side; {总之|zǒng zhī} at the
end.

## Say it

```speak
# Science and technology
{学生|xué sheng}{凭|píng}{学生证|xué sheng zhèng}{可以|kě yǐ}{免费|miǎn fèi}{参观|cān guān}。
= Students can visit free on showing a student card.
{她|tā}{凭|píng}{自己|zì jǐ}{的|de}{努力|nǔ lì}，{考|kǎo}{上|shàng}{了|le}{一|yì}{所|suǒ}{好|hǎo}{大学|dà xué}。
= Through her own hard work she got into a good university.
{这|zhè}{种|zhǒng}{说法|shuō fǎ}{没有|méi yǒu}{科学|kē xué}{依据|yī jù}。
= There's no scientific basis for this claim.
{城市|chéng shì}{越|yuè}{来|lái}{越|yuè}{现代化|xiàn dài huà}{了|le}。
= The city is getting more and more modern.
{我们|wǒ men}{先|xiān}{收集|shōu jí}{数据|shù jù}，{再|zài}{做|zuò}{实验|shí yàn}。
= First we collect data, then we do the experiment.
{这个|zhè ge}{机器人|jī qì rén}{采用|cǎi yòng}{了|le}{最|zuì}{先进|xiān jìn}{的|de}{技术|jì shù}。
= This robot uses the most advanced technology.
```

## Pronunciation

- {实验|shí yàn} shí yàn and {试验|shì yàn} shì yàn: 2+4 and 4+4. The tone of the first syllable is all that tells them
  apart in speech.
- {好奇|hào qí} hào qí: {好|hào} is hào (to be fond of, lesson 10), not hǎo.
- {系统|xì tǒng} xì tǒng, {程序|chéng xù} chéng xù, {操作|cāo zuò} cāo zuò (c, an aspirated ts), {测试|cè shì} cè shì (c, then sh).
- {依据|yī jù} yī jù; {凭借|píng jiè} píng jiè; {领域|lǐng yù} lǐng yù (ü after y is written u).
- {研制|yán zhì} yán zhì and {研发|yán fā} yán fā; {制造|zhì zào} zhì zào: zh, then z.

## Common mistakes

- For a method or an idea, {想|xiǎng}{出|chū} is more natural than {发明|fā míng} ({我|wǒ}{想|xiǎng}{出|chū}{了|le}{一|yí}{个|gè}{新|xīn}{办法|bàn fǎ}); {发明|fā míng} is for a new thing, a
  technique or a device. And ~~{哥伦布|Gē lún bù}{发明|fā míng}{了|le}{美洲|Měi zhōu}~~: something already there is {发现|fā xiàn} ({哥伦布|Gē lún bù}{发现|fā xiàn}{了|le}{美洲|Měi zhōu}, Columbus
  discovered America).
- {凭|píng}{票|piào}{入场|rù chǎng} is the language of signs; in speech, say {要|yào}{有|yǒu}{票|piào}{才|cái}{能|néng}{进|jìn}.
- ~~{依据|yī jù}{我|wǒ}{看|kàn}，…~~: {依据|yī jù} isn't for opinions: {我|wǒ}{认为|rèn wéi}… / {在我看来|zài wǒ kàn lái}….
- ~~{城市|chéng shì}{越|yuè}{来|lái}{越|yuè}{现代|xiàn dài}{了|le}{化|huà}~~: {化|huà} is part of the word: {越|yuè}{来|lái}{越|yuè}{现代化|xiàn dài huà}{了|le}.
- {实验|shí yàn} and {试验|shì yàn}: writing {试验|shì yàn}{室|shì} for a lab is wrong: {实验室|shí yàn shì}.

## Key points

- Basis prepositions: {凭|píng} ({凭|píng}{票|piào}{入场|rù chǎng}; {凭|píng}{自己|zì jǐ}{的|de}{努力|nǔ lì}), {凭借|píng jiè} (written: {凭借|píng jiè}{先进|xiān jìn}{的|de}{技术|jì shù}), {依据|yī jù} (written: {依据|yī jù}{规定|guī dìng};
  noun: {科学|kē xué}{依据|yī jù}), {根据|gēn jù} (everyday). Preview: {据|jù}{调查|diào chá}, {据说|jù shuō} (lesson 24).
- Suffix {化|huà}: adjective / noun + {化|huà} = becoming so ({现代化|xiàn dài huà}, {智能化|zhì néng huà}, {简单化|jiǎn dān huà}, {国际化|guó jì huà}).
- Research: {科研|kē yán}, {研发|yán fā}, {研制|yán zhì}, {调研|diào yán}, {实验|shí yàn} / {试验|shì yàn}, {测试|cè shì}, {数据|shù jù}, {收集|shōu jí}, {问卷|wèn juàn}; technology: {系统|xì tǒng}, {程序|chéng xù}, {操作|cāo zuò}, {设备|shè bèi},
  {机器人|jī qì rén}, {人工智能|rén gōng zhì néng}; invention: {发明|fā míng} vs {发现|fā xiàn}, {创造|chuàng zào} vs {制造|zhì zào}, {利用|lì yòng} vs {应用|yìng yòng}.
- New characters (simplified): {={采|cǎi}✎ {测|cè}✎ {造|zào}✎ {域|yù} {迹|jì} {凭|píng} {统|tǒng} {智|zhì}=}; five differ in traditional, and {={迹|jì}=} is
  蹟 in {+{奇迹|qí jì}+} (跡 in other words).

The words from this lesson are listed below; they join your vocabulary reviews when you complete
the lesson.

lessons.title: Life online: accounts, apps and shopping
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

Most of the Chinese you'll read every day is on a screen: buttons, settings, product pages,
reviews, messages from customer service. This lesson gives you that vocabulary, all 64 words of
it, grouped so it's easy to learn, and three pieces of grammar:

- the suffix {族|zú}, which names a group of people by what they do: {上班族|shàng bān zú} (office workers);
- {自动|zì dòng} (automatic, by itself), beside {主动|zhǔ dòng} (lesson 03) and {自觉|zì jué} (lesson 16);
- {移动|yí dòng} (to move; mobile).

{安娜|Ān nà} (Anna) returns a broken lamp through an online chat, and the reading is a product page with its
reviews. The module's opinion question for the speaking test comes at the end.

## The suffix {族|zú}: a group of people

{族|zú} is HSK 4's {民族|mín zú} (an ethnic group, a nation). As a suffix it makes informal names for groups of
people who share a way of life, the way English uses "-ers" or "the … generation":

| Word | Literally | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| {上班族|shàng bān zú} | the go-to-work group | office workers, commuters |
| {低头族|dī tóu zú} | the heads-down group | people always looking at their phones |
| {追星族|zhuī xīng zú} | the star-chasing group | (devoted) fans of celebrities |
| {月光族|yuè guāng zú} | the month-cleaned-out group | people who spend their whole salary every month |

{上班族|shàng bān zú}{每|měi}{天|tiān}{早上|zǎo shang}{都|dōu}{要|yào}{挤|jǐ}{地铁|dì tiě}。 — Office workers have to squeeze onto the metro every morning ({挤|jǐ}: lesson 21).

{地铁|dì tiě}{上|shàng}{到处|dào chù}{都|dōu}{是|shì}{低头族|dī tóu zú}。 — The metro is full of people staring at their phones.

These words come and go with fashion; the media coin new ones all the time. They're informal: fine in
conversation, articles and blogs, but not in a formal report. {月光族|yuè guāng zú} is a pun on {月光|yuè guāng} (moonlight): {光|guāng} is
also "used up" ({吃光|chī guāng}, {花光|huā guāng}).

## {自动|zì dòng}, {主动|zhǔ dòng}, {自觉|zì jué}

Three ways of doing something "by yourself":

- {自动|zì dòng} (automatic, automatically): **a machine** does it by itself, or something happens without anyone
  doing it: {门|mén}{会|huì}{自动|zì dòng}{打开|dǎ kāi} (the door opens by itself); {手机|shǒu jī}{每|měi}{天|tiān}{晚上|wǎn shang}{自动|zì dòng}{更新|gēng xīn} (the phone updates automatically
  every night); {自动|zì dòng}{关闭|guān bì} (to close automatically). It's also an adjective: {自动|zì dòng}{的|de} (automatic).
- {主动|zhǔ dòng} (lesson 03): **a person** acts on their own initiative, without being asked: {他|tā}{主动|zhǔ dòng}{帮|bāng}{我|wǒ}{搬|bān}{东西|dōng xi} (he offered
  to help me move my things).
- {自觉|zì jué} (lesson 16): **a person** does what they should without being told: {自觉|zì jué}{排队|pái duì} (queue without being told to).

So a machine is {自动|zì dòng}, never {主动|zhǔ dòng}; and a person who "automatically" helps is {主动|zhǔ dòng}, not {自动|zì dòng}.

## {移动|yí dòng}: to move; mobile

{移动|yí dòng} is "to move (something), to shift position" (written): {请|qǐng}{不要|bú yào}{移动|yí dòng}{桌子|zhuō zi} (please don't move the tables).
Before a noun it means "mobile": {移动电话|yí dòng diàn huà} (a mobile phone, formal: everyday {手机|shǒu jī}), {移动网络|yí dòng wǎng luò} (the mobile network),

- ~~{他|tā}{很|hěn}{自动|zì dòng}，{每|měi}{天|tiān}{帮|bāng}{妈妈|mā ma}{做饭|zuò fàn}~~: people act {主动|zhǔ dòng} (on their own initiative): {他|tā}{很|hěn}{主动|zhǔ dòng}.
- ~~{我|wǒ}{分享|fēn xiǎng}{了|le}{一|yí}{辆|liàng}{单车|dān chē}~~: using a shared bike is {共享单车|gòng xiǎng dān chē} / {骑|qí}{共享单车|gòng xiǎng dān chē}; {分享|fēn xiǎng} is sharing something you have with
  others.
- {我|wǒ}{注册|zhù cè}{了|le}{这个|zhè ge}{网站|wǎng zhàn} is understood, but the usual form is {在|zài}{这个|zhè ge}{网站|wǎng zhàn}{上|shàng}{注册|zhù cè} ({了|le}{一|yí}{个|gè}{账号|zhàng hào}), or {注册|zhù cè}{账号|zhàng hào}.
- ~~{东西|dōng xi}{很|hěn}{涨价|zhǎng jià}~~: {涨价|zhǎng jià} is a verb with no degree adverb: {东西|dōng xi}{涨价|zhǎng jià}{了|le}, or {东西|dōng xi}{涨|zhǎng}{得|de}{很|hěn}{厉害|lì hai}.

- {移动|yí dòng}: to move (written); mobile ({移动支付|yí dòng zhī fù}, {移动网络|yí dòng wǎng luò}).
- Accounts ({注册|zhù cè}, {登录|dēng lù}, {退出|tuì chū}, {设置|shè zhì}, {升级|shēng jí}, {更新|gēng xīn}), actions ({搜索|sōu suǒ}, {浏览|liú lǎn}, {复制|fù zhì}, {删除|shān chú}, {保存|bǎo cún}, {下载|xià zǎi}, {上传|shàng chuán}), sharing ({分享|fēn xiǎng} vs {共享|gòng xiǎng},
  {点赞|diǎn zàn}, {留言|liú yán}, {直播|zhí bō}), the phone ({充电|chōng diàn}, {充值|chōng zhí}, {话费|huà fèi}, {拨打|bō dǎ}, {占线|zhàn xiàn}), shopping ({挑选|tiāo xuǎn}, {售价|shòu jià}, {物价|wù jià}, {涨价|zhǎng jià}, {折扣|zhé kòu}, {优惠|yōu huì}, {运费|yùn fèi}, {押金|yā jīn},
  {二手|èr shǒu}, {好评|hǎo píng}).
- New characters: {拨|bō} {池|chí} {闭|bì}✎ {浏|liú} {删|shān} {置|zhì} {升|shēng}✎ {络|luò} {搜|sōu} {索|suǒ} {押|yā} {载|zǎi}✎ {惠|huì} {扣|kòu} {占|zhàn}✎ {涨|zhǎng}.

The words from this lesson are listed below; they join your vocabulary reviews when you complete
the lesson.

lessons.title: Fables and the idioms they left
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

Many {成语|chéng yǔ} (idioms) are a whole story folded into four characters. Lesson 18 said that an idiom often
{出自|chū zì} (comes from) an old text; this lesson tells three of those stories. All three come from books
of the last centuries BCE, written by thinkers who used short fables to make a point about how
people reason. For each you'll find:

- the story retold in our own modern Chinese, at your level;
- its short classical source line, with pinyin and notes;
- what the idiom means today, and a modern sentence that uses it.

You don't need to learn classical Chinese ({文言文|wén yán wén}, wén yán wén) to enjoy the source lines. A handful of
its grammar words will help: {者|zhě} (a person who), {而|ér} (and, but), {其|qí} (his, its), {之|zhī} (him, it; of), {矣|yǐ} (a
particle closing a statement, like {了|le}), {乎|hū} (a question particle, like {吗|ma}), {为|wéi} wéi (to be; by: {为|wéi}…{笑|xiào},
laughed at by), {安|ān} (how?).

## {守株待兔|shǒu zhū dài tù}: waiting by the tree stump

The source is the book of the philosopher Han Fei ({韩非子|Hán Fēi zǐ}, *Hán Fēizǐ*, who died in 233 BCE), in its
chapter 《{五蠹|Wǔ dù}》 *Wǔ dù*. Han Fei used the story against rulers who wanted to govern in the old ways
just because they had once worked.

> **{守株待兔|shǒu zhū dài tù}**
>
> {古时候|gǔ shí hou}，{宋国|Sòng guó}{有|yǒu}{一|yí}{个|gè}{农民|nóng mín}，{每|měi}{天|tiān}{都|dōu}{在|zài}{地|dì}{里|lǐ}{干活|gàn huó}。{有|yǒu}{一|yì}{天|tiān}，{一|yì}{只|zhī}{兔子|tù zi}{跑|pǎo}{得|de}{太|tài}{快|kuài}，{一|yì}{头|tóu}{撞|zhuàng}{在|zài}{田|tián}{边|biān}{的|de}{一|yí}{个|gè}{树桩|shù zhuāng}{上|shàng}，{撞|zhuàng}{断|duàn}{了|le}{脖子|bó zi}，{死|sǐ}{了|le}。{农民|nóng mín}{没|méi}{花|huā}{一点儿|yì diǎnr}{力气|lì qi}，{就|jiù}{捡|jiǎn}{到|dào}{了|le}{一|yì}{只|zhī}{兔子|tù zi}，{高兴|gāo xìng}{极|jí}{了|le}。{他|tā}{想|xiǎng}：{要是|yào shi}{每|měi}{天|tiān}{都|dōu}{能|néng}{捡|jiǎn}{到|dào}{一|yì}{只|zhī}{兔子|tù zi}，{我|wǒ}{就|jiù}{不用|bú yòng}{这么|zhè me}{辛苦|xīn kǔ}{地|de}{种地|zhòng dì}{了|le}。{从|cóng}{那|nà}{以后|yǐ hòu}，{他|tā}{放|fàng}{下|xià}{农具|nóng jù}，{天|tiān}{天|tiān}{坐|zuò}{在|zài}{树桩|shù zhuāng}{旁边|páng biān}，{等|děng}{着|zhe}{兔子|tù zi}{再|zài}{撞|zhuàng}{上来|shàng lái}。{可是|kě shì}，{兔子|tù zi}{再|zài}{也|yě}{没有|méi yǒu}{来|lái}{过|guo}，{他|tā}{的|de}{地|dì}{里|lǐ}{却|què}{长满|zhǎng mǎn}{了|le}{草|cǎo}。{宋国|Sòng guó}{的|de}{人|rén}{都|dōu}{笑话|xiào hua}{他|tā}。

{宋国|Sòng guó}: the state of Song ({古时候|gǔ shí hou}, in ancient times). {农民|nóng mín}: a farmer (lesson 24); {兔子|tù zi}: a rabbit, a hare (lesson
25); {撞|zhuàng}: to crash into (lesson 23); {树桩|shù zhuāng} shù zhuāng: a tree stump; {脖子|bó zi}: the neck (HSK 6); {种地|zhòng dì}: to farm
(HSK 6); {农具|nóng jù}: farm tools; {长满|zhǎng mǎn}: to grow all over ({长|zhǎng} zhǎng); {笑话|xiào hua}: here a verb, to laugh at.

**The classical line**

{宋|Sòng}{人|rén}{有|yǒu}{耕|gēng}{者|zhě}，{田|tián}{中|zhōng}{有|yǒu}{株|zhū}，{兔|tù}{走|zǒu}{触|chù}{株|zhū}，{折|zhé}{颈|jǐng}{而|ér}{死|sǐ}，{因|yīn}{释|shì}{其|qí}{耒|lěi}{而|ér}{守|shǒu}{株|zhū}，{冀|jì}{复|fù}{得|dé}{兔|tù}，{兔|tù}{不|bù}{可|kě}{复|fù}{得|dé}，{而|ér}{身|shēn}{为|wéi}{宋|Sòng}{国|guó}{笑|xiào}。

| Classical | Modern | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| {耕|gēng}{者|zhě} | {种地|zhòng dì}{的|de}{人|rén} | a ploughman, a farmer |
| {株|zhū} | {树桩|shù zhuāng} | a tree stump |
| {走|zǒu} | {跑|pǎo} | to run (classical {走|zǒu} is "run") |
| {折|zhé}{颈|jǐng} | {断|duàn}{了|le}{脖子|bó zi} | broke its neck |
| {释|shì}{其|qí}{耒|lěi} | {放下|fàng xià}{他|tā}{的|de}{农具|nóng jù} | put down his plough |
| {冀|jì}{复|fù}{得|dé}{兔|tù} | {希望|xī wàng}{再|zài}{得到|dé dào}{兔子|tù zi} | hoping to get another hare |
| {身|shēn}{为|wéi}{宋|Sòng}{国|guó}{笑|xiào} | {自己|zì jǐ}{被|bèi}{宋|Sòng}{国|guó}{人|rén}{笑话|xiào hua} | he himself became the laughing stock of Song |

Our translation: "In Song there was a farmer. In his field there was a tree stump. A hare ran into
the stump, broke its neck and died. So he put down his plough and kept watch by the stump, hoping
to get another hare. No hare came again, and he became the laughing stock of Song."

**The idiom today.** {守株待兔|shǒu zhū dài tù} (shǒu zhū dài tù: keep watch by the stump, wait for a hare) describes
waiting for luck to come to you instead of making an effort, or sticking to one lucky experience:

{找|zhǎo}{工作|gōng zuò}{不|bù}{能|néng}{守株待兔|shǒu zhū dài tù}，{要|yào}{主动|zhǔ dòng}{去|qù}{投简历|tóu jiǎn lì}。 — When you're looking for a job you can't just sit and wait for
luck: send out your CV ({投简历|tóu jiǎn lì}).

## {刻舟求剑|kè zhōu qiú jiàn}: marking the boat to find the sword

The source is the 《{吕氏春秋|Lǚ shì Chūn qiū}》 (*Lǚshì Chūnqiū*, the "Springs and Autumns of Mr Lü"), a book compiled for the
statesman Lü Buwei around 239 BCE, in its chapter 《{察今|Chá jīn}》 *Chá jīn* ("examining the present"). The
chapter argues that laws must change with the times.

> **{刻舟求剑|kè zhōu qiú jiàn}**
>
> {楚国|Chǔ guó}{有|yǒu}{一|yí}{个|gè}{人|rén}{坐|zuò}{船|chuán}{过|guò}{江|jiāng}。{船|chuán}{走|zǒu}{到|dào}{江|jiāng}{中间|zhōng jiān}{的|de}{时候|shí hou}，{他|tā}{身|shēn}{上|shàng}{的|de}{剑|jiàn}{一|yí}{不|bù}{小心|xiǎo xīn}{掉|diào}{进|jìn}{了|le}{水|shuǐ}{里|lǐ}。{他|tā}{马上|mǎ shàng}{拿|ná}{出|chū}{一|yì}{把|bǎ}{小刀|xiǎo dāo}，{在|zài}{船|chuán}{边|biān}{刻|kè}{了|le}{一|yí}{个|gè}{记号|jì hao}，{说|shuō}：“{我|wǒ}{的|de}{剑|jiàn}{是|shì}{从|cóng}{这儿|zhèr}{掉|diào}{下去|xià qù}{的|de}。”{船|chuán}{靠岸|kào àn}{以后|yǐ hòu}，{他|tā}{从|cóng}{刻|kè}{记号|jì hao}{的|de}{地方|dì fang}{跳|tiào}{进|jìn}{水|shuǐ}{里|lǐ}{找|zhǎo}{剑|jiàn}，{找|zhǎo}{了|le}{半天|bàn tiān}{也|yě}{没|méi}{找|zhǎo}{到|dào}。{船|chuán}{一直|yì zhí}{在|zài}{往|wǎng}{前|qián}{走|zǒu}，{剑|jiàn}{却|què}{留|liú}{在|zài}{原来|yuán lái}{的|de}{地方|dì fang}，{用|yòng}{这样|zhè yàng}{的|de}{办法|bàn fǎ}{找|zhǎo}{剑|jiàn}，{不|bú}{是|shì}{太|tài}{糊涂|hú tu}{了|le}{吗|ma}？

{楚国|Chǔ guó}: the state of Chu. {剑|jiàn} jiàn: a sword (HSK 6). {刻|kè}: to carve. {记号|jì hao}: a mark. {靠岸|kào àn}: to come in to the bank ({岸|àn}
àn, HSK 6). {糊涂|hú tu} hú tu: muddled, foolish.

**The classical line**

{舟|zhōu}{已|yǐ}{行|xíng}{矣|yǐ}，{而|ér}{剑|jiàn}{不|bù}{行|xíng}。

| Classical | Modern | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| {舟|zhōu} | {船|chuán} | a boat |
| {已|yǐ} | {已经|yǐ jīng} | already (HSK 4's written {已|yǐ}) |
| {行|xíng} | {走|zǒu} | to move, go |
| {矣|yǐ} | {了|le} | (closes the statement) |
| {而|ér} | {可是|kě shì} | but |

Our translation: "The boat had moved on, but the sword had not." The man had marked where the sword
fell in relation to the boat, and the boat was the one thing that kept moving.

**The idiom today.** {刻舟求剑|kè zhōu qiú jiàn} (kè zhōu qiú jiàn: carve the boat, seek the sword) describes someone who
doesn't see that things have changed and keeps using an old way of judging them:

{情况|qíng kuàng}{已经|yǐ jīng}{变|biàn}{了|le}，{还|hái}{用|yòng}{去年|qù nián}{的|de}{办法|bàn fǎ}，{这|zhè}{不|bú}{是|shì}{刻舟求剑|kè zhōu qiú jiàn}{吗|ma}？ — Things have changed: using last year's methods is
just marking the boat to find the sword.

## {画蛇添足|huà shé tiān zú}: drawing feet on a snake

The source is the 《{战国策|Zhàn guó cè}》 (*Zhànguó cè*, "Strategies of the Warring States"), a collection of stories about
the advisers of the Warring States, put together in the 1st century BCE by the scholar Liu Xiang. In the
book, an adviser tells this story to a general to persuade him not to push a victory too far.

> **{画蛇添足|huà shé tiān zú}**
>
> {楚国|Chǔ guó}{有|yǒu}{一|yí}{个|gè}{人|rén}{祭祀|jì sì}{以后|yǐ hòu}，{把|bǎ}{一壶酒|yì hú jiǔ}{送|sòng}{给|gěi}{帮|bāng}{他|tā}{做|zuò}{事|shì}{的|de}{几|jǐ}{个|gè}{人|rén}。{这|zhè}{几|jǐ}{个|gè}{人|rén}{商量|shāng liang}{说|shuō}：“{这|zhè}{壶|hú}{酒|jiǔ}，{几|jǐ}{个|gè}{人|rén}{喝|hē}{不够|bú gòu}，{一|yí}{个|gè}{人|rén}{喝|hē}{还|hái}{有|yǒu}{剩|shèng}。{我们|wǒ men}{比赛|bǐ sài}{在|zài}{地|dì}{上|shàng}{画蛇|huà shé}{吧|ba}，{谁|shéi}{先|xiān}{画|huà}{好|hǎo}，{酒|jiǔ}{就|jiù}{归|guī}{谁|shéi}。”{有|yǒu}{一|yí}{个|gè}{人|rén}{很|hěn}{快|kuài}{就|jiù}{画|huà}{好|hǎo}{了|le}，{他|tā}{拿|ná}{起|qǐ}{酒壶|jiǔ hú}{正|zhèng}{要|yào}{喝|hē}，{看见|kàn jiàn}{别人|bié ren}{还|hái}{没|méi}{画|huà}{完|wán}，{就|jiù}{得意|dé yì}{地|de}{说|shuō}：“{我|wǒ}{还|hái}{能|néng}{给|gěi}{蛇|shé}{画|huà}{上|shàng}{脚|jiǎo}{呢|ne}！”{他|tā}{左|zuǒ}{手|shǒu}{拿|ná}{着|zhe}{酒壶|jiǔ hú}，{右|yòu}{手|shǒu}{给|gěi}{蛇|shé}{画|huà}{脚|jiǎo}。{脚|jiǎo}{还|hái}{没|méi}{画|huà}{完|wán}，{另|lìng}{一|yí}{个|gè}{人|rén}{的|de}{蛇|shé}{已经|yǐ jīng}{画|huà}{好|hǎo}{了|le}。{那个|nà ge}{人|rén}{把|bǎ}{酒壶|jiǔ hú}{抢|qiǎng}{过去|guò qù}，{说|shuō}：“{蛇|shé}{本来|běn lái}{就|jiù}{没有|méi yǒu}{脚|jiǎo}，{你|nǐ}{怎么|zěn me}{能|néng}{给|gěi}{它|tā}{画|huà}{脚|jiǎo}{呢|ne}？”{说|shuō}{完|wán}{就|jiù}{把|bǎ}{酒|jiǔ}{喝|hē}{了|le}。{给|gěi}{蛇|shé}{画|huà}{脚|jiǎo}{的|de}{人|rén}，{最后|zuì hòu}{一口|yì kǒu}{酒|jiǔ}{也|yě}{没|méi}{喝|hē}{到|dào}。

{祭祀|jì sì} jì sì: to offer a sacrifice (to ancestors or spirits). {壶|hú} hú: a pot, a jug (HSK 6); {一壶酒|yì hú jiǔ}: a jug of
wine. {归|guī}: to go to, to belong to (HSK 6). {得意|dé yì}: pleased with oneself (HSK 4). {抢|qiǎng} (lesson 23): to snatch.

**The classical lines**

{蛇|shé}{固|gù}{无|wú}{足|zú}，{子|zǐ}{安|ān}{能|néng}{为|wéi}{之|zhī}{足|zú}？……{为|wéi}{蛇|shé}{足|zú}{者|zhě}，{终|zhōng}{亡|wáng}{其|qí}{酒|jiǔ}。

| Classical | Modern | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| {固|gù} | {本来|běn lái} | in the first place, by nature |
| {子|zǐ} | {你|nǐ} | you (polite) |
| {安|ān} | {怎么|zěn me} | how? |
| {为|wéi}{之|zhī}{足|zú} | {给|gěi}{它|tā}{画|huà}{脚|jiǎo} | make feet for it ({为|wéi} wéi: to make, to do) |
| {为|wéi}{蛇|shé}{足|zú}{者|zhě} | {给|gěi}{蛇|shé}{画|huà}{脚|jiǎo}{的|de}{人|rén} | the one who made the snake's feet |
| {终|zhōng}{亡|wáng}{其|qí}{酒|jiǔ} | {最后|zuì hòu}{失去|shī qù}{了|le}{他|tā}{的|de}{酒|jiǔ} | in the end lost his wine |

Our translation: "'A snake has no feet in the first place: how can you give it feet?' … The one who
drew feet on the snake lost his wine in the end."

**The idiom today.** {画蛇添足|huà shé tiān zú} (huà shé tiān zú: draw a snake, add feet; {添|tiān} is "to add") describes
spoiling something by adding what isn't needed:

{这|zhè}{篇|piān}{文章|wén zhāng}{已经|yǐ jīng}{写|xiě}{得|de}{很|hěn}{好|hǎo}{了|le}，{最后|zuì hòu}{再|zài}{加|jiā}{一|yí}{段|duàn}，{就是|jiù shì}{画蛇添足|huà shé tiān zú}{了|le}。 — The essay is already very good: adding
another paragraph at the end would just spoil it.

## Three stories, three mistakes

| Idiom | The mistake | Used of |
|---|---|---|
| {守株待兔|shǒu zhū dài tù} | taking one lucky event for a rule | waiting for luck instead of working |
| {刻舟求剑|kè zhōu qiú jiàn} | forgetting that things change | judging by out-of-date standards |
| {画蛇添足|huà shé tiān zú} | not knowing when to stop | spoiling a job by overdoing it |

All three are critical: you use them of a mistake, often with {这|zhè}{是|shì}…, {这|zhè}{不|bú}{是|shì}…{吗|ma}? or {就是|jiù shì}…{了|le}. Each acts as
a whole verb phrase in the sentence: {他|tā}{这样|zhè yàng}{做|zuò}{是|shì}{守株待兔|shǒu zhū dài tù} (what he's doing is waiting for a hare by the
stump). They're common in speech and writing, and in the exam's reading paper you may be asked what
one means in its context: think of the story, then of what kind of mistake it describes.

## Key points

- {守株待兔|shǒu zhū dài tù} (《{韩非子|Hán Fēi zǐ}》): don't wait for luck; {刻舟求剑|kè zhōu qiú jiàn} (《{吕氏春秋|Lǚ shì Chūn qiū}》): things change; {画蛇添足|huà shé tiān zú} (《{战国策|Zhàn guó cè}》): don't add
  what isn't needed.
- Classical words: {者|zhě} (a person who), {而|ér} (and, but), {其|qí} (his, its), {之|zhī} (it), {矣|yǐ} (= {了|le}), {安|ān} (how?), {固|gù} (by nature),
  {走|zǒu} (run), {舟|zhōu} (boat), {为|wéi} wéi (to make; by).
- Each idiom stands for a mistake: use it as a judgment ({这|zhè}{是|shì}…, {这|zhè}{不|bú}{是|shì}…{吗|ma}?, {就是|jiù shì}…{了|le}).

lessons.title: How idioms work
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

HSK 5 is where {成语|chéng yǔ} (chéng yǔ, idioms) begin: six of this level's words are idioms, and you met three
famous ones with their stories in lesson 20h1. This lesson steps back and asks what an idiom is,
where idioms come from, how their four characters fit together, and, most useful of all, how to put
one into a sentence without sounding odd.

## What makes a {成语|chéng yǔ}

Four things, most of the time:

1. **A fixed form.** You can't swap a character for a synonym: {画蛇添足|huà shé tiān zú} can't become ×{画蛇|huà shé}{加|jiā}{足|zú}, even though {加|jiā}
   and {添|tiān} both mean "add".
2. **Four characters.** By far the most common length. A few have three, five or more characters,
   but those are usually called by other names ({惯用语|guàn yòng yǔ}, {俗语|sú yǔ}: set expressions and sayings).
3. **A meaning beyond the parts.** {守株待兔|shǒu zhū dài tù} isn't about hares: it's about waiting for luck. Some are
   transparent ({五颜六色|wǔ yán liù sè}: "five colours, six colours", many colours), some are figures of speech
   ({比喻|bǐ yù}) that you have to know.
4. **An old style.** Many keep the grammar of classical Chinese ({之|zhī}, {其|qí}, {而|ér}, {无|wú}), and many come from a
   source text: a fable, a historical event, a poem or a philosopher's saying. That source is
   called the idiom's {出处|chū chù} (chū chù).

Not every four-character phrase is a {成语|chéng yǔ}. Patterns like {想|xiǎng}{来|lái}{想|xiǎng}{去|qù} (lesson 16) or {说|shuō}{走|zǒu}{就|jiù}{走|zǒu} (lesson 10) are
grammar: you fill them with any suitable verb. A {成语|chéng yǔ} is one fixed item that you learn as a word.

## Where idioms come from

- **Stories and fables**: {守株待兔|shǒu zhū dài tù}, {刻舟求剑|kè zhōu qiú jiàn}, {画蛇添足|huà shé tiān zú} (lesson 20h1). The idiom is a four-character summary of
  the story.
- **Old texts**: a line or part of a line from a classic, shortened to four characters.
- **Everyday language**, fixed by long use: {五颜六色|wǔ yán liù sè}, {各行各业|gè háng gè yè}, {亲朋好友|qīn péng hǎo yǒu}, {一路顺风|yí lù shùn fēng}. These have no story; they
  sound natural and are easy to understand.

The idioms of this level are mostly of the last kind, which makes them a good place to start.

## How the four characters fit together

The commonest shape is **two pairs** that mirror each other. ({丰富多彩|fēng fù duō cǎi} and {酸甜苦辣|suān tián kǔ là} are lesson 25's words,
{一路顺风|yí lù shùn fēng} lesson 29's; the others you've met.)

| Idiom | Shape | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| {五颜六色|wǔ yán liù sè} | number + noun, number + noun ({五|wǔ}A{六|liù}B) | all kinds of colours |
| {各行各业|gè háng gè yè} | {各|gè}A{各|gè}B | every trade and profession |
| {亲朋好友|qīn péng hǎo yǒu} | two pairs of near-synonyms ({亲朋|qīn péng} + {好友|hǎo yǒu}) | friends and relatives |
| {丰富多彩|fēng fù duō cǎi} | two adjectives side by side ({丰富|fēng fù} + {多彩|duō cǎi}) | rich and colourful, varied |
| {酸甜苦辣|suān tián kǔ là} | four parallel words | sour, sweet, bitter, hot: all life's experiences |

Others are **two verb phrases** in sequence, like the fables: {守株|shǒu zhū} + {待兔|dài tù} (keep watch by the stump, wait for
a hare), {刻舟|kè zhōu} + {求剑|qiú jiàn}, {画蛇|huà shé} + {添足|tiān zú}. And some are like a short sentence: {一路顺风|yí lù shùn fēng} is {一路|yí lù} (all the way) +
{顺风|shùn fēng} (a following wind), "a good wind all the way", said to someone setting off on a journey.

Knowing the shape helps you guess a new idiom: if the two halves mirror each other, the meaning is
usually what they have in common.

## Putting an idiom into a sentence

Most idioms work like one of the ordinary parts of speech. The trick is to know which.

| Use | Example |
|---|---|
| predicate (like an adjective) | {大学|dà xué}{生活|shēng huó}{丰富多彩|fēng fù duō cǎi}。 University life is rich and varied. |
| attributive, with {的|de} | {我们|wǒ men}{举办|jǔ bàn}{了|le}{丰富多彩|fēng fù duō cǎi}{的|de}{活动|huó dòng}。 We held all kinds of events. / {五颜六色|wǔ yán liù sè}{的|de}{花|huā} flowers of every colour |
| object or subject | {各行各业|gè háng gè yè}{都|dōu}{需要|xū yào}{人才|rén cái}。 Every line of work needs talented people. |
| a judgment, with {是|shì} / {就是|jiù shì}…{了|le} | {再|zài}{加|jiā}{一|yí}{段|duàn}{就是|jiù shì}{画蛇添足|huà shé tiān zú}{了|le}。 Adding another paragraph would be gilding the lily. |
| a whole sentence (a wish) | {祝|zhù}{你|nǐ}{一路顺风|yí lù shùn fēng}！ Have a good journey! |

Some can be adverbials with {地|de}, but far fewer than you'd think: check before using one that way.
Two practical rules:

- **Don't add degree words** to an idiom that is already strong: ×{很|hěn}{五颜六色|wǔ yán liù sè}. Say {五颜六色|wǔ yán liù sè}{的|de} or {颜色|yán sè}{很|hěn}{多|duō}.
- **Don't over-use them.** One well-chosen idiom in a paragraph sounds educated; four sound like a
  textbook. In speech, the everyday ones ({一路顺风|yí lù shùn fēng}, {亲朋好友|qīn péng hǎo yǒu}, {五颜六色|wǔ yán liù sè}) are natural; the classical ones
  ({刻舟求剑|kè zhōu qiú jiàn}) are for making a point.

## Register and tone

Idioms carry an attitude as well as a meaning. {丰富多彩|fēng fù duō cǎi} always praises; {画蛇添足|huà shé tiān zú} and {守株待兔|shǒu zhū dài tù} always criticise.
Using a critical idiom about yourself can be modest or funny ({我|wǒ}{这|zhè}{是|shì}{画蛇添足|huà shé tiān zú}{了|le}, I overdid it there), but
using it about someone senior to their face is rude. {酸甜苦辣|suān tián kǔ là} is neutral: life's ups and downs. Before
you use a new idiom, check two things: what it is said of (people, things, situations), and whether it
praises or blames.

## Reading: idioms in everyday life

> **{生活|shēng huó}{中|zhōng}{的|de}{成语|chéng yǔ}**
>
> {很|hěn}{多|duō}{人|rén}{觉得|jué de}{成语|chéng yǔ}{只|zhǐ}{在|zài}{书|shū}{里|lǐ}{出现|chū xiàn}，{其实|qí shí}{我们|wǒ men}{每|měi}{天|tiān}{都|dōu}{在|zài}{用|yòng}。
>
> {早上|zǎo shang}{打开|dǎ kāi}{手机|shǒu jī}，{新闻|xīn wén}{里|lǐ}{说|shuō}：“{今年|jīn nián}{各行各业|gè háng gè yè}{都|dōu}{在|zài}{使用|shǐ yòng}{人工智能|rén gōng zhì néng}。”{这里|zhè lǐ}{的|de}“{各行各业|gè háng gè yè}”，{意思|yì si}{是|shì}“{所有|suǒ yǒu}{的|de}{行业|háng yè}”，{说|shuō}{的|de}{人|rén}{多|duō}，{听|tīng}{的|de}{人|rén}{也|yě}{一下子|yí xià zi}{就|jiù}{明白|míng bai}。
>
> {走|zǒu}{进|jìn}{学校|xué xiào}，{门口|mén kǒu}{的|de}{通知|tōng zhī}{写|xiě}{着|zhe}：“{本|běn}{周末|zhōu mò}{将|jiāng}{举办|jǔ bàn}{丰富多彩|fēng fù duō cǎi}{的|de}{校园|xiào yuán}{活动|huó dòng}，{欢迎|huān yíng}{同学|tóng xué}{们|men}{参加|cān jiā}。”{通知|tōng zhī}{用|yòng}“{丰富多彩|fēng fù duō cǎi}”，{比|bǐ}{说|shuō}“{很|hěn}{多|duō}{有意思|yǒu yì si}{的|de}{活动|huó dòng}”{更|gèng}{正式|zhèng shì}，{也|yě}{更|gèng}{简单|jiǎn dān}。
>
> {中午|zhōng wǔ}{去|qù}{花店|huā diàn}，{店|diàn}{里|lǐ}{摆满|bǎi mǎn}{了|le}{五颜六色|wǔ yán liù sè}{的|de}{鲜花|xiān huā}。{卖|mài}{花|huā}{的|de}{阿姨|ā yí}{说|shuō}：“{下|xià}{个|gè}{月|yuè}{我|wǒ}{女儿|nǚ ér}{结婚|jié hūn}，{请|qǐng}{了|le}{很|hěn}{多|duō}{亲朋好友|qīn péng hǎo yǒu}。”{你|nǐ}{看|kàn}，{几|jǐ}{句|jù}{普通|pǔ tōng}{的|de}{话|huà}{里|lǐ}，{就|jiù}{有|yǒu}{两|liǎng}{个|gè}{成语|chéng yǔ}。
>
> {下午|xià wǔ}{路过|lù guò}{公园|gōng yuán}，{几|jǐ}{个|gè}{孩子|hái zi}{正在|zhèng zài}{玩|wán}{成语接龙|chéng yǔ jiē lóng}：{第|dì}{一|yī}{个|gè}{人|rén}{说|shuō}{一|yí}{个|gè}{成语|chéng yǔ}，{下|xià}{一|yí}{个|gè}{人|rén}{要|yào}{用|yòng}{这个|zhè ge}{成语|chéng yǔ}{的|de}{最后|zuì hòu}{一|yí}{个|gè}{字|zì}{开头|kāi tóu}，{再说|zài shuō}{一|yí}{个|gè}{新|xīn}{的|de}{成语|chéng yǔ}，{说|shuō}{不|bu}{出来|chū lái}{就|jiù}{输|shū}{了|le}。{孩子|hái zi}{们|men}{一边|yì biān}{想|xiǎng}{一边|yì biān}{笑|xiào}，{玩|wán}{得|de}{很|hěn}{开心|kāi xīn}。{不知不觉|bù zhī bù jué}{中|zhōng}，{他们|tā men}{又|yòu}{学|xué}{会|huì}{了|le}{好几|hǎo jǐ}{个|gè}{成语|chéng yǔ}。
>
> {晚上|wǎn shang}，{一|yí}{位|wèi}{朋友|péng you}{要|yào}{坐|zuò}{飞机|fēi jī}{出国|chū guó}{留学|liú xué}。{大家|dà jiā}{在|zài}{机场|jī chǎng}{跟|gēn}{他|tā}{告别|gào bié}，{最后|zuì hòu}{说|shuō}{的|de}{一|yí}{句|jù}{话|huà}{一定|yí dìng}{是|shì}：“{一路顺风|yí lù shùn fēng}！”{这|zhè}{四|sì}{个|gè}{字|zì}，{表达|biǎo dá}{了|le}{所有|suǒ yǒu}{人|rén}{的|de}{祝福|zhù fú}。
>
> {回|huí}{到|dào}{家|jiā}，{奶奶|nǎi nai}{在|zài}{讲|jiǎng}{她|tā}{年轻|nián qīng}{时候|shí hou}{的|de}{故事|gù shi}。{她|tā}{说|shuō}：“{我|wǒ}{这|zhè}{一辈子|yí bèi zi}，{酸甜苦辣|suān tián kǔ là}{都|dōu}{尝|cháng}{过|guo}{了|le}。”{四|sì}{个|gè}{字|zì}，{就|jiù}{把|bǎ}{几|jǐ}{十|shí}{年|nián}{的|de}{经历|jīng lì}{概括|gài kuò}{了|le}。
>
> {有的|yǒu de}{成语|chéng yǔ}{背后|bèi hòu}{还|hái}{有|yǒu}{一|yí}{个|gè}{故事|gù shi}，{比如|bǐ rú}“{画蛇添足|huà shé tiān zú}”{和|hé}“{守株待兔|shǒu zhū dài tù}”。{知道|zhī dào}{了|le}{故事|gù shi}，{再|zài}{用|yòng}{这个|zhè ge}{成语|chéng yǔ}，{就|jiù}{不|bù}{容易|róng yì}{用|yòng}{错|cuò}{了|le}。
>
> {成语|chéng yǔ}{之所以|zhī suǒ yǐ}{能|néng}{流传|liú chuán}{几|jǐ}{百|bǎi}{年|nián}、{几|jǐ}{千|qiān}{年|nián}，{就是|jiù shì}{因为|yīn wèi}{它们|tā men}{用|yòng}{很|hěn}{少|shǎo}{的|de}{字|zì}，{表达|biǎo dá}{了|le}{很|hěn}{丰富|fēng fù}{的|de}{意思|yì si}。{学|xué}{会|huì}{用|yòng}{成语|chéng yǔ}，{你|nǐ}{的|de}{汉语|Hàn yǔ}{会|huì}{更|gèng}{生动|shēng dòng}，{也|yě}{更|gèng}{地道|dì dao}。{不过|bú guò}，{用|yòng}{成语|chéng yǔ}{也|yě}{要|yào}{注意|zhù yì}{场合|chǎng hé}，{不|bù}{懂|dǒng}{的|de}{成语|chéng yǔ}{千万|qiān wàn}{别|bié}{乱用|luàn yòng}，{不然|bù rán}{就|jiù}{成|chéng}{了|le}{画蛇添足|huà shé tiān zú}。

{校园|xiào yuán}: campus. {摆满|bǎi mǎn}: to be laid out all over. {成语接龙|chéng yǔ jiē lóng} chéng yǔ jiē lóng: the idiom chain game ({接|jiē}{龙|lóng}, to
continue a chain). {不知不觉|bù zhī bù jué}: without noticing (an idiom). {祝福|zhù fú}: good wishes. {一辈子|yí bèi zi}: a whole lifetime. {尝|cháng}: to taste. {之所以|zhī suǒ yǐ}…
{是|shì}{因为|yīn wèi}…: the reason why… is that… (written). {场合|chǎng hé} chǎng hé: an occasion, a context (HSK 6). {乱用|luàn yòng}: to misuse.

1. What is the text's main point?
2. Why does the school notice use {丰富多彩|fēng fù duō cǎi}?
3. What does the grandmother mean by {酸甜苦辣|suān tián kǔ là}{都|dōu}{尝|cháng}{过|guo}{了|le}?

<details>
<summary>Answers and translation</summary>

1. Idioms aren't only for books: we use them every day, because they say a lot in a few characters;
   but they should be used with care.
2. It's more formal and more concise than saying "lots of interesting activities".
3. That she has been through every kind of experience in her life, good and bad.

"**Idioms in everyday life.** Many people think idioms only appear in books, but in fact we use
them every day. In the morning you open your phone and the news says: 'This year every trade and
profession is using artificial intelligence.' {各行各业|gè háng gè yè} here means 'all industries': lots of people say
it, and listeners understand it at once. At school, the notice at the gate says: 'A rich programme
of campus activities will be held this weekend; all students are welcome.' The notice uses {丰富多彩|fēng fù duō cǎi},
which is more formal and more concise than 'lots of interesting activities'. At lunchtime you go to
a florist's, full of flowers of every colour. The woman selling flowers says: 'My daughter's getting
married next month and we've invited lots of friends and relatives.' See: a few ordinary sentences with
two idioms in them. Passing the park in the afternoon, you see some children playing the idiom chain game: the first says an idiom, the next has to start a new idiom with its last character, and whoever can't think of one loses. The children laugh as they think, and have a great time; without noticing it, they've learned several more idioms. In the evening a friend is flying abroad to study. Everyone says goodbye at the
airport, and the last thing they say is sure to be '{一路顺风|yí lù shùn fēng}!' Those four characters carry
everyone's good wishes. Back home, Grandma is telling stories of when she was young. She says: 'In
my life I've tasted every flavour, sour, sweet, bitter and hot.' Four characters sum up decades of
experience. Some idioms have a story behind them, like 'drawing feet on a snake' and 'waiting by the stump for a hare': once you know the story, you're less likely to use the idiom wrongly. The reason idioms have been handed down for hundreds and thousands of years is that they
express a great deal in very few characters. Learn to use them and your Chinese will be livelier and
more natural. But watch the occasion when you use them, and never use one you don't understand:
otherwise you'll be adding feet to the snake."
</details>

## Key points

- A {成语|chéng yǔ}: fixed form, usually four characters, a meaning beyond the parts, often classical grammar and a
  source ({出处|chū chù}).
- Shapes: mirrored pairs ({五颜六色|wǔ yán liù sè}, {各行各业|gè háng gè yè}, {亲朋好友|qīn péng hǎo yǒu}, {丰富多彩|fēng fù duō cǎi}, {酸甜苦辣|suān tián kǔ là}), two verb phrases ({守株待兔|shǒu zhū dài tù}, {画蛇添足|huà shé tiān zú}), a
  short sentence ({一路顺风|yí lù shùn fēng}).
- In a sentence: predicate, attributive with {的|de}, subject or object, a judgment ({就是|jiù shì}…{了|le}), a whole wish ({祝|zhù}{你|nǐ}{一路顺风|yí lù shùn fēng}).
  No {很|hěn} before them; don't over-use them.
- Check what an idiom is said of and whether it praises or blames.

lessons.title: City and countryside
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

Module 5 turns from people to the society around them: towns and villages, nature, safety and the
law, the media, and the traditions that hold it all together. This lesson is about places: where
people live, how a city works, and how the countryside is changing. You'll learn to:

- describe change with {随着|suí zhe} (review: HSK 4 met it), {进一步|jìn yí bù} (further) and {逐步|zhú bù} (step by step);
- say where things are in written style: {位于|wèi yú} (to be located at) and {距|jù} (at a distance of), beside
  spoken {在|zài} and {离|lí};
- give directions along a road or a river with {沿|yán} / {沿|yán}{着|zhe} and {顺|shùn}{着|zhe};
- talk about towns and villages: {城区|chéng qū}, {社区|shè qū}, {居民|jū mín}, {胡同|hú tòng}, {乡村|xiāng cūn}, {山区|shān qū}, {设施|shè shī}, {发达|fā dá}, {繁荣|fán róng}, {穷|qióng}, and the
  family of "building" words {建|jiàn}, {建设|jiàn shè}, {建造|jiàn zào}, {修建|xiū jiàn}, {建筑|jiàn zhù}.

At the end you'll read a piece by Wang Fang about her grandfather's village, then and now, and give
your own opinion: would you rather live in a city or in the countryside?

## {随着|suí zhe}: as… changes, so…

HSK 4 taught {随着|suí zhe} (along with, as): it links a change that is going on to a second change that
follows from it. At this level you'll meet it at the start of almost every text about society:

{随着|suí zhe}{城市|chéng shì}{的|de}{发展|fā zhǎn}，{越|yuè}{来|lái}{越|yuè}{多|duō}{的|de}{人|rén}{从|cóng}{乡村|xiāng cūn}{搬|bān}{到|dào}{了|le}{城区|chéng qū}。 — As the city has grown, more and more people have
moved from the countryside into the urban districts.

{随着|suí zhe}{人口|rén kǒu}{的|de}{增加|zēng jiā}，{这个|zhè ge}{社区|shè qū}{的|de}{设施|shè shī}{也|yě}{逐步|zhú bù}{改善|gǎi shàn}{了|le}。 — As the population has grown, the neighbourhood's
facilities have gradually been improved too.

Three things make a {随着|suí zhe} sentence work:

- **What follows {随着|suí zhe} is a change, written as a noun phrase**: {随着|suí zhe}{经济|jīng jì}{的|de}{发展|fā zhǎn}, {随着|suí zhe}{年龄|nián líng}{的|de}{增长|zēng zhǎng}, {随着|suí zhe}{交通|jiāo tōng}{的|de}{改善|gǎi shàn}
  (as transport improves). The pattern is very often {随着|suí zhe} + X + {的|de} + a two-syllable verb of change
  ({发展|fā zhǎn}, {变化|biàn huà}, {增加|zēng jiā}, {提高|tí gāo}, {改善|gǎi shàn}).
- **The second clause changes too**, and usually says so with {越|yuè}{来|lái}{越|yuè}, {也|yě}, {逐步|zhú bù}, {进一步|jìn yí bù} or {了|le}:
  {随着|suí zhe}{天气|tiān qì}{变|biàn}{冷|lěng}，{来|lái}{公园|gōng yuán}{的|de}{人|rén}{越|yuè}{来|lái}{越|yuè}{少|shǎo}。 (As the weather turns cold, fewer and fewer people come to the park.)
- **A single moment usually doesn't fit.** {随着|suí zhe} is for something that goes on over time. For one moment, use
  {一|yī}…{就|jiù} or {以后|yǐ hòu}: {他|tā}{来|lái}{了|le}{以后|yǐ hòu}，{大家|dà jiā}{都|dōu}{很|hěn}{高兴|gāo xìng} (after he came, everyone was happy), not ×{随着|suí zhe}{他|tā}{来|lái}{了|le}. News does write {随着|suí zhe}{地铁|dì tiě}{的|de}{开通|kāi tōng}…: the opening
  is one event, but it starts a change that goes on.

{随着|suí zhe} is at home in writing and in careful speech (news, reports, a talk). In a chat people more often
say {现在|xiàn zài}……{了|le} or {越|yuè}{来|lái}{越|yuè}: {现在|xiàn zài}{城|chéng}{里|lǐ}{的|de}{车|chē}{越|yuè}{来|lái}{越|yuè}{多了|duō le}。

## {进一步|jìn yí bù}: further

{进一步|jìn yí bù} (literally "go forward one step") is an adverb meaning "further, to a further degree". It
goes before a verb, almost always a two-syllable one:

{我们|wǒ men}{想|xiǎng}{进一步|jìn yí bù}{了解|liǎo jiě}{当地|dāng dì}{居民|jū mín}{的|de}{生活|shēng huó}。 — We'd like to learn more about the residents' lives.

{公交车|gōng jiāo chē}{开通|kāi tōng}{以后|yǐ hòu}，{村|cūn}{里|lǐ}{的|de}{交通|jiāo tōng}{进一步|jìn yí bù}{改善|gǎi shàn}{了|le}。 — Once the bus started running, transport in the village
improved further.

It can also be an adjective before {的|de} + a noun: {进一步|jìn yí bù}{的|de}{研究|yán jiū} (further research), {进一步|jìn yí bù}{的|de}{消息|xiāo xi} (further
news). Mind the tones: {一|yī} is yí before {步|bù} bù (fourth tone), so it is said jìn yí bù. In notices you'll
often see {进一步|jìn yí bù} + {加强|jiā qiáng} / {推动|tuī dòng} / {促进|cù jìn}: {进一步|jìn yí bù}{推动|tuī dòng}{社区|shè qū}{建设|jiàn shè} (to further push forward the building of the
community).

## {逐步|zhú bù}: step by step

{逐步|zhú bù} ({逐|zhú} "one after another" + {步|bù} "step") is "step by step, gradually", for change that **someone
carries out in stages**, usually by plan:

{学校|xué xiào}{逐步|zhú bù}{改善|gǎi shàn}{了|le}{学生|xué sheng}{宿舍|sù shè}{的|de}{设施|shè shī}。 — The school improved the dorms' facilities step by step.

{这|zhè}{条|tiáo}{铁路|tiě lù}{会|huì}{逐步|zhú bù}{开放|kāi fàng}{给|gěi}{公众|gōng zhòng}{使用|shǐ yòng}。 — This railway will open to the public in stages.

You know {渐渐|jiàn jiàn} (gradually, HSK 5 lesson 17), and lesson 22 brings {逐渐|zhú jiàn}. The difference is who's doing
it:

| Word | Used for | Example |
|---|---|---|
| {逐步|zhú bù} | deliberate change in planned steps | {城市|chéng shì}{逐步|zhú bù}{建设|jiàn shè}{了|le}{地下|dì xià}{铁路|tiě lù}。 The city built its underground railway in stages. |
| {逐渐|zhú jiàn} | change that happens by itself, little by little (lesson 22) | {天气|tiān qì}{逐渐|zhú jiàn}{变|biàn}{冷|lěng}{了|le}。 The weather slowly got colder. |
| {渐渐|jiàn jiàn} | the same, a little more spoken and descriptive | {天|tiān}{渐渐|jiàn jiàn}{黑|hēi}{了|le}。 It slowly got dark. |

So the weather can {逐渐|zhú jiàn} change, but not {逐步|zhú bù}: nobody plans it.

## {沿|yán} / {沿|yán}{着|zhe} and {顺|shùn}{着|zhe}: along

{沿|yán}{着|zhe} + a road, river or wall + a verb of movement means "along": you follow the line of something.

{沿|yán}{着|zhe}{这|zhè}{条|tiáo}{河|hé}{往|wǎng}{东|dōng}{走|zǒu}，{十|shí}{分钟|fēn zhōng}{就|jiù}{到|dào}{了|le}。 — Walk east along this river and you'll be there in ten minutes.

{我们|wǒ men}{沿|yán}{着|zhe}{胡同|hú tòng}{走|zǒu}{了|le}{一|yì}{圈|quān}。 — We walked all the way round the hutong.

{沿|yán} alone is the written form, common in fixed phrases: {沿|yán}{河|hé} (along the river), {沿|yán}{路|lù} (along the
road), {沿|yán}{街|jiē} (along the street). {沿|yán}{街|jiē}{的|de}{房屋|fáng wū} are the buildings lining the street.

{顺|shùn}{着|zhe} ({顺|shùn} "in the same direction as, smooth") is very close: "following, along". It suits things you
follow naturally, like a flow or a slope: {顺|shùn}{着|zhe}{这|zhè}{条|tiáo}{路|lù}{一直|yì zhí}{走|zǒu} (follow this road straight on), {水|shuǐ}{顺|shùn}{着|zhe}{墙|qiáng}{流|liú}{下来|xià lái}
(water ran down the wall). For directions, {沿|yán}{着|zhe} and {顺|shùn}{着|zhe} are both fine. {顺|shùn} alone is also "smooth, going
well": {今天|jīn tiān}{的|de}{工作|gōng zuò}{很|hěn}{顺|shùn} (work went smoothly today), and you'll meet {一路顺风|yí lù shùn fēng} (have a good trip) in lesson
29.

## {位于|wèi yú} and {距|jù}: where something is, in writing

Notices, guidebooks and reports say where a place is with two written verbs:

- {位于|wèi yú} + place: "is located at / in". {这个|zhè ge}{村子|cūn zi}{位于|wèi yú}{山区|shān qū}。 (The village is in the mountains.) {广场|guǎng chǎng}{位于|wèi yú}
  {城区|chéng qū}{中心|zhōng xīn}。 (The square is in the centre of the urban district.)
- {距|jù} + place + distance: "is … away from". {村子|cūn zi}{距|jù}{市中心|shì zhōng xīn}80{公里|gōng lǐ}。 (The village is 80 kilometres from
  the city centre.) {距|jù} is the written short form of {距离|jù lí} (HSK 4).

In speech you'd say the same with {在|zài} and {离|lí}: {这个|zhè ge}{村子|cūn zi}{在|zài}{山|shān}{里|lǐ}，{离|lí}{市中心|shì zhōng xīn}80{公里|gōng lǐ}。 {位于|wèi yú} and {距|jù} in a chat
sound stiff, like saying "is situated" to a friend.

| Written | Spoken | Example (written) |
|---|---|---|
| {位于|wèi yú} | {在|zài} | {博物馆|bó wù guǎn}{位于|wèi yú}{广场|guǎng chǎng}{北边|běi bian}。 The museum is on the north side of the square. |
| {距|jù} | {离|lí} | {酒店|jiǔ diàn}{距|jù}{火车站|huǒ chē zhàn}{两|liǎng}{公里|gōng lǐ}。 The hotel is two kilometres from the station. |

### Stroke order

- **{繁|fán}**: top half first ({敏|mǐn}: its left part, then 攵), then 糸 below: its two turning strokes, the
  dot, the vertical hook, then a short left-falling stroke and a dot. 17 strokes.
- **{胡|hú}**: {古|gǔ} first (horizontal, vertical, then {口|kǒu}), then {月|yuè} on the right.
- **{挤|jǐ}**: 扌 first (horizontal, vertical hook, rising stroke), then {齐|qí}: dot, horizontal,
  left-falling, right-falling, then its two lower strokes, left-falling before vertical.
- **{群|qún}**: {君|jūn} first, including its long left-falling stroke, and {羊|yáng}'s long vertical last.
- **{穷|qióng}**, **{窄|zhǎi}**: 穴 on top first (a dot, a short left dot, the horizontal hook, then a short
  left-falling stroke and a dot under it), then the part below.
- **{逐|zhú}**: 豕 first, 辶 last, as in every character with 辶.

"**My grandfather's village.** My grandfather lives in a small village in the south. The
village is in the mountains, more than 100 kilometres from the nearest city. When I was little, my
mother took me back to the village for a few weeks every summer holiday.

"In those days the village was poor. There was only one dirt road, and whenever it rained it was
hard going. To get to the city you first walked for half an hour, then took a bus that ran only
twice a day. Most of the houses were old and small, and very cold in winter. Many young people went
off to work in the city, and those left in the village were mostly the old and the children.

"In recent years, as transport has developed, the village has changed a great deal. First a road
was built, then a bus service started, and now it takes only an hour and a half from the village to
the city. The village has also built a little square, where the old people dance and chat in the
evenings. Lots of families have bought electric bikes, and things bought online arrive in two or
three days.

"The biggest change is in the people. Some young people who had worked elsewhere have come back.
Some have opened small restaurants; some have turned their family homes into guesthouses for visitors
from the city. My grandfather laughs that there used to be empty houses everywhere, and now at the
weekend even the road at the entrance to the village is jammed.

"The village school has changed too. There used to be only thirty-odd pupils, and one teacher
often had to teach several subjects. Now the school has new classrooms, computers and a library, and
teachers from the city come every week. But because many young people have taken their children to
the city, the number of pupils hasn't grown much.

"Of course, not all the changes are good. The village has less farmland, and the field where my
grandfather used to grow maize is a car park now. Sometimes he says the village is getting more and
more like a city, and quiet days are getting fewer and fewer.

"Still, whenever I ask him whether he'd like to move to the city and live with us, he always shakes
his head: 'What's so good about the city? I've lived here for more than seventy years, and I'm not
going anywhere.'"

"I think it's better to live in a city while you're young. First, there are more jobs in cities,
and transport is convenient: the metro takes you anywhere easily. Second, city facilities are more
complete: seeing a doctor, going to school and shopping don't involve long trips. Of course cities
have their downsides, such as too many people, jammed roads and packed metro trains. The countryside

**A picture story.** The exam's first writing task gives four pictures to turn into a story of at
least 100 characters (as reported). Here the pictures are described in words. Write 100–150
characters, using at least three of {堵|dǔ}, {挤|jǐ}, {沿|yán}{着|zhe}, {步行|bù xíng}.

1. Monday morning: a young man drives to work; the road is jammed, and he looks at his watch.
2. Tuesday: he takes the metro; the carriage is packed and he can hardly move.
3. Wednesday: he cycles along a river in the sunshine.
4. He arrives at the office first; his colleagues are surprised.

<details>
<summary>A model story</summary>

{小张|Xiǎo Zhāng}{每天|měi tiān}{开车|kāi chē}{上班|shàng bān}。{星期|xīng qī}{一|yī}{早上|zǎo shang}，{路上|lù shang}{堵|dǔ}{得|de}{很|hěn}，{一|yí}{个|gè}{小时|xiǎo shí}{只|zhǐ}{走|zǒu}{了|le}{几|jǐ}{公里|gōng lǐ}，{他|tā}{到|dào}{公司|gōng sī}{的|de}{时候|shí hou}{已经|yǐ jīng}{迟到|chí dào}{了|le}。{星期|xīng qī}{二|èr}{他|tā}{改|gǎi}{坐|zuò}{地铁|dì tiě}，
{可是|kě shì}{地铁|dì tiě}{里|lǐ}{挤|jǐ}{得|de}{要命|yào mìng}，{他|tā}{连|lián}{手机|shǒu jī}{都|dōu}{拿|ná}{不|bu}{出来|chū lái}。{星期|xīng qī}{三|sān}，{他|tā}{决定|jué dìng}{骑|qí}{自行车|zì xíng chē}。{他|tā}{沿|yán}{着|zhe}{河边|hé biān}{慢慢|màn màn}{骑|qí}，{阳光|yáng guāng}{很|hěn}{好|hǎo}，{空气|kōng qì}{也|yě}{很|hěn}{新鲜|xīn xiān}。
{没|méi}{想|xiǎng}{到|dào}，{那|nà}{天|tiān}{他|tā}{第|dì}{一|yī}{个|gè}{到|dào}{了|le}{公司|gōng sī}。{同事|tóng shì}{们|men}{都|dōu}{很|hěn}{吃惊|chī jīng}，{问|wèn}{他|tā}{是|shì}{怎么|zěn me}{做|zuò}{到|dào}{的|de}。

"Xiao Zhang drives to work every day. On Monday morning the roads were completely jammed: in an hour
he covered only a few kilometres, and he was late by the time he got to the office. On Tuesday he
took the metro instead, but it was so packed that he couldn't even get his phone out. On Wednesday
he decided to cycle. He rode slowly along the river; the sun was out and the air was fresh. To his
surprise, he was the first to arrive at the office that day. His colleagues were amazed and asked
him how he'd done it."

({挤|jǐ}{得|de}{要命|yào mìng}: packed to death, a spoken degree complement; {新鲜|xīn xiān}: fresh, HSK 3; {没|méi}{想|xiǎng}{到|dào}: unexpectedly.)
</details>

**An essay.** Write 200–300 characters on {我|wǒ}{住|zhù}{的|de}{地方|dì fang}{的|de}{变化|biàn huà} (how the place I live has changed). Plan
it in three parts: how it was, what changed and why ({随着|suí zhe}…), and what you think of the change.

<details>
<summary>A model essay and a checklist</summary>

{我|wǒ}{住|zhù}{在|zài}{一|yí}{个|gè}{中等|zhōng děng}{城市|chéng shì}，{这|zhè}{几|jǐ}{年|nián}{它|tā}{的|de}{变化|biàn huà}{非常|fēi cháng}{大|dà}。{十|shí}{年|nián}{前|qián}，{城|chéng}{里|lǐ}{只有|zhǐ yǒu}{几|jǐ}{条|tiáo}{主要|zhǔ yào}{的|de}{路|lù}，{一|yí}{到|dào}{下班|xià bān}{时间|shí jiān}{就|jiù}{堵车|dǔ chē}。{城区|chéng qū}{很|hěn}{小|xiǎo}，{晚上|wǎn shang}{八|bā}{点|diǎn}{以后|yǐ hòu}
{街|jiē}{上|shàng}{就|jiù}{没|méi}{什么|shén me}{人|rén}{了|le}。

{随着|suí zhe}{经济|jīng jì}{的|de}{发展|fā zhǎn}，{城市|chéng shì}{逐步|zhú bù}{建设|jiàn shè}{了|le}{地铁|dì tiě}，{还|hái}{修建|xiū jiàn}{了|le}{一|yí}{个|gè}{很|hěn}{大|dà}{的|de}{公园|gōng yuán}。{现在|xiàn zài}{我|wǒ}{从|cóng}{家|jiā}{里|lǐ}{步行|bù xíng}{五|wǔ}{分钟|fēn zhōng}{就|jiù}{能|néng}{坐|zuò}{上|shàng}{地铁|dì tiě}，{去|qù}{市中心|shì zhōng xīn}{只要|zhǐ yào}
{二十|èr shí}{分钟|fēn zhōng}。{新|xīn}{城区|chéng qū}{有|yǒu}{了|le}{图书馆|tú shū guǎn}、{体育馆|tǐ yù guǎn}{和|hé}{很|hěn}{多|duō}{商场|shāng chǎng}，{周末|zhōu mò}{四处|sì chù}{都|dōu}{是|shì}{人|rén}，{非常|fēi cháng}{热闹|rè nao}。

{我|wǒ}{觉得|jué de}{这些|zhè xiē}{变化|biàn huà}{大多|dà duō}{是|shì}{好|hǎo}{的|de}，{生活|shēng huó}{比|bǐ}{以前|yǐ qián}{便利|biàn lì}{多了|duō le}。{不过|bú guò}，{老|lǎo}{城区|chéng qū}{的|de}{一些|yì xiē}{老|lǎo}{房子|fáng zi}{被|bèi}{拆|chāi}{了|le}，{我|wǒ}{小时候|xiǎo shí hou}{常|cháng}{去|qù}{的|de}{那|nà}{家|jiā}{小|xiǎo}{饭馆|fàn guǎn}{也|yě}{没有|méi yǒu}{了|le}。
{我|wǒ}{希望|xī wàng}{城市|chéng shì}{在|zài}{进一步|jìn yí bù}{发展|fā zhǎn}{的|de}{同时|tóng shí}，{也|yě}{能|néng}{保留|bǎo liú}{一些|yì xiē}{老|lǎo}{的|de}{东西|dōng xi}。

"I live in a medium-sized city, and it has changed enormously in the last few years. Ten years ago
there were only a few main roads, and they jammed every evening rush hour. The urban area was small,
and after eight in the evening there was hardly anyone in the streets. As the economy has grown, the
city has built a metro in stages and laid out a very large park. Now I can walk five minutes from my
home and get on the metro, and it's only twenty minutes to the centre. The new districts have a
library, a sports hall and lots of malls; at weekends there are people everywhere, and it's very
lively. I think most of these changes are good: life is much more convenient than before. But some
old houses in the old town have been pulled down, and the little restaurant I used to go to as a
child has gone. I hope that as the city develops further, it can also keep some of the old things."

{中等|zhōng děng}: medium (HSK 6); {主要|zhǔ yào}: main (HSK 3); {拆|chāi} (lesson 09): to pull down; {保留|bǎo liú}: to keep (lesson 25);
{在|zài}…{的|de}{同时|tóng shí}: while…, at the same time as.

Checklist:
- **Structure**: three paragraphs: then, the change and its cause, your view.
- **Connectors**: {随着|suí zhe}, {现在|xiàn zài}, {不过|bú guò}, {我|wǒ}{希望|xī wàng}…; one {逐步|zhú bù} or {进一步|jìn yí bù}.
- **Register**: a personal essay can use {我|wǒ}{觉得|jué de} and {非常|fēi cháng}; keep {位于|wèi yú} and {距|jù} for a description.
- **Length**: count your characters (about 250 here).
</details>

## Say it

```speak
# Places and change
{随着|suí zhe}{城市|chéng shì}{的|de}{发展|fā zhǎn}，{越|yuè}{来|lái}{越|yuè}{多|duō}{的|de}{人|rén}{搬|bān}{到|dào}{了|le}{城区|chéng qū}。
= As the city has grown, more and more people have moved into the urban districts.
{这个|zhè ge}{村子|cūn zi}{位于|wèi yú}{山区|shān qū}，{距|jù}{市中心|shì zhōng xīn}80{公里|gōng lǐ}。
= The village is in the mountains, 80 kilometres from the city centre.
{沿|yán}{着|zhe}{这|zhè}{条|tiáo}{河|hé}{往|wǎng}{东|dōng}{走|zǒu}，{十|shí}{分钟|fēn zhōng}{就|jiù}{到|dào}{了|le}。
= Walk east along the river and you'll be there in ten minutes.
{胡同|hú tòng}{太|tài}{窄|zhǎi}，{车|chē}{开|kāi}{不|bu}{进去|jìn qù}。
= The hutong is too narrow for a car to get in.
{我们|wǒ men}{想|xiǎng}{进一步|jìn yí bù}{了解|liǎo jiě}{当地|dāng dì}{居民|jū mín}{的|de}{生活|shēng huó}。
= We'd like to learn more about the residents' lives.
{学校|xué xiào}{逐步|zhú bù}{改善|gǎi shàn}{了|le}{宿舍|sù shè}{的|de}{设施|shè shī}。
= The school improved the dorms' facilities step by step.
```

## Pronunciation

- {窄|zhǎi} zhǎi (narrow, third tone) and {摘|zhāi} zhāi (to pick, lesson 22, first tone): same syllable, different
  tone.
- {沿|yán} yán (second tone) sounds just like {盐|yán} yán (salt) and {言|yán} (speech): context tells them apart.
- {进一步|jìn yí bù} jìn yí bù: {一|yī} rises before the fourth tone of {步|bù}. Said fast it's almost jìn yi bù.
- {居民|jū mín} jū mín, {居住|jū zhù} jū zhù: *ju* is jü, with rounded lips (the dots on ü are dropped after j).
- {穷|qióng} qióng: *q* + *iong*, a rising tone. Don't let it slide into *chong*.
- {繁荣|fán róng} fán róng: the *r* of {荣|róng} is close to the *s* in "pleasure".
- {胡同|hú tòng} hú tòng: in Beijing you'll hear hútòngr or hútong; the course writes hú tòng.

## Common mistakes

- ~~{随着|suí zhe}{他|tā}{来|lái}{了|le}，{大家|dà jiā}{都|dōu}{很|hěn}{高兴|gāo xìng}~~: {随着|suí zhe} needs a process, not one event: {他|tā}{来|lái}{了|le}{以后|yǐ hòu}，{大家|dà jiā}{都|dōu}{很|hěn}{高兴|gāo xìng}. With a
  real change it works: {随着|suí zhe}{时间|shí jiān}{的|de}{变化|biàn huà}…, {随着|suí zhe}{年龄|nián líng}{的|de}{增长|zēng zhǎng}….
- {天气|tiān qì}{逐步|zhú bù}{变|biàn}{冷|lěng} sounds wrong: {逐步|zhú bù} is for planned steps someone takes. The weather changes {逐渐|zhú jiàn} (by
  itself): {天气|tiān qì}{逐渐|zhú jiàn}{变|biàn}{冷|lěng}{了|le}.
- {改善|gǎi shàn}{汉语|Hàn yǔ}: {改善|gǎi shàn} is for poor conditions ({生活|shēng huó}, {环境|huán jìng}, {交通|jiāo tōng}). A skill is improved with {提高|tí gāo}:
  {提高|tí gāo}{汉语|Hàn yǔ}{水平|shuǐ píng}.
- {当地|dāng dì} for "here": a local in their own town says {我|wǒ}{是|shì}{本地|běn dì}{人|rén}; {当地|dāng dì} refers to the place being talked about
  ({当地|dāng dì}{居民|jū mín}, the residents there).
- {位于|wèi yú} and {距|jù} in a chat aren't wrong, but they sound stiff. Say {在|zài} and {离|lí} to a friend: {我|wǒ}{家|jiā}{离|lí}{这儿|zhèr}{不|bù}{远|yuǎn}.
- ~~{我|wǒ}{沿|yán}{着|zhe}{河|hé}~~ alone: {沿|yán}{着|zhe} needs a verb of movement after the place: {我|wǒ}{沿|yán}{着|zhe}{河|hé}{走|zǒu} / {跑|pǎo} / {骑车|qí chē}.

## Key points

- {随着|suí zhe} + change (often X {的|de} + {发展|fā zhǎn} / {变化|biàn huà} / {增加|zēng jiā})，second clause with {越|yuè}{来|lái}{越|yuè} / {也|yě} / {逐步|zhú bù} / {了|le}: "as…, so…".
- {进一步|jìn yí bù} + two-syllable verb: further (jìn yí bù). {逐步|zhú bù}: in planned steps; {逐渐|zhú jiàn} (lesson 22): little
  by little, by itself.
- {沿|yán}{着|zhe} / {顺|shùn}{着|zhe} + route + verb of movement: along; written {沿|yán} in {沿|yán}{河|hé}, {沿|yán}{街|jiē}.
- Written {位于|wèi yú} (= {在|zài}) and {距|jù} (= {离|lí}) for locations in notices and reports.
- {本地|běn dì} (here) vs {当地|dāng dì} (there, the place in question); {建|jiàn} / {建造|jiàn zào} / {修建|xiū jiàn} / {建设|jiàn shè} / {建筑|jiàn zhù} each with its own
  objects; {改善|gǎi shàn} conditions, {提高|tí gāo} skills.
- New characters: {繁|fán} {荣|róng} {胡|hú} {挤|jǐ} {筑|zhù} {欧|ōu} {群|qún} {施|shī} {穷|qióng} {沿|yán} {窄|zhǎi} {逐|zhú}; {胡|hú} and {挤|jǐ} are handwriting characters.

The words from this lesson are listed below; they join your vocabulary reviews when you complete
the lesson.

lessons.title: Nature and the land
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

Lesson 21 looked at the places people build. This one goes outside them: land and water, plants and
animals, and the way the natural world changes. It's the vocabulary of every popular-science text
and nature documentary, and of the exam's expository reading passages. You'll learn:

- {朝|cháo} (towards; facing): {朝|cháo}{南|nán}{的|de}{房间|fáng jiān}, {他|tā}{朝|cháo}{我|wǒ}{走|zǒu}{过来|guò lái}, and how it differs from {向|xiàng} and {往|wǎng};
- {逐渐|zhú jiàn} (gradually), the natural change beside lesson 21's planned {逐步|zhú bù};
- three measure words: {颗|kē} for small round things, {根|gēn} for long thin ones, {群|qún} for groups;
- words for the land ({陆地|lù dì}, {沙漠|shā mò}, {河流|hé liú}, {湖|hú}), for living things ({种子|zhǒng zi}, {果实|guǒ shí}, {昆虫|kūn chóng}, {蝴蝶|hú dié}, {翅膀|chì bǎng}, {尾巴|wěi ba}) and for
  how nature changes ({形成|xíng chéng}, {分布|fēn bù}, {生长|shēng zhǎng}, {生存|shēng cún}, {消失|xiāo shī}, {破坏|pò huài});
- words for shape and light: {圆|yuán}, {平|píng}, {直|zhí}, {弯|wān}, {斜|xié}, {浅|qiǎn}, {暗|àn}, {模糊|mó hu}, {形状|xíng zhuàng}, {光线|guāng xiàn}.

The reading is an expository text on deserts in five paragraphs, written so that its order follows
from its linking words: the exam's paragraph-ordering task.

## {朝|cháo}: towards, facing

{朝|cháo} marks the direction something faces or moves towards. It's a preposition before a verb, and
a verb of its own in "to face":

{这个|zhè ge}{房间|fáng jiān}{朝|cháo}{南|nán}，{阳光|yáng guāng}{很|hěn}{好|hǎo}。 — The room faces south: it gets plenty of sun.

{他|tā}{朝|cháo}{我|wǒ}{走|zǒu}{了|le}{过来|guò lái}。 — He walked towards me.

{她|tā}{朝|cháo}{窗|chuāng}{外|wài}{看|kàn}{了|le}{一|yì}{眼|yǎn}。 — She glanced out of the window.

You know two other words for direction: {往|wǎng} (HSK 2) and {向|xiàng} (HSK 3). They overlap, but not
completely:

| | {朝|cháo} | {向|xiàng} | {往|wǎng} |
|---|---|---|---|
| a direction + movement | {朝|cháo}{前|qián}{走|zǒu} ✓ | {向|xiàng}{前|qián}{走|zǒu} ✓ | {往|wǎng}{前|qián}{走|zǒu} ✓ |
| facing, a body action (look, smile, wave) | {朝|cháo}{他|tā}{笑|xiào}{了|le}{笑|xiào} ✓ | {向|xiàng}{他|tā}{笑|xiào}{了|le}{笑|xiào} ✓ | ✗ |
| as a verb: to face | {大|dà}{门|mén}{朝|cháo}{南|nán} ✓ | (written: {面向|miàn xiàng}) | ✗ |
| a person in an abstract sense (learn from, ask for) | ✗ | {向|xiàng}{他|tā}{学习|xué xí} ✓ | ✗ |
| after the verb | ✗ | {走|zǒu}{向|xiàng}{未来|wèi lái}, {飞|fēi}{向|xiàng}{南方|nán fāng} (written) | {开|kāi}{往|wǎng}{上海|Shàng hǎi} (of trains, buses) |

So {朝|cháo} is concrete: a physical direction or the way someone is facing. "Learn from him" is {向|xiàng}{他|tā}{学习|xué xí}, not
×{朝|cháo}{他|tā}{学习|xué xí}. And only {向|xiàng} and {往|wǎng} can follow a verb: {这|zhè}{趟|tàng}{车|chē}{开|kāi}{往|wǎng}{上海|Shàng hǎi} (this train is bound for Shanghai).

Two more useful {朝|cháo} phrases: {朝|cháo}{南|nán} / {朝|cháo}{北|běi} (facing south / north, of rooms and houses, a selling point in
northern China, where south-facing rooms are warmer and brighter) and {朝|cháo}{着|zhe} (towards, for a goal):
{朝|cháo}{着|zhe}{目标|mù biāo}{努力|nǔ lì} (work towards a goal).

## {逐渐|zhú jiàn}: little by little

{逐渐|zhú jiàn} is "gradually", for change that happens by itself, without a plan, in small steps:

{天|tiān}{逐渐|zhú jiàn}{暗|àn}{了|le}{下来|xià lái}。 — It slowly grew dark.

{随着|suí zhe}{气温|qì wēn}{升|shēng}{高|gāo}，{河|hé}{里|lǐ}{的|de}{冰|bīng}{逐渐|zhú jiàn}{消失|xiāo shī}{了|le}。 — As the temperature rose, the ice on the river gradually
disappeared.

{这些|zhè xiē}{石头|shí tou}{经过|jīng guò}{几|jǐ}{万|wàn}{年|nián}，{逐渐|zhú jiàn}{形成|xíng chéng}{了|le}{现在|xiàn zài}{的|de}{形状|xíng zhuàng}。 — Over tens of thousands of years these rocks gradually took
their present shape.

With lesson 21's {逐步|zhú bù} and lesson 17's {渐渐|jiàn jiàn} you now have three words for "gradually":

| | Who's doing it? | Register | Example |
|---|---|---|---|
| {逐步|zhú bù} | people, by plan, in stages | written, formal | {学校|xué xiào}{逐步|zhú bù}{改善|gǎi shàn}{了|le}{设施|shè shī}。 |
| {逐渐|zhú jiàn} | nobody: it just happens | neutral, common in writing | {天气|tiān qì}{逐渐|zhú jiàn}{变|biàn}{冷|lěng}{了|le}。 |
| {渐渐|jiàn jiàn} | nobody: it just happens | a little more spoken, descriptive | {他|tā}{渐渐|jiàn jiàn}{习惯|xí guàn}{了|le}{这里|zhè lǐ}{的|de}{生活|shēng huó}。 |

{逐渐|zhú jiàn} and {渐渐|jiàn jiàn} are nearly the same; {渐渐|jiàn jiàn} can also stand at the head of a sentence with {地|de} ({渐渐|jiàn jiàn}{地|de}，{天|tiān}{黑|hēi}{了|le}),
which suits stories. In a report or a science text, {逐渐|zhú jiàn} is the usual choice.

## {颗|kē}, {根|gēn}, {群|qún}: three measure words

Chinese counts things by their shape. These three are among the most common:

| Measure word | Used for | Examples |
|---|---|---|
| {颗|kē} | small, round things | {一|yì}{颗|kē}{种子|zhǒng zi} (a seed), {一|yì}{颗|kē}{星星|xīng xing} (a star), {一|yì}{颗|kē}{牙|yá} (a tooth), {一|yì}{颗|kē}{糖|táng} (a sweet), {一|yì}{颗|kē}{心|xīn} (a heart) |
| {根|gēn} | long, thin things | {一|yì}{根|gēn}{竹子|zhú zi} (a bamboo cane), {一|yì}{根|gēn}{头发|tóu fa} (a hair), {一|yì}{根|gēn}{针|zhēn} (a needle), {一|yì}{根|gēn}{绳子|shéng zi} (a rope) |
| {群|qún} | groups, crowds, flocks | {一|yì}{群|qún}{人|rén}, {一|yì}{群|qún}{孩子|hái zi}, {一|yì}{群|qún}{鸭子|yā zi} (a flock of ducks), {一|yì}{群|qún}{羊|yáng} |

- {颗|kē} and {棵|kē} (HSK 4, for trees) are the same syllable, kē, and look alike: {颗|kē} has {页|yè} (a head: round things), {棵|kē} has {木|mù} (wood: trees). {一|yì}{棵|kē}{树|shù} but {一|yì}{颗|kē}{种子|zhǒng zi}.
- {根|gēn} is also a noun: "root" ({树|shù}{根|gēn}, the roots of a tree), and in {根本|gēn běn} (lesson 13: basically; at all).

**The land.** {陆地|lù dì} (land, as against sea) and {海洋|hǎi yáng} (ocean, HSK 4). {沙漠|shā mò} (desert) and {沙子|shā zi} (sand), {石头|shí tou}

**Plants.** {种子|zhǒng zi} (seed) → {生长|shēng zhǎng} (to grow) → {果实|guǒ shí} (fruit, of a plant). {种植|zhòng zhí} (to plant, grow: crops, trees)

### Two new radicals: {虫|chóng} and {羽|yǔ}

- **{虫|chóng} (insect, worm, small creature)** is a radical you'll see in the names of animals that crawl,
  fly or wriggle. It's on the left of {蝴|hú} and {蝶|dié} (a butterfly is two {虫|chóng} characters), on its own in
  {虫子|chóng zi} and {昆虫|kūn chóng}, and underneath in {蛋|dàn} (egg, HSK 1) and {虽|suī} ({虽然|suī rán}, HSK 2, where it no longer gives the
  meaning). Lesson 25 adds {蛇|shé} (snake). In traditional characters "insect" is {+{虫|chóng}+}, three {虫|chóng} together;
  as a radical ({蝴|hú}, {蝶|dié}, {蛋|dàn}) {虫|chóng} is the same in both scripts.
- **{羽|yǔ} (feather)** you met as a character in {羽毛球|yǔ máo qiú} (HSK 3). As a radical it's in {翻|fān} (to turn over,
  {翻译|fān yì}, HSK 4) and now {翅|chì} (wing, with {支|zhī} zhī). Feathers and wings belong together.

### Families and look-alikes

- **{胡|hú}'s sound family, complete.** Lesson 21 promised it: {湖|hú} hú (氵: water), {蝴|hú} hú ({虫|chóng}), {糊|hú} hú ({米|mǐ}: rice
  paste, "blurred" in {模糊|mó hu}). Three characters, one sound part.
- **{莫|mò} mò**: the sound part of {漠|mò} mò ({沙漠|shā mò}), and of {模|mó} mó (lesson 04's {模式|mó shì}), {摸|mō} mō (lesson 09) and {幕|mù} mù
  (lesson 02's {屏幕|píng mù}). Water + {莫|mò}: {沙漠|shā mò} is a desert of sand.
- **{然|rán} and {燃|rán}.** The 《{说文解字|Shuō wén jiě zì}》 explains {然|rán} as "to burn" (fire 灬 at the bottom). When {然|rán} came to be used
  for "so, like this" ({然后|rán hòu}, {当然|dāng rán}), a second {火|huǒ} was added on the left to write "burn": {燃|rán}. So {燃|rán} has fire
  twice: {火|huǒ} and 灬.
- **{戋|jiān} in {浅|qiǎn}.** The right side of {浅|qiǎn} qiǎn is also in {钱|qián} qián (money) and {践|jiàn} jiàn ({实践|shí jiàn}): a sound part,
  now only roughly.
- **{同|tóng} in {洞|dòng}.** {洞|dòng} dòng is 氵 + {同|tóng} tóng: water, and a sound part that has shifted.
- **{果|guǒ} in {颗|kē}.** {果|guǒ} guǒ is on the left of {颗|kē} kē, and on the right of {课|kè} kè and {棵|kē} kē: an old sound part in all three.
- **{石|shí} as a radical**: {破|pò} (to break), {研|yán} ({研究|yán jiū}), {础|chǔ} ({基础|jī chǔ}), {确|què} ({确实|què shí}), {碎|suì} (lesson 09) all have {石|shí} on the
  left, squeezed so that its {撇|piě} is short.
- **{晒|shài} = {日|rì} + {西|xī}**: the sun, and {西|xī} (the west). A memory aid: things dry in the afternoon sun from the
  west. Traditional {+{晒|shài}+} is {日|rì} + {+{丽|lì}+}, quite different.
- **{暗|àn} = {日|rì} + {音|yīn}**, **{昆|kūn} = {日|rì} + {比|bǐ}**: {日|rì} on the left of {暗|àn}, on top of {昆|kūn}.
- **{震|zhèn} = {雨|yǔ} + 辰** chén, a sound part (as in {振|zhèn} zhèn). The 《{说文解字|Shuō wén jiě zì}》 explains {震|zhèn} as a thunderclap that
  shakes things: hence the rain on top.
- **{朝|cháo} has two readings**: cháo (towards; a dynasty: {唐朝|Táng cháo}, the Tang dynasty) and zhāo (morning, in
  written phrases such as {朝夕|zhāo xī}, morning and evening). In this course it's cháo.

### Stroke order

- **{虫|chóng}**: {口|kǒu}-like box first (vertical, horizontal-turn, horizontal), then the long vertical through
  it, then the bottom stroke, and the dot on the right last.
- **{布|bù}**, **{石|shí}**: horizontal first, then the left-falling stroke, then what's under them.
- **{湖|hú}**: 氵 (dot, dot, rising stroke), then {古|gǔ}, then {月|yuè}.
- **{陆|lù}**: 阝 first (one turning stroke and a vertical), then the right side: two horizontals, the
  long vertical, then the turning stroke and the short vertical of the bottom.
- **{晒|shài}**: {日|rì} first, then {西|xī}: its top horizontal, then the box with its two strokes inside, and the
  bottom horizontal last.
- **{燃|rán}**: {火|huǒ} on the left, then {然|rán}: {夕|xī}-like part, {犬|quǎn}, and the four dots of 灬 last. 16 strokes.

1. What is the text mainly about?
2. Why do some places become deserts?
3. How do desert plants keep their water?
4. Paragraph 3 begins {不过|bú guò} and paragraph 5 begins {然而|rán ér}. What does each of them turn against?

<details>
<summary>Answers and translation</summary>

1. That deserts, though very dry, are full of life that has adapted to them, and that human activity
   can spread them.
2. Lack of water: they're too far from the sea for moist air to reach them, or mountains block the
   moist air; over time the land dries out, plants disappear, and wind and heat and cold wear rock into sand.
3. Some have tiny, needle-like leaves so water doesn't escape; some have very long roots that reach
   deep underground for water.
4. {不过|bú guò} turns against paragraph 2's picture of land drying out and plants disappearing: "but a desert
   isn't lifeless". {然而|rán ér} turns against paragraphs 3–4's picture of a desert full of life: "however,
   people are making deserts bigger". Each one points back to the paragraph before it, which is how
   you can put the paragraphs in order.

"**Life in the desert.** When people think of deserts, many picture endless sand, fierce sunshine and
dry air. Deserts are indeed the driest places on earth: some get only a few showers of rain a year.
Deserts are widespread: there are large deserts on the land of Africa, Asia, the Americas and
Australia.

"How do deserts form? Mainly through lack of water. Some places are too far from the sea for air
carrying moisture to reach them; others are surrounded by high mountains, and the moist air is
blocked by them. In deserts the temperature changes a great deal between day and night: often over
forty degrees by day, it can fall below ten at night. Over time the land gets drier and drier, plants gradually disappear, and the wind
and the change between heat and cold slowly turn rock into sand.

"But a desert isn't a place without life. To survive, many plants have grown into special shapes:
some have very small leaves, like needles, so water doesn't escape easily; some have very long roots
that reach deep underground to find water. After a shower of rain, seeds that have been sleeping
grow quickly, flower and bear fruit.

"Besides plants, deserts have quite a few animals. In the daytime the sun makes the ground very hot,
so many insects and small animals hide in holes or under stones, and come out to look for food only
in the evening, when it cools down. One large animal, the camel, can go several days without
drinking, so people have long relied on it to carry things across the desert. Some small animals hardly drink
at all: they get the water their bodies need from the plants and seeds they eat.

"However, as human activity increases, deserts in some regions are slowly growing. When trees are
cut down and grass is damaged, the land gradually turns into desert. So taking care of trees and
grassland and saving water matter a great deal for protecting the land around deserts. In some places people have planted many
trees along the edge of the desert to hold back the wind and sand."
</details>
