hadn't brought raincoats, our clothes were soon wet through, and we had to shelter under a big rock.
After about half an hour the rain stopped and the sun came out again, and a rainbow appeared over the
distant hills. This taught me that nature is beautiful and also hard to predict. From now on, before
going to the mountains, I'll always check the weather forecast and take an extra layer."

{叫声|jiào shēng}: a call, a cry; {脚步声|jiǎo bù shēng}: footsteps ({脚步|jiǎo bù}, lesson 06); {山顶|shān dǐng} (HSK 6): the summit; {天空|tiān kōng} (lesson 29): the sky; {彩虹|cǎi hóng} (cǎi hóng): a rainbow; {预测|yù cè} (lesson 28): to
predict; {天气预报|tiān qì yù bào} ({预报|yù bào}, lesson 29): the weather forecast.

Checklist:
- **Structure**: setting, what happened (a turn: {可是|kě shì}…{突然|tū rán}), what you learned.
- **Connectors**: {那|nà}{天|tiān}, {中午|zhōng wǔ}, {接着|jiē zhe}, {大概|dà gài}{过|guò}{了|le}…, {以后|yǐ hòu}; one {逐渐|zhú jiàn}.
- **Description**: two senses at least (sight and sound); shapes and light ({浅|qiǎn}, {暗|àn}).
- **Register**: a personal narrative: spoken words are fine; {沿|yán}{着|zhe} and {登|dēng}{上|shàng} add a little polish.
</details>

## Say it

```speak
# Nature words in sentences
{这个|zhè ge}{房间|fáng jiān}{朝|cháo}{南|nán}，{阳光|yáng guāng}{很|hěn}{好|hǎo}。
= This room faces south: it gets plenty of sun.
{天|tiān}{逐渐|zhú jiàn}{暗|àn}{了|le}{下来|xià lái}。
= It slowly grew dark.
{天上|tiān shàng}{有|yǒu}{无数|wú shù}{颗|kē}{星星|xīng xing}。
= There are countless stars in the sky.
{湖|hú}{边|biān}{有|yǒu}{一|yì}{群|qún}{鸭子|yā zi}。
= There's a flock of ducks by the lake.
{竹子|zhú zi}{生长|shēng zhǎng}{得|de}{很|hěn}{快|kuài}。
= Bamboo grows fast.
{没有|méi yǒu}{水|shuǐ}，{植物|zhí wù}{就|jiù}{无法|wú fǎ}{生存|shēng cún}。
= Without water, plants can't survive.
```

## Pronunciation

- {朝|cháo} cháo (towards) has a rising tone; the same character is zhāo in {朝夕|zhāo xī} (morning and evening). {潮|cháo}
  cháo (tide; damp) sounds like {朝|cháo}.
- {颗|kē} kē (round things) and {棵|kē} kē (trees) are the same syllable: only the radical tells them apart.
- {湿|shī} shī (wet), {石|shí} shí (stone), {使|shǐ} shǐ, {是|shì} shì: the four tones on shi.
- {蝴蝶|hú dié} hú dié: rising, rising. The *ie* of dié is like "ye" in "yes".
- {模糊|mó hu} mó hu: the second syllable is light. {糊|hú} is hú on its own (paste), as in {胡|hú} hú.
- {划|huá} huá (to row) rises; in {计划|jì huà} (HSK 4) the character is huà.
- {昆虫|kūn chóng} kūn chóng, {虫子|chóng zi} chóng zi: *ch* + *ong*, rising; not *zhong*.

## Common mistakes

- ~~{朝|cháo}{他|tā}{学习|xué xí}~~: {朝|cháo} is only for physical direction. Learning from someone is {向|xiàng}{他|tā}{学习|xué xí}.
- ~~{一|yì}{棵|kē}{种子|zhǒng zi}~~: trees take {棵|kē}, seeds take {颗|kē}: {一|yì}{颗|kē}{种子|zhǒng zi}, {一|yì}{棵|kē}{树|shù}.
- {天气|tiān qì}{逐步|zhú bù}{变|biàn}{冷|lěng} sounds wrong (lesson 21): nature changes {逐渐|zhú jiàn} or {渐渐|jiàn jiàn}, not {逐步|zhú bù}.
- {这个|zhè ge}{房间|fáng jiān}{朝|cháo}{着|zhe}{南|nán} sounds unnatural: for which way a room faces, say {朝|cháo}{南|nán} (no {着|zhe}). {朝|cháo}{着|zhe} is "towards" a moving goal:
  {朝|cháo}{着|zhe}{门口|mén kǒu}{走|zǒu}{去|qù}.
- {衣服|yī fu}{很|hěn}{湿|shī}{了|le} is fine but {衣服|yī fu}{湿|shī}{了|le} is what people say: {湿|shī} changes state with {了|le}. "Wet through" is {湿透|shī tòu}{了|le}.
- {燃烧|rán shāo} in a chat sounds like a textbook: {木头|mù tou}{烧|shāo}{起来|qǐ lái}{了|le} (the wood caught fire) is the everyday way.

## Key points

- {朝|cháo} + direction / person + verb: towards (concrete only); {朝|cháo}{南|nán}: facing south. {向|xiàng} can be abstract ({向|xiàng}{他|tā}{学习|xué xí})
  and can follow a verb; {往|wǎng} can follow verbs of travel ({开|kāi}{往|wǎng}{上海|Shàng hǎi}).
- {逐渐|zhú jiàn}: gradual change by itself; {逐步|zhú bù}: planned stages; {渐渐|jiàn jiàn}: like {逐渐|zhú jiàn}, a little more spoken.
- {颗|kē} (small round things), {根|gēn} (long thin things), {群|qún} (groups); {度|dù} for degrees.
- Shape and light: {圆|yuán} {平|píng} {直|zhí} {弯|wān} {斜|xié} {浅|qiǎn} {暗|àn} {模糊|mó hu} {形状|xíng zhuàng} {光线|guāng xiàn}; change: {形成|xíng chéng} {分布|fēn bù} {生长|shēng zhǎng} {生存|shēng cún} {消失|xiāo shī} {破坏|pò huài}.
- New radicals: {虫|chóng} ({蝴|hú} {蝶|dié} {虫|chóng}, and {蛋|dàn} {虽|suī}) and {羽|yǔ} ({羽|yǔ} {翻|fān} {翅|chì}).
- New characters: {翅|chì} {膀|bǎng} {虫|chóng} {朝|cháo} {暗|àn} {洞|dòng} {震|zhèn} {布|bù} {湖|hú} {蝴|hú} {蝶|dié} {昆|kūn} {陆|lù} {糊|hú} {颗|kē} {漠|mò} {燃|rán} {晒|shài} {浅|qiǎn} {石|shí}; ✎ {虫|chóng} {布|bù} {湖|hú} {陆|lù} {晒|shài} {石|shí}.

The words from this lesson are listed below; they join your vocabulary reviews when you complete
the lesson.

lessons.title: Accidents, safety and the law
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

Accidents happen, and when they do, two kinds of Chinese come into play: what you say on the spot
({小心|xiǎo xīn}！{糟糕|zāo gāo}！) and what gets written down afterwards (a notice, a police record, a rule). This lesson
teaches both. You'll learn:

- **{没有|méi yǒu}…{就|jiù}{没有|méi yǒu}** (without… there would be no…), a strong statement of what something depends on;
- **{不|bù}…{不|bù}…**: {不见不散|bú jiàn bú sàn} (we won't leave till we've met) and {不|bù}{冷|lěng}{不|bú}{热|rè} (neither hot nor cold);
- {造成|zào chéng} and {导致|dǎo zhì} for bad results, beside {引起|yǐn qǐ} and {使|shǐ};
- {一旦|yí dàn}…{就|jiù} again (lesson 03), now for emergencies;
- the language of rules: {不得|bù dé}, {禁止|jìn zhǐ}, {严禁|yán jìn}, {请勿|qǐng wù}, {此处|cǐ chù}, {违者|wéi zhě};
- words for accidents ({事故|shì gù}, {车祸|chē huò}, {撞|zhuàng}, {冲|chōng}, {滑|huá}, {倒|dǎo} dǎo), traffic ({驾驶|jià shǐ}, {车辆|chē liàng}, {超速|chāo sù}, {安全带|ān quán dài}), safety ({措施|cuò shī},
  {确保|què bǎo}, {保安|bǎo ān}) and the law ({法院|fǎ yuàn}, {合法|hé fǎ}, {违法|wéi fǎ}, {遵守|zūn shǒu}, {罚款|fá kuǎn}, {派出所|pài chū suǒ}).

The reading follows one small accident from the notice that warned about it to the record the
police wrote, and the speaking task asks you to tell a story from three photos.

## {没有|méi yǒu}…{就|jiù}{没有|méi yǒu}…: without X, no Y

{没有|méi yǒu} + A，{就|jiù}{没有|méi yǒu} + B says that B depends entirely on A: take A away and B is gone too. It's the
**{没有|méi yǒu}…{就|jiù}{没有|méi yǒu}** pattern, a favourite of speeches, slogans and thank-you notes:

{没有|méi yǒu}{大家|dà jiā}{的|de}{帮助|bāng zhù}，{就|jiù}{没有|méi yǒu}{今天|jīn tiān}{的|de}{成功|chéng gōng}。 — Without everyone's help, today's success wouldn't have
happened.

{没有|méi yǒu}{安全|ān quán}，{就|jiù}{没有|méi yǒu}{一切|yí qiè}。 — Without safety, there's nothing. (a safety slogan)

{没有|méi yǒu}{老师|lǎo shī}{的|de}{鼓励|gǔ lì}，{我|wǒ}{就|jiù}{没有|méi yǒu}{学|xué}{下去|xià qù}{的|de}{勇气|yǒng qì}。 — Without my teacher's encouragement, I wouldn't have had the
courage to keep studying.

- Both halves usually have a noun phrase after {没有|méi yǒu}; the second is often "today's…, this…" ({今天|jīn tiān}{的|de}{我|wǒ},
  {这|zhè}{次|cì}{的|de}{成功|chéng gōng}): what exists now.
- With a subject in the second half, {就|jiù} goes after it: {没有|méi yǒu}{你|nǐ}，{我|wǒ}{就|jiù}{没有|méi yǒu}{勇气|yǒng qì}.
- It's stronger than {如果|rú guǒ}{没有|méi yǒu}…{就|jiù}{不|bú}{会|huì}…: it presents A as the condition for B, not just a supposition.
  Compare {如果|rú guǒ}{没有|méi yǒu}{你|nǐ}{的|de}{帮助|bāng zhù}，{我|wǒ}{就|jiù}{不|bú}{会|huì}{成功|chéng gōng} (if you hadn't helped, I wouldn't have succeeded), a plain
  condition.

## {不|bù}…{不|bù}…: two patterns

**1. {不|bù} A {不|bù} B: unless A, not B.** Two verbs, each negated, make a condition: "if not A, then not
B". The famous one is a promise to meet:

{明天|míng tiān}{下午|xià wǔ}{三|sān}{点|diǎn}，{学校|xué xiào}{门口|mén kǒu}，{不见不散|bú jiàn bú sàn}！ — Three tomorrow afternoon at the school gate: we won't leave till
we've met!

{这|zhè}{件|jiàn}{事|shì}{你|nǐ}{不|bù}{说|shuō}{不行|bù xíng}。 — You have to tell them about this. (not telling won't do)

{他|tā}{这个|zhè ge}{人|rén}，{不|bú}{到|dào}{最后|zuì hòu}{不|bú}{放弃|fàng qì}。 — He's someone who never gives up till the very end.

**2. {不|bù} A {不|bù} B: neither A nor B, just right.** With two opposite adjectives, {不|bù}…{不|bù}… means "neither
too… nor too…": the happy middle.

{今天|jīn tiān}{的|de}{天气|tiān qì}{不|bù}{冷|lěng}{不|bú}{热|rè}，{正好|zhèng hǎo}{出去|chū qù}{走走|zǒu zou}。 — It's neither cold nor hot today: just right for a walk.

{这|zhè}{双|shuāng}{鞋|xié}{不|bú}{大|dà}{不|bù}{小|xiǎo}，{正|zhèng}{合适|hé shì}。 — These shoes are neither too big nor too small: they fit perfectly.

{他|tā}{来|lái}{得|de}{不|bù}{早|zǎo}{不|bù}{晚|wǎn}，{刚好|gāng hǎo}{赶上|gǎn shàng}。 — He came neither early nor late: just in time.

Both are the **{不|bù}…{不|bù}…** pattern. Tell them apart by what goes in: two verbs ({见|jiàn} / {散|sàn}, {说|shuō} / {行|xíng}) make a
condition; two opposite adjectives ({冷|lěng} / {热|rè}, {大|dà} / {小|xiǎo}) make "just right". Mind {不|bù}'s tone: bú before a
fourth tone ({不见不散|bú jiàn bú sàn} bú jiàn bú sàn, {不|bú}{大|dà}{不|bù}{小|xiǎo} bú dà bù xiǎo), bù before the others ({不|bù}{冷|lěng}{不|bú}{热|rè} bù lěng bú
rè).

## {造成|zào chéng} and {导致|dǎo zhì}: bad results

Both mean "to cause, to lead to", and both usually bring bad news:

| Verb | Typical objects | Register | Example |
|---|---|---|---|
| {造成|zào chéng} | {损失|sǔn shī}, {事故|shì gù}, {影响|yǐng xiǎng}, {伤害|shāng hài}, {后果|hòu guǒ} | neutral; very common | {大|dà}{雨|yǔ}{造成|zào chéng}{了|le}{很|hěn}{大|dà}{的|de}{损失|sǔn shī}。 The heavy rain caused great losses. |
| {导致|dǎo zhì} | a result, often a whole clause | written, a little formal | {超速|chāo sù}{导致|dǎo zhì}{了|le}{这|zhè}{次|cì}{车祸|chē huò}。 Speeding led to this accident. |
| {引起|yǐn qǐ} (HSK 4) | {注意|zhù yì}, {兴趣|xìng qù}, {问题|wèn tí} | neutral; good or bad | {这个|zhè ge}{问题|wèn tí}{引起|yǐn qǐ}{了|le}{大家|dà jiā}{的|de}{注意|zhù yì}。 |
| {使|shǐ} (HSK 4) | person + feeling or change | written | {这|zhè}{次|cì}{经历|jīng lì}{使|shǐ}{他|tā}{更|gèng}{小心|xiǎo xīn}{了|le}。 |

- {造成|zào chéng} takes a noun: {造成|zào chéng}{损失|sǔn shī}, {造成|zào chéng}{交通堵塞|jiāo tōng dǔ sè} (a traffic jam). {导致|dǎo zhì} can take a clause: {路面|lù miàn}{太|tài}{滑|huá}，{导致|dǎo zhì}{很|hěn}{多|duō}{车辆|chē liàng}
  {无法|wú fǎ}{通行|tōng xíng} (the road was so slippery that many vehicles couldn't get through).
- For good results, use {带来|dài lái} (to bring) or {使|shǐ}: {新|xīn}{的|de}{地铁|dì tiě}{给|gěi}{市民|shì mín}{带来|dài lái}{了|le}{很|hěn}{大|dà}{的|de}{方便|fāng biàn}. ×{造成|zào chéng}{了|le}{方便|fāng biàn} sounds odd.

## {一旦|yí dàn}…{就|jiù}: once, if ever

Lesson 03 taught {一旦|yí dàn}…{就|jiù} (once…, if ever…). It's at home in safety notices, where it introduces
something you hope won't happen:

{一旦|yí dàn}{发生|fā shēng}{火灾|huǒ zāi}，{请|qǐng}{马上|mǎ shàng}{离开|lí kāi}{大楼|dà lóu}。 — In the event of a fire, leave the building at once.

{一旦|yí dàn}{发现|fā xiàn}{自己|zì jǐ}{违反|wéi fǎn}{了|le}{规则|guī zé}，{就|jiù}{应该|yīng gāi}{马上|mǎ shàng}{改正|gǎi zhèng}。 — Once you realise you've broken a rule, you should put it right
at once.

{如果|rú guǒ} is any supposition; {一旦|yí dàn} is "the moment it happens", usually something serious or final. {火灾|huǒ zāi}
(huǒ zāi, HSK 6) is a fire, a blaze.

## The language of rules

Signs and notices have their own short, written forms. Here they are beside what you'd say:

| Written | Meaning | Spoken | Example |
|---|---|---|---|
| {不得|bù dé} | must not (rules) | {不|bù}{能|néng} / {不|bù}{可以|kě yǐ} | {车辆|chē liàng}{不得|bù dé}{停放|tíng fàng}{在|zài}{此处|cǐ chù}。 Vehicles may not park here. |
| {禁止|jìn zhǐ} (HSK 4) | it is forbidden to | {不许|bù xǔ} / {别|bié} | {禁止|jìn zhǐ}{吸|xī}{烟|yān} No smoking |
| {严禁|yán jìn} (HSK 6) | strictly forbidden | {绝对|jué duì}{不|bù}{能|néng} | {严禁|yán jìn}{超速|chāo sù} Speeding strictly prohibited |
| {请勿|qǐng wù} | please do not | {请|qǐng}{不要|bú yào} | {请勿|qǐng wù}{靠近|kào jìn} Please keep away |
| {此处|cǐ chù} | here, this place | {这儿|zhèr} | {此处|cǐ chù}{禁止|jìn zhǐ}{通行|tōng xíng} No entry here |
| {违者|wéi zhě} | offenders, anyone who breaks this | {不|bù}{遵守|zūn shǒu}{的|de}{人|rén} | {违者|wéi zhě}{罚款|fá kuǎn}200{元|yuán} Offenders fined 200 yuan |

- {不得|bù dé} is the rule-book "must not": it's not the same as {不得不|bù dé bù} (HSK 4, "have to"): {不得|bù dé}{停车|tíng chē} (no
  parking) but {我|wǒ}{不得不|bù dé bù}{停车|tíng chē} (I had to stop).
- {请勿|qǐng wù} uses {勿|wù}, the classical "don't", which you met in the Analects (HSK 4 30h2).
- {此|cǐ} (HSK 4) is the written {这|zhè}: {此处|cǐ chù} (here), {此时|cǐ shí} (at this moment, lesson 27).
- {处|chù} chù is "place; office": {此处|cǐ chù} (here), {办事处|bàn shì chù} (a branch office), {售票处|shòu piào chù} (a ticket office). A local
  police station is a {所|suǒ}: {派出所|pài chū suǒ}. The same character is chǔ in {处理|chǔ lǐ} and {相处|xiāng chǔ} (lesson 11).

## Accidents and traffic

| Word | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| {事故|shì gù} | accident (traffic, work) | {交通|jiāo tōng}{事故|shì gù} (a traffic accident) |
| {车祸|chē huò} | car crash, road accident | {他|tā}{在|zài}{一|yí}{次|cì}{车祸|chē huò}{中|zhōng}{受|shòu}{了|le}{伤|shāng}。 He was hurt in a road accident. |
| {意外|yì wài} | an accident; unexpected | {发生|fā shēng}{了|le}{意外|yì wài} (something unexpected happened); {这个|zhè ge}{消息|xiāo xi}{很|hěn}{意外|yì wài} |
| {撞|zhuàng} | to bump into, crash into | {一|yí}{辆|liàng}{车|chē}{撞|zhuàng}{到|dào}{了|le}{树|shù}{上|shàng}。 A car crashed into a tree. |
| {冲|chōng} | to rush, charge | {他|tā}{冲|chōng}{了|le}{出去|chū qù}。 He rushed out. |
| {滑|huá} | slippery; to slide | {路|lù}{很|hěn}{滑|huá}，{小心|xiǎo xīn}！ The road's slippery: careful! |
| {倒|dǎo} dǎo | to fall over | {他|tā}{被|bèi}{撞|zhuàng}{倒|dǎo}{了|le}。 He was knocked down. {摔|shuāi}{倒|dǎo} (to fall, trip) |
| {断|duàn} | to break, snap; to cut off | {腿|tuǐ}{断|duàn}{了|le} (a broken leg), {电话|diàn huà}{断|duàn}{了|le} (the line went dead) |
| {沉|chén} | to sink; heavy | {船|chuán}{沉|chén}{了|le} (the boat sank); {这个|zhè ge}{箱子|xiāng zi}{很|hěn}{沉|chén} (this case is heavy) |
| {挡|dǎng} | to block | {一|yí}{辆|liàng}{车|chē}{挡住|dǎng zhù}{了|le}{路|lù}。 A car was blocking the road. |
| {躲|duǒ} | to dodge, hide | {他|tā}{躲|duǒ}{开|kāi}{了|le}{那|nà}{辆|liàng}{车|chē}。 He dodged the car. {躲|duǒ}{雨|yǔ} (shelter from the rain) |
| {车辆|chē liàng} / {车主|chē zhǔ} | vehicles (written) / a car's owner | {车辆|chē liàng}{请|qǐng}{减速|jiǎn sù}{慢行|màn xíng} (vehicles: slow down) |
| {驾驶|jià shǐ} / {驾照|jià zhào} | to drive (written) / driving licence | {驾驶|jià shǐ}{车辆|chē liàng} (to drive a vehicle); {考|kǎo}{驾照|jià zhào} (take the driving test) |
| {行驶|xíng shǐ} | to travel (of a vehicle) | {车辆|chē liàng}{在|zài}{路上|lù shang}{行驶|xíng shǐ} |
| {超速|chāo sù} | to speed | {超速|chāo sù}{是|shì}{违法|wéi fǎ}{的|de} (speeding is illegal) |
| {安全带|ān quán dài} | seat belt | {系|jì}{好|hǎo}{安全带|ān quán dài} (fasten your seat belt, as in lesson 15's {系|jì}{领带|lǐng dài}, to tie a tie) |
| {通行|tōng xíng} | to pass through | {禁止|jìn zhǐ}{通行|tōng xíng} (no thoroughfare) |

### Two new radicals: {鸟|niǎo} and {身|shēn}

- **{鸟|niǎo} (bird)** is on the right of {鸭|yā} (duck) and of {鸡|jī} (chicken, HSK 1), and is a character itself ({鸟|niǎo},

  {隹|zhuī}, another bird radical, instead.
- **{身|shēn} (body)** is on the left of {躺|tǎng} (to lie down, HSK 4) and {躲|duǒ} (to hide: the body tucked away), and
  is the character {身|shēn} ({身体|shēn tǐ}). On the left {身|shēn} is narrower: its long horizontal becomes a rising stroke, and its last
  left-falling stroke stops short.

### Families and look-alikes

- **{朵|duǒ} in {躲|duǒ}.** {躲|duǒ} duǒ is {身|shēn} + {朵|duǒ} duǒ (lesson 15's measure word for flowers): the sound part matches
  exactly.
- **{当|dāng} in {挡|dǎng}.** {挡|dǎng} dǎng is 扌 + {当|dāng} dāng, a sound part (traditional {+{挡|dǎng}+} = 扌 + {+{当|dāng}+}).
- **{加|jiā} in {驾|jià}.** {驾|jià} jià is {加|jiā} jiā over {马|mǎ} (horse): to harness a horse, to drive. {加|jiā} is also the sound part
  of {架|jià} jià (lesson 09) and {嘉|jiā} jiā (lesson 24).
- **{史|shǐ} in {驶|shǐ}.** {驶|shǐ} shǐ is {马|mǎ} + {史|shǐ} shǐ (history): a sound part that matches. Both {驾|jià} and {驶|shǐ} have {马|mǎ}:
  driving began with horses.
- **{呙|guō} in {祸|huò} and {锅|guō}.** The right side of {祸|huò} huò (disaster) is also the right side of {锅|guō} guō (lesson 07's
  wok), and of the traditional {+{过|guo}+}. 礻 (spirits, the gods) is on the left: the 《{说文解字|Shuō wén jiě zì}》 defines {祸|huò} as harm, the gods withholding their
  blessing.
- **{昔|xī} in {措|cuò}.** {措|cuò} cuò sounds just like {错|cuò} cuò (mistake), which has the same right side, {昔|xī}. You know {昔|xī}
  in {借|jiè} (to borrow) and {惜|xī} ({可惜|kě xī}) too.
- **{原|yuán} in {源|yuán}.** {源|yuán} yuán is 氵 + {原|yuán} yuán: water at its source. {原|yuán}'s old meaning is "a spring, a source" (as the
  《{说文解字|Shuō wén jiě zì}》 has it), and {源|yuán} adds 氵 to write that sense apart from {原|yuán} "original".
- **{交|jiāo} in {咬|yǎo}.** {咬|yǎo} yǎo is {口|kǒu} + {交|jiāo} jiāo: a mouth, and a sound part that has drifted.
- **{员|yuán} in {圆|yuán}.** {圆|yuán} yuán is {囗|wéi} + {员|yuán} yuán, exactly the sound of {员|yuán} ({员工|yuán gōng}, {服务员|fú wù yuán}). Traditional {+{圆|yuán}+} = {囗|wéi} + {+{员|yuán}+}.

- **{罚|fá} = 罒 + 讠 + 刂.** The 《{说文解字|Shuō wén jiě zì}》 explains {罚|fá} as a punishment for a lesser offence, made of {刀|dāo} (a

  has {言|yán}.
- **{尾|wěi} = 尸 + {毛|máo}.** 尸 is a body seen from the side, and {毛|máo} (hair) is under its back: the 《{说文解字|Shuō wén jiě zì}》

- **{竹|zhú} as a radical.** On top of a character {竹|zhú} shrinks to ⺮: {笔|bǐ}, {第|dì}, {等|děng}, {简|jiǎn}, {篇|piān}, {管|guǎn}, {算|suàn} and lesson 21's {筑|zhù}.

### Stroke order

- **{冲|chōng}**: 冫 first (a dot, then a rising stroke), then {中|zhōng}: the box, then the vertical through it.
- **{圆|yuán}**: the left side and top of {囗|wéi} first (vertical, then the horizontal-turn), then {员|yuán} inside, and
  the bottom horizontal last, closing the box.
- **{竹|zhú}**: the left half (left-falling, horizontal, vertical), then the right half (left-falling,
  horizontal, vertical hook).
- **{咬|yǎo}**: {口|kǒu} first, then {交|jiāo}: dot, horizontal, then the two short strokes, and the long left-falling and
  right-falling strokes that cross.
- **{挡|dǎng}**: 扌, then {当|dāng}: the short vertical and the two short strokes on top, then the 彐-like part.
- **{躲|duǒ}**: {身|shēn} first (narrowed, as above), then {朵|duǒ}: {几|jǐ} on top, {木|mù} below.
- **{罚|fá}**: 罒 first (a box with two short verticals inside), then 讠, then 刂.

## Reading: from the notice to the police record

Two written texts about the same afternoon, and a chat message. The first is a notice from the management company of
Wang Fang and Anna's compound, posted the day before; the second is the record the traffic police
wrote after the accident (in December 2029, Anna's final year). Places and names are invented. Notice how the written register works: {近日|jìn rì},
{不得|bù dé}, {请勿|qǐng wù}, {一旦|yí dàn}, {某|mǒu}, {由|yóu}, {造成|zào chéng}, {导致|dǎo zhì}.

{其实|qí shí}，{很|hěn}{多|duō}{交通|jiāo tōng}{事故|shì gù}{就是|jiù shì}{这些|zhè xiē}{小|xiǎo}{事|shì}{导致|dǎo zhì}{的|de}。{我|wǒ}{的|de}{一|yí}{个|gè}{同学|tóng xué}{就|jiù}{因为|yīn wèi}{骑车|qí chē}{时|shí}{看|kàn}{手机|shǒu jī}，{撞|zhuàng}{到|dào}{了|le}{路边|lù biān}{的|de}{车|chē}{上|shàng}，{腿|tuǐ}{也|yě}{摔|shuāi}{断|duàn}{了|le}。

{没有|méi yǒu}{安全|ān quán}，{就|jiù}{没有|méi yǒu}{一切|yí qiè}。{规则|guī zé}{不|bú}{是|shì}{为了|wèi le}{限制|xiàn zhì}{我们|wǒ men}，{而|ér}{是|shì}{为了|wèi le}{保护|bǎo hù}{每|měi}{一|yí}{个|gè}{人|rén}。{我|wǒ}{希望|xī wàng}{大家|dà jiā}{都|dōu}{能|néng}{从|cóng}{自己|zì jǐ}{做起|zuò qǐ}，{遵守|zūn shǒu}{交通|jiāo tōng}{规则|guī zé}。

"In cities we often see people crossing on a red light, phoning while driving, or riding electric
bikes without a helmet. Why do some people not keep the traffic rules? I think there are three main
reasons. First, many people are in a hurry and feel a minute at a red light is a waste of time.
Second, some people think they're lucky: 'Other people have accidents, not me.' Third, some people
don't know how much harm this behaviour does. In fact, many traffic accidents are caused by small
things like these. A classmate of mine crashed into a parked car because he was looking at his
phone while cycling, and broke his leg. Without safety, there's nothing. Rules aren't there to limit
us, but to protect everyone. I hope we can all start with ourselves and keep the traffic rules."

{赶时间|gǎn shí jiān}: to be in a hurry; {运气|yùn qi} (lesson 25): luck; {出事|chū shì}: to have an accident; {从|cóng}{自己|zì jǐ}{做起|zuò qǐ}: to start with oneself.

Checklist:
- **Structure**: the problem, three reasons ({第|dì}{一|yī}…{第|dì}{二|èr}…{第|dì}{三|sān}), an example, your view.
- **Connectors**: {为什么|wèi shén me}…{呢|ne}？, {其实|qí shí}, {就|jiù}{因为|yīn wèi}…, {不|bú}{是|shì}…{而|ér}{是|shì} (HSK 4); one {没有|méi yǒu}…{就|jiù}{没有|méi yǒu}.
- **Register**: an essay: {我|wǒ}{觉得|jué de} is fine; use {导致|dǎo zhì}, {危害|wēi hài}, {行为|xíng wéi} for the serious points.
- **Length**: about 260 characters.
</details>

## Say it

```speak
# Safety and rules
{没有|méi yǒu}{安全|ān quán}，{就|jiù}{没有|méi yǒu}{一切|yí qiè}。
= Without safety, there's nothing.
{明天|míng tiān}{三|sān}{点|diǎn}，{学校|xué xiào}{门口|mén kǒu}，{不见不散|bú jiàn bú sàn}！
= Three o'clock tomorrow at the school gate: we won't leave till we've met!
{今天|jīn tiān}{不|bù}{冷|lěng}{不|bú}{热|rè}，{正好|zhèng hǎo}{出去|chū qù}{走走|zǒu zou}。
= It's neither cold nor hot today: just right for a walk.
{超速|chāo sù}{导致|dǎo zhì}{了|le}{这|zhè}{次|cì}{车祸|chē huò}。
= Speeding led to this accident.
{一旦|yí dàn}{发生|fā shēng}{火灾|huǒ zāi}，{请|qǐng}{马上|mǎ shàng}{离开|lí kāi}{大楼|dà lóu}。
= In the event of a fire, leave the building at once.
{车辆|chē liàng}{不得|bù dé}{停放|tíng fàng}{在|zài}{此处|cǐ chù}。
= Vehicles may not park here.
```

## Pronunciation

- {倒|dǎo} dǎo (to fall over) dips; HSK 4's {倒|dào} dào (to pour) falls. {摔|shuāi}{倒|dǎo} shuāi dǎo, {倒|dào}{水|shuǐ} dào shuǐ.
- {处|chù} chù (place, office) falls; {处|chǔ} chǔ ({处理|chǔ lǐ}, {相处|xiāng chǔ}) dips.
- {冲|chōng} chōng: high and level, with *ch* + *ong*. Don't say *zhōng* ({中|zhōng}) or *chóng* ({虫|chóng}).
- {驾驶|jià shǐ} jià shǐ: {驶|shǐ} has *sh*, like {史|shǐ} shǐ, its sound part.
- {车祸|chē huò} chē huò, {措施|cuò shī} cuò shī: *cuo* has a *ts* sound; *shi* in {施|shī} is first tone, high.
- {罚款|fá kuǎn} fá kuǎn: {罚|fá} rises; {发|fā} fā (to send) is level.
- {不见不散|bú jiàn bú sàn} bú jiàn bú sàn: both {不|bù} rise before the falling tones.
- {遵守|zūn shǒu} zūn shǒu, {违反|wéi fǎn} wéi fǎn: {违|wéi} rises (wéi), like {为|wéi} in {成为|chéng wéi}.

## Common mistakes

- ~~{没有|méi yǒu}{你|nǐ}{的|de}{帮助|bāng zhù}，{我|wǒ}{就|jiù}{不|bù}{有|yǒu}{今天|jīn tiān}~~: the second half is {没有|méi yǒu} too: {没有|méi yǒu}{你|nǐ}{的|de}{帮助|bāng zhù}，{就|jiù}{没有|méi yǒu}{今天|jīn tiān}{的|de}{我|wǒ}. {不|bù}{有|yǒu} is never
  Chinese.
- {造成|zào chéng}{了|le}{方便|fāng biàn} sounds wrong: {造成|zào chéng} and {导致|dǎo zhì} bring bad results. Good ones: {带来|dài lái}{了|le}{方便|fāng biàn}, {使|shǐ}{生活|shēng huó}{更|gèng}{方便|fāng biàn}.
- {不得不|bù dé bù}{停车|tíng chē} means "had to stop", not "no parking": {不得不|bù dé bù} is "have to". The sign says {不得|bù dé}{停车|tíng chē} or
  {禁止|jìn zhǐ}{停车|tíng chē}.
- {他|tā}{被|bèi}{撞|zhuàng}{倒|dǎo}{了|le} (he was knocked down) is the natural form: {倒|dǎo} is already the result. {倒|dǎo}{下|xià} is "to fall down"
  on its own: {他|tā}{倒|dǎo}{下|xià}{了|le}.
- {冲咖啡|chōng kā fēi} (to make coffee) is everyday Chinese, but in traditional characters this {冲|chōng} is a different
  character from "rush": see the character notes.
- {赔|péi} is "to pay for damage", not "to pay" for goods: {修|xiū}{车|chē}{的|de}{钱|qián}{他|tā}{来|lái}{赔|péi} (he'll pay for the repair) but {付|fù}{钱|qián}
  (to pay) at a shop.

## Key points

- {没有|méi yǒu} A，{就|jiù}{没有|méi yǒu} B: B depends on A entirely ({没有|méi yǒu}{安全|ān quán}，{就|jiù}{没有|méi yǒu}{一切|yí qiè}).
- {不|bù} A {不|bù} B: unless A, not B ({不见不散|bú jiàn bú sàn}, {不|bù}{说|shuō}{不行|bù xíng}); with opposite adjectives, "just right" ({不|bù}{冷|lěng}{不|bú}{热|rè}, {不|bú}{大|dà}{不|bù}{小|xiǎo}).
- {造成|zào chéng} + bad noun; {导致|dǎo zhì} + bad result or clause (written); good results with {带来|dài lái} or {使|shǐ}.
- {一旦|yí dàn}…{就|jiù}: in case of, once (something serious) happens.
- Rules: {不得|bù dé} (must not), {禁止|jìn zhǐ} / {严禁|yán jìn} (forbidden), {请勿|qǐng wù} (please don't), {此处|cǐ chù} (here), {违者|wéi zhě} (offenders).
- {倒|dǎo} dǎo (fall over) vs dào (pour); {处|chù} chù (place, office) vs chǔ ({处理|chǔ lǐ}).
- New radicals: {鸟|niǎo} ({鸡|jī} {鸟|niǎo} {鸭|yā}), {身|shēn} ({身|shēn} {躺|tǎng} {躲|duǒ}).
- New characters: {尾|wěi} {威|wēi} {胁|xié} {湿|shī} {弯|wān} {鸭|yā} {咬|yǎo} {斜|xié} {圆|yuán} {竹|zhú} {源|yuán} {摘|zhāi} {祸|huò} {冲|chōng} {措|cuò} {挡|dǎng} {躲|duǒ} {罚|fá} {驾|jià} {驶|shǐ}; ✎ {咬|yǎo} {圆|yuán} {竹|zhú} {冲|chōng} {挡|dǎng}.

The words from this lesson are listed below; they join your vocabulary reviews when you complete
the lesson.

lessons.title: News, media and society
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

Wang Fang is a reporter now, and this is her lesson: how news is gathered, written and passed on,
and the words for the society it reports on. News Chinese is the most written Chinese you'll meet
every day, and the exam's listening and reading parts are full of it. You'll learn:

- to say where information comes from: {据说|jù shuō}, {据|jù}…{报道|bào dào}, {据|jù}{了解|liǎo jiě}, {据|jù}{统计|tǒng jì};
- three adverbs that news stories love: {陆续|lù xù} (one after another), {纷纷|fēn fēn} (one after another, all of
  them) and {即将|jí jiāng} (about to);
- the measure words {册|cè} (volumes, copies) and {集|jí} (episodes);
- the verbs of publishing, each with its own object: {发表|fā biǎo}, {发布|fā bù}, {公布|gōng bù}, {宣布|xuān bù}, {宣传|xuān chuán}, {出版|chū bǎn}, {印刷|yìn shuā};
- media words ({媒体|méi tǐ}, {采访|cǎi fǎng}, {报道|bào dào}, {现场|xiàn chǎng}, {嘉宾|jiā bīn}, {纪录片|jì lù piàn}) and society words ({人民|rén mín}, {老百姓|lǎo bǎi xìng}, {农民|nóng mín}, {农业|nóng yè}, {工业|gōng yè}, {政府|zhèng fǔ},
  {省|shěng}, {县|xiàn}, {乡|xiāng}).

You'll read a news report Wang Fang wrote, hear the interview behind it, and retell a short news
story, the first task of the speaking exam.

## {据|jù}: according to

{据|jù} (HSK 5's preposition, the written form of {根据|gēn jù}) introduces the source of what you're reporting:

| Phrase | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| {据说|jù shuō} | it is said, they say | {据说|jù shuō}{这|zhè}{部|bù}{电影|diàn yǐng}{是|shì}{根据|gēn jù}{真实|zhēn shí}{的|de}{事件|shì jiàn}{拍|pāi}{的|de}。 They say the film is based on a true story. |
| {据|jù}…{报道|bào dào} | according to … reports | {据|jù}{当地|dāng dì}{媒体|méi tǐ}{报道|bào dào}，{大|dà}{雨|yǔ}{造成|zào chéng}{了|le}{很|hěn}{大|dà}{的|de}{损失|sǔn shī}。 According to local media, the heavy rain caused serious losses. |
| {据|jù}{了解|liǎo jiě} | we understand, it is learnt | {据|jù}{了解|liǎo jiě}，{这个|zhè ge}{活动|huó dòng}{已经|yǐ jīng}{办|bàn}{了|le}{五|wǔ}{年|nián}。 We understand the event has been running for five years. |
| {据|jù}{统计|tǒng jì} | according to statistics | {据|jù}{统计|tǒng jì}，{来|lái}{参观|cān guān}{的|de}{人|rén}{超过|chāo guò}{了|le}{十万|shí wàn}。 Figures show more than 100,000 visitors. |
| {据|jù} + person + {说|shuō} / {介绍|jiè shào} | according to someone | {据|jù}{工作人员|gōng zuò rén yuán}{介绍|jiè shào}，{展览|zhǎn lǎn}{下个月|xià gè yuè}{结束|jié shù}。 According to the staff, the exhibition ends next month. |

- {据说|jù shuō} is the everyday one, in speech as well as writing: {据说|jù shuō}{他|tā}{下个月|xià gè yuè}{结婚|jié hūn} (I hear he's getting married
  next month). To name the source, put the person between {据|jù} and {说|shuō}: {据|jù}{她|tā}{说|shuō} (according to her). {据说|jù shuō}{她|tā}…
  means "it's said that she…": she's the subject of the rumour, not its source.
- The others are written and formal: news, reports, notices. They start the sentence and are followed
  by a comma.
- {统计|tǒng jì} (statistics; to count up) is lesson 28's; {工作人员|gōng zuò rén yuán} are the staff.

## {陆续|lù xù} and {纷纷|fēn fēn}: one after another

Both describe many people or things doing something, not all at once. They look at it differently:

{陆续|lù xù} is about **time**: they come, arrive or happen in a row, one, then another, over a
period. {陆陆续续|lù lù xù xù} is the same, a little more spoken.

{客人|kè rén}{们|men}{陆续|lù xù}{到|dào}{了|le}。 — The guests arrived one after another.

{这个|zhè ge}{月|yuè}，{新|xīn}{的|de}{地铁站|dì tiě zhàn}{陆续|lù xù}{开通|kāi tōng}{了|le}。 — New metro stations opened one after another this month.

{纷纷|fēn fēn} is about **many reacting in the same way**: lots of people, each of them, all doing
it, usually in response to something:

{听|tīng}{到|dào}{这个|zhè ge}{消息|xiāo xi}，{大家|dà jiā}{纷纷|fēn fēn}{表示|biǎo shì}{支持|zhī chí}。 — When they heard the news, everyone came out in support.

{视频|shì pín}{发出|fā chū}{去|qù}{以后|yǐ hòu}，{网友|wǎng yǒu}{纷纷|fēn fēn}{转发|zhuǎn fā}。 — Once the video was posted, people online shared it one after
another.

| | {陆续|lù xù} | {纷纷|fēn fēn} |
|---|---|---|
| looks at | the order in time | the number of people reacting |
| subject | people or things | always many people (or things) |
| typical verbs | {到|dào}, {来|lái}, {离开|lí kāi}, {开通|kāi tōng}, {出版|chū bǎn} | {表示|biǎo shì}, {转发|zhuǎn fā}, {报名|bào míng}, {赶|gǎn}{来|lái}, {离开|lí kāi} |

A single person can't {纷纷|fēn fēn} anything: ×{他|tā}{纷纷|fēn fēn}{表示|biǎo shì}{同意|tóng yì}. With one subject, use {都|dōu} or {一|yí}{个|gè}{一|yí}{个|gè}{地|de}.

## {即将|jí jiāng}: about to

{即将|jí jiāng} is the written "be about to, will soon": {即|jí} (at once) + {将|jiāng} (will, HSK 4). It goes
before the verb, usually with no {了|le} at the end:

{展览|zhǎn lǎn}{即将|jí jiāng}{开幕|kāi mù}。 — The exhibition is about to open.

{这|zhè}{本|běn}{书|shū}{即将|jí jiāng}{出版|chū bǎn}。 — The book will be published soon.

In speech you'd say {快要|kuài yào}…{了|le} or {就|jiù}{要|yào}…{了|le}: {展览|zhǎn lǎn}{快要|kuài yào}{开幕|kāi mù}{了|le}。 {即将|jí jiāng} is for news, notices and
announcements: {列车|liè chē}{即将|jí jiāng}{到站|dào zhàn} (the train is about to arrive at the station).

## {册|cè} and {集|jí}: volumes and episodes

| Measure word | Used for | Examples |
|---|---|---|
| {册|cè} | copies of a book; volumes of a set | {这|zhè}{本|běn}{书|shū}{已经|yǐ jīng}{卖|mài}{了|le}{五万|wǔ wàn}{册|cè}。 It has sold 50,000 copies. {第|dì}{一|yī}{册|cè} (Volume 1) |
| {集|jí} | episodes of a series; a collection | {这|zhè}{部|bù}{电视剧|diàn shì jù}{一共|yí gòng}{有|yǒu}40{集|jí}。 The series has 40 episodes. {第|dì}{三|sān}{集|jí} (episode 3) |
| {部|bù} (HSK 4) | a whole film, series or book | {一|yí}{部|bù}{电影|diàn yǐng}, {一|yí}{部|bù}{电视剧|diàn shì jù}, {一|yí}{部|bù}{小说|xiǎo shuō} |
| {本|běn} (HSK 1) | a single book | {一|yì}{本|běn}{书|shū} |

So a TV series is {一|yí}{部|bù}{电视剧|diàn shì jù}, and it has 40 {集|jí}. A book is {一|yì}{本|běn}{书|shū}; a print run is so many {册|cè}. {集|jí} is
also a noun: {诗集|shī jí} (a collection of poems), {文集|wén jí} (collected works).

## Publishing and announcing

Seven verbs that are easy to mix up. Each has its own objects:

| Verb | Meaning | Typical objects |
|---|---|---|
| {发表|fā biǎo} | to publish (writing); to express (a view) | {发表|fā biǎo}{文章|wén zhāng}, {发表|fā biǎo}{论文|lùn wén}, {发表|fā biǎo}{意见|yì jiàn}, {发表|fā biǎo}{讲话|jiǎng huà} |
| {发布|fā bù} | to release, issue (officially) | {发布|fā bù}{消息|xiāo xi}, {发布|fā bù}{新闻|xīn wén}, {发布|fā bù}{新|xīn}{产品|chǎn pǐn}, {发布|fā bù}{天气预报|tiān qì yù bào} |
| {公布|gōng bù} | to make public | {公布|gōng bù}{结果|jié guǒ}, {公布|gōng bù}{名单|míng dān} (a list), {公布|gōng bù}{考试|kǎo shì}{成绩|chéng jì} |
| {宣布|xuān bù} | to announce (a decision, a fact) | {宣布|xuān bù}{开幕|kāi mù}, {宣布|xuān bù}{结果|jié guǒ}, {宣布|xuān bù}{一|yí}{个|gè}{好|hǎo}{消息|xiāo xi} |
| {宣传|xuān chuán} | to publicise; publicity | {宣传|xuān chuán}{新|xīn}{产品|chǎn pǐn}, {宣传|xuān chuán}{活动|huó dòng}, {做|zuò}{宣传|xuān chuán} |
| {出版|chū bǎn} | to publish (a book, a magazine) | {出版|chū bǎn}{一|yì}{本|běn}{书|shū}, {出版社|chū bǎn shè} (a publisher) |
| {印刷|yìn shuā} | to print; printing | {印刷|yìn shuā}{书|shū}, {印刷厂|yìn shuā chǎng} (a printing works) |

- {发表|fā biǎo} is what a writer does; {出版|chū bǎn} is what a publisher does with a whole book.
- {宣布|xuān bù} is said aloud or formally, often by one person in charge: {主持|zhǔ chí}{人|rén}{宣布|xuān bù}{比赛|bǐ sài}{开始|kāi shǐ}。 {公布|gōng bù} makes
  something available for all to see: {学校|xué xiào}{公布|gōng bù}{了|le}{考试|kǎo shì}{成绩|chéng jì}。
- {电子版|diàn zǐ bǎn} is the electronic version: {这|zhè}{本|běn}{书|shū}{有|yǒu}{电子版|diàn zǐ bǎn}{吗|ma}？ (Is there an e-book?)

## Media words

| Word | Meaning | Note |
|---|---|---|
| {媒体|méi tǐ} | the media | {新闻媒体|xīn wén méi tǐ}, {当地|dāng dì}{媒体|méi tǐ} |
| {大众|dà zhòng} | the public, the masses | {大众媒体|dà zhòng méi tǐ} (mass media) |
| {报道|bào dào} | to report; a report | {报道|bào dào}{新闻|xīn wén}; {一|yì}{篇|piān}{报道|bào dào} |
| {采访|cǎi fǎng} | to interview (as a reporter) | {记者|jì zhě}{采访|cǎi fǎng}{了|le}{几|jǐ}{位|wèi}{居民|jū mín}。 |
| {访问|fǎng wèn} | to visit (formally); to access (a website) | {访问|fǎng wèn}{中国|Zhōng guó}; {访问|fǎng wèn}{网站|wǎng zhàn} |
| {传播|chuán bō} | to spread, disseminate | {传播|chuán bō}{消息|xiāo xi}, {传播|chuán bō}{文化|wén huà} |
| {反映|fǎn yìng} | to reflect; to report (a problem) | {这|zhè}{部|bù}{电影|diàn yǐng}{反映|fǎn yìng}{了|le}{农民|nóng mín}{的|de}{生活|shēng huó}; {向|xiàng}{社区|shè qū}{反映|fǎn yìng}{问题|wèn tí} |
| {电视台|diàn shì tái} / {收看|shōu kàn} | TV station / to watch (a programme) | {欢迎|huān yíng}{收看|shōu kàn}{今天|jīn tiān}{的|de}{节目|jié mù} (welcome to today's programme) |

**People**: {人民|rén mín} (the people, formal and collective: {中国|Zhōng guó}{人民|rén mín}), {老百姓|lǎo bǎi xìng} (ordinary people, everyday and warm:

### Shapes and stories

- **{守|shǒu} = 宀 + {寸|cùn}**: a roof and a hand ({寸|cùn}): keeping watch over a house. A memory aid; the character is
  the same in both scripts.
- **{裹|guǒ} = {衣|yī} split by {果|guǒ}**: {衣|yī} (clothing) opens to wrap {果|guǒ} (guǒ, the sound part, as the 《{说文解字|Shuō wén jiě zì}》 has it):
  亠 above, the rest of {衣|yī} below.
- **{违|wéi} and {遵|zūn}**: two 辶 characters about rules: {遵守|zūn shǒu} (keep) and {违反|wéi fǎn} (break).
- **{劳|láo}** shares its top with {荣|róng} and {营|yíng} (lesson 21); traditional {+{劳|láo}+} has two {火|huǒ} on top.
- **{滑|huá} = 氵 + {骨|gǔ}**: water and a bone ({骨|gǔ} gǔ, the sound part long ago).
- **{捐|juān} = 扌 + {肙|yuān}**: the right side is also in {绢|juàn} (silk) and {娟|juān} (graceful, in names).
- **{嘉|jiā}** has {加|jiā} (lesson 23's sound part of {驾|jià}) at the bottom: jiā = jiā.

### Stroke order

- **{守|shǒu}**: 宀 first (dot, short left dot, horizontal hook), then {寸|cùn}: horizontal, vertical hook, dot.
- **{访|fǎng}**: 讠 first (dot, then the turning rising stroke), then {方|fāng}: dot, horizontal, the turning hook,
  and the left-falling stroke last.
- **{版|bǎn}**: {片|piàn} first (left-falling, vertical, horizontal, then the turn), then {反|fǎn}: two left-falling
  strokes, then the turning stroke and the right-falling stroke.
- **{映|yìng}**: {日|rì} first, then {央|yāng}: the box-like top, the long horizontal, then left-falling and right-falling.
- **{劳|láo}**: 艹, then 冖, then {力|lì}: the turning hook before the left-falling stroke.
- **{遵|zūn}**, **{违|wéi}**: 辶 last, as always.

1. A volunteer group of university students teaching older residents of a community to use
   smartphones, and how well it's working.
2. Many things are now done on phones, but many residents over sixty can't use a smartphone, which
   makes everyday errands hard for them.

"**University volunteers teach older residents to use smartphones.** This website reports (reporter
Wang Fang): Recently, at the Xincheng community centre, this reporter saw more than thirty older
people carefully learning to use their phones with a few young people. We understand that this is a
'phone class' started by a team of volunteers from a university, which has now kept going for more
than a year.

"As the internet has developed, many things, such as booking a hospital appointment, shopping and
paying bills, can be done on a phone. However, according to community staff, many of the
community's residents over sixty can't use a smartphone, and going out to get things done is very
inconvenient for them.

"When the class first started, not many older people came. The volunteers went from door to door to
publicise it, residents told one another, and more and more came. The volunteers have also turned
the class content into an *Older People's Smartphone Handbook*, of which three volumes have been
printed so far, given free to residents.

"'I used to be afraid of getting lost when I went out. Now I can look at the map on my phone myself,'
said Mr Ma, a 72-year-old resident, happily. He has also learned to send videos to his grandson
online, and chats with him every day.

"At every class the volunteers first ask the older residents what difficulties they've met recently,
then plan the content around what people need. Some want to learn video calls, to see their children
who work far away; some want to book hospital appointments online, because queuing at the hospital is
exhausting. One volunteer said: 'The most important thing in teaching older people to use phones is
patience. Sometimes you explain the same thing five or six times.'

"The class has been widely welcomed by residents, and several nearby communities have come one after
another to learn from it. Jiang Xiaoyan, the team's leader, said that the electronic version of the
fourth volume will soon be released online, and the team also plans to make a short documentary
recording how the older residents learn. 'We hope more young people will join us,' she said, 'so
that older people can enjoy the convenience technology brings too.'"

updated fast: within minutes of a major event there are reports, some with live video from the scene.
And afterwards I can post my own views and talk them over with others online. But news on a phone
has its problems too. Some stories have no clear source, and what they say isn't necessarily true; a
false story is often shared by lots of people and spreads very fast. So when I see an important
story, I first check whether a well-known outlet has published it before deciding whether to believe
it. I think the more information there is, the more we need to learn to judge it."

{获取|huò qǔ} (HSK 4): to obtain; {更新|gēng xīn} (lesson 20): to update; {判断|pàn duàn} (HSK 4): to judge; {信息|xìn xī} (HSK 4): information.

Checklist:
- **Structure**: then and now, the advantages, the problems, your conclusion.
- **Connectors**: {以前|yǐ qián}…{现在|xiàn zài}, {而且|ér qiě}, {不过|bú guò}, {所以|suǒ yǐ}, {越|yuè}…{越|yuè}.
- **Vocabulary**: {发表|fā biǎo}, {发布|fā bù}, {来源|lái yuán}, {真实|zhēn shí}, {传播|chuán bō} used with their own objects.
- **Length**: about 270 characters.
</details>

## Say it

```speak
# Reporting the news
{据说|jù shuō}{这|zhè}{部|bù}{电影|diàn yǐng}{是|shì}{根据|gēn jù}{真实|zhēn shí}{的|de}{事件|shì jiàn}{拍|pāi}{的|de}。
= They say the film is based on a true story.
{据|jù}{当地|dāng dì}{媒体|méi tǐ}{报道|bào dào}，{大|dà}{雨|yǔ}{造成|zào chéng}{了|le}{很|hěn}{大|dà}{的|de}{损失|sǔn shī}。
= According to local media, the heavy rain caused serious losses.
{客人|kè rén}{们|men}{陆续|lù xù}{到|dào}{了|le}。
= The guests arrived one after another.
{听|tīng}{到|dào}{这个|zhè ge}{消息|xiāo xi}，{大家|dà jiā}{纷纷|fēn fēn}{表示|biǎo shì}{支持|zhī chí}。
= When they heard the news, everyone came out in support.
{展览|zhǎn lǎn}{即将|jí jiāng}{开幕|kāi mù}。
= The exhibition is about to open.
{这|zhè}{部|bù}{电视剧|diàn shì jù}{一共|yí gòng}{有|yǒu}40{集|jí}。
= The series has forty episodes.
```

## Pronunciation

- {报道|bào dào} bào dào and {报到|bào dào} bào dào (lesson 01) are said exactly alike.
- {陆续|lù xù} lù xù: *xu* is xü, lips rounded. {陆|lù} lù is the {陆|lù} of {陆地|lù dì}.
- {纷纷|fēn fēn} fēn fēn: two level tones; {分|fēn} fēn has the same sound.
- {即将|jí jiāng} jí jiāng: {即|jí} rises (jí), unlike {几|jǐ} jǐ and {记|jì} jì.
- {采访|cǎi fǎng} cǎi fǎng: two dipping tones in a row, said cái fǎng (3+3 sandhi, not written).
- {媒体|méi tǐ} méi tǐ, {嘉宾|jiā bīn} jiā bīn, {省会|shěng huì} shěng huì, {县|xiàn} xiàn, {乡|xiāng} xiāng.
- {劳动|láo dòng} láo dòng: *l*, not *n*: {劳|láo} rhymes with {老|lǎo} lǎo in its vowel.

## Common mistakes

- {据说|jù shuō} and {据|jù}{她|tā}{说|shuō}: "according to her" is {据|jù}{她|tā}{说|shuō} (or just {她|tā}{说|shuō}). {据说|jù shuō}{她|tā}{明天|míng tiān}{放假|fàng jià} means "I hear she's off
  tomorrow": the source isn't named.
- ~~{他|tā}{纷纷|fēn fēn}{表示|biǎo shì}{同意|tóng yì}~~: {纷纷|fēn fēn} needs many people. One person: {他|tā}{表示|biǎo shì}{同意|tóng yì}.
- {展览|zhǎn lǎn}{即将|jí jiāng}{开幕|kāi mù}{了|le} is heard, but {即将|jí jiāng} already points forward, and written style leaves out the final {了|le}:
  {展览|zhǎn lǎn}{即将|jí jiāng}{开幕|kāi mù}. In speech, {展览|zhǎn lǎn}{快要|kuài yào}{开幕|kāi mù}{了|le}.
- {发表|fā biǎo}{一|yì}{本|běn}{书|shū} is odd: a book is {出版|chū bǎn}; {发表|fā biǎo} is for an article or a view. {发表|fā biǎo}{文章|wén zhāng}, {出版|chū bǎn}{小说|xiǎo shuō}.
- {宣布|xuān bù} and {公布|gōng bù}: you {宣布|xuān bù} a decision aloud ({宣布|xuān bù}{开会|kāi huì}); you {公布|gōng bù} results or lists for everyone to see
  ({公布|gōng bù}{成绩|chéng jì}).
- {一|yí}{部|bù}{电视剧|diàn shì jù}{有|yǒu}{三十|sān shí}{集|jí}, not ~~{三十|sān shí}{部|bù}~~: {部|bù} counts the whole series, {集|jí} its episodes.

## Key points

- {据说|jù shuō} (it's said), {据|jù}…{报道|bào dào}, {据|jù}{了解|liǎo jiě}, {据|jù}{统计|tǒng jì}, {据|jù} + person + {说|shuō} / {介绍|jiè shào}: where information comes from;
  all but {据说|jù shuō} are written.
- {陆续|lù xù}: one after another in time; {纷纷|fēn fēn}: many people reacting in the same way (never one person).
- {即将|jí jiāng} + verb: about to (written; no {了|le}). Spoken {快要|kuài yào}…{了|le}.
- {册|cè} (copies, volumes), {集|jí} (episodes); {部|bù} (a whole film or series), {本|běn} (a book).
- {发表|fā biǎo} (an article, a view), {发布|fā bù} (official news, products), {公布|gōng bù} (results), {宣布|xuān bù} (a decision, aloud),
  {宣传|xuān chuán} (publicity), {出版|chū bǎn} (a book), {印刷|yìn shuā} (printing).
- Society: {人民|rén mín} (formal) vs {老百姓|lǎo bǎi xìng} (everyday); {省|shěng} → {市|shì} / {县|xiàn} → {乡|xiāng} → {村|cūn}.
- New radical: {片|piàn} ({片|piàn} {牌|pái} {版|bǎn}).
- New characters: {滑|huá} {捐|juān} {赔|péi} {骗|piàn} {守|shǒu} {损|sǔn} {倡|chàng} {违|wéi} {撞|zhuàng} {阻|zǔ} {遵|zūn} {糟|zāo} {裹|guǒ} {访|fǎng} {版|bǎn} {映|yìng} {纷|fēn} {嘉|jiā} {泛|fàn} {劳|láo}; ✎ {守|shǒu} {访|fǎng} {版|bǎn} {映|yìng} {劳|láo}.

The words from this lesson are listed below; they join your vocabulary reviews when you complete
the lesson.

lessons.title: Traditions, festivals and the zodiac
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

The module ends with what holds a society together over time: its festivals, customs and stories.
You'll learn:

- **{再|zài}…{也|yě}** (however…, still…): {再|zài}{忙|máng}{也|yě}{要|yào}{回家|huí jiā}{过年|guò nián};
- **…{为|wèi}{的|de}{是|shì}…** (…, the purpose being…), the written way to give a reason at the end;
- {至今|zhì jīn} (up to now, to this day) and the words for long ago: {古代|gǔ dài}, {近代|jìn dài}, {现代|xiàn dài}, {时代|shí dài}, {时期|shí qī}, {年代|nián dài}, {早期|zǎo qī}, {悠久|yōu jiǔ},
  {久远|jiǔ yuǎn};
- the Spring Festival: {除夕|chú xī}, {年夜饭|nián yè fàn}, {压岁钱|yā suì qián}, {福|fú}, and the twelve animals of the zodiac ({生肖|shēng xiào});
- two idioms ({成语|chéng yǔ}): {丰富多彩|fēng fù duō cǎi} (rich and varied) and {酸甜苦辣|suān tián kǔ là} (the ups and downs of life), and how each
  fits into a sentence.

The reading explains the customs of the Spring Festival and where some of them come from; the
dialogue is a New Year's Eve video call between Beijing and the north of England.

## {再|zài}…{也|yě}: however…, still…

{再|zài} + an adjective or verb, then {也|yě} + what still holds, means "however…, still…; even if…, still…".
It's a **[[concessive]]** sentence, the **{再|zài}…{也|yě}** pattern: it admits something as strongly as possible
and then says it changes nothing.

{再|zài}{忙|máng}{也|yě}{要|yào}{回家|huí jiā}{过年|guò nián}。 — However busy you are, you go home for New Year.

{这|zhè}{件|jiàn}{衣服|yī fu}{再|zài}{贵|guì}{我|wǒ}{也|yě}{要|yào}{买|mǎi}。 — However expensive this coat is, I'm buying it.

{你|nǐ}{再|zài}{说|shuō}{也|yě}{没有|méi yǒu}{用|yòng}，{他|tā}{已经|yǐ jīng}{决定|jué dìng}{了|le}。 — It's no use however much you say: he's already decided.

- {再|zài} goes before the adjective or verb of the first half; {也|yě} goes before the verb of the second, after
  its subject: {再|zài}{累|lèi}，{我|wǒ}{也|yě}{要|yào}{做|zuò}{完|wán} / {我|wǒ}{再|zài}{累|lèi}{也|yě}{要|yào}{做|zuò}{完|wán}.
- The first half is often very short, just {再|zài} + adjective, and the two halves can run together with
  no comma: {再|zài}{远|yuǎn}{也|yě}{要|yào}{去|qù}.
- {不管|bù guǎn}{多|duō}…{都|dōu} (HSK 4) says nearly the same: {不管|bù guǎn}{多|duō}{忙|máng}，{都|dōu}{要|yào}{回家|huí jiā}{过年|guò nián}. {再|zài}…{也|yě} is shorter and stronger, and
  usually leads to a resolve: {要|yào}, {得|děi}, {不|bù} + verb.
- {即使|jí shǐ}…{也|yě} (HSK 4) supposes a fact ("even if"); {再|zài}…{也|yě} pushes a degree to the limit ("however much").

## …{为|wèi}{的|de}{是|shì}…: the purpose is…

You know {为了|wèi le} (HSK 3): {为了|wèi le} + purpose, then the action. **{为|wèi}{的|de}{是|shì}** puts the purpose at the end, as an
explanation added after the fact: "…, the reason being…", "…, so as to…". It's written, or careful
speech:

{他|tā}{每天|měi tiān}{早上|zǎo shang}{五|wǔ}{点|diǎn}{起床|qǐ chuáng}，{为|wèi}{的|de}{是|shì}{赶|gǎn}{第|dì}{一|yī}{班|bān}{地铁|dì tiě}。 — He gets up at five every morning so as to catch the first
metro.

{春节|Chūn jié}{前|qián}{人|rén}{们|men}{打扫|dǎ sǎo}{房子|fáng zi}，{为|wèi}{的|de}{是|shì}{迎接|yíng jiē}{新|xīn}{的|de}{一|yì}{年|nián}。 — Before the Spring Festival people clean their homes, the
purpose being to welcome the new year.

{我们|wǒ men}{这样|zhè yàng}{做|zuò}，{为|wèi}{的|de}{是|shì}{让|ràng}{孩子们|hái zi men}{了解|liǎo jiě}{传统|chuán tǒng}{文化|wén huà}。 — We do this so that children learn about their traditional
culture.

| Pattern | Order | Register | Example |
|---|---|---|---|
| {为了|wèi le} + purpose，action | purpose first | neutral | {为了|wèi le}{迎接|yíng jiē}{新年|xīn nián}，{大家|dà jiā}{打扫|dǎ sǎo}{房子|fáng zi}。 |
| action，{是|shì}{为了|wèi le} + purpose | purpose at the end | neutral | {大家|dà jiā}{打扫|dǎ sǎo}{房子|fáng zi}，{是|shì}{为了|wèi le}{迎接|yíng jiē}{新年|xīn nián}。 |
| action，{为|wèi}{的|de}{是|shì} + purpose | purpose at the end | written, explanatory | {大家|dà jiā}{打扫|dǎ sǎo}{房子|fáng zi}，{为|wèi}{的|de}{是|shì}{迎接|yíng jiē}{新年|xīn nián}。 |

{为|wèi} here is wèi, as in {为了|wèi le} and {为什么|wèi shén me}; lesson 27's {为|wéi} (by, in {为|wéi}…{所|suǒ}) is a different word.

## {至今|zhì jīn}: up to now

{至今|zhì jīn} ({至|zhì} "to, until" + {今|jīn} "now", both written) means "up to now, to this day". It goes before the verb,
often with {已经|yǐ jīng} / {还|hái} / {仍|réng}:

{这个|zhè ge}{风俗|fēng sú}{至今|zhì jīn}{还|hái}{保留|bǎo liú}{着|zhe}。 — The custom is still kept to this day.

{这|zhè}{座|zuò}{桥|qiáo}{建于|jiàn yú}1950{年|nián}，{至今|zhì jīn}{已|yǐ}{有|yǒu}80{年|nián}{了|le}。 — The bridge was built in 1950: it's eighty years old now.

{我们|wǒ men}{至今|zhì jīn}{没有|méi yǒu}{收到|shōu dào}{他|tā}{的|de}{回信|huí xìn}。 — We still haven't had a reply from him.

In speech, people say {到|dào}{现在|xiàn zài} or {一直|yì zhí}: {我们|wǒ men}{到|dào}{现在|xiàn zài}{还没|hái méi}{收到|shōu dào}{他|tā}{的|de}{回信|huí xìn}. {至今|zhì jīn} is for writing and formal speech.
({建于|jiàn yú}: built in, the written {于|yú} of HSK 4: {于|yú} + a time or place after a verb.)

## Long ago and now

| Word | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| {古|gǔ} / {古老|gǔ lǎo} | ancient / ancient, very old | {古城|gǔ chéng} (an ancient city); {一|yí}{个|gè}{古老|gǔ lǎo}{的|de}{传说|chuán shuō} |
| {古代|gǔ dài} | ancient times (in China, before the mid-19th century) | {中国|Zhōng guó}{古代|gǔ dài}{的|de}{诗人|shī rén} (poets of ancient China; {诗人|shī rén}, lesson 29) |
| {近代|jìn dài} | modern times (about 1840 to 1919 in Chinese history books) | {近代史|jìn dài shǐ} (modern history) |
| {现代|xiàn dài} | the present age; modern | {现代|xiàn dài}{社会|shè huì}, {现代化|xiàn dài huà} (lesson 21) |
| {时代|shí dài} | an era, an age | {网络时代|wǎng luò shí dài} (the internet age); {时代|shí dài}{变|biàn}{了|le} |
| {时期|shí qī} | a period (with a beginning and an end) | {唐朝时期|Táng cháo shí qī} (the Tang period); {大学|dà xué}{时期|shí qī} (university days) |
| {年代|nián dài} | a decade; an era | 80{年代|nián dài} (the 1980s); {那个|nà ge}{年代|nián dài} (those days) |
| {早期|zǎo qī} | the early stage | {早期|zǎo qī}{的|de}{作品|zuò pǐn} (early works) |
| {悠久|yōu jiǔ} | long-standing | {历史|lì shǐ}{悠久|yōu jiǔ} (with a long history): almost always with {历史|lì shǐ} |
| {久远|jiǔ yuǎn} | long ago, far back | {年代|nián dài}{久远|jiǔ yuǎn} (dating far back) |
| {初|chū} | the beginning (of a period) | {月|yuè}{初|chū} (the start of the month), {年初|nián chū} (lesson 28), {初|chū}{一|yī} (the first day of a lunar month) |

The labels {古代|gǔ dài} / {近代|jìn dài} / {现代|xiàn dài} follow Chinese history books, which date {近代|jìn dài} from the 1840s; English
"modern" usually covers both {近代|jìn dài} and {现代|xiàn dài}. Most everyday talk needs only {古代|gǔ dài} and {现代|xiàn dài}.

## The Spring Festival and other festivals

{春节|Chūn jié} (HSK 3) is the lunar New Year. Its eve, the last night of the old year, is {除夕|chú xī}: the
family eats {年夜饭|nián yè fàn} (New Year's Eve dinner), and children get {压岁钱|yā suì qián} (New Year money, in a red
envelope, {红包|hóng bāo}). Doors carry a big {福|fú} (good fortune). People wish each other {好运|hǎo yùn} (good luck),
{平安|píng ān} (safe and sound) and a {光明|guāng míng} (bright) future.

Other days of the calendar ({日历|rì lì}): {元旦|yuán dàn} (New Year's Day, 1 January), {国庆|guó qìng} (National Day, 1
October: {国庆节|Guó qìng jié}), and every kind of {纪念日|jì niàn rì} (a day of remembrance; an anniversary) with its {周年|zhōu nián}
(a full year: {结婚|jié hūn}{十|shí}{周年|zhōu nián}, a tenth wedding anniversary). To {纪念|jì niàn} is to commemorate; a {纪念品|jì niàn pǐn} is a
souvenir.

Big events open and close with ceremonies: {开幕|kāi mù} (to open, raise the curtain), {开幕式|kāi mù shì} (an
opening ceremony), {闭幕式|bì mù shì} (a closing ceremony), with {灯光|dēng guāng} (lights). The suffix {式|shì} marks a
style or a ceremony: {开幕式|kāi mù shì}, {中|zhōng}{式|shì} (Chinese-style), {西|xī}{式|shì} (Western-style), {新|xīn}{式|shì} (new-type).

And some verbs of festivals: {迎|yíng} / {迎接|yíng jiē} (to welcome, meet: {迎接|yíng jiē}{新年|xīn nián}, {迎接|yíng jiē}{客人|kè rén}; {迎|yíng} alone in set
phrases: {欢迎|huān yíng}, {迎新年|yíng xīn nián}), {赏|shǎng} (to enjoy looking at: {赏月|shǎng yuè}, enjoy the moon at the Mid-Autumn Festival;
{赏花|shǎng huā}), **{扇|shān}** (to fan) with a {扇子|shàn zi} (a fan), {充满|chōng mǎn} (to be full of: {充满|chōng mǎn}{了|le}{节日|jié rì}{的|de}{气氛|qì fēn}, full of
festive atmosphere; {气氛|qì fēn} qì fēn, HSK 6).

## Luck, fate and stories

| Word | Meaning | Note |
|---|---|---|
| {运气|yùn qi} | luck | {运气|yùn qi}{好|hǎo} / {不|bù}{好|hǎo}; neutral |
| {好运|hǎo yùn} | good luck | {祝|zhù}{你|nǐ}{好运|hǎo yùn}！ (Good luck!) |
| {幸运|xìng yùn} | lucky | {他|tā}{很|hěn}{幸运|xìng yùn}; {幸运|xìng yùn}{的|de}{是|shì}… (luckily…) |
| {命运|mìng yùn} | fate, destiny | {改变|gǎi biàn}{命运|mìng yùn} |
| {福|fú} | good fortune, blessing | {福气|fú qi} (good fortune, of a person) |
| {平安|píng ān} | safe and sound | {一路平安|yí lù píng ān} (a safe journey) |
| {光明|guāng míng} | bright; brightness | {光明|guāng míng}{的|de}{未来|wèi lái} |
| {神秘|shén mì} | mysterious | {一|yí}{个|gè}{神秘|shén mì}{的|de}{地方|dì fang} |
| {传说|chuán shuō} | a legend; it is said | {一|yí}{个|gè}{古老|gǔ lǎo}{的|de}{传说|chuán shuō}; {传说|chuán shuō}… (legend has it that…) |
| {神话|shén huà} | a myth | {中国|Zhōng guó}{神话|shén huà} |

The story words: {传统|chuán tǒng} (tradition; traditional), {风俗|fēng sú} (a custom), {特色|tè sè} (a special feature,
character: {有|yǒu}{特色|tè sè}), {特有|tè yǒu} (unique to: {中国|Zhōng guó}{特有|tè yǒu}{的|de}{动物|dòng wù}), {象征|xiàng zhēng} (a symbol; to symbolise: {龙|lóng}{象征|xiàng zhēng}{着|zhe}{力量|lì liang}),
{保留|bǎo liú} (to keep, preserve: {保留|bǎo liú}{传统|chuán tǒng}), {流传|liú chuán} (to be handed down, spread: {这个|zhè ge}{故事|gù shi}{流传|liú chuán}{了|le}{很|hěn}{多|duō}{年|nián}), {传|chuán}
(to pass on: {传下去|chuán xià qù}), {记载|jì zǎi} (to record in writing; a record: {古|gǔ}{书|shū}{上|shàng}{记载|jì zǎi}…), {讲述|jiǎng shù} (to tell, narrate:
written for {讲|jiǎng}), {敌人|dí rén} (an enemy), {伟大|wěi dà} (great: {伟大|wěi dà}{的|de}{发明|fā míng}), {统一|tǒng yī} (unified; to unify: {秦朝|Qín cháo}{统一|tǒng yī}{了|le}
{中国|Zhōng guó}, the Qin unified China), {中华|Zhōng huá} (China, in a cultural and formal sense: {中华文化|Zhōng huá wén huà}) and {中华民族|Zhōng huá mín zú}
(the Chinese nation).

## Two idioms

{丰富多彩|fēng fù duō cǎi} (rich and varied): {丰富|fēng fù} (rich, HSK 4) + {多|duō} (many) + {彩|cǎi} (colours). It describes events,
activities and lives, in writing and in careful speech:

- as the predicate: {春节|Chūn jié}{的|de}{活动|huó dòng}{丰富多彩|fēng fù duō cǎi}。 (Spring Festival activities are rich and varied.)
- before a noun with {的|de}: {丰富多彩|fēng fù duō cǎi}{的|de}{校园|xiào yuán}{生活|shēng huó} (a rich and varied campus life).

{酸甜苦辣|suān tián kǔ là} (the ups and downs of life): literally sour, sweet, bitter, spicy: the four tastes
standing for every experience. It's a noun phrase, used as an object or a subject:

- {他|tā}{尝遍|cháng biàn}{了|le}{生活|shēng huó}{的|de}{酸甜苦辣|suān tián kǔ là}。 (He's tasted all of life's ups and downs.) {尝遍|cháng biàn}: to taste every one.
- {留学|liú xué}{一|yì}{年|nián}，{酸甜苦辣|suān tián kǔ là}{都|dōu}{有|yǒu}。 (A year abroad: it's had everything, good and bad.)

Careful usage puts no {很|hěn} before them ({很|hěn}{丰富多彩|fēng fù duō cǎi} is heard, but teachers correct it): an idiom is
already complete, so it usually stands without degree words. Both are neutral to formal; in a chat, {活动|huó dòng}{很|hěn}{多|duō} or {有好有坏|yǒu hǎo yǒu huài} are plainer.

## The twelve animals

Each year of the lunar calendar has an animal, the year's {生肖|shēng xiào}, in a cycle of twelve:

| | | | | | |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| {鼠|shǔ} rat | {牛|niú} ox | {虎|hǔ} tiger | {兔|tù} rabbit ({兔子|tù zi}) | {龙|lóng} dragon | {蛇|shé} snake |
| {马|mǎ} horse | {羊|yáng} goat, sheep | {猴|hóu} monkey ({猴子|hóu zi}) | {鸡|jī} rooster | {狗|gǒu} dog | {猪|zhū} pig |

To ask someone's animal, say {你|nǐ}{属|shǔ}{什么|shén me}？ ({属|shǔ}, to belong to: lesson 26's {属于|shǔ yú}). The answer is {我|wǒ}{属|shǔ}{马|mǎ} (I was
born in a horse year). Wang Fang, for instance, {属|shǔ}{马|mǎ}; Anna, born in 1998, {属|shǔ}{虎|hǔ}. Because the cycle has
twelve years, {你|nǐ}{属|shǔ}{什么|shén me} is also a polite, roundabout way of asking someone's age.

In the zodiac, the animal on its own is often the one-syllable word ({属|shǔ}{兔|tù}, {属|shǔ}{猴|hóu}); in ordinary speech
the animals are {兔子|tù zi}, {猴子|hóu zi}, {老虎|lǎo hǔ}, {老鼠|lǎo shǔ} (rat, mouse; HSK 6). The dragon, {龙|lóng}, is a {神话|shén huà} animal: it stands
for power and good fortune, and dragons appear on New Year decorations and in festival dances.

### A new radical: 厶

**厶** (sī, an old form of "private") is a small two-stroke shape, a left-falling turn and a dot. It's
the radical of {去|qù} (HSK 1: {土|tǔ} over 厶), {参|cān} ({参加|cān jiā}, HSK 3) and now {县|xiàn}, where it sits at the bottom. Most
dictionaries file {去|qù} under {土|tǔ} or 厶; the course follows Make Me a Hanzi, the tracing data, which uses 厶.

### Stroke order

- **{夕|xī}**: left-falling, the horizontal-turn, then the dot.
- **{古|gǔ}**: horizontal, vertical, then {口|kǒu}.
- **{龙|lóng}**: horizontal, left-falling, the long vertical-bend hook, then a short left-falling stroke and
  the dot.
- **{华|huá}**: {化|huà} on top (亻 then {匕|bǐ}), then {十|shí}: horizontal, then the long vertical last.
- **{伟|wěi}**: 亻, then 韦: two horizontals, the horizontal-turn hook, and the vertical last.
- **{县|xiàn}**: {且|qiě}-like top (the box and its horizontals), then 厶 at the bottom: the turning stroke, then
  the dot.
- **{猪|zhū}**, **{猴|hóu}**: 犭 first (left-falling, the bent hook, left-falling), then the right side.
- **{府|fǔ}**: {广|guǎng} first (dot, horizontal, left-falling), then {付|fù} inside.

1. The Spring Festival: its date, the legend of "Nian", its customs (the dinner, New Year money, the

2. The monster "Nian" was afraid of red, light and loud noises, so they kept it away.

"**The customs of the Spring Festival.** The Spring Festival is the most important traditional
festival of the Chinese nation. In ancient China people used the lunar calendar, and the Spring
Festival was the start of the lunar new year, so people also call celebrating it 'passing the year'.
Today, New Year's Day is 1 January in the Gregorian calendar, while the date of the Spring Festival
changes every year, usually falling between late January and mid-February.

"About 'Nian', an ancient legend is told among the people. Long ago there was a monster called
'Nian', which came out every New Year's Eve to harm people and animals. Later people discovered that
Nian was most afraid of the colour red, of lights and of loud noises. So every New Year's Eve
everyone stuck red paper on their doors, lit lamps in the house and set off firecrackers. After that,
Nian never dared come again.

"The customs of the Spring Festival are rich and varied, and many places keep them to this day. On
New Year's Eve the family eats dinner together. In the north, the dinner can't do without dumplings;
in the south, many families cook a fish, because 'fish' sounds the same as 'surplus' and stands for
'a surplus year after year'. After dinner the older generation gives the children New Year money,
so that the children will pass the new year safe and well. Many families also stick a {福|fú} (good
fortune) on the door, and some put it upside down on purpose, because 'fortune is upside down'
sounds like 'fortune has arrived'.

"The Spring Festival is also linked to the twelve zodiac animals. Each year has an animal to stand
for it, in a cycle of twelve: rat, ox, tiger, rabbit, dragon, snake, horse, goat, monkey, rooster,
dog, pig. People often ask each other, 'What's your animal?' The zodiac is not only a way of counting
years; it also adds a good deal of fun to the traditional festival.

"Around the Spring Festival many cities also hold temple fairs and lantern shows. Temple fairs have
snacks and performances; at the lantern shows every kind of lantern is hung up, some made as dragons,
some as the animal of the year, drawing crowds of residents and tourists.

"As times change, the ways of celebrating the New Year are changing too: some people send red
envelopes to family and friends online, some take the whole family travelling. But for many Chinese
people the meaning of the Spring Festival has not changed to this day: however far away you are, you
go home, so as to be together with your family."

- {除夕|chú xī} chú xī: rising, then level. {夕|xī} xī is said like {西|xī} xī.
- {压岁钱|yā suì qián} yā suì qián: level, falling, rising.
- {生肖|shēng xiào} shēng xiào; {肖|xiào} xiào sounds like {笑|xiào} xiào (to laugh).
- {猪|zhū} zhū, {蛇|shé} shé, {猴|hóu} hóu, {兔|tù} tù, {龙|lóng} lóng: the animal syllables. *zhu* and *shé* need the retroflex *zh*, *sh*.
- {扇|shàn} has two readings: shàn ({扇子|shàn zi}, a fan) and shān ({扇|shān}, to fan).
- {悠久|yōu jiǔ} yōu jiǔ: level, then dipping. {优|yōu} yōu ({优秀|yōu xiù}) has the same sound.
- {至今|zhì jīn} zhì jīn, {纪念|jì niàn} jì niàn, {记载|jì zǎi} jì zǎi: *zh* in {至|zhì}, *j* in {纪|jì} and {记|jì}.
- {酸甜苦辣|suān tián kǔ là} suān tián kǔ là: level, rising, dipping, falling: all four tones in a row, in order.

## Common mistakes

- ~~{再|zài}{忙|máng}{我|wǒ}{要|yào}{回家|huí jiā}~~: the second half needs {也|yě}: {再|zài}{忙|máng}{我|wǒ}{也|yě}{要|yào}{回家|huí jiā}.
- ~~{为|wèi}{的|de}{是|shì}{迎接|yíng jiē}{新年|xīn nián}，{大家|dà jiā}{打扫|dǎ sǎo}{房子|fáng zi}~~: {为|wèi}{的|de}{是|shì} comes after the action: {大家|dà jiā}{打扫|dǎ sǎo}{房子|fáng zi}，{为|wèi}{的|de}{是|shì}{迎接|yíng jiē}{新年|xīn nián}. To put the
  purpose first, use {为了|wèi le}.
- {这个|zhè ge}{活动|huó dòng}{很|hěn}{丰富多彩|fēng fù duō cǎi} is heard in speech, but careful usage drops {很|hěn} before an idiom: {这个|zhè ge}{活动|huó dòng}{丰富多彩|fēng fù duō cǎi}, or
  {很|hěn}{丰富|fēng fù} without the idiom.
- ~~{我|wǒ}{属于|shǔ yú}{马|mǎ}~~: for the zodiac it's {属|shǔ} alone: {我|wǒ}{属|shǔ}{马|mǎ}. {属于|shǔ yú} (lesson 26) is "to belong to (a group, a
  category)".
- {历史|lì shǐ}{很|hěn}{悠久|yōu jiǔ} is fine, but {悠久|yōu jiǔ} almost always goes with {历史|lì shǐ}: {悠久|yōu jiǔ}{的|de}{传说|chuán shuō} is odd; use {古老|gǔ lǎo}{的|de}{传说|chuán shuō}.
- {现代|xiàn dài} and {近代|jìn dài}: {近代|jìn dài} in Chinese history is the 1840s to 1919, not "recent": "recently" is {最近|zuì jìn} or
  {近来|jìn lái}.

## Key points

- {再|zài} + adj. / verb，(subject) {也|yě}…: however…, still… ({再|zài}{忙|máng}{也|yě}{要|yào}{回家|huí jiā}{过年|guò nián}).
- action，{为|wèi}{的|de}{是|shì} + purpose: written purpose at the end; {为了|wèi le} + purpose puts it first.
- {至今|zhì jīn} (+ {已经|yǐ jīng} / {还|hái} / {没|méi}): up to now, to this day (written); spoken {到|dào}{现在|xiàn zài}.
- {古代|gǔ dài}, {近代|jìn dài}, {现代|xiàn dài}; {时代|shí dài}, {时期|shí qī}, {年代|nián dài}, {早期|zǎo qī}; {悠久|yōu jiǔ} ({历史|lì shǐ}{悠久|yōu jiǔ}), {久远|jiǔ yuǎn}, {古老|gǔ lǎo}.
- {除夕|chú xī}, {年夜饭|nián yè fàn}, {压岁钱|yā suì qián}, {福|fú}; {你|nǐ}{属|shǔ}{什么|shén me}？{我|wǒ}{属|shǔ}{马|mǎ}; the twelve {生肖|shēng xiào}.
- Idioms: {丰富多彩|fēng fù duō cǎi} (predicate or {的|de} + noun), {酸甜苦辣|suān tián kǔ là} (a noun phrase); no {很|hěn} before an idiom.
- New radical: 厶 ({去|qù} {参|cān} {县|xiàn}).
- New characters: {媒|méi} {县|xiàn} {宣|xuān} {府|fǔ} {夕|xī} {敌|dí} {俗|sú} {古|gǔ} {猴|hóu} {龙|lóng} {扇|shàn} {蛇|shé} {肖|xiào} {兔|tù} {伟|wěi} {征|zhēng} {悠|yōu} {华|huá} {猪|zhū}; ✎ {县|xiàn} {宣|xuān} {府|fǔ} {夕|xī} {敌|dí} {古|gǔ} {龙|lóng} {伟|wěi} {华|huá} {猪|zhū}.

lessons.title: Romance of the Three Kingdoms
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

Lesson 25 was about stories that are handed down ({流传|liú chuán}) from generation to generation. The best-known
of them all is a long novel, 《{三国演义|Sān guó yǎn yì}》 (*Sānguó yǎnyì*, the Romance of the Three Kingdoms), and the
real history behind it. Almost everyone in China knows its heroes, from plays, films, comics, games
and sayings. This lesson keeps two things apart that are often mixed up: **the history** of the
Three Kingdoms and **the novel** written more than a thousand years later. Then you'll read two of
its most famous episodes, retold in simple modern Chinese.

New words you'll meet (glossed where they appear, not for your reviews): {演义|yǎn yì} (a historical
novel), {东汉|Dōng Hàn} (the Eastern Han dynasty), {魏|Wèi} / {蜀|Shǔ} / {吴|Wú} (the three kingdoms), {结义|jié yì} (to swear
brotherhood), {箭|jiàn} (an arrow), {船|chuán} (a boat).

## The history: 220–280

At the end of the Eastern Han dynasty ({东汉|Dōng Hàn}), in the late second century, the government grew weak,
a great rebellion broke out in 184, and military leaders fought one another for land. By the 220s
three states had formed, each ruled by its own emperor:

| State | Founder | Where | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| {魏|Wèi} Wèi | {曹丕|Cáo Pī} (Cáo Pī), son of {曹操|Cáo Cāo} (Cáo Cāo) | the north | the strongest; founded in 220, when the Han ended |
| {蜀|Shǔ} Shǔ | {刘备|Liú Bèi} (Liú Bèi) | the south-west, around today's Sichuan | founded in 221 |
| {吴|Wú} Wú | {孙权|Sūn Quán} (Sūn Quán) | the south-east, along the Yangtze | its ruler took the title of emperor in 229 |

This is the **Three Kingdoms** period, usually dated 220 to 280. It ended when the Jin dynasty ({晋|Jìn})
reunited the country in 280. Its history was written down soon afterwards by {陈寿|Chén Shòu} (Chén Shòu) in
《{三国志|Sān guó zhì}》 (*Sānguó zhì*, the Records of the Three Kingdoms), at the end of the third century. That is
a work of history; the novel came much later.

## The novel: Ming dynasty, about 120 chapters

《{三国演义|Sān guó yǎn yì}》 ({演义|yǎn yì}, a historical novel that "expands on" history) was written down in the Ming dynasty
and **traditionally attributed to {罗贯中|Luó Guàn zhōng}** (Luó Guànzhōng), a writer who probably lived in the 14th
century; very little is known about him. The oldest printed edition that survives dates from 1522.
In the 1660s, in the early Qing dynasty, {毛宗岗|Máo Zōng gǎng} (Máo Zōnggǎng) and his father revised the text, and
their 120-chapter version is the one most people read today.

The novel follows the history closely in its outline: the same people, the same states, the same
end. But it adds speeches, battles, tricks and whole episodes, and it takes sides: {刘备|Liú Bèi} and his
followers are the heroes, {曹操|Cáo Cāo} the clever villain. People often describe it as {七分事实|qī fēn shì shí}，{三分虚构|sān fēn xū gòu}
("seven parts fact, three parts fiction"; {虚构|xū gòu} xū gòu, to make up), after the Qing scholar
{章学诚|Zhāng Xué chéng} (Zhāng Xuéchéng), whose own words were {七分实事|qī fēn shí shì}，{三分虚构|sān fēn xū gòu}.

Its famous first sentence sums up how it sees history:

> {天下|tiān xià}{大势|dà shì}，{分久必合|fēn jiǔ bì hé}，{合久必分|hé jiǔ bì fēn}。

"The great trend of the world: what has long been divided must unite, and what has long been united
must divide." ({天下|tiān xià}, the whole country, "all under heaven"; {大势|dà shì}, the general trend; {久|jiǔ}, long; {必|bì},
must, lesson 27.) The 120-chapter text begins {话说|huà shuō}{天下|tiān xià}{大势|dà shì}…, with {话说|huà shuō}, the storyteller's "now, the
story goes".

## Episode 1: the oath in the peach garden

In the novel, three men meet at the start of the troubles: {刘备|Liú Bèi}, a poor man of the imperial family who
sells straw sandals; {关羽|Guān Yǔ} (Guān Yǔ), a tall man with a red face and a long beard; and {张飞|Zhāng Fēi} (Zhāng Fēi),
a loud, strong butcher. Here is their first scene, in our own simple Chinese:

> {东汉|Dōng Hàn}{末|mò}{年|nián}，{天下|tiān xià}{大乱|dà luàn}。{有一天|yǒu yì tiān}，{刘备|Liú Bèi}{在|zài}{城|chéng}{里|lǐ}{看|kàn}{到|dào}{一|yì}{张|zhāng}{告示|gào shi}，{叹|tàn}{了|le}{一|yì}{口|kǒu}{气|qì}。{旁边|páng biān}{一|yí}{个|gè}{人|rén}{大声|dà shēng}{说|shuō}："{大丈夫|dà zhàng fu}{不|bú}{为|wèi}{国家|guó jiā}{出力|chū lì}，
> {叹|tàn}{什么|shén me}{气|qì}？"{这个|zhè ge}{人|rén}{就是|jiù shì}{张飞|Zhāng Fēi}。{两|liǎng}{个|gè}{人|rén}{一起|yì qǐ}{去|qù}{喝|hē}{酒|jiǔ}，{又|yòu}{遇到|yù dào}{了|le}{关羽|Guān Yǔ}。{三|sān}{个|gè}{人|rén}{谈|tán}{得|de}{非常|fēi cháng}{投机|tóu jī}，{都|dōu}{想|xiǎng}{为|wèi}{老百姓|lǎo bǎi xìng}{做|zuò}{点儿|diǎnr}{事|shì}。
>
> {张飞|Zhāng Fēi}{家|jiā}{后面|hòu miàn}{有|yǒu}{一|yí}{个|gè}{桃园|táo yuán}，{正|zhèng}{是|shì}{桃花|táo huā}{开|kāi}{的|de}{时候|shí hou}。{第二天|dì èr tiān}，{三|sān}{个|gè}{人|rén}{在|zài}{桃园|táo yuán}{里|lǐ}{摆上|bǎi shàng}{香|xiāng}，{对|duì}{着|zhe}{天|tiān}{发誓|fā shì}："{我们|wǒ men}{三|sān}{人|rén}{虽然|suī rán}{不|bú}{是|shì}{一家人|yì jiā rén}，
> {但是|dàn shì}{从|cóng}{今天|jīn tiān}{起|qǐ}{结为|jié wéi}{兄弟|xiōng dì}，{同心协力|tóng xīn xié lì}，{救国救民|jiù guó jiù mín}。'{不求|bù qiú}{同|tóng}{年|nián}{同|tóng}{月|yuè}{同|tóng}{日|rì}{生|shēng}，{但愿|dàn yuàn}{同|tóng}{年|nián}{同|tóng}{月|yuè}{同|tóng}{日|rì}{死|sǐ}。'"{按|àn}{年纪|nián jì}，{刘备|Liú Bèi}{是|shì}{大哥|dà gē}，
> {关羽|Guān Yǔ}{是|shì}{二哥|èr gē}，{张飞|Zhāng Fēi}{是|shì}{三弟|sān dì}。

{告示|gào shi}: a public notice; {叹气|tàn qì}: to sigh; {大丈夫|dà zhàng fu} (dà zhàng fu): a real man; {出力|chū lì}: to put in effort; {投机|tóu jī}: to get on well; {桃园|táo yuán}: a peach orchard; {桃花|táo huā}: peach blossom; {摆上|bǎi shàng}{香|xiāng}: to set out incense;
{发誓|fā shì}: to swear; {结为|jié wéi}{兄弟|xiōng dì}: to become sworn brothers; {同心协力|tóng xīn xié lì}: with one heart; {救国救民|jiù guó jiù mín}: to save the
country and the people; {但愿|dàn yuàn}: if only, I wish. The line in single quotation marks, "we don't ask to be born
in the same year, month and day; we only wish to die in the same year, month and day", is the novel's
own (its first chapter); the rest is our retelling.

**Novel and history.** The 《{三国志|Sān guó zhì}》 has no oath. It does say, in {关羽|Guān Yǔ}'s biography, that {刘备|Liú Bèi} treated
{关羽|Guān Yǔ} and {张飞|Zhāng Fēi} like brothers: the three of them shared a bed ({寝则同床|qǐn zé tóng chuáng}, a written phrase), and were {恩若兄弟|ēn ruò xiōng dì}
("as close as brothers"). The novel built its famous scene on lines like these. The oath has become
the model of loyal friendship in China, and {桃园结义|táo yuán jié yì} is a set phrase for it.

## Episode 2: borrowing arrows with straw boats

Before the great battle of the Red Cliffs ({赤壁|Chì bì}, Chì bì, 208), {刘备|Liú Bèi}'s adviser {诸葛亮|Zhū gě Liàng} (Zhūgě Liàng) is
staying with the {吴|Wú} army, the ally of {刘备|Liú Bèi} against {曹操|Cáo Cāo}. The {吴|Wú} commander, {周瑜|Zhōu Yú} (Zhōu Yú), is jealous
of {诸葛亮|Zhū gě Liàng}'s cleverness and sets him an impossible task:

> {周瑜|Zhōu Yú}{对|duì}{诸葛亮|Zhū gě Liàng}{说|shuō}："{我们|wǒ men}{和|hé}{曹操|Cáo Cāo}{打仗|dǎ zhàng}，{需要|xū yào}{十万|shí wàn}{支|zhī}{箭|jiàn}。{请|qǐng}{你|nǐ}{在|zài}{十|shí}{天|tiān}{内|nèi}{做|zuò}{好|hǎo}，{行|xíng}{不|bu}{行|xíng}？"{诸葛亮|Zhū gě Liàng}{说|shuō}："{十|shí}{天|tiān}{太|tài}{长|cháng}{了|le}，{三|sān}{天|tiān}{就|jiù}{够|gòu}{了|le}。
> {要是|yào shi}{做|zuò}{不|bu}{到|dào}，{我|wǒ}{愿意|yuàn yì}{接受|jiē shòu}{处罚|chǔ fá}。"{大家|dà jiā}{都|dōu}{觉得|jué de}{他|tā}{疯|fēng}{了|le}。
>
> {诸葛亮|Zhū gě Liàng}{向|xiàng}{朋友|péng you}{借|jiè}{了|le}{二十|èr shí}{条|tiáo}{船|chuán}，{每|měi}{条|tiáo}{船|chuán}{的|de}{两|liǎng}{边|biān}{放满|fàng mǎn}{了|le}{草把子|cǎo bǎ zi}，{船|chuán}{的|de}{四周|sì zhōu}{用|yòng}{布|bù}{围|wéi}{起来|qǐ lái}。{前|qián}{两|liǎng}{天|tiān}，{他|tā}{什么|shén me}{也|yě}{没|méi}{做|zuò}。{第三天|dì sān tiān}{夜里|yè li}，{江|jiāng}{上|shàng}{起|qǐ}{了|le}
> {大雾|dà wù}，{什么|shén me}{都|dōu}{看不清|kàn bu qīng}。{诸葛亮|Zhū gě Liàng}{让|ràng}{人|rén}{把|bǎ}{船|chuán}{一|yì}{条|tiáo}{一|yì}{条|tiáo}{地|de}{连起来|lián qǐ lái}，{朝|cháo}{着|zhe}{曹操|Cáo Cāo}{的|de}{军营|jūn yíng}{开|kāi}{过去|guò qù}，{船|chuán}{上|shàng}{的|de}{士兵|shì bīng}{一边|yì biān}{打鼓|dǎ gǔ}，{一边|yì biān}{大声|dà shēng}{喊叫|hǎn jiào}。
>
> {曹操|Cáo Cāo}{听|tīng}{到|dào}{声音|shēng yīn}，{以为|yǐ wéi}{敌人|dí rén}{来|lái}{了|le}。{可是|kě shì}{雾|wù}{太|tài}{大|dà}，{他|tā}{不|bù}{敢|gǎn}{让|ràng}{士兵|shì bīng}{出去|chū qù}，{就|jiù}{让|ràng}{弓箭手|gōng jiàn shǒu}{朝|cháo}{着|zhe}{江|jiāng}{上|shàng}{不|bù}{停|tíng}{地|de}{射箭|shè jiàn}。{箭|jiàn}{一支|yì zhī}{一支|yì zhī}{地|de}{射|shè}{在|zài}
> {草把子|cǎo bǎ zi}{上|shàng}。{过|guò}{了|le}{一会儿|yí huìr}，{诸葛亮|Zhū gě Liàng}{让|ràng}{船|chuán}{掉过头来|diào guò tóu lái}，{让|ràng}{另|lìng}{一边|yì biān}{也|yě}{受箭|shòu jiàn}。{天|tiān}{快|kuài}{亮|liàng}{的|de}{时候|shí hou}，{船|chuán}{上|shàng}{已经|yǐ jīng}{插满|chā mǎn}{了|le}{箭|jiàn}，{诸葛亮|Zhū gě Liàng}{这才|zhè cái}{高高兴兴|gāo gāo xìng xìng}{地|de}
> {回去|huí qù}{了|le}。{一|yì}{数|shǔ}，{正好|zhèng hǎo}{十万|shí wàn}{多|duō}{支|zhī}。{周瑜|Zhōu Yú}{听|tīng}{了|le}，
> {不得不|bù dé bù}{说|shuō}："{诸葛亮|Zhū gě Liàng}{真|zhēn}{是|shì}{比|bǐ}{我|wǒ}{聪明|cōng ming}{啊|a}！"

{箭|jiàn} (jiàn): an arrow; {支|zhī} (lesson 10): the measure word for arrows; {处罚|chǔ fá}: punishment; {草把子|cǎo bǎ zi}: bundles of straw;
{布|bù} (lesson 22's character): cloth; {雾|wù} (lesson 29): fog; {连起来|lián qǐ lái}: to tie together; {军营|jūn yíng}: a camp; {士兵|shì bīng}: soldiers;
{打鼓|dǎ gǔ} ({鼓|gǔ}, lesson 10): to beat drums; {喊叫|hǎn jiào}: to shout; {弓箭手|gōng jiàn shǒu}: archers; {射箭|shè jiàn}: to shoot arrows; {插满|chā mǎn}: to be
stuck full of; {掉过头来|diào guò tóu lái}: to turn round; {受箭|shòu jiàn}: to take the arrows; {这才|zhè cái}: only then; {不得不|bù dé bù} (HSK 4): to have to.

**Novel and history.** No history credits {诸葛亮|Zhū gě Liàng} with this trick. A similar story is told about {孙权|Sūn Quán},
the ruler of {吴|Wú}, in 213 at the Battle of {濡须|Rú xū} (Rú xū). According to an early history quoted in the
notes to the 《{三国志|Sān guó zhì}》, {孙权|Sūn Quán} sailed out in a big boat to look at {曹操|Cáo Cāo}'s army; {曹操|Cáo Cāo}'s archers shot at it
until one side of the boat was so full of arrows that it began to tip over, and {孙权|Sūn Quán} turned the boat
round so that the other side took arrows too, and sailed home safely. The novel gave the story to
{诸葛亮|Zhū gě Liàng}, made it a plan, and added the fog, the straw and the hundred thousand arrows.

## Why it matters

- **Sayings about its characters** are in everyday Chinese (folk sayings, not lines from the novel). {三|sān}{个|gè}{臭皮匠|chòu pí jiang}，{顶|dǐng}{个|gè}{诸葛亮|Zhū gě Liàng} ("three cobblers together
  make a {诸葛亮|Zhū gě Liàng}": three ordinary people, put together, are as clever as a genius), {说|shuō}{曹操|Cáo Cāo}，{曹操|Cáo Cāo}{到|dào} ("speak
  of {曹操|Cáo Cāo} and he appears": speak of the devil).
- **The characters live on stage and on screen.** {关羽|Guān Yǔ} with his red face (HSK 3's Peking opera
  lesson), {诸葛亮|Zhū gě Liàng} with his feather fan ({扇子|shàn zi}, lesson 25), {张飞|Zhāng Fēi} shouting: every Chinese audience knows them.
- **Keep the two apart.** When someone says "in the Three Kingdoms…", ask: the novel, or the history?
  Both are worth knowing, but they don't always agree.

## Reading: a visitor's question

Anna is guiding a group of British students round a museum exhibition on the Three Kingdoms (she
volunteers there in her final year), and one of them asks her a question.

> {一|yí}{个|gè}{英国|Yīng guó}{学生|xué sheng}{问|wèn}{安娜|Ān nà}："{我|wǒ}{看|kàn}{过|guo}{一|yí}{部|bù}{三国|Sān guó}{的|de}{电影|diàn yǐng}，{里面|lǐ miàn}{的|de}{诸葛亮|Zhū gě Liàng}{用|yòng}{草|cǎo}{船|chuán}{借|jiè}{了|le}{十万|shí wàn}{支|zhī}{箭|jiàn}。{这|zhè}{是|shì}{真|zhēn}{的|de}{吗|ma}？"
>
