1. Which work is history, and which is a novel?
2. According to Anna, what in the novel is mostly real?
3. What really happened, according to the history, that is like the straw-boats story?
4. What is Anna's advice, and how does she feel about the novel?

<details>
<summary>Answers and translation</summary>

1. 《{三国志|Sān guó zhì}》, by {陈寿|Chén Shòu}, is history; 《{三国演义|Sān guó yǎn yì}》, of the Ming dynasty, attributed to {罗贯中|Luó Guàn zhōng}, is a novel.
2. The people, the states and the big events.
3. Someone's boat really was shot full of arrows, but it was {孙权|Sūn Quán} of {吴|Wú}, not {诸葛亮|Zhū gě Liàng}, and he didn't set
   out to collect them.
4. Enjoy the novel and the films, but don't take them for a history book. She likes the novel: its
   {诸葛亮|Zhū gě Liàng} is much more interesting than the real one.

"A British student asked Anna: 'I saw a film about the Three Kingdoms in which Zhuge Liang borrowed
a hundred thousand arrows with straw boats. Is it true?' Anna smiled: 'That's a question lots of
people ask. First we need to tell two things apart: history and the novel. The Three Kingdoms
period ran from 220 to 280, when China was split into three states, Wei, Shu and Wu. Later a man
called Chen Shou wrote this history into the *Records of the Three Kingdoms*. The *Romance of the
Three Kingdoms* is a novel that only appeared more than a thousand years later, in the Ming dynasty;
tradition says its author was Luo Guanzhong.'

"'So are the stories in the novel all made up?'

"'Not all of them. Most of the people, the states and the big events really existed. But many of the
details, such as the straw boats, were added by the author. In history someone's boat really was
shot full of arrows, but that person was Sun Quan of Wu, not Zhuge Liang, and he didn't go out on
purpose to "borrow" arrows.'

"Another student asked: 'What about the oath in the peach garden?' Anna said: 'The history books
don't say they swore an oath in a peach garden. They only say Liu Bei treated Guan Yu and Zhang Fei
very well, and the three of them slept in one bed, like brothers. The novel turned those few lines
into a famous story. Even Guan Yu's red face was added later, by novels and plays.'

"'And was Zhuge Liang a real person?'

"'Of course. He was a famous chancellor of Shu, and in history he was very clever too, just not as
superhuman as in the novel.'

"The students said, one after another, 'So that's how it was!' Anna went on: 'That's why people say
the *Romance* is "seven parts fact, three parts fiction". Reading the novel and watching the films is
fine; just don't treat them as a history book. But to tell the truth, the Zhuge Liang of the novel
is far more interesting than the real one!' Everyone laughed. One student said: 'When I get home, I'm going to read the novel first, and then the
history books!'"
</details>

## Key points

- History: the Three Kingdoms, {魏|Wèi} {蜀|Shǔ} {吴|Wú}, about 220–280, recorded in {陈寿|Chén Shòu}'s 《{三国志|Sān guó zhì}》 (late third century).
- The novel: 《{三国演义|Sān guó yǎn yì}》, Ming, traditionally attributed to {罗贯中|Luó Guàn zhōng} (14th century, little known); oldest
  surviving edition 1522; the usual 120-chapter text revised in the 1660s.
- {天下|tiān xià}{大势|dà shì}，{分久必合|fēn jiǔ bì hé}，{合久必分|hé jiǔ bì fēn}: the novel's view of history in its first sentence.
- {桃园结义|táo yuán jié yì} (the peach garden oath) and {草船借箭|cǎo chuán jiè jiàn} (borrowing arrows with straw boats) are the novel's;
  the history has the brotherly bond, and a boat full of arrows belonging to {孙权|Sūn Quán}.
- {七分事实|qī fēn shì shí}，{三分虚构|sān fēn xū gòu}: enjoy the novel, don't read it as history.

lessons.title: Shadow puppets
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

At a Spring Festival temple fair ({庙会|miào huì}, miào huì) you may still come across a small stage with a
white screen glowing in the dark and coloured figures fighting, dancing and flying across it to the
sound of drums and singing. This is {皮影戏|pí yǐng xì} (pí yǐng xì), shadow puppetry: "the play of leather
shadows". This lesson explains what the figures are, how they're made and worked, where the art is
found, and how it has been handed down ({流传|liú chuán}), the theme of lesson 25.

Words you'll meet, glossed where they appear: {皮影|pí yǐng} (a leather shadow figure), {幕布|mù bù} (the screen),
{关节|guān jié} (a joint), {艺人|yì rén} (a performer, an artist), {唱腔|chàng qiāng} (the singing style).

## Figures, screen and light

A shadow play needs three things:

- **The figures** ({皮影|pí yǐng}, {影人|yǐng rén}). In UNESCO's words, they are colourful silhouettes made of **leather or
  paper**. Leather ones are made of animal hide (donkey, goat and sheep hide are all recorded), scraped until it's thin enough to let light through, then carved and coloured,
  so that on the screen they glow like stained glass rather than showing as black shadows.
- **The screen** ({幕布|mù bù}), a sheet of white cloth stretched on a frame, with **a light behind it**: once
  an oil lamp, now usually an electric one.
- **The puppeteers** behind the screen, who move each figure with thin **rods** ({杆子|gān zi}, gānzi). The main rod
  holds the figure at the neck, and usually two more move the hands.

Each figure has **between twelve and twenty-four moveable joints** ({关节|guān jié}), according to UNESCO, at
the neck, shoulders, elbows, waist and knees, so it can walk, bow, fight and turn. Heads are often
made separately and changed, so one body can play many characters. In many traditions the faces
follow the role types of Chinese opera: the upright and loyal look one way, the villains another, and
clowns have their own painted faces.

## Music and stories

A shadow play is music theatre. According to UNESCO, the performances are **accompanied by music and
singing**, and the performers need many skills: improvised singing, falsetto ({假声|jiǎ shēng}, jiǎ shēng), playing
several instruments, and working the figures, often all at once. A large troupe has **seven to nine
performers**, a small one **two to five**.

The stories come from history, legend and popular novels: tales of the Three Kingdoms (this module's
25h1) were favourites already in the Song dynasty, according to one history of the art, long before the
novel was written down; gods, ghosts and lovers have their plays too. Battles are the
audience's delight: horses gallop, swords flash, and a figure can be made to fly or turn head over
heels in a way no human actor could.

## Where and when

Shadow puppetry is found in many provinces of China, each with its own styles of carving, music and
singing ({唱腔|chàng qiāng}). Among the best known are the styles of {陕西|Shǎn xī} (Shǎnxī, Shaanxi in the north-west), of
{滦州|Luán zhōu} (Luánzhōu, in Hebei, around today's {唐山|Táng shān} Tángshān), and of Shandong and Sichuan; it's also
performed in Taiwan.

It was performed above all for entertainment, and for religious rituals, weddings, funerals and other
special occasions (UNESCO). Some puppeteers were professionals; others were farmers who performed in
the slack farming seasons.

**How old is it?** A well-known legend links shadow theatre to Emperor Wu of the Han dynasty ({汉武帝|Hàn Wǔ dì},
who reigned in the second and first centuries BCE), who is said to have been consoled after the death of a beloved consort when
a magician cast her shadow on a curtain. Historians of puppetry treat this as a story, not a record.
What is clear is that by the **Song dynasty** (960–1279) shadow plays were a popular entertainment in
the cities.

**Handed down.** The skills, UNESCO says, are passed on **in families, in troupes, and from master to
pupil**, and many older performers can perform dozens of traditional plays. In **2011** Chinese shadow
puppetry was inscribed on UNESCO's Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity.
Today troupes also perform in theatres, schools and museums, and on video.

## Reading: a shadow play at the temple fair

Anna writes about the third day of the New Year, which she spent with Wang Fang at a temple fair.
The fair, the troupe and the puppeteer are invented.

> {就|jiù}{能|néng}{演|yǎn}{另|lìng}{一|yí}{个|gè}{人物|rén wù}。{以前|yǐ qián}{村|cūn}{里|lǐ}{有人|yǒu rén}{结婚|jié hūn}、{过节|guò jié}，{常常|cháng cháng}{请|qǐng}{他们|tā men}{去|qù}{表演|biǎo yǎn}，{一|yì}{演|yǎn}{就是|jiù shì}{一|yí}{个|gè}{晚上|wǎn shang}。
>
> {我|wǒ}{问|wèn}{他|tā}，{现在|xiàn zài}{年轻人|nián qīng rén}{还|hái}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{看|kàn}{皮影戏|pí yǐng xì}{吗|ma}？{他|tā}{想|xiǎng}{了|le}{想|xiǎng}{说|shuō}："{看|kàn}{的|de}{人|rén}{确实|què shí}{比|bǐ}{以前|yǐ qián}{少|shǎo}{了|le}。{不过|bú guò}{这|zhè}{几|jǐ}{年|nián}，{常常|cháng cháng}{有|yǒu}{学校|xué xiào}{请|qǐng}{我们|wǒ men}{去|qù}{表演|biǎo yǎn}，
> {还|hái}{有|yǒu}{孩子|hái zi}{跟|gēn}{我|wǒ}{学|xué}{刻|kè}{皮影|pí yǐng}。{只要|zhǐ yào}{有人|yǒu rén}{愿意|yuàn yì}{学|xué}，{这|zhè}{门|mén}{手艺|shǒu yì}{就|jiù}{会|huì}{传下去|chuán xià qù}。"
>
> {离开|lí kāi}{的|de}{时候|shí hou}，{孔师傅|Kǒng shī fu}{送|sòng}{给|gěi}{我|wǒ}{一|yí}{个|gè}{小小|xiǎo xiǎo}{的|de}{皮影|pí yǐng}：{一|yì}{只|zhī}{红色|hóng sè}{的|de}{小|xiǎo}{猪|zhū}。{他|tā}{说|shuō}："{明年|míng nián}{是|shì}{猪|zhū}{年|nián}，{送|sòng}{你|nǐ}{一|yí}{个|gè}{好运|hǎo yùn}！"

{大|dà}{年初|nián chū}{三|sān}: the third day of the New Year ({初|chū}{三|sān}); {人山人海|rén shān rén hǎi}: crowds of people (an idiom); {将军|jiāng jūn} (jiāng jūn): a
general; {透亮|tòu liàng}: shining, translucent; {锣鼓|luó gǔ} (luó gǔ): gongs and drums; {艺人|yì rén}: a performer; {小人儿|xiǎo rénr}: the little
figures; {翻跟头|fān gēn tou} (fān gēn tou): to turn somersaults; {唱词|chàng cí}: the words of a song; {着迷|zháo mí}: to be enthralled;
{叫好|jiào hǎo}: to cheer; {杆子|gān zi}: a rod, a pole; {操作|cāo zuò} (lesson 19): to operate; {驴皮|lǘ pí} (lǘ pí): donkey hide; {刮|guā}{得|de}{很|hěn}{薄|báo}: scraped very thin; {刻|kè} (HSK 3's {刻|kè}): to
carve; {花纹|huā wén}: a pattern; {上颜色|shàng yán sè}: to colour in; {手艺|shǒu yì}: a craft, a skill; {门|mén}: the measure word for a craft or
a subject.

1. What did Anna see on the screen first, and why did the figure look "like glass"?
2. How many people were working the show behind the screen, and what did each do?
3. How did {孔师傅|Kǒng shī fu} learn his craft, and why is he hopeful about its future?
4. What does the last gift suggest about the date and about {孔师傅|Kǒng shī fu}?

<details>
<summary>Answers and translation</summary>

1. A general on horseback; the leather figure is thin and coloured, so the lamp shines through it.
2. Three: one sang, one played the drums, and one worked two figures at once with three thin rods.
3. From his father, who learned from his grandfather: it was handed down in the family. Schools
   invite them to perform, and some children are learning to carve figures: as long as someone wants
   to learn, the craft will be passed on.
4. Next year will be a pig year, so he gives her a pig "for good luck": he's warm and
   generous, and the gift fits the New Year customs of lesson 25.

"On the third day of the New Year Wang Fang took me to a temple fair. It was packed with people:
there were stalls selling snacks, people performing martial arts, and a tiny stage with a white
screen hung in front of it. Wang Fang said: 'Quick, the shadow play's about to start!'

"The moment the lamp came on, a general on horseback appeared behind the screen. His clothes were
red and green, and lit by the lamp they shone like glass. Next an enemy charged out from the other
side, and the two of them began to fight. The gongs and drums never stopped, and the performers
behind sang while they made the little figures turn somersaults. Although I couldn't really follow
the words, I was spellbound, and the children beside me were clapping and cheering loudly.

"After the show, an old performer named Kong invited us behind the screen to have a look. It turned
out there were only three people: one singing, one drumming, and one working two figures at the same
time with three thin rods. Master Kong told me the figures were made of donkey hide: first the hide is
scraped very thin, then the patterns are carved out cut by cut, and last of all it's coloured. 'A
good figure takes thousands of cuts,' he said with a smile. 'I learned this craft from my father,
and my father learned it from my grandfather.'

"Master Kong also opened an old trunk to show us: it held hundreds of figures, some of them very old.
He said the figures' heads and bodies are separate, so by changing the head you can play another
character. In the old days, when people in the villages married or held a festival, they often
invited his troupe to perform, and a show would go on all night.

"I asked him whether young people still liked shadow plays. He thought for a moment and said: 'It's
true fewer people watch than before. But these last few years schools have often invited us to
perform, and there are children learning to carve figures with me. As long as someone wants to
learn, this craft will be passed on.'

"When we left, Master Kong gave me a tiny figure: a little red pig. He said: 'Next year is the Year of
the Pig: here's some good luck for you!'"
</details>

## Key points

- {皮影戏|pí yǐng xì}: figures of leather (or paper), thin, carved and coloured, worked with rods behind a white
  screen lit from behind; 12 to 24 joints; music and singing.
- Troupes of two to nine; stories from history, legend and novels such as the 《{三国演义|Sān guó yǎn yì}》.
- Found in many provinces, each with its styles ({陕西|Shǎn xī}, {滦州|Luán zhōu} / {唐山|Táng shān}, Shandong, Sichuan…); popular by the
  Song dynasty; the Han legend of Emperor Wu is a legend.
- Handed down in families, troupes and from master to pupil; on UNESCO's Representative List in 2011.

lessons.title: Making an argument
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

Module 6 is about the Chinese you need to say what you think and back it up: in a discussion, in an
essay and in the HSK 5 exam, whose writing part ends with a short essay on a set theme. The level-5
standard asks you to discuss an everyday social phenomenon: describe it, give your view with
reasons and evidence, and come to a conclusion. This lesson gives you the tools:

- {可见|kě jiàn} and {由此|yóu cǐ}{可见|kě jiàn}: "so it can be seen that…", the words that lead from facts to a conclusion;
- {使得|shǐ de} and {促使|cù shǐ}: one thing causing another;
- {在于|zài yú}: where the point lies ({问题|wèn tí}{在于|zài yú}…, {关键|guān jiàn}{在于|zài yú}…);
- {针对|zhēn duì} (aimed at) and {围绕|wéi rào} (centred on);
- {视为|shì wéi}, {看作|kàn zuò} and {属于|shǔ yú}: putting something in a category;
- the vocabulary of an argument: {观点|guān diǎn}, {理由|lǐ yóu}, {事实|shì shí}, {证据|zhèng jù}, {客观|kè guān} / {主观|zhǔ guān}, {具体|jù tǐ}, {合理|hé lǐ}, {有力|yǒu lì}…

The story moves on too. {王芳|Wáng Fāng} (Wang Fang) is now a reporter at the news website, and her editor
{郑华|Zhèng Huá} (Zheng Hua) wants a story on online reviews. At the end of the lesson you'll read Wang Fang's
commentary and write an argued essay of your own.

## {可见|kě jiàn} and {由此|yóu cǐ}{可见|kě jiàn}: drawing a conclusion

{可见|kě jiàn} (it can be seen that, which shows that) introduces the **[[conclusion]]** that a fact points to.
The fact comes first, then a comma or a full stop, then {可见|kě jiàn}:

{这|zhè}{本|běn}{书|shū}{三|sān}{个|gè}{月|yuè}{卖|mài}{了|le}{十万|shí wàn}{本|běn}，{可见|kě jiàn}{很|hěn}{受|shòu}{读者|dú zhě}{欢迎|huān yíng}。 — The book sold a hundred thousand copies in three months, which shows how popular it is with readers.

{这|zhè}{道|dào}{题|tí}{全|quán}{班|bān}{只有|zhǐ yǒu}{两|liǎng}{个|gè}{人|rén}{做|zuò}{对|duì}{了|le}，{可见|kě jiàn}{难度|nán dù}{相当|xiāng dāng}{大|dà}。 — Only two people in the whole class got this question right: it must be really hard.

{他|tā}{每|měi}{天|tiān}{都|dōu}{练|liàn}{两|liǎng}{个|gè}{小时|xiǎo shí}{钢琴|gāng qín}，{可见|kě jiàn}{是|shì}{真|zhēn}{的|de}{热爱|rè ài}{音乐|yīn yuè}。 — He practises the piano for two hours every day: he clearly loves music.

In speech you'd often say {看来|kàn lái} (it seems) or {说明|shuō míng} (that shows): {他|tā}{每|měi}{天|tiān}{都|dōu}{练|liàn}{两|liǎng}{个|gè}{小时|xiǎo shí}，{看来|kàn lái}{是|shì}{真|zhēn}{的|de}{喜欢|xǐ huan}。 {可见|kě jiàn}
is a little more formal and states the conclusion more firmly.

{由此|yóu cǐ}{可见|kě jiàn} (from this it can be seen that) is the written version for a conclusion drawn from several
facts. It usually starts a new sentence or a new paragraph, often the last one of an essay:

{由此|yóu cǐ}{可见|kě jiàn}，{学习|xué xí}{的|de}{效果|xiào guǒ}{不|bú}{在于|zài yú}{时间|shí jiān}{长短|cháng duǎn}，{而|ér}{在于|zài yú}{方法|fāng fǎ}。 — It's clear from this that how well you learn depends not on how long you study but on how you do it.

{由此|yóu cǐ} is "from this" (lesson 27 has more words like it), and {可见|kě jiàn} "it can be seen". Use {由此|yóu cǐ}{可见|kě jiàn} once, at
the point where your facts add up. An essay with a {可见|kě jiàn} in every paragraph sounds as if it's
proving the same thing over and over.

> {可见|kě jiàn} and {由此|yóu cǐ}{可见|kě jiàn} are **[[discourse markers]]**: words that don't add facts but show how one part of a
> text relates to another. You know others: {首先|shǒu xiān}, {其次|qí cì}, {总之|zǒng zhī} (lesson 16), {另外|lìng wài}, {因此|yīn cǐ}. An argued text
> uses a few of them to guide the reader from the problem to the conclusion.

## {使得|shǐ de} and {促使|cù shǐ}: making something happen

{使得|shǐ de} (to make, cause) takes a whole clause: the cause is the subject, and what happens is the clause
after {使得|shǐ de}. It's written style, a heavier {使|shǐ} or {让|ràng}:

{这|zhè}{场|chǎng}{大|dà}{雨|yǔ}{使得|shǐ de}{很|hěn}{多|duō}{航班|háng bān}{推迟|tuī chí}{了|le}。 — The heavy rain caused many flights to be delayed.

{网络|wǎng luò}{的|de}{普及|pǔ jí}{使得|shǐ de}{人|rén}{们|men}{的|de}{生活|shēng huó}{方式|fāng shì}{发生|fā shēng}{了|le}{很|hěn}{大|dà}{的|de}{变化|biàn huà}。 — The spread of the internet has changed the way people live a great deal.

{促使|cù shǐ} (to prompt, push someone to) usually takes a person and what the person then does: something
pushes someone into an action.

{那|nà}{次|cì}{失败|shī bài}{促使|cù shǐ}{他|tā}{重新|chóng xīn}{考虑|kǎo lǜ}{自己|zì jǐ}{的|de}{计划|jì huà}。 — That failure prompted him to rethink his plans.

{一|yí}{次|cì}{去|qù}{中国|Zhōng guó}{的|de}{旅行|lǚ xíng}{促使|cù shǐ}{她|tā}{下|xià}{决心|jué xīn}{学|xué}{好|hǎo}{中文|Zhōng wén}。 — A trip to China made her determined to learn Chinese properly.

| Word | Register | Typical use |
|---|---|---|
| {让|ràng} / {叫|jiào} | spoken | {这|zhè}{件|jiàn}{事|shì}{让|ràng}{我|wǒ}{很|hěn}{高兴|gāo xìng}。 |
| {使|shǐ} (HSK 4) | written and spoken | {这|zhè}{件|jiàn}{事|shì}{使|shǐ}{我|wǒ}{很|hěn}{高兴|gāo xìng}。 |
| {令|lìng} (lesson 14) | written | feelings: {令|lìng}{人|rén}{失望|shī wàng}, {令|lìng}{人|rén}{感动|gǎn dòng} |
| {使得|shǐ de} | written | a result: {大|dà}{雨|yǔ}{使得|shǐ de}{航班|háng bān}{推迟|tuī chí}{了|le}。 |
| {促使|cù shǐ} | written | pushes someone to act: {促使|cù shǐ}{他|tā}{改变|gǎi biàn}{计划|jì huà} |

## {在于|zài yú}: where the point lies

X {在于|zài yú} Y says that X lies in Y, rests on Y: Y is the heart of the matter. It's how an argument
names the real issue:

{问题|wèn tí}{在于|zài yú}{时间|shí jiān}{不够|bú gòu}。 — The problem is that there isn't enough time.

{成功|chéng gōng}{的|de}{关键|guān jiàn}{在于|zài yú}{坚持|jiān chí}。 — The key to success lies in keeping at it.

{这|zhè}{两|liǎng}{个|gè}{词|cí}{的|de}{区别|qū bié}{在于|zài yú}{语气|yǔ qì}。 — The difference between these two words lies in their tone.

The subject of {在于|zài yú} is usually an abstract noun: {问题|wèn tí}, {关键|guān jiàn}, {原因|yuán yīn}, {区别|qū bié}, {价值|jià zhí}, {意义|yì yì}. With {不|bú}{在于|zài yú}…{而|ér}{在于|zài yú}… you
reject one answer and give the right one: {问题|wèn tí}{不|bú}{在于|zài yú}{钱|qián}，{而|ér}{在于|zài yú}{时间|shí jiān}。 (The problem isn't money: it's time.)

{在于|zài yú} can also mean "depends on, is up to": {去|qù}{不|bu}{去|qù}，{在于|zài yú}{你|nǐ}{自己|zì jǐ}。 (Whether you go is up to you.)

## {针对|zhēn duì} and {围绕|wéi rào}: aimed at, centred on

{针对|zhēn duì} (to be aimed at, to target) points what you do or say at a particular problem or group. It
starts a phrase before the verb, or describes a noun with {的|de}:

{针对|zhēn duì}{这个|zhè ge}{问题|wèn tí}，{学校|xué xiào}{采取|cǎi qǔ}{了|le}{新|xīn}{的|de}{措施|cuò shī}。 — The school has taken new measures to deal with this problem.

{这|zhè}{本|běn}{教材|jiào cái}{是|shì}{针对|zhēn duì}{初级|chū jí}{学生|xué sheng}{的|de}。 — This textbook is aimed at beginners.

{很|hěn}{多|duō}{人|rén}{都|dōu}{针对|zhēn duì}{同一|tóng yī}{个|gè}{问题|wèn tí}{提出|tí chū}{了|le}{意见|yì jiàn}。 — Many people have raised complaints about the same problem.

{围绕|wéi rào} (to go round; to centre on) is first a movement round something, then a topic that everything
turns on:

{地球|dì qiú}{围绕|wéi rào}{着|zhe}{太阳|tài yang}{转|zhuàn}。 — The earth goes round the sun.

{这|zhè}{次|cì}{讨论|tǎo lùn}{围绕|wéi rào}{网上|wǎng shàng}{评价|píng jià}{展开|zhǎn kāi}。 — The discussion centred on online reviews.

So {针对|zhēn duì} is about a target (a problem to solve, people to reach) and {围绕|wéi rào} about a centre (a topic to
keep to). An essay should {围绕|wéi rào} its theme; a measure is taken {针对|zhēn duì} a problem.

## {视为|shì wéi}, {看作|kàn zuò} and {属于|shǔ yú}: putting things in a category

{把|bǎ} A {视为|shì wéi} B and {把|bǎ} A {看作|kàn zuò} B both mean "to regard A as B". {视为|shì wéi} is written and formal, often in the
passive ({被|bèi}{视为|shì wéi}); {看作|kàn zuò} is neutral. Lesson 12's {当作|dàng zuò} is closer to "to treat as" and is about how you
act:

{茶|chá}{被|bèi}{视为|shì wéi}{中国|Zhōng guó}{文化|wén huà}{的|de}{代表|dài biǎo}{之|zhī}{一|yī}。 — Tea is regarded as one of the symbols of Chinese culture.

{很|hěn}{多|duō}{人|rén}{把|bǎ}{这|zhè}{次|cì}{失败|shī bài}{看作|kàn zuò}{一|yí}{次|cì}{学习|xué xí}{的|de}{机会|jī huì}。 — Many people see this failure as a chance to learn.

{他|tā}{把|bǎ}{我|wǒ}{当作|dàng zuò}{自己|zì jǐ}{的|de}{弟弟|dì di}。 — He treats me like his own younger brother.

{属于|shǔ yú} (to belong to) puts something in a class or gives its owner:

{这个|zhè ge}{问题|wèn tí}{属于|shǔ yú}{技术|jì shù}{问题|wèn tí}，{不|bù}{属于|shǔ yú}{管理|guǎn lǐ}{问题|wèn tí}。 — This is a technical problem, not a management one.

{这些|zhè xiē}{书|shū}{属于|shǔ yú}{学校|xué xiào}{图书馆|tú shū guǎn}，{不|bù}{能|néng}{带|dài}{回|huí}{家|jiā}。 — These books belong to the school library and can't be taken home.

{处于|chǔ yú} (chǔ yú, to be in a situation or state) is the {处|chǔ} chǔ of lesson 11: {公司|gōng sī}{现在|xiàn zài}{处于|chǔ yú}{困难|kùn nan}{时期|shí qī}。 (The company is
going through a difficult period.) {他|tā}{处于|chǔ yú}{不利|bú lì}{的|de}{位置|wèi zhì}。 (He's in an unfavourable position.)

## The words of an argument

An argument has a **[[viewpoint]]** ({观点|guān diǎn}), **[[reasons]]** ({理由|lǐ yóu}) and **[[evidence]]** ({证据|zhèng jù}): facts ({事实|shì shí}) and
examples that support it. The facts and reasons a writer gives are called {论据|lùn jù} (lùn jù, the
grounds of an argument: HSK 6's word), and the conclusion is {结论|jié lùn} (lesson 16). These are the words
you'll need to build one:

| Words | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| {观点|guān diǎn} | a point of view, a position | {我|wǒ}{同意|tóng yì}{你|nǐ}{的|de}{观点|guān diǎn}。 |
| {理由|lǐ yóu} | a reason (for a view or a choice) | {你|nǐ}{有|yǒu}{什么|shén me}{理由|lǐ yóu}{这么|zhè me}{说|shuō}？ |
| {事实|shì shí} | a fact | {事实|shì shí}{证明|zhèng míng}，{他|tā}{是|shì}{对|duì}{的|de}。 |
| {证据|zhèng jù} | evidence | {你|nǐ}{这么|zhè me}{说|shuō}，{有|yǒu}{证据|zhèng jù}{吗|ma}？ |
| {道理|dào li} | sense, a good reason | {你|nǐ}{说|shuō}{得|de}{很|hěn}{有|yǒu}{道理|dào li}。 |
| {现象|xiàn xiàng} | a phenomenon, something that happens | {这|zhè}{种|zhǒng}{现象|xiàn xiàng}{很|hěn}{普遍|pǔ biàn}。 |
| {因素|yīn sù} | a factor | {天气|tiān qì}{是|shì}{一|yí}{个|gè}{重要|zhòng yào}{的|de}{因素|yīn sù}。 |
| {角度|jiǎo dù} | an angle, a point of view | {换|huàn}{个|gè}{角度|jiǎo dù}{看|kàn}{这个|zhè ge}{问题|wèn tí}。 |
| {程度|chéng dù} | a degree, an extent | {在|zài}{很|hěn}{大|dà}{程度|chéng dù}{上|shàng} (to a great extent) |
| {范围|fàn wéi} | a scope, a range | {调查|diào chá}{的|de}{范围|fàn wéi}{太|tài}{小|xiǎo}{了|le}。 |
| {价值|jià zhí} | value, worth | {这些|zhè xiē}{意见|yì jiàn}{很|hěn}{有|yǒu}{价值|jià zhí}。 |
| {疑问|yí wèn} | a doubt, a question | {我|wǒ}{还|hái}{有|yǒu}{一|yí}{个|gè}{疑问|yí wèn}。 |
| {现实|xiàn shí} | reality; realistic | {这个|zhè ge}{计划|jì huà}{不|bú}{太|tài}{现实|xiàn shí}。 |
| {细节|xì jié} | a detail | {好|hǎo}{的|de}{评价|píng jià}{有|yǒu}{很|hěn}{多|duō}{细节|xì jié}。 |
| {特征|tè zhēng} | a characteristic (written) | {这|zhè}{种|zhǒng}{花|huā}{的|de}{特征|tè zhēng}{是|shì}{颜色|yán sè}{很|hěn}{深|shēn}。 |
| {差别|chā bié} | a difference | {两|liǎng}{种|zhǒng}{方法|fāng fǎ}{的|de}{差别|chā bié}{不|bú}{大|dà}。 |
| {整体|zhěng tǐ} | the whole | {从|cóng}{整体|zhěng tǐ}{来|lái}{看|kàn}，{情况|qíng kuàng}{不错|bú cuò}。 |

- {补|bǔ}: 衤 (the clothing radical, the side form of {衣|yī}) and 卜 bǔ, which gives the sound exactly. 衤 has one
  stroke more than 礻 (as in {社|shè}, {神|shén}): mending is done to clothes. Traditional 補 has the same 衤 on the left and 甫
  on the right (12 strokes).
- {范|fàn}: 艹 on top, then 氵 and 㔾 below. In traditional script {范围|fàn wéi} is written 範圍, with a different character, 範
  ({竹|zhú} on top, 15 strokes). The character {范|fàn} itself is kept in traditional script as a surname ({范|Fàn}).
- {乏|fá}: only four strokes: a left-falling stroke, a dot, a horizontal that turns into a left-falling stroke, and
  the long right-falling stroke. It's in {缺乏|quē fá} (to lack).
- {属|shǔ}: 尸 on top, as in {层|céng} and {屋|wū}, over a part with {口|kǒu} inside. Traditional 屬 keeps 尸, over a longer part (氺 above 蜀) (21 strokes).
- {绕|rào}: 纟 (silk) and 尧, a sound part you've met in {烧|shāo} shāo (lesson 07) and {浇|jiāo} jiāo (lesson 09). Its
  sound has drifted: it no longer matches rào. Traditional 繞 has 糸 and 堯 (18 strokes).
- {殊|shū}: 歹 on the left and 朱 (zhū) on the right, which gives a close sound: zhū, shū.
- {素|sù}: the top of {青|qīng} and {责|zé}, then 糸 (silk) below. It's in {因素|yīn sù} (a factor) and in {素|sù} "plain,
  vegetarian" (HSK 6).

The radical 衤 (clothing) has come up before in {被|bèi}, {裤|kù} and {袜|wà}: all of them are about
cloth, or once were. 歹 is the radical of death and harm ({死|sǐ}): in {殊|shū} it has nothing to do with
either.

### Stroke order

- **{补|bǔ}**: 衤 first: the dot, the horizontal-turn-left-falling stroke, the vertical, the left-falling and the short dot on
  the right; then 卜: the vertical and its dot.
- **{乏|fá}**: the left-falling stroke on top, then the dot, then the horizontal that turns down to the left, and the long
  right-falling stroke at the bottom last.
- **{殊|shū}**: 歹 first, with its last stroke a dot; then 朱: the left-falling stroke, the two horizontals, the
  vertical, then the left-falling stroke and the right-falling stroke at the bottom.

1. What is the writer's main point?
2. Give the two reasons the writer finds for good reviews that aren't genuine.
3. Why, according to the writer, are bad reviews worth reading?
4. The writer says good reviews still have value. What does this tell you about the writer's attitude

<details>
<summary>Answers and translation</summary>

1. Online reviews still have value; what matters is reading them well: look at the details, take bad
   reviews seriously and treat reviews as one source among others ({{关键|guān jiàn}{在于|zài yú}{我们|wǒ men}{能|néng}{不|bu}{能|néng}{从|cóng}{大量|dà liàng}{评价|píng jià}{中|zhōng}{找|zhǎo}{出|chū}{真实|zhēn shí}、{有用|yǒu yòng}{的|de}{信息|xìn xī}}).
2. Some sellers pay for good reviews (small presents, cash, or paid fake reviews); and reviews are
   subjective anyway, since people's tastes differ ({{评价|píng jià}{本来|běn lái}{就是|jiù shì}{很|hěn}{主观|zhǔ guān}{的|de}}).
3. If many people complain about the same problem, the problem is probably real
   ({{如果|rú guǒ}{很|hěn}{多|duō}{人|rén}{都|dōu}{针对|zhēn duì}{同一|tóng yī}{个|gè}{问题|wèn tí}{提出|tí chū}{意见|yì jiàn}，{那|nà}{就|jiù}{说明|shuō míng}{这个|zhè ge}{问题|wèn tí}{很|hěn}{可能|kě néng}{真|zhēn}{的|de}{存在|cún zài}}).
4. Balanced, neither trusting nor dismissive: the writer rejects the idea that reviews are worthless
   ({{我|wǒ}{并|bìng}{不|bú}{赞成|zàn chéng}{这|zhè}{种|zhǒng}{看法|kàn fǎ}}) but wants readers to keep their own judgement ({{也|yě}{要|yào}{有|yǒu}{自己|zì jǐ}{的|de}{判断|pàn duàn}}).

"**Good reviews online: how far can we trust them?** These days, before buying something or
choosing a restaurant, many people first look at the reviews online. The more good reviews a shop
has, the more easily it draws customers. Lately, though, quite a few internet users have found that
some products with plenty of good reviews are a disappointment once they get them home. This
phenomenon is worth thinking about.

Why would good reviews not be 'genuine'? There are two main reasons. On the one hand, some sellers,
to make their products sell better, offer customers small presents or cash for a good review, or
even pay people to write fake ones. On the other hand, reviews are subjective by nature: of the same
restaurant, one person finds the food just right while another finds it too salty. People's tastes
and expectations differ, so naturally their reviews differ too.

Does that mean online reviews are worthless? I don't agree. A large number of reviews taken
together can still reflect the overall picture of a product. The question is how we read them. I
have three suggestions. First, don't just look at how many good reviews there are; look more at
what they actually say. A review with details and pictures is more convincing than a hundred that
just say 'very good' or 'not bad'. Second, pay particular attention to bad reviews. A few bad
reviews may just be chance, but if many people raise the same problem, the problem very probably
exists. Third, be objective when you read reviews: treat them as a reference, not as the only
standard.

So online reviews are not wrong in themselves; the key lies in whether we can pick out the genuine,
useful information from a great many reviews. As consumers, we should value other people's
experience, and also keep our own judgement."

## Write it: an argued essay

The HSK 5 exam asks for at least 200 characters on a set theme. Write 200–300 characters on this
phenomenon: {在|zài}{饭馆|fàn guǎn}{吃|chī}{饭|fàn}{的|de}{时候|shí hou}，{很|hěn}{多|duō}{人|rén}{菜|cài}{一|yí}{上来|shàng lái}{就|jiù}{先|xiān}{拍照|pāi zhào}，{再|zài}{发|fā}{到|dào}{网上|wǎng shàng}。{你|nǐ}{怎么|zěn me}{看|kàn}？ (In restaurants, many people take a photo
of each dish as soon as it arrives, and post it online. What do you think?)

Plan before you write:

1. **Phenomenon**: one or two sentences describing what happens.
2. **View**: say clearly whether you're for, against, or somewhere in between ({我|wǒ}{认为|rèn wéi}…, {我|wǒ}{不|bù}{完全|wán quán}{赞成|zàn chéng}…).
3. **[[Reasons]]**: two reasons, each with an example ({首先|shǒu xiān}…{其次|qí cì}…, {一|yì}{方面|fāng miàn}…{另|lìng}{一|yì}{方面|fāng miàn}…).
4. **[[Conclusion]]**: one or two sentences ({由此|yóu cǐ}{可见|kě jiàn}…, {总之|zǒng zhī}…), ideally with a balanced point ({问题|wèn tí}{不|bú}{在于|zài yú}…，{而|ér}{在于|zài yú}…).

Checklist when you've finished: Does each paragraph do one job? Did you use two or three connectors,
not ten? Is the register written ({是否|shì fǒu}, {由此|yóu cǐ}{可见|kě jiàn}, {应当|yīng dāng}) rather than chatty ({呢|ne}, {吧|ba}, {啊|a})? Did you count the
characters? (On Chinese squared paper each punctuation mark takes a square of its own.)

"**What to make of 'photos before the meal'.** In restaurants today you often see this: as soon as
the food is on the table, nobody picks up their chopsticks; instead out come the phones for photos,
which then go online. Some people think it's rude, but I don't entirely agree. First, taking photos
is a personal habit: as long as it doesn't bother others, there's no need to reject it. Second,
sharing good food is a way of keeping in touch, and friends can learn about good restaurants from
it. Of course, if the photos take so long that the food goes cold, or they bother the people you're
eating with, that isn't reasonable. So the question isn't whether to take photos, but whether you
know where to stop. I think one or two shots are enough; at the table, it's better to talk to the

## Pronunciation

- {有力|yǒu lì} and {有利|yǒu lì} are both yǒu lì, said alike: {有|yǒu} stays low (a half third tone) before the fourth tone. Context decides:
  {有力|yǒu lì}{的|de}{证据|zhèng jù} (strong evidence), {有利|yǒu lì}{的|de}{条件|tiáo jiàn} (favourable conditions).
- {属于|shǔ yú} shǔ yú and {处于|chǔ yú} chǔ yú: {于|yú} is yú, second tone, so {属|shǔ} and {处|chǔ} are said as a low half third tone before it.
- {视为|shì wéi} shì wéi: {为|wéi} is wéi (second tone) here, as in {作为|zuò wéi} and {成为|chéng wéi}, not the wèi of {为了|wèi le}.
- {道理|dào li} dào li: the second syllable is light.
- {缺乏|quē fá} quē fá: quē with ü-like *ue* after q (written *ue*, said *üe*).

## Common mistakes

- {这|zhè}{本|běn}{书|shū}{卖|mài}{了|le}{十万|shí wàn}{本|běn}，{由此|yóu cǐ}{可见|kě jiàn}{很|hěn}{受|shòu}{欢迎|huān yíng} isn't wrong, but it's heavy: after one fact, {可见|kě jiàn} is enough. Keep {由此|yóu cǐ}{可见|kě jiàn}
  for a conclusion drawn from several facts, at the start of a sentence.
- ~~{大|dà}{雨|yǔ}{使得|shǐ de}{航班|háng bān}~~: {使得|shǐ de} takes a whole clause, not just an object: {大|dà}{雨|yǔ}{使得|shǐ de}{航班|háng bān}{推迟|tuī chí}{了|le}。
- ~~{成功|chéng gōng}{的|de}{关键|guān jiàn}{在于|zài yú}{是|shì}{坚持|jiān chí}~~: {在于|zài yú} is already the verb; don't add {是|shì}: {成功|chéng gōng}{的|de}{关键|guān jiàn}{在于|zài yú}{坚持|jiān chí}。
- ~~{他|tā}{把|bǎ}{这|zhè}{次|cì}{失败|shī bài}{视|shì}{作为|zuò wéi}{机会|jī huì}~~: mixing {视为|shì wéi} and {看作|kàn zuò}. Say {把|bǎ}{这|zhè}{次|cì}{失败|shī bài}{视为|shì wéi}{机会|jī huì} or {把|bǎ}{这|zhè}{次|cì}{失败|shī bài}{看作|kàn zuò}{机会|jī huì}.
- {这个|zhè ge}{问题|wèn tí}{是|shì}{属于|shǔ yú}{技术|jì shù}{问题|wèn tí} is heard in speech, but {属于|shǔ yú} doesn't need {是|shì} before it: {这个|zhè ge}{问题|wèn tí}{属于|shǔ yú}{技术|jì shù}{问题|wèn tí} is the written form.
- "Strong evidence" is {有力|yǒu lì}{的|de}{证据|zhèng jù}. {有利|yǒu lì}{的|de}{证据|zhèng jù} is also Chinese, but it means something else: evidence that
  favours someone ({对|duì}{他|tā}{有利|yǒu lì}{的|de}{证据|zhèng jù}). {有利|yǒu lì} is "favourable": {对|duì}{我们|wǒ men}{有利|yǒu lì}.

## Key points

- Fact + {可见|kě jiàn} + conclusion; {由此|yóu cǐ}{可见|kě jiàn} (written) after several facts, starting a sentence.
- {使得|shǐ de} + clause (a result, written); {促使|cù shǐ} + person + action (prompts someone to act).
- X {在于|zài yú} Y: the point lies in Y ({问题|wèn tí}{在于|zài yú}, {关键|guān jiàn}{在于|zài yú}, {区别|qū bié}{在于|zài yú}); {不|bú}{在于|zài yú}…{而|ér}{在于|zài yú}….
- {针对|zhēn duì} (aimed at a problem or group), {围绕|wéi rào} (centred on a topic; going round).
- {把|bǎ} A {视为|shì wéi} B (written) / {看作|kàn zuò} B: regard as; {当作|dàng zuò}: treat as; A {属于|shǔ yú} B: belong to; {处于|chǔ yú} + state.
- An argued text: phenomenon, view, reasons with evidence, conclusion. Words: {观点|guān diǎn} {理由|lǐ yóu} {事实|shì shí} {证据|zhèng jù} {结论|jié lùn}; {客观|kè guān} / {主观|zhǔ guān}, {具体|jù tǐ}, {合理|hé lǐ}, {有力|yǒu lì}.
- New characters: {补|bǔ} {范|fàn} {乏|fá} {属|shǔ} {绕|rào} {殊|shū} {素|sù} (✎ {补|bǔ} {范|fàn} {素|sù}).

The words from this lesson are listed below; they join your vocabulary reviews when you complete
the lesson.

lessons.title: Formal Chinese: notices, rules and reports
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

Since HSK 4 you've met a written word now and then: {此|cǐ} for {这|zhè}, {与|yǔ} for {和|hé}, {已|yǐ} for {已经|yǐ jīng}, {将|jiāng} for {会|huì}. HSK 5 has
dozens more, and the exam's reading texts are full of them: notices, rules, news reports, the
introduction to an exhibition. This lesson puts the **[[written register]]** ({书面语|shū miàn yǔ}) in one place:

- the short written words and their spoken partners: {便|biàn} ({就|jiù}), {较|jiào} ({比较|bǐ jiào}), {及|jí} / {以及|yǐ jí} ({和|hé}), {其|qí} ({他|tā}{的|de}, {它|tā}{的|de}), {某|mǒu} ({有|yǒu}{个|gè}),
  {如何|rú hé} ({怎么|zěn me}), {如此|rú cǐ} ({这么|zhè me}), {需|xū} ({需要|xū yào}), {应当|yīng dāng} ({应该|yīng gāi}), {至|zhì} ({到|dào}), {首次|shǒu cì} ({第|dì}{一|yī}{次|cì}), {今日|jīn rì} ({今天|jīn tiān})…;
- the time words of reports: {此时|cǐ shí}, {此后|cǐ hòu}, {此前|cǐ qián}, {随后|suí hòu}, {近日|jìn rì}, {近期|jìn qī}, {期间|qī jiān}, {先后|xiān hòu}, {最初|zuì chū}, {早已|zǎo yǐ};
- the connectors {因而|yīn ér} (therefore) and {从而|cóng ér} (thereby), and {以|yǐ} (with, by means of; {以|yǐ}…{为|wéi}…);
- the written passive {为|wéi}…{所|suǒ} ({为|wéi}{人|rén}{们|men}{所|suǒ}{熟悉|shú xī}: familiar to people);
- the words of rules ({制度|zhì dù}, {制定|zhì dìng}, {执行|zhí xíng}, {实施|shí shī}, {权利|quán lì}, {义务|yì wù}) and of categories ({类型|lèi xíng}, {种类|zhǒng lèi}, {性质|xìng zhì}, {结构|jié gòu}, {甲|jiǎ} / {乙|yǐ}).

You won't use most of these in conversation: a friend who says {今日|jīn rì} instead of {今天|jīn tiān} sounds like a news
reader. But you need to understand them on every notice board, and to use some of them in your
own essays. At the end, {安娜|Ān nà} (Anna), who now guides visitors at a museum, reads her museum's new
rules, and {王芳|Wáng Fāng} tells the same news twice: once in a chat, once as a news item.

## Spoken and written: the pairs

Most written words are short (one syllable) and the spoken ones longer, or the other way round. Learn
them in pairs:

| Written | Spoken | Example (written) |
|---|---|---|
| {便|biàn} | {就|jiù} | {他|tā}{一|yí}{到|dào}{便|biàn}{开始|kāi shǐ}{工作|gōng zuò}。 (He started work the moment he arrived.) |
| {较|jiào} | {比较|bǐ jiào}; {比|bǐ} | {价格|jià gé}{较|jiào}{高|gāo}。 {今年|jīn nián}{的|de}{游客|yóu kè}{较|jiào}{去年|qù nián}{多|duō}。 |
| {及|jí}, {以及|yǐ jí} | {和|hé} | {老师|lǎo shī}、{学生|xué sheng}{以及|yǐ jí}{家长|jiā zhǎng} |
| {其|qí} | {他|tā}{的|de}, {她|tā}{的|de}, {它|tā}{的|de}, {他们|tā men}{的|de} | {这|zhè}{家|jiā}{公司|gōng sī}{及|jí}{其|qí}{员工|yuán gōng} (the company and its staff) |
| {其余|qí yú} | {别的|bié de}, {剩下|shèng xià}{的|de} | {其余|qí yú}{的|de}{人|rén}{明天|míng tiān}{再|zài}{来|lái}。 |
| {某|mǒu} | {有|yǒu}{个|gè}, {一|yí}{个|gè} | {某|mǒu}{公司|gōng sī}, {某|mǒu}{人|rén}, {某|mǒu}{天|tiān} |
| {如何|rú hé} | {怎么|zěn me}, {怎么样|zěn me yàng} | {如何|rú hé}{学|xué}{好|hǎo}{中文|Zhōng wén}？ {你|nǐ}{觉得|jué de}{如何|rú hé}？ |
| {如此|rú cǐ} | {这么|zhè me}, {这样|zhè yàng} | {原来|yuán lái}{如此|rú cǐ}。 (So that's how it is.) |
| {如|rú}, {如同|rú tóng} | {如果|rú guǒ}; {像|xiàng}, {好像|hǎo xiàng} | {如|rú}{有|yǒu}{疑问|yí wèn}，{请|qǐng}{咨询|zī xún}{服务|fú wù}{台|tái}。 |
| {需|xū} | {需要|xū yào} | {参观|cān guān}{需|xū}{提前|tí qián}{预约|yù yuē}。 |
| {应当|yīng dāng} | {应该|yīng gāi} | {讲解|jiǎng jiě}{内容|nèi róng}{应当|yīng dāng}{准确|zhǔn què}。 |
| {必|bì} | {一定|yí dìng}, {必须|bì xū} | {这|zhè}{是|shì}{学生|xué sheng}{必|bì}{读|dú}{的|de}{一|yì}{本|běn}{书|shū}。 |
| {至|zhì} | {到|dào} | {周|zhōu}{二|èr}{至|zhì}{周|zhōu}{日|rì}{开放|kāi fàng}。 |
| {同|tóng} | {跟|gēn}, {和|hé} | {我|wǒ}{同|tóng}{他|tā}{一起|yì qǐ}{去|qù}。 |
| {或是|huò shì} | {或者|huò zhě} | {周|zhōu}{六|liù}{或是|huò shì}{周|zhōu}{日|rì} |
| {首次|shǒu cì} | {第|dì}{一|yī}{次|cì} | {这些|zhè xiē}{画|huà}{是|shì}{首次|shǒu cì}{展出|zhǎn chū}。 |
| {今日|jīn rì} | {今天|jīn tiān} | {今日|jīn rì}{闭馆|bì guǎn}。 |
| {早已|zǎo yǐ} | {早|zǎo}{就|jiù} | {他|tā}{早已|zǎo yǐ}{离开|lí kāi}{了|le}。 |
| {众多|zhòng duō} | {很|hěn}{多|duō} | {众多|zhòng duō}{观众|guān zhòng} |
| {随意|suí yì} | {随便|suí biàn} | {不要|bú yào}{随意|suí yì}{摸|mō}{展出|zhǎn chū}{的|de}{物品|wù pǐn}。 |
| {原|yuán} | {原来|yuán lái}{的|de} | {原|yuán}{计划|jì huà}, {原|yuán}{价|jià} (the original price) |

A few notes:

- **{便|biàn}** is an adverb like {就|jiù}, so it goes after the subject: {一|yī}…{便|biàn}…, {只要|zhǐ yào}…{便|biàn}…. It's biàn here, not the pián of {便宜|pián yi}.
- **{较|jiào}** works two ways: before an adjective it's "rather, comparatively" ({较|jiào}{高|gāo}, {较|jiào}{多|duō}), and before a noun it's
  "than", like {比|bǐ}: {今年|jīn nián}{的|de}{游客|yóu kè}{较|jiào}{去年|qù nián}{多|duō}。 (There are more visitors this year than last year.)
- **{及|jí}** and **{以及|yǐ jí}** join nouns. {以及|yǐ jí} can also join longer phrases, and comes before the last item of a list:
  {时间|shí jiān}、{地点|dì diǎn}{以及|yǐ jí}{参加|cān jiā}{的|de}{人数|rén shù}.
- **{其|qí}** points back to something already named, like "its" or "their": {这|zhè}{家|jiā}{公司|gōng sī}{及|jí}{其|qí}{员工|yuán gōng}. You know it
  from {其中|qí zhōng} (among them), {其他|qí tā} (other) and {其余|qí yú} (the rest, the others).
- **{某|mǒu}** is "a certain, some": the writer knows, or doesn't need to say, which one: {某|mǒu}{公司|gōng sī} (a certain company),
  {某|mǒu}{些|xiē}{人|rén} (some people).
- **{如|rú}** in notices is {如果|rú guǒ}: {如|rú}{有|yǒu}{疑问|yí wèn} (if you have any questions), {如|rú}{需|xū}{帮助|bāng zhù} (if you need help). {如同|rú tóng} is {好像|hǎo xiàng}: {时间|shí jiān}{如同|rú tóng}{流|liú}{水|shuǐ}
  (time is like flowing water). {如下|rú xià} is "as follows": {具体|jù tǐ}{安排|ān pái}{如下|rú xià} (the arrangements are as follows), followed by a list.
- **{需|xū}** is the short {需要|xū yào}, before a verb or a noun: {需|xū}{提前|tí qián}{预约|yù yuē} (advance booking needed), {需|xū}{凭|píng}{证件|zhèng jiàn} (ID required).
- **{同|tóng}** "with" is written or regional in this use; in standard speech say {跟|gēn}. {同|tóng} also means "the same" ({同一|tóng yī}, {相同|xiāng tóng}).

And four that have no simple spoken partner:

- **{白|bái}** (in vain, for nothing): {白|bái}{跑|pǎo}{一|yí}{趟|tàng} (make a trip for nothing), {白|bái}{等|děng}{了|le}{一|yí}{个|gè}{小时|xiǎo shí} (waited an hour for nothing).
- **{随|suí}** (to follow; along with): {价格|jià gé}{随|suí}{季节|jì jié}{变化|biàn huà} (prices change with the season); you know it from {随着|suí zhe}, {随时|suí shí}, {随便|suí biàn}.
- **{正如|zhèng rú}** (just as): {正如|zhèng rú}{大家|dà jiā}{所|suǒ}{知|zhī} (as everyone knows), {正如|zhèng rú}{老师|lǎo shī}{说|shuō}{的|de}{那样|nà yàng} (just as the teacher said).
- **{在内|zài nèi}** (included), after {包括|bāo kuò}: {包括|bāo kuò}{我|wǒ}{在内|zài nèi}，{一共|yí gòng}{五|wǔ}{个|gè}{人|rén}。 (Five people, including me.)

## Time in reports: {此时|cǐ shí}, {此后|cǐ hòu}, {此前|cǐ qián}, {随后|suí hòu}…

News and reports place events in time with their own words:

| Word | Meaning | Spoken |
|---|---|---|
| {此时|cǐ shí} | at this moment, at that time | {这|zhè}{时候|shí hou} |
| {此后|cǐ hòu} | after this, from then on | {从|cóng}{那|nà}{以后|yǐ hòu} |
| {此前|cǐ qián} | before this, previously | {在|zài}{那|nà}{以前|yǐ qián} |
| {随后|suí hòu} | soon after, then | {接着|jiē zhe}, {然后|rán hòu} |
| {今日|jīn rì} | today | {今天|jīn tiān} |
| {近日|jìn rì} | in the last few days, recently | {最近|zuì jìn}{几|jǐ}{天|tiān} |
| {近期|jìn qī} | recently; in the near future | {最近|zuì jìn} |
| {期间|qī jiān} | during (a period) | …{的|de}{时候|shí hou} |
| {先后|xiān hòu} | one after another, successively | {一|yí}{个|gè}{一|yí}{个|gè}{地|de} |
| {最初|zuì chū} | at first, originally | {一|yì}{开始|kāi shǐ} |
| {时刻|shí kè} | a moment; at every moment | {时候|shí hou} |
| {早晚|zǎo wǎn} | morning and evening; sooner or later | {早上|zǎo shang}{和|hé}{晚上|wǎn shang}; {迟早|chí zǎo} |

{博物馆|bó wù guǎn}{近日|jìn rì}{宣布|xuān bù}，{暑假|shǔ jià}{期间|qī jiān}{每|měi}{周|zhōu}{五|wǔ}{开放|kāi fàng}{至|zhì}{晚上|wǎn shang}{八|bā}{点|diǎn}。 — The museum announced recently that during the summer holidays it will open until 8 p.m. on Fridays.

{他|tā}{最初|zuì chū}{并|bìng}{不|bù}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{这|zhè}{份|fèn}{工作|gōng zuò}，{此后|cǐ hòu}{却|què}{越|yuè}{做|zuò}{越|yuè}{有|yǒu}{兴趣|xìng qù}。 — At first he didn't like the job, but after that he grew more and more interested in it.

{会议|huì yì}{开始|kāi shǐ}{以后|yǐ hòu}，{经理|jīng lǐ}{先后|xiān hòu}{介绍|jiè shào}{了|le}{三|sān}{个|gè}{新|xīn}{项目|xiàng mù}。{随后|suí hòu}，{大家|dà jiā}{开始|kāi shǐ}{讨论|tǎo lùn}。 — After the meeting began, the manager presented three new projects one after another. Then the discussion began.

{在|zài}{关键|guān jiàn}{时刻|shí kè}，{他|tā}{总是|zǒng shì}{很|hěn}{冷静|lěng jìng}。 — At crucial moments he's always calm.

{这|zhè}{药|yào}{早晚|zǎo wǎn}{各|gè}{吃|chī}{一|yí}{次|cì}。 — Take this medicine once in the morning and once in the evening.

{这|zhè}{件|jiàn}{事|shì}{他|tā}{早晚|zǎo wǎn}{会|huì}{知道|zhī dào}{的|de}。 — He'll find out about this sooner or later.

{近期|jìn qī} looks both ways: {近期|jìn qī}{的|de}{天气|tiān qì} is the weather of the last few days, and {近期|jìn qī}{将|jiāng}{举办|jǔ bàn}{展览|zhǎn lǎn} "an exhibition will be held
soon": the verb tells you which.

## {以|yǐ} and {以|yǐ}…{为|wéi}…

{以|yǐ} (with, by means of; written) introduces how something is done:

{以|yǐ}{最|zuì}{快|kuài}{的|de}{速度|sù dù}{完成|wán chéng}{任务|rèn wu}。 — Finish the task as fast as possible (at the fastest speed).

{以|yǐ}…{为|wéi}… is "to take X as Y", a frame you'll meet in every kind of formal text:

{这个|zhè ge}{班|bān}{的|de}{学生|xué sheng}{以|yǐ}{年轻|nián qīng}{人|rén}{为|wéi}{主|zhǔ}。 — The students in this class are mostly young people (take young people as the main part).

{我们|wǒ men}{的|de}{服务|fú wù}{以|yǐ}{满足|mǎn zú}{学生|xué sheng}{的|de}{需求|xū qiú}{为|wéi}{目标|mù biāo}。 — Our service aims to meet students' needs (takes meeting them as its goal).

{以|yǐ}{这|zhè}{次|cì}{活动|huó dòng}{为|wéi}{例|lì}，… — Take this event as an example: …

## {因而|yīn ér} and {从而|cóng ér}: therefore, thereby

The **[[written connectors]]** {因而|yīn ér}, {从而|cóng ér} and {便|biàn} join clauses the way {所以|suǒ yǐ} and {就|jiù} do in speech. {因而|yīn ér} (therefore) is the written {因此|yīn cǐ} / {所以|suǒ yǐ}: a result follows from a cause.

{这|zhè}{条|tiáo}{路|lù}{车辆|chē liàng}{较|jiào}{多|duō}，{因而|yīn ér}{经常|jīng cháng}{堵车|dǔ chē}。 — There's a lot of traffic on this road, so it's often jammed.

{从而|cóng ér} (thereby, and so) joins an action to the result it brings about, usually with the same subject:
the first clause is what someone does, the second what they achieve by it.

{博物馆|bó wù guǎn}{调整|tiáo zhěng}{了|le}{开放|kāi fàng}{时间|shí jiān}，{从而|cóng ér}{让|ràng}{更|gèng}{多|duō}{上班|shàng bān}{族|zú}{有|yǒu}{机会|jī huì}{来|lái}{参观|cān guān}。 — The museum has changed its opening hours, so that more office workers can come.

{他|tā}{每|měi}{天|tiān}{坚持|jiān chí}{练习|liàn xí}，{从而|cóng ér}{提高|tí gāo}{了|le}{自己|zì jǐ}{的|de}{水平|shuǐ píng}。 — By practising every day he raised his level.

{因而|yīn ér} looks back at a cause; {从而|cóng ér} looks forward from a means to its result. And {由此|yóu cǐ} (from this) points
back to what was just said: {由此|yóu cǐ}{可见|kě jiàn} (lesson 26), {由此|yóu cǐ}{看来|kàn lái} (judging from this).

## {为|wéi}…{所|suǒ}: the written passive

The **[[written passive]]** {为|wéi} + doer + {所|suǒ} + verb is a formal passive, mostly in fixed phrases. The verb is often two syllables
and takes no {了|le}:

{这个|zhè ge}{故事|gù shi}{为|wéi}{人|rén}{们|men}{所|suǒ}{熟悉|shú xī}。 — This story is familiar to people.

{他|tā}{的|de}{观点|guān diǎn}{逐渐|zhú jiàn}{为|wéi}{大家|dà jiā}{所|suǒ}{接受|jiē shòu}。 — His view gradually came to be accepted by everyone.

In speech you'd say {被|bèi}: {他|tā}{的|de}{观点|guān diǎn}{被|bèi}{大家|dà jiā}{接受|jiē shòu}{了|le}。 {为|wéi} here is wéi, the {为|wéi} of {作为|zuò wéi} and {成为|chéng wéi}, not the {为|wèi} of {为了|wèi le}.

## Rules and rights

| Word | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| {制度|zhì dù} | a system (of rules), regulations | {管理|guǎn lǐ}{制度|zhì dù} |
| {制定|zhì dìng} | to draw up, formulate (rules, plans) | {制定|zhì dìng}{计划|jì huà}, {制定|zhì dìng}{规定|guī dìng} |
| {执行|zhí xíng} | to carry out, execute | {执行|zhí xíng}{任务|rèn wu} |
| {实施|shí shī} | to implement (a plan, a rule) | {新|xīn}{规定|guī dìng}{从|cóng}{七|qī}{月|yuè}{一|yī}{日|rì}{起|qǐ}{实施|shí shī}。 |
| {实行|shí xíng} | to put into practice (a system) | {实行|shí xíng}{新|xīn}{的|de}{管理|guǎn lǐ}{制度|zhì dù} |
| {权|quán}, {权利|quán lì} | a right | {你|nǐ}{有|yǒu}{权利|quán lì}{知道|zhī dào}。 |
| {义务|yì wù} | a duty, an obligation | {遵守|zūn shǒu}{规定|guī dìng}{是|shì}{每|měi}{个|gè}{人|rén}{的|de}{义务|yì wù}。 |
| {公平|gōng píng} | fair | {这样|zhè yàng}{做|zuò}{不|bù}{公平|gōng píng}。 |
| {自由|zì yóu} | free; freedom | {自由|zì yóu}{时间|shí jiān}, {自由|zì yóu}{选择|xuǎn zé} |

{制定|zhì dìng} is drawing up rules, {实施|shí shī} and {实行|shí xíng} putting them into effect, {执行|zhí xíng} carrying them out day by day. {权|quán} is

## Kinds and categories

Reports also sort things into kinds, with words you'll see in titles and lists:

- {类|lèi} (a kind, a class), {类型|lèi xíng} (a type), {种类|zhǒng lèi} (a variety, a kind): {这|zhè}{类|lèi}{问题|wèn tí}, {两|liǎng}{种|zhǒng}{类型|lèi xíng}, {种类|zhǒng lèi}{很|hěn}{多|duō}.
- {名称|míng chēng} (the name of a thing, not a person): {产品|chǎn pǐn}{名称|míng chēng}, {公司|gōng sī}{名称|míng chēng}.
- {性质|xìng zhì} (nature, character), {结构|jié gòu} (structure), {本质|běn zhì} (essence): {问题|wèn tí}{的|de}{性质|xìng zhì}, {文章|wén zhāng}{的|de}{结构|jié gòu}, {从|cóng}{本质|běn zhì}{上|shàng}{看|kàn}.
- {概念|gài niàn} (a concept), {事物|shì wù} (a thing, an object, in general): {新|xīn}{的|de}{概念|gài niàn}, {新|xīn}{事物|shì wù}.
- {甲|jiǎ} and {乙|yǐ} (the first and second of the old "heavenly stems") label two items in a list, like A and B: {甲方|jiǎ fāng}
  and {乙方|yǐ fāng} are the two parties to a contract, {甲|jiǎ}{类|lèi} and {乙|yǐ}{类|lèi} two classes. The series goes on with {丙|bǐng} and {丁|dīng}.

<details>
<summary>A model retelling</summary>

{城市|chéng shì}{博物馆|bó wù guǎn}{最近|zuì jìn}{说|shuō}，{从|cóng}{七|qī}{月|yuè}{一|yī}{号|hào}{开始|kāi shǐ}{要|yào}{改|gǎi}{开放|kāi fàng}{时间|shí jiān}。{暑假|shǔ jià}{的|de}{时候|shí hou}，{每|měi}{个|gè}{星期|xīng qī}{五|wǔ}{和|hé}{星期|xīng qī}{六|liù}{开|kāi}{到|dào}{晚上|wǎn shang}{八|bā}{点|diǎn}。{以前|yǐ qián}{博物馆|bó wù guǎn}{下午|xià wǔ}{五|wǔ}{点|diǎn}{就|jiù}{关|guān}{门|mén}，{很|hěn}{多|duō}{上班|shàng bān}{的|de}{人|rén}{下|xià}{了|le}{班|bān}{去|qù}{参观|cān guān}，{可是|kě shì}{去|qù}{了|le}{也|yě}{进|jìn}{不|bu}{去|qù}。{这|zhè}{次|cì}{改|gǎi}{时间|shí jiān}，{就是|jiù shì}{因为|yīn wèi}{观众|guān zhòng}{提|tí}{了|le}{意见|yì jiàn}，{这样|zhè yàng}{下班|xià bān}{以后|yǐ hòu}{也|yě}{能|néng}{去|qù}{看|kàn}{了|le}。

"The City Museum said recently that it will change its opening hours from 1 July. In the summer
holidays it'll be open until 8 p.m. on Fridays and Saturdays. Before, it closed at 5, and many working
people who went after work couldn't get in. The change came because visitors complained, so now people
can go after work too."
</details>

## Write it: turn speech into a notice

Rewrite this message from a manager as a short written notice (60–100 characters), using at least four
written words from this lesson ({需|xū}, {如|rú}, {至|zhì}, {期间|qī jiān}, {应当|yīng dāng}, {及|jí}, {自|zì}…{起|qǐ}…):

> {大家|dà jiā}{注意|zhù yì}{一下|yí xià}：{下|xià}{个|gè}{星期|xīng qī}{一|yī}{到|dào}{星期|xīng qī}{三|sān}，{会议|huì yì}{室|shì}{要|yào}{修|xiū}，{不|bù}{能|néng}{用|yòng}。{要|yào}{开会|kāi huì}{的话|de huà}，{先|xiān}{跟|gēn}{小李|Xiǎo Lǐ}{说|shuō}{一|yì}{声|shēng}，{到|dào}{三|sān}{楼|lóu}{的|de}{小|xiǎo}{会议|huì yì}{室|shì}{开|kāi}。{有|yǒu}{问题|wèn tí}{就|jiù}{来|lái}{问|wèn}{我|wǒ}。

<details>
<summary>A model</summary>

> **{通知|tōng zhī}**
>
> {下|xià}{周一|zhōu yī}{至|zhì}{周|zhōu}{三|sān}，{会议|huì yì}{室|shì}{维修|wéi xiū}，{暂停|zàn tíng}{使用|shǐ yòng}。{维修|wéi xiū}{期间|qī jiān}{如|rú}{需|xū}{开会|kāi huì}，{请|qǐng}{提前|tí qián}{通知|tōng zhī}{李秘书|Lǐ mì shū}，{并|bìng}{前往|qián wǎng}{三|sān}{楼|lóu}{小|xiǎo}{会议|huì yì}{室|shì}。{如|rú}{有|yǒu}{疑问|yí wèn}，{请|qǐng}{与|yǔ}{办公室|bàn gōng shì}{联系|lián xì}。
>
> {办公室|bàn gōng shì}　5{月|yuè}8{日|rì}

{暂停|zàn tíng} (to suspend, HSK 4), {维修|wéi xiū} (to repair, lesson 09), {前往|qián wǎng} (to go to, written: lesson 29).
"**Notice.** From Monday to Wednesday next week the meeting room is being repaired and can't be used.
If you need to hold a meeting during the repairs, please tell Secretary Li in advance and use the small
meeting room on the third floor. If you have any questions, please contact the office. Office, 8 May."
</details>

## Say it

```speak
# Formal phrases you'll hear
{具体|jù tǐ}{安排|ān pái}{如下|rú xià}。
= The arrangements are as follows.
{如|rú}{有|yǒu}{疑问|yí wèn}，{请|qǐng}{咨询|zī xún}{服务|fú wù}{台|tái}。
= If you have any questions, please ask at the information desk.
{新|xīn}{规定|guī dìng}{从|cóng}{七|qī}{月|yuè}{一|yī}{日|rì}{起|qǐ}{实施|shí shī}。
= The new rules take effect from the first of July.
{原来|yuán lái}{如此|rú cǐ}。
= So that's how it is.
{我|wǒ}{白|bái}{跑|pǎo}{了|le}{一|yí}{趟|tàng}。
= I made the trip for nothing.
{这个|zhè ge}{故事|gù shi}{为|wéi}{人|rén}{们|men}{所|suǒ}{熟悉|shú xī}。
= This story is familiar to people.
```

## Pronunciation

- {便|biàn} biàn (then, written) and {便|biàn} pián in {便宜|pián yi} (cheap): same character, two readings.
- {较|jiào} jiào, like {叫|jiào} and {觉|jiào} (in {睡觉|shuì jiào}): fourth tone.
- {某|mǒu} mǒu: one syllable *m-ou*, third tone; don't say *mou* with a level tone.
- {为|wéi}…{所|suǒ}: {为|wéi} is wéi (second tone); {所|suǒ} is suǒ.
- {甲|jiǎ} jiǎ and {假|jiǎ} jiǎ (false, HSK 4) are the same syllable; {乙|yǐ} yǐ is like {以|yǐ} and {已|yǐ}.
- {执行|zhí xíng} zhí xíng: zh with the tongue curled back, then x with the tongue flat.

## Common mistakes

- {今日|jīn rì}{我|wǒ}{很|hěn}{累|lèi} is understood, but in conversation it sounds like a news reader: written words belong in
  written texts. Say {今天|jīn tiān}{我|wǒ}{很|hěn}{累|lèi}。
- ~~{他|tā}{一|yí}{到|dào}，{便|biàn}{他|tā}{开始|kāi shǐ}{工作|gōng zuò}~~: {便|biàn} is an adverb, after the subject: {他|tā}{一|yí}{到|dào}{便|biàn}{开始|kāi shǐ}{工作|gōng zuò}。
- ~~{学生|xué sheng}{及|jí}{努力|nǔ lì}{学习|xué xí}~~: {及|jí} joins nouns, not clauses: {老师|lǎo shī}{及|jí}{学生|xué sheng} is fine, but for clauses use {并且|bìng qiě} or {而且|ér qiě}.
- ~~{这个|zhè ge}{故事|gù shi}{为|wéi}{人|rén}{们|men}{所|suǒ}{熟悉|shú xī}{了|le}~~: {为|wéi}…{所|suǒ} takes no {了|le}: {这个|zhè ge}{故事|gù shi}{为|wéi}{人|rén}{们|men}{所|suǒ}{熟悉|shú xī}。
- {较|jiào} before a noun is "than": {今年|jīn nián}{较|jiào}{去年|qù nián}{多|duō} (more than last year). As with {比|bǐ}, {更|gèng} can be added:
  {今年|jīn nián}{较|jiào}{去年|qù nián}{更|gèng}{多|duō}。
- ~~{请|qǐng}{某|mǒu}{人|rén}{来|lái}{一下|yí xià}~~ when you know who it is: {某|mǒu} is "a certain (unnamed)", not "someone you're thinking of":
  say {请|qǐng}{小王|Xiǎo Wáng}{来|lái}{一下|yí xià}.

## Key points

- Written ↔ spoken: {便|biàn} / {就|jiù}, {较|jiào} / {比较|bǐ jiào} or {比|bǐ}, {及|jí} / {以及|yǐ jí} / {和|hé}, {其|qí} / {他|tā}{的|de}, {某|mǒu} / {有|yǒu}{个|gè}, {如何|rú hé} / {怎么|zěn me}, {如此|rú cǐ} / {这么|zhè me}, {如|rú} / {如果|rú guǒ}, {需|xū} / {需要|xū yào},
  {应当|yīng dāng} / {应该|yīng gāi}, {至|zhì} / {到|dào}, {首次|shǒu cì} / {第|dì}{一|yī}{次|cì}, {今日|jīn rì} / {今天|jīn tiān}, {早已|zǎo yǐ} / {早|zǎo}{就|jiù}, {众多|zhòng duō} / {很|hěn}{多|duō}, {随意|suí yì} / {随便|suí biàn}.
- Time in reports: {此时|cǐ shí}, {此后|cǐ hòu}, {此前|cǐ qián}, {随后|suí hòu}, {近日|jìn rì}, {近期|jìn qī}, {期间|qī jiān}, {先后|xiān hòu}, {最初|zuì chū}.
- {以|yǐ}…{为|wéi}… (take X as Y: {以|yǐ}…{为|wéi}{主|zhǔ}, {以|yǐ}…{为|wéi}{例|lì}); {因而|yīn ér} (therefore), {从而|cóng ér} (thereby: means → result).
- {为|wéi} + doer + {所|suǒ} + verb: written passive, no {了|le}.
- Rules: {制定|zhì dìng}, {实施|shí shī} / {实行|shí xíng}, {执行|zhí xíng}; {权利|quán lì} and {义务|yì wù}. Categories: {类型|lèi xíng}, {种类|zhǒng lèi}, {性质|xìng zhì}, {结构|jié gòu}, {本质|běn zhì}, {概念|gài niàn}; {甲|jiǎ} and {乙|yǐ}.
- New characters: {甲|jiǎ} {某|mǒu} {权|quán} {乙|yǐ} {执|zhí} (✎ {甲|jiǎ} {某|mǒu} {权|quán} {乙|yǐ}).

The words from this lesson are listed below; they join your vocabulary reviews when you complete
the lesson.

lessons.title: Describing change: numbers, trends and data
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

News, reports and the exam's reading texts are full of numbers: sales went up by a fifth, the gap is
narrowing, nearly half the people asked, a river two metres deep. This lesson gives you the words
to read and write them:

- going up and going down: {增长|zēng zhǎng}, {上升|shàng shēng}, {上涨|shàng zhǎng}, {提升|tí shēng}, {增|zēng}, {涨|zhǎng}, {升|shēng} against {下降|xià jiàng} and {减少|jiǎn shǎo}; {扩大|kuò dà} / {缩小|suō xiǎo}, {延长|yán cháng} / {缩短|suō duǎn}, {加速|jiā sù}, {持续|chí xù}, {连续|lián xù};
- "by" and "to": {增长|zēng zhǎng}{了|le}{百分之|bǎi fēn zhī}{二十|èr shí} (by 20%) and {增长|zēng zhǎng}{到|dào} / {增|zēng}{至|zhì}… (to…);
- comparing numbers: {大于|dà yú}, {小于|xiǎo yú}, {等于|děng yú}, {超出|chāo chū}, {接近|jiē jìn}, {将近|jiāng jìn}, {上下|shàng xià}, {比例|bǐ lì}, {占|zhàn}, {平均|píng jūn}, {差距|chā jù};
- the words of a trend: {趋势|qū shì}, {现状|xiàn zhuàng}, {形势|xíng shì}, {阶段|jiē duàn}, {季度|jì dù}, {近年来|jìn nián lái}, {当前|dāng qián}, {预计|yù jì}, {预测|yù cè}, {统计|tǒng jì};
- sizes and measurements: {长度|cháng dù}, {宽度|kuān dù}, {高度|gāo dù}, {厚度|hòu dù}, {深度|shēn dù}, {重量|zhòng liàng}, {面积|miàn jī}, {强度|qiáng dù}; {厘米|lí mǐ}, {吨|dūn}, {亿|yì}.

You'll follow {大卫|Dà wèi} (David) and his partner {白涛|Bái Tāo} (Bai Tao) through their company's figures, and read a
report built on a survey, in five paragraphs whose order you can work out from the connectors.

## Going up, going down

Chinese has several verbs for "to rise". They aren't interchangeable: each goes with its own kind of
subject.

| Verb | Goes with | Example |
|---|---|---|
| {增长|zēng zhǎng} (HSK 4) | quantities, numbers of people, the economy | {游客|yóu kè}{人数|rén shù}{增长|zēng zhǎng}{了|le}{百分之|bǎi fēn zhī}{二十|èr shí}。 |
| {增|zēng} | the same, written, usually before {至|zhì} or {加|jiā} | {人数|rén shù}{增|zēng}{至|zhì}{三千|sān qiān}。 |
| {上升|shàng shēng} | figures, temperatures, a rank: anything that moves up a scale | {气温|qì wēn}{上升|shàng shēng}{了|le}{五|wǔ}{度|dù}。 |
| {升|shēng} | to rise; to go up (a level), be promoted | {气温|qì wēn}{升|shēng}{到|dào}{了|le}{三十五|sān shí wǔ}{度|dù}。 {他|tā}{升|shēng}{为|wéi}{经理|jīng lǐ}{了|le}。 |
| {升温|shēng wēn} | to warm up; (of interest, a market) to heat up | {最近|zuì jìn}{天气|tiān qì}{开始|kāi shǐ}{升温|shēng wēn}。 |
| {上涨|shàng zhǎng}, {涨|zhǎng} | prices, water levels | {菜|cài}{价|jià}{上涨|shàng zhǎng}{了|le}。 {河|hé}{水|shuǐ}{涨|zhǎng}{了|le}。 |
| {提升|tí shēng} | a level or quality, raised by effort | {提升|tí shēng}{服务|fú wù}{质量|zhì liàng} |

The opposite is {下降|xià jiàng} (HSK 4) for most of them, and {减少|jiǎn shǎo} (HSK 4) for quantities. Pairs that go together:

- {扩大|kuò dà} (to expand) and {缩小|suō xiǎo} (to narrow, reduce): {规模|guī mó}{扩大|kuò dà}{了|le}, {差距|chā jù}{缩小|suō xiǎo}{了|le}.
- {延长|yán cháng} (to extend) and {缩短|suō duǎn} (to shorten), for time and length: {延长|yán cháng}{开放|kāi fàng}{时间|shí jiān}, {缩短|suō duǎn}{行程|xíng chéng}.
- {加速|jiā sù} (to accelerate): {增长|zēng zhǎng}{正在|zhèng zài}{加速|jiā sù}。 (Growth is speeding up.)

And two words for "going on":

- {持续|chí xù} (to continue, last) is without a break: {雨|yǔ}{持续|chí xù}{了|le}{三|sān}{天|tiān}。 (The rain went on for three days.) {人数|rén shù}{持续|chí xù}{上升|shàng shēng}。
- {连续|lián xù} (in a row) counts repeated units: {他|tā}{连续|lián xù}{三|sān}{年|nián}{得|dé}{了|le}{冠军|guàn jūn}。 (He won three years running.)

### By and to

The commonest trap in reports is the difference between "rose by" and "rose to":

- verb + {了|le} + amount = **by**: {销量|xiāo liàng}{增长|zēng zhǎng}{了|le}{百分之|bǎi fēn zhī}{二十|èr shí}。 (Sales rose by 20%.)
- verb + {到|dào} / {至|zhì} + amount = **to**: {销量|xiāo liàng}{增长|zēng zhǎng}{到|dào}{两万|liǎng wàn}{件|jiàn}。 {销量|xiāo liàng}{增|zēng}{至|zhì}{两万|liǎng wàn}{件|jiàn}。 (Sales rose to 20,000 units.)

{至|zhì} (lesson 27) is the written {到|dào}. Percentages are {百分之|bǎi fēn zhī} + the number ({百分之|bǎi fēn zhī}{二十|èr shí}, 20%), fractions put the bottom number first: {三|sān}{分之|fēn zhī}{一|yī}
(one third), and decimals {点|diǎn}: {三|sān}{点|diǎn}{五|wǔ} (3.5).

## Comparing numbers

| Word | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| {大于|dà yú}, {小于|xiǎo yú}, {等于|děng yú} | greater than, less than, equal to | {今年|jīn nián}{的|de}{收入|shōu rù}{大于|dà yú}{去年|qù nián}。 {一|yì}{公里|gōng lǐ}{等于|děng yú}{一千|yì qiān}{米|mǐ}。 |
| {超|chāo} / {超出|chāo chū} | to exceed, go beyond | {超出|chāo chū}{预计|yù jì}, {超出|chāo chū}{范围|fàn wéi} |
| {接近|jiē jìn} | to approach, be close to (a verb) | {接近|jiē jìn}{一半|yí bàn} (close to half) |
| {将近|jiāng jìn} | nearly, almost (an adverb, before the number) | {将近|jiāng jìn}{一|yì}{年|nián} (nearly a year) |
| {上下|shàng xià} | about (after the number) | {三十|sān shí}{岁|suì}{上下|shàng xià} (about thirty) |
| {整整|zhěng zhěng} | a full, a whole | {整整|zhěng zhěng}{三|sān}{个|gè}{小时|xiǎo shí} (three whole hours) |
| {大多|dà duō} | mostly | {来|lái}{参观|cān guān}{的|de}{人|rén}{大多|dà duō}{是|shì}{学生|xué sheng}。 |
| {比例|bǐ lì} | proportion, ratio | {女生|nǚ shēng}{的|de}{比例|bǐ lì} |
| {占|zhàn} | to make up, take up (a share) | {女生|nǚ shēng}{占|zhàn}{百分之|bǎi fēn zhī}{六十|liù shí}。 |
| {平均|píng jūn} | average; on average | {平均|píng jūn}{每|měi}{天|tiān}{两|liǎng}{个|gè}{小时|xiǎo shí} |
| {总数|zǒng shù}, {总体|zǒng tǐ} | the total; overall | {总数|zǒng shù}{将近|jiāng jìn}{八百|bā bǎi}。 {总体|zǒng tǐ}{来|lái}{看|kàn}… |
| {差距|chā jù} | a gap (between figures, people, places) | {差距|chā jù}{越|yuè}{来|lái}{越|yuè}{小|xiǎo}。 |
| {对比|duì bǐ} | to contrast; a comparison | {跟|gēn}{去年|qù nián}{对比|duì bǐ} |

{占|zhàn} (zhàn: in traditional script 佔) takes the share as its object: {年轻|nián qīng}{人|rén}{占|zhàn}{总数|zǒng shù}{的|de}{一半|yí bàn}。 (Young people make up half the
total.) Its partner for the share of a whole is {比例|bǐ lì}: {年轻|nián qīng}{人|rén}{的|de}{比例|bǐ lì}{是|shì}{百分之|bǎi fēn zhī}{五十|wǔ shí}.

{接近|jiē jìn} and {将近|jiāng jìn} both mean "nearly", but {接近|jiē jìn} is a verb ({接近|jiē jìn}{一半|yí bàn}, {接近|jiē jìn}{目标|mù biāo}) and {将近|jiāng jìn} an adverb, straight before a number
({将近|jiāng jìn}{一半|yí bàn}, {将近|jiāng jìn}{三|sān}{年|nián}). {上下|shàng xià} and {左右|zuǒ yòu} (HSK 4) come after the number: {一百|yì bǎi}{人|rén}{上下|shàng xià}.

## The words of a trend

- {趋势|qū shì} (a trend): {上升|shàng shēng}{的|de}{趋势|qū shì} (an upward trend). {现状|xiàn zhuàng} (the present state of things), {形势|xíng shì} (the situation, often of a
  market or a match), {当前|dāng qián} (current, present): {当前|dāng qián}{的|de}{形势|xíng shì}.
- {阶段|jiē duàn} (a stage, phase), {初期|chū qī} / {中期|zhōng qī} (the early / middle period), {年初|nián chū} (the beginning of the year), {季度|jì dù} (a quarter of a
  year: {第|dì}{三|sān}{季度|jì dù}, the third quarter), {近年来|jìn nián lái} (in recent years).
- {统计|tǒng jì} (statistics; to count up), {计算|jì suàn} (to calculate), {排列|pái liè} (to arrange in order: {从|cóng}{大|dà}{到|dào}{小|xiǎo}{排列|pái liè}).
- {预计|yù jì} (to estimate, expect) and {预测|yù cè} (to predict, forecast): {预计|yù jì}{下|xià}{个|gè}{月|yuè}{完成|wán chéng} (expected to be finished next month),
  {预测|yù cè}{明年|míng nián}{的|de}{销量|xiāo liàng}.
- {销量|xiāo liàng} (sales volume) and {产量|chǎn liàng} (output): {量|liàng}, "an amount", as in {重量|zhòng liàng} and {工作量|gōng zuò liàng} (workload).
- Adjectives of speed and size: {迅速|xùn sù} (rapid), {缓慢|huǎn màn} (slow, written), {明显|míng xiǎn} (obvious, marked), {巨大|jù dà} (huge).

{近年来|jìn nián lái}，{网上|wǎng shàng}{购物|gòu wù}{的|de}{人数|rén shù}{迅速|xùn sù}{增长|zēng zhǎng}，{而|ér}{去|qù}{商场|shāng chǎng}{的|de}{人|rén}{明显|míng xiǎn}{减少|jiǎn shǎo}{了|le}。 — In recent years the number of people shopping online has grown rapidly,
while the number going to shopping centres has clearly fallen.

### Stroke order

- **{延|yán}** and **{建|jiàn}**: the part inside comes first and 廴 last: for {延|yán}, the left-falling stroke, the vertical, the short
  horizontal and the bent stroke, then 廴's two strokes.
- **{迅|xùn}**: 卂 first, then 辶 last, as in every character with 辶 ({这|zhè}, {近|jìn}, {速|sù}).
- **{巨|jù}**: the top horizontal, then the horizontal-turn on the right, the short horizontal inside, and the vertical-turn
  that makes the left side and the bottom: four strokes.
- **{亿|yì}**: 亻, then {乙|yǐ} in one stroke.

   sales didn't fall, they just grew slowly.
3. Paragraph 3 begins with {此外|cǐ wài} ("in addition"), so a point must come before it; paragraph 4 says the gap is
   "also" ({{也|yě}}) clear, pointing back to the e-book and paper-book contrast of paragraph 3. Only paragraph 2,
   which begins {{这|zhè}{份|fèn}{报告|bào gào}{显示|xiǎn shì}} (this report shows), follows straight on from the introduction.
4. Adjust its services: open longer at weekends and offer more kinds of e-books
   ({{延长|yán cháng}{周末|zhōu mò}{的|de}{开放|kāi fàng}{时间|shí jiān}，{增加|zēng jiā}{电子书|diàn zǐ shū}{的|de}{种类|zhǒng lèi}}).

"**A survey of residents' reading.** To find out about residents' reading habits, a city library
recently published a survey report. The survey was carried out at the start of 2030; more than three
thousand residents aged between eighteen and seventy took part. The survey used a questionnaire covering
three areas: reading time, ways of reading and what people read.

The report shows that in recent years the time residents spend reading has clearly increased. In 2029
residents read for 52 minutes a day on average, fifteen minutes more than in 2025. The number of
readers has also kept rising: people who read more than five books a year are now close to half of
the total. Reading time rose most among office workers aged twenty-five to forty: busy as they are,
they often read on the metro.

In addition, in terms of how people read, the share of e-books has grown rapidly. In 2025 e-book
readers made up only 30%; by 2029 the share had risen to 55%, exceeding paper-book readers for the
first time. Sales of paper books did not fall as a result, however; they simply grew more slowly. The survey also
found that many people use both: e-books on the move, paper books at home.

Among people of different ages the gap in reading habits is also marked. Most young people under
thirty read on their phones, while people over sixty still read mainly paper books. People
between forty and sixty use the two about equally. As for what they read, young people prefer novels,
while older people prefer history and books on health.

Finally, the report expects electronic reading to keep rising over the next few years. It also notes that
about 10% of residents still read no books at all in a year. The library
says it will adjust its services in the light of these figures, for example by opening for longer at
weekends and adding more kinds of e-books, so as to meet the needs of different readers."
</details>

## Write it: describe a chart

Here is a chart described in words: the number of visitors to a city museum in each quarter of
2029. Write a short report of 100–150 characters: the overall trend, the highest and lowest quarters,
the change from one to the next (by and to), and a sentence predicting the next quarter.

| Quarter | Visitors |
|---|---|
| {第|dì}{一|yī}{季度|jì dù} | 4{万|wàn} |
| {第|dì}{二|èr}{季度|jì dù} | 5{万|wàn} |
| {第|dì}{三|sān}{季度|jì dù} | 8{万|wàn} |
| {第|dì}{四|sì}{季度|jì dù} | 6{万|wàn} |

<details>
<summary>A model (about 130 characters)</summary>

> 2029{年|nián}，{城市|chéng shì}{博物馆|bó wù guǎn}{的|de}{观众|guān zhòng}{总数|zǒng shù}{达到|dá dào}{二十三万|èr shí sān wàn}{人|rén}。{从|cóng}{总体|zǒng tǐ}{来|lái}{看|kàn}，{观众|guān zhòng}{人数|rén shù}{呈|chéng}{先|xiān}{升|shēng}{后|hòu}{降|jiàng}{的|de}{趋势|qū shì}。{第|dì}{一|yī}{季度|jì dù}{人数|rén shù}{最|zuì}{少|shǎo}，{只有|zhǐ yǒu}{四万|sì wàn}{人|rén}；{第|dì}{二|èr}{季度|jì dù}{增长|zēng zhǎng}{到|dào}{五万|wǔ wàn}{人|rén}；{第|dì}{三|sān}{季度|jì dù}{是|shì}{暑假|shǔ jià}，{人数|rén shù}{迅速|xùn sù}{上升|shàng shēng}，{比|bǐ}{第|dì}{二|èr}{季度|jì dù}{增长|zēng zhǎng}{了|le}{百分之|bǎi fēn zhī}{六十|liù shí}，{达到|dá dào}{全|quán}{年|nián}{最|zuì}{高|gāo}。{第|dì}{四|sì}{季度|jì dù}{人数|rén shù}{有所|yǒu suǒ}{下降|xià jiàng}，{为|wéi}{六万|liù wàn}{人|rén}。{预计|yù jì}{明年|míng nián}{第|dì}{一|yī}{季度|jì dù}{人数|rén shù}{仍|réng}{将|jiāng}{较|jiào}{少|shǎo}。

"In 2029 the City Museum had 230,000 visitors in all. Overall, visitor numbers first rose and
then fell. The first quarter had the fewest, only 40,000; the second rose to 50,000; the third, with
the summer holidays, rose rapidly, 60% higher than the second, reaching the year's peak. The fourth
quarter fell somewhat, to 60,000. Numbers in the first quarter of next year are expected to remain
lower." {呈|chéng} (to show: a trend, written), {有所|yǒu suǒ} (somewhat, written) and {为|wéi} (to be: {为|wéi}{六万|liù wàn}{人|rén}) are
the written touches; {达到|dá dào} (to reach) is HSK 4.
</details>

## Say it

```speak
# Talking about figures
{销量|xiāo liàng}{比|bǐ}{去年|qù nián}{增长|zēng zhǎng}{了|le}{百分之|bǎi fēn zhī}{二十|èr shí}。
= Sales are up twenty per cent on last year.
{人数|rén shù}{增长|zēng zhǎng}{到|dào}{了|le}{三千|sān qiān}。
= The number has risen to three thousand.
{年轻|nián qīng}{人|rén}{占|zhàn}{总数|zǒng shù}{的|de}{一半|yí bàn}。
= Young people make up half the total.
{差距|chā jù}{越|yuè}{来|lái}{越|yuè}{小|xiǎo}。
= The gap is getting smaller and smaller.
{预计|yù jì}{明年|míng nián}{会|huì}{继续|jì xù}{上升|shàng shēng}。
= It's expected to keep rising next year.
{这|zhè}{条|tiáo}{路|lù}{宽|kuān}{二十|èr shí}{米|mǐ}。
= This road is twenty metres wide.
```

## Pronunciation

- {量|liàng} (an amount: {重量|zhòng liàng}, {销量|xiāo liàng}, {产量|chǎn liàng}) and {量|liáng} (to measure, HSK 4): same character, two tones.
- {涨|zhǎng} (to rise) has the same sound as {长|zhǎng} (to grow), not {长|cháng} (long). In {延长|yán cháng} and {长度|cháng dù} it's cháng.
- {亿|yì} yì, like {一|yī} yì before a first tone: {一|yí}{亿|yì} is yí yì ({一|yī} before a fourth tone).
- {趋势|qū shì} qū shì: q + u is said qü (the dots are left off after q).
- {吨|dūn} dūn, {均|jūn} jūn, {宽|kuān} kuān: all first tones.
- {将近|jiāng jìn} jiāng jìn: {将|jiāng} is jiāng, as in {将来|jiāng lái}.

## Common mistakes

- {这|zhè}{条|tiáo}{路|lù}{的|de}{宽|kuān}{是|shì}{二十|èr shí}{米|mǐ} is how a maths problem puts it, but in a description give the size with the adjective: {这|zhè}{条|tiáo}{路|lù}{宽|kuān}{二十|èr shí}{米|mǐ}, or with the noun {宽度|kuān dù}: {这|zhè}{条|tiáo}{路|lù}{的|de}{宽度|kuān dù}{是|shì}{二十|èr shí}{米|mǐ}。
- ~~{百分之|bǎi fēn zhī}{五十五|wǔ shí wǔ}{人|rén}~~: a percentage needs {的|de} before a noun: {百分之|bǎi fēn zhī}{五十五|wǔ shí wǔ}{的|de}{人|rén}.
- ~~{三十|sān shí}{岁|suì}{上下|shàng xià}{左右|zuǒ yòu}~~ / ~~{整整|zhěng zhěng}{一|yí}{个|gè}{月|yuè}{左右|zuǒ yòu}~~: one word for "about" is enough, and {整整|zhěng zhěng} (a full) can't be "about".
- ~~{将近|jiāng jìn}{二十|èr shí}{岁|suì}{以上|yǐ shàng}~~: {将近|jiāng jìn} is "nearly", just below the number; {以上|yǐ shàng} is "over". Say {将近|jiāng jìn}{二十|èr shí}{岁|suì} or {二十|èr shí}{岁|suì}{以上|yǐ shàng}.
- {增长|zēng zhǎng}{了|le} / {增长|zēng zhǎng}{到|dào}: not a grammar error but a change of meaning: {增长|zēng zhǎng}{了|le}{两万|liǎng wàn} (by 20,000), {增长|zēng zhǎng}{到|dào}{两万|liǎng wàn} (to 20,000).
  Read the verb's complement before you read the number.
- {人口|rén kǒu}{上涨|shàng zhǎng}{了|le} is understood but unidiomatic: prices and water {上涨|shàng zhǎng}; numbers of people {增长|zēng zhǎng} or {增加|zēng jiā}.

## Key points

- Rise: {增长|zēng zhǎng} (quantities), {上升|shàng shēng} (figures on a scale), {上涨|shàng zhǎng} / {涨|zhǎng} (prices, water), {提升|tí shēng} (level, quality), {升温|shēng wēn} (warming);
  fall: {下降|xià jiàng}, {减少|jiǎn shǎo}. Pairs: {扩大|kuò dà} / {缩小|suō xiǎo}, {延长|yán cháng} / {缩短|suō duǎn}. {持续|chí xù} (without a break), {连续|lián xù} (in a row).
- Verb + {了|le} + amount = by; verb + {到|dào} / {至|zhì} + amount = to.
- {占|zhàn} + share ({占|zhàn}{百分之|bǎi fēn zhī}{六十|liù shí}); {比例|bǐ lì}; {平均|píng jūn}; {将近|jiāng jìn} + number, {接近|jiē jìn} + number; number + {上下|shàng xià} / {左右|zuǒ yòu}; {整整|zhěng zhěng} + amount.
- Trends: {趋势|qū shì}, {现状|xiàn zhuàng}, {形势|xíng shì}, {阶段|jiē duàn}, {季度|jì dù}, {近年来|jìn nián lái}, {当前|dāng qián}; {统计|tǒng jì}, {预计|yù jì}, {预测|yù cè}.
- Sizes: adjective + number ({宽|kuān}{二十|èr shí}{米|mǐ}) or {长度|cháng dù} / {宽度|kuān dù} / {高度|gāo dù} / {深度|shēn dù} / {重量|zhòng liàng} / {面积|miàn jī}; {万|wàn}, {亿|yì} (100 million); {吨|dūn}, {厘米|lí mǐ}.
- New characters: {吨|dūn} {宽|kuān} {扩|kuò} {巨|jù} {厘|lí} {趋|qū} {均|jūn} {缩|suō} {延|yán} {迅|xùn} {亿|yì} (✎ {吨|dūn} {宽|kuān} {巨|jù} {均|jūn} {亿|yì}).

The words from this lesson are listed below; they join your vocabulary reviews when you complete
the lesson.

lessons.title: Journeys and stories: writing and speaking practice
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

The last new words of the course are for journeys: booking, trains and flights, the weather on the
way, and a few words for the poems travellers have always written. Then the lesson turns to the
exam's two productive parts, as reported from the sample papers:

- **writing**: a story of at least 100 characters from four pictures, and an essay of at least 200
  characters on a set theme (the sample asks about something you tried and how you felt);
- **speaking**: retelling a passage you hear, telling a story from three photos, and giving your
  opinion on two questions.

Along the way, {大卫|Dà wèi} takes a group of British students to Xi'an by train, and {李明|Lǐ Míng} (Li Ming) flies home
from England at the end of his master's.

## Travel words

### Planning and booking

| Word | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| {旅行社|lǚ xíng shè} | a travel agency | {通过|tōng guò}{旅行社|lǚ xíng shè}{订|dìng}{票|piào} |
| {预订|yù dìng} | to book, reserve | {预订|yù dìng}{机票|jī piào}, {预订|yù dìng}{酒店|jiǔ diàn} |
| {住宿|zhù sù} | accommodation; to stay (overnight) | {住宿|zhù sù}{费|fèi} (the cost of accommodation) |
| {行程|xíng chéng} | an itinerary, a trip's plan | {行程|xíng chéng}{安排|ān pái}{得|de}{很|hěn}{紧|jǐn}。 (The schedule is tight.) |
| {路线|lù xiàn} | a route (for a trip, a walk) | {旅游|lǚ yóu}{路线|lù xiàn} |
| {线路|xiàn lù} | a line (bus, metro); a circuit | {这|zhè}{条|tiáo}{公交|gōng jiāo}{线路|xiàn lù} |
| {往返|wǎng fǎn} | to go there and back; return (ticket) | {往返|wǎng fǎn}{机票|jī piào} (a return ticket) |
| {长途|cháng tú} | long-distance | {长途|cháng tú}{汽车|qì chē} (a coach), {长途|cháng tú}{电话|diàn huà} |

{路线|lù xiàn} is the way you plan to go; {线路|xiàn lù} is a fixed line that a bus or train runs on (and an electric circuit).

### On the way

| Word | Meaning | Spoken partner |
|---|---|---|
| {列车|liè chē} | a train (written, announcements) | {火车|huǒ chē} |
| {车厢|chē xiāng} | a carriage, a coach (of a train) | |
| {站台|zhàn tái} | a platform | |
| {乘务员|chéng wù yuán} | an attendant (train, plane) | |
| {前往|qián wǎng} | to go to, leave for (written) | {去|qù} |
| {到达|dào dá} | to arrive (written) | {到|dào} |
| {返回|fǎn huí} | to return (written) | {回|huí} |
| {停留|tíng liú} | to stop over, stay (briefly) | {停|tíng} |
| {飞行|fēi xíng} | to fly; a flight | {飞|fēi} |
| {时差|shí chā} | a time difference; jet lag | |
| {海关|hǎi guān} | customs | |

{前往|qián wǎng}, {到达|dào dá} and {返回|fǎn huí} take the place straight after them: {前往|qián wǎng}{北京|Běi jīng}, {到达|dào dá}{上海|Shàng hǎi}, {返回|fǎn huí}{学校|xué xiào}. You'll hear them in
announcements: {开|kāi}{往|wǎng}{西安|Xī'ān}{的|de}{列车|liè chē}{即将|jí jiāng}{到达|dào dá}{三|sān}{号|hào}{站台|zhàn tái}。 (The train for Xi'an will soon arrive at platform 3.) To get over
jet lag is {倒时差|dǎo shí chā}.

### On foot

- {游览|yóu lǎn} (to tour, go sightseeing): {游览|yóu lǎn}{古|gǔ}{城|chéng} (tour the old town).
- {行走|xíng zǒu} (to walk, written): {在|zài}{城墙|chéng qiáng}{上|shàng}{行走|xíng zǒu} (walk on the city wall).
- {迷路|mí lù} (to get lost: a verb with no object): {我|wǒ}{在|zài}{北京|Běi jīng}{迷路|mí lù}{了|le}。
- {绕|rào} (to go round; to make a detour): {前面|qián miàn}{堵车|dǔ chē}，{我们|wǒ men}{绕|rào}{一下|yí xià}{吧|ba}。 You've met {绕|rào} in {围绕|wéi rào} (lesson 26).
- {一路|yí lù} (the whole way; along the way): {一路|yí lù}{上|shang} (on the way), {一路|yí lù}{走|zǒu}{来|lái}.
- {一路顺风|yí lù shùn fēng} (have a good trip, literally "all the way with the wind behind you"): an idiom you say to someone
  setting off. It works as a whole sentence: {祝|zhù}{你|nǐ}{一路顺风|yí lù shùn fēng}！ Some people prefer {一路平安|yí lù píng ān} (a safe journey) for
  flights.

### Weather on the road

- {天空|tiān kōng} (the sky) and {天上|tiān shàng} (in the sky): {天空|tiān kōng}{很|hěn}{蓝|lán}。 {天上|tiān shàng}{一|yí}{片|piàn}{云|yún}{也|yě}{没有|méi yǒu}。
- {雾|wù} (fog): {起|qǐ}{雾|wù}{了|le} (it's getting foggy), {大|dà}{雾|wù}.
- {暴雨|bào yǔ} (a rainstorm), {雨水|yǔ shuǐ} (rainwater; rainfall: {今年|jīn nián}{雨水|yǔ shuǐ}{很|hěn}{多|duō}), {降水|jiàng shuǐ} (precipitation, the word of weather reports).
- {阵|zhèn} (a spell, a burst: a measure word): {一|yí}{阵|zhèn}{雨|yǔ}, {一|yí}{阵|zhèn}{风|fēng}, {一|yí}{阵|zhèn}{笑|xiào}{声|shēng}.
- {预报|yù bào} (to forecast; a forecast): {天气|tiān qì}{预报|yù bào}.
- {傍晚|bàng wǎn} (dusk, early evening).

{天气|tiān qì}{预报|yù bào}{说|shuō}，{明天|míng tiān}{傍晚|bàng wǎn}{有|yǒu}{一|yí}{阵|zhèn}{暴雨|bào yǔ}，{降水|jiàng shuǐ}{的|de}{可能性|kě néng xìng}{很|hěn}{大|dà}。 — The forecast says there'll be a spell of heavy rain tomorrow evening: rain is very likely.

### Poems on the road

Chinese literature ({文学|wén xué}) is full of travel. {诗人|shī rén} (poets) like {李白|Lǐ Bái} (Li Bai) and {王维|Wáng Wéi} (Wang Wei: the honors
lesson 30h2) wrote {诗|shī} (poems) on the road, about mountains, rivers and the home they had left. Lines from
those poems are still quoted for their {智慧|zhì huì} (wisdom): what a journey teaches about time and distance.

## Characters
{=

| Character | Meaning | Pinyin | Radical | Strokes | Words |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| {傍|bàng} | near (in time); beside | bàng | 亻 | 12 | {傍晚|bàng wǎn} |
| {暴|bào} | violent, sudden | bào | {日|rì} | 15 | {暴雨|bào yǔ} |
| {厢|xiāng} (traditional 廂) | carriage; side room | xiāng | {厂|chǎng} | 11 | {车厢|chē xiāng} |
| {返|fǎn} | return | fǎn | 辶 | 7 | {返回|fǎn huí}, {往返|wǎng fǎn} |
| {诗|shī} ✎ (traditional 詩) | poem | shī | 讠 | 8 | {诗|shī}, {诗人|shī rén} |
| {雾|wù} (traditional 霧) | fog | wù | {雨|yǔ} | 13 | {雾|wù} |
| {慧|huì} | wise | huì | {心|xīn} | 15 | {智慧|zhì huì} |
| {阵|zhèn} (traditional 陣) | a spell, a burst | zhèn | 阝 | 6 | {阵|zhèn} |

- {傍|bàng}: 亻 and {旁|páng} ({旁边|páng biān}), which gives a close sound: páng, bàng. {傍晚|bàng wǎn} is the time "next to" the night.
- {暴|bào}: {日|rì} on top, then {共|gòng}-like strokes and 氺 at the bottom. It's in {暴雨|bào yǔ}; the same character is used
  for violence and sudden storms.
- {厢|xiāng}: {厂|chǎng} and {相|xiāng} ({相信|xiāng xìn}), which gives the sound exactly. Traditional 廂 has {广|guǎng} instead of {厂|chǎng} (12 strokes).
- {返|fǎn}: {反|fǎn} (reverse) inside 辶 (walking): to go the reverse way. {反|fǎn} gives the sound.
- {诗|shī}: 讠 (speech) and {寺|sì} (a temple), which gives a close sound. {寺|sì} is also in {持|chí} ({持续|chí xù}) and {特|tè},
  where the sound has drifted. Traditional 詩 has {言|yán} (13 strokes).
- {雾|wù}: {雨|yǔ} (the rain radical) on top of {务|wù} ({服务|fú wù}), which gives the sound. Traditional 霧 has 務 under {雨|yǔ} (19 strokes).
- {慧|huì}: two {丰|fēng} side by side, then 彐 (the radical of lesson 12) and {心|xīn} at the bottom. 彐 is the same part as in
  {雪|xuě} and {扫|sǎo}.
- {阵|zhèn}: 阝 on the left and {车|chē} on the right. A memory aid: chariots lined up by a hill. Traditional 陣 has 車 (9
  strokes).

### Stroke order

- **{返|fǎn}**: {反|fǎn} first (the left-falling stroke, the vertical-left-falling, then {又|yòu}), 辶 last.
- **{暴|bào}**: from the top down: {日|rì}, then the middle part, and 氺 last.
- **{慧|huì}**: the two {丰|fēng} (left one first), then 彐 (three strokes), and {心|xīn} last.
- **{阵|zhèn}**: 阝 first (two strokes), then {车|chē}.

```trace
傍暴厢返诗雾慧阵
```

**Write it**: {诗|shī} is a handwriting character (✎). Write it three times from memory, then {诗人|shī rén} and {写|xiě}{诗|shī}.

### Handwriting review

Five handwriting characters of HSK 4 that every journey needs: {顺|shùn} {程|chéng} {停|tíng} {转|zhuǎn} {夜|yè}. Write each, then
{顺利|shùn lì}, {行程|xíng chéng}, {停留|tíng liú}, {转机|zhuǎn jī} and {夜里|yè lǐ}. (Traditional: 順 12 strokes, 轉 18; the
other three are the same.)
