The advice is neither "always" nor "never". ({读者|dú zhě} dú zhě: readers, HSK 4; {生意|shēng yi} shēng yi: business, HSK 4; {半|bàn}{路|lù}: halfway; {自由|zì yóu} zì yóu: free, lesson 27; {原来|yuán lái}: original, HSK 4.)

questions.stem: Read part of an advice column: “{创业|chuàng yè}{的|de}{前|qián}{两|liǎng}{年|nián}，{很|hěn}{多|duō}{公司|gōng sī}{不但|bú dàn}{不|bú}{挣|zhèng}{钱|qián}，{还|hái}{会|huì}{亏|kuī}{钱|qián}。{假如|jiǎ rú}{你|nǐ}{的|de}{存款|cún kuǎn}{只|zhǐ}{够|gòu}{用|yòng}{半|bàn}{年|nián}，{万一|wàn yī}{生意|shēng yi}{不|bù}{好|hǎo}，{你|nǐ}{就|jiù}{会|huì}{面临|miàn lín}{很|hěn}{大|dà}{的|de}{困难|kùn nan}。{最好|zuì hǎo}{准备|zhǔn bèi}{至少|zhì shǎo}{两|liǎng}{年|nián}{的|de}{生活|shēng huó}{费用|fèi yòng}。” ({生意|shēng yi}: business) How much money does the writer suggest having?
choices: enough to live on for at least two years
enough to pay for the company only
questions.explanation: {最好|zuì hǎo}{准备|zhǔn bèi}{至少|zhì shǎo}{两|liǎng}{年|nián}{的|de}{生活|shēng huó}{费用|fèi yòng}: it's best to have at least two years' living costs, because new companies often lose money in the first two years. Half a year's savings is the risky case.

questions.stem: Read the end of an advice column on starting a business: “{如果|rú guǒ}{这|zhè}{三|sān}{个|gè}{问题|wèn tí}{你|nǐ}{都|dōu}{想|xiǎng}{好|hǎo}{了|le}，{那|nà}{就|jiù}{大胆|dà dǎn}{地|de}{去|qù}{尝试|cháng shì}{吧|ba}。{要不然|yào bù rán}，{说不定|shuō bu dìng}{留|liú}{在|zài}{原来|yuán lái}{的|de}{工作|gōng zuò}，{一边|yì biān}{上班|shàng bān}{一边|yì biān}{准备|zhǔn bèi}，{是|shì}{更|gèng}{好|hǎo}{的|de}{选择|xuǎn zé}。” ({原来|yuán lái}: original) What does the writer mean by the last sentence?
choices: You should never leave your job.
You should start the business while unemployed.
If you aren't ready, staying in your job and preparing may be wiser.
questions.explanation: {要不然|yào bù rán} (otherwise: if you haven't thought it through), {说不定|shuō bu dìng}…{是|shì}{更|gèng}{好|hǎo}{的|de}{选择|xuǎn zé} (perhaps… is the better choice): stay in the job and prepare while working. It's a hedge ({说不定|shuō bu dìng}), not a ban.

questions.stem: In 《{题西林壁|Tí Xī lín Bì}》 by Su Shi, which line follows “{横|héng}{看|kàn}{成|chéng}{岭|lǐng}{侧|cè}{成|chéng}{峰|fēng}”?
choices: {不|bù}{识|shí}{庐山|Lú Shān}{真面目|zhēn miàn mù}
questions.explanation: The poem runs: {横|héng}{看|kàn}{成|chéng}{岭|lǐng}{侧|cè}{成|chéng}{峰|fēng}，{远|yuǎn}{近|jìn}{高|gāo}{低|dī}{各|gè}{不同|bù tóng}。{不|bù}{识|shí}{庐山|Lú Shān}{真面目|zhēn miàn mù}，{只|zhǐ}{缘|yuán}{身|shēn}{在|zài}{此|cǐ}{山|shān}{中|zhōng}。 {千|qiān}{里|lǐ}{共|gòng}{婵娟|chán juān} ends Su Shi's 《{水调歌头|Shuǐ diào gē tóu}》.

questions.stem: In Su Shi's line “{只|zhǐ}{缘|yuán}{身|shēn}{在|zài}{此|cǐ}{山|shān}{中|zhōng}”, what does {只|zhǐ}{缘|yuán} mean?
questions.explanation: {只|zhǐ}{缘|yuán} = {只|zhǐ}{因为|yīn wèi} (only because): {缘|yuán} is a written "because of". The line: only because I am inside this mountain.

questions.stem: People today say “{不|bù}{识|shí}{庐山|Lú Shān}{真面目|zhēn miàn mù}，{只|zhǐ}{缘|yuán}{身|shēn}{在|zài}{此|cǐ}{山|shān}{中|zhōng}” about someone who…
choices: has never been to Mount Lu
is too close to a situation to see it clearly
questions.explanation: The lines say you can't see the mountain's true face because you're inside it: someone in the middle of a situation can't judge it whole. Compare {当局者迷|dāng jú zhě mí}，{旁观者清|páng guān zhě qīng} (the player is confused, the onlooker sees clearly).

questions.stem: In “{不|bù}{识|shí}{庐山|Lú Shān}{真面目|zhēn miàn mù}”, the classical word {识|shí} means the same as…
questions.explanation: {识|shí} here is "to know, recognise", the modern {认识|rèn shi}: I cannot recognise Mount Lu's true face. {不|bù}{识|shí} is read bù shí.

questions.stem: When and why did Su Shi write 《{水调歌头|Shuǐ diào gē tóu}·{明月几时有|míng yuè jǐ shí yǒu}》?
choices: at the Spring Festival, for his parents
at Mid-Autumn 1076, thinking of his brother
questions.explanation: His preface dates it to the Mid-Autumn Festival of 1076 ({丙|bǐng}{辰|chén}{中秋|zhōng qiū}) in Mizhou, and says he wrote it thinking of his brother {子由|Zǐ yóu} ({苏辙|Sū Zhé}). 1084 is the year of 《{题西林壁|Tí Xī lín Bì}》.

questions.stem: In Su Shi's 《{水调歌头|Shuǐ diào gē tóu}》, which line follows “{但|dàn}{愿|yuàn}{人|rén}{长久|cháng jiǔ}”?
choices: {月|yuè}{有|yǒu}{阴晴圆缺|yīn qíng yuán quē}
{人|rén}{有|yǒu}{悲欢离合|bēi huān lí hé}
questions.explanation: {人|rén}{有|yǒu}{悲欢离合|bēi huān lí hé}，{月|yuè}{有|yǒu}{阴晴圆缺|yīn qíng yuán quē}，{此|cǐ}{事|shì}{古|gǔ}{难|nán}{全|quán}。{但|dàn}{愿|yuàn}{人|rén}{长久|cháng jiǔ}，{千|qiān}{里|lǐ}{共|gòng}{婵娟|chán juān}。

questions.stem: In “{千|qiān}{里|lǐ}{共|gòng}{婵娟|chán juān}” (Su Shi), what is {婵娟|chán juān}?
questions.explanation: {婵娟|chán juān} chán juān is a literary word for a lovely woman, and here the lovely moon: though a thousand li apart, we share the moon.

questions.stem: What does {悲欢离合|bēi huān lí hé} mean, as in "{人生|rén shēng}{的|de}{悲欢离合|bēi huān lí hé}"?
choices: sorrow and joy, parting and reunion
questions.explanation: {悲|bēi} (sorrow), {欢|huān} (joy), {离|lí} (parting), {合|hé} (coming together): all of life's ups and downs. {阴晴圆缺|yīn qíng yuán quē} is the moon's changes.

questions.stem: Where does Su Shi's other name, {苏东坡|Sū Dōng pō}, come from?
choices: the eastern city where he was born
a plot of land on an eastern slope he farmed in Huangzhou
questions.explanation: {东坡|Dōng pō} is the "eastern slope" where he farmed in Huangzhou (from 1080); he called himself {东坡居士|Dōng pō Jū shì}. {东坡肉|Dōng pō ròu} (Dongpo pork) is named after him, not the other way round.

questions.stem: Listen. When do people most often quote this line?

audio.text: 但愿人长久，千里共婵娟。

choices: at the Mid-Autumn Festival, to people far away
on the first day of a new job
questions.explanation: {但|dàn}{愿|yuàn}{人|rén}{长久|cháng jiǔ}，{千|qiān}{里|lǐ}{共|gòng}{婵娟|chán juān} (I only wish us long lives, and, a thousand li apart, to share the lovely moon) is the Mid-Autumn line: families apart look at the same full moon.

questions.stem: Listen. Which is NOT said about Su Shi?

audio.text: 苏轼是宋代有名的诗人，他也是书法家和画家，还做过官。

questions.explanation: {诗人|shī rén} (poet), {书法|shū fǎ}{家|jiā} (calligrapher), {画家|huà jiā} (painter), {做|zuò}{过|guo}{官|guān} (served as an official): nothing about music.

questions.stem: Read: “《{题西林壁|Tí Xī lín Bì}》{只有|zhǐ yǒu}{二十八|èr shí bā}{个|gè}{字|zì}，{用|yòng}{的|de}{都|dōu}{是|shì}{简单|jiǎn dān}{的|de}{字|zì}，{可是|kě shì}{说|shuō}{出|chū}{了|le}{一|yí}{个|gè}{深刻|shēn kè}{的|de}{道理|dào li}：{看|kàn}{问题|wèn tí}{的|de}{时候|shí hou}，{站|zhàn}{的|de}{位置|wèi zhì}{不同|bù tóng}，{看|kàn}{到|dào}{的|de}{样子|yàng zi}{也|yě}{不同|bù tóng}。” ({深刻|shēn kè}: profound; {道理|dào li}: truth, point) According to this, why is the poem popular?
choices: It is very long and detailed.
It uses simple words to say something profound.
It was written by an emperor.
questions.explanation: {只有|zhǐ yǒu}{二十八|èr shí bā}{个|gè}{字|zì}，{用|yòng}{的|de}{都|dōu}{是|shì}{简单|jiǎn dān}{的|de}{字|zì}，{可是|kě shì}{说|shuō}{出|chū}{了|le}{一|yí}{个|gè}{深刻|shēn kè}{的|de}{道理|dào li}: few, simple characters, a profound point.

questions.stem: Listen. Which tones are the two syllables?
questions.explanation: {诗人|shī rén} shī rén (poet): a high level tone, then a rising one, 1+2.

questions.stem: Why did paper money first appear in Sichuan in the Song dynasty?
choices: Sichuan had no metal at all.
The coins used there were heavy iron coins of low value.
Paper was cheaper than anywhere else.
questions.explanation: Sichuan used mainly iron coins ({铁钱|tiě qián}), worth much less than copper and heavy to carry, so trade needed something lighter.

questions.stem: Who issued the first {交子|jiāo zǐ}?
questions.explanation: The first {交子|jiāo zǐ} were private notes: merchants in {成都|Chéng dū} (then {益州|Yì zhōu}) took in iron coins and gave paper receipts that could be traded and changed back.

questions.stem: When were official, government-issued {交子|jiāo zǐ} first issued?
questions.explanation: The court approved the {益州交子务|Yì zhōu jiāo zǐ wù} at the end of 1023 by the Chinese calendar (early 1024), and the first official notes appeared in 1024.

questions.stem: What problem made the government take over the issuing of {交子|jiāo zǐ}?
choices: Some issuers printed too many and couldn't pay people back.
questions.explanation: {有的|yǒu de}{商人|shāng rén}{发行|fā xíng}{了|le}{太|tài}{多|duō}{交子|jiāo zǐ}，{最后|zuì hòu}{没法儿|méi fǎr}{把|bǎ}{钱|qián}{还|huán}{给|gěi}{大家|dà jiā}: private notes rested on one issuer's credit ({信用|xìn yòng}), and when it failed, holders lost money.

questions.stem: Which word means "banknote, paper money"?
questions.explanation: {纸币|zhǐ bì} zhǐ bì: paper ({纸|zhǐ}) + money ({币|bì}, lesson 04). {铁钱|tiě qián} are iron coins, {存款|cún kuǎn} savings, {黄金|huáng jīn} gold.

questions.stem: After the government took over, “{交子|jiāo zǐ}{就|jiù}{有|yǒu}{了|le}{国家|guó jiā}{的|de}{信用|xìn yòng}”. What does {信用|xìn yòng} mean here?
choices: the state's backing that people could trust
questions.explanation: {信用|xìn yòng} is trust, credit-worthiness: the notes now had the state behind them, so people used them with more confidence ({用|yòng}{的|de}{人|rén}{也|yě}{更|gèng}{放心|fàng xīn}{了|le}).

questions.stem: Listen. What was wrong with iron coins?

audio.text: 铁钱不但很重，而且不值钱，带着很不方便。

choices: They were heavy and worth little.
They were too valuable to carry.
They were made only in the capital.
questions.explanation: {不但|bú dàn}{很|hěn}{重|zhòng}，{而且|ér qiě}{不|bù}{值钱|zhí qián} (not only heavy but worth little), {带|dài}{着|zhe}{很|hěn}{不|bù}{方便|fāng biàn} (very inconvenient to carry).

questions.stem: Listen. What happened in that year?

audio.text: 1024年，政府在益州设立的机构开始发行官方的交子。

choices: A government office began issuing official notes.
questions.explanation: {政府|zhèng fǔ}{在|zài}{益州|Yì zhōu}{设立|shè lì}{的|de}{机构|jī gòu}{开始|kāi shǐ}{发行|fā xíng}{官方|guān fāng}{的|de}{交子|jiāo zǐ}: an office the government had set up in Yizhou began issuing official jiaozi ({发行|fā xíng}: to issue).

questions.stem: Read: “{为了|wèi le}{节省|jié shěng}{力气|lì qi}，{成都|Chéng dū}{的|de}{一些|yì xiē}{商人|shāng rén}{想|xiǎng}{出|chū}{了|le}{一|yí}{个|gè}{办法|bàn fǎ}：{顾客|gù kè}{把|bǎ}{铁钱|tiě qián}{存在|cún zài}{他们|tā men}{那儿|nàr}，{他们|tā men}{给|gěi}{顾客|gù kè}{一|yì}{张|zhāng}{纸|zhǐ}，{上面|shàng miàn}{写|xiě}{着|zhe}{钱|qián}{数|shù}。{拿|ná}{着|zhe}{这|zhè}{张|zhāng}{纸|zhǐ}，{就|jiù}{可以|kě yǐ}{去|qù}{买|mǎi}{东西|dōng xi}，{也|yě}{可以|kě yǐ}{再|zài}{换|huàn}{回|huí}{铁钱|tiě qián}。” ({力气|lì qi}: effort) How did the first {交子|jiāo zǐ} work?
choices: Customers paid merchants to print money.
Customers left coins with merchants and got a paper note they could spend or change back.
Merchants lent paper to the government.
The paper could only be used once.
questions.explanation: {顾客|gù kè}{把|bǎ}{铁钱|tiě qián}{存在|cún zài}{他们|tā men}{那儿|nàr} (customers left iron coins with them), {给|gěi}{顾客|gù kè}{一|yì}{张|zhāng}{纸|zhǐ} (a paper with the sum), which could be spent or changed back ({再|zài}{换|huàn}{回|huí}{铁钱|tiě qián}).

questions.stem: Read: “{交子|jiāo zǐ}{的|de}{出现|chū xiàn}，{说明|shuō míng}{当时|dāng shí}{的|de}{商业|shāng yè}{已经|yǐ jīng}{很|hěn}{发达|fā dá}，{人们|rén men}{需要|xū yào}{一|yì}{种|zhǒng}{又|yòu}{轻|qīng}{又|yòu}{方便|fāng biàn}{的|de}{钱|qián}。{可见|kě jiàn}，{纸币|zhǐ bì}{不|bú}{是|shì}{谁|shéi}{一下子|yí xià zi}{想|xiǎng}{出来|chū lái}{的|de}，{而|ér}{是|shì}{在|zài}{交易|jiāo yì}{中|zhōng}{慢慢|màn màn}{产生|chǎn shēng}{的|de}。” ({发达|fā dá}: developed; {产生|chǎn shēng}: to come into being) What does the writer conclude?
choices: One clever person invented paper money in a day.
Paper money was forced on unwilling traders.
Paper money grew gradually out of the needs of trade.
Trade in the Song was not developed.
questions.explanation: {可见|kě jiàn} introduces the conclusion: {不|bú}{是|shì}{谁|shéi}{一下子|yí xià zi}{想|xiǎng}{出来|chū lái}{的|de}，{而|ér}{是|shì}{在|zài}{交易|jiāo yì}{中|zhōng}{慢慢|màn màn}{产生|chǎn shēng}{的|de} (not suddenly thought up by someone, but slowly born from trade).

questions.stem: Which city was called {益州|Yì zhōu} in the Song dynasty?
questions.explanation: {益州|Yì zhōu} is the old name of the Chengdu area in Sichuan, where the {益州交子务|Yì zhōu jiāo zǐ wù} issued the official notes.

questions.stem: Listen. Which tones are the two syllables?
questions.explanation: {纸币|zhǐ bì} zhǐ bì (banknote): a dipping tone, then a falling one, 3+4.

questions.stem: Choose the word: {他|tā}{站|zhàn}{在|zài}{那儿|nàr}{一|yí}{动|dòng}{不|bú}{动|dòng}，___ {没|méi}{听见|tīng jiàn}{我|wǒ}{的话|de huà}{似的|shì de}。 (He stood there without moving, as if he hadn't heard me.)
questions.explanation: "As if…" with {似的|shì de} at the end is {仿佛|fǎng fú}…{似的|shì de} (or {好像|hǎo xiàng}…{似的|shì de}). {反正|fǎn zhèng} is "anyway", {刚好|gāng hǎo} "as it happens", {从不|cóng bù} "never".

questions.stem: How is 似的 read (as in {他|tā}{好像|hǎo xiàng}{什么|shén me}{都|dōu}{知道|zhī dào}似的)?
questions.explanation: {似的|shì de} is shì de, with a light {的|de}. The same character is sì in {似乎|sì hū} sì hū (it seems). {的|de} is dí only in {的确|dí què} (indeed).

questions.stem: What does the second half of "{你|nǐ}{去|qù}{不|bu}{去|qù}{都|dōu}{行|xíng}，{反正|fǎn zhèng}{我|wǒ}{是|shì}{要|yào}{去|qù}{的|de}。" tell you?
choices: The speaker is going whatever the listener decides.
The speaker will only go if the listener goes.
The speaker has changed their mind and won't go.
The speaker went already and doesn't want to go again.
questions.explanation: {反正|fǎn zhèng} says the conclusion holds whatever else is true: "you go or not, as you like; I'm going anyway". "Only if you go" would be {只有|zhǐ yǒu}{你|nǐ}{去|qù}，{我|wǒ}{才|cái}{去|qù}.

questions.stem: Which sentence means "I've never been to a bar."?
questions.explanation: Experience ("never, up to now") is {从|cóng}{没|méi} + verb + {过|guo}: {我|wǒ}{从|cóng}{没|méi}{去|qù}{过|guo}{酒吧|jiǔ bā}. {从不|cóng bù} is for a habit or a rule ({我|wǒ}{从不|cóng bú}{去|qù}{酒吧|jiǔ bā}, I never go to bars) and doesn't take {过|guo}.

questions.stem: Which is the usual way to say "She glanced at me."?
questions.explanation: {眼|yǎn} counts looks, after the verb and {了|le}: {看|kàn}{了|le}{一|yì}{眼|yǎn}. A pronoun object goes between them: {看|kàn}{了|le}{我|wǒ}{一|yì}{眼|yǎn}. A noun object can go either side ({看|kàn}{了|le}{一|yì}{眼|yǎn}{手机|shǒu jī}, {看|kàn}{了|le}{手机|shǒu jī}{一|yì}{眼|yǎn}).

questions.stem: What does "{跑|pǎo}{完|wán}{步|bù}，{他|tā}{累|lèi}{得|de}{站不起来|zhàn bu qǐ lái}{了|le}。" mean?
choices: After the run he was too tired to stand up.
He was tired, so he didn't go for a run.
He ran until he was tired, then stood up.
He wasn't tired at all after the run.
questions.explanation: {累|lèi}{得|de}{站不起来|zhàn bu qǐ lái} is a state complement: after {得|de} comes the state the tiredness led to (he couldn't get up). {跑|pǎo}{完|wán}{步|bù} says the run is over.

questions.stem: Which sentence means "It was so hot we were dripping with sweat."?
choices: {天|tiān}{太|tài}{热|rè}，{我们|wǒ men}{热|rè}{得|de}{很|hěn}{出|chū}{了|le}{一|yì}{身|shēn}{汗|hàn}。
{天|tiān}{太|tài}{热|rè}，{我们|wǒ men}{不|bú}{热|rè}{得|de}{出|chū}{汗|hàn}。
{天|tiān}{太|tài}{热|rè}，{我们|wǒ men}{出|chū}{了|le}{一|yì}{身|shēn}{汗|hàn}{得|de}{热|rè}。
{天|tiān}{太|tài}{热|rè}，{我们|wǒ men}{热|rè}{得|de}{出|chū}{了|le}{一|yì}{身|shēn}{汗|hàn}。
questions.explanation: Adjective + {得|de} + the state it leads to: {热|rè}{得|de}{出|chū}{了|le}{一|yì}{身|shēn}{汗|hàn}. Nothing goes between {得|de} and the state (not {热|rè}{得|de}{很|hěn}{出|chū}{了|le}…), and the complement comes after {热|rè}{得|de}, never before it.

questions.stem: Fill the gaps: {小王|Xiǎo Wáng}{最近|zuì jìn}{工作|gōng zuò}{很|hěn}{忙碌|máng lù}，{常常|cháng cháng} (1) {到|dào}{半夜|bàn yè}。{长期|cháng qī}{睡眠|shuì mián}{不足|bù zú}，{他|tā}{白天|bái tiān}{总是|zǒng shì} (2) {很|hěn}{累|lèi}。{同事|tóng shì}{说|shuō}："{你|nǐ}{要|yào} (3) {一下|yí xià}{自己|zì jǐ}{的|de}{状态|zhuàng tài}，{别|bié}{忽视|hū shì}{了|le}{身体|shēn tǐ}。"
questions.explanation: (1) {熬夜|áo yè}{到|dào}{半夜|bàn yè}: stays up till the middle of the night. (2) {显得|xiǎn de}{很|hěn}{累|lèi}: looks tired ({显得|xiǎn de} + adjective). choices: How the writer changed their sleeping habits, and what that changed.

questions.explanation: The writer stayed up late, felt worse and worse, set three rules, and two months later slept better and worked better. The meeting is one example, and the text says the opposite of the last two choices.

questions.stem: A writer who stopped staying up late ends: "{现在|xiàn zài}{我|wǒ}{明白|míng bai}{了|le}：{熬夜|áo yè}{看|kàn}{起来|qǐ lái}{是|shì}{多|duō}{了|le}{一些|yì xiē}{时间|shí jiān}，{其实|qí shí}{是|shì}{在|zài}{花|huā}{明天|míng tiān}{的|de}{精力|jīng lì}。" What do they mean?
choices: Staying up gives you more time for tomorrow's work.
The time you gain at night is paid for with the next day's energy.
Energy is more important at night than in the morning.
They now spend less money than before.
questions.explanation: {看|kàn}{起来|qǐ lái}…{其实|qí shí} is "it looks like…, but in fact": the extra hours seem a gain, but they use up ({花|huā}, to spend) tomorrow's {精力|jīng lì} (energy). {花|huā} here is spending energy, not money.

questions.stem: Listen. What does the speaker plan to do?

audio.text: 我最近工作太忙了，每天都熬夜，白天显得很没有精神。我打算从下个月开始调整一下，每天十一点以前睡觉。

choices: work late every night next month
go to bed before eleven from next month
questions.explanation: {打算|dǎ suàn}{从|cóng}{下|xià}{个|gè}{月|yuè}{开始|kāi shǐ}{调整|tiáo zhěng}{一下|yí xià}，{每|měi}{天|tiān}{十一|shí yī}{点|diǎn}{以前|yǐ qián}{睡觉|shuì jiào}: from next month, bed before eleven every night. Staying up is what happens now.

questions.stem: Listen. How does the speaker feel?

audio.text: 你又要去酒吧？反正我说什么你也不会听，你自己决定吧。

questions.explanation: {反正|fǎn zhèng}{我|wǒ}{说|shuō}{什么|shén me}{你|nǐ}{也|yě}{不|bú}{会|huì}{听|tīng} ("you won't listen whatever I say anyway"), then {你|nǐ}{自己|zì jǐ}{决定|jué dìng}{吧|ba} (decide for yourself): the speaker has given up arguing. {又|yòu} (again) shows the annoyance.

questions.stem: Listen. What will the speaker do?

audio.text: 我刚好也要去楼下的便利店，你要买什么？我帮你带回来。

choices: go to the shop and bring something back for the listener
stay in and wait for the listener

questions.explanation: {刚好|gāng hǎo}{也|yě}{要|yào}{去|qù}: is going anyway, as it happens; {我|wǒ}{帮|bāng}{你|nǐ}{带|dài}{回来|huí lái}: I'll bring it back for you.

questions.stem: Listen. What does the speaker suggest doing next?

audio.text: 你已经坐了三个小时了，腰不疼吗？站起来伸一伸，我们去楼下走走吧。

choices: having a stretch and a walk downstairs

questions.explanation: {站|zhàn}{起来|qǐ lái}{伸一伸|shēn yi shēn} (get up and stretch), {去|qù}{楼|lóu}{下|xià}{走走|zǒu zou} (go for a walk downstairs). The back is a question ({腰|yāo}{不|bù}{疼|téng}{吗|ma}？), not a reason to see a doctor.

questions.stem: Listen. Which tones are the two syllables?
questions.explanation: {熬夜|áo yè} áo yè (to stay up late): a rising tone, then a falling one, 2+4.

questions.stem: Listen. Which tones are the two syllables?
questions.explanation: {失眠|shī mián} shī mián (to be unable to sleep): a level tone, then a rising one, 1+2.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Chinese.
questions.prompt: Wang Fang is so busy she doesn't even have time to eat.
questions.explanation: {王芳|Wáng Fāng}{忙|máng}{得|de}{连|lián}{吃|chī}{饭|fàn}{的|de}{时间|shí jiān}{都|dōu}{没有|méi yǒu}。 A state complement ({忙|máng}{得|de}…) with {连|lián}…{都|dōu} (even). {很|hěn} can't go between {得|de} and the state.

questions.stem: Write the missing character (in characters, or pinyin with tone marks): {他|tā}{今天|jīn tiān}{显得|xiǎn de}{很|hěn}{有|yǒu}{精|jīng}___。 (He looks very lively today.)
questions.explanation: {精神|jīng shén} jīng shén (spirit; liveliness). {={神|shén}=}: 礻 (the radical of gods and rites) + {申|shēn} shēn for the sound, 9 strokes.

questions.stem: Write the missing character (in characters, or pinyin with tone marks): {他|tā}___ {乎|hū}{不|bú}{太|tài}{高兴|gāo xìng}。 (He doesn't seem very happy.)
questions.explanation: {似乎|sì hū} sì hū (it seems). {={似|sì}=}: 亻 + {以|yǐ}, 6 strokes; it is also shì in {似的|shì de}.

questions.stem: What does "{你|nǐ}{尽量|jǐn liàng}{早|zǎo}{点儿|diǎnr}{回来|huí lái}。" mean?
choices: You must be back early, or else.
Come back early, as you did last time.
Try to come back as early as you can.
You came back a bit early.
questions.explanation: {尽量|jǐn liàng} + verb: as far as possible, as much as you can. It asks politely and admits the other person may not fully manage. "You must" would be {你|nǐ}{一定|yí dìng}{要|yào}{早|zǎo}{点儿|diǎnr}{回来|huí lái}.

questions.stem: Which sentence is correct written Chinese? (Your diet shouldn't be too simple.)
choices: {饮食|yǐn shí}{不要|bú yào}{过于|guò yú}{很|hěn}{简单|jiǎn dān}。
{饮食|yǐn shí}{不要|bú yào}{过于|guò yú}{简单|jiǎn dān}。
{饮食|yǐn shí}{过于|guò yú}{不要|bú yào}{简单|jiǎn dān}。
{饮食|yǐn shí}{不要|bú yào}{简单|jiǎn dān}{过于|guò yú}。
questions.explanation: {过于|guò yú} is the written "too": it goes straight before the adjective (no {很|hěn} between them), and written style leaves out the spoken {了|le}. The spoken version is {吃|chī}{的|de}{东西|dōng xi}{不要|bú yào}{太|tài}{简单|jiǎn dān}{了|le}, with {太|tài}…{了|le}.

questions.stem: What does "{夜市|yè shì}{的|de}{烧烤|shāo kǎo}{好吃|hǎo chī}{得|de}{不得了|bù dé liǎo}。" mean?
choices: The night-market barbecue is terribly good.
The night-market barbecue isn't good enough.
You mustn't eat the night-market barbecue.
The night-market barbecue was a disaster.
questions.explanation: Adjective + {得|de}{不得了|bù dé liǎo} is the strongest degree: "unbelievably good". {不得了|bù dé liǎo} alone is an exclamation that something terrible has happened, but after {好吃|hǎo chī}{得|de} it only says how good it is.

questions.stem: You're full and the plate is huge. Which sentence says "I can't eat this much."?
choices: {我|wǒ}{吃不得|chī bu de}{这么|zhè me}{多|duō}。
{我|wǒ}{吃不了|chī bu liǎo}{这么|zhè me}{多|duō}。
questions.explanation: A limit of amount or ability is V{不了|bu liǎo} ({吃不了|chī bu liǎo}, can't manage). {吃不得|chī bu de} would mean you mustn't eat it, because it would harm you. The other two aren't sentences.

questions.stem: What does "{过期|guò qī}{的|de}{牛奶|niú nǎi}{喝不得|hē bu de}。" mean?
choices: Nobody wants to drink out-of-date milk.
There's too much out-of-date milk to drink.
questions.explanation: V{不得|bu de} says something mustn't be done because of what would happen: drinking it would make you ill. It doesn't say the milk can't be found ({找不到|zhǎo bu dào}) or that there's too much ({喝不完|hē bu wán}).

questions.stem: Choose the word: ___ {运动|yùn dòng}{对|duì}{身体|shēn tǐ}{有益|yǒu yì}。 (Exercise in moderation is good for you.)
questions.explanation: {适当|shì dàng} is "suitable, in moderation". {过度|guò dù}{运动|yùn dòng} is excessive exercise (not beneficial), {过于|guò yú} goes before adjectives ({过于|guò yú}{紧张|jǐn zhāng}), and {不得了|bù dé liǎo} follows {得|de}.

questions.stem: Choose the word: {水|shuǐ}{是|shì}{人体|rén tǐ}___ {的|de}。 (Water is essential to the body.)
questions.explanation: {必需|bì xū} is "essential, a thing you must have" ({必需|bì xū}{品|pǐn}, necessities). {必须|bì xū} (same sound) is "must do" and goes before a verb: {你|nǐ}{必须|bì xū}{喝|hē}{水|shuǐ}. {足够|zú gòu} is "enough".

questions.stem: Fill the gaps: {李明|Lǐ Míng}{在|zài}{英国|Yīng guó}{学|xué}{会|huì}{了|le}{做饭|zuò fàn}。{他|tā} (1) {每|měi}{天|tiān}{自己|zì jǐ}{做|zuò}，{因为|yīn wèi}{天天|tiān tiān}{吃|chī}{西餐|xī cān}，{他|tā}{真|zhēn}{的|de}{受不了|shòu bu liǎo}{了|le}。{他|tā}{说|shuō}，{那儿|nàr}{的|de}{黄瓜|huáng guā}{特别|tè bié}{大|dà}， (2) {也|yě}{跟|gēn}{国内|guó nèi}{的|de}{不|bù}{一样|yí yàng}。{有|yǒu}{一|yí}{次|cì}，{他|tā}{的|de}{牛奶|niú nǎi} (3) {三|sān}{天|tiān}{了|le}，{王芳|Wáng Fāng}{说|shuō}："{过期|guò qī}{的|de}{牛奶|niú nǎi}{可|kě}{喝不得|hē bu de}！"
questions.explanation: (1) {尽量|jǐn liàng}{每|měi}{天|tiān}{自己|zì jǐ}{做|zuò}: cooks for himself every day as far as he can. (2) {口味|kǒu wèi}{也|yě}{跟|gēn}{国内|guó nèi}{的|de}{不|bù}{一样|yí yàng}: they don't taste the same as at home. (3) {过期|guò qī}{三|sān}{天|tiān}{了|le}: three days past its date. {适当|shì dàng} (in moderation) and {必需|bì xū} (essential) don't fit.

questions.stem: Kaolin, the white clay of porcelain, is called {高岭土|gāo lǐng tǔ} in Chinese. Where does the name come from?
choices: the Gaoling hills near Jingdezhen, whose clay the potters used
questions.explanation: {高岭|Gāo lǐng} (Gāolǐng, "High Ridge") is a range of hills near {景德镇|Jǐng dé zhèn}; its clay was used at the Jingdezhen kilns for centuries. English "kaolin" comes from the same name.

questions.stem: What colour is the glaze of {青瓷|qīng cí} (celadon)?
questions.explanation: {青|qīng} is the blue-green of lesson 10 ({青|qīng}{山|shān}, green hills): {青瓷|qīng cí} has a green or blue-green glaze and little painting. White with blue painting is {青花|qīng huā} (blue-and-white).

questions.stem: Why does the blue of {青花|qīng huā} (blue-and-white) porcelain stay bright for centuries?
choices: It is painted on after the firing.
It is repainted every few years.
It is painted under a clear glaze and fired once.
It is made of blue clay.
questions.explanation: The cobalt blue is painted straight onto the dried body, a clear glaze goes over it, and the piece is fired once: the colour is sealed under the glass ({画|huà}{在|zài}{釉|yòu}{的|de}{下面|xià miàn}).

questions.stem: In which dynasty was the blue-and-white technique established?
questions.explanation: Blue-and-white was established under the Yuan ({元代|Yuán dài}): the earliest dated pieces bear the year 1351, and the cobalt was imported from Iran (Persia). Under the Ming and Qing it became Jingdezhen's great export.

questions.stem: Jingdezhen ({景德镇|Jǐng dé zhèn}) is known as {瓷都|cí dū}. What does {瓷都|cí dū} mean?
questions.explanation: {瓷|cí} (porcelain) + {都|dū} dū (a capital, as in {首都|shǒu dū}): the porcelain capital. {景德镇|Jǐng dé zhèn} took its name in 1004, from the Song emperor's Jingde ({景德|Jǐng dé}) reign.

questions.stem: Why is porcelain called "china" in English?
choices: A European potter named it after his dog.
It is made of a clay called "china" in Chinese.
It came from China, which for a long time was where porcelain came from.
questions.explanation: For centuries porcelain came from China, so English called it after the country; kaolin is "china clay" for the same reason. In Chinese, porcelain is {瓷器|cí qì}.

({在于|zài yú}: lies in)

They are too simple to be in a museum.

questions.stem: A museum guide says: "{在|zài}{英语|Yīng yǔ}{里|lǐ}，{瓷器|cí qì}{和|hé}{中国|Zhōng guó}{用|yòng}{的|de}{是|shì}{一|yí}{个|gè}{词|cí}：\"china\"。{这|zhè}{说明|shuō míng}{在|zài}{很|hěn}{长|cháng}{的|de}{时间|shí jiān}{里|lǐ}，{外国|wài guó}{人|rén}{一|yí}{看|kàn}{到|dào}{瓷器|cí qì}，{就|jiù}{会|huì}{想|xiǎng}{到|dào}{中国|Zhōng guó}。" What point is the guide making?
choices: China learned to make porcelain from abroad.
For a long time, porcelain and China went together in foreigners' minds.
questions.explanation: {一|yī}…{就|jiù}…: the moment foreigners saw porcelain, they thought of China; the shared English word shows it.

questions.stem: Put the steps of making porcelain in order.
choices: {做坯|zuò pī}: shape the clay and let it dry
{上釉|shàng yòu}: cover it with glaze
{冷|lěng}: let it cool, then open the kiln
questions.explanation: Shape and dry ({做坯|zuò pī}), paint ({画|huà}), glaze ({上釉|shàng yòu}), fire in the kiln ({窑|yáo}{里|lǐ}{烧|shāo}) at well over 1,200 °C, and let it cool slowly. For blue-and-white, the painting goes on before the glaze, so it ends up under it.

questions.stem: Between which two values did Zu Chongzhi ({祖冲之|Zǔ Chōng zhī}) place π?
questions.explanation: The 《{隋书|Suí shū}》 (Book of Sui) records 3.1415926 < π < 3.1415927: π correct to seven decimal places.

questions.stem: Zu Chongzhi's {密率|mì lǜ} ("close ratio") for π is the fraction…
questions.explanation: {密率|mì lǜ} is 355/113 (3.1415929…, correct to six places); {约率|yuē lǜ}, the "approximate ratio", is 22/7.

questions.stem: How do you read 22/7 in Chinese?
choices: {七二十二|qī èr shí èr}{分|fēn}{之|zhī}
questions.explanation: A fraction is read denominator first: {七|qī}{分|fēn}{之|zhī}{二十二|èr shí èr} ("of seven parts, twenty-two"). 355/113 is {一百一十三|yì bǎi yī shí sān}{分|fēn}{之|zhī}{三百五十五|sān bǎi wǔ shí wǔ}.

questions.stem: Why don't historians know exactly how Zu Chongzhi calculated π?
choices: He kept it a secret from everyone.
He copied it from another country.
His book, 《{缀术|Zhuì shù}》, has been lost.
questions.explanation: His mathematical book, 《{缀术|Zhuì shù}》, was lost centuries ago. Historians think he used {刘徽|Liú Huī}'s {割圆术|gē yuán shù} (cutting the circle with polygons).

questions.stem: How does {割圆术|gē yuán shù} ("cutting the circle") approach π?
choices: by doubling the sides of a polygon inside the circle again and again
by measuring a real wheel with a rope
questions.explanation: Start with a regular hexagon inside the circle, double the sides (12, 24, 48…), and the polygon's perimeter comes ever closer to the circle's. Historians suggest Zu went to 12,288 or 24,576 sides.

questions.stem: About how long did Zu Chongzhi's value of π remain the most exact in the world?
questions.explanation: From the fifth century until the fifteenth, when the Persian astronomer al-Kashi calculated further: about nine hundred years.

questions.stem: What is true of Zu Chongzhi's calendar, the {大明历|Dà míng lì}?
choices: It was adopted the year he made it.
It was made by Liu Hui.
It was adopted only in 510, after his death, and allowed for the precession ({岁差|suì chā}).
questions.explanation: He presented it around 462; it was adopted in 510, helped by his son {祖暅|Zǔ Gèng}. It was the first Chinese calendar to take account of the precession of the equinoxes ({岁差|suì chā}).

questions.stem: A text about Zu Chongzhi says: "{那|nà}{时候|shí hou}{没有|méi yǒu}{计算机|jì suàn jī}，{也|yě}{没有|méi yǒu}{计算器|jì suàn qì}，{人们|rén men}{用|yòng}{一|yì}{种|zhǒng}{叫|jiào}\"{算筹|suàn chóu}\"{的|de}{小|xiǎo}{木棍|mù gùn}{来|lái}{计算|jì suàn}。" What did people calculate with? ({计算器|jì suàn qì}: a calculator)
questions.explanation: {算筹|suàn chóu} are counting rods, small sticks of wood ({小|xiǎo}{木棍|mù gùn}). There were no computers or calculators.

questions.stem: A text says of Zu Chongzhi's method: "{每|měi}{一|yí}{步|bù}{都|dōu}{要|yào}{开方|kāi fāng}，{非常|fēi cháng}{麻烦|má fan}。{祖冲之|Zǔ Chōng zhī}{能|néng}{做|zuò}{到|dào}{这|zhè}{一|yì}{点|diǎn}，{说明|shuō míng}{他|tā}{不但|bú dàn}{聪明|cōng ming}，{而且|ér qiě}{非常|fēi cháng}{有|yǒu}{耐心|nài xīn}。" What does the writer admire? ({开方|kāi fāng}: to take a square root)
choices: his cleverness and his great patience
questions.explanation: {不但|bú dàn}{聪明|cōng ming}，{而且|ér qiě}{非常|fēi cháng}{有|yǒu}{耐心|nài xīn}: not only clever but extremely patient, because every step needed a square root by hand.

A polygon can never have more than six sides.
The more sides, the closer the polygon comes to a circle.
questions.explanation: {越|yuè}…{越|yuè}…: the more sides ({边|biān}{越|yuè}{多|duō}), the closer it comes to the circle ({就|jiù}{越|yuè}{接近|jiē jìn}{圆|yuán}).

questions.explanation: {三|sān}{点|diǎn}{一四一五九二六|yī sì yī wǔ jiǔ èr liù}: 3.1415926. Digits after the point are read one by one, and {一|yī} keeps its first tone (yī).

questions.stem: Which word fills the gap? {这|zhè}{次|cì}{谈话|tán huà}{增进|zēng jìn}{了|le}___ {的|de}{了解|liǎo jiě}。 (This conversation improved our understanding of each other.)
questions.explanation: {彼此|bǐ cǐ} is a pronoun, so it can stand before {的|de} and describe a noun: {彼此|bǐ cǐ}{的|de}{了解|liǎo jiě}. {互相|hù xiāng} is an adverb and goes before a verb ({互相|hù xiāng}{了解|liǎo jiě}), so {互相|hù xiāng}{的|de}{了解|liǎo jiě} would be unusual. {自己|zì jǐ}{的|de}{了解|liǎo jiě} is "one's own understanding", and {一起|yì qǐ} (together) can't stand before {的|de} here.

questions.stem: Which word fills the gap? {昨天|zuó tiān}{我|wǒ}___ {等到|děng dào}{晚上|wǎn shang}{十|shí}{点|diǎn}，{他|tā}{也|yě}{没|méi}{来|lái}。 (Yesterday I waited right up to ten in the evening, and he still didn't come.)
questions.explanation: {一直|yì zhí} can run up to a point in time: {一直|yì zhí}{等到|děng dào}{十|shí}{点|diǎn}. {始终|shǐ zhōng} also means "all along", but it covers a stretch from start to finish and doesn't take an end point with {到|dào} ({他|tā}{始终|shǐ zhōng}{没|méi}{来|lái} "he never came, the whole time" is fine). {从来|cóng lái} needs a negative ({从来|cóng lái}{没|méi}…) and {总是|zǒng shì} is "always, every time".

questions.stem: What does {分别|fēn bié} mean in {他们|tā men}{俩|liǎ}{分别|fēn bié}{来自|lái zì}{北京|Běi jīng}{和|hé}{上海|Shàng hǎi}？

questions.stem: Which sentence is correct?

questions.explanation: {毕竟|bì jìng} gives the deciding fact: he's new, so mistakes are understandable. {居然|jū rán} marks a surprise, {根本|gēn běn} strengthens a negative ({根本|gēn běn}{不|bù}), and {从来|cóng lái} needs a negative ({从来|cóng lái}{没|méi}).

questions.stem: Which word fills the gap? {我|wǒ}___ {不|bú}{认识|rèn shi}{他|tā}，{怎么|zěn me}{会|huì}{给|gěi}{他|tā}{打电话|dǎ diàn huà}{呢|ne}？ (I don't know him at all, so why would I phone him?)
questions.explanation: {根本|gēn běn}{不|bù}: not at all, a strong negative. {毕竟|bì jìng} (after all) and {果然|guǒ rán} (as expected) don't go with {不|bú}{认识|rèn shi} here, and {依然|yī rán} (still) would mean "I still don't know him", which doesn't fit "at all".

questions.stem: Which sentence is wrong?
choices: {他|tā}{毕竟|bì jìng}{还是|hái shi}{个|gè}{孩子|hái zi}。
{毕竟|bì jìng}{是|shì}{第|dì}{一|yī}{次|cì}，{紧张|jǐn zhāng}{很|hěn}{正常|zhèng cháng}。
questions.explanation: {毕竟|bì jìng} is never used in questions. "What on earth do you want to say?" is {你|nǐ}{到底|dào dǐ}{想|xiǎng}{说|shuō}{什么|shén me}？ The other two {毕竟|bì jìng} sentences are statements giving the deciding fact (he's a child; it's the first time).

questions.stem: How is the character 看 read in {周末|zhōu mò}{我|wǒ}{得|děi}{在|zài}{家|jiā}看{孩子|hái zi} (At the weekend I have to stay home and mind the kids)?
questions.explanation: "To look after, to mind" is {看|kān} kān, first tone: {看|kān}{孩子|hái zi}, {看|kān}{家|jiā}. {看|kàn} kàn (to look) would make {看|kàn}{孩子|hái zi} "to look at the children".

questions.stem: Which word fits? {这些|zhè xiē}{老|lǎo}{照片|zhào piàn}，{奶奶|nǎi nai}{一|yì}{张|zhāng}{也|yě}___ {扔|rēng}。 (Grandma can't bear to throw away a single one of these old photos.)
questions.explanation: {舍不得|shě bu de} + verb: can't bear to do it. {舍得|shě de} is the opposite (willing to), {不得不|bù dé bù} is "have to" (HSK 4), and {不得了|bù dé liǎo} (lesson 07) is "extremely; terrible".

questions.stem: Someone from Beijing talks about their mother's mother. What are they most likely to call her?
questions.explanation: In the north, Beijing included, the mother's parents are {姥姥|lǎo lao} lǎo lao and {姥爷|lǎo ye} lǎo ye; in the south and in much standard usage, {外婆|wài pó} and {外公|wài gōng}. {奶奶|nǎi nai} is the father's mother, {大妈|dà mā} a polite address for an older woman, and {太太|tài tai} a wife.

questions.stem: Which word fits? {父母|fù mǔ}{应该|yīng gāi}___ {孩子|hái zi}{自己|zì jǐ}{的|de}{选择|xuǎn zé}。 (Parents should respect their children's own choices.)
questions.explanation: {尊重|zūn zhòng} (HSK 4) is to respect a choice, a wish, a right. {尊敬|zūn jìng} is to respect a person, to look up to them ({尊敬|zūn jìng}{老人|lǎo rén}). {看望|kàn wàng} is to visit and {依靠|yī kào} to rely on.

questions.explanation: {={相册|xiàng cè} xiàng cè: {册|cè}, five strokes, two narrow frames crossed by one long horizontal (bamboo slips tied together). {用|yòng} has a frame and a vertical through it, {再|zài} has an extra horizontal on top, and {角|jiǎo} a short left-falling stroke at the top.=}

audio.text: 我今天有事，不能去参加婚礼了，你替我向新郎新娘说一声恭喜吧。

choices: go to the wedding instead of the speaker

audio.text: 先生您好，欢迎光临！请问您几位？

questions.stem: Listen. What is the speaker doing?

audio.text: 这是我们家乡的特产，一点儿心意，请您一定收下。

questions.explanation: {这|zhè}{是|shì}{我们|wǒ men}{家乡|jiā xiāng}{的|de}{特产|tè chǎn} (a speciality of our home town), {一点儿|yì diǎnr}{心意|xīn yì} (a small token), {请|qǐng}{您|nín}{一定|yí dìng}{收|shōu}{下|xià} (please do accept it): the polite words for handing over a gift.

questions.stem: Listen. What does the speaker want to know?

questions.stem: Listen. Which tones are the two syllables?
questions.explanation: {恭喜|gōng xǐ} gōng xǐ (congratulations): a high level tone, then a dipping one, 1+3.

questions.stem: When did {郑和|Zhèng Hé} Zheng He make his voyages to the "Western Ocean" ({西洋|Xī yáng})?
questions.explanation: The seven voyages ran from 1405 to 1433, under the early Ming ({明朝|Míng cháo}), most of them in the reign of the Yongle Emperor ({永乐|Yǒng lè}). 1271–1295 is Marco Polo's time.

questions.stem: How many voyages did Zheng He lead?
questions.explanation: {郑和|Zhèng Hé}{一共|yí gòng}{七|qī}{次|cì}{下西洋|xià Xī yáng}: seven voyages in all, most of them lasting about two years.

questions.stem: What did people of Zheng He's time mean by {西洋|Xī yáng} (the "Western Ocean")?
choices: the seas and lands south and west of China, from South-East Asia to the Indian Ocean
the Pacific Ocean east of China
questions.explanation: {那|nà}{时候|shí hou}{人们|rén men}{说|shuō}{的|de}"{西洋|Xī yáng}"，{指|zhǐ}{的|de}{是|shì}{中国|Zhōng guó}{南|nán}{边|biān}{和|hé}{西|xī}{边|biān}{的|de}{大|dà}{海|hǎi}{和|hé}{附近|fù jìn}{的|de}{地方|dì fang}: the seas south and west of China and the lands round them. Today {西洋|Xī yáng} often means "the West", but not in the Ming.

questions.stem: What was the farthest the fleets reached, according to the records?
questions.explanation: The fifth to seventh voyages reached ports such as Malindi and Mogadishu on the East African coast ({最|zuì}{远|yuǎn}{到|dào}{了|le}{非洲|Fēi zhōu}{的|de} {东部|dōng bù}), as well as Hormuz and Aden.

questions.stem: Which statement about the "treasure ships" ({宝船|bǎo chuán}) is true?
choices: Historians agree they were exactly 120 metres long.
Their size is disputed: there is no agreed answer.
None of them sailed beyond China's coast.
questions.explanation: Ming records give very large sizes, which many historians doubt; estimates differ widely ({宝船|bǎo chuán}{到底|dào dǐ}{有|yǒu}{多|duō}{大|dà}…{至今|zhì jīn}{还|hái} {没有|méi yǒu}{一致|yí zhì}{的|de}{答案|dá àn}).

questions.stem: People at the Ming court compared the giraffe ({长颈鹿|cháng jǐng lù}) the fleet brought back with what?
choices: the qilin ({麒麟|qí lín}), a lucky animal of legend
questions.explanation: The giraffe was seen as the qilin of legend, a sign of good fortune: {觉得|jué de}{它|tā}{很|hěn}{像|xiàng}{古书|gǔ shū}{里|lǐ}{说|shuō}{的|de}"{麒麟|qí lín}".

questions.stem: Who was {马欢|Mǎ Huān} Ma Huan?
choices: an interpreter on three voyages, who wrote a book about the countries he saw
the emperor who sent the fleets
the captain of the largest treasure ship
questions.explanation: Ma Huan sailed as an interpreter on the fourth, sixth and seventh voyages and wrote 《{瀛涯胜览|Yíng yá shèng lǎn}》, published in 1451.

questions.stem: Read: {历史|lì shǐ}{书|shū}{上|shàng}{说|shuō}，{第|dì}{一|yī}{次|cì}{出发|chū fā}{的|de}{时候|shí hou}，{有|yǒu}{两百|liǎng bǎi}{多|duō}{条|tiáo}{船|chuán}，{两万|liǎng wàn}{多|duō}{人|rén}。 What does it say about the first voyage?
choices: It had about two hundred people.
It had more than two hundred ships and more than twenty thousand people.
questions.explanation: {两百|liǎng bǎi}{多|duō}{条|tiáo}{船|chuán} (more than two hundred ships: {条|tiáo} is the measure word for boats), {两万|liǎng wàn}{多|duō}{人|rén} (more than twenty thousand people). Other sources give over three hundred ships; the figures differ.

questions.stem: Read: {郑和|Zhèng Hé}1371{年|nián}{左右|zuǒ yòu}{出生|chū shēng}{在|zài}{云南|Yún nán}，{原来|yuán lái}{姓|xìng}{马|Mǎ}。 What was Zheng He's family name at birth?
questions.explanation: {原来|yuán lái}{姓|xìng}{马|Mǎ}: his family name was originally Ma (he was known as {马和|Mǎ Hé}). {郑|Zhèng} was a surname given to him later.

questions.stem: Listen. How far did the fleets go?

audio.text: 郑和一共七次下西洋，最远到了非洲的东部。

choices: as far as the east of Africa
questions.explanation: {最|zuì}{远|yuǎn}{到|dào}{了|le}{非洲|Fēi zhōu}{的|de}{东部|dōng bù}: at the farthest, to the east of Africa. {一共|yí gòng}{七|qī}{次|cì} is "seven times in all".

questions.stem: Listen. What did people rush to see?

audio.text: 船队还带回了长颈鹿，很多人都跑去看。

questions.explanation: {船队|chuán duì}{还|hái}{带|dài}{回|huí}{了|le}{长颈鹿|cháng jǐng lù}: the fleet also brought back a giraffe; {很|hěn}{多|duō}{人|rén}{都|dōu}{跑|pǎo}{去|qù}{看|kàn}: lots of people ran to see it.

questions.stem: What did the fleets carry from China?
questions.explanation: They took {瓷器|cí qì}、{丝绸|sī chóu}{和|hé}{茶叶|chá yè} (porcelain, silk and tea) and gifts for foreign rulers, and brought back spices, medicines, gems and animals.

questions.stem: Listen. Which tones are the two syllables?
questions.explanation: {船队|chuán duì} chuán duì (a fleet): a rising tone, then a falling one, 2+4.

questions.stem: Where is the home of the Naxi ({纳西族|Nà xī zú}) and the Dongba script?

choices: not to be late for tomorrow's speech
to give the speech instead of someone else
to arrive late but stay to the end

questions.stem: Which character completes the word? {意|yì}___ (significance)
questions.explanation: {意义|yì yì} yì yì: {={义|yì}=} is three strokes, a dot, then a left-falling and a right-falling stroke crossing. {={叉|chā}=} (a fork) has a hook and a dot; {={又|yòu}=} and {={文|wén}=} have no dot inside. Traditional {+{义|yì}+} is {羊|yáng} over {我|wǒ}.

questions.stem: What does the idiom {守株待兔|shǒu zhū dài tù} describe today?

questions.stem: In the classical line "{兔|tù}{走|zǒu}{触|chù}{株|zhū}，{折|zhé}{颈|jǐng}{而|ér}{死|sǐ}", what does {走|zǒu} mean?

questions.stem: What does the idiom {刻舟求剑|kè zhōu qiú jiàn} describe today?

questions.explanation: The man marked the boat where his sword fell, but the boat moved on. The idiom describes judging by out-of-date standards, not seeing that things have changed.

questions.stem: What does the idiom {画蛇添足|huà shé tiān zú} describe today?

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Chinese.
questions.prompt: They say this film was made from a true story.
questions.explanation: {据说|jù shuō}{这|zhè}{部|bù}{电影|diàn yǐng}{是|shì}{根据|gēn jù}{一|yí}{个|gè}{真实|zhēn shí}{的|de}{故事|gù shi}{拍|pāi}{的|de}。 {据说|jù shuō} opens the sentence (it's said), or follows the subject ({这|zhè}{部|bù}{电影|diàn yǐng}{据说|jù shuō}{是|shì}…); {是|shì}…{的|de} frames how the film was made, with {根据|gēn jù} (based on) + the story before {拍|pāi}. {纷纷|fēn fēn} needs many people reacting, so it has no place here.

questions.stem: Choose the word: {听|tīng}{到|dào}{这个|zhè ge}{好|hǎo}{消息|xiāo xi}，{同学们|tóng xué men} ___ {表示|biǎo shì}{祝贺|zhù hè}。 (When they heard the good news, the classmates all sent their congratulations.)
questions.explanation: {纷纷|fēn fēn}: many people, each reacting in the same way. {即将|jí jiāng} is "about to", {据说|jù shuō} "it's said", {逐步|zhú bù} "step by step" (for planned change).

questions.stem: Which sentence is NOT correct?
choices: {新|xīn}{的|de}{地铁站|dì tiě zhàn}{即将|jí jiāng}{开通|kāi tōng}。
{他|tā}{纷纷|fēn fēn}{表示|biǎo shì}{同意|tóng yì}。
{据说|jù shuō}{他|tā}{下个月|xià gè yuè}{结婚|jié hūn}。
questions.explanation: {纷纷|fēn fēn} always has many people (or things) as its subject, so one person can't {纷纷|fēn fēn} anything: {他|tā}{表示|biǎo shì}{同意|tóng yì}. The other three are correct: {陆续|lù xù} (one after another), {即将|jí jiāng} (about to), {据说|jù shuō} (it's said).

questions.stem: Choose the measure word: {这|zhè}{部|bù}{电视剧|diàn shì jù}{一共|yí gòng}{有|yǒu}{四十|sì shí} ___。 (The series has forty episodes.)
questions.explanation: {集|jí} counts episodes. {部|bù} counts the whole series or film, {册|cè} volumes and copies of books, {本|běn} books.

questions.stem: Choose the word: {她|tā}{在|zài}{报纸|bào zhǐ}{上|shàng} ___ {了|le}{一|yì}{篇|piān}{文章|wén zhāng}。 (She published an article in the paper.)
questions.explanation: {发表|fā biǎo} is the verb for an article or a view: {发表|fā biǎo}{文章|wén zhāng}. {出版|chū bǎn} is for a whole book or magazine, {公布|gōng bù} for results and lists, and {收看|shōu kàn} is "to watch" a programme.

questions.stem: Choose the word: {考试|kǎo shì}{成绩|chéng jì}{明天|míng tiān}{在|zài}{网上|wǎng shàng} ___。 (The exam results will be published online tomorrow.)
questions.explanation: {公布|gōng bù} makes results or lists public for everyone to see: {公布|gōng bù}{成绩|chéng jì}. {采访|cǎi fǎng} is to interview, {收看|shōu kàn} to watch, {主持|zhǔ chí} to host.

questions.stem: Two neighbours are chatting about prices. Which word sounds most natural in: "___ {最|zuì}{关心|guān xīn}{的|de}{就是|jiù shì}{物价|wù jià}。" (What ordinary people care about most is prices.)?
questions.explanation: {老百姓|lǎo bǎi xìng} is the everyday, warm word for ordinary people. {人民|rén mín} (the people) is formal and collective, the word of speeches; {大众|dà zhòng} (the public) is written; {人物|rén wù} is a figure or a character in a story.

questions.stem: Listen. Which tones are the two syllables?
questions.explanation: {除夕|chú xī}, New Year's Eve: second tone + first tone. {夕|xī} xī is said like {西|xī} xī.

questions.stem: Listen. Which tones are the two syllables?
questions.explanation: {悠久|yōu jiǔ}, long-standing: first tone + third tone.

questions.stem: Listen. What does the speaker say many Chinese people think?

audio.text: 再忙也要回家过年，这是很多中国人的想法。

choices: New Year is too busy a time to go home.
You only go home for New Year if you are free.
