glossary.definition: The style of contracts, notices, news, reports and essays. Many of its words are short or classical forms with an everyday partner in speech: {曾|céng} / {曾经|céng jīng}, {与|yǔ} / {和|hé}, {出售|chū shòu} / {卖|mài}, {召开|zhào kāi} / {开|kāi}, {以及|yǐ jí} / {和|hé}, {须|xū} / {必须|bì xū}. Use them in writing and formal speech; in a chat they sound stiff.

An adverb that places an action in time, before the verb: {曾经|céng jīng} (once, at one time: past and usually over), {已经|yǐ jīng} (already: done and still so), {早已|zǎo yǐ} (long since, written for {早|zǎo}{就|jiù}), {即将|jí jiāng} (about to, written: lesson 24).

"Since", from a past starting point up to now: {自从|zì cóng}{去年|qù nián}{来|lái}{这儿|zhèr}{实习|shí xí}{以来|yǐ lái}，{她|tā}{写|xiě}{了|le}{三十|sān shí}{多|duō}{篇|piān}{文章|wén zhāng}。 {自从|zì cóng}…{以后|yǐ hòu} is the common spoken form; X {以来|yǐ lái} alone is written ({今年|jīn nián}{以来|yǐ lái}). Never with a future point: from now on is {从|cóng}…{起|qǐ} / {从|cóng}…{开始|kāi shǐ}.

Whole + {由|yóu} + parts + {组成|zǔ chéng}: "to be made up of". {我们|wǒ men}{部门|bù mén}{由|yóu}{五|wǔ}{个|gè}{人|rén}{组成|zǔ chéng}。 The whole is the subject; {由|yóu} introduces the members. {组成|zǔ chéng} can also take the whole as its object: {组成|zǔ chéng}{一|yí}{个|gè}{小组|xiǎo zǔ} (form a group).

An adverb that says how much, before an adjective or verb: {比较|bǐ jiào} (fairly), {相当|xiāng dāng} (quite), {很|hěn} / {非常|fēi cháng} / {十分|shí fēn} (very), {格外|gé wài} (more than usual), {极其|jí qí} (extremely, written, before two-syllable words), {过于|guò yú} (too, written).

"Once…, if ever…": a condition that may or may not happen, and the result that follows as soon as it does, often a serious one: {一旦|yí dàn}{出|chū}{了|le}{问题|wèn tí}，{我们|wǒ men}{就|jiù}{要|yào}{马上|mǎ shàng}{处理|chǔ lǐ}。 Common in rules and warnings. {一|yī}…{就|jiù} is for a real sequence (as soon as), {如果|rú guǒ}…{就|jiù} for a plain supposition.

A comparison that says by how much: the amount goes after the adjective, {这|zhè}{件|jiàn}{比|bǐ}{那|nà}{件|jiàn}{贵|guì}{两|liǎng}{百|bǎi}{块|kuài}. With a verb, {早|zǎo} / {晚|wǎn} / {多|duō} / {少|shǎo} go before it: {他|tā}{比|bǐ}{我|wǒ}{早|zǎo}{到|dào}{十|shí}{分钟|fēn zhōng}. With a few measurable adjectives, mainly {大|dà}, {小|xiǎo}, {高|gāo}, {矮|ǎi}, {早|zǎo}, {晚|wǎn} (in speech also {多|duō}, {长|cháng}, {重|zhòng}…), a short form drops {比|bǐ}: {他|tā}{大|dà}{我|wǒ}{三|sān}{岁|suì} (he is three years older than me); with {贵|guì}, {好|hǎo} and most others it is not standard.

A complex sentence whose first clause supposes something and whose second says what follows: {如果|rú guǒ}…{就|jiù}, {假如|jiǎ rú}…{就|jiù} (a little formal; often untrue: {假如|jiǎ rú}{我|wǒ}{是|shì}{你|nǐ}…), {万一|wàn yī}… (an unlikely, usually unwelcome possibility: {万一|wàn yī}{下雨|xià yǔ}{怎么办|zěn me bàn}？) and {要不是|yào bu shì}… (imagining a real fact away: {要不是|yào bu shì}{你|nǐ}{帮|bāng}{我|wǒ}，{我|wǒ}{早|zǎo}{就|jiù}{放弃|fàng qì}{了|le}).

A complex sentence that grants a condition and says the result holds anyway: {即使|jí shǐ}…{也|yě} (neutral), {哪怕|nǎ pà}…{也|yě} (spoken, emphatic: {哪怕|nǎ pà}{失败|shī bài}{了|le}，{我|wǒ}{也|yě}{不|bú}{后悔|hòu huǐ}), {尽管|jǐn guǎn}…{但是|dàn shì} (although). {也|yě} or {都|dōu} goes after the subject of the second clause.

A complement after {得|de} that describes the state an action or feeling leads to, often a whole verb phrase or clause: {我|wǒ}{累|lèi}{得|de}{不|bù}{想|xiǎng}{说话|shuō huà} (I'm so tired I don't want to talk), {他|tā}{说|shuō}{得|de}{大家|dà jiā}{都|dōu}{笑|xiào}{了|le} (he spoke so that everyone laughed), {她|tā}{高兴|gāo xìng}{得|de}{跳|tiào}{了|le}{起来|qǐ lái}. English often says "so… that…". Unlike the degree complement ({说|shuō}{得|de}{很|hěn}{好|hǎo}, a judgement of how it's done), the state complement tells what followed; the negative goes inside it ({累|lèi}{得|de}{不|bù}{想|xiǎng}{吃|chī}{饭|fàn}). Its strongest form is {得|de}{不得了|bù dé liǎo}. Taught in lesson 06.

An adverb that shows how the speaker sees what is said, not what happened: how sure they are, or how they feel about it. {似乎|sì hū} (it seems: a careful guess), {仿佛|fǎng fú} (as if), {好像|hǎo xiàng} (it seems; as if), {反正|fǎn zhèng} (anyway, whatever happens), and later {居然|jū rán}, {果然|guǒ rán}, {毕竟|bì jìng}, {根本|gēn běn}, {简直|jiǎn zhí} (lessons 12–14). It goes before the verb, or before the subject for emphasis: {反正|fǎn zhèng}{我|wǒ}{不|bú}{去|qù} / {我|wǒ}{反正|fǎn zhèng}{不|bú}{去|qù}. Taught from lesson 06.

The strongest degree: adjective (or a verb of feeling) + {得|de} + {不得了|bù dé liǎo}, "extremely, beyond words": {好吃|hǎo chī}{得|de}{不得了|bù dé liǎo} (unbelievably good), {高兴|gāo xìng}{得|de}{不得了|bù dé liǎo} (over the moon), {热|rè}{得|de}{不得了|bù dé liǎo} (terribly hot). Nothing goes between {得|de} and {不得了|bù dé liǎo} (not {高兴|gāo xìng}{得|de}{很|hěn}{不得了|bù dé liǎo}). On its own, {不得了|bù dé liǎo} is an exclamation that something terrible has happened: {不得了|bù dé liǎo}{了|le}！ Read bù dé liǎo. Taught in lesson 07.

A potential complement with {不得|bu de} (both syllables light) after a verb: the action mustn't be done, because the result would be harmful. {过期|guò qī}{的|de}{牛奶|niú nǎi}{喝不得|hē bu de} (you mustn't drink out-of-date milk), {这|zhè}{种|zhǒng}{蘑菇|mó gu}{吃不得|chī bu de} (this mushroom mustn't be eaten), {那个|nà ge}{地方|dì fang}{去不得|qù bu de}, {这|zhè}{件|jiàn}{事|shì}{急不得|jí bu de} (it can't be rushed). Compare {不|bù}{能|néng} (not allowed) and V{不了|bu liǎo} (unable: {吃不了|chī bu liǎo}{这么|zhè me}{多|duō}, can't eat this much). The positive V{得|de} ({吃得|chī de}) is rare, mostly in questions. Taught in lesson 07.

A direction complement used for a change of state rather than a movement: {起来|qǐ lái} (a state begins: {好|hǎo}{起来|qǐ lái}, {热|rè}{起来|qǐ lái}; also {看|kàn}{起来|qǐ lái}, {想|xiǎng}{起来|qǐ lái}), {下来|xià lái} (settling, keeping: {安静|ān jìng}{下来|xià lái}, {停|tíng}{下来|xià lái}, {记|jì}{下来|xià lái}), {下去|xià qù} (carrying on: {坚持|jiān chí}{下去|xià qù}, {说|shuō}{下去|xià qù}), {过来|guò lái} (back to normal: {醒|xǐng}{过来|guò lái}, {恢复|huī fù}{过来|guò lái}), {过去|guò qù} (out of the normal state: {晕|yūn}{过去|guò qù}), {出来|chū lái} (made or made out: {看|kàn}{出来|chū lái}, {想|xiǎng}{出来|chū lái}). The object of {起来|qǐ lái} goes in the middle: {下|xià}{起|qǐ}{雨|yǔ}{来|lái}. Taught in lesson 08; all of them are in the reference sheet on complements.

A {把|bǎ} sentence whose verb has a second object after it: the {把|bǎ} object is the thing handled, the second says who gets it, what it becomes, or what it counts as. {把|bǎ} A + verb + {给|gěi} B ({把|bǎ}{钥匙|yào shi}{交|jiāo}{给|gěi}{师傅|shī fu}, give the keys to the workman), {把|bǎ} A + verb + {成|chéng} B ({把|bǎ}{储藏室|chǔ cáng shì}{改|gǎi}{成|chéng}{书房|shū fáng}, turn the storeroom into a study), {把|bǎ} A + {当|dàng}({作|zuò}) / {当成|dàng chéng} B ({把|bǎ}{他|tā}{当|dàng}{朋友|péng you}, treat him as a friend). The {把|bǎ} object is definite; negatives and modal verbs go before {把|bǎ}. Taught in lesson 09, with {把|bǎ} + {一|yī} + verb ({他|tā}{把|bǎ}{门|mén}{一|yì}{关|guān}，{就|jiù}{走|zǒu}{了|le}).

aliases: passive with 叫 and 让
glossary.definition: The everyday passive: {叫|jiào} or {让|ràng} used like {被|bèi}, often with {给|gěi} before the verb. Thing affected + {叫|jiào} / {让|ràng} / {被|bèi} + doer + ({给|gěi}) + verb with a result or {了|le}: {我|wǒ}{的|de}{自行车|zì xíng chē}{叫|jiào}{人|rén}{给|gěi}{骑|qí}{走|zǒu}{了|le} (someone's gone off with my bike), {窗户|chuāng hu}{让|ràng}{风|fēng}{给|gěi}{吹|chuī}{开|kāi}{了|le}. Unlike {被|bèi}, {叫|jiào} and {让|ràng} need the doer ({人|rén} if you don't know who); {给|gěi} alone can also mark the passive ({杯子|bēi zi}{给|gěi}{打碎|dǎ suì}{了|le}). It is mostly for things that went wrong. The written passive is {为|wéi}…{所|suǒ} (lesson 27). Taught in lesson 12, with the reference sheet on {把|bǎ} and {被|bèi}.

A sentence whose second part says the opposite of what the first part leads you to expect, with {反而|fǎn ér} (on the contrary, instead) before the verb: {我|wǒ}{想|xiǎng}{帮|bāng}{他|tā}，{他|tā}{反而|fǎn ér}{生气|shēng qì}{了|le} (I wanted to help him, but he got angry instead), {吃|chī}{了|le}{药|yào}{以后|yǐ hòu}，{病|bìng}{反而|fǎn ér}{更|gèng}{重|zhòng}{了|le}. The full form is {不但不|bú dàn bù} / {不但没|bú dàn méi}…，{反而|fǎn ér}…: {雨|yǔ}{不但|bú dàn}{没|méi}{停|tíng}，{反而|fǎn ér}{越|yuè}{下|xià}{越|yuè}{大|dà}{了|le}. {反而|fǎn ér} goes after the subject, never at the very start. Previewed in lesson 11, taught in lesson 14.

aliases: X 也不是，Y 也不是
glossary.definition: Two choices side by side, each followed by {也不是|yě bú shì} ("isn't right either"), for being caught with no good way out: {我|wǒ}{说|shuō}{也不是|yě bú shì}，{不|bù}{说|shuō}{也不是|yě bú shì} (I couldn't say it and I couldn't keep quiet), {他|tā}{站|zhàn}{在|zài}{门口|mén kǒu}，{进|jìn}{也不是|yě bú shì}，{走|zǒu}{也不是|yě bú shì}. The two parts are usually opposites, and often just one verb each. It describes an awkward feeling more than a real choice. Taught in lesson 14.

Written with signs that are pictures of what they mean. A few Chinese characters began this way ({山|shān}, {水|shuǐ}, {人|rén}, {日|rì}, {月|yuè}), and Chinese calls them {象形|xiàng xíng}{字|zì}; most characters today combine a meaning part and a sound part instead. The Dongba script of the Naxi in Lijiang stays much closer to pictures: {东巴文|Dōng bā wén}{很|hěn}{像|xiàng}{图画|tú huà}. Honors lesson 15h2.

A {成语|chéng yǔ}: a fixed phrase, almost always of four characters, whose meaning goes beyond its parts and which often comes from an old story or text (its {出处|chū chù}). The form can't be changed ({画蛇添足|huà shé tiān zú}, never {画蛇|huà shé}{加|jiā}{足|zú}). In a sentence an idiom works like a predicate ({生活|shēng huó}{丰富多彩|fēng fù duō cǎi}), an attributive with {的|de} ({丰富多彩|fēng fù duō cǎi}{的|de}{活动|huó dòng}), a subject or object ({各行各业|gè háng gè yè}{都|dōu}{需要|xū yào}{人才|rén cái}) or a whole wish ({祝|zhù}{你|nǐ}{一路顺风|yí lù shùn fēng}！). Careful usage puts no {很|hěn} before an idiom, and each one praises, blames or simply describes.

A grammatical frame of four syllables that you fill with your own words, unlike an idiom, which is fixed. A{来|lái}A{去|qù} repeats a one-syllable verb ({想|xiǎng}{来|lái}{想|xiǎng}{去|qù}, after thinking it over and over; {走|zǒu}{来|lái}{走|zǒu}{去|qù}, walking up and down); {说|shuō}A{就|jiù}A is "do it the moment it's said" ({说|shuō}{走|zǒu}{就|jiù}{走|zǒu}); {没|méi}A{没|méi}B is "with no A or B" ({没|méi}{完|wán}{没|méi}{了|le}); A{着|zhe}A{着|zhe} is "while doing A" ({说|shuō}{着|zhe}{说|shuō}{着|zhe}{就|jiù}{哭|kū}{了|le}). A second clause usually says how things turned out: {我|wǒ}{想|xiǎng}{来|lái}{想|xiǎng}{去|qù}，{还是|hái shi}{决定|jué dìng}{不|bú}{去|qù}{了|le}。

A preposition that says what something rests on: what you show, rely on or judge by. {凭|píng} (on presentation of; by virtue of: {凭|píng}{票|piào}{入场|rù chǎng}, {凭|píng}{自己|zì jǐ}{的|de}{努力|nǔ lì}), {凭借|píng jiè} (written: {凭借|píng jiè}{先进|xiān jìn}{的|de}{技术|jì shù}), {依据|yī jù} (written: on the basis of; as a noun, grounds: {依据|yī jù}{规定|guī dìng}, {科学|kē xué}{依据|yī jù}), {根据|gēn jù} (everyday: {根据|gēn jù}{地图|dì tú}), and {据|jù} (according to: {据|jù}{调查|diào chá}, {据说|jù shuō}).

A frame at the start of a sentence giving the evidence or the angle of a judgment: {从|cóng} + noun phrase + {来|lái}{看|kàn} (also {从|cóng}…{看|kàn}, {从|cóng}…{上|shàng}{看|kàn}). {从|cóng}{这|zhè}{次|cì}{比赛|bǐ sài}{来|lái}{看|kàn}，{他|tā}{的|de}{实力|shí lì}{还|hái}{不够|bú gòu}{强|qiáng}。 (Judging from this match, he isn't strong enough yet.) {从|cóng}{时间|shí jiān}{上|shàng}{看|kàn}，{坐|zuò}{高铁|gāo tiě}{更|gèng}{方便|fāng biàn}。 For a person's own view, Chinese uses {在|zài} + person + {看来|kàn lái}: {在我看来|zài wǒ kàn lái}….

A syllable added after a word to make a new one. {头|tou} tou (neutral tone) makes nouns ({石头|shí tou}, {木头|mù tou}, {里头|lǐ tou}); {化|huà} makes words for a process, "becoming so" ({现代化|xiàn dài huà}, {智能化|zhì néng huà}, {简单化|jiǎn dān huà}); {族|zú} names a group of people by their way of life ({上班族|shàng bān zú}, {低头族|dī tóu zú}); {者|zhě} is "a person who" ({学者|xué zhě}, {读者|dú zhě}); {家|jiā} is an expert ({专家|zhuān jiā}, {科学|kē xué}{家|jiā}).

A conditional pattern that says the second thing depends entirely on the first: {没有|méi yǒu} + A，{就|jiù}{没有|méi yǒu} + B, "without A, there would be no B". {没有|méi yǒu}{大家|dà jiā}{的|de}{帮助|bāng zhù}，{就|jiù}{没有|méi yǒu}{今天|jīn tiān}{的|de}{成功|chéng gōng}。 (Without everyone's help, today's success wouldn't have happened.) {没有|méi yǒu}{安全|ān quán}，{就|jiù}{没有|méi yǒu}{一切|yí qiè}。 Both halves take {没有|méi yǒu}; with a subject in the second half, {就|jiù} follows it ({没有|méi yǒu}{你|nǐ}，{我|wǒ}{就|jiù}{没有|méi yǒu}{勇气|yǒng qì}). It is stronger than {如果|rú guǒ}{没有|méi yǒu}…{就|jiù}{不|bú}{会|huì}…, and is at home in speeches, slogans and thank-you notes.

Two uses of {不|bù} A {不|bù} B. With two verbs it is a condition, "unless A, not B": {不见不散|bú jiàn bú sàn} (we won't leave until we've met), {这|zhè}{件|jiàn}{事|shì}{你|nǐ}{不|bù}{说|shuō}{不行|bù xíng} (you have to say something). With two opposite adjectives it means "neither A nor B: just right": {不|bù}{冷|lěng}{不|bú}{热|rè} (neither cold nor hot), {不|bú}{大|dà}{不|bù}{小|xiǎo} (just the right size). {不|bù} is bú before a fourth tone ({不见不散|bú jiàn bú sàn} bú jiàn bú sàn) and bù before the others.

A concessive pattern: {再|zài} + adjective or verb, then (subject) {也|yě} + what still holds: "however…, still…". {再|zài}{忙|máng}{也|yě}{要|yào}{回家|huí jiā}{过年|guò nián} (however busy you are, you go home for New Year); {这|zhè}{件|jiàn}{衣服|yī fu}{再|zài}{贵|guì}{我|wǒ}{也|yě}{要|yào}{买|mǎi}; {你|nǐ}{再|zài}{说|shuō}{也|yě}{没有|méi yǒu}{用|yòng}. It pushes a degree to the limit and usually leads to a resolve ({要|yào}, {得|děi}, {不|bù} + verb). Compare {不管|bù guǎn}{多|duō}…{都|dōu} (nearly the same, longer) and {即使|jí shǐ}…{也|yě} ("even if", which supposes a fact).

A written way of giving a purpose after the action: action，{为|wèi}{的|de}{是|shì} + purpose ("…, the purpose being…", "so as to…"). {他|tā}{每天|měi tiān}{早上|zǎo shang}{五|wǔ}{点|diǎn}{起床|qǐ chuáng}，{为|wèi}{的|de}{是|shì}{赶|gǎn}{第|dì}{一|yī}{班|bān}{地铁|dì tiě}。 {春节|Chūn jié}{前|qián}{人|rén}{们|men}{打扫|dǎ sǎo}{房子|fáng zi}，{为|wèi}{的|de}{是|shì}{迎接|yíng jiē}{新|xīn}{的|de}{一|yì}{年|nián}。 {为|wèi} is wèi, as in {为了|wèi le}. To put the purpose first, use {为了|wèi le}: {为了|wèi le}{赶|gǎn}{第|dì}{一|yī}{班|bān}{地铁|dì tiě}，{他|tā}{每天|měi tiān}{五|wǔ}{点|diǎn}{起床|qǐ chuáng}. In speech, {是|shì}{为了|wèi le} at the end is more common.

A word or phrase that adds no facts but shows how one part of a text relates to another: it orders points ({首先|shǒu xiān}, {其次|qí cì}, {最后|zuì hòu}), adds one ({此外|cǐ wài}, {另外|lìng wài}), turns against what came before ({然而|rán ér}, {不过|bú guò}), or leads to a conclusion ({可见|kě jiàn}, {由此|yóu cǐ}{可见|kě jiàn}, {总之|zǒng zhī}). {可见|kě jiàn} follows a fact: {这|zhè}{道|dào}{题|tí}{只有|zhǐ yǒu}{两|liǎng}{个|gè}{人|rén}{做|zuò}{对|duì}{了|le}，{可见|kě jiàn}{很|hěn}{难|nán}。 {由此|yóu cǐ}{可见|kě jiàn} (written) starts a sentence after several facts. An argued text uses a few of them to guide the reader; one in every sentence is too many.

Linking words of the written register with spoken partners: {因而|yīn ér} (therefore; spoken {所以|suǒ yǐ}), {从而|cóng ér} (thereby: an action and the result it brings: {他|tā}{每|měi}{天|tiān}{坚持|jiān chí}{练习|liàn xí}，{从而|cóng ér}{提高|tí gāo}{了|le}{水平|shuǐ píng}), {便|biàn} (then; spoken {就|jiù}: {一|yī}…{便|biàn}…). {因而|yīn ér} looks back to a cause; {从而|cóng ér} forward from a means to its result. Use them in reports, notices and essays, not in conversation.

The formal passive {为|wéi} + doer + {所|suǒ} + verb, mostly in set phrases: {这个|zhè ge}{故事|gù shi}{为|wéi}{人|rén}{们|men}{所|suǒ}{熟悉|shú xī} (this story is familiar to people), {他|tā}{的|de}{观点|guān diǎn}{为|wéi}{大家|dà jiā}{所|suǒ}{接受|jiē shòu}. {为|wéi} is wéi here; the verb usually has two syllables and takes no {了|le}. In speech, {被|bèi}: {他|tā}{的|de}{观点|guān diǎn}{被|bèi}{大家|dà jiā}{接受|jiē shòu}{了|le}。

A text or a spoken answer that defends a view. At HSK 5 it has four parts: the phenomenon or question ({现象|xiàn xiàng}), the view ({观点|guān diǎn}: {我|wǒ}{认为|rèn wéi}…, {我|wǒ}{不|bù}{完全|wán quán}{赞成|zàn chéng}…), the grounds ({论据|lùn jù}: reasons and evidence, each with an example), and the conclusion ({结论|jié lùn}: {由此|yóu cǐ}{可见|kě jiàn}…, {总之|zǒng zhī}…, {问题|wèn tí}{不|bú}{在于|zài yú}…{而|ér}{在于|zài yú}…). The exam's essay and the speaking test's opinion questions both ask for it.

The position an argument defends: {观点|guān diǎn} (more formal than {看法|kàn fǎ}, HSK 4). State it early and clearly: {我|wǒ}{认为|rèn wéi}…, {我|wǒ}{赞成|zàn chéng}…, {我|wǒ}{并|bìng}{不|bú}{赞成|zàn chéng}{这|zhè}{种|zhǒng}{看法|kàn fǎ}. {我|wǒ}{同意|tóng yì}{你|nǐ}{的|de}{观点|guān diǎn} is "I agree with your view".

What supports a view: reasons ({理由|lǐ yóu}) and evidence ({证据|zhèng jù}): facts ({事实|shì shí}), figures and examples. Together they are the {论据|lùn jù} (lùn jù, the grounds of an argument). Good grounds are specific ({具体|jù tǐ}), objective ({客观|kè guān}) and strong ({有力|yǒu lì}{的|de}{证据|zhèng jù}); a few cases ({个别|gè bié}{现象|xiàn xiàng}) don't prove a general claim.

What an argument arrives at from its grounds ({结论|jié lùn}, lesson 16). Introduce it with {可见|kě jiàn} or {由此|yóu cǐ}{可见|kě jiàn} (written), {总之|zǒng zhī} or {所以|suǒ yǐ}; a balanced conclusion often takes {问题|wèn tí}{不|bú}{在于|zài yú}…，{而|ér}{在于|zài yú}… (the issue isn't…, it's…). It should follow from the facts given, and go no further than they do ({不|bù}{能|néng}{因此|yīn cǐ}{就|jiù}{说|shuō}…).

Words that habitually go together: {采取|cǎi qǔ}{措施|cuò shī} (take measures), {发挥|fā huī}{作用|zuò yòng} (play a role), {达成|dá chéng}{协议|xié yì} (reach an agreement), {满足|mǎn zú}{需求|xū qiú} (meet a need), {扩大|kuò dà}{规模|guī mó} (expand), {缩小|suō xiǎo}{差距|chā jù} (narrow a gap), {提高|tí gāo}{水平|shuǐ píng} (raise the level). The exam's gap passages often test them: the right word is the one that goes with its neighbour.

The Chinese Proficiency Test ({汉语|Hàn yǔ}{水平|shuǐ píng}{考试|kǎo shì}) of Chinese Testing International. The new version (HSK 3.0, syllabus of 2025, in force from July 2026) has nine levels. Level 5 covers 3,600 words and 1,527 characters (550 to write by hand). Its written part has 72 questions in 105 minutes (listening 35, reading 35, writing 2), scored out of 300 (official site); its speaking test, as reported from the sample papers, has five tasks in about 23 minutes. No pass mark had been published.

A reading task of the new HSK 5 (as reported): five paragraphs, A–E, to put in order. The order follows from the text: the first paragraph introduces its topic and points back to nothing; the last concludes ({总之|zǒng zhī}, {由此|yóu cǐ}{可见|kě jiàn}, {最后|zuì hòu}, {如今|rú jīn}); in between, {这|zhè} + noun and pronouns point back, {此外|cǐ wài} and {也|yě} add, {然而|rán ér} and {不过|bú guò} turn, and time words follow each other ({最初|zuì chū}, {后来|hòu lái}, {如今|rú jīn}).

The first writing task of the new HSK 5 (as reported): a story of at least 100 characters from four pictures. Give the person a name and a place, tell each picture in order with time words ({上|shàng}{车|chē}{以后|yǐ hòu}, {不|bù}{知道|zhī dào}{过|guò}{了|le}{多|duō}{久|jiǔ}), mark the turn ({没|méi}{想|xiǎng}{到|dào}, {这|zhè}{时|shí}) and end with how it turned out ({从|cóng}{那|nà}{以后|yǐ hòu}).

The speaking part of the new HSK 5, as reported: five tasks in about 23 minutes, including 10 minutes' preparation: retelling two passages you hear (about 1½ minutes each), a story from three numbered photos (2 minutes), and two questions on which you give your opinion (2½ minutes each). Reports differ on whether it is taken in the same session as the written exam.

references.title: 把 and 被 at HSK 5
references.body:
## {把|bǎ}: what the doer does to the object

The {把|bǎ} sentence puts a definite object before the verb: doer + {把|bǎ} + object + verb + what happens to
it. HSK 3 and 4 taught the basic forms ({把|bǎ} + object + verb + {了|le} / a result / {在|zài} + place / {一下|yí xià}). HSK 5
adds these.

| Pattern | Example | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| {把|bǎ} + object + verb + {给|gěi} + person | {我|wǒ}{把|bǎ}{钥匙|yào shi}{交|jiāo}{给|gěi}{房东|fáng dōng}{了|le}。 | I gave the keys to the landlord. |
| {把|bǎ} + object + verb + {在|zài} + place | {请|qǐng}{把|bǎ}{箱子|xiāng zi}{放|fàng}{在|zài}{门口|mén kǒu}。 | Please put the box by the door. |
| {把|bǎ} A + {当成|dàng chéng} / {当作|dàng zuò} / {当|dàng} + B | {她|tā}{把|bǎ}{我|wǒ}{当成|dàng chéng}{亲|qīn}{妹妹|mèi mei}。 | She treats me like her own sister. |
| {把|bǎ} A + {当作|dàng zuò} + B (use as) | {我们|wǒ men}{把|bǎ}{书房|shū fáng}{当作|dàng zuò}{卧室|wò shì}。 | We use the study as a bedroom. |
| {把|bǎ} A + verb + {成|chéng} + B (into, as) | {他|tā}{把|bǎ}"{爱|ài}"{写|xiě}{成|chéng}{了|le}"{受|shòu}"。 | He wrote {爱|ài} as {受|shòu} by mistake. |
| {把|bǎ} + object + {一|yī} + verb，(subject) {就|jiù}… | {他|tā}{把|bǎ}{门|mén}{一|yì}{关|guān}{就|jiù}{走|zǒu}{了|le}。 | He shut the door and was gone. |
| {把|bǎ} + object + {给|gěi} + verb + result (spoken) | {弟弟|dì di}{把|bǎ}{我|wǒ}{的|de}{电脑|diàn nǎo}{给|gěi}{弄|nòng}{坏|huài}{了|le}。 | My brother's gone and broken my computer. |

- **{把|bǎ} with two objects**: the {把|bǎ} object is the thing handled; the second is a person (after {给|gěi}) or
  what it becomes or is taken for (after {成|chéng}, {作|zuò}, {当成|dàng chéng}). The verb comes between them.
- **{把|bǎ} + {一|yī} + verb**: the action is quick and sudden, and the next clause says what followed at
  once, usually with {就|jiù}. {一|yī} is yì or yí by the tone after it ({一|yì}{关|guān} yì guān, {一|yí}{放|fàng} yí fàng).
- The verb never stands alone after {把|bǎ}: add {了|le}, a result, a place, {给|gěi} + person, {成|chéng} + B, or the next
  clause.
- {没|méi} and {别|bié} go before {把|bǎ}: {他|tā}{没|méi}{把|bǎ}{钥匙|yào shi}{交|jiāo}{给|gěi}{房东|fáng dōng}; {别|bié}{把|bǎ}{我|wǒ}{当|dàng}{孩子|hái zi}.

## {被|bèi}, {叫|jiào}, {让|ràng}, {给|gěi}: what happens to the receiver

| Pattern | Example | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| receiver + {被|bèi} + doer + verb + result | {我|wǒ}{的|de}{蛋糕|dàn gāo}{被|bèi}{弟弟|dì di}{吃|chī}{了|le}。 | My cake was eaten by my brother. |
| receiver + {被|bèi} + verb + result (no doer) | {我|wǒ}{的|de}{自行车|zì xíng chē}{被|bèi}{骑|qí}{走|zǒu}{了|le}。 | My bike's been taken. |
| receiver + {叫|jiào} / {让|ràng} + doer + verb + result | {窗户|chuāng hu}{让|ràng}{风|fēng}{吹|chuī}{开|kāi}{了|le}。 | The wind blew the window open. |
| receiver + {被|bèi} / {叫|jiào} / {让|ràng} + doer + {给|gěi} + verb + result | {我|wǒ}{的|de}{蛋糕|dàn gāo}{被|bèi}{弟弟|dì di}{给|gěi}{吃|chī}{了|le}！ | My cake got eaten by my brother! |
| receiver + {给|gěi} + verb + result (no doer) | {杯子|bēi zi}{给|gěi}{打|dǎ}{碎|suì}{了|le}。 | The glass got broken. |
| receiver + {被|bèi} + verb + {成|chéng} + B | "{令|lìng}"{字|zì}{常|cháng}{被|bèi}{写|xiě}{成|chéng}"{今|jīn}"。 | {令|lìng} is often miswritten as {今|jīn}. |

- **{叫|jiào} and {让|ràng} need the doer**: ~~{杯子|bēi zi}{叫|jiào}{打|dǎ}{碎|suì}{了|le}~~; say {杯子|bēi zi}{叫|jiào}{他|tā}{打|dǎ}{碎|suì}{了|le} or {杯子|bēi zi}{被|bèi}{打|dǎ}{碎|suì}{了|le}.
- **{给|gěi} before the verb** is spoken and lively, typical of unwelcome events. Leave it out in formal
  writing, which uses {被|bèi} (or {为|wéi}…{所|suǒ}, lesson 27).
- {没|méi}, {别|bié} and time words go before {被|bèi} / {叫|jiào} / {让|ràng}: {我|wǒ}{的|de}{伞|sǎn}{昨天|zuó tiān}{被|bèi}{风|fēng}{吹|chuī}{走|zǒu}{了|le}; {我|wǒ}{的|de}{自行车|zì xíng chē}{没|méi}{被|bèi}{骑|qí}{走|zǒu}.
- For everyday events with no sense of something happening to the subject, use an active sentence.

## The same event from both sides

| Doer first: {把|bǎ} | Receiver first: {被|bèi} / {叫|jiào} / {让|ràng} |
|---|---|
| {弟弟|dì di}{把|bǎ}{我|wǒ}{的|de}{蛋糕|dàn gāo}{给|gěi}{吃|chī}{了|le}。 | {我|wǒ}{的|de}{蛋糕|dàn gāo}{被|bèi}{弟弟|dì di}{给|gěi}{吃|chī}{了|le}。 |
| {风|fēng}{把|bǎ}{窗户|chuāng hu}{吹|chuī}{开|kāi}{了|le}。 | {窗户|chuāng hu}{让|ràng}{风|fēng}{吹|chuī}{开|kāi}{了|le}。 |
| {他|tā}{把|bǎ}{我|wǒ}{当成|dàng chéng}{了|le}{服务员|fú wù yuán}。 | {我|wǒ}{被|bèi}{他|tā}{当成|dàng chéng}{了|le}{服务员|fú wù yuán}。 |
| {大家|dà jiā}{把|bǎ}{她|tā}{称为|chēng wéi}"{李老师|Lǐ lǎo shī}"。 | {她|tā}{被|bèi}{大家|dà jiā}{称为|chēng wéi}"{李老师|Lǐ lǎo shī}"。 |

references.title: The 431 characters of HSK 5
references.body:
Every new character of this course in the order it is taught. With the 1,096 of the pinyin course and HSK 1–4 they make the 1,527 characters of the level. Pinyin gives the readings our words use ("and others" when the character has more readings in later levels). Radical is the one the stroke-order data (Make Me a Hanzi) gives, which is usually but not always the radical a dictionary files it under. Strokes follow mainland stroke order. ✎ marks the 150 characters HSK expects you to write by hand at level 5; the second table lists all 550 handwriting characters of levels 1–5.

The list shows the simplified forms the course teaches, so it stays in simplified characters when the script switch is on Traditional; the Traditional column gives the Taiwan form the switch shows ("same" when the two scripts write it alike, and the form each of our words uses when a character has two). Radicals and stroke counts are those of the simplified form.

references.title: Complements, levels 1–5 (看完, 走进去, 吃得完, 吃不得, 累得站不起来, 好起来)
references.body:
## Everything that can follow a verb

A complement comes after a verb (or an adjective) and adds what happened, where it went, whether it
can happen, how it was done, what state it led to, or how often and how long. HSK 1–3 taught the
basic kinds; HSK 4 added the strong degree complements; HSK 5 adds V{不得|bu de}, the state complement and
the extended senses of the direction complements.

| Kind | Pattern | Example | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| result | verb + result | {我|wǒ}{看|kàn}{完|wán}{了|le}。 | I've finished reading it. |
| direction, simple | verb + {来|lái} / {去|qù} | {他|tā}{进来|jìn lái}{了|le}。 | He came in. |
| direction, compound | verb + {上|shàng} / {下|xià} / {进|jìn} / {出|chū} / {回|huí} / {过|guò} / {起|qǐ} + {来|lái} / {去|qù} ({起|qǐ} only with {来|lái}) | {他|tā}{走|zǒu}{进去|jìn qù}{了|le}。 | He walked in (away from me). |
| direction, extended | verb or adjective + {起来|qǐ lái} / {下来|xià lái} / {下去|xià qù} / {过来|guò lái} / {过去|guò qù}, of a change of state | {天气|tiān qì}{热|rè}{起来|qǐ lái}{了|le}。 | It's getting warm. (lesson 08) |
| potential | verb + {得|de} / {不|bu} + result or direction | {我|wǒ}{吃不完|chī bu wán}。 | I can't finish it. |
| potential V{不得|bu de} | verb + {不得|bu de} | {过期|guò qī}{的|de}{牛奶|niú nǎi}{喝不得|hē bu de}。 | You mustn't drink out-of-date milk. (lesson 07) |
| degree | verb + {得|de} + description | {她|tā}{说|shuō}{得|de}{很|hěn}{好|hǎo}。 | She speaks well. |
| degree, strong | adjective + {极|jí}{了|le} / {得|de}{很|hěn} / {死|sǐ}{了|le} / {得|de}{厉害|lì hai} / {得|de}{不得了|bù dé liǎo} | {好吃|hǎo chī}{得|de}{不得了|bù dé liǎo}。 | Unbelievably good. (lesson 07) |
| state | verb or adjective + {得|de} + the state it leads to | {他|tā}{累|lèi}{得|de}{站不起来|zhàn bu qǐ lái}。 | He's so tired he can't stand up. (lesson 06) |
| quantity: times | verb + number + {次|cì} / {遍|biàn} / {下|xià} / {眼|yǎn} | {他|tā}{看|kàn}{了|le}{我|wǒ}{一|yì}{眼|yǎn}。 | He glanced at me. (lesson 06) |
| quantity: duration | verb + length of time | {我|wǒ}{等|děng}{了|le}{半|bàn}{个|gè}{小时|xiǎo shí}。 | I waited half an hour. |

## Result complements

| Result | Meaning | Examples |
|---|---|---|
| {完|wán} | finished | {吃|chī}{完|wán}, {看|kàn}{完|wán}, {写|xiě}{完|wán} |
| {懂|dǒng} | understood | {听|tīng}{懂|dǒng}, {看|kàn}{懂|dǒng} |
| {到|dào} | reached, got | {买|mǎi}{到|dào}, {找|zhǎo}{到|dào}, {收到|shōu dào} |
| {见|jiàn} | perceived | {看见|kàn jiàn}, {听见|tīng jiàn} |
| {好|hǎo} | done properly; ready | {做|zuò}{好|hǎo}, {准备|zhǔn bèi}{好|hǎo}, {弄|nòng}{好|hǎo} |
| {错|cuò} / {对|duì} | wrong / right | {写|xiě}{错|cuò}, {说|shuō}{对|duì} |
| {成|chéng} | into, as | {把|bǎ}{储藏室|chǔ cáng shì}{改|gǎi}{成|chéng}{书房|shū fáng} (lesson 09), {翻译|fān yì}{成|chéng}{中文|Zhōng wén} |
| {给|gěi} | to someone | {把|bǎ}{钥匙|yào shi}{交|jiāo}{给|gěi}{他|tā} (lesson 09) |
| {在|zài} / {到|dào} + place | placed at, moved to | {放|fàng}{在|zài}{桌子|zhuō zi}{上|shàng}, {移|yí}{到|dào}{阳台|yáng tái}{上|shàng} |
| {住|zhù} | firmly, fast | {记|jì}{住|zhù} (remember), {站|zhàn}{住|zhù} (stop) |
| {碎|suì} | to pieces | {摔|shuāi}{碎|suì}, {打|dǎ}{碎|suì} (lesson 09) |
| {干净|gān jìng} | clean | {洗|xǐ}{干净|gān jìng} |

The negative takes {没|méi}, with no {了|le}: {我|wǒ}{没|méi}{听|tīng}{懂|dǒng}。 With {把|bǎ}: {把|bǎ}{杯子|bēi zi}{摔|shuāi}{碎|suì}{了|le}。

## Direction complements and their extended senses

In the plain sense, {来|lái} is towards the speaker and {去|qù} away; a place goes before {来|lái} / {去|qù}, a thing before or
after it ({拿|ná}{出来|chū lái}{一|yì}{本|běn}{书|shū} / {拿|ná}{出|chū}{一|yì}{本|běn}{书|shū}{来|lái}). In the extended sense the same complements describe a change of
state (lesson 08):

| Complement | Plain sense | Extended sense | Examples |
|---|---|---|---|
| {起来|qǐ lái} | up | a state begins and grows; judging; recalling; putting together | {好|hǎo}{起来|qǐ lái}, {热|rè}{起来|qǐ lái}, {笑|xiào}{起来|qǐ lái}, {下|xià}{起|qǐ}{雨|yǔ}{来|lái}; {看|kàn}{起来|qǐ lái} (it looks…); {想|xiǎng}{起来|qǐ lái} (remember); {收|shōu}{起来|qǐ lái} (put away) |
| {下来|xià lái} | down (towards me) | settling, slowing, calming; keeping, fixing in place; from past to now | {安静|ān jìng}{下来|xià lái}, {停|tíng}{下来|xià lái}, {慢|màn}{下来|xià lái}; {记|jì}{下来|xià lái}, {留|liú}{下来|xià lái}, {拍|pāi}{下来|xià lái}; {坚持|jiān chí}{下来|xià lái} (kept it up, to this day) |
| {下去|xià qù} | down (away) | carrying on into the future | {坚持|jiān chí}{下去|xià qù}, {说|shuō}{下去|xià qù}, {住|zhù}{下去|xià qù} |
| {过来|guò lái} | over (towards me) | back to the normal state | {醒|xǐng}{过来|guò lái} (come round), {恢复|huī fù}{过来|guò lái}, {明白|míng bai}{过来|guò lái}, {改|gǎi}{过来|guò lái} (correct) |
| {过去|guò qù} | over (away) | out of the normal state | {晕|yūn}{过去|guò qù} (faint), {睡|shuì}{过去|guò qù} |
| {出来|chū lái} | out | becoming known or produced | {看|kàn}{出来|chū lái} (make out), {想|xiǎng}{出来|chū lái} (think up), {做|zuò}{出来|chū lái} |

- The object of {起来|qǐ lái} goes in the middle: {下|xià}{起|qǐ}{雨|yǔ}{来|lái}{了|le}, {唱|chàng}{起|qǐ}{歌|gē}{来|lái}.
- {下来|xià lái} looks back (from then to now: {坚持|jiān chí}{下来|xià lái}{了|le}), {下去|xià qù} looks forward (from now on: {坚持|jiān chí}{下去|xià qù}).
- {过来|guò lái} and {过去|guò qù} are a pair: back to normal ({醒|xǐng}{过来|guò lái}) and away from it ({晕|yūn}{过去|guò qù}).
- Extended complements combine with the potential: {停不下来|tíng bu xià lái} (can't stop), {站不起来|zhàn bu qǐ lái} (can't get up),
  {想不起来|xiǎng bu qǐ lái} (can't remember).

## Potential complements (HSK 3) and V{不得|bu de} (HSK 5)

| Can | Can't | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| {吃得完|chī de wán} | {吃不完|chī bu wán} | can / can't finish (eating) |
| {看得见|kàn de jiàn} | {看不见|kàn bu jiàn} | can / can't see |
| {听得懂|tīng de dǒng} | {听不懂|tīng bu dǒng} | can / can't understand |
| {买得到|mǎi de dào} | {买不到|mǎi bu dào} | can / can't get hold of |
| {放得下|fàng de xià} | {放不下|fàng bu xià} | fits / won't fit |
| {睡得着|shuì de zháo} | {睡不着|shuì bu zháo} | can / can't fall asleep |
| {受得了|shòu de liǎo} | {受不了|shòu bu liǎo} | can / can't stand it |

- {得|de} and {不|bu} in the middle are light.
- The object follows the verb or comes first: {这么|zhè me}{多|duō}{菜|cài}{我|wǒ}{吃不完|chī bu wán}。 Not in a {把|bǎ} sentence.

Three negatives of possibility (lesson 07):

| Form | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| {不|bù}{能|néng} + verb | not allowed; not possible | {这儿|zhèr}{不|bù}{能|néng}{抽|chōu}{烟|yān}。 |
| V{不了|bu liǎo} | unable to (a limit of amount or ability) | {我|wǒ}{吃不了|chī bu liǎo}{这么|zhè me}{多|duō}。 |
| V{不得|bu de} | mustn't, the result would be harmful | {这|zhè}{种|zhǒng}{蘑菇|mó gu}{吃不得|chī bu de}。 ({蘑菇|mó gu} mógu: mushroom) |

V{不得|bu de} belongs to a few verbs: {吃不得|chī bu de}, {喝不得|hē bu de}, {去不得|qù bu de}, {急不得|jí bu de} (can't be rushed),
{说不得|shuō bu de}, {动不得|dòng bu de}.

## Degree and state complements

| Kind | After {得|de} | Example | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| degree | a judgement of the action | {他|tā}{跑|pǎo}{得|de}{很|hěn}{快|kuài}。 {他|tā}{跑|pǎo}{得|de}{不|bú}{快|kuài}。 | the negative goes after {得|de} |
| degree, strong | {很|hěn}, {不得了|bù dé liǎo}, {厉害|lì hai}, {要命|yào mìng}; or {极|jí}{了|le} / {死|sǐ}{了|le} without {得|de} | {累|lèi}{得|de}{要命|yào mìng}, {热|rè}{死|sǐ}{了|le}, {好|hǎo}{极|jí}{了|le} | {不得了|bù dé liǎo} is the strongest |
| state | what the action or feeling led to: a verb phrase or a whole clause | {我|wǒ}{累|lèi}{得|de}{不|bù}{想|xiǎng}{说话|shuō huà}。 {他|tā}{说|shuō}{得|de}{大家|dà jiā}{都|dōu}{笑|xiào}{了|le}。 | often "so… that…" in English |

- With an object, repeat the verb or put the object first: {他|tā}{汉语|Hàn yǔ}{说|shuō}{得|de}{很|hěn}{好|hǎo} / {他|tā}{说|shuō}{汉语|Hàn yǔ}{说|shuō}{得|de}{很|hěn}{好|hǎo}。
- In a state complement the negative stays inside the state: {累|lèi}{得|de}{不|bù}{想|xiǎng}{吃|chī}{饭|fàn}.
- {得|de}{不得了|bù dé liǎo} never takes {很|hěn}: not ~~{高兴|gāo xìng}{得|de}{很|hěn}{不得了|bù dé liǎo}~~.

## Quantity complements

| Pattern | Example | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| verb + {过|guo} / {了|le} + number + {次|cì} / {遍|biàn} | {我|wǒ}{去|qù}{过|guo}{三|sān}{次|cì}{北京|Běi jīng}。 | I've been to Beijing three times. |
| verb + pronoun + number + {次|cì} / {眼|yǎn} | {我|wǒ}{见|jiàn}{过|guo}{他|tā}{一|yí}{次|cì}。 {他|tā}{看|kàn}{了|le}{我|wǒ}{一|yì}{眼|yǎn}。 | I've met him once. He glanced at me. |
| verb + {了|le} + length of time | {他|tā}{睡|shuì}{了|le}{八|bā}{个|gè}{小时|xiǎo shí}。 | He slept eight hours. |
| separable verb + length of time | {他|tā}{熬|áo}{了|le}{一|yí}{夜|yè}。 {他|tā}{睡|shuì}{了|le}{八|bā}{个|gè}{小时|xiǎo shí}{的|de}{觉|jiào}。 | He was up all night. He had eight hours' sleep. |

references.title: Complex sentences of HSK 5
references.body:
The connectors HSK 5 adds to those of HSK 3 and HSK 4 ({尽管|jǐn guǎn}…{但是|dàn shì}, {即使|jí shǐ}…{也|yě}, {不管|bù guǎn}…{都|dōu}, {既然|jì rán}…{就|jiù}, {不|bú}{是|shì}…{而|ér}{是|shì}, {不仅|bù jǐn}…{还|hái}…),
grouped by what the two clauses do. As before, a connector that is an adverb ({就|jiù}, {也|yě}, {便|biàn}, {反而|fǎn ér}) goes after the
subject of its clause, before the verb; a conjunction ({假如|jiǎ rú}, {哪怕|nǎ pà}, {一旦|yí dàn}, {万一|wàn yī}) goes at the start of its clause or
straight after the subject. "Register" says where each one belongs; the last column is the lesson that
teaches it.

## Time: since, once

| Pattern | Meaning | Register | Example | Lesson |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| {自从|zì cóng} X ({以来|yǐ lái} / {以后|yǐ hòu})… | since X (past only) | {以后|yǐ hòu}: any; {以来|yǐ lái}: a little formal | {自从|zì cóng}{毕业|bì yè}{以来|yǐ lái}，{他|tā}{一直|yì zhí}{在|zài}{新闻|xīn wén}{行业|háng yè}{工作|gōng zuò}。 | 01 |
| X {以来|yǐ lái}… | since X, up to now | written | {今年|jīn nián}{以来|yǐ lái}，{就业|jiù yè}{的|de}{人|rén}{越|yuè}{来|lái}{越|yuè}{多|duō}。 | 01 |
| {一旦|yí dàn} X，{就|jiù} Y | once X happens, Y | neutral, rules and warnings | {一旦|yí dàn}{出|chū}{了|le}{问题|wèn tí}，{我们|wǒ men}{就|jiù}{要|yào}{马上|mǎ shàng}{处理|chǔ lǐ}。 | 03, 08 |
| X，{便|biàn} Y | X, and then at once Y | written (spoken {就|jiù}) | {他|tā}{一|yí}{下班|xià bān}{便|biàn}{回|huí}{家|jiā}{了|le}。 | 27 |

## Conditions and suppositions

| Pattern | Meaning | Register | Example | Lesson |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| {假如|jiǎ rú} X，({就|jiù}) Y | if, supposing X | a little formal | {假如|jiǎ rú}{我|wǒ}{是|shì}{你|nǐ}，{我|wǒ}{就|jiù}{不|bú}{会|huì}{辞职|cí zhí}。 | 05 |
| {万一|wàn yī} X，({怎么办|zěn me bàn} / {就|jiù}) Y | in case, if by any chance X (usually unwelcome) | neutral | {万一|wàn yī}{下雨|xià yǔ}{怎么办|zěn me bàn}？ | 05 |
| {要不是|yào bu shì} X，({早|zǎo}{就|jiù} / {就|jiù}) Y | if it weren't for X (X is true) | spoken and written | {要不是|yào bu shì}{你|nǐ}{帮|bāng}{我|wǒ}，{我|wǒ}{早|zǎo}{就|jiù}{放弃|fàng qì}{了|le}。 | 05 |
| X，{不然|bù rán} / {要不|yào bù} / {要不然|yào bù rán} Y | X, otherwise Y | {不然|bù rán} neutral; {要不|yào bù} / {要不然|yào bù rán} spoken | {快|kuài}{走|zǒu}{吧|ba}，{不然|bù rán}{要|yào}{迟到|chí dào}{了|le}。 | 05 |
| {没有|méi yǒu} X，{就|jiù}{没有|méi yǒu} Y | without X there would be no Y | neutral, often in speeches | {没有|méi yǒu}{大家|dà jiā}{的|de}{努力|nǔ lì}，{就|jiù}{没有|méi yǒu}{今天|jīn tiān}{的|de}{成功|chéng gōng}。 | 23 |
| {不|bù} X {不|bù} Y | no Y unless X | fixed phrases | {不见|bú jiàn}{不|bù}{散|sǎn} (be there, whatever happens) | 23 |

## Concession: even if, however

| Pattern | Meaning | Register | Example | Lesson |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| {哪怕|nǎ pà} X，{也|yě} Y | even if X, still Y | spoken, emphatic ({即使|jí shǐ}…{也|yě}: neutral) | {哪怕|nǎ pà}{失败|shī bài}{了|le}，{我|wǒ}{也|yě}{不|bú}{后悔|hòu huǐ}。 | 05 |
| {再|zài} X {也|yě} Y | however X, still Y | neutral | {再|zài}{忙|máng}{也|yě}{要|yào}{回|huí}{家|jiā}{过年|guò nián}。 | 25 |

## Contrast and going further

| Pattern | Meaning | Register | Example | Lesson |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| {不但|bú dàn}{不|bù} / {没|méi} X，{反而|fǎn ér} Y | not only not X, but on the contrary Y | neutral | {他|tā}{不但|bú dàn}{没|méi}{生气|shēng qì}，{反而|fǎn ér}{笑|xiào}{了|le}。 | 11, 14 |

## Result, conclusion and purpose

| Pattern | Meaning | Register | Example | Lesson |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X，{可见|kě jiàn} Y | X, so it's clear that Y | formal to neutral | {天天|tiān tiān}{排队|pái duì}，{可见|kě jiàn}{东西|dōng xi}{很|hěn}{受|shòu}{欢迎|huān yíng}。 | 04, 26 |
| X，{由此|yóu cǐ}{可见|kě jiàn} Y | from this it can be seen that Y | written | {由此|yóu cǐ}{可见|kě jiàn}，{沟通|gōu tōng}{十分|shí fēn}{重要|zhòng yào}。 | 26 |
| X，{因而|yīn ér} Y | X, and so Y | written (spoken {所以|suǒ yǐ}) | {成本|chéng běn}{降低|jiàng dī}{了|le}，{因而|yīn ér}{价格|jià gé}{也|yě}{降低|jiàng dī}{了|le}。 | 27 |
| X，{从而|cóng ér} Y | X, thereby Y | written | {公司|gōng sī}{改进|gǎi jìn}{了|le}{方法|fāng fǎ}，{从而|cóng ér}{提高|tí gāo}{了|le}{效率|xiào lǜ}。 | 27 |
| X，{为|wèi}{的|de}{是|shì} Y | X; the purpose is Y | neutral | {他|tā}{每|měi}{天|tiān}{加班|jiā bān}，{为|wèi}{的|de}{是|shì}{早点儿|zǎo diǎnr}{完成|wán chéng}{项目|xiàng mù}。 | 25 |

## Choice

| Pattern | Meaning | Register | Example | Lesson |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| {或是|huò shì} X，{或是|huò shì} Y | either X or Y | written (spoken {或者|huò zhě}) | {或是|huò shì}{坐|zuò}{车|chē}，{或是|huò shì}{走路|zǒu lù}，{都|dōu}{可以|kě yǐ}。 | 27 |

The words that make these patterns also work on their own: {说不定|shuō bu dìng} (maybe), {没法儿|méi fǎr} (no way to), {可见|kě jiàn} at the start
of a sentence, {要不|yào bù} as "how about…?" ({要不|yào bù}{我们|wǒ men}{明天|míng tiān}{再|zài}{去|qù}?).

references.title: Fixed formats of HSK 5
references.body:
A fixed format is a frame with slots: some words are given, and you fill the others. HSK 4's formats
were {在|zài}…{方面|fāng miàn}, {拿|ná}…{来|lái}{说|shuō}, {够|gòu}…{的|de} and their friends (the HSK 4 sheet `fixed-formats-4.md`). These are the
level-5 ones. "Lesson" says where the course teaches a format; "reference" means it's listed here
for recognition (you'll meet it in reading and listening). The examples are our own. The four-character
patterns (A{来|lái}A{去|qù}, {说|shuō}A{就|jiù}A, {没|méi}A{没|méi}B, A{着|zhe}A{着|zhe}) are on the idioms sheet.

## Conditions, concession and purpose

| Format | Meaning | Example | Register | Lesson |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| {没有|méi yǒu} A，{就|jiù}{没有|méi yǒu} B | without A, there would be no B | {没有|méi yǒu}{大家|dà jiā}{的|de}{帮助|bāng zhù}，{就|jiù}{没有|méi yǒu}{今天|jīn tiān}{的|de}{成功|chéng gōng}。 Without everyone's help, today's success wouldn't have happened. | speeches, writing, careful speech | 23 |
| {不|bù} A {不|bù} B (two verbs) | unless A, not B | {明天|míng tiān}{九|jiǔ}{点|diǎn}，{不见不散|bú jiàn bú sàn}！ Nine tomorrow: we won't leave till we've met! | neutral | 23 |
| {不|bù} A {不|bù} B (opposite adjectives) | neither A nor B: just right | {这|zhè}{双|shuāng}{鞋|xié}{不|bú}{大|dà}{不|bù}{小|xiǎo}，{正|zhèng}{合适|hé shì}。 These shoes fit perfectly: neither too big nor too small. | neutral | 23 |
| {再|zài} A {也|yě} B | however A, still B | {再|zài}{忙|máng}{也|yě}{要|yào}{回家|huí jiā}{过年|guò nián}。 However busy you are, you go home for New Year. | neutral | 25 |
| {哪怕|nǎ pà} A {也|yě} B | even if A, still B | {哪怕|nǎ pà}{只有|zhǐ yǒu}{一|yí}{个|gè}{人|rén}{来|lái}，{我们|wǒ men}{也|yě}{要|yào}{上课|shàng kè}。 Even if only one person comes, we'll hold the class. | neutral | 05 |
| action，{为|wèi}{的|de}{是|shì} + purpose | …, the purpose being… | {他|tā}{每天|měi tiān}{五|wǔ}{点|diǎn}{起床|qǐ chuáng}，{为|wèi}{的|de}{是|shì}{赶|gǎn}{第|dì}{一|yī}{班|bān}{地铁|dì tiě}。 He gets up at five every day so as to catch the first metro. | written, explanatory | 25 |
| {一旦|yí dàn} A，{就|jiù} B | once A (happens), B | {一旦|yí dàn}{发生|fā shēng}{火灾|huǒ zāi}，{请|qǐng}{马上|mǎ shàng}{离开|lí kāi}{大楼|dà lóu}。 In case of fire, leave the building at once. | notices, neutral | 03, 08, 23 |

## Time, structure and viewpoint

| Format | Meaning | Example | Register | Lesson |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ({自从|zì cóng} / {自|zì}) A {以来|yǐ lái} | since A, ever since | {自|zì}{开业|kāi yè}{以来|yǐ lái}，{这|zhè}{家|jiā}{店|diàn}{一直|yì zhí}{很|hěn}{受|shòu}{欢迎|huān yíng}。 Since it opened, the shop has always been popular. | {自|zì}…{以来|yǐ lái} written; {自从|zì cóng}…{以来|yǐ lái} neutral | 01 |
| {由|yóu} A {组成|zǔ chéng} | to consist of A | {这个|zhè ge}{团队|tuán duì}{由|yóu}{五|wǔ}{名|míng}{成员|chéng yuán}{组成|zǔ chéng}。 The team is made up of five members. | written, formal | 02 |
| {从|cóng} A {来|lái}{看|kàn} | judging from A | {从|cóng}{这|zhè}{次|cì}{考试|kǎo shì}{的|de}{成绩|chéng jì}{来|lái}{看|kàn}，{他|tā}{进步|jìn bù}{很|hěn}{大|dà}。 Judging from this exam, he's made great progress. | neutral, a little formal | 16 |
| {不管怎样说|bù guǎn zěn yàng shuō} | whatever one says, anyway | {不管怎样说|bù guǎn zěn yàng shuō}，{他|tā}{是|shì}{你|nǐ}{哥哥|gē ge}，{你|nǐ}{应该|yīng gāi}{帮|bāng}{他|tā}。 Whatever you say, he's your brother: you should help him. | spoken | reference |

## Spoken formats: attitude and emphasis

| Format | Meaning | Example | Note | Lesson |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X {也|yě}{不|bú}{是|shì}，Y {也|yě}{不|bú}{是|shì} | can't decide between X and Y; either is wrong | {他|tā}{站|zhàn}{在|zài}{门口|mén kǒu}，{进|jìn}{也|yě}{不|bú}{是|shì}，{走|zǒu}{也|yě}{不|bú}{是|shì}。 He stood in the doorway, unable to go in or leave. | X and Y are often opposites | 14 |
| X {也|yě} X {不|bu}{得|de}，Y {也|yě} Y {不|bu}{得|de} | can neither X nor Y | {这|zhè}{孩子|hái zi}{打|dǎ}{也|yě}{打|dǎ}{不|bu}{得|de}，{骂|mà}{也|yě}{骂|mà}{不|bu}{得|de}，{真|zhēn}{让|ràng}{人|rén}{头疼|tóu téng}。 You can't smack this child or scold him: what a headache. | V{不|bu}{得|de} (lesson 07): mustn't, can't | reference |
| A {的|de} A，B {的|de} B | some A, others B | {晚会|wǎn huì}{上|shàng}，{大家|dà jiā}{唱|chàng}{的|de}{唱|chàng}，{跳|tiào}{的|de}{跳|tiào}，{热闹|rè nao}{极|jí}{了|le}。 At the party some sang, others danced: it was great fun. | describes a lively scene | reference |
| X {着|zhe}{也|yě}{是|shì} X {着|zhe} | might as well, since you're X-ing anyway | {闲着|xián zhe}{也|yě}{是|shì}{闲着|xián zhe}，{我们|wǒ men}{去|qù}{看|kàn}{电影|diàn yǐng}{吧|ba}。 We've nothing to do anyway, so let's go to a film. | {闲|xián}, {等|děng}, {坐|zuò}, {空|kòng} are usual X | reference |
| {不|bù} X {白|bái}{不|bù} X | it'd be a waste not to X | {这|zhè}{是|shì}{免费|miǎn fèi}{的|de}，{不|bù}{吃|chī}{白|bái}{不|bù}{吃|chī}。 It's free: it'd be a waste not to eat it. | {白|bái} (lesson 27): for nothing | reference |
| X {来|lái} X {去|qù}，{都|dōu}{是|shì}… | however you X it, it comes down to… | {说来说去|shuō lái shuō qù}，{都|dōu}{是|shì}{钱|qián}{的|de}{问题|wèn tí}。 When all's said and done, it's about money. | X{来|lái}X{去|qù} is a four-character pattern (lesson 16) | 16 |
| X {什么|shén me} X | there's no need to X (impatient) | {急什么急|jí shén me jí}，{还|hái}{有|yǒu}{半|bàn}{个|gè}{小时|xiǎo shí}{呢|ne}！ What's the rush? There's still half an hour! | rude to a stranger; fine with family and friends | reference |
| {什么|shén me} X {不|bù} X {的|de} | never mind X | {什么|shén me}{钱|qián}{不|bu}{钱|qián}{的|de}，{朋友|péng you}{之间|zhī jiān}{别|bié}{说|shuō}{这个|zhè ge}。 Never mind the money: don't talk about that between friends. | waves something aside | reference |
| {真有你的|zhēn yǒu nǐ de} | you're really something | {一|yí}{个|gè}{人|rén}{做|zuò}{完|wán}{了|le}{三|sān}{个|gè}{人|rén}{的|de}{工作|gōng zuò}，{真有你的|zhēn yǒu nǐ de}！ You did three people's work on your own: you're amazing! | admiring, or ironic | reference |
| {成|chéng}{也|yě} X，{败|bài}{也|yě} X | X brought both the success and the failure | {他|tā}{成|chéng}{也|yě}{大胆|dà dǎn}，{败|bài}{也|yě}{大胆|dà dǎn}：{生意|shēng yi}{是|shì}{靠|kào}{大胆|dà dǎn}{做|zuò}{起来|qǐ lái}{的|de}，{最后|zuì hòu}{也|yě}{是|shì}{因为|yīn wèi}{太|tài}{大胆|dà dǎn}{亏|kuī}{了|le}{钱|qián}。 Boldness made him and broke him: he built the business on it, and in the end lost money by being too bold. | from the saying {成|chéng}{也|yě}{萧何|Xiāo Hé}，{败|bài}{也|yě}{萧何|Xiāo Hé} (Xiao He, a Han-dynasty minister, was behind both a general's rise and his fall); a little literary | reference |
| V {什么|shén me}{就|jiù} V {什么|shén me} | V whatever (there is, you like) | {家|jiā}{里|lǐ}{有|yǒu}{什么|shén me}{就|jiù}{吃|chī}{什么|shén me}{吧|ba}。 Let's just eat whatever there is at home. | a question word used twice (HSK 3) | reference |

## Notes

- {不|bù} changes tone in these formats as everywhere: {不见不散|bú jiàn bú sàn} bú jiàn bú sàn, {不|bú}{大|dà}{不|bù}{小|xiǎo} bú dà bù xiǎo, {不|bù}{吃|chī}{白|bái}{不|bù}{吃|chī}
  bù chī bái bù chī.
- The spoken formats carry attitude. {急什么急|jí shén me jí} and {什么|shén me}{钱|qián}{不|bu}{钱|qián}{的|de} sound abrupt or warm depending on who you're
  talking to; in a formal email, say {不用|bú yòng}{着急|zháo jí} or {钱|qián}{的|de}{事|shì}{您|nín}{不用|bú yòng}{担心|dān xīn}.
- {为|wèi}{的|de}{是|shì} and {由|yóu}…{组成|zǔ chéng} belong to writing. In a chat, say {是|shì}{为了|wèi le} and {有|yǒu}: {我们|wǒ men}{队|duì}{有|yǒu}{五|wǔ}{个|gè}{人|rén}.

references.title: Idioms, set phrases and four-character patterns of HSK 5
references.body:
The {成语|chéng yǔ} (idioms) and set phrases of this level, the four-character patterns that work like grammar,
and the three fable idioms of lesson 20h1. "Use" says how each one behaves in a sentence; "Tone"
says whether it praises, blames or just describes. Lesson 20h2 explains how idioms are built.

## The level's idioms

| Idiom | Literally | Meaning | Use | Tone | Lesson |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| {各行各业|gè háng gè yè} | every trade, every profession | all lines of work | subject or object: {各行各业|gè háng gè yè}{都|dōu}{需要|xū yào}{人才|rén cái}。 | neutral | 01 |
| {五颜六色|wǔ yán liù sè} | five colours, six colours | of every colour | attributive with {的|de}: {五颜六色|wǔ yán liù sè}{的|de}{花|huā}; predicate: {花园|huā yuán}{里|lǐ}{五颜六色|wǔ yán liù sè}{的|de} | describes, often admiring | 10 |
| {亲朋好友|qīn péng hǎo yǒu} | relatives, friends, good friends | friends and relatives | object: {请|qǐng}{了|le}{很|hěn}{多|duō}{亲朋好友|qīn péng hǎo yǒu} | neutral | 15 |
| {丰富多彩|fēng fù duō cǎi} | rich and many-coloured | rich and varied | attributive: {丰富多彩|fēng fù duō cǎi}{的|de}{活动|huó dòng}; predicate: {生活|shēng huó}{丰富多彩|fēng fù duō cǎi} | praises | 25 |
| {酸甜苦辣|suān tián kǔ là} | sour, sweet, bitter, hot | all life's experiences | subject or object: {酸甜苦辣|suān tián kǔ là}{都|dōu}{尝|cháng}{过|guo}{了|le} | neutral | 25 |
| {一路顺风|yí lù shùn fēng} | a following wind all the way | have a good journey | a wish: {祝|zhù}{你|nǐ}{一路顺风|yí lù shùn fēng}！ | a wish | 29 |

Careful usage puts no {很|hěn} before them: ×{很|hěn}{五颜六色|wǔ yán liù sè}. {很|hěn}{丰富多彩|fēng fù duō cǎi} is heard in speech, but teachers correct it
(lesson 25): say {丰富多彩|fēng fù duō cǎi} alone, or {很|hěn}{丰富|fēng fù} without the idiom.

## Set phrases

| Phrase | Meaning | Example | Lesson |
|---|---|---|---|
| {不得了|bù dé liǎo} | extremely (after {得|de}); terrible! | {好吃|hǎo chī}{得|de}{不得了|bù dé liǎo} (incredibly tasty); {不得了|bù dé liǎo}{了|le}！ (oh no!) | 07 |
| {说不定|shuō bu dìng} | perhaps, maybe | {说不定|shuō bu dìng}{他|tā}{已经|yǐ jīng}{走|zǒu}{了|le}。 (Maybe he's already gone.) | 05 |
| {没法儿|méi fǎr} | no way to, can't (spoken) | {这么|zhè me}{多|duō}{作业|zuò yè}，{我|wǒ}{没法儿|méi fǎr}{做|zuò}{完|wán}。 | 05 |
| {用不着|yòng bu zháo} | not needed, no need to | {用不着|yòng bu zháo}{带|dài}{伞|sǎn}。 (No need to take an umbrella.) | (set phrase of the level) |

## Four-character patterns

These are grammar: you fill them with suitable words.

| Pattern | Meaning | Examples | Lesson |
|---|---|---|---|
| A{来|lái}A{去|qù} | do again and again, back and forth | {想|xiǎng}{来|lái}{想|xiǎng}{去|qù}, {找|zhǎo}{来|lái}{找|zhǎo}{去|qù}, {走|zǒu}{来|lái}{走|zǒu}{去|qù}; {说|shuō}{来|lái}{说|shuō}{去|qù} (all said and done) | 16 |
| {说|shuō}A{就|jiù}A | do it the moment it's said | {说|shuō}{走|zǒu}{就|jiù}{走|zǒu}, {说|shuō}{做|zuò}{就|jiù}{做|zuò} | 10 |
| {没|méi}A{没|méi}B | with no A or B; endlessly | {没|méi}{完|wán}{没|méi}{了|le} (endless) | 10 |
| A{着|zhe}A{着|zhe} | while doing A (something else happens) | {说|shuō}{着|zhe}{说|shuō}{着|zhe}{就|jiù}{哭|kū}{了|le} (while talking she began to cry) | 13 |

## Fable idioms (lesson 20h1)

| Idiom | Literally | Meaning | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| {守株待兔|shǒu zhū dài tù} | keep watch by the stump, wait for a hare | wait for luck instead of making an effort | 《{韩非子|Hán Fēi zǐ}》 |
| {刻舟求剑|kè zhōu qiú jiàn} | carve the boat, look for the sword | not see that things have changed | 《{吕氏春秋|Lǚ shì Chūn qiū}》 |
| {画蛇添足|huà shé tiān zú} | draw a snake, add feet | spoil something by adding what isn't needed | 《{战国策|Zhàn guó cè}》 |

All three are critical: use them of a mistake ({这|zhè}{是|shì}…, {这|zhè}{不|bú}{是|shì}…{吗|ma}?, {就是|jiù shì}…{了|le}).

## Talking about idioms

| Word | Use |
|---|---|
| {出自|chū zì} | {这个|zhè ge}{成语|chéng yǔ}{出自|chū zì}{一|yí}{个|gè}{古代|gǔ dài}{的|de}{故事|gù shi}。 (comes from) |
| {比喻|bǐ yù} | {画蛇添足|huà shé tiān zú}{比喻|bǐ yù}{做|zuò}{了|le}{多余|duō yú}{的|de}{事|shì}。 (is a figure for) |
| {形容|xíng róng} | {五颜六色|wǔ yán liù sè}{形容|xíng róng}{颜色|yán sè}{很|hěn}{多|duō}。 (describes) |
| {意味着|yì wèi zhe} | {学|xué}{会|huì}{用|yòng}{成语|chéng yǔ}，{意味着|yì wèi zhe}{你|nǐ}{的|de}{汉语|Hàn yǔ}{更|gèng}{地道|dì dao}{了|le}。 (means) |

references.title: Spoken and written Chinese (HSK 5)
references.body:
HSK 4's sheet set the first written words ({此|cǐ}, {与|yǔ}, {由|yóu}, {将|jiāng}, {已|yǐ}, {仅|jǐn}, {是否|shì fǒu}…) beside their spoken partners. HSK 5
adds many more: the words of contracts, notices, news, reports and essays. Each written word below
stands beside the everyday word that does the same job. Use the written word in writing and formal
speech (a speech, a report, the news); in a chat it sounds stiff. The last column is the lesson that
teaches it (27 brings most of them together).

## Time

| Written | Spoken | Meaning | Example | Lesson |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| {曾|céng} / {曾经|céng jīng} | {以前|yǐ qián}…{过|guo} | once, at one time | {本人|běn rén}{曾|céng}{在|zài}{网站|wǎng zhàn}{实习|shí xí}。 I once worked as an intern at a website. | 01 |
| X {以来|yǐ lái} / {自从|zì cóng} X {以来|yǐ lái} | {从|cóng} X {到|dào}{现在|xiàn zài} | since | {今年|jīn nián}{以来|yǐ lái}，{就业|jiù yè}{的|de}{人|rén}{越|yuè}{来|lái}{越|yuè}{多|duō}。 Since the start of the year, more people have found work. | 01 |
| {早已|zǎo yǐ} | {早|zǎo}{就|jiù} | long since | {这|zhè}{件|jiàn}{事|shì}{他|tā}{早已|zǎo yǐ}{忘|wàng}{了|le}。 He forgot about it long ago. | 27 |
| {事先|shì xiān} | {先|xiān} / {提前|tí qián} | in advance | {请|qǐng}{事先|shì xiān}{通知|tōng zhī}{大家|dà jiā}。 Please let everyone know in advance. | 02 |
| {首次|shǒu cì} | {第|dì}{一|yī}{次|cì} | for the first time | {公司|gōng sī}{首次|shǒu cì}{在|zài}{上海|Shàng hǎi}{设立|shè lì}{办公室|bàn gōng shì}。 The company has set up an office in Shanghai for the first time. | 27 |
| {随后|suí hòu} | {然后|rán hòu} | then, afterwards | {会议|huì yì}{九|jiǔ}{点|diǎn}{开始|kāi shǐ}，{随后|suí hòu}{参观|cān guān}{工厂|gōng chǎng}。 The meeting starts at nine, followed by a visit to the factory. | 27 |
| {此时|cǐ shí} / {此后|cǐ hòu} / {此前|cǐ qián} | {这|zhè}{时候|shí hou} / {以后|yǐ hòu} / {以前|yǐ qián} | at this time / after this / before this | {此后|cǐ hòu}，{他|tā}{再|zài}{也|yě}{没|méi}{回来|huí lái}{过|guo}。 After that he never came back. | 27 |
| {今日|jīn rì} / {近日|jìn rì} / {近期|jìn qī} | {今天|jīn tiān} / {这|zhè}{几|jǐ}{天|tiān} / {最近|zuì jìn} | today / recently / in the near term | {本|běn}{店|diàn}{今日|jīn rì}{休息|xiū xi}。 The shop is closed today. | 27 |
| {期间|qī jiān} | {的|de}{时候|shí hou} | during | {培训|péi xùn}{期间|qī jiān}{工资|gōng zī}{照|zhào}{发|fā}。 Pay continues as usual during training. | 27 |

## This, some, each

| Written | Spoken | Meaning | Example | Lesson |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| {本|běn} + noun | {这|zhè} / {我们|wǒ men} | this, our | {本|běn}{公司|gōng sī}{由|yóu}{五|wǔ}{个|gè}{部门|bù mén}{组成|zǔ chéng}。 Our company is made up of five departments. | 02 |
| {某|mǒu} | {有|yǒu}{个|gè} / {一|yí}{个|gè} | a certain, some | {某|mǒu}{公司|gōng sī} a certain company | 27 |
| {其|qí} | {他|tā}{的|de} / {她|tā}{的|de} / {它|tā}{的|de} | his, her, its, their | {公司|gōng sī}{及|jí}{其|qí}{员工|yuán gōng} the company and its employees | 27 |
| {其余|qí yú} | {别的|bié de} / {剩|shèng}{下|xià}{的|de} | the rest | {其余|qí yú}{的|de}{人|rén}{明天|míng tiān}{来|lái}。 The rest come tomorrow. | 27 |
| {如此|rú cǐ} | {这样|zhè yàng} / {这么|zhè me} | so, like this | {情况|qíng kuàng}{如此|rú cǐ}{复杂|fù zá}。 The situation is so complicated. | 27 |
| {如何|rú hé} | {怎么|zěn me} / {怎么样|zěn me yàng} | how | {如何|rú hé}{写|xiě}{简历|jiǎn lì} how to write a CV | 27 |

## Degree and amount

| Written | Spoken | Meaning | Example | Lesson |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| {极其|jí qí} | {非常|fēi cháng} | extremely | {这|zhè}{次|cì}{合作|hé zuò}{极其|jí qí}{重要|zhòng yào}。 This cooperation is extremely important. | 03 |
| {过于|guò yú} | {太|tài} | too, excessively | {你|nǐ}{过于|guò yú}{紧张|jǐn zhāng}{了|le}。 You're too tense. | 07 |
| {较|jiào} | {比较|bǐ jiào} | relatively, rather | {价格|jià gé}{较|jiào}{高|gāo} the price is rather high | 27 |
| {需|xū} | {需要|xū yào} | to need | {如|rú}{需|xū}{帮助|bāng zhù}，{请|qǐng}{联系|lián xì}{客服|kè fú}。 If you need help, contact customer service. | 27 |
| {应当|yīng dāng} | {应该|yīng gāi} | should | {员工|yuán gōng}{应当|yīng dāng}{遵守|zūn shǒu}{规定|guī dìng}。 Staff should follow the rules. | 27 |
| {总共|zǒng gòng} | {一共|yí gòng} | in all | {总共|zǒng gòng}{三百|sān bǎi}{块|kuài} three hundred in all (both are spoken; {总共|zǒng gòng} a little firmer) | 04 |

## Joining words and sentences

| Written | Spoken | Meaning | Example | Lesson |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| {以及|yǐ jí} / {及|jí} | {和|hé} / {还|hái}{有|yǒu} | and, as well as | {姓名|xìng míng}、{电话|diàn huà}{以及|yǐ jí}{住址|zhù zhǐ} name, phone number and address | 02, 27 |
| {假如|jiǎ rú} | {如果|rú guǒ} | if, supposing | {假如|jiǎ rú}{没有|méi yǒu}{你们|nǐ men}，{公司|gōng sī}{不|bù}{可能|kě néng}{成立|chéng lì}。 Without you, the company couldn't have been founded. | 05 |
| {便|biàn} | {就|jiù} | then, at once | {一|yí}{到|dào}{北京|Běi jīng}，{他|tā}{便|biàn}{给|gěi}{我|wǒ}{打|dǎ}{了|le}{电话|diàn huà}。 As soon as he reached Beijing, he called me. | 27 |
| {因而|yīn ér} / {从而|cóng ér} | {所以|suǒ yǐ} | so, thus / thereby | {成本|chéng běn}{降低|jiàng dī}{了|le}，{因而|yīn ér}{价格|jià gé}{也|yě}{降低|jiàng dī}{了|le}。 Costs fell, so prices fell too. | 27 |
| {可见|kě jiàn} / {由此|yóu cǐ}{可见|kě jiàn} | {看来|kàn lái} / {说明|shuō míng} | it's clear that | {天天|tiān tiān}{排队|pái duì}，{可见|kě jiàn}{很|hěn}{受|shòu}{欢迎|huān yíng}。 There's a queue every day: clearly it's popular. | 04, 26 |
| {如|rú} / {如同|rú tóng} | {像|xiàng} | like, as | {如下|rú xià} as follows | 27 |

## Verbs

| Written | Spoken | Meaning | Example | Lesson |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| {从事|cóng shì} | {做|zuò} (…{工作|gōng zuò}) | to work in | {从事|cóng shì}{新闻|xīn wén}{工作|gōng zuò} to work in journalism | 01 |
| {聘请|pìn qǐng} | {请|qǐng} | to engage, hire | {公司|gōng sī}{聘请|pìn qǐng}{她|tā}{当|dāng}{顾问|gù wèn}。 The company engaged her as an adviser. | 01 |
| {召开|zhào kāi} | {开|kāi} ({会|huì}) | to convene | {召开|zhào kāi}{会议|huì yì} to hold a meeting | 02 |
| {出席|chū xí} | {参加|cān jiā} | to attend | {出席|chū xí}{会议|huì yì} to attend a meeting | 02 |
| {出售|chū shòu} | {卖|mài} | to sell | {本|běn}{店|diàn}{出售|chū shòu}{各种|gè zhǒng}{水果|shuǐ guǒ}。 This shop sells all kinds of fruit. | 04 |
| {退还|tuì huán} | {退|tuì} / {还|huán} | to give back, refund | {退还|tuì huán}{押金|yā jīn} to refund a deposit | 04 |
| {拥有|yōng yǒu} | {有|yǒu} | to have, own | {拥有|yōng yǒu}{自己|zì jǐ}{的|de}{公司|gōng sī} to own one's own company | 05 |
| {敢于|gǎn yú} | {敢|gǎn} | to dare to | {敢于|gǎn yú}{尝试|cháng shì} to dare to try | 05 |
| {面临|miàn lín} | {遇到|yù dào} | to face (a problem) | {面临|miàn lín}{挑战|tiǎo zhàn} to face a challenge | 05 |
| {作出|zuò chū} | {做|zuò} | to make (a decision) | {作出|zuò chū}{决定|jué dìng} to make a decision | 05 |

## Contracts and notices

| Written | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| {以下|yǐ xià}{简称|jiǎn chēng} | hereafter called | {甲方|jiǎ fāng}：×××（{以下|yǐ xià}{简称|jiǎn chēng}“{公司|gōng sī}”） |
| {须|xū} xū | must (= {必须|bì xū}) | {员工|yuán gōng}{须|xū}{于|yú}{九|jiǔ}{点|diǎn}{报到|bào dào}。 Staff must report at nine. |
| {于|yú} yú | at, on, in (= {在|zài}) | {成立|chéng lì}{于|yú}2010{年|nián} founded in 2010 |
| {与|yǔ} | and, with (= {和|hé}, {跟|gēn}) | {公司|gōng sī}{与|yǔ}{员工|yuán gōng}{签订|qiān dìng}{本|běn}{合同|hé tong}。 |
| X {的|de} (closing a condition) | in the case where X | {工作|gōng zuò}{时间|shí jiān}{不|bú}{固定|gù dìng}{的|de}，{按|àn}{规定|guī dìng}{支付|zhī fù}{加班|jiā bān}{工资|gōng zī}。 Where hours are irregular, overtime is paid as set out. |
| {另|lìng}{行|xíng}{通知|tōng zhī} | notice will be given separately | {下|xià}{次|cì}{会议|huì yì}{时间|shí jiān}{另|lìng}{行|xíng}{通知|tōng zhī}。 |

({甲方|jiǎ fāng} jiǎ fāng and {乙方|yǐ fāng} yǐ fāng, Party A and Party B, are the two sides of a contract: {甲|jiǎ} and {乙|yǐ} are lesson 27's
characters.)

language.name: Chinese
language.vocabSource: covers the words and characters of HSK 3.0 level 5 (2025 exam syllabus; 3,600 words and 1,527 characters with levels 1-4); grouping, glosses and examples are our own

vocab.note: yī when you count and inside numbers ({十一|shí yī}, eleven). Before other words its tone changes, and this app writes the change: {一|yí}{个|gè} (one, of something), {一起|yì qǐ} (together).
vocab.example: {一|yī}、{二|èr}、{三|sān}！
vocab.exampleEn: One, two, three!

vocab.note: For counting and inside numbers ({十二|shí èr}, twelve). Before a measure word Chinese says {两|liǎng} instead: {两|liǎng}{个|gè}{人|rén}, two people (Chinese HSK 1).
vocab.example: {一|yī}、{二|èr}、{三|sān}、{四|sì}、{五|wǔ}。
vocab.exampleEn: One, two, three, four, five.

vocab.example: {我们|wǒ men}{是|shì}{三|sān}{个|gè}{人|rén}。
vocab.exampleEn: There are three of us.

vocab.note: Tens are built with it: {二十|èr shí} (20 = two tens), {十二|shí èr} (12 = ten and two).
vocab.example: {三|sān}{十|shí}{个|gè}{人|rén}。
vocab.exampleEn: Thirty people.

vocab.note: After a country it gives the people: {中国|Zhōng guó}{人|rén}, a Chinese person, Chinese people.
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{是|shì}{中国|Zhōng guó}{人|rén}。
vocab.exampleEn: I'm Chinese.

vocab.note: Also used for age: {你|nǐ}{多|duō}{大|dà}？ How old are you? (Chinese HSK 1). Its opposite is {小|xiǎo}.
vocab.example: {中国|Zhōng guó}{很|hěn}{大|dà}。
vocab.exampleEn: China is big.

vocab.note: Fourth tone, falling. Don't confuse it with {十|shí} (ten, rising): {四十四|sì shí sì} is 44.
vocab.example: {我们|wǒ men}{是|shì}{四|sì}{个|gè}{人|rén}。
vocab.exampleEn: There are four of us.

vocab.example: {五|wǔ}{个|gè}{人|rén}。
vocab.exampleEn: Five people.

vocab.note: Spelled liù, a short form of liòu: you hear a light o before the u. The tone mark goes on the u.
vocab.example: {六|liù}{十|shí}{六|liù}。
vocab.exampleEn: Sixty-six.

vocab.note: q is said like the ch of "cheese", with a puff of air.
vocab.example: {七|qī}{月|yuè}。
vocab.exampleEn: July (the seventh month).

vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{八|bā}{岁|suì}。
vocab.exampleEn: I'm eight (years old).

vocab.example: {九十九|jiǔ shí jiǔ}{个|gè}{人|rén}。
vocab.exampleEn: Ninety-nine people.

vocab.note: To one person: a friend, a classmate, anyone your age. The polite form for older people and strangers is {您|nín} (Chinese HSK 1).
vocab.example: {你|nǐ}{是|shì}{王芳|Wáng Fāng}{吗|ma}？
vocab.exampleEn: Are you Wang Fang?

vocab.note: One word for "I" and "me": {我|wǒ} doesn't change.
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{是|shì}{王芳|Wáng Fāng}。
vocab.exampleEn: I'm Wang Fang.

vocab.note: Said ní hǎo (two third tones: the first rises). Answer with {你好|nǐ hǎo} too.
vocab.example: {你好|nǐ hǎo}，{我|wǒ}{是|shì}{王芳|Wáng Fāng}。
vocab.exampleEn: Hello, I'm Wang Fang.

vocab.note: Alone it also means "OK, all right": {好|hǎo}！
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{很|hěn}{好|hǎo}。
vocab.exampleEn: I'm fine. / I'm well.

vocab.note: bù, but bú before a fourth tone: {不|bú}{是|shì}, {不客气|bú kè qi}. This app writes the change; most dictionaries write bù everywhere.
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{不|bú}{是|shì}{王芳|Wáng Fāng}。
vocab.exampleEn: I'm not Wang Fang.

vocab.note: Links two nouns: A {是|shì} B. It never changes for I, you or they. Its negative is {不|bú}{是|shì}.
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{是|shì}{中国|Zhōng guó}{人|rén}。
vocab.exampleEn: I'm Chinese.

vocab.note: Before a surname it's a friendly way to address a younger person: {小|xiǎo}{王|Wáng}, "young Wang".
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{的|de}{狗|gǒu}{很|hěn}{小|xiǎo}。
vocab.exampleEn: My dog is small.

vocab.note: Literally "middle country". A capital Z in pinyin, as for every name.
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{是|shì}{中国|Zhōng guó}{人|rén}。
vocab.exampleEn: I'm Chinese. / I'm from China.

vocab.note: The second xie is light and short (neutral tone). Reply: {不客气|bú kè qi}.
vocab.example: {谢谢|xiè xie}{你|nǐ}！
vocab.exampleEn: Thank you!

vocab.note: The reply to {谢谢|xiè xie}. Literally "don't be so polite". 不 is bú here, before the fourth tone kè.
vocab.example: — {谢谢|xiè xie}！— {不客气|bú kè qi}。
vocab.exampleEn: — Thanks! — You're welcome.

vocab.note: An apology for something you did. The 不 in the middle is light (neutral tone). Reply: {没关系|méi guān xi}.
vocab.example: {对不起|duì bu qǐ}，{我|wǒ}{不|bú}{是|shì}{王芳|Wáng Fāng}。
vocab.exampleEn: Sorry, I'm not Wang Fang.

vocab.note: The reply to {对不起|duì bu qǐ}. Literally "there's no connection".
vocab.example: — {对不起|duì bu qǐ}！— {没关系|méi guān xi}。
vocab.exampleEn: — Sorry! — That's all right.

vocab.note: Literally "again see". Two fourth tones: both fall.
vocab.example: {再见|zài jiàn}，{王芳|Wáng Fāng}！
vocab.exampleEn: Goodbye, Wang Fang!

vocab.note: Sounds the same as {她|tā} (she); only the writing differs: 亻 "person" here, 女 "woman" in 她.
vocab.example: {他|tā}{是|shì}{老师|lǎo shī}。
vocab.exampleEn: He's a teacher.

vocab.note: Sounds the same as {他|tā} (he). The radical 女 "woman" shows it means a woman.
vocab.example: {她|tā}{叫|jiào}{王芳|Wáng Fāng}。
vocab.exampleEn: Her name is Wang Fang.

vocab.note: For teachers, older people, customers and strangers; {你|nǐ} for friends and people your age.
vocab.example: {您|nín}{是|shì}{王老师|Wáng lǎo shī}{吗|ma}？
vocab.exampleEn: Are you Teacher Wang?

vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{叫|jiào}{李明|Lǐ Míng}。
vocab.exampleEn: My name is Li Ming.

vocab.note: Stays where the answer goes: {你|nǐ}{叫|jiào}{什么|shén me}？ — {我|wǒ}{叫|jiào}{安娜|Ān nà}。 Second syllable neutral.
vocab.example: {他|tā}{叫|jiào}{什么|shén me}？
vocab.exampleEn: What's he called?

vocab.note: Second syllable neutral: míng zi.
vocab.example: {你|nǐ}{叫|jiào}{什么|shén me}{名字|míng zi}？
vocab.exampleEn: What's your name?

vocab.note: At the end of a statement, makes a yes-or-no question. Not used with question words such as {什么|shén me}.
vocab.example: {你|nǐ}{是|shì}{学生|xué sheng}{吗|ma}？
vocab.exampleEn: Are you a student?

vocab.note: Before an adjective in a plain statement, usually unstressed: {我|wǒ}{很|hěn}{好|hǎo} is just "I'm fine".
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{很|hěn}{好|hǎo}，{谢谢|xiè xie}。
vocab.exampleEn: I'm fine, thanks.

vocab.note: Also a title after a family name: {王老师|Wáng lǎo shī}, Teacher Wang.
vocab.example: {她|tā}{不|bú}{是|shì}{老师|lǎo shī}。
vocab.exampleEn: She isn't a teacher.

vocab.note: Second syllable neutral in mainland speech: xué sheng.
vocab.example: {他|tā}{是|shì}{学生|xué sheng}，{不|bú}{是|shì}{老师|lǎo shī}。
vocab.exampleEn: He's a student, not a teacher.

vocab.note: Only for people, never after a number: {三|sān}{个|gè}{学生|xué sheng}, not 三个学生们.
vocab.example: {老师们|lǎo shī men}{好|hǎo}！
vocab.exampleEn: Hello, teachers!

vocab.example: {我们|wǒ men}{都|dōu}{是|shì}{学生|xué sheng}。
vocab.exampleEn: We're all students.

vocab.example: {你们|nǐ men}{是|shì}{哪|nǎ}{国|guó}{人|rén}？
vocab.exampleEn: Where are you all from?

vocab.note: Sounds the same as {她们|tā men} (they, all women). Used for any mixed group.
vocab.example: {他们|tā men}{都|dōu}{会|huì}{说|shuō}{英语|Yīng yǔ}。
vocab.exampleEn: They can all speak English.

vocab.note: Only when everyone in the group is a woman; otherwise {他们|tā men}.
vocab.example: {她们|tā men}{是|shì}{老师|lǎo shī}。
vocab.exampleEn: They're teachers.

vocab.note: In country names: {中国|Zhōng guó}, {美国|Měi guó}. {哪|nǎ}{国|guó}{人|rén}: a person of which country?
vocab.example: {你|nǐ}{是|shì}{哪|nǎ}{国|guó}{人|rén}？
vocab.exampleEn: Where are you from?

vocab.note: Third tone. Don't confuse with {那|nà} (that), fourth tone.
vocab.example: {他|tā}{是|shì}{哪|nǎ}{国|guó}{人|rén}？
vocab.exampleEn: Where is he from? (Which country is he from?)

vocab.note: The usual word in classes and textbooks. {中文|Zhōng wén} means the same, especially written Chinese.
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{会|huì}{说|shuō}{汉语|Hàn yǔ}。
vocab.exampleEn: I can speak Chinese.

vocab.note: Used for the language in general and for written Chinese: a menu or a website in Chinese.
vocab.example: {她|tā}{也|yě}{会|huì}{说|shuō}{中文|Zhōng wén}。
vocab.exampleEn: She speaks Chinese too.

vocab.example: {他|tā}{说|shuō}{英语|Yīng yǔ}。
vocab.exampleEn: He speaks English.

vocab.note: A skill you have learned: {会|huì}{说|shuō}{汉语|Hàn yǔ}. Also "will (probably)" later in the course.
vocab.example: {你|nǐ}{会|huì}{说|shuō}{汉语|Hàn yǔ}{吗|ma}？
vocab.exampleEn: Can you speak Chinese?

vocab.note: After a noun or pronoun: {你|nǐ}{呢|ne}？ "And you?" Neutral tone.
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{是|shì}{英国人|Yīng guó rén}，{你|nǐ}{呢|ne}？
vocab.exampleEn: I'm British. And you?

vocab.note: Before the verb, never at the end: {我|wǒ}{也|yě}{是|shì}{学生|xué sheng}. With {不|bù}: "not ... either".
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{也|yě}{是|shì}{学生|xué sheng}。
vocab.exampleEn: I'm a student too.

vocab.note: After the plural subject, before the verb. With {也|yě}: {也|yě}{都|dōu}, never 都也.
vocab.example: {我们|wǒ men}{都|dōu}{是|shì}{美国人|Měi guó rén}。
vocab.exampleEn: We're both American.

vocab.note: Negative {没有|méi yǒu}, never 不有. "There is" comes in lesson 17.
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{有|yǒu}{一|yí}{个|gè}{哥哥|gē ge}。
vocab.exampleEn: I have an older brother.

vocab.note: The negative of {有|yǒu}. Later also "didn't" (lesson 25).
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{没有|méi yǒu}{姐姐|jiě jie}。
vocab.exampleEn: I don't have an older sister.

vocab.note: Owner + {的|de} + thing: {老师|lǎo shī}{的|de}{名字|míng zi}. Usually dropped with family and home: {我|wǒ}{妈妈|mā ma}.
vocab.example: {这|zhè}{是|shì}{老师|lǎo shī}{的|de}{名字|míng zi}。
vocab.exampleEn: This is the teacher's name.

vocab.note: Also said zhèi in speech, especially before a measure word.
vocab.example: {这|zhè}{是|shì}{我|wǒ}{妈妈|mā ma}。
vocab.exampleEn: This is my mum.

vocab.note: Fourth tone. {哪|nǎ} (which) has the third tone. Also said nèi in speech.
vocab.example: {那|nà}{是|shì}{我们|wǒ men}{老师|lǎo shī}。
vocab.exampleEn: That's our teacher.

vocab.note: Joins nouns and pronouns only, never sentences or verbs.
vocab.example: {爸爸|bà ba}{和|hé}{妈妈|mā ma}{都|dōu}{是|shì}{老师|lǎo shī}。
vocab.exampleEn: Dad and Mum are both teachers.

vocab.note: No {的|de} after a pronoun: {我|wǒ}{家|jiā}, my home or my family. Later also a measure word for shops and companies.
vocab.example: {你|nǐ}{家|jiā}{有|yǒu}{几|jǐ}{个|gè}{人|rén}？
vocab.exampleEn: How many people are there in your family?

vocab.example: {这|zhè}{是|shì}{我|wǒ}{的|de}{家人|jiā rén}。
vocab.exampleEn: These are my family.

vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{爸爸|bà ba}{是|shì}{老师|lǎo shī}。
vocab.exampleEn: My dad is a teacher.

vocab.example: {这|zhè}{是|shì}{我|wǒ}{妈妈|mā ma}。
vocab.exampleEn: This is my mum.

vocab.example: {你|nǐ}{有|yǒu}{哥哥|gē ge}{吗|ma}？
vocab.exampleEn: Do you have an older brother?

vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{姐姐|jiě jie}{会|huì}{说|shuō}{汉语|Hàn yǔ}。
vocab.exampleEn: My older sister speaks Chinese.

vocab.note: For a small number you expect, with a measure word: {几|jǐ}{个|gè}. For any number: {多少|duō shao}.
vocab.example: {你|nǐ}{有|yǒu}{几|jǐ}{个|gè}{姐姐|jiě jie}？
vocab.exampleEn: How many older sisters do you have?

vocab.note: Between a number and a noun: {一|yí}{个|gè}{人|rén}. Often light in speech. {一|yī} becomes yí before it.
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{家|jiā}{有|yǒu}{五|wǔ}{个|gè}{人|rén}。
vocab.exampleEn: There are five people in my family.

vocab.note: Said once for each gap inside a number: {一千零五|yì qiān líng wǔ} (1,005).
vocab.example: {一百零五|yì bǎi líng wǔ}
vocab.exampleEn: one hundred and five

vocab.note: Always with a number in front: {一百|yì bǎi}, never 百 alone for 100.
vocab.example: {三百四十五|sān bǎi sì shí wǔ}
vocab.exampleEn: three hundred and forty-five

vocab.example: {两千零二十六|liǎng qiān líng èr shí liù}
vocab.exampleEn: two thousand and twenty-six

vocab.note: Before a measure word: {两|liǎng}{个|gè}{人|rén}. In counting and inside numbers it's {二|èr}: {十二|shí èr}.
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{有|yǒu}{两|liǎng}{个|gè}{妹妹|mèi mei}。
vocab.exampleEn: I have two younger sisters.

vocab.note: Age needs no {是|shì}: {我|wǒ}{二十|èr shí}{岁|suì}. Ask children {几岁|jǐ suì}, adults {多大|duō dà}.
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{女儿|nǚ ér}{六|liù}{岁|suì}。
vocab.exampleEn: My daughter is six.

vocab.note: Usually with {很|hěn}: {很多|hěn duō}{人|rén}. Before an adjective it asks "how": {多大|duō dà}, how old.
vocab.example: {中国|Zhōng guó}{有|yǒu}{很多|hěn duō}{人|rén}。
vocab.exampleEn: China has a lot of people.

vocab.note: For any number; the measure word is optional. {几|jǐ} is for small numbers and needs one.
vocab.example: {中国|Zhōng guó}{有|yǒu}{多少|duō shao}{人|rén}？
vocab.exampleEn: How many people does China have?

vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{儿子|ér zi}{九|jiǔ}{岁|suì}。
vocab.exampleEn: My son is nine.

vocab.note: Both syllables keep their tones: nǚ ér.
vocab.example: {这|zhè}{是|shì}{我|wǒ}{女儿|nǚ ér}。
vocab.exampleEn: This is my daughter.

vocab.example: {您|nín}{有|yǒu}{几|jǐ}{个|gè}{孩子|hái zi}？
vocab.exampleEn: How many children do you have?

vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{弟弟|dì di}{十五|shí wǔ}{岁|suì}。
vocab.exampleEn: My younger brother is fifteen.

vocab.example: {你|nǐ}{妹妹|mèi mei}{多大|duō dà}？
vocab.exampleEn: How old is your younger sister?

meanings: mouth (also: measure word for family members)
vocab.note: As a measure word for people, only for the size of a family: {我|wǒ}{家|jiā}{有|yǒu}{五|wǔ}{口|kǒu}{人|rén}.
vocab.example: {你|nǐ}{家|jiā}{有|yǒu}{几|jǐ}{口|kǒu}{人|rén}？
vocab.exampleEn: How many people are there in your family?

vocab.note: Also before a verb, for where it happens: {我|wǒ}{在|zài}{公司|gōng sī}{工作|gōng zuò}. Sounds like {再|zài} (again).
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{妈妈|mā ma}{在|zài}{家|jiā}。
vocab.exampleEn: My mum is at home.

vocab.note: Verb and noun: {我|wǒ}{在|zài}{大学|dà xué}{工作|gōng zuò} (I work at a university); {你|nǐ}{有|yǒu}{工作|gōng zuò}{吗|ma}？ (Do you have a job?)
vocab.example: {他|tā}{在|zài}{公司|gōng sī}{工作|gōng zuò}。
vocab.exampleEn: He works for a company.

vocab.example: {她|tā}{是|shì}{医生|yī shēng}。
vocab.exampleEn: She's a doctor.

vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{爸爸|bà ba}{在|zài}{公司|gōng sī}{工作|gōng zuò}。
vocab.exampleEn: My dad works for a company.

vocab.example: {我们|wǒ men}{在|zài}{学校|xué xiào}{说|shuō}{汉语|Hàn yǔ}。
vocab.exampleEn: We speak Chinese at school.

vocab.example: {王老师|Wáng lǎo shī}{在|zài}{大学|dà xué}{工作|gōng zuò}。
vocab.exampleEn: Teacher Wang works at a university.

vocab.note: {生|shēng} keeps its first tone here, unlike {学生|xué sheng}.
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{哥哥|gē ge}{是|shì}{大学生|dà xué shēng}。
vocab.exampleEn: My older brother is a university student.

vocab.note: Before a noun: {男|nán}{老师|lǎo shī}, a male teacher. Not used alone as "a man".
vocab.example: {我们|wǒ men}{的|de}{汉语|Hàn yǔ}{老师|lǎo shī}{是|shì}{男|nán}{老师|lǎo shī}。
vocab.exampleEn: Our Chinese teacher is a man.

vocab.note: Before a noun: {女|nǚ}{医生|yī shēng}, a female doctor. Not used alone as "a woman".
vocab.example: {她|tā}{是|shì}{女|nǚ}{医生|yī shēng}。
vocab.exampleEn: She's a (female) doctor.

vocab.example: {今天|jīn tiān}{星期一|xīng qī yī}。
vocab.exampleEn: Today is Monday.

vocab.example: {明天|míng tiān}{我|wǒ}{在|zài}{家|jiā}。
vocab.exampleEn: I'll be at home tomorrow.

vocab.example: {昨天|zuó tiān}{星期天|xīng qī tiān}。
vocab.exampleEn: Yesterday was Sunday.

vocab.note: Counts without {个|gè}: {一天|yì tiān}, {两天|liǎng tiān}. Also "sky", as in {天气|tiān qì} (weather, lesson 20). Can be a measure word too.
vocab.example: {他|tā}{在|zài}{中国|Zhōng guó}{工作|gōng zuò}{三天|sān tiān}。
vocab.exampleEn: He's working in China for three days.

vocab.note: Takes {个|gè} when counted: {两个星期|liǎng gè xīng qī}. Add {一|yī} to {六|liù} for Monday to Saturday: {星期一|xīng qī yī}, {星期六|xīng qī liù}.
vocab.example: {一个星期|yí gè xīng qī}{有|yǒu}{七天|qī tiān}。
vocab.exampleEn: A week has seven days.

vocab.note: The written and more formal word, seen on calendars and timetables; in everyday speech {星期天|xīng qī tiān}.
vocab.example: {星期日|xīng qī rì}{学校|xué xiào}{没有|méi yǒu}{人|rén}。
vocab.exampleEn: There's nobody at the school on Sunday.

vocab.note: The everyday spoken word; {星期日|xīng qī rì} is the written one. There is no {星期七|xīng qī qī}.
vocab.example: {星期天|xīng qī tiān}{我|wǒ}{不|bù}{工作|gōng zuò}。
vocab.exampleEn: I don't work on Sundays.

vocab.note: Month names are number + {月|yuè}: {一月|yī yuè} (January), {十二月|shí èr yuè} (December). "One month" is {一个月|yí gè yuè}.
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{十月|shí yuè}{不|bù}{工作|gōng zuò}。
vocab.exampleEn: I'm not working in October.

vocab.note: Number + {号|hào} in speech: {十六号|shí liù hào} (the 16th); writing uses {日|rì}. Also "number", as in {手机号|shǒu jī hào} (mobile number, lesson 10). Can be a measure word too.
vocab.example: {今天|jīn tiān}{几号|jǐ hào}？
vocab.exampleEn: What's the date today?

vocab.note: Written and formal: 11{月|yuè}16{日|rì}. In speech, {号|hào}. As a noun, {日|rì} is also "sun".
vocab.example: {今天|jīn tiān}{是|shì}11{月|yuè}16{日|rì}。
vocab.exampleEn: Today is 16 November.

vocab.note: Counts without {个|gè}: {两年|liǎng nián}. Years are read digit by digit: 2026{年|nián}, èr líng èr liù nián.
vocab.example: {一年|yì nián}{有|yǒu}{十二个月|shí èr gè yuè}。
vocab.exampleEn: A year has twelve months.

vocab.note: Two o'clock is {两点|liǎng diǎn}. An amount of hours is {小时|xiǎo shí}. Also "a little" in {一点儿|yì diǎnr} (lesson 12).
vocab.example: {现在|xiàn zài}{几点|jǐ diǎn}？
vocab.exampleEn: What time is it?

vocab.note: Clock minutes: {八点十分|bā diǎn shí fēn} (8:10). An amount of minutes is {分钟|fēn zhōng}. Also a fen, a hundredth of a yuan.
vocab.example: {现在|xiàn zài}{九点二十分|jiǔ diǎn èr shí fēn}。

vocab.note: An amount of time, with no {个|gè}: {十分钟|shí fēn zhōng} (ten minutes). On the clock, {分|fēn}.
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{有|yǒu}{十分钟|shí fēn zhōng}。
vocab.exampleEn: I have ten minutes.

vocab.note: After the hour, half past: {八点半|bā diǎn bàn}. Half an hour: {半个小时|bàn gè xiǎo shí}.
vocab.example: {现在|xiàn zài}{七点半|qī diǎn bàn}。
vocab.exampleEn: It's half past seven.

vocab.note: Usually with {个|gè}: {两个小时|liǎng gè xiǎo shí} (two hours). Two o'clock is {两点|liǎng diǎn}.
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{一天|yì tiān}{工作|gōng zuò}{八个小时|bā gè xiǎo shí}。
vocab.exampleEn: I work eight hours a day.

vocab.example: {现在|xiàn zài}{两点|liǎng diǎn}。
vocab.exampleEn: It's two o'clock now.

vocab.note: Time you have or spend: {有时间|yǒu shí jiān} (to have time). To ask the clock time, use {几点|jǐ diǎn}.
vocab.example: {你|nǐ}{有|yǒu}{时间|shí jiān}{吗|ma}？
vocab.exampleEn: Do you have time?

vocab.note: The whole morning up to noon. Goes before the clock time: {上午|shàng wǔ}{十点|shí diǎn} (10 a.m.).
vocab.example: {王老师|Wáng lǎo shī}{上午|shàng wǔ}{在|zài}{学校|xué xiào}。
vocab.exampleEn: Teacher Wang is at school in the morning.

vocab.note: Before the clock time: {下午|xià wǔ}{三点|sān diǎn} (3 p.m.).
vocab.example: {下午|xià wǔ}{三点|sān diǎn}{我|wǒ}{在|zài}{家|jiā}。
vocab.exampleEn: I'm at home at three in the afternoon.

vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{中午|zhōng wǔ}{在|zài}{公司|gōng sī}。
vocab.exampleEn: I'm at the office at noon.

vocab.note: The early part of the morning, getting up and breakfast; {上午|shàng wǔ} is the whole morning until noon.
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{早上|zǎo shang}{六点|liù diǎn}{起床|qǐ chuáng}。
vocab.exampleEn: I get up at six in the morning.

vocab.note: From about six until bedtime: {晚上|wǎn shang}{十一点|shí yī diǎn} is 11 p.m.
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{晚上|wǎn shang}{在|zài}{家|jiā}。
vocab.exampleEn: I'm at home in the evening.

vocab.note: A separable verb: {起|qǐ} (rise) + {床|chuáng} (bed).
vocab.example: {你|nǐ}{几点|jǐ diǎn}{起床|qǐ chuáng}？
vocab.exampleEn: What time do you get up?

vocab.note: A separable verb: {睡|shuì} (sleep) + {觉|jiào} (a sleep), so no object follows it. "Sleep eight hours" uses {睡|shuì} alone (lesson 21).
vocab.example: {他|tā}{晚上|wǎn shang}{十一点|shí yī diǎn}{睡觉|shuì jiào}。
vocab.exampleEn: He goes to bed at eleven at night.

vocab.note: A separable verb: {上|shàng} (go on) + {班|bān} (a shift). The opposite is {下班|xià bān}.
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{八点|bā diǎn}{上班|shàng bān}。
vocab.exampleEn: I start work at eight.

vocab.example: {你|nǐ}{几点|jǐ diǎn}{下班|xià bān}？
vocab.exampleEn: What time do you finish work?

vocab.note: With {吃|chī} (to eat, lesson 11): {吃早饭|chī zǎo fàn}, to have breakfast.
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{七点|qī diǎn}{吃|chī}{早饭|zǎo fàn}。
vocab.exampleEn: I have breakfast at seven.

vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{在|zài}{公司|gōng sī}{吃|chī}{午饭|wǔ fàn}。
vocab.exampleEn: I have lunch at the office.

vocab.example: {我们|wǒ men}{七点|qī diǎn}{吃|chī}{晚饭|wǎn fàn}。
vocab.exampleEn: We have dinner at seven.

vocab.note: Also a morning greeting: {早|zǎo}！ or {你早|nǐ zǎo}！ (Morning!). Opposite: {晚|wǎn}.
vocab.example: {你|nǐ}{很|hěn}{早|zǎo}！
vocab.exampleEn: You're early!

vocab.example: {晚上|wǎn shang}{十二点|shí èr diǎn}{很|hěn}{晚|wǎn}。
vocab.exampleEn: Twelve at night is late.

vocab.note: Away from the speaker. No word for "to" before the place: {去|qù}{学校|xué xiào}.
vocab.example: {你|nǐ}{去|qù}{哪儿|nǎr}？
vocab.exampleEn: Where are you going?

vocab.note: Towards the speaker: if you aren't there yourself, use {去|qù}.
vocab.example: {你|nǐ}{来|lái}{我|wǒ}{家|jiā}{吗|ma}？
vocab.exampleEn: Are you coming to my place?

vocab.note: Back to where you belong: {回家|huí jiā} (go home), {回国|huí guó} (go back to your country).
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{晚上|wǎn shang}{回|huí}{家|jiā}。
vocab.exampleEn: I go home in the evening.

vocab.note: A wish, gentle and polite. Also "to think" and "to miss" someone. Negative: {不想|bù xiǎng}.
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{想|xiǎng}{去|qù}{中国|Zhōng guó}。
vocab.exampleEn: I'd like to go to China.

vocab.note: More decided than {想|xiǎng}; also takes a noun ("I'd like…"). "Don't want to" is {不想|bù xiǎng}: {不要|bú yào} + verb means "don't!" (lesson 21).
vocab.example: {明天|míng tiān}{我|wǒ}{要|yào}{上班|shàng bān}。
vocab.exampleEn: Tomorrow I have to work.

vocab.note: {做什么|zuò shén me}: (to) do what. Not {坐|zuò} (to sit, lesson 18), which sounds the same.
vocab.example: {你|nǐ}{星期六|xīng qī liù}{做|zuò}{什么|shén me}？
vocab.exampleEn: What are you doing on Saturday?

vocab.note: {有事|yǒu shì}: to be busy, have something on. A thing you can hold is {东西|dōng xi}.
vocab.example: {你|nǐ}{明天|míng tiān}{有|yǒu}{事|shì}{吗|ma}？
vocab.exampleEn: Are you busy tomorrow?

vocab.note: Neutral second syllable. With full tones, {东西|dōng xī} means "east and west". {买东西|mǎi dōng xi}: to go shopping.
vocab.example: {你|nǐ}{买|mǎi}{什么|shén me}{东西|dōng xi}？
vocab.exampleEn: What are you buying?

vocab.note: Third tone; {卖|mài} (to sell, lesson 13) is the same syllable with the fourth tone.
vocab.example: {你|nǐ}{想|xiǎng}{买|mǎi}{什么|shén me}？
vocab.exampleEn: What would you like to buy?

vocab.note: Also "to go and see, visit" a person: {看|kàn}{妈妈|mā ma}. "To see, catch sight of" is {看见|kàn jiàn} (lesson 24).
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{星期天|xīng qī tiān}{去|qù}{看|kàn}{妈妈|mā ma}。
vocab.exampleEn: On Sunday I'm going to see my mum.

vocab.note: One syllable with erhua. {哪里|nǎ lǐ} (lesson 16) means the same and is used everywhere. Not {那儿|nàr} (there).
vocab.example: {你|nǐ}{在|zài}{哪儿|nǎr}？
vocab.exampleEn: Where are you?

vocab.note: Said wéi, rising, when you answer the phone; a sharp falling wèi is "Hey!".
vocab.example: {喂|wéi}，{你好|nǐ hǎo}！
vocab.exampleEn: Hello? (on the phone)

vocab.note: {打|dǎ} (strike) + {电话|diàn huà}. "To phone someone" needs {给|gěi} (lesson 23).
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{在|zài}{打电话|dǎ diàn huà}。
vocab.exampleEn: I'm on the phone.

vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{家|jiā}{没有|méi yǒu}{电话|diàn huà}。
vocab.exampleEn: We don't have a phone at home.

vocab.note: Literally "hand machine". {手机号|shǒu jī hào}: mobile number.
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{在|zài}{找|zhǎo}{我|wǒ}{的|de}{手机|shǒu jī}。
vocab.exampleEn: I'm looking for my phone.

vocab.note: Before a verb: the action is going on right now. {在|zài} alone and a final {呢|ne} do the same job.
vocab.example: {他|tā}{正在|zhèng zài}{睡觉|shuì jiào}。
vocab.exampleEn: He's sleeping right now.

vocab.note: On the phone or at a door, {我|wǒ}{找|zhǎo} + person means "I'd like to speak to…".
vocab.example: {你|nǐ}{找|zhǎo}{谁|shéi}？
vocab.exampleEn: Who are you looking for?

vocab.note: Often said zhīdao, with a light second syllable. Knowing a person is {认识|rèn shi} (lesson 23).
vocab.example: {我|wǒ}{不|bù}{知道|zhī dào}。
